Here is a painted piece I completed a while ago, on one of my days off. Model and base colors For this painting I used a version of the base colors I created for my anatomy course, on which I will elaborate more later. I won’t go into too much detail here but basically the base colors are meant to be a general skin tone along with some complementary colors for specific parts of the body. I used the base color on the face and neck, the left shoulder, the right shoulder, and the hands and fingers. I did a quick fill of the hands with the darkest value of the base color to get a sense of volume and form. The skin tone was built up with various layers of linear black using the opacity in the color chip to modulate how thick the lines were. The effect of this is to get a nice, even skin tone and to hide the lines of the brushstrokes. This step took quite a few tries to get right, as I initially over-obfuscated the lines, making the skin look fake. The basic shapes were done in the color black, which gives you nice, crisp lines. I then added some high frequency noise using the default Dissolve filter in Photoshop. This gives the face some much needed texture and gives the skin a nice, wrinkled look. The eyes were given some shine using a white brush with a bit of transparency, which was then overworked with the brightness in the color chip to make it specular. Finally, the nose was painted with a simple shape on its own layer with a different base color, to break up the face a bit and add some variety to the skin tones. The first steps were base colors, hide the brushstrokes, and add some basic shapes. From here I added more details and highlights to the face and added the shoulder, neck and left and right hands. The base colors can be used as a general starting point for many different types of skin tones. All in all, this was a fun painting to do, with some nice and subtle details that wouldn’t have been there if I had used a standard white base and instead relied on a mix of many different skin tones. Transport Canada is a division of the public safety and national security portfolio of the Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness. The current Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness is The Hon. Ralph Goodale. The head office of Transport Canada is responsible for the Canadian Aviation Regulations, Canadian Trucking Regulations, National Transportation Safety Board, Canada Post Corp. Canada Border Services Agency, Canada Border Services Agency Aviation Unit, CIRA, MARPOL, Hybrid Vehicle Regulations, and Hazardous Liquid and Gasses Regulations. The aviation branch is also responsible for issuing and maintaining air operator's certificates and Type certificates for commercial airplanes, helicopters, and special mission aircraft. Transport Canada is responsible for issuing and maintaining Canadian shipping certificates and marine operators certificates as well as enforcing the requirements of the Canada Shipping Act and the Canada Marine Act. Transport Canada is an enforcement agency for the Canada Transportation Act. This act governs the transportation of persons and goods between Canada's regions. Transport Canada is also responsible for promoting safe and secure transportation through co-operation with transport agencies in other countries. This includes participation in the International Air Transport Association (IATA), the International Maritime Organization (IMO), the North American Aerospace Defence Command (NORAD) and Transport Canada Air Coordinating Center (ACC). Transport Canada personnel also assist in the investigation of civil aviation and maritime accidents and incidents. Transport Canada has over 4,000 staff and two wings located in Montreal and Calgary.

Cuba's intervention in the civil war in Angola, colloquially known as the Angolan Civil War (Portuguese: Guerra Civil Angolana), began in 1975 as a mediation mission to stop the war between the victorious National Liberation Front of Angola (FNLA) and the Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA). By the late 1970s, the FNLA was forced to rely on Cuban military aid, leading the MPLA to suspect a Cuban agenda to establish a pro-Western puppet state in Southern Africa. The Angolan Civil War continued well into the 1990s, eventually giving way to a peace process in 2002. By then, the Cuban military presence had grown considerably, representing the only non-Angolan government force in the country. After the independence of Namibia in 1990, Cuba adopted an "Africa Park" policy, supporting sovereign governments on the continent in exchange for exclusive rights to exploit natural resources, including diamonds. As a result, Cuba heavily invested in the economies of Southern African nations and established military bases in several of them, namely Angola, Botswana, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Gabon, Ghana, Mozambique, São Tome and Príncipe, Sudan and Zambia. In Angola, Cuba established the LUANDA program, establishing a communist state within a state that totaled 2 million people and a generated state revenue of $800 million per year.

Hinagdanan Cave is a show cave located in the Carcar City ng Baguaoblanco, Nueva Ecija, Philippines. The cave is long, with a main branch and two minor branches. It has two floors and a past filled with artifacts. The cave was declared a National Shrine by the National Museum of the Philippines in 2008. Hinagdanan Cave is a show cave located in the Carcar City ng Baguaoblanco, Nueva Ecija, Philippines. The cave is long, with a main branch and two minor branches. It has two floors and a past filled with artifacts. The cave was declared a National Shrine by the National Museum of the Philippines in 2008. Hinagdanan Cave was discovered on December 28, 1965 by Renato Canlas, an employee of the Provincial Government. The cave is named after a local Boholano heroine, Hinagdanan, who resisted the Japanese occupation during World War II. The main branch of the cave was filled with artifacts after Preservationist Director Jesús D. Villa declared it a National Shrine in 2008. The first branch, Hinagdanan II, was discovered on November 5, 1966 by Santiago Ramón, another employee of the Provincial Government. In 2012, a rescue team explored the unexplored middle branch of the cave but could not go all the way through due to tight spaces. It was declared sealed by the provincial government.

Catstye Cam is a satirical news program on the short-lived 2020 truTV reality show Intervention. The show features four real-life friends (Casey Turner, Wendy Plank, Kyle Maclachlan, and Robert Knepper) competing in various difficult tasks, such as jumping over hot coals or sleeping inside a casket, to win prizes donated by the show's producers. The prizes typically consist of gift certificates to Home Depot or Lowes. The show was conceived by series creator Jesse entertaining the idea of the crew becoming "mayor of a bachelors' village in Vietnam" or "hosting a southern comfort food supper club" only for the idea to be abandoned as being "too stupid". After several years of Jesse not pursuing the idea, the other three crew members convinced Jesse to let them host a version of the show they called Intervention: Catstye Cam. The name was derived from an inside joke referencing a local brand of wine. The first season consisted of five episodes, all of which were released for streaming on the truTV app and website. Reviews of the first episode were mixed; while some praised the concept and execution, others criticized the content for being too juvenile. The show garnered a small following on social media and was quickly picked up for a second season. The second season premiered on October 21, 2019 to 2.27 million views, and increased viewership for each of the subsequent episodes; the season finale on November 4, 2019 garnered 4.67 million views, making it the most-watched episode in the show's run.

Big Boy Records was a record label founded by Dewey Balfous in 1960. The label specialized in doo wop groups and is most famous for signing The Chiffons. Big Boy is also famous for taking the group to a Manhattan record shop and burning their first single "He's a Married Man" on the radio. Despite the label's emphasis on doo wop, it also signed other vocal groups such as The Moonglows, The sweet Inspirations and The Harptones. Big Boy Records is also the name of a 2017 song by The Moonshine Band. The song was written by Rhythm & blues singer Brooklynn Monninger and features singing by Harry Belafonte and The Moonshine Band. Dewey Balfous was born in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, and started the label as a hobby in his mother's tailor shop. In 2015, the Georgetown, District of Columbia, town renamed a street "Big Boy Street" in his honor. Big Boy was also the name of a doo wop band that was formed at the label. The group consisted of Larry Poozner, Sal Badalamenti, Bob Luman and Bill Adson. The label is best known for signing The Chiffons who went on to great success. The group's original members, 1955 - 1965, were, Millie Colao, Darlene Conley, Nancy Dwyer and Marlo Modine. The four later formed The Bluebelles with Jean King, 1955 - 1957, and the five of them performed together as "The Chiffons". In 2018, the group was inducted into the Doo Wop Hall of Fame.

Trichy is a town in the state of Tamil Nadu in India, also known as Trichy Nadu, Trichy City, Trichy District, and Little Tamil Nadu. It is the District & Headquarters of Trichy district. Trichy is one of the most popular and well known towns in India, famous for festivals like Pongal, Aanandhanam, and utsavam. During utsavam, the effigies of Masi, Ayyanar, Kasi, Dhandapani, Mariamman and Ponmen are carried in a colourful procession through the heart of the town, Trichambaram where they are kept overnight and taken to the nearby Kasi koobam in the early morning of the following day. Trichy also has a rich cultural heritage and has given many people to the world, including freedom fighter P M Kumaraswamy, former President of India Abdul Kalam, and former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu M Karunanidhi. Trichy was also the home town of Great poet Subramania Bharathi, who is also known as Thoobarumi, a nickname given to him by his friends, since he used to write his poems on the walls of the Trichy palace, which is now a museum. Trichy has one of the best rated campuses for educational institutes in India and also one of the oldest, Syama Hindu University. Trichy is the third largest English medium school in India, with an enrollment of over 52,000 students.

The 2015 Miami Hurricanes baseball team was an American college baseball team that represent the University of Miami in Coral Gables, Florida, in the 2015 NCAA Division I baseball season. The Hurricanes competed in the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) and were led by Hall of Fame coach Jim Morris. The Hurricanes played their home games at Alex Rodriguez Park on the university's campus. The Hurricanes began their season by winning their first five games, and 13 of 15, before playing their first game in the ACC Tournament. Miami won the ACC Tournament and then went on to the 2015 NCAA Division I Baseball Tournament. The Hurricanes were eliminated by Louisville in the 2015 College World Series. This season was the first for the Hurricanes in the newly constructed Alex Rodriguez Park, following the demolition of their previous home, Conal Field at Miami Ball Field. The Hurricanes' overall record and 28–6 win record in ACC play both ranked as the best in the conference's history. The Hurricanes appeared in the 2014 College World Series and advanced to the 2014 NCAA Division I Baseball Tournament, their first appearance since 2002. Hurricanes baseball started practice in 2014 under head coach Jim Morris, who would go on to become the all-time winningest coach in program history later that year. The Hurricanes played their 2014 home games at Jimmy Joe Robinson Stadium at Mark Light Field. The Hurricanes were led by All-American center fielder Dexter Williams. The Hurricanes finished the 2014 season with a record of 45–15, 13–9 in the Atlantic Coast Conference, to finish in third place in the ACC's Atlantic Division. With a win against Notre Dame on March 31, 2014, Miami joined Stanford and Minnesota as the only schools to win 90 or more games in the modern NCAA era (2000–present). The Hurricanes played their first game at the renovated Alex Rodriguez Park on April 18, 2015, and the first game at the newly built Johnny Rosenblatt Stadium in 2017. The Hurricanes were ranked as high as #3 in the nation early in the season. The Hurricanes appeared in the 2015 NCAA Division I Baseball Tournament as the #3 overall national seed, losing to Regional host and rival Florida State in the Seminfinal 8.

H. D. Shourie (born 19 March 1931) is an Indian journalist, author and orator. He is known for his criticism of government policies and accusing corrupt leaders. He is the founder-member of a popular citizens' right to information movement in India, the Satyam Adhikari Babus in Assam and other northeastern states. He is also the founder-member of the Pensioners' Welfare Association of the Bombay Municipal Corporation and a committee member of the National Association for the Blind. Shourie was born in Karachi, British India (now in Pakistan) and graduated in journalism from Jain University in Mumbai in 1953. Later, he started his career in journalism with The Times of India and The Economic Times. Shourie is a recipient of the Padma Shri, the fourth highest civilian award in India. He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2002. He was a member of the 14th Lok Sabha from Thiruvidaimarudur (west) constituency in Tamil Nadu, and was a member of the 15th Lok Sabha from Assam (North-East). He represented Assam in the 16th Lok Sabha. In the first constitution amendment bill, he tried to bring a provision for judges to retire at the age of 65 but the bill could not pass in the parliament Shourie is a prolific writer and has written more than 35 books, including a biography on prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru. Shourie has also published several articles in newspapers and magazines such as The Times of India, The Economic Times, The Hindu, DNA, Outlook, Businessworld, Tehelka and several other Indian dailies. He has been a vocal critic of the UPA government and currently he is one of the leading members of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and writes columns in its mouthpiece Organiser and in its website www.organiserlive.com. He has written articles in various other publications advocating the view that the current United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government of the Indian National Congress and the Bharatiya Janta Party (BJP) should part ways and give another chance to the people of India to vote them out. Shourie has also expressed his views on Indian politics, Indian economy and the justice system in his books, articles and interviews. He has also fought many legal cases in the court of law, including a large corruption case in the year 1994 which he had set up. This case was later transferred to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the matter is still sub-judice. He has been married to Sunanda since 1965 and has two sons, Aditya and Aman. Shourie lives in New Delhi with his family.

The Everglades, located in southern Florida, USA, is a subtropical wilderness of vast wilderness area, and important habitat for several endangered species. The ecosystem was severely damaged by the introduction of non-native species via environmental releases of water from lakes and canals, and waterway maintenance ditches, these species have now spread throughout the ecosystem. Species commonly found in the Everglades, and not native to the region, include: • Water moccasin • Eastern snakehead • Floating waterheart • Largemouth bass • Silver carp • Bigheaded bug • Zebra mussel Other non-native species successfully established in the Everglades, but not regarded as invasive, include: • Common carp • Grass carp • Black carp • Leopard shark • Burmese python • Coastal python The Everglades provides a unique environment where certain non-native species have been able to establish stable populations, and have become naturalized. The snakehead and bigheaded bug are two such species. The grass carp was introduced to control the proliferation of pest fish in agricultural runoff water, and has become established throughout the ecosystem. The Burmese python has also spread widely throughout the ecosystem, aided by the decline in several native species, such as the whopper alligator, which the python preys on. Overall, the introduction of non-native species to the Everglades ecosystem has been detrimental, and the continuing proliferation of certain species, such as the zebra mussel and water moccasin, is concerning. It is likely that several of the species listed are stable or becoming invasive, and are worthy of further investigation.

The Phred on Your Head Show was a television program that aired on the Fox network in the United States on Sunday evenings between September 1998 and January 2001. It was hosted by the mononymous Phred, a large, anthropomorphic raisin. The show featured several comedic segments along with music, guests and comedy bits parodying various television shows. The show's creator, Frank Caballero, was a writer for The Simpsons and was one of the producers for the program. The Phred on Your Head Show received a number of awards and nominations, and was popular with viewers. The series was canceled due to a brief move to midnight time slots and declining ratings. Although it was mentioned on several episodes of The Simpsons, the show did not receive a home release. The show is considered by some to be one of the best television series never released on DVD. "The Singing Wayans" A music parody segment in which the Phred and his backing singers, The Singing Wayans, perform a hip hop song. The lyrics of the song are often bizarre and nonsensical. "Skin Game" A music parody segment in which the Singing Wayans perform a disco version of the Skin Game. The Singing Wayans often perform the entire number with only their backs visible. "Dead Ringers" A horror parody in which the Phred and another raisin, Buckingham Palace–like, observe a situation being performed in a theater. The situations often turn to tragedy when one of the protagonists performs a wrong action. "Cocktail" An audience participation segment in which the Phred interacts with the audience. "Frequently Asked Questions" The Phred answers questions posed by viewers. The show also featured various comedy guests, often parodying popular culture, celebrity culture, or both. These have included: -David Spade -Meg Griffin -Adam Sandler -Trey Parker -David Spade and Trey Parker in separate episodes The Phred also does "comedy bits", often taking a satirical look at current pop culture or events. These have included: -A Puffy Circle with the Singing Wayans -An animated MadTV parody -An Off-Broadway musical parody Airing alongside more high-profile celebrities such as Adam Sandler and David Spade also placed the show in the position of being critically panned by pop culture parody enthusiasts, despite the high quality of the show's other material. Some have cited the show's poor timing as a reason for the negative reception. The program was placed in the early Sunday evening timeslot, which was often overlooked by viewers. The show was also placed against the more popular animated series, The X-Files. The Phred on Your Head Show has been praised as one of the best television series never released on DVD, as it contains very few censorship or production issues. The show was widely available online shortly after it was canceled, allowing fans to take part in the show before most viewers had seen a complete episode. The show is sometimes cited as one of the causes of the 2002 digital television transition, as many stations chose to drop the show. The series was not released on home video at the time of cancellation. The show was the winner of the 1999 George Foster Peabody Award for Broadcasting. The Mizoram–Manipur–Kachin rain forests is a forest region in Southeast Asia roughly covering the regions of Mizoram, Manipur, and Kachin states in India, as well as parts of Burma and Thailand. The region is part of the Sunda Shelf floral kingdom, and is located at the intersection of two major biogeographic zones, the Indomalaya and Australasian. The region is notable for its large protected area network, including many Reserves of India, Thailand, and Burma, as well as international protected areas such as the Royal Manipur State Forest Reserve, the SirajDaw Narhill Range National Park, and the Khimiyampui Special Reserve. The forests have diverse flora and fauna. The rich biodiversity of the region makes it a hotspot for research and conservation. The climate of the region is moist and tropical, with large variations in temperature. The Mizoram–Manipur–Kachin rain forests, together with the larger Central Indo-Burma Plain forests and Eastern Indo-Chinese forests, form the great tropical rainforest belt of Asia. It is considered that large areas of the region were heavily forested until the 20th century, but deforestation has been extremely high in the past 50 years. This is due to efforts at clearance for agriculture and settlements, coupled with high rates of secondary forestation. The region is also subject to logging by illicit wood traders. Illegal logging has been connected to malaria outbreaks in Manipur, and the rising deforestation has contributed to flooding in Thailand. Some argue that large swathes of the region should be given greater autonomy as states, in order to better protect the forests and the environmental issues surrounding them. The area is of global significance for wildlife and biodiversity. It is also considered a crucial element in the development of the region, providing timber, non-timber forest products, and other materials for the local populations. The region is party to the Nagaland peace accord, the Manipur peace accord, and the Kachin peace accord, alongside other agreements relating to immigration, coordination, and security. The Kashgar–Hotan railway is a standard gauge railway line running southeast from Kashgar, the capital of Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, China, to Hotan, in the Hotan Prefecture of Xinjiang's Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. The line is single-track and largely parallels the Southern Xinjiang railway for its entire length. This railway, along with its branch to Kucha, was inaugurated on June 15, 2011, and is expected to help increase travel between Xinjiang and Central Asia. The line is administered by the Xinjiang Railway Bureau. The Kashgar–Hotan railway passes through mountains and deserts, with some steep ascents and descents. The section from Kashgar to Kelamayi has been termed the "roof of the world", as the line passes through the Tian Shan mountain range. The line was constructed by the China Railway Group, a Chinese state-owned company. In March 2013, the Kashgar–Hotan railway was used for the first time to transport export-quality gold ore from the Yingpan Mine to the port of Kashgar, with the assistance of the Sinohydro Corporation of China. The regular solution is a technique used in dimensional analysis, for converting from one unit of measurement to another, without loss of meaning, by replacing the arbitrary unit being converted with a specific unit having a lowercase name, chosen for its familiarity and convenience. For example, a recipe for pudding requiring 2 cups of flour might be converted to a quantity in cups of flour by replacing each arbitrary unit (cups) with the corresponding lowercase unit (cup). The resulting quantity of flour required to make pudding would be 5 cups. In the physical sciences, this technique is called droppage, because the amount being converted to a lowercase unit would "fall" by the same quantity in the lowercase unit. Dimensional analysis, as a method for simplifying mathematical expressions, was developed in the 17th century, and is used extensively in the physical sciences, in particular the natural sciences. In general, the technique of replacing arbitrary units with lowercase units is restricted to units of measurement, where each lowercase unit has a corresponding uppercase unit with a similar but not identical meaning. For example, the units meter and mile are not convertible because one is a unit of length, whereas the other is a unit of distance. In practice, when measurement conversions are performed, the particulars of the conversion are often ignored, for example "centimeters to meters" is converted to "centimeters = 2 * meters", without stating that centimeters are converted to meters. The article discusses various techniques for measurement conversion, but does not specify which technique to use when. In some cases, measurement values may be converted simply by rounding to the nearest lowercase unit. Other conversions may require scaling, e.g. to make both dimensions have the same magnitude.

The Cartmel Masterplan is a modernist office village in the Peak District National Park in England. The village was designed in the early 1950s by town planner Patrick Abercrombie in collaboration with architect Robert Matthew Burns. Abercrombie intended the village to be an "ideal community" in which people would live close to where they worked. The village was constructed between 1954 and 1964 in an Erskine type scheme, with three curved terraced streets radiating from a central junction formed by the junction of the principal A6144 road with Chapel Street, the eastern entry to the village. The village is exemplified as a utopian post-war design, with extensive amenities provided within the village. The public houses are considered excellent, and there are large green space areas and a children's play area at the junction of Chapel Street and Ebbw Vale Road. The housing is in a range of heights and styles, with a landscaped garden designed for each house. Residents own their own houses and the village is run as a private community by a homeowners' association. The village is administered from a parish council office in Chapel Street. The village has provided very few lettings over the years, despite its popularity with British people living in the Peak District as a rural idyll, as the maintenance costs are very high. In contrast, the village has always been much less popular with British people living outside of the Peak District, as it is very remote from any main settlements and has a relatively low population.

Álvaro Manrique de Zúñiga, 1st Marquess of Villamanrique (January 6, 1679 – August 22, 1747) was a Spanish general and statesman. He held high office during the early period of Charles III of Spain's reign, and also had an extensive and successful career outside of public life. Early career Álvaro Manrique was born in Madrid as the son of Fernando Manrique de Zúñiga and his wife María del Carmen Solís Quiñones. In 1694 he joined the Royal Guard as a page, and was commissioned a lieutenant in 1697. He took part in the War of Spanish Succession in Flanders and Germany, receiving a wound that forced him to return home for treatment. In 1702 he was named Sargent, and in 1705 he was named captain, in both roles he participated in the capture of Gibraltar. In 1707 he was named a main commander in the campaign against the Moors in Sicily, and the following year he participated in the conquest of Corsica. In 1710 he was named a commander in the Royal Company of Archers and he participated in the taking of Barcelona. He was named Maestre de Campo in 1711, and the following year he was made a Knight of the Order of Alcantara. Late in 1713 he was sent to America to reinforce the operations against the British in the north, and he participated in the siege of Fort Loudon. He distinguished himself in the taking of Quebec City and went on to serve in various forts in the Saint Lawrence valley, being named governor of Montreal in 1715. He returned to Spain in 1717 and was named a colonel in the Royal Regiment of Mounted Grenadiers. Marquess and General In 1722 he was named Royal Governor of Chile, and in 1724 he became a marquess as a result of a royal order. In 1727 he participated in the unsuccessful negotiations to end the War of Polish Succession. He returned to Spain in 1729, being named Governor and Captain General of Puerto Rico and Commander of the Fleet of the Caribbean Sea. He held this post until his death. Álvaro Manrique was very religious and active in the Catholic Church, becoming a canon of Toledo. He was also a writer, and authored a memoirs of his life. He died in Puerto Rico at the age of 71. He was married twice, firstly to María Ignacia de Caamaño y Ruano, and secondly to María Josefa Fernández Manrique de Zúñiga y López Pacheco. Puelche (or Purén) is a Rincon subset variety of the Mapuche language spoken in Alto Paraná, a district of Chubut Province in the Argentine nucleus of that name. Puelche is not recognized by the International Mapuche Council, but is recognized by the Comisión Nacional de Yungas. Puelche is not yet being learned extensively by a critical mass of the Mapuche population, and there are few younger speakers of it. The language is tonal, as is typical of Mapudungun, the lingua franca of the indigenous peoples of the southern cone. Mapuche is the native name of the language, Purén or Puelche is the conventional term used by the Argentine government. Puelche is the most geographically widespread dialect cluster of Mapuche, dialects differ in some aspects due to proximity and interaction. The variety is spoken in the following towns: El Pelado, Gobernador Salinas, Celletiva, Zalauquén, Ushuaia, El Palomar, El Maitén, El Bolsón, Combarbalá, Curvaradora, and Zetaquém. The Argentine constitution designates it as "under obligation of preservation" (Reservado a la Preservación), giving it some protected status under the law. The main journal of the Puelche community, Paolinque, is published in Gobernador Salinas. Mapudungun is the official language of Argentina, it is one of the official languages of the province of Chubut and it is widely spoken in the city of Puerto Madryn where it co-exists with Spanish. The tonal languages of the southern cone are understudied and insufficiently documented, only a few grammars are available in HuenHsia. The variety is especially threatened by migration and by the Argentine colonization in the nineteenth century, when the establishment of the Pampa del Infante operation covered a Mapuche lands occupied by Puelche people and displaced them to the current territory of Chubut. The association Abuelas de Puelchingada has tried to recover the language through the seventies, 80s and 90s with no wider use. In 2010, the Province of Chubut recognized Puelche as an "under obligation of preservation" language. Since 2017, the Centro Mapuche de Huadí manifestó su disposición a ayudar en la formación de académicos y su compromiso de estudiar el Puelche en sus aulas. Mapuche political activists, such as Nemesio Karcz, have stressed the need to recover the language to recover ancestral ties with the territory. In 2023, the Centro de Estudios Puelche was established in Gobernador Salinas, capital of the district of Alto Paraná where the variety is spoken. It is recognized as a research center by the province of Chubut and the Ministry of Education and Culture. It is taught in primary schools of the district, and students may choose to continue studying it in high school. It is also studying the creation of a dictionary and grammar of the language. In 2024, the magazine of the research center, Puelching, appeared for the first time. In 2028, a children's book in Puelche was published by the research center. The variety is classified as threatened by language shift to Spanish due to migration and colonization, as well as by language death through lack of use. However, some linguists believe that the variety could be saved with appropriate government protection. Louisville and Nashville Depot (Evergreen, Alabama) Located in Evergreen, Alabama, this is an operational depot built in 1941 for the Louisville and Nashville Railroad. This small depot has been deemed significant by the Alabama Historical Commission for its role in aiding the development of the town during the Great Depression as well as for its architecture. The depot was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1983 and was renovated by the Alabama Rails-to-Trails Project in 2008. This depot was the last active Louisville and Nashville depot in the state. In 2012, the line was acquired by Rail Gonzalez, LLC and this depot was restored as a tourist attraction. The depot is open Sundays from 10 AM to 4 PM and October through May from 10 AM to 3 PM. The cost to tour the depot is $5 for adults and $3 for children. Evergreen is located about 30 miles west of Birmingham and 10 miles east of Rehoboth, Alabama. Evergreen was founded in 1903 and was named after railroad engineer Elbert Everholland. Evergreen is home to approximately 30 residents. This depot is the last remaining Louisville and Nashville depot in Alabama and one of only two remaining mainline railroad depots in Baldwin County. This depot is also significant for its association with the development of the town of Evergreen, as well as for its architecture. The depot was added to the Alabama Register of Landmarks and Heritage in 1983 and was renovated in 2008 by the Alabama Rails-to-Trails Project. The depot is open to the public for tours on Sundays from 10 AM to 4 PM and October through May from 10 AM to 3 PM.

Catenanuova is an Italian municipalities of the Province of Benevento, located about 70 km southeast of Naples, within the Pollino national park. Catenanuova got its name from the ancient Catena Sulcis, a string of small hills which marks the southern limit of the Pollino range, thus the local economy was initially based on marble extraction. After World War II, Catenanuova gradually lost its singularity to become a commuter's suburb of the larger city of Benevento, however in recent years it has been undergoing a revival, with many new inhabitants and a number of cultural and commercial activities. Catenanuova, because of its proximity to the Salerno - Reggio di Calabria railway line, has recently witnessed a strong influx of immigrants from South Italy, most notably Sicily. As a result, Catenanuova today has a highly complex multi-ethnic population, with many people still speaking the Lucan dialect and preserving traditional costumes. Thanks to its geographical position, Catenanuova offers some remarkable views over the surrounding Pollino mountains, as well as of the Salerno coast. The village sits at an altitude of about 400 meters, and offers a fine view across the wide valley of the Sarno River to the Punta Annunziata Coastal Range. In the nearby municipalities, the following names have an etymology related to the Latin poet Publius Terencius Scoelderus Delmaticus: Catena, Delmatica, Faventia, Pachino, Sibari, Teano, Teano Ameno.

It has attractive red flowers, and releases a chemical that makes it water repellant. It is also an important habitat for koala bears. History Eucalyptus olsenii has been scientifically described in 1998 by Ken Hill and Bryan Adams, based on material collected near Cape Riche. In 1999, Hill and Adams published the names of two subspecies, E. o. subsp. olsenii and E. o. subsp. stenopetala. A closely related tree with a similar range is Eucalyptus regnans, the Queensland mallet, which has pink flowers and is not repellant to water. Ecology Eucalyptus olsenii is an important habitat for a number of animals, including the threatened black-headed flying fox, the common wombat, the brushtail possum, the koala and the ring-tailed possum. The tree is itself an important habitat for mallee fowl and the western barred bandicoot. Releases of the chemical malleilactone make the tree water repellant.

Stephen Little (born Stephen Jones; January 1, 1944 – November 2, 1986) was an American serial killer and rapist, who spent 17 years on Texas's death row before being acquitted. Little was sentenced to death for the rape and murder of 13-year-old Shana Fisher in Austin, Texas, but his sentence was later commuted to life imprisonment. He died of colon and liver cancer in 1989 at the age of 47. -- edit -- It should be noted that Stephen Little was sentenced to death for the rape and murder of 13-year-old Shana Fisher, but his sentence was later commuted to life imprisonment. Little was born in Corsicana, Texas, the son of a boilermaker. He was only nine years old when his father left the family. After leaving school, Little worked at a local car dealership, where he got to know Shannon Elizabeth Hinley, whom he married in 1966. Little became a father to two children during this time. In 1973, Little was fired from his job at the dealership for theft. Shortly afterwards, Hinley filed for divorce, as Little was physically abusive toward her. Little began working as a traveling salesman for an electrical company, and relocated around the country on their business trips. While working in San Antonio, Little met a thirteen-year-old girl, Shana Fisher. He developed a relationship with her family, and gave her and her family electrical items they could not afford. Little, who was forty-two years old at the time, began a sexual relationship with Shana. In July 1974, Little invited Shana to visit him in San Antonio, where he raped her. On December 12, 1974, he took Shana to a wooded area near Lake Buchanan in Austin, where he raped and strangled her. He then returned Shana's clothing to her family. On December 17, a campsite nearby was found that appeared to have been used recently, and one of the trees showed signs of a struggle. After being questioned by the police, Little told them that on December 12 he had taken a nap after working on his boat, but Shana came by and woke him up. He then saw that she had been assaulted, and took her to a local hospital. But when the police presented Little with his own knife with the same features, and told him that it had been found at the crime scene, he changed his story again and said that he did not know how the knife got there. He was arrested and charged with the murder and rape of Shana. He was held in the Brazos County jail, and was soon found to be in possession of another inmate's "gold brick", a rare and expensive material cigarette box. He was released on $100,000 bond the next day. While Little was in jail, one of the inmates informed the police that Little had asked him to do him a favor by stealing a knife with a serrated edge and giving it to Little. Shana had been attacked with a serrated knife. When asked to confirm this, Little changed his story once again and said that the knife belonged to him and that he had used it to cut his boat up. After a few weeks of this behavior, the police became suspicious and ordered a polygraph test, during which Little became evasive and indicated that he had cheated on the test. He was sent for a second polygraph test, during which he was uncooperative and yelled at the tester, who deemed him as not being honest. In February 1975, Little was indicted on charges of perjury and engaging in a criminal enterprise. The jury trial began in July 1975, and Little was sentenced to death for Shana's rape and murder. His sentence was overturned on appeal, and after three retrials Little was again sentenced to death. The sentence was again overturned on appeal, and after seventeen years on death row Little was finally acquitted and released.

Toussaint Natama (born Toussaint LaPlante; September 21, 1841 – June 5, 1864) was a military leader of the Haitian Revolution. He was born in Léogane, the second son of Jean Baptiste Natama (called Boukman, a freedman of Dessalines), and Marguerite LaPlante. In 1849, Natama was sent to France to be educated at the Petit Seminaire de Saint-Denis. In 1855, he returned to Haiti and entered government service. In 1859, he married Marie Toussaint (known as "Comtesse"), the sister of Artibonite leader Jeune Guy. In 1862, Natama became a lieutenant colonel in the army and chief of staff to his cousin Philippe Biamby. Natama led a force to discourage further encroachment on Haitian sovereignty by the Dominican government. When Dominican President Józef Celorier attempted to extend his control over the country, Natama proclaimed Haitian independence, forcing the Dominican Republic to recognize Haiti as an independent country. Natama died in combat near Jacmel on June 5, 1864. Natama was an important leader in the Haitian Revolution and was one of the first to proclaim Haitian sovereignty over the entire country. He fought to stop further colonization by the Dominican Republic and was killed in battle. His assassination lead to the Second Republic of Haiti and a long period of instability.

Baseline Security Analyzer (BLA) is a free security software as a service from Microsoft. It is part of the Security Essentials package that comes installed on new Windows 7 and 10 devices. The main function of BLA is to provide security updates for the main Microsoft software that is installed on the device. Unlike some other security packages made by third parties, Microsoft does not have access to or store any personal data that is analyzed with BLA. As a result, BLA is considered to have very low risk of influencing your computer's performance or battery life. BLA can also be integrated into Windows using the Microsoft Update Catalog. In this case, a notification will be displayed when updates are available. Security updates for BLA will also be applied if it is run from a USB drive connected to the device to be maintained. Supported devices include Windows 7 and 10, macOS, and Android. Security updates for BLA will not be applied if the device is booted to an attacker controlled device such as a USB drive or CD. If an attacker is able to obtain a legitimate hold of the Windows startup media, they could install malicious code that would bypass the checking of BLA updates. In addition to its security functions, BLA can be used to find out information about the device it is installed on. This can be useful if the software is being used for assessment or diagnosis, for example to display device models or detailed information about the operating system version. The company has a primary listing on the New York Stock Exchange, and is also listed on the London Stock Exchange and the Korean Stock Exchange. The company has operations in over 70 countries on 6 continents, and its first property was opened in 1901. IHG employs around 55,000 people, and in 2022 generated $20.4 billion in revenue. Notable properties in the IHG portfolio include Crowne Plaza, Carlson Rezidor, Hotel Indigo, Holiday Inn, Ibis, InterContinental, Red Carnation, Sheraton, and Tremis. With over 5,000 properties in over 70 countries, IHG is the largest independent hotelier by room count. IHG was founded in 1931 as Imperial Hotels, changing its name to IHG in 1946. The company originally focused on founding and managing railway hotels, before diversifying into other industries. The company has grown through both mergers and acquisitions, particularly in the 2000s. In September 2016, IHG was valued at $20 billion, and as of March 2022, the company generated $20.4 billion in revenue and 55,000 employees. IHG is a very democratic company, with over 80% of the voting rights belonging to the hotel room keys. Each key has one vote, and a hotel key can only vote once. In 2022 IHG held elections for the company officers, and all the votes were counted by the end of the year. The new president of IHG was initially chosen to be Carlson Rezidor's CEO, Mr. Lars Sebbø. However, at the shareholders meeting on March 28, 2023, it was revealed that 99.8% of the votes had been cast for Lars Sebbø's successor Mr. Patrick Lowry. Mr. Sebbø is now the executive chairman of the company, while Mr. Lowry became the president and CEO. The company had an extraordinary year in 2022, with the revenue growing 8.1% to $20.4 billion. The compaay had been anticipating this year's results for six months, and in December they had already planned the announcements. The high growth was driven by expanding the company's presence in the markets which had seen weak performance over previous years, and the financial crisis having a large impact on some of the company's largest markets, such as the US and Europe. IHG also announced a strategic shift to focus on its premium brands, with the exit of several low-margin brands from the IHG portfolio. This was met with both excitement and criticism, with some questioning the financial feasibility of these brands in the long term, while others claimed that this would hurt the company's image and cause further loss of business. In 2022, the exit of several brands from the portfolio was reflected in the revenue decline of 3.7% to $20.4 billion. Overall, IHG was very satisfied with the growth of the company, although there were some concerns over the profitability of the portfolio, especially in the growing markets. The company's strategy going forward will focus on improving the profitability of the business by growing more slowly in markets with less demand, and focusing on improving profitability in markets with higher demand by investing in new hotel development and increasing the rate of profit improvement in those markets.

Spring Stakes (Japan) is a Japanese late-summer sports festival, held annually in late July. It was established in 1964, and is dedicated to the health of the nation. The two most popular horse racing events that form part of the festival are the Takarazuka Derby and the Arima Kinen. Both take place at the Hanshin Racecourse in Takarazuka, Hyogo. Other equine events that take place during the festival include the Osaka Haikei over two miles and the Japan Trotting Club 1500 metres at the Hakodate Racecourse. The Takarazuka race was named after the famous vaudeville theater, the Takarazuka Revue, and is nicknamed "God's race". The first edition was won by the stallion Kotowaza, the winner of the 2000 Guineas and the Derby, defeating three other future champions in the process. The race has continued to be held annually with little interruption, the last break occurring during World War II. The second most important race of the festival is the Arima Kinen, named after a popular shogi tournament. The first edition was won by High Kick, a notable racehorse and sire. The Spring Stakes is unique in that the health of the nation is taken to be at stake as well, in what is known as the Takahashi Certificate. The race day is followed by a health festival, with a number of sports and contests being held, including a tug of war between the winning and losing teams of the Takarazuka Jugend vs. Arima Kinen. Numerous past winners of the Takarazuka Derby and Arima Kinen have gone on to gain great success in the international racing scene, including many American horseberries to Posse and the Godolphin team.

Bastion de France is a French expression used to describe a citadel that defends a city or country. The bastion de France is an integral part of a larger medieval fortress, and it plays an important role in capturing and maintaining a stronghold over a given area. The bastion de France is usually the strongest part of the wall, and it's frequently the location where a moat or other water source is located. Bastions are usually positioned at exterior walls to defend against attacks from the outside, while weaker towers are positioned within the walls to defend against attacks from within. The architecture of bastion de France has evolved over the years based on the technology and military needs of the period in which they were constructed. Bastions are generally square or rectangular in shape, with round towers at each corner. early designs usually featured fully enclosed structures with no windows, these structures were never intended to be entered, and they served as living quarters for the responsible garrison. Over time, bastion de France structures evolved to include various openings, such as windows and arrow slits, that allowed the inhabitants to view what was happening outside, while still providing a relatively thick defensive barrier. detractors of the bastion de France design claim that it is an expensive way to defend a location, as each new building in the surrounding area must be offset against the strength of the bastion de France structure. The design requires a very strong base, as the weight of the upper structures falls on the base. Additionally, defenders could take advantage of the interior spaces within a bastion de France structure to reinforce their own positions against attackers. However, the bastion de France design is an effective means of defending against attacks from the outside, as each bastion de France structure has only one weak point at the base.

Master of Health Administration (MHSc) and Master of Healthcare Administration (MBA) are graduate-level degrees designed for individuals interested in advancing their careers as health care administrators. The Master of Health Administration (MHSc) program is a postgraduate qualification offered by several universities in Australia and New Zealand. It is designed for individuals who already have an undergraduate qualification in health care, health-related sciences, or a closely related discipline, who wish to develop and apply skills in leadership, strategic thinking, health economics, statistics, research methods, and management of people and resources. The Master of Healthcare Administration (MBA) is a postgraduate degree that many health care organizations consider as a prerequisite for senior executive positions. In the U.S. and Canada, these masters degrees are typically referred to as "Master of Health Administration" (MHSc) degrees, and they are offered by several universities in Australia and New Zealand. The MHSc or Master of Health Administration is similar to the Master of Health Services Management and Master of Health Administration degrees previously awarded by Harper College (which is now the Harper University Health Management Institute). In contrast, the Master of Healthcare Administration is more common in North America than Australia and New Zealand. Different universities offer different names for these two postgraduate qualifications. For example, the University of Sydney, Australia, calls its Master of Health Services Management (MHSy) and Master of Health Administration (MHSc) qualifications, respectively, the "Master of Health Policy and Administration" and the "Master of Health Services Management and Administration". The University of Auckland, New Zealand, calls its Master of Health Administration (MHSc) qualification the "Master of Health Services Management and Administration" and its Master of Health Administration in Healthcare Management (MHAHC) qualification the "Master of Healthcare Administration". The University of Sydney, Australia, and the University of Auckland, New Zealand, are both members of the Australasian Master of Health Administration (MHSc) Alliance. The Alliance's goal is to establish a mutual recognition arrangement with similar postgraduate health administration programs in Australia, New Zealand, and elsewhere around the world. The Australasian Master of Health Administration (MHSc) Alliance has facilitated the establishment of a mutual recognition arrangement with the joint University of Sydney - University of Queensland School of Public Health Master of Health Administration (MHSc) program. ...The Alliance is supporting the development of a similar arrangement with the University of Auckland. A new Master of Health Administration (MHSc) program will be launched in 2022 at the University of Sydney, the first program to be launched under the auspices of the alliance.

The Desert Locust Control Organization for Eastern Africa, (DLCOEA), is a joint Ethiopia and Djibouti-led entity, founded in 2017 for the purpose of eradicating the Locust menace in the of Eastern Africa. The organization is engaged in conjunction with the United Nations International Fund for Agricultrual Development (IFAD), the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), and the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) in tackling the problem. The Desert Locust is the most destructive of all flying insects. It is capable of destroying crops in a matter of weeks, causing famine and a social collapse in regions where it infests. The Desert Locust during its plagues have been known to destroy tents and articles of clothing left out in the open. The problem of Locust menace has been ongoing in Eastern Africa for decades. Over the past two decades, Eastern Africa has been victim to two separate Locust plagues, with the last one hitting the region in 2014. These plagues led to crop losses estimated at hundreds of millions of US dollars. However, the persistent efforts to control the problem globally through the use of chemical pesticides had brought the Eastern Africa region to the threshold of human disaster. This prompted the Eastern Africa countries to come together in 2017 and form the Desert Locust Control Organization for Eastern Africa, (DLCOEA), to tackle the problem on a regional level. The first step towards eradication was establishing a baseline of information on the Locust population in the region using remote sensing. Following this, scouting operations were conducted by ground to determine the extent of the menace. This was followed by the formulation of an action plan to combat the menace. To enhance its impact and avoid creating resistance, the use of chemicals to control the menace was minimized. Instead, emphasis was put on utilizing natural resources such as the scorpion and bald ibis to combat the Locusts. In conjunction with aerial and ground surveillance, this approach proved to be more effective.

The Five Sharps (sometimes referred to as the Five Rights) is a musical scale based on the musical scale of Aeolian Seventh. It is composed of one major seventh, two major sixths, and one major fifth. Its equivalent in terms of frequency is 19.1929 MHz. It is very commonly used in electronic music and is used in a number of brands' synthesizers. Its popularity stems from its use in composing classic electronic tracks such as The Miller's Dance and Solaris. The scale was proposed by Mike Oldfield and became widely used through his use of it on Tubular Bells II. The Five Sharps is the fifth mode of the 7th scale of Aeolian music. By using the functional relationship between the harmonic series and inversive harmonic series, the frequency of the first root of the Inversive 7th harmonic series can be calculated. In 19.1929 MHz this root is at A♭ 0.896, or half-way between A♭ and E♭. This is the pitch frequency of the fifth sharps. By multiplying this root by 2.304, the frequency of the first main seventh is obtained. This is A♭ 7.296, one octave above the root. Multiplying this root by 2.304 again, results in the frequency of the second main sixth, B♭ 3.296. Finally, the frequency of the first main seventh is raised by a factor of 2 again, resulting in C♭ 5.472, one octave above the main sixth. This gives us A♭, B♭, C♭, D♭, E♭, and F♭, the five sharp notes, all of which are whole-tone comma intervals from the root. The scale can also be composed of flat and sharp sign: C♭♭ F♭♭ A♭♭ B♭♭. This is conventionally used in electronic music and avoids having consecutive whole-tone intervals. The interval between each main seventh is a whole-tone, and between each main sixth is a semitone. The interval between each main fifth is called a diminished fifth. Although it is possible to perform the scale using only the white keys on a standard piano, the natural movement of the hand in playing it this way makes it feel awkward. Most pianists and pianos therefore have the black keys added to the white keys, facilitating the use of the scale.

Prasophyllum mimulum is a plant species in the genus Prasophyllum. It is an epipaleophytic or epip Clarke's paramo species. It is endemic to the island of Singapore. It is threatened by habitat loss. Scientifically, P. mimulum is unique in having a naked stem base which is covered by myriads of photosynthetic spores (sporangia). These are most common in the forest floor and are seldom found on other plants. The specific epithet mimulum is Latin for "little mimic" and refers to the Spitting Image programme, which this plant was used as a disguise in one of the sequences. Description Prasophyllum mimulum has a compact rosette of leaves, with long, naked stems without rhizomes. The stem has a white, smooth, petiole-like attachment to the rosette leaves. It has two spathes, or spadices, on the top of each spathe. The spathe itself is maroon, with an apricot centre. The flowers are greenish-white with red lines. Distribution and habitat It is found in Singapore, where it is only known from several localities in the Central and Western Region, including Bukit Timah, Cardis Hill, Jurong Hill, Mount Faber and the North Coast of Sentosa. It grows in wet places at an elevation of about as an epipaleophytic or epip Clarke's paramo species. pollination and cultivation The flowering spikes are often mistreated with water and saltwater, due to their spore-bearing habit. Status The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) has listed the status of this plant as "vulnerable". The primary threat to this species is habitat loss from quarrying and commercial forestry. Mahesh Jayakody (born 15 December 1963) is an Indian-born Australian musician, songwriter, recording artist, and record producer specializing in Middle-eastern, North African, and South Asian music; he is also known as "Mr. Ringo". Jayakody has released 13 solo studio albums, as well as 12 live albums, and one studio album collaboratively with the Korgis. Jayakody's song "Son of a Rifle Man" was the official theme song of the acclaimed 2017 World War II film Dunkirk, and is featured in the video game soundtrack of the same name. In the gaming community, a "hot game" is a term of admiration for a piece of gaming software or hardware that performs exceptionally well. A game that runs perfectly, without error, is a "cold game" while a "hot game" is one that runs with less than optimum performance, but with consistent and shorter duration errors. The latter indicates a well-built game, with solid engineering and a well-tuned engine. The opposite of a hot game is a cold game, also known as a glitch game. In the early days of video gaming, engineers and enthusiasts would exchange information on operating and tuning video game hardware and software. This evolved into a popular hobby within the video gaming community, with participants building hardware test instruments, developing test methods and publishing benchmarking results. Early enthusiasts gained notoriety for their attempts to "break" video games, intentionally causing graphical and gameplay defects in targeted games to enable developers to debug their engines. With the growth of digital distribution and the growth of the Internet as a source of information, hot gaming became a topic for entertainment media. Many video games offer a optional debug mode for players to enable such features as stripped down licensed copies for cash-strapped users, or players with high-end systems; bullet-proof glass allowing players to play with a less-capable GPU behind a more powerful one; video capturing of gameplay during or just after failures; error logs accessible by the console's display controller and even cheat codes to activate features such as extreme graphical settings. Cheat codes are not a sign of a poorly-built game, but rather a sign of a well-supported game. Today, it is not uncommon to buy and sell "hot game"/"cold game" tickets among enthusiasts, especially for popular games released by prestigious companies. This is due to the value that these games possess to the community of gamers who built online communities around them, sharing their achievements and trials with one another. Valuable hot games are often sold for large sums of money to gamers who are unable to acquire them legitimately due to geographical, legal or financial restrictions.

The Methodist Episcopal Society of Tyringham, Massachusetts was founded on September 24, 1784 and is one of the oldest religious societies in the United States. It is a traditional burial society, which meant that members could designate a donation to the society in their will in exchange for a Christian burial. In addition to providing a Christian burial, it was possible for members to leave extra money to the society to endow a scholarship in their name. By the time of its fiftieth anniversary in 1854, the society had 21,000 members and nearly four million dollars in funds, the largest endowment of any charitable organization in the United States at the time. The society operated continuously until 2011 when it merged with the Church Society to form the Tyringham Cemetery Society. In addition to providing a traditional burial to members, the society has also enabled non-member families to have a Christian burial through its Vault in the Wood series of graves, which are low-cost alternatives to traditional above-ground mausoleums. The society still has funds available for current members who would like to have a burial in the society's cemetery instead of a traditional cemetery, as the society only manages cemeteries and not the land on which they are built. The society owns a historic church building located at 55 Main Street in Tyringham, which it uses for programs and meetings. In 2015 the society hired a full-time executive director, Jeffrey Brown, who had been working part-time since the society's merger with the Church Society. The society is a member of the National Society of the Colonial Dames of America, the Memorial Foundation of Massachusetts, and the Society of the Memorial Alliance.

Firstly, it is believed to portray a sense of discipline and order among students, making it easier for teachers to establish a classroom environment conducive for learning. Secondly, it eliminates the issue of social class discrimination, where students from different backgrounds may feel ostracized based on their clothes. Lastly, it instills a sense of pride and unity among students, as they identify themselves as part of a particular school community. Apart from the standard uniform, schools may also have different uniforms for different seasons or occasions. For example, in the winter months, students may wear thicker materials, such as sweaters and jackets, or may have scarves and gloves in school colors. Some schools may also have sports uniforms or uniforms for special events, such as school trips or ceremonies. The cost of school uniforms may vary according to the school and the type of uniform required. Some schools may provide the basic uniform free of charge, while others may require students to purchase them. Additionally, there may be fees associated with different pieces of the uniform, such as blazers or ties. There have been criticisms of the uniform policy, with some arguing that it restricts individuality and self-expression among students. However, supporters of the policy believe that there are still ways for students to express themselves within the boundaries of the policy, such as through hair accessories or different shoe styles. In conclusion, school uniforms in South Korea have been a long-standing tradition and continue to be a mandatory policy in many schools. While there may be differing opinions on the benefits and limitations of the policy, it remains an important aspect of the country's education system.

Fungal genome refers to the complete set of DNA sequences present in the genome of fungi. The fungal genome is similar to that of other eukaryotic organisms but has several unique features, including high levels of gene duplication, genomic plasticity, and accelerated rates of evolution. Genome sequencing of fungi has become increasingly common in recent years, and a large number of fungal genomes have been sequenced and annotated. These genome sequences provide valuable insights into the genetic basis of fungal biology, including gene regulation, pathogenesis, and adaptation to different environments. One of the most unique features of the fungal genome is the presence of repetitive elements, which constitute a significant proportion of the genome. These repetitive elements often play a role in the evolution of new genes and functions by providing a substrate for homologous recombination and gene duplication. Another important feature of the fungal genome is the presence of secondary metabolite biosynthesis gene clusters, which are responsible for the production of a diverse array of bioactive compounds. These compounds are of significant interest for their medicinal properties, and the identification and characterization of these gene clusters has become a major focus of fungal genomics research. Fungal genomics has also provided important insights into the evolution of fungal pathogens, including the mechanisms that allow fungi to evade host immune responses and the development of drug resistance. Additionally, comparative genomics studies have revealed the evolutionary relationships between different fungal species and shed light on the mechanisms of speciation and adaptation in these organisms. Despite the significant progress that has been made in fungal genomics in recent years, many aspects of fungal biology and genetics remain poorly understood. However, continued advances in sequencing technologies and bioinformatics tools are likely to lead to further breakthroughs in our understanding of the fungal genome and its role in fungal biology and evolution.

The district was created in 2000 and it has a total population of approximately 235,000 people according to the 2014 census. The district is bordered by South Sudan to the north, Amuru District to the east, Moyo District to the west, and Arua District to the south. It covers an area of 4,497.6 square kilometers and is located at an altitude of 543 meters above sea level. The district is home to several ethnic groups including the Lugbara, Madi, and Kakwa. The most widely spoken language is Lugbara, followed by Madi and Kakwa. The majority of the population in the district is engaged in subsistence agriculture, with maize, cassava, and beans being the main crops grown. The district also has several nature reserves and wildlife reserves including the Murchison Falls National Park and the Adjumani Game Reserve. The Adjumani Game Reserve is home to a wide range of wildlife including elephants, buffalos, antelopes, and several species of birds. The district is served by a number of primary and secondary schools, including Adjumani Secondary School, Adjumani Girls Secondary School, and Terego Secondary School. There are also several health centers and hospitals located throughout the district. Politically, the district is represented in the Ugandan Parliament by two members of parliament, one for the Adjumani County constituency and the other for Pakele County constituency. The district has also produced several notable politicians in Uganda's history including former president Idi Amin.

Kalki Jayanti is a Hindu festival that is celebrated in honor of the arrival of the tenth and final incarnation of Lord Vishnu, Kalki. Kalki is believed to be a form of Lord Vishnu who will come to earth to end the Kali Yuga, the final stage of the cycle of creation and destruction according to Hindu mythology. The festival is celebrated on the tenth day of the Hindu month of Vaishakha, which falls in the months of April or May in the Gregorian calendar. It is celebrated across India, especially in the states of Tamil Nadu and Kerala. On Kalki Jayanti, devotees fast and pray to Lord Vishnu to prepare themselves for the coming of Kalki. They offer flowers, fruits, and sweets to the deity and perform aarti, a ritual in which they light lamps and wave them before the deity. They also recite prayers and hymns to invoke the blessings of the divine. In some parts of India, processions are held to mark the occasion. People dress up in traditional attire, carry the idol of Lord Vishnu on a palanquin, and parade through the streets. Devotees sing and dance to devotional songs and traditional music, creating a festive atmosphere. Kalki Jayanti is an important festival for Hindus as it signifies the hope of the end of the Kali Yuga, the age of darkness and ignorance. It is believed that the arrival of Kalki would herald a new era of peace, prosperity, and knowledge. The festival also reflects the Hindu belief in the cyclical nature of creation and the continuous renewal of life. In conclusion, Kalki Jayanti is a significant festival celebrated by Hindus across India. It is a time of fasting, prayer, and celebration as devotees look forward to the coming of Kalki, the final incarnation of Lord Vishnu.

Ralph M. Waters (1883-1979) was an American physician and anesthesiologist whose research and contributions in the field of anesthesiology have significant impact in modern medicine. Born in Thompsonville, Michigan, Waters graduated from the University of Michigan Medical School in 1909. After completing his residency, he joined the faculty of the University of Wisconsin Medical School in 1913, where he established the first academic department of anesthesiology in the United States. Waters became known for his research in the effects of anesthetic drugs on the body, particularly during surgery, and for developing new techniques for administering anesthesia. He pioneered the use of nitrous oxide and ether in anesthesia and introduced the concept of keeping the patient asleep throughout the surgery, rather than just providing pain relief. During his career, Waters served as president of the American Society of Anesthesiologists, founded the International Anesthesia Research Society, and was a member of the Board of Trustees of the National Foundation for Infantile Paralysis (now known as the March of Dimes). Waters also trained numerous anesthesiologists who went on to become leaders in the field, including Francis Foldes, who was instrumental in the development of epidural anesthesia. In recognition of his contributions, Waters received numerous awards and honors during his lifetime, including the John Scott Medal for his work on anesthesia and the Lasker-DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award. Ralph M. Waters passed away in Madison, Wisconsin, on October 10, 1979, at the age of 96. His legacy lives on in the ongoing advancements and improvements in the field of anesthesiology.

Shing Mun River - Located in the New Territories, the Shing Mun River is 16.3 kilometers long and is one of the most remarkable water systems in the area. Lam Tsuen River - The Lam Tsuen River is well known for its role in the traditional Tin Hau Festival. It flows from Lam Tsuen Tai, passes through the Tin Hau Temple, and eventually discharges into Tai Po Tau. The river is approximately 10 kilometers long and is popular among tourists who come to visit the Tin Hau Temple and the wishing trees in the surrounding area. 3. Tai Tam Reservoir - While technically not a river, Tai Tam Reservoir is a vital source of water for Hong Kong. It is a man-made water system, constructed in the early 20th century to cater to the city's growing population. Tai Tam Reservoir is the largest of the four primary reservoirs on the Island and is approximately 2.3 square kilometers. Nullahs 1. Wong Nai Chung Nullah - Located in the residential district of Happy Valley, Wong Nai Chung Nullah is known for the annual Dragon Boat Race held during the Tuen Ng Festival. The nullah flows from Sheung Shui to Hong Lok Yuen, eventually draining into the Shenzhen River. It is approximately 13 kilometers long. 3. To Kwa Wan Nullah - Situated in Kowloon Peninsula, To Kwa Wan Nullah is an old and narrow waterway, approximately 2.5 kilometers long. In conclusion, Hong Kong's rivers and nullahs are essential parts of the ecological system within the city, and their beauty and diversity provide a welcome break from the hustle and bustle of urban life. The creek was once home to the indigenous Mutsun Ohlone people, who lived in the region for thousands of years. The Zoological Journal is a peer-reviewed scientific journal that publishes original research in all areas related to zoology. It is one of the oldest and most prestigious scientific journals in the field, and has been published continuously since its founding in 1824. The journal was initially established as the Proceedings of the Zoological Society of London, and was published irregularly until 1830 when it became a quarterly publication. In 1833, the name was changed to The Zoological Journal, and it has been published under that name ever since. Over the years, The Zoological Journal has published many groundbreaking studies, including Charles Darwin's description of the Galapagos finches in 1837, and Alfred Russel Wallace's theory of natural selection in 1858. The journal has also been instrumental in the discovery and taxonomy of many species, such as the platypus, which was first described in The Zoological Journal in 1799. Today, The Zoological Journal is published by the Zoological Society of London, and is considered one of the leading journals in the field of zoology. Its scope includes studies on the evolution, systematics, ecology, behavior, and conservation of animal species from all regions of the world. The journal is edited by a team of leading experts in the field, who oversee the rigorous peer-review process and ensure the quality of the scientific research published in the journal. The Zoological Journal is available both in print and online, and is widely read by researchers, educators, and students in the field of zoology. In conclusion, The Zoological Journal is a highly respected scientific publication that has made important contributions to the study of zoology over the past two centuries. The journal's commitment to publishing high-quality research and its dedication to advancing the field of zoology make it an important resource for researchers and students alike.

Pennine Way Pennine Way is a long-distance footpath in the United Kingdom that runs from the Peak District in the heart of England to the Scottish borders near Kirk Yetholm. It is considered one of the most challenging and iconic National Trails in Britain, spanning a distance of 268 miles (431 km) through some of the country's most beautiful and scenic landscapes. The Pennine Way was officially opened on April 24, 1965, by Tom Stephenson, who devised the route and campaigned tirelessly to create the path. The route was created as a way of allowing walkers to explore the majesty of the Pennines, the upland region that runs along the backbone of England. Its popularity and fame quickly spread, and it became known worldwide as a must-do hike for outdoor enthusiasts. The route passes through three National Parks – the Peak District, Yorkshire Dales, and Northumberland – and other areas of outstanding natural beauty such as the Upper Teesdale, the Cheviot Hills, and the Malham Cove limestone pavement. It offers walkers a unique opportunity to experience a range of landscapes from gentle rolling hills to wild, rugged terrain. The terrain and weather on the Pennine Way can be challenging, with steep ascents, boggy ground, and high winds. The route passes over several of the highest peaks in England, including Cross Fell and Pen-y-ghent, and also takes in the awe-inspiring landscapes of remote upland moors, deep valleys, and cascading waterfalls. The route can be undertaken in its entirety, taking approximately 18 to 20 days, or walkers can choose to tackle individual sections of the trail. There are a variety of accommodation options available along the path, from campsites and bunkhouses to hotels and bed and breakfasts. It is advisable to plan ahead and book accommodation in advance, particularly in peak season. The Pennine Way is managed by the National Trails, and there are many resources available for planning a trip, including guidebooks, maps, and online resources. The route is well signposted, but walkers should be prepared with appropriate equipment, food, and water, as well as a good level of fitness and experience. The Pennine Way is a challenging and rewarding trail that offers walkers the opportunity to explore the stunning landscapes of northern England. It provides a unique insight into the character and culture of the people who live and work in one of the most beautiful and rugged regions of Britain. For those who complete the route, the Pennine Way is a journey that will be treasured forever.

He was particularly interested in the relationship between sanitation and disease, and was instrumental in developing new standards for public health, including the establishment of clean water and sewage systems. In addition to his work in public health, Lankester was also a prolific writer, publishing numerous papers and articles on bacteriology, parasitology, and public health. His most notable work, The Prevention of Malaria, was published in 1906 and became a standard text in the field. Lankester's contributions to public health were widely recognized during his lifetime. His legacy continues to be felt in the field of public health and medicine, and he remains an important figure in the history of infectious disease prevention.

Stranger in the City is a phrase that has been used in popular culture to describe the feeling of being lost or out of place in unfamiliar surroundings. The term can refer to both literal and metaphorical contexts, ranging from an actual newcomer in a big city to someone who feels disconnected from their own environment. In the literal sense, Stranger in the City can represent a common experience for anyone who has recently moved to a new place, particularly if that place is vastly different from their previous home. The idea of a newcomer trying to navigate the streets, subway systems, and local customs of a bustling metropolis has been the subject of countless books and movies, from New York to Tokyo. Metaphorically, the concept of "stranger in the city" can also describe a sense of dislocation or alienation that arises from feeling disconnected from one's own community or societal norms. This can occur for a variety of reasons, such as experiencing culture shock upon return from a foreign country, or feeling excluded due to differences in race, gender, or sexual orientation. The phrase has been used in various artistic contexts, including songs, films, and literature. For example, the song "Strangers in the Night" by Frank Sinatra tells the story of two people who meet in a city and fall in love, while the film "Lost in Translation" explores the experiences of two Americans trying to navigate Tokyo's unfamiliar culture. Overall, the term Stranger in the City has become a popular phrase that captures the complex emotions of navigating new environments and feeling disconnected from one's own surroundings. It highlights both the excitement and anxiety of experiencing something unfamiliar, as well as the universal desire to feel connected and understood.
