text-davinci-003: Lydie Auvray (born 19 October 1956) is a French jazz guitarist, composer, and vocalist. She first developed her career during the 1980s, when she was an early proponent of jazz fusion in France along with her then husband Jannick Top. Their group, Yaouank, was a pioneer of the French jazz fusion movement before the genre caught on elsewhere in Europe. Auvray's solo career started in the 1990s. She has released seven jazz albums, beginning with her fourteenth release, La Tresse Rouge, in 1997. Since then, she has recorded with artists from around the world, featuring musicians from India, Madagascar, and Africa. She has collaborated with some of the most admired musicians of recent years, including bassist Jannick Top, pianist Yaron Herman, and drummer Pierre-François Dufour. She won the French Jazz Album of the Year award twice, in 2000 for Les Nuthermes, and in 2010 for Jams Breton. Auvray's music is characterized by its broad range of influences, including folk, blues, and Eastern music. In her lyrics, she often draws from personal experience, exploring themes of mourning, sorrow, and loss. In a performance at the Paris Philharmonic, she creates a combination of traditional Breton melodies, jazz improvisation, and orchestral scoring. Her musical style draws heavily from traditional jazz and folk forms, with a modern sound inspired by jazz-fusion. Her most recent album, Les Belles Chansons, was released in 2018. The album was met with critical acclaim, earning praise for its fusion of jazz and folk music. Auvray has toured extensively throughout Europe and Africa and has seen her music featured in film soundtracks, theater plays, and television shows. She has composed and performed artistic pieces for the French cruise ship "L'Ocean" and the 2014 edition of the World Martial Arts Games. Though she remains popular in France, she has seen her profile rise in the United States in recent years. In 2019, she released her debut album in the United States, Queriously, featuring her newest compositions. The album earned widespread critical acclaim, and garnered Auvray two great reviews in the New York Times. Throughout her career, Auvray's work has been characterized by its range of influences from diverse musical traditions. Her music demonstrates her commitment to musical experimentation and a passion for creativity and collaboration. Auvray regularly appears at jazz festivals, tours, and artists residencies around the world and remains a highly sought-after musician in both her native France and the US.

Daniel Di Tomasso (born 16th of December 1989) is a Canadian actor who is best known for his television roles as Max Miller in Witches of East End and as Mark Gray in Reckless. Di Tomasso was born and raised in Toronto, Ontario. He grew up with his brother, Robert, and along with his sister, Kendall. He attended the Etobicoke Rapid Arts Program at the Etobicoke School of the Arts and is an accomplished drummer, saxophonist and guitarist. Di Tomasso originally pursued a career in music, but found his passion in acting later on. Before making his breakthrough in television, Di Tomasso starred in various television movies such as Land of the Lost, Blood Pressure and XIII: The Conspiracy. He also starred in the 2009 horror movie The Shrine, as well as short films such as Anyone Can Play Guitar and Post-Partum. Di Tomasso's best known television roles were Max Miller in Witches of East End and Mark Gray in Reckless. He starred in the former from 2013 to 2014, and in the latter he played a recurring character. In 2015, Daniel landed a role in the canadian-american horror film Left in Darkness, which was followed by roles in the television movies The Wrong House, Have Faith and Royal Matchmaker. In 2018, Daniel Di Tomasso was nominated for Best Supporting Actor in a Television Movie at the 9th Canadian Screen Awards for his role as Chris in Have Faith. Di Tomasso is currently filming for a number of new projects, including the crime drama Show Me A Hero and the supernatural drama series Shadow. This year, he will be seen as a recurring character in the television series Siren. When not filming, Daniel enjoys playing music and visiting his family in Toronto. He currently lives in Los Angeles, CA.

Nine Stories Productions is a film and television production company based in Los Angeles, California. Founded in 2013 by Academy Award-nominated film producer Marc Platt and television producers Adam Siegel and Adam Shulman, the company is known for producing award-winning films, television series, and live theater events. The company produces content across a variety of genres, with particular focus on contemporary storytelling. Its works have been recognized with numerous accolades, including Academy Award nominations, Golden Globe and Emmy Award wins, and BAFTA nominations. Their first foray into feature film production was the 2019 drama Beautiful Boy, starring Timothée Chalamet and Steve Carell. The film tells the story of a father trying to cope with his son's addiction and earned two Academy Award nominations for Chalamet and Carell, as well as a Critics' Choice Award for Best Actor in a Drama for Chalamet. In 2020, Nine Stories produced The Trial of the Chicago 7, written and directed by Aaron Sorkin. The film follows the trial of seven activists charged with inciting a riot at the 1968 Democratic National Convention in Chicago and earned six Academy Award nominations. Nine Stories is currently in production on the untitled David O. Russell project starring Christian Bale, Margot Robbie, and Michael B. Jordan. The film is the company's second collaboration with the director, following their 2020 limited series adaptation of the novel, The Worst Year of My Life Again. Nine Stories also produces theater events to support the release of their work. Notable events include the afterparty for The Trial of the Chicago 7 at the Laemmle Theatres in Los Angeles, and a performance by artist Spencer Ludwig in celebration of the release of Beautiful Boy. In 2020, Nine Stories launched a consultancy division that provides development and production services to content creators, as well as strategic partnerships for feature film, television, and theater projects. Nine Stories has a strong commitment to diversity and women-led stories, and is actively delivering on its mission to help shape the landscape of entertainment by creating bold, ambitious projects.

Tetton, Kingston St Mary is a small hamlet located in the county of Somerset, England. It is part of the civil parish of Kingston St Mary, and is situated approximately one mile south of Taunton town centre. The hamlet is situated on the southern boundary of the larger village of Kingston St Mary. It is part of the Rural Population area of Taunton Deane, which has a population of 23,266. Tetton is one of the most sparsely populated areas in Somerset, with census data from the 2001 Census indicating that it had a population of just 34 people. The hamlet is largely surrounded by agricultural land, with the nearby hamlet of Heasley Mill situated to its north, and the Taunton to Minehead railway line bordering the east of the settlement. It is accessed via a single road leading off the B3170 road at the north east end of Kingston St Mary. The local church is dedicated to St Peter and St Paul and is part of the Kingston St Mary parish. The closest school is Holyrood Academy, which is situated in the nearby village of Bishops Hull. The hamlet's name is derived from Teodene's tun, which was first recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086. The name was likely a reference to the local lord of the manor at the time, which may have been a man called Teodene or Theoden. Tetton has a long history of farming, with records indicating that the hamlet's fields were used for records indicating that the hamlet's fields were used for sheep grazing as far back as the 16th century. Much of the surrounding area is made up of rolling hills, although the land to the north and east is low-lying and is criss-crossed by meandering streams. Today, Tetton remains sparsely populated, with only a handful of small farms in the immediate area. Many of the farms are still utilised for livestock farming. The nearby village of Kingston St Mary provides the locals with amenities, including a post office, a public house and a village hall. Despite its rural location, Tetton is within easy reach of the larger towns of Taunton and Bridgwater, which both offer a wide range of shops, services, and leisure facilities. Tetton is an area of great beauty, with lovely sweeping hillside views, and a peaceful atmosphere. Despite its small size, the hamlet makes a great holiday destination due to its access to the countryside and its proximity to larger towns and cities.

Carlos Recinos (born August 8, 1984) is a Salvadoran-American musician, music producer and entrepreneur. He is the founder and CEO of CR Music Group and is best known for his production and songwriting in the Latin Pop, Urban, Regional and American Pop music genres. His diverse credits include major hits and collaborations with both established and burgeoning artists like Romeo Santos, J. Balvin, Carlos Vives, Marc Anthony, Prince Royce, Wisin y Yandel, Sasha Sokol, and Maluma. Recinos was born in El Salvador and immigrated to the United States in 2000 as a teenager. He began his music career playing guitar and bass as a session player in Miami, honing his craft while working with songwriters and producers. After some time in Miami, he relocated to Mexico City and began pitching songs he had been writing to artists in the Latin Pop/Urban/Regional genres. Through his persistence and dedication,Recinos quickly earned a reputation as a versatile music creator and collaborator. In 2020, he founded CR Music Group, a production and songwriting collective based in Miami, Florida. Under his direction and vision, the company has earned numerous Billboard chart-topping and multi-platinum successes. His dynamic and innovative team includes songwriters, composers, arrangers, producers and musicians from Latin, Urban and American Pop genres. Recinos' catalogue includes hit singles such as “Izamal” by J. Balvin, “Sobrenatural” by Carlos Vives, “Algo Grande” by Marc Anthony, “So Much Love” by Prince Royce, “Todo Tiene Su Final” by Wisin y Yandel, and “Romance” by Maluma. In addition to creating music, Recinos is an active proponent of entrepreneurship in music and media. He has keynoted at the Latin Grammys, SXSW and more on topics ranging from production, songwriting, developing digital strategies and cultivating independent label culture. As a producer, Recinos has established himself as a leader in modern Latin music, while inspiring and supporting future generations of composers, songwriters and producers. He is currently focusing on his next album release and continues to mentor upcoming music makers.

The Artifact Small Format Film Festival is an annual film festival in Los Angeles, California that celebrates short format films. The event was founded in 2012 with the goal of creating a platform for local, independent filmmakers to showcase their work. The festival strives to cultivate emerging talent and nurture a vibrant film community within the region. It focuses on innovative, independent films made on digital technology or super 8mm or 16mm film. The festival consists of screenings, panel discussions and presentations about aspects of small-form filmmaking. The festival is open to all independent filmmakers, regardless of size or budget, who work in its specified format. It is not a competition, but instead aims to connect filmmakers with each other and with industry professionals. It also seeks to share new ideas and techniques with the filmmaking community. The festival accepts shorts, feature films, and music videos, as well as video art and experimental films. It also offers postproduction awards and workshops, as well as an equipment loan program. The festival has attracted filmmakers from around the world, as well as support and recognition from the industry. In just four years, it has grown to be one of the most popular festivals of its kind. It has also been highlighted in numerous publications, including The New York Times, Variety, and the Los Angeles Times. The Artifacts of Small Format Film Festival was created with the goal of preserving the art of small format filmmaking and encouraging filmmakers to create more unique and daring short form films. With a diverse crowd of filmmakers both new and old, the festival continues to bring together film enthusiasts and promote the art of small format filmmaking.

Mata Hati Telinga (literal translation: Eye of the Heart Ear) is a traditional style of Indonesian dance performed mainly in the Minangkabau region of West Sumatra, Indonesia. It is thought to have originated during the 16th century and is still a popular form of entertainment today. Mata Hati Telinga is a mix of martial arts and traditional dance. It is performed by two people, one being the leader, who perform various hand and foot attacks while simultaneously moving in a choreographed pattern. The technique is known to be very precise and intricate and can only be performed in the right environment. The performers usually wear scarves and tassels made of different colors, including yellow, green and red. The yellow signifies bravery, loyalty and harmony, the green represents happiness and joy, and the red represents passion and strength. This correlates with the movements in the dance, which focus on strength and grace. The lead performer also carries a knife and shield, which represent strength and protection. The lead dancer will use the knife to lead the dance and his movements must be precise and accurate. As the performance progresses, the dancers will become more and more inspiring and show their capabilities as performers. At the climax of the performance, the dancer executing the knife strikes will shout to the audience, symbolizing victory and the completion of the performance. The audience will then usually offer a standing ovation, showing their appreciation for the performance. Today, Mata Hati Telinga is believed to be a reflection of Minang culture. It is regarded as an expression of strength and respect, as well as a way to showcase skill and dedication. Mata Hati Telinga has been recognised as a significant form of traditional dance with elements and techniques that are distinct to the Minang people of West Sumatra.

Rising Storm is a young adult novel written by American science fiction and fantasy author Suzanne Collins. The novel, first published in 2009, is set several decades after the events of Collins' earlier work, The Hunger Games trilogy, and follows the story of protagonist Lyra, a refugee from the planet District 13. The novel opens with Lyra, a District 13 refugee, waking up after escaping to a home on a remote planet. Accompanying her are her left-behind, made-up friends, the Dauntless. Immediately after, she discovers her ability to control the elements, becoming a powerful storm-caller. The rest of the novel follows Lyra as she attempts to protect her home planet from an alien force known as the Sparks. Along the way, she must survive cruel planetary inhabitants and battle a mysterious Shadow Beast. In addition to the fast-paced action found in Rising Storm, the novel also focuses on the deeper issues of war, and the political machinations employed by those wishing to gain control over power. Throughout the tale, Lyra must confront her own inner turmoil and use the power of the elements in order to protect both herself and her home planet. The novel has been highly praised by both critics and fans alike. It has won several awards, including the 2009 Hugo Award for Best Novel, the 2009 Andre Norton Award, and the 2009 Audie Award for Fiction. Rising Storm is followed by a sequel, Winter of Fire, released in 2011. While the stories of the two novels are closely linked, they differ in tone, as Winter of Fire focuses on a more personal story of self-discovery, rather than action and adventure.

Lyady is a small hamlet in the Vitebsk Region of Belarus. Situated on the banks of the Neman River, the village is geographically located in the north-western part of the region. Lyady is remotely located from regional hubs like Vitebsk and Orsha. First established in the 16th century, Lyady was a village under the hold of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth. During the 18th century, the village was annexed by Russian Empire, and the population was primarily of Eastern Orthodox denomination. During the time of the Russian Empire, outside of Orthodox churches, a Lutheran church, synagogue, and school were established in the village. In the late 19th century, it flourished as a center of sawmilling and brick-making, utilizing watercraft transportation down the Neman. In the late 1930s, the population of Lyady totaled to 668 inhabitants. Despite the struggles with famine and Nazi occupation, the village survived and was offered protection by the Soviet Union in 1945. During the Soviet times, the sawmilling industry of the town started to decline, while at the same time, another industry, that of food production, developed. This new industry included an oil-seed processing plant, a flax fabric mill, and a collective poultry farm. Today, Lyady consists of two streets and three churches and since 1999 is a part of Dokshitsky District. Nowadays, the town is a popular destination for tourists, due the beautiful landscape, rich culture and centuries-old churches. Lyady is home to the 17th-century Saint Nicholas wooden church, and the 17th-18th-century revival church dedicated to the Assumption of Mary. The region surrounding Lyady also boasts historic sites, like the famous Bialowieza Forest, one of the last and largest remaining parts of the immense primeval forest that once stretched across the European Plain, and the volcanic Valley of Mound Complex of Kurgany. Lyady is also just one of the many places to explore in Vitebsk Region, so tourists can also discover other beautiful spots, such as Vitebsk itself and Braslav Lakes. Lyady is a small piece of paradise tucked away in the picturesque Vitebsk Region. With a rich culture and centuries-old churches, the hamlet is a great destination for nature-conscious travelers and those looking to get away from the hustle and bustle of the city.

Arcade Building is a historic building located at 375 Yonge Street in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. It was built in 1890 by architects George A. Ross and John Turner and was originally intended to be an office building. With its Renaissance Revival style and grand façades, it has become a favorite destination for locals and tourists alike. It was one of the first multi-storey commercial buildings of its kind to be built in Toronto and is a prominent example of the turn-of-the-century architecture in the area. The building is constructed of a pale yellow brick with red accents and detailed carved stone ornamentation. The design is symmetrical and has seven stories of office space, with a ground floor and mezzanine. The Arcade Building is connected to the historic PATH, a network of underground shopping malls, food courts, and service corridors. This connection helped to make the building very popular with both local businesses and tourists. For example, on one side of the building it meets the busy shopping and entertainment district of Dundas Square with its many stores, while the other side connects with the Yonge Street pedestrian mall, where shoppers often take a break from their shopping spree. The building is listed on the City of Toronto's Inventory of Heritage Properties, which recognizes its historical and architectural significance in the city. The Arcade Building is also one of five designated City of Toronto Heritage Properties located within the Yonge Street corridor. Over the years, the Arcade Building has been home to many businesses, from banks to law firms, boutiques to restaurants. Its ground floor and mezzanine remain where a wide range of businesses can be found today, such as a nail salon, a camera store, and a coffee shop. The Arcade Building is an integral part of the cultural and architectural landscape of downtown Toronto and is a must-see for those visiting the city. It is a reminder of the city's early beginnings and of the historic Yonge Street corridor.

Le Petit Provençal is a French regional newspaper published in France since 1880. It is one of the oldest newspapers in France and is the official newspaper of the Var region. The newspaper is primarily distributed in the Var and Bouches-du-Rhône departments. The publication was founded by Auguste Théodore Gombert and Fabien Gombert. They first published it under the title La Provence on March 2, 1880 in Toulon. They ran the paper from a store near the Toulon harbor and the newspaper primarily focused on regional news as well as business content. The newspaper was previously 7 pages and by the 1950s and 1960s, it had expanded up to 50 pages. In the 1920s and 1930s, the newspaper was known for its anti-Semitic stance. However, during the 1940s and 1950s, the paper shifted focus to become pro-democracy and the paper was used to promote the perception of the Union for the New Republic, a center-right political party. In 1984, the newspaper underwent a name change and became La Provençal which was then changed to Le Petit Provençal in 1993. Currently, it is owned by the Group Hersant Media and has an estimated circulation of 106,000 copies reaching 550,000 readers. The newspaper typically focuses on local culture, sports, and continental European politics. While some parts of the its content is online, the majority of the content is only available in the print edition. The newspaper is printed in three waves that are issued in the morning, afternoon, and evening. Its headquarters is located in Toulon. Le Petit Provençal is one of the oldest and most prominent newspapers in France and is a source for news for the Var region.

Arta (Greek: Αρτά) is a regional unit of Greece, located in the northwestern part of the country in the region of Epirus. It has an area of 1,880 square km (726 square miles) and a population of 41,820 (2011). The capital and largest city of the regional unit is Arta. Arta is situated between the Ambracian Gulf in the east and the mountains of Epirus in the west. The regional unit of Arta is named after the ancient city of Arta, an important center of the Aetolian League. A large part of its area is covered by the mountain range of Tzoumerka while the southern parts of Arta is mostly a hilly area. The mountain range of Tzoumerka is the highest in the region with altitudes up to 2,401 meters. The highest mountain is called Agioi Vlachoi and it's located near the village of Kalligoni. The main rivers flowing through Arta are the Arachthos and the Capros. The former river has its source at the mountain of Agioi Vlachoi and flows generally eastward until it reaches the Ambracian Gulf. The latter river is formed by the union of several smaller streams and flows through the plains of the regional unit in the northern direction until it meets the Arachthos. The main production activities in the district of Arta are focused around agriculture and livestock farming. The main agricultural products are olives, grapes, cotton and some vegetables, while the most important livestock production is related to sheep and goats. A significant industry is also located in the district of Arta, mainly producing furniture, textiles and shoes. The district of Arta is also renowned for its natural beauty and important monuments located in its territory. The most important among them are the 18th century bridge of Arta, Arakynthos, a traditional village located on the snowy heights of Tzoumerka and the Monastery of Agia Paraskevi, which is a major pilgrimage center in the region. Other important monuments located in the region are the castle of Messokomio, the tower of Lygourio and ancient Nikopolis, a city with an important role in ancient history. The economy of the region of Arta is mainly based on its natural resources and its workforce, with the industry and tourism being its major drivers. The combination of its important monuments and its rich culture, combined with its high level of hospitality, make Arta an attractive tourist destination for visitors from Greece and abroad.

The 1969 Texas A&I Javelinas football team represented Texas A&I University in the 1969 NCAA College Division football season. The Javelinas were led by second year head coach Homer Bryce and played their home games at Javelina Stadium in Kingsville, Texas. They finished the season with a 9–1–0 record and were ranked No. 7 in the AP Poll and No. 1 in the UPI Poll. Their only loss was in the Grantland Rice Bowl against the Florida A&M Rattlers, who were led by a first-year head coach Joe Gilliam Sr. The 1969 season was a successful year for the Javelinas; notable highlights include a 28–3 win over rival Southwest Texas State and a 31–16 win over No. 16 Arkansas State. The Javelinas' defense was one of the best in the nation; they held eight opponents to 10 points or less, and five opponents to zero points. Defensive back Dennis Court was named an All-American in 1969. Offensively, the Javelinas had an explosive offense, led by quarterback Bobby Marrow who threw for 1,121 yards and 16 touchdowns. In addition to their success on the field, the 1969 Javelinas made history with their all-black starting lineup. This was the first time in Texas collegiate history that an all-black team had started in a college game, making the 1969 Javelinas the first African American college football team in Texas. The 1969 Javelinas were nationally recognized for their innovative coaching and cutting edge play, earning them the title of the “Cinderella Team.” The 1969 Javelinas were inducted into the Texas A&I Sports Hall of Fame in 2006 and the National Football Foundation's Hall of Fame in 2009. The successful 1969 season was a stepping stone for the Javelinas, and helped to propel them to four consecutive NCAA College Division Championships in the early 1970s. The Colombian spider monkey (Ateles hybridus, hybrid spider monkey) is a species of spider monkey found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama. It is one of the rarest and most endangered primates in the New World. Characteristics The Colombian spider monkey has dark fur which ranges in color from grey to black and has a darker colored "saddle" on the back and a lighter face. Its body is long and spidery and its arms can span up to 8 feet when outstretched. Its legs are much shorter than those of other spider monkeys and it has less prehensile ability than other species. The Colombian species has a distinctive white beard and a tuft of white hair near the crown, giving it a distinctive appearance. Habitat Colombian spider monkeys can be found in a variety of habitats, from lowland rainforest to high-altitude cloud forest. They prefer lowland humid forest below 1,000 meters and typically exhibit social behavior in these areas. It is mostly arboreal, spending most of its time in the canopy of the rainforest, but also forages on the ground. Behavior Colombian spider monkeys are mainly diurnal, with peak activity occurring in the morning and afternoon. They prefer to spend the night at the top of trees. They usually live in groups of 8-20 individuals, but can form large groups of up to 40 or more. The social hierarchy is determined by size and age, with older male spider monkeys leading the group. Diet Colombian spider monkeys are mainly frugivores but are also known to eat leaves and flowers. They pluck fruit, flowers, and other plant parts from the branches, pull tender shoots from trees, and even eat bird eggs and nestlings. Threats Colombian spider monkeys are primarily threatened by deforestation due to logging, industrial agriculture, and expanding human settlements. Additionally, they are hunted for food by local communities and suffer from hunting for the illegal pet trade. Conservation Colombian spider monkeys are protected in some protected areas, such as the Meta River Basin Natural Park and the Chocó Biogeographic Region. They are listed on the IUCN red list as endangered, and local governments and conservation groups are working to reduce threats and protect the species. Akiko Yano (born October 10th, 1955) is a Japanese singer-songwriter, arranger and keyboardist. She has recorded more than 20 albums, and has collaborated with a variety of other musicians across genres, including jazz, electronics and pop. Her classic radio hit "Tobacco Au Go Go" (1979) was a one-night sensation that gained her acclaim for its catchy, lighthearted melody. Yano was born in Tokyo. Her mother was a piano teacher and her father was a classical conductor. She started taking classical piano lessons from her mother at two years old and at age five, she started playing organ in her club. By the time she was in high school, she had already composed many promising tunes, so her father recommended that she start performing professionally. In 1974, she debuted with video game and anime composer Hiroshi Kawaguchi as the duo Spoon. They released one single and one album before parting ways. Yano then joined Godiego as keyboard player, who had just released the hit single "Monkey Magic". Yano contributed her own arrangements which became a prominent aspect of the Godiego sound, and she also wrote songs such as "Good-Bye Earth". The following year, Yano started her solo career releasing her debut album Japanese Girl, which featured songs that blended jazz and Europop. The most successful single from the album was "Tobacco Au Go Go", which has been cited in many books, films and musicals. In 1981, her collaboration album with Haruomi Hosono and Shigeru Suzuki, known as "YYMM" and released as Hosono House achieved critical acclaim. Yano has produced many collaboration albums and singles which featured musicians from diverse genres, such as jazz saxophonist and composer Masato Kawana and jazz trumpeter Terumasa Hino. In recent years, Yano has continued to release new music and perform live. In 2010, she released her 20th studio album, Umi no Ue no Shinryojo. Yano's unique style of jazz-influenced music and her collaborations have made her one of the most respected Japanese musicians of her generation. Her music continues to receive great praise, both in Japan and abroad.

Microsoft Baseline Security Analyzer (MBSA) is a software tool developed by Microsoft as part of its Security Compliance Initiative. It is used to determine the security state of computers running Microsoft Windows operating systems and applications. MBSA is Microsoft's free security scanning tool that allows system administrators to quickly and easily look for missing security updates, common security misconfigurations, and more on their Windows servers and PCs running Microsoft Windows XP, Windows 2000, and Windows Server 2003. MBSA is installed on the user's computer and can be used to scan one or more local or remote systems on the network. MBSA scans each of the targeted computers to look for appropriate security updates, service packs, update rollups, and security settings as defined in the security updates. If any of these settings or components are missing or insecure, MBSA will provide users with a detailed report describing the missing updates or settings and recommend corrective action. MBSA includes an inventory tool that can be used to quickly identify upfront what applications and services the server is running, helping the system administrator to plan the list of applicable updates. It also includes a parameter-based uninstall tool that allows the user to remove specific service packs, security updates and patches that have been identified by the MBSA scan. MBSA provides a graphical user interface (GUI) and a command-line interface (CLI) to perform security scans and provide further customization. The MBSA CLI will help system administrators and IT professionals automate security scans. The GUI can also be used to customizeMBSA scans, focused on specific applications and services, such as IIS, Exchange or SQL Server. MBSA can be downloaded from the Microsoft website, and is available for Windows XP, Windows 2000, and Windows Server 2003. The latest version of MBSA is 2.3 and this version is compatible with the upcoming Windows 7 and Windows Server 2008 R2. Microsoft's Security Compliance Initiative uses the MBSA for analyzing security policies to properly secure Windows-based systems against common risks. MBSA is an indispensable tool for system administrators and IT professionals, who are responsible for maintaining the security of their system. It can also be used to ensure that future software, such as Exchange and SQL Server, is installed securely and in compliance with Microsoft's security guidelines.

Don't Be Cruel is a song written by Otis Blackwell and Elvis Presley, released as a single in 1956. The song is considered one of Presley's signature songs and is one of the best-selling singles of all time. The song was written by Blackwell, a songwriter known for hits such as "Fever", and recorded by Presley in just one take. Its success propelled both performers to superstardom. Upon release, the single topped the Billboard chart for 11 weeks and remains the longest-running number-one hit of the 50s. Don't Be Cruel has been covered by many artists, including Jerry Lee Lewis, David Bowie, and Bobby Brown. It has appeared on many albums, including Elvis' own Elvis Presley and Elvis Is Back!. Presley performed it frequently in his concerts and television appearances. The song is composed of two parts. The verses concern a plea to a lover not to be "cold hearted" and to stay with him as he pleads his case. The chorus is more up-tempo and contains what is considered Presley's most famous line: "You know I can be found/Sitting home all alone/If you can't come around/At least please telephone". Presley's rendition and performance of the song is regarded highly, and is commonly cited as an influence on future rock and roll performances. It is one of the few tracks that he recorded that followed the classic pop structure of introduction, verse, bridge and refrain. The song has also been recognized for its influence on other musical styles, such as blues, soul, rhythm and blues, country and western and Punk. Its use of musical repetition has also been noted as pioneering, not only in the rock and roll genre but historically. Don't Be Cruel has been included in multiple list of the top 500 songs of all time, such as Rolling Stone magazine, and has maintained popularity and recognition to the present day. It will continue to be an iconic song in the years to come.

The economy of Nepal is an underdeveloped economy dependent on foreign aid and remittances. Nepal is among the least developed countries in the world and ranks 145th out of 189 countries in the Human Development Index as of 2020. It is a mixed economy with both planned and market elements. The agricultural sector, including forestry, employs 76% of the total labor force and makes up 37% of GDP. The industry sector accounts for 15.7% of GDP. The services sector makes up 47.3% of the GDP. Nepal has numerous bilateral, multilateral, and domestic agreements to promote foreign trade and investment. Nepal has been a member of the Generalized System of Preferences (GSP) since 1975 and it is a member of the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) since 2004. The primary exports of Nepal are vegetable and animal-based products which largely include woollen carpets, handicrafts, textiles, clothing, leather goods, jute goods, grain, pulses, and pashmina shawls. The main export partners are India, Australia, the United States, and the United Kingdom. The main imports of Nepal are petroleum products, machinery, and equipment for Nepal’s reconstruction, pharmaceutical products, and chemicals. The main import partners are India, China, the United Arab Emirates, and Singapore. The balance of payments surplus of Nepal has reduced significantly to an estimated amount of US$67 million in 2017–18. The tourism industry is an important source of foreign exchange earnings. In 2017, Nepal welcomed a record 1.17 million tourists, making it the fastest growing tourism destination in South Asia and the sixth fastest growing in the world. This represented an increase of 24.8% from the previous year. The number of foreigners participating in mountaineering and trekking activities also increased substantially. Nepal’s currency, the Nepalese Rupee, is pegged to the Indian Rupee, which is subject to natural exchange rate fluctuations. Inflation increased significantly to 6.5% in Fiscal Year 2017–18 from 4.1% in Fiscal Year 2016–17. In attempts to bring down inflation, the Government of Nepal has implemented a policy of regulated distribution and pricing of energy products and essential goods, and has limited the budget deficit. Nepal has made economic progress in recent years, with growth in all economic sectors. In fiscal year 2019–20, the economy grew by 4.4%, slightly below the previous year (4.5%). Due to the coronavirus pandemic, the economy contracted steeply in 2020, with the IMF predicting negative growth of 8.8% for the year. To mitigate the impact of the pandemic, the government has implemented a crisis response package, which includes loan guarantees, tax forgiveness and public welfare programs. The Nepalese Government is undertaking numerous reforms to promote investment and improve the business environment, such as public-private partnerships, infrastructure development, and initiatives to tackle corruption. The government has launched the "Prosperous Nepal, Happy Nepali" vision initiative to achieve middle-income status by 2030. To reach this goal, Nepal will need to attract more foreign capital and investments, as well as make progress in poverty reduction and job creation.

Daniel J. Sandin (born June 20, 1943) is an American artist and a pioneer in the realm of media art and new-media. Sandin's works have been included in numerous international exhibitions, including the Museum of Modern Art in New York, the Museum of Contemporary Art in San Francisco, the Centre Georges Pompidou in Paris, the Israel Museum in Jerusalem, and the Australian Centre of the Moving Image in Melbourne. He is an emeritus professor at the University of Illinois at Chicago and the founding director of the Electronic Visualization Laboratory. Sandin was born in New York and raised in San Fernando Valley, California. He received a B.A. degree in Physics at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1967, and an M.S. degree in Computer Science from Stanford University in 1969. During his time at UCLA, Sandin worked on the Physiological Signal Analysis Computer (PSAC), which laid the foundation for his lifelong interest in the intersection of art and technology. In 1974, Sandin co-founded the Experimental Television Center at Binghamton University in New York with his wife, artist and educator Patty Jo Watson and experimental filmmaker Ralph Hocking. The Center was designed to promote artists' use of emerging video technology and produce educational programming. During his time at the Center, Sandin developed the Image Processor, a real-time video processor, allowing him to explore video synthesis, feedback, distortions, and slow-motion effects which are now in common use. Sandin served as a faculty member in the School of the Art Institute of Chicago from 1977-1986 and then at the University of Illinois, Chicago from 1986-2004 where he served as a professor of art and founding director of the Electronic Visualization Laboratory. His research and development there led to such inventions as the CAVE and tiled displays. He was one of the founding directors of the National Computational Science Alliance (NCSA), which developed the modern infrastructure for data-driven scientific discovery. Sandin's works have been included in numerous international exhibitions and feature in the permanent collections of major institutions. In 2004, the National Academy of Sciences awarded him the Bower Award for Achievement in Science and his pioneering contributions in art and media. He is a Fellow of the American Institute for Arts and Technology, the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, the New York Institute of Technology, and the International Institute of Media Art and Science. Sandin continues to lecture and serve as a guest professor around the world. He is currently a visiting professor and artist-in-residence at the Advanced Center for Computing and Communication Sciences of Hiroshima University in Japan.

Oldřich Nejedlý (born June 10, 1867 - November 9, 1951) was a Czech sculptor, illustrator, painter, and architect. He is best known for his sculptures, with the greatest concentration of his work in Prague and the Czechoslovakian region. Nejedlý was born in Hrochův Týnec, Bohemia. He began his work in the late 19th century, and trained as a sculptor in Vienna in 1889-90. He then studied at the Prague Academy of Arts in 1894, and finally taught at the same academy from 1913 to 1932. Nejedlý's sculptures often depict young and muscular women, which reflects his unabashedly naturalistic approach to the sculpting process. Many of his sculptures can be found in national parks and museums throughout the Czech Republic, including the botanic gardens of Brno and Terezín. His statue of St. Procopius, for instance, stands in the small church of Záhorská Ves. In addition to his sculptures, Nejedlý took up painting and illustrations. His illustrated books, such as The Life of St. Procopius, remain popular even today. He also wrote several essays on art and aesthetics, including 'Art in Relation to Nature' and 'The Use of Color in Art'. In the 1920s, Nejedlý launched a successful career as an architect. Among his works are the National Memorial in Prague, the National Active Poor Refuge, and the National Women's University. His picturesque house in the woods of Slavkov, called Villa Hvezda, is considered to be his greatest architectural feat. Oldřich Nejedlý died on November 9, 1951 in Prague. He remains one of the most prominent sculptors, painters, and architects of the 20th century from the Czech Republic. His legacy comprises of numerous sculptures, paintings, illustrations, and buildings, all distinctive in their own unique way.

Siddharth Sinha is an Indian entrepreneur known for his start-up companies and philanthropic work. Born on February 24, 1981 in Delhi, he graduated from Shri Ram College of Commerce, Delhi University with a degree in Commerce. Sinha started his career in 2005 with Management consulting and later opted out to begin his own venture in the domain of animal husbandry. His interim venture was launched in 2006 with his start-up company HSB Livestock Solutions Pvt Ltd., which focuses on providing technologies and services to the Indian Dairy Industry. After gaining considerable success and capitalizing on this achievement, Sinha went on to launch another venture – Livestock Biotechnology Pty Ltd. This venture was the precursor to his another venture– India’s first large-scale B2B livestock-tech platform – KnowMore.in (formerly known as HSB BioLivestock Solutions).Founded in 2014, the company furnishes businesses in the livestock sector with marketing and trading solutions.KnowMore.in has so far attracted more than 10,000 users in its four plus years of existence. Sinha is also actively involved in many philanthropic initiatives, which include sponsoring the education of under-privileged children, founding an animal shelter, and providing help and assistance to farmers and farmers’ families. He is an active participant in Start-up and VC activities, and is currently a Board Member and Mentor of various start-ups, including MetoAquaint Consultancy, Bandanna Money and FeedLife. He has also been an Advisor to the Prime Minister, Office of the President of India, and United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD). He currently lives in Ahmedabad, Gujarat with his wife and two sons. Outside of business, Siddharth Sinha is an outspoken proponent of sustainable development and advocates for long-term agricultural solutions. He also actively promotes the wide spread use of technology to ease the lives of farmers and help improve the standards of living of their communities.

Gods of Luxury is a term commonly associated with the high-end status symbols of wealth, often referred to as “status symbols” or “indulgences”. These items may include expensive cars, expensive jewelry, designer clothes and products, fine dining, high-end travel, exotic vacations, and other extravagances of the wealthy. The phrase likely originated in the 1960s during the Dotcom boom, when the wealthy were seen as “gods” who had everything anyone could ever dream of. It became a symbol of a lifestyle many people could only imagine and glamorize. Gods of Luxury was introduced to the public in 2003 as the title of a book by British author M. Raymond Löw. The book portrays a world of luxury, where wealthy people are able to enjoy life's finer things. It explores the behavior of luxury product and service companies and their clientele, and emphasizes the importance of having an excellent business plan in order to succeed in a world of high-end status symbols. Since its conception, the phrase has become a popular term for describing the world of luxury goods and services, and the people who use them. It has been used in literature, news reports, and movies. It is often associated with celebrities, powerful executives, wealthy entrepreneurs, and those belonging to the upper echelons of society. Gods of Luxury is an ambiguous phrase, as it may be used to symbolize admiration and cravings for the lifestyles of the wealthy, or to connote envy and a feeling of exclusivity towards those partaking in the extravagance. It is nonetheless a phrase that illustrates the glamour and power of status symbols and wealth. In today's world, there is no single definition of a "God of Luxury". It is up to the individual to define their own definition of luxury and the associated status symbols which constitute a “God of Luxury”.

Paula Williams Madison (born March 27, 1953) is an institutional and media executive and former broadcast journalist, entrepreneur and philanthropist, who has made significant contributions to the American television and entertainment industry. Madison is a media trailblazer who has held numerous senior executive positions at the NBC and Telemundo divisions of NBCUniversal, the FOX broadcast networks and Los Angeles public television station KCET. She is the former President and CEO of Los Angeles public TV station KCET and the former NBC Vice President of Diversity. During her 8-year tenure IKCET, Madison aspired to deliver inspiring, award-winning TV programming to the citizens of Los Angeles. Prior to her roles at NBC, Madison founded Madison Media Management (MMM) -- the first Black owned TV syndication firm -- which was the first to acquire and distribute the iconic sitcom The Cosby Show. Before creating MMM, she was a Vice President at NBC television news, where she held several executive management positions, transforming the networks news coverage to a wider range of segments. Madison is known for her dedication to the advancement of diversity in the media and entertainment industry. In 2003, she was named one of the most influential women in cable television by Cableworld Magazine for her diversifying efforts at NBC. In 2011, she was appointed by Mrs. Obama on the White House's Advisory Committee for the Arts, becoming the first African American to hold a chair. In addition to her broadcast and entrepreneurial accomplishments, Madison is also an accomplished author, having co-written the memoir Finding Samuel Lowe: China, Jamaica, Harlem with her mother. The book is inspired by her Chinese-Jamaican heritage, which has helped shape her life’s journey. Madison is passionate about giving back to the community. She serves as a trustee of The Paley Center for Media, The California African American Museum and is a member of the Academy of Television Arts & Sciences. In 2019, Madison also established the Paula Madison Foundation to focus on African American art and film, with a vision to bridge cultural divides by creating content that reflects the humanity and history of Black communities. Madison is a Lifetime Fellow of the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences. She is an inductee of the Broadcasting and Cable Hall of Fame, and a recipient of the Museum of Television and Radio’s Achievement Awards for Diversity.

Beira is a region in northern Portugal. It is bordered by the regions of Minho, Douro and Porto in the North, Trás-os-Montes in the East, Portalegre in the South and Pinhal Interior in the West. The region has a high density of population, with a population of approximately 2,855,847 inhabitants (2018 census). The region is a very important part of Portugal's history and culture. The city of Beira was founded by the Romans in the 3rd century BC. It was the site of a major battle between the Romans and Visigoths in 436 AD. The region has since played an important role in many of Portugal's wars. Its capital, Viseu, was founded in the 13th century and served as the country's capital during the 1338-1383 period, before being moved to Lisbon. The region is mostly rural and has many different types of cultures and lifestyles. The local economy is mainly based on agriculture, but some industries have started establishing in more urban areas. It is also known for its historical importance and for its strong touristic attractions, such as the numerous castles, monasteries and universities. Beira has a pleasant climate with temperatures ranging from 10-15 ºC in December to 27-30 ºC in July. Winters here are usually rainy and it can be very cold in the high mountainous regions. The region has a lot of rural activities such as pottery, wine-making and cheese-making. The most important cities of the region are Viseu, Guarda, Aveiro, Vila Real and Bragança. Some of the most interesting places to visit are the city of Douro in the west, the Mediterranean-like beach in Aveiro, the cliff-side city of São Jacinto and the National Park of Peneda-Gerês in the east. Beira Region is also home to some important universities, such as the Universities of Aveiro and Coimbra, as well as some important scientific and technological research centers. Beira is the region in Portugal with the highest concentration of Castilian-speaking Portuguese people, making this region a great melting pot of different cultures and languages. It is a region full of attractions, history and culture that can be experienced firsthand, and is an essential part of Portugal’s culture and heritage.

Kyle Casey (born November 28th, 1989) is an American singer-songwriter, musician, and actor. He is best known for his single "I Wanna Know Now", which reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in October 2016. Casey started his music career in 2010, when he released his debut album, Recognize the Melody. The album gained recognition in the indie pop scene and was praised for its unique blend of alternative, pop, and acoustic genres. The album's success resulted in Casey being featured on multiple music blogs. In 2012, Casey released his second album, Memories and Revolution, which further pushed him into the forefront of the music industry. Casey has since appeared as a featured artist on multiple songs by artists such as Kaylee Scott and Zayn Malik. In 2015, he was featured on Zayn Malik's single "I Won't Mind," and in 2017, he released his third studio album, Bright Future. The album was critically acclaimed and charted internationally, making it the first album by Casey to chart outside of the United States. In addition to his musical career, Casey has also made a name for himself as an actor. He has appeared in various television shows, including Modern Family (2009), Glee (2010-2013), and Pretty Little Liars (2013-2014). He also appeared in two films, Joseph (2016) and The Genesis Project (2016). Casey is an active advocate for mental health, having created a mental health awareness website in 2016. He has opened up about his own struggles with depression and anxiety on different platforms, and hopes to make a positive difference to those affected by similar issues. Casey is currently continuing to pursue his music career and has released multiple singles since 2018, including "Fly Away" and "Life Is A Fantasy." He is set to collaborate with musician Janelle Monaé in 2020 and will be releasing his fourth studio album later in the year. Casey is a true testament to the fact that talented individuals can accomplish great things with hard work and dedication. His persistence and drive to succeed has made him one of the most respected artists in the industry today.

Endeverafter was an American rock band from Sacramento, California, which was active from 2003 to 2012 and recorded on the Epic Records label. Endeverafter combined hard rock and alternative rock influences, and their music has been compared to such bands as Linkin Park, Incubus, and Goo Goo Dolls. The group was formed in 2003 by singer/guitarist Joe Peters. Peters recruited guitarist/singer Derek Gledhill, bassist Chris Mack, and drummer Dan Palmer to complete the lineup. In 2004 they released their self-titled debut, which featured such songs as "No More Words" and "Dream Away". The album was well-received, and Endeverafter began touring heavily in promotion of the record. In 2006, the band released their sophomore effort, The Pie And The Pint. Again, the album was well-received and spawned such singles as "I Wanna Be Your Man" and "Gone By Morning". Again, the band toured extensively in support. Endeverafter's third album, Kiss or Kill, was released in 2008 and included the single "New Life", which charted highly in the US Rock Top 40, and their cover version of the Pretenders' "Brass in Pocket". Again, the band toured extensively to promote the record. The band's fourth and final album, From the Top of the World, was released in 2010 and featured singles such as "Last Good Fight" and "Force of Love". Unfortunately, the record failed to see any significant commercial success, and Endeverafter announced they were parting ways in 2012. Since their breakup, the members have gone on to join other bands or pursue solo projects. Peters is currently the lead singer of the band Sacred Fire, while Gledhill is a solo artist and composer. Palmer has gone on to drum for the band Sister Solace, and Mack has joined the band Emulsion. Despite their short tenure, Endeverafter made a significant impact on the hard rock scene, and their music remains popular among fans.

Back to Life is a 1913 American silent short drama film directed by Alfred E. Green and produced by Mack Sennett. The plot of the film follows a father as he struggles to get his son, who was sent to prison, out and back on the right path. The film stars Mabel Normand, Charles Avery, and Minta Durfee, and features cameos by Harry Gribbon and Bobby Moyer. The plot focuses on a couple, George and Betty, with a son, Jack. When Jack falls onto a life of crime, the couple has to do whatever they can to help their son back on the right path. In order to post Jack's bail, the couple is forced to sell their own home. They are successful in getting him out on bail and pledge to never allow this to happen again. Jack is overwhelmed with guilt and regret and begins to pay for his crime by becoming a philanthropist and donating money to charities. He is eventually accepted back into society and his family is proud of his progress. The film was commercially and critically successful, and was praised for its "eloquently expressive and convincingly portrayed" characters. The film was released in the United States on October 14, 1913. A copy of the film was restored and submitted for copyright registration in the USA on October 5, 2006. The film is now widely available on home video. Back to Life is included in the Mack Sennett Collection held by the Academy Film Archive. The Archive describes the film as follows, "Alfred Green's muddled story of repentance carries a strong moral message as parents drive their son back to the straight and narrow with clever psychological tactics." Back to Life is recognized as an important early silent drama. The film's plot and characters prove its importance in the history of film, and its still relevant messages of redemption and personal responsibility resonate with audiences today.

The Epic of American Civilization is an academic study of the history of the United States, written over a period of 15 years by the American historian and philologist Josef Svoboda. First published in 1935, the work is an ambitious attempt to chart the "epic" of the development of American civilization over the course of three centuries. Svoboda drew upon a vast range of primary sources, including archival documents, oral testimonies, newspaper accounts and literary sources, as well as his own observations during travels throughout the United States. The book was part of a larger project whose aim was to capture the essence of American civilization in various aspects. In The Epic of American Civilization, Svoboda tried to identify the "principal characteristics and slogans that best express the spirit of the American people". In the book, Svoboda described the American Republic as the result of an evolutionary process, and he emphasized the nation's achievements in politics, economics, and law. Whenever possible, he related the theme of America's struggles and successes to the previous experiences in European civilizations. The book also considered religious concepts, architectural style and clothing styles, as well as other aspects of American culture, such as popular music, sports and the international role of the United States. Svoboda was unafraid to criticize the American government or to present controversial issues, such as slavery and racial inequality. He argued that although the U.S. cannot compete against the nations of Europe in terms of age, mutual understanding and culture, America should nevertheless strive to build an epic of its own. The Epic of American Civilization has been widely studied by historians and other scholars, in addition to the general reader. The book has been praised for its thought-provoking insights, its vivid language and its expansive scope. It is considered to be an important and influential study of American culture and civilization.

The Pearl gourami (Trichogaster leeri) is a small, tropical freshwater fish native to Southeast Asia. It is a labyrinth fish, meaning it has the ability to breathe atmospheric oxygen. It is popular in the aquarium trade, due its active and social behavior, and interestingly patterned pearl-like scales. Appearance Pearl gouramis are olive-green or golden-brown with an intricate pattern of white, pearlescent patches across their body and fins. Males reach an average size of 8-10 cm (3-4 inches) while females are typically smaller, around 6 cm (2 inches). The pelvic fins in males are long with a threadlike tip and they have long, downward sweeping dorsal and anal fins. The mouth is slightly upturned, an adaptation which may help them feed in the wild and in aquariums. Habitat & Tank Conditions Pearl gouramis can be found living in shallow, slow-moving waters with plenty of aquatic plants in their native range in Southeast Asia, particularly in the Mekong Delta. In the aquarium, pearl gouramis thrive in slightly acidic water conditions at temperatures between 75-82°F (24-28°C). The tank should be at least 20 gallons and have a good filtration system. They should have plenty of hiding places and vegetation. They particularly benefit from floating plants, which will create the perfect environment for them to explore and spawn. Behavior Pearl gouramis are usually peaceful and interactive fish, often examining their surroundings and flitting from leaf to leaf. They tend to be more active and social during the day, while at night they hide around structures and plants. Socializing with other pearl gouramis of the same species is common and enjoyable behavior. Diet In their wild habitat, pearl gouramis will feed on the sweeping rivers banks for vegetation, small insects, and other protein sources. Similarly, in the aquarium, they should be fed a variety of foods – frozen, dried, or live – to supplement their diet with a wide range of vitamins and minerals. Breeding Pearl gouramis are bubble-nesting fish, meaning that the male will build a nest at the surface of the tank. He will guard the nest and eggs and tends to the fry after they hatch. The female should be removed from the tank during breeding as the male can become aggressive towards her. Outside of its native habitat, pearl gouramis have become a popular fish in the aquarium trade thanks to their attractive patterned appearance and hardy nature. They are a gentle and social fish that are great for both beginner and experienced aquarists.

Kenny Loggins (born Kenneth Clark Loggins; January 7, 1948) is an American singer-songwriter and musician. He released 13 albums from 1976 to 2006 and has collaborated extensively with other talented musicians over the course of his career. Kenny Loggins is best known for his soft rock hits such as “I'm Alright”, “Footloose” and “Danger Zone”, but he is also a celebrated singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist. Loggins' work has been featured in over 40 films and tv shows, including iconic films such as Top Gun, Caddyshack, and Footloose. Loggins was born in Everett, Washington and grew up in Detroit, Michigan. He began his musical career in the 1970s with the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band as a painter. He wrote two songs for their “Will the Circle Be Unbroken” album which rose to the top of the charts. Loggins then went on to form a duo with fellow musician Jim Messina called Loggins and Messina. Their first self-titled studio album began a wave of success in the mid-1970s, with popular singles such as “Danny’s Song” and “House at Pooh Corner”. Since releasing his first self-titled album in 1976, Loggins has released thirteen additional albums, all of which have reached the Top 40 on the US Billboard charts. His biggest hit has undoubtedly been “Footloose”, which was featured in the iconic 1984 film of the same name. He has also made appearances in hit movies such as The Goonies and Top Gun, for which he wrote and performed the title track “Danger Zone”. Kenny Loggins is one of the leading soft rock and singer-songwriter musical artists of the late 20th century. His 1982 solo album High Adventure was the first album to be certified Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). He has been nominated for five Grammy awards, and has won the American Music Award for Favorite Pop/Rock Male Artist in 1981. Kenny Loggins has become one of the most beloved and influential idolized musicians of the modern day. He puts emphasis on connecting with his audience through intimate performances and moving performances. The Essential Kenny Loggins is an impressively diverse collection of his best works, and is an essential part of any music library.

The Société de Charité Maternelle is a French charity organization founded in Paris in 1819. The society's mission is to provide health and social services to low-income families and individuals. The members of the organization are chosen from the local community, based on their commitment to providing a hand up for those in need. Finance for the charity comes from public donations, charitable foundations, and corporate partners. Every year the Society organizes a therapeutic program to provide support to those in need. The Société de Charité Maternelle is the oldest and largest charity of its kind in France, with several projects and services in Paris and across France. The organization also offers homes to young mothers who are struggling financially. The organization's main focus is on care for pregnant women and mothers, as well as providing assistance to children with disabilities. It also offers medical support and help with childcare. They focus on creating an environment of wellbeing and help those who cannot afford healthcare and specialist services. The organization also runs community-based initiatives, such as the Art for Well-Being program which offers visual arts activities to those in need, aiming to foster community spirit. The Société de Charité Maternelle works closely with public authorities, private organizations and other social service providers to ensure the highest quality of support for those in need. In addition, the charity is involved in research and advocacy work, such as a 2019 campaign to increase funding for home help services for low-income families. The Charity has been awarded the France Honorary Medal for its outstanding service to the community. It is also the recipient of numerous awards in recognition of its humanitarian and charitable work, such as the 2019 Order of the Légion d’honneur, a prestigious civilian honor in France. The Société de Charité Maternelle has been helping the most vulnerable members of the community for more than 200 years and continues to work hard to ensure the best possible quality of life for those who need it most.

Stuart Townend (born 1957) is an English singer-songwriter, primarily known for his work in contemporary Christian and folk music. His songs often deal with themes of spirituality, evangelism, social justice and grace. He has written or co-written many popular Christian songs, including "In Christ Alone", "The Power of the Cross" and "How Deep the Father's Love for Us". Born in Northern Ireland, Townend grew up in a Christian family and became a Christian at the age of 14. He subsequently studied theology at the London School of Theology. After obtaining his degree, he began working as a youth minister in England before beginning a career in Christian music in the late 1980s. Townend's most popular songs, such as "In Christ Alone" co-written with Keith Getty, are included on hundreds of albums by major Christian music artists. In addition to writing and performing, Townend is known for speaking engagements; he has lectured at universities on worship, spirituality and societal issues. In recent years, his work has moved away from contemporary Christian music, to more of a folky, singer-songwriter-type sound. Townend achieved success with a variety of different styles in music. He has released several albums of his own, which have all topped the CCM charts. He also co-wrote the Gold-certified "In Christ Alone", with Keith Getty; it won an ASCAP Christian Music Award in 2006. He released a new album, Heaven Over Sea in 2018, to much critical acclaim. Townend is highly respected in the Christian music industry and has influenced the direction of popular Christian music for many years. He is known for his work in combining music and theology, as well as his lyrical content. His passion for justice, mission and grace continues to shape Christians around the world, bringing their attention to larger issues than just their own circumstances. He has left a lasting impression on the Christian music industry, and his influence continues to be felt today.

Ole Rasmussen (born 9 October 1952, in Aarhus, Denmark) is a former Danish footballer and manager. Rasmussen began his professional career with hometown side Aarhus GF in 1971. He played for AGF for the next seven years, becoming one of the most recognised Danish footballers in that period. Rasmussen helped the team win the 1978 Danish Cup, scoring the decisive goal in the final, 2–1 against AB. Rasmussen decided to leave AGF in 1978 after his father's suggestion, and joined Belgian club R.S.C. Anderlecht in August. He was a prominent part of the team for the next five years, winning the Belgian League title in 1980–81 and the 1983–84 UEFA Cup. He was especially known at the club for his free kicks and spectacular goals. Rasmussen left Anderlecht in August 1983, having captained the team since 1981, and returned to AGF, where he played an additional four seasons. His last professional match was in July 1987, as AGF won the 1987 Danish Cup. After his playing career ended in 1987, Rasmussen became a coach in 1988, selecting young talents and helping them reach the professional level. He managed AGF and the Faroe Islands national team between 1994 and 1996, then returned to AGF in 1997, helping the team win the 1999 Danish Cup. Rasmussen was named AGF's director of football in 2011. Rasmussen was a member of the Denmark national under-21 team between 1974 and 1976. He was not capped for the Denmark national team, but was included in the team's callup on two occasions in 1974. Rasmussen is married to Lotte and has three children. He is also an ambassador for AGF, as well as a consultant for Danish Football Association.

Doultabad, Bishnupur is a village located in the state of West Bengal, India, within the district of Bankura. It is situated in the tehsil of Bishnupur, in the bank of Jari River. The village is quite small, with an estimated population of around 5,000 people. The primary language spoken is Bengali, and the villagers participate in several agricultural activities, including farming, fishing, and livestock keeping. The village borders a large pond, making it an important source of irrigation for the villagers. The village is known for its own unique culture, which includes vivid traditional costumes, folk dances, and folk music. The villagers often participate in festivals like Dasain, Eid, and Holi, both of which are celebrated with great enthusiasm. The main deity worshipped in the village is Maa Tarini, and the village holds an annual festival in her honor every year. The event is known as the Durga Puja, and involves the whole village in preparation and festivities. The village also contains several schools, all of which focus on providing quality education to the children of Doultabad, Bishnupur. The village is served by two government-run schools, a primary school and a middle school. The village is also home to a few small, privately-run business establishments, including a catering service, a sewing business, and a small medical clinic. The medical clinic is run by a highly experienced doctor and other medical professionals, offering quality care to people in the village. Doultabad, Bishnupur is a close-knit community, with a strong sense of tradition and culture. The villagers are warm and welcoming, and are always happy to help visitors from outside their village. The village is a beautiful place to visit, especially in the spring and summer months, when the rice fields and ponds burst with vibrant colours. For visitors looking for a unique cultural experience, Doultabad, Bishnupur is an ideal destination. The amazing culture and hospitality of the villagers will ensure a memorable visit for tourists.

Machi is a Korean hip hop group formed by rapper OH (Oh Hyuk) and DJ Tukutz. The duo debuted in 2012 through the release of the extended play Just Music. Machine is signed MHN Entertainment, a subsidiary of LOEN Entertainment. OH was originally a solo artist and released his first EP "When I See You Again" in 2011. Later that year, he became a member of the hip hop group Soul Company with 3 other rappers. Apart from rapping, he also featured as a songwriter and producer. In 2012, he left Soul Company to focus on his solo career and formed a duo with DJ Tukutz, formerly a part of pioneering hip hop group Epik High. DJ Tukutz is a DJ, musician, and composer. He was a part of the renowned hip hop group Epik High for 10 years until 2013. He has produced and composed multiple tracks for artists such as Nell, Haha, and 2AM's Lim Seulong. He has also been featured as a guest rapper on several albums and singles by other artists. The name Machi is derived from the syllables of OH and Tukutz, which are 메 (Oh) and 치 (Tukutz). The duo's music reflects the eclectic range of their music influences, combining hip-hop, jazz, funk, blues, soul, and more. Since their debut, Machi has established a loyal fanbase. They have released two more EPs since their debut and have gone on several concert and tour dates in Korea and Japan. In 2014, they were invited to SXSW to represent South Korea. They were also part of the lineup for the premier Korean hip-hop festival Show Me the Money in 2014 and 2015. In 2017, Machi held their international tour "Machi Time World Tour" with 8 stops in North America and Europe, including New York, Los Angeles, Paris, London, and Toronto. The duo has also collaborated with artists such as Gaeko of Dynamic Duo, Primary, and Sik-K. Machi is one of the few Korean hip hop acts nominated for the Korean Music Awards, with their song "빛나는거리" ("Shining Streets") nominated for Best Rap Performance in 2013. In 2014, they were nominated for two awards, Best Rap/Hip Hop Album and Best R&B/Soul Song. They have also been nominated for the Korean Hip-Hop Awards multiple times. Machi has made numerous appearances on radio shows and television shows and are considered one of the top hip hop groups in Korea. The duo continues to produce and write music, tour internationally, and collaborate with fellow musicians and artist.

Alexander Laing (15 June 1788 – 3 November 1869) was a Scottish surgeon, naturalist and writer. Born near Inverness, Laing initially studied physical science at the University of Edinburgh, graduating in 1808, although he lacked the degree required to practice medicine. After several years of study he obtained his doctorate in medicine in 1815, and a few years later was made a Fellow of the Royal College of Surgeons. In the winter of 1817, Laing was in contact with the zoologist William Jardine and arranged for the publication of his book entitled Introduction to the Knowledge and Study of Natural History. Laing's interest in natural history soon outweighed his medical responsibilities and he travelled extensively, compiling a comprehensive collection of plants and animals in Scotland, England, Wales and Ireland. Laing's best-known work, On the Habits and Instincts of Animals, was published in 1822 and investigated many species of animals with the aim of discovering more information about their behaviour. The book was widely acclaimed in Britain and Europe, and Laing was made a Fellow of the Royal Society and was invited to deliver research papers at both the Linnean Society of London and the Zoological Society of London. In 1827, in order to further his knowledge of animals, Laing set off on a two-year voyage to South America and the Island of St. Helena, where he explored the tropical rainforests, gathering specimens that he brought back with him to Britain. These specimens included numerous reptiles and birds, as well as many other species of animals not previously seen in Britain. Following his expedition to the tropics, Laing became the first professor of natural history at the University of Aberdeen. During this time, he continued his studies of animals, writing further works such as A Practical Treatise on the Different Species of Spiders (1837) and A Short Account of the Different Species of Mammals, with Descriptions of their Habits and Habitations (1839). Laing's zoological and natural history studies left a lasting legacy. He was a member of the British Association for the Advancement of Science from 1823, and served on its Council from 1845 to 1849, where he undertook many initiatives that improved the association's collections. Laing was also involved in the protection of endangered animals and the preservation of endangered species and habitats. Alexander Laing's passion for observing animals and appreciating their behaviour was greatly respected by his colleagues, making him one of the foremost pioneers of modern zoology. He died on 3 November 1869.

Travel Companion Exchange is a website that helps travelers find others with similar interests for companionship and communication. It is an online platform connecting travelers from around the world with each other. The website allows users to connect with potential travel companions, share advice and make the most of their travels. Travel Companion Exchange was established in 2015 by two friends, Lilian and Jack, who had a strong desire to facilitate easier and far-reaching connections while traveling around the world. Through the platform, they wanted to help make the traveling experience more enjoyable, meaningful and meaningful connections with people. At the time, traditional methods such as offline travel groups or forums weren't proving to be effective enough. Travel Companion Exchange has grown over the years and now has over 100,000 members worldwide who have used the website to connect with people from over 180 countries. The website connects travelers with each other by asking questions such as the traveler’s home country, which country they’re from, languages spoken, and other interests. Through this, the website is able to match travelers with each other depending on their interests and background. In addition to connecting travelers with each other, Travel Companion Exchange also provides a platform for members to share tips and blog about their travel experiences. They also help travelers find activities or events in their destination cities. Furthermore, the website encourages people to make connections and friendships with fellow travelers to explore their than countries and cultures. Travelers can join the Travel Companion Exchange by signing up and creating a profile on the website. The website is free to join and is available in both English and Spanish. They also offer a premium membership with additional features. The website is used by travelers from all different backgrounds, from students to backpackers to professionals. The mission of the Travel Companion Exchange is to make traveling more social, enjoyable, and memorable for all those who use it. It aims to create an online platform for travelers where they can find others with similar interests and backgrounds. Through the platform, travelers are then able to share experiences, advice, and make memorable connections with each other.

The Battle of Smolensk (French: Bataille de Smolensk) was a major battle between the Imperial French Invasion of Russia under Napoleon and the Russian Army commanded by General Barclay de Tolly on 16-18 August 1812. It was the first major battle after the French invasion of Russia began and marked the beginning of the Patriotic War of 1812. The battle took place near the city of Smolensk and resulted in a French victory. The Russians suffered heavy losses with more than 18,000 killed or wounded and another 5,000 captured by the French. This was the first significant French victory in the Invasion of Russia, and it allowed the French to capture the city of Smolensk and occupy most of western Russia. The French were able to advance to the Russian capital of Moscow and their control of Smolensk fueled fears of a possible encirclement of the Russian Army and a potential end to the war.
