Napoleon's initial aim in the campaign had been to threaten St. Petersburg in order to draw Russian forces away from the Polish front; this aim had been achieved and the French had proceeded further into central Russia. To counter this move the Russians had moved their armies to the east, but it was too late. The French had already crossed the Dnieper, and had reached the banks of the Vop river, in the vicinity of Smolensk, by the 15th of August. The Imperial French Army had reached a strength of about 500,000 men, 230,000 of whom had crossed the Dnieper and were facing the larger Russian army numbering around 310,000 men. Both sides deployed in a line stretching from Vyazma to the western bank of the Vop river, with Barclay de Tolly in command of the Russians. Napoleon's plan was to attack on the flanks and split the Russian army in two, then attack the northern sector with a majority of his forces while sending a smaller intercepted of cavalry, 20,000 men under marshal Pierre-Nicolas Lahure, to the south to block the communication between the two halves. Throughout the entire day of the 16 August, and the whole next day of the 17 August, the French heavily attacked the outnumbered Russian forces, and on the 18th the French finally managed to break the Russian lines. Barclay de Tolly attempted to retreat, but was blocked from the road to Moscow. He was eventually forced to retreat further east to Borodino, where the decisive Battle of Borodino would take place just a week later. The Battle of Smolensk was the first major victory for the French in the war, and it would be the impetus that pushed Napoleon to push harder and fight his way to Moscow. Although short, the battle resulted in heavy casualties for both sides and is an important date in the history of the French invasion of 1812.

Advice to a Friend on Choosing a Mistress is a book published in 1745 by the English philosopher and satirist Jonathan Swift. Originally published anonymously, the book outlines what Swift believes are basic principles for a man to keep in mind when establishing a romantic relationship outside of marriage. The book has long been considered an early feminist work, as it was written at a time when women's equality was not widely accepted. Swift begins the book with an introduction for the reader, giving advice about why one should consider a mistress. He argues that since men are expected to maintain an upper-class lifestyle, they must choose women who can contribute to that lifestyle--women of "rank, fortune, beauty, and discretion." In this way, he presents the mistress as a financial partner, an enterprise that benefits both the man and the woman. In the following chapters, Swift outlines the qualities he believes will make a woman successful in her role. He advises his readers to seek out women of fortune, beauty, and understanding; he also insists that the man be a gentleman, respectful of the woman's intelligence, dignity and authority. Swift also cautions men to be careful in their selection of a mistress, reminding them that infidelity can have serious repercussions. Throughout the book, Swift emphasizes the importance of mutual respect and kindness between the man and the woman. He condemns women who take advantage of men, as well as men who take advantage of women. He also speaks out against domestic abuse and encourages emotional openness between partners. In this way, he stands in stark contrast to many of his peers, advocating for a form of partnership that is equal and balanced. Advice to a Friend on Choosing a Mistress is a valuable guide for both men and women to consider when entering a romantic relationship. It stands as an early example of feminist advice, demonstrating Swift's awareness of the power dynamics between individuals and the importance of mutual understanding and respect in a romantic relationship. References: 1. Jonathan Swift, Advice to a Friend on Choosing a Mistress, 1745. 2. Betty S. Flowers, "Jonathan Swift and the Feminist Philosophy of Relationships," Studies in English Literature, 1550-1900, vol. 3, no. 3, Autumn 1963, pp. 381-390. 3. Pamela Kleibrink Thompson, “On Swift’s Advice to a Friend on Choosing a Mistress,” Explicator, vol. 48, no. 2, Winter 1990, pp. 52-54.

Koupaki (Greek: Κουπάκι) is a seaside village in the Phocis region of central Greece. It is located on the eastern shore of the Gulf of Corinth, approximately 12 km south of Delphi and 4 km west of Galaxidi. In antiquity, the area surrounding the present-day village was known as Erineos, named after the eponymous ancient greek city located on the promontory of the same name, which is now an uninhabited plateau between Koupaki and Galaxidi. Koupaki has been inhabited continuously since at least the Byzantine period, with some archaeological evidence for settlement as far back as the 2nd century AD. The modern village was founded in the 15th century by Greek fishermen from northwest Peloponese. It has since grown to around 1000 inhabitants, mainly engaged in tourism and fishing. The village itself consists of two main settlements, the larger of which is built along the sand covered shoreline, and a smaller one of seasonal dwellings further up the hill. It's characterized by narrow cobblestone pathways, old stone churches and traditional white-washed houses. The port of Koupaki is the main economic activity of the village, serving fishing vessels, sailing boats and small ferries that link the area to Delphi and Galaxidi. There are also several cafes and small restaurants which serve traditional greek specialities. Koupaki is popular with tourists looking to explore the nearby archaeological sites, including Delphi and Erineos. It is also a popular spot for sunbathing among locals and tourists alike, as well as a hub for water sports activities. In the late spring, Koupaki is the setting for the Pan-Hellenic triathlon, comprising of a 2000 meter swim in the gulf, a 15 km bike ride and a 5 km run around the village and the surrounding hillsides. The event has been held every year since 1993. Koupaki is also known for its picturesque sunsets, which are visible from the beach and nearby promontories. The postcard view of the setting sun and the small boats silhouetted against the horizon has become well known amongst travelers. Today, Koupaki has become an ideal destination for rural Greek tourism, offering a plethora of activities for visitors, such as bicycle tours, sailing trips, activities on the beach and nearby archaeological sites. The village also boasts a variety of traditional guesthouses, small family hotels and apartment rentals. Koupaki is well connected to the nearby cities and villages of Delphi, Galaxidi, Amfissa and Itea via public buses, as well as the sea port of Agios Konstantinos. There are also daily ferry services to the island of Evia.

Utricularia andongensis, commonly known as the Andong bladderwort, is a species of aquatic carnivorous plant in the family Lentibulariaceae. It is native to Thailand and Cambodia, where it is found in swamps, ditches, and streams. U. Andongensis is a very small bladderwort, typically no more than 1–2 cm in size. Its floating stems are anchored in the substrate with numerous fine roots, and bear a number of small, globular bladders, arising singly or in pairs. Each bladder is enclosed in a pair of purplish-brown, feathery "leaves". It is pollinated by small insects attracted to the bright yellow flowers, which appear from mid-winter to mid-spring. U. Andongensis is considered to be of conservation concern and is listed as ‘Vulnerable’ on the IUCN Red List. The primary threats to this species are habitat destruction or degradation due to human activities, such as shrimp farming and pollution from agricultural runoff. The species is also threatened by over-collecting for the ornamental plant trade. To ensure the survival of U. Andongensis in its natural range, there is a need for habitat protection, habitat restoration, and measures to reduce the impacts of pollution. U. Andongensis is an attractive and relatively easy-to-cultivate species in aquaria and water gardens. It is usually grown in an aquatic habitat, with fairly strong light. The aquarium should be supplied with lots of fine-leaved aquatic plants to provide habitat for the small insects needed to pollinate the flowers. Maintaining suitable water quality and temperature is important, with temperatures between 20 and 24°C (68–75°F) being ideal. In addition, the aquarium should be regularly fertilized with a liquid fertilizer to provide additional nutrients. Despite its threatened status, U. Andongensis is still available in the ornamental plant trade, both in specialist nurseries and for sale online. It is, however, recommended that plants purchased for aquaria or water gardens should come from sustainably cultivated sources, to help preserve wild populations of this species. Utricularia andongensis, is an unusual and rewarding species for aquarists and water gardeners alike, and its conservation is of great importance. With appropriate care and suitable conditions, this species can be grown successfully in captivity, helping to ensure its future.

Yabba Dabba Doo! is an iconic catchphrase which originated in the American animated television series The Flintstones, the first major primetime animated series on television. It is typically used as a celebration of good times and was most famously uttered by the show’s main protagonist Fred Flintstone when excited. In addition to its use in The Flintstones, the phrase has become a popular cultural reference, with multiple uses in popular media and merchandise. The Flintstones aired for six seasons on ABC from 1960 to 1966, and was created by Hanna-Barbera Productions. Released in the same era as The Simpsons, it is believed to have greatly contributed to the success of primetime animation in the United States. The Flintstones centered around the Stone Age adventures of the titular family, who lived in the fictional town of Bedrock. and were comprised of Fred Flintstone, the breadwinner and husband, Wilma Flintstone, his wife, Pebbles Flintstone, their young daughter and Dino, their pet dinosaur. The catchphrase “Yabba Dabba Doo!” was introduced into the show in 1962 by Fred’s character as a way to express joy and excitement, and was said in reaction to moments like a successful golf swing or a beneficial spin in a game of chance. As the series progressed, the phrase began to take on a life of its own, appearing in promotional materials and other pieces of media outside of the show, such as statues and buttons. In addition to becoming a cultural icon in its own right, the saying has made appearances in various movies and television programs over the years. It was most recently used in an episode of the TV show Futurama, as well as an episode of The Simpsons. It has also been featured in songs and video games, such as in an update to the classic game Worms in which a character exclaims “Yabba Dabba Doo!” after victory. As well as its appearance in pop culture, the phrase has also been used to name various clothing brands, toys and other products. In 2010, a popular online clothing store, Yabba Dabba Doo!, was opened in the United Kingdom, and has since expanded to several countries over the years. The phrase has also been used in advertising campaigns and as the name of a beer brand produced by the American brewing company, Anheuser-Busch. In conclusion, “Yabba Dabba Doo!” has become an iconic phrase which has been embraced by the general public as a lighthearted way to show enthusiasm or happiness. Despite its humble origins in the 1960’s, the phrase has been adopted by modern cultures and is now used in various pieces of media, products, and advertisements.

The National Museum of Contemporary Art, Athens, commonly referred to as EMST, is a nationally funded museum located in Athens, Greece. Founded in 2000, EMST is the premier museum for current Greek and international art. The museum's collection spans a wide variety of artistic mediums, from photography, painting and sculpture to video, performance and installation art. The museum is home to many groundbreaking and interdisciplinary projects that have been praised around the world. Located in the historic Faliro Delta, EMST was first opened as an information and documentation centre in 2000. The centre also hosted temporary exhibitions by some of the leading artists of the time. In 2007, EMST was declared a national museum of modern art, and since then, the museum has expanded significantly. Currently, the museum occupies more than 35,000 square meters, with three permanent and rotating exhibits. As well as the nine-storey main building, EMST is home to the restored Stavros Niarchos Art Center, which houses a library, workshops, an auditorium, and a shop. The EMST Summer Academy also operates from May to October and acts as an art school for budding local and international artists, and a learning space for children. The museum’s collections feature an array of 20th and 21st century art by both established and emerging Greek artists. The vast collection is presented in the form of solo and group exhibitions that cover a broad spectrum of topics, from identity and history to gender and immigration. In addition, EMST has a number of special performances, talks, and events throughout the year. Aside from hosting its own curated exhibitions, the museum also has collaborations with some of the leading art venues around the world. EMST is also home to, and hosts, the ARRES residence program, which invites international artists and curators to collaborate, create, and present their work in Athens. The museum also serves as a cultural hub for education, providing educational activities for young audiences and hosting artist residencies. Located close to Athens’ thriving art scene, EMST is a hub for culture, education, and creativity in Greece. With an expansive digital resource, diverse exhibitions, and educational activities, EMST is one of the leading contemporary art museums in the world.

West Liberty Foods is an American processing company that specializes in the production of custom-made poultry, pork, and beef products. It is based in West Liberty, Iowa and is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Japanese food manufacturer Nipponham Group. West Liberty Foods was founded in 1996 by Duane Hosek, a poultry processing industry veteran. The company currently produces and delivers custom-made poultry, pork, and beef products to various customers ranging from retail to food service. It also manufactures cooked poultry entrées and delicatessen salads. The company's main processing plant is located in West Liberty, Iowa with other facilities located in Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, and North Carolina. It employs over 3,000 people and has operated two processing plants using state-of-the-art technology. West Liberty Foods is a leader in the deli-chicken and deli-beef industries with the ability to provide a wide variety of products that are fully cooked, sliced, and diced. The company is focused on quality, custom-made products, tailored to the specific needs of their customers. It works closely with its customers to ensure that the highest quality products are produced. The company is a GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice) and SQF (Safe Quality Food Program) certified processor and employs the HACCP (Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point) program in its facilities. It is also registered as a USDA inspection agency. West Liberty Foods prides itself on its commitment to collaboration, customer service, and product safety. The company works diligently with its customers to develop custom solutions that meet their needs. West Liberty Foods customers are not only able to rely on the quality of the products, but also on the safe preparation and processing. Overall, West Liberty Foods is a reliable and successful American poultry and meat processing company that produces quality products that customers across the US can trust. It is dedicated to providing excellent customer service and continuously improving its processes and products.

Hon’inbō Shūei (本因坊秀栄, 1863 – 1933) was one of the greatest of all professional Go players. During his career, he developed a number of influential playing styles that remain important today. Shūei was born in 1863 to a family of Go professionals in Kyoto, Japan. His father, Hon'inbō Shūhaku, tutored him in the game from an early age. His father died when he was 11, but Shūei continued to practice Go with his father’s pupils. At the age of 12, he moved to Tokyo and entered the service of the Maruyama family, who were also Go professionals. He remained with the Maruyama House for the rest of his life. In 1883, at the age of 20, he became the 10th Hon’inbō, a hereditary title that was awarded to the best Go player in Japan at the time. During his career, Hon’inbō Shūei won several major tournament titles, including the first Japan Professional Go Championship held in 1898. He was also a noted teacher, writing the book Intensive Go Study (1897) and inventing the Shūsei joseki (opening moves) which has been adopted as the standard for modern Go play. He also founded the Hon’inbō School, the first of its kind in Japan. Though Hon’inbō Shūei passed away in 1933 at the age of 70, his legacy continues to be felt in the game of Go. Professionals and amateurs alike continue to study his strategies and games, seeking to emulate his success. He is honoured as one of the greats of professional Go, and his influence can be seen even in the modern game.

Yo Baby is an American rapper from Los Angeles, California. He is best known for his hit single, "Yo Baby Remix," which was released in 2017 and peaked at number 5 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100. Yo Baby was born Christopher Thorne on April 25, 1995 in Los Angeles, California. He started his music career at age 14, performing at local talent shows and clubs. He moved to Los Angeles in 2017 to pursue music professionally and was soon signed to Interscope Records. Yo Baby's debut single, "Go Get It," was released in 2017 and quickly gained recognition, peaking at number 59 on the US Billboard Hot 100. The second single, "Yo Baby Remix," was even more successful, becoming a hit all over the world, charting in over 13 countries and reaching number 5 on the US Billboard Hot 100. In 2018, Yo Baby released his debut EP, 'The Getup'. The EP includes three previously released singles and features appearances from Western, Chris Brown, and J-Lo. The EP was well-received, peaking at number 12 on the US Music chart and selling over 500,000 copies. Yo Baby has since gone on to collaborate with a number of high-profile artists, including Lil Wayne, Rick Ross, YG, and Ty Dolla Sign. He also released his debut album, 'Moneymaker', in 2020. The album peaked at number 3 on the US Music chart and featured the hit single "Live for the Night," which was certified triple-platinum. Today, Yo Baby is one of the most popular rappers in the United States. His songs have been streamed over 1 billion times and have earned him awards such as a Grammy, an American Music Award, and MTV Video Music Awards. He has also been featured on the covers of magazines such as XXL and The Source.

Des Ball (born April 26, 1982) is an Australian football (soccer) coach and former player. Ball is a former member of the Australian National Football Team, making his debut in 2004. He made over 50 appearances for the national team and helped the Socceroos to qualify for the 2006 FIFA World Cup in Germany. He also represented Australia in two Asian Cup campaigns, in 2004 and 2007, and was a member of the squad that won the OFC Nation’s Cup in 2008. He was named Oceania Footballer of the Year in 2005. Ball began his club career as a junior at Blacktown City in 1999, playing in the NSW Premier League until 2003. After a brief stint at League of Ireland club Longford Town, Ball joined Sydney FC in 2005 and went on to make over 50 appearances in the A-League over three seasons. Ball went on to play with several clubs in Australia and the United Kingdom, including Melbourne Victory, Melbourne Heart, Leicester City and Kent United F.C. In 2014, Ball ended his professional career and returned to coaching. Ball started his coaching career at Victoria's Olympic (National Premier Leagues) team, Box Hill United SC, in 2013. In 2015, Ball moved to the Australian Institute of Sport to work as an assistant coach, and then in 2016 he moved to New Zealand to become the Assistant Technical Director at Auckland Football Federation. Ball currently holds the position of Technical Director at Football Federation Northern Territory. In addition to his coaching roles, Ball has held several roles in football development. He is a member of the Australian Technical Directors Network, and has coached in numerous football clinics across Australia and New Zealand. He also served as an assistant coach for the Newcastle Jets Academy team from 2017-18, before moving to the Northern Territory in 2019. Ball is an avid traveller and is passionate about inspiring the next generation of footballers. He is involved in several youth football initiatives and organisations, including Football United, which is an international community football organisation with a focus on culture, health and social integration. He currently resides in Darwin and he is a fan of the Darwin Rovers Football Club. He also holds coaching qualifications from the Football Federation Australia (FIFA Pro) and Football Coaches Australia (A-License).

Felicitas and Gonzalo Mendez High School is a public high school in Los Angeles, California. It is located in the Pico-Union neighborhood of Los Angeles. It is operated by the Los Angeles Unified School District, and is part of the Los Angeles High School district. Felicitas and Gonzalo Mendez High School did not exist until after 1988 when it was approved as a new, comprehensive high school by the LAUSD Board of Education in response to overcrowding at nearby Garfield and Roosevelt high schools. The school was named after a the husband and wife duo, Felicitas and Gonzalo Mendez, for their roles in the Mendez v. Westminster court case, which established Mexican American desegregation in California schools. The current enrollment stands at around 500 and the school has four small academies: * Academy of Business, Entrepreneurship, and Technology (ABET) * Academy of Law, Human Services and Education (ALHSE) * Academy of Medical Science and Public Service (AMPS) * Academy of Arts and Global Communication (AAGC) The school also boasts a unique student-teacher program which features teachers from nearby elementary schools serving as mentors for students at Mendez. The sports teams at Mendez are known as the Wildcats and they offer various team sports. A variety of clubs are also available, such as Art Club, Debate and Robotics. Mendez also has an award-winning marching band. In addition to improved academic offerings, Mendez has recently become more involved in the community, and offers enrichment activities, such as language courses, music and theater classes, and a variety of community-focused programs. The school also offers career technical education and fourth year electives including: advanced design and development, project-based learning, media and classroom technology, algebra, Spanish, and ESL. The principal of the school is Richard Alatorre, who has been with the school since 2010. Under Alatorre's leadership, the school has seen several improvements, including higher graduation rates, better attendance, and a decrease in suspension rates. The future of the school depends largely on continued improvements and creating a stronger community for students. With increased focus on student safety, academic programs, extracurricular activities, and career education, the future of Mendez High School looks brighter than ever.

Park Hyeon-Joo (born January 1,1992) is a South Korean actress. She started her career in the entertainment industry by being a model, then making her acting debut in 2012. She has since went on to star in several successful television series, short films and web series. Park was born and raised in South Chungcheong Province, South Korea. She attended Seoul Arts University where she graduated in 2014 with a degree in Theater. During her time at the university, Park participated in many plays, theatrical works and participated in university festivals. After completing her education, Park set out to become an actress. In 2012, Park made her acting debut in the television series Hello Counselor as guest star. She then landed a recurring role as the female protagonist in I Live in Cheongdam-dong, which premiered in 2013. This marked her first major role in a television series. She then went on to make further TV appearances in All About My Mom and Six Flying Dragons. In 2016, Park appeared in the short film Rambling, where she played the lead, Ahn Sol-bin. This was followed by her first feature film role in The King's Case Note, where she played the female protagonist Son Hong-yi. Park starred in the 2017 web drama series Love Playlist, where she starred opposite actor and singer Kim Min-gyu. The series was a huge success and earned Park a lot of recognition. Following her success in Love Playlist, Park went on to appear in the Netflix original series Love Alarm in 2019, playing the female protagonist Lee Hye-young. Park has also appeared in various music videos and has released several singles. She released the single I Hate It in 2018, which peaked at number 4 on the Gaon Digital Chart. She also participated in OSTs for the shows Rambling and Love Alarm. In 2020, Park appeared in the lead role in the web drama Ctrl + S, where she played the aspiring journalist Hwang Ga-rim. Park is currently working on upcoming projects, including the film 8 Seconds which is scheduled for release in 2021. In addition to her work in the entertainment industry, Park also engages in philanthropic activities. She supported single mothers in need through a donation made in 2018. Park is also an active supporter of animal rights and a volunteer for an animal rescue organization in South Korea. Park Hyeon-Joo is a rising talent in the South Korean entertainment industry. Having been in the business for over eight years, Park has proven herself to be a successful and versatile actress, and continues to shine with her performances both on-screen and off.

The Methodist Episcopal Society of Tyringham is a society dedicated to preserving and sharing the history of the Methodist Episcopal Church in the community of Tyringham, Massachusetts. Founded in 1817 by the local circuit riders, the society is one of the oldest Methodism societies in the United States. The Methodist Episcopal Church began to take shape in Tyringham as early as 1790 when Jesse Lee began his mission of visiting local homes in the area. This became a semi-organized mission shortly after when the Rev. John Allen from the power of the Woodbury Circuit in Connecticut visited Tyringham. On November 11th, 1817, the first Methodist Episcopal Society of Tyringham Church was officially organized after a full afternoon of church services. The congregation quickly grew and by the early 1900s was one of the most influential denominations in the town. The society today continues to keep the mission alive with educational and service opportunities. Through their efforts, the Methodist Episcopal Society of Tyringham has been able to preserve records and materials that provide insight into the history of the church and its influence on the community. They are working to restore and maintain the chapel on the society’s property, which dates back to 1826. The chapel is the last remaining Methodist Episcopal chapel in Tyringham. The Society offers a variety of instructional and volunteer activities related to their history and mission. This includes hosting guest speakers, field trips, church services, and seminars and workshops. For those interested in the history of Methodism, the society has created a museum and library, both of which hold numerous books, artifacts, and documents pertaining to the local church and its people. Additionally, the society operates a youth group and Sunday school for adolescents to promote the Methodist Episcopal's teachings and values. The Methodist Episcopal Society of Tyringham has a long standing history of outreach and service. Each year, the society collects food, clothing, and other items for local charitable organizations and for those in need. They also partner with other local churches and organizations to provide support and guidance to members of the community. Through their efforts to honor the past, the Society continues to make a difference in the present and in the future of the Methodist Episcopal Church in Tyringham and beyond.

Clara Louise Burnham (1860 - 1917) was an American writer and lyricist. She is best known for her collection of poems and verses for children, which were highly praised for their beauty and charm. Burnham was born in 1860 in Kingston, New York, to William J. and Julia A. Burnham. Her mother was a well-known singing teacher, and taught her daughter from a young age. Burnham started publishing her poetry in newspapers by the age of 11. At 17, she moved to New York City, where she wrote for various magazines. Burnham quickly gained recognition as a skilled poet, and in 1881, she published her first book of verse, Sylvan Songs. The book was an immediate success and established her as a major writer. Her writing was praised by leading literary figures of the time, including Walt Whitman, Thomas Bailey Aldrich, and Edward Everett Hale. Over the next several years, Burnham wrote several more books of poetry and children's verses, which were widely anthologized. In addition to her poetry and literature, Burnham was also an accomplished linguist, translating works from French and German into English. She was also a frequent contributor to the music industry, writing lyrics for a variety of songs in different genres. Burnham passed away in 1917 at the age of 57. She was survived by a sister, a brother and two children. Burns' works continue to be read to this day and remain a celebrated part of the American literary canon.

Meharia is a small village located in the Banasath district of Uttar Pradesh, India. It is situated on the banks of the Ganges River and is home to about five hundred people. The history of Meharia dates back to the medieval period when the land was owned by the local Thakur family. The village has been known for its unique culture and architecture for centuries. The traditional mud-huts with thatched roofs house the villagers who are generally involved in subsistence farming. The village is also known for its natural beauty with several waterfalls and a wide variety of flora and fauna. The village is famous for its vibrant festivals, mainly Basanti Poojan, which is held on the first day of the year according to the Hindu calendar. The village is also home to several educational institutions. The main school is the Government Primary School, which is attended by most of the children from the village. The school has been in existence for more than sixty years and provides basic education for up to class 8. Meharia is also known for its ancient temples, the most prominent being the Meharia Shiv Mandir. It is said to be more than three centuries old and was built in honor of the Hindu God Shiva. The temple has several idols of Hindu gods and goddesses and houses several ancient manuscripts which have been passed down through generations. In recent years, Meharia has also been developing its infrastructure. The roads have been improved, and local businesses such as shops, banks and medical centers have been established. There are also plans to develop a housing complex in the village which will bring in more amenities and resources to the inhabitants. Overall, Meharia is an important landmark in the district of Banasath and is cherished for its unique culture, traditions, natural beauty and history. Despite the development, the villagers of Meharia continue to keep alive their ancient heritage and strive to keep their indigenous culture alive.

Cheryl S. McWatters is a Canadian business scholar, university professor, and administrator. She is the past President and Vice-Chancellor of the Royal Military College of Canada and is a Vice-President of the Business and Higher Education Roundtable. McWatters is particularly renowned for her work in financial and economic analysis, a field she has devoted herself to for over 35 years. She has made considerable contributions to the fields of strategic management, and international business and finance. In 2009, McWatters was appointed a fellow of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants. McWatters received her undergraduate and graduate degrees in business and economics from the University of Waterloo and Queen's University, respectively. She then went on to earn a master's degree in international business from Queen's University in 1989, and a doctorate of business administration degree in 2003. McWatters has worked in industry, consulting in the area of financial and economic analysis. She has been a leader in the development of financial methodologies and techniques for the investment, planning, and control of business operations. McWatters teaches and conducts research in a variety of areas including economics, finance, strategic management, economic analysis, financial markets and business strategies. Her research focuses on international capital markets, financial and economic risk modeling, and investment portfolios. In 2009, McWatters was appointed President and Vice-Chancellor of the Royal Military College of Canada (RMC). She was the first woman to hold this position and served until 2018. During her term she championed new academic programmes and the advancement of research initiatives in areas such as artificial intelligence and strategic management. In 2019 McWatters joined the Business and Higher Education Roundtable as a Vice-President. The Roundtable’s mission is to enhance links between academia and business. McWatters was appointed to the Order of Canada in 2013 for her “contributions to higher education and financial management”. McWatters has made a substantial impact in academia and in Canadian higher education. She has served on a number of boards and committees of universities, professional and business associations, and government agencies. McWatters continues to serve and advise on numerous boards, committees, and organisations in both the public and private sectors.

Sonnia Agu (born January 1, 1990) is a Nigerian journalist and writer who focuses on issues of democracy and development in Africa. She has written extensively on the topics of political corruption, economic development, gender, education and human rights. Agu studied economics and finance at the University of Nigeria, Nimbo. She also did a year of postgraduate studies in Advanced Leadership and Social Responsibility at the Konrad Adenauer Foundation in Germany. In 2013, Agu founded Nigeria's first feminist think-tank - the Nigerian Institute for Women in Politics (NIWP). NIWP promotes women's rights and political inclusion for all citizens, especially those in marginalized communities. The organization provides mentorship to young women seeking political office and has advocated for greater representation of women at the local and national levels. Agu is a former editor-in-chief of Nigeria's Daily Star newspaper. During her tenure as editor, the newspaper reported extensively on issues of public accountability and transparency. She has written for a variety of publications, including The Guardian, The New York Times, CNN, and the BBC. Agu is a vocal advocate for social change in Africa. She speaks at various conferences around the world on topics of democracy and economic development. In January 2020, she was named the keynote speaker at the Global Youth Summit in Nigeria. In her speech, Agu highlighted the importance of youth engagement in democratic processes, stating that “we need to actively participate in the political process to ensure that our voices are heard and our needs are met. We need to build a country where young people are not just seen but are also empowered to make meaningful changes.” Agu has received various awards and recognitions for her work. In 2017, she was named as one of the BBC's 100 Most Influential African Women. She is also a recipient of the 2019 World Bank Development Leadership Award. Agu is a passionate defender of freedom of expression and a fierce opponent of misrule and impunity in Africa. She is a strong believer in the power of youth activism to bring about social and political change in the continent.

Jane Thorne (b. 1828-d. 1900) was a British botanical artist who is best known for her illustrations of ferns and other plants, as well as her depictions of animal species. She was born in Yorkshire and studied under the tutelage of botanical artist and lithographer Paul Ferdinand Willman. Thorne's work focused on providing accurate, detailed renderings of the plants she came across, often collaborated with botanists and naturalists, such as Charles Gordon Bennett, who assisted with the identification of species. Her work was highly regarded from her contemporaries and by researchers, who found her work incredibly useful and important. During her lifetime Thorne produced numerous watercolour illustrations, many of which were collected and published in volumes such as: A Monograph of the British Fossil Rove Beetles (1868) by Charles Gordon Bennett and Daniel Edward Home; A Synopsis of British Fungi (1871) by the Rev. Miles Joseph Berkeley; and Fungi of Great Britain and Ireland (1874–1886). Her illustrations featured in a number of other botanical works and in important publications such as British Ferns (1848) by Edward Charles Jeffrey, and British Mosses (1857) by Edward Charles Jeffrey. During her career, Thorne collaborated with countless esteemed botanists and naturalists such as George James Allman and William Henry Harvey. Regional natural history museums across the globe, including the Natural History Museum in London, Canada's Royal Ontario Museum, and the Field Museum in Chicago, hold a considerable number of Thoer's works in their collections. An exhibition dedicated to the artist was held in London at the Great Exhibition of 1898. Thorne was awarded a bronze medal for her watercolour artworks. She was also appointed an Associate of the Royal Botanic Garden, Edinburgh as well as a Member of the Linnean Society of London. Thorne died in 1900 and was buried in Kensal Green Cemetery, London. Despite her contributions to botanical illustration, she has largely been forgotten by history. Her contribution to the advancement of plant sciences, however, is still shrouded in mystery. Her legacy remains, as her works contain many of the details which are still totally relevant today.

HMCS Margaret Brooke (FFH-342) was a Royal Canadian Navy Halifax-class frigate that served from 1988 to 2009. She was the second ship to bear the name Margaret Brooke, the first being the Abercrombie-class frigate that served during the Second World War. The frigate was named for Rear-Admiral Margaret Brooke, the first woman to rise to a flag rank in the Canadian navy. The frigate first entered service in 1988 and underwent major upgrades from 1998-2002. During this time she was taken out of service and placed in "Extended Ready Reserve" (ERR). She went back in service in 2002 following her major refit and modernization, and served until 2009 when she was retired and transferred to Pakistan. The Halifax-class frigates are multi-role warships, designed to perform anti-submarine warfare (ASW), anti-surface warfare (ASUW), and anti-air warfare (AAW). They are outfitted with Sea Sparrow missiles, Surface-to-Air Harpoon launchers, an identification friend or foe system, and many other defence systems. Additionally, the frigates can accommodate one CH-124 Sea King helicopter. Margaret Brooke performed many duties during her service career, including coastal surveillance and convoy escort. In 2002 the frigate operated as part of Operation Apollo, the Canadian mission in the War in Afghanistan. The frigate also participated in several multi-national deployments, including a deployment to South America in 2006. In 2009 HMCS Margaret Brooke completed her final deployment as part of Operation Sentry in the Mediterranean Sea. She was then taken to Halifax Naval Dockyard, where she was prepared for her transfer to the Pakistani Navy in August 2009. In 2014, a decommissioned HMCS Margaret Brooke was presented to the citizens of Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, where it was put on display in Somba K’e Civic Plaza. In 2017, the frigate's remains were gathered and sold to a Pakistani firm in order to be salvaged and reused. HMCS Margaret Brooke will be remembered as a multi-mission frigate and a symbol of service and honour in the Royal Canadian Navy. Her legacy lives on as a reminder of the dedication, bravery and hard work of the thousands of sailors who served aboard her.

Minuscule 868 (in the Gregory-Aland numbering), ε1311 (Soden), is a Greek minuscule manuscript of the New Testament, on parchment, palimpseste. Palimpsest, in Greek, literally means ‘scraped clean’. It manuscript is dated palaeographically to the 12th century. The codex contains almost the complete Gospel of John and some lacunae in the other books. It is very lacunose at the end of each book. The manuscript is written in one column per page, 18 lines per page, in small letters. It contains the Ammonian Sections (in Mark 238, the Eusebian Canons (in Mark 12 - 16; Luke 17:10). The numbers of the κεφαλαια (chapters) are given at the margin, with their τιτλοι (titles) at top of the pages, for every section and for each book. There is no a division according to the smaller Ammonian Sections. It has a textual advantage over the more important Minuscule 88 and 157, by having an additional 113 reading found in no other early witnesses. The Greek text of the codex is the Byzantine. Aland placed it in Category V. It was written by the same scribe who wrote minuscule 866, 867, 869 after him. The manuscript was examined by Tischendorf, Jacob van Tatenhove, and later scribes and was included in the list of Tischendorf, Gregory-Aland, and the Claremont Profile Method. Currently the codex is housed at the Biblioteca Ambrosiana (F 96 sup. 6) in Milan. See also * List of New Testament minuscules * Hesychios's text of the Gospels * Biblical manuscript * Textual criticism Citations Bibliography * Gregor Friedländer, Die griechischen Handschriften des Neuen Testaments in der UdSSR: eine systematische Auswertung des Texthandschriften in Leningrad, Moskau, Kiev, Odessa, Tbilisi und Erevan, T & U 90 (Berlin: 1966), p. 218.

Cavanaquill is a fantastical magical creature from the folklore of South America. It is said to have the head of a horse and the body of a lion. It has three talons on each of its four feet, and it is often described as having a long mane, a tail, and a horn at the top of its head. The Cavanaquill is thought to bring good luck and protect the area it inhabits. In folklore, the Cavanaquill is a wise creature, often consulted by shamans and other wise people. It has the ability to speak, and is able to provide wise counsel when asked. It is also said to be able to transform itself into a bird or a beast, or to shapeshift into any other creature. The Cavanaquill is a figure in South American mythology and appears in numerous tales from Peru, Brazil, Colombia, and Ecuador. It is usually depicted as a powerful entity with a strong connection to nature. In some of the folklore, it is said to be the master of the winds and the rains, able to control the elements and affect weather patterns. It is also said to have a profound connection to spirits and to be able to communicate with them. In some stories, the Cavanaquill is seen as a guardian angel, sent to protect a land or a specific person. In other stories, it is a powerful being that can be manipulated and is sometimes associated with evil. The Cavanaquill is sometimes seen as a symbol of the unification of different cultures, as it often appears to be a combination of different animals. It has come to represent the diversity of culture that exists in South America. The Cavanaquill is often seen as a symbol of strength, courage, and protection. It is a popular creature in South American youth culture, and is used as a mascot in some communities. Many people believe that having a Cavanaquill as a companion can bring luck and protection. The Cavanaquill remains an important part of South American folklore, and continues to be seen as a protector and source of wisdom.

Brymbo F.C. is a Welsh football club based in the town of Brymbo, Wrexham County Borough. The club was founded in 1901 and currently competes in the Welsh National League (WNL) Division One South, the fifth tier of the Welsh football pyramid. The club plays its home matches at Brymbo Sports Complex, which has a capacity of 1,250. The club also owns a training ground near Y Wern. The club's colours are red, yellow and black and the club mascot is Byron the Bear. The club's most successful period began in 1948, when it won promotion to the Welsh National League Division One for the first time in its history. It won the division in 1951 and went on to win the Welsh Amateur Cup in 1953, allowing them to qualify for the FA of Wales Amateur Cup. Brymbo achieved fame in the 1961-62 season, when they reached the fourth round of the Welsh Cup, beating several higher-division teams along the way, before losing 4-1 to Shrewsbury Town. From the late 80s the club began struggling financially, leading to them entering the Wrexham and District League in 1992. They returned to the WNL first division in 2001 after spending several seasons in the lower divisions. The club has been regular participants in the Welsh Cup since their reformation in 2001, reaching the fourth round of the competition twice in 2007 and 2014. The club also achieved success in the 2012-13 season, winning the WNL Division One South and gaining promotion to the WNL Division One. The club also have an active youth policy, fielding teams in the Wrexham Junior Leagues and the North East Wales Youth League. They also have a junior school programme for children aged 8-10 in the local community. Brymbo F.C. remains a popular amateur club in the area and is run by a team of dedicated volunteers who strive to make the club successful. The club is grateful for the continued support from the local community and looks forward to continue it's proud history.

Amal Tamimi (born 1979) is a Palestinian feminist and human rights activist who has gained international recognition for her unrelenting commitment to justice and rights of Palestinian people, as well as political and social advocacy. Born and raised in the occupied West Bank, she currently resides in the Palestinian village of Nabi Saleh in the occupied West Bank and works as a coordinator of the Urif Committee, a local non-governmental organization devoted to the promotion of the village’s rights and activism. In 2011, Amal founded a local grassroots civil campaign aimed at protecting Nabi Saleh land from Israeli settlers and the Israeli occupation forces. This local resistance has been highlighted as a model of peaceful struggle and resilience. Amal’s works has earned her the David Tartaglione Prize for International Solidarity from the International Peace and Solidarity Council of Italy in 2015, as well as 2016 Human Rights Defender of the Year Award from Human Rights Watch. Amal holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Politics and Social Science from Birzeit University (Palestine), in addition to a Master level certification in Conflict Transformation and Human Rights Protection. She has been a guest speaker at universities around the world, such as Harvard, Columbia, Stanford, and Max Planck Institute, among others. In 2016, Amal addressed the European Parliament in Brussels in support of the recognition of Palestinian statehood. The same year, she organized a demonstration outside the United Nations Security Council headquarters in New York City on the 8th Anniversary of the Palestinian civil uprising A day before, Amal participated in a protest, naked, in the city of Bilbao (Spain) organized to support of the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) Movement. Amal has dedicated her life to advocacy and resistance against all forms of human violations and occupation, worldwide. She was an advisor for the “Freedom for Palestine” mission in support of the International Solidarity Movement (ISM) in Gaza and is currently affiliated to various Palestinian, regional, and global human rights and peace initiatives. In her own words, Amal’s perpetual fight for Palestinian freedom and justice remains “just the beginning.” Through her courage and activism, Amal has become an international symbol of peaceful Palestinian resistance and a champion of human rights around the world.

George Washington Carroll (July 10th, 1856–July 11th, 1932) was an American businessman and philanthropist. Born in Troy, Mississippi, he was the oldest son of James Madison and Harriet Carroll. Carroll left home at an early age and moved to Kansas, where he worked in the grain business. After a few years of invaluable experience in the grain trade, he moved to Atchison and established a grain commission house. This business allowed him to become very wealthy, buying large tracts of land and becoming one of the largest owners of such land in the county. He was a member of the Masonic Lodge, the Free and Accepted Masons. He also contributed to various orphanages and charities, as well as sponsoring a number of public works projects in and around Atchison. During his lifetime, Carroll contributed significantly to the city of Atchison, and he was honored multiple times for his philanthropy. He created the first library in Atchison and was a major donor to what eventually became the University of St. Mary. He also provided financial support for the creation of parks and playgrounds in the city. Carroll was also a successful businessman and investor. His largest single venture outside of Atchison was in the purchase of the Troy and Leake County Rail Company. He operated this line until the turn of the twentieth century, when it was sold to the Chicago and Alton Railway. Carroll was married twice during his lifetime. He was a strong supporter of education, and founded the Atchison Free School Movement, which sought to provide free education to children in his city. He was also one of the Executors of the will of Alexander Augusta, a large landowner in Atchison. In 1932, Carroll died in Atchison at the age of 76. Upon his death, the Atchison papers ran a three-part series to honor his memory and contributions. He was cited for his “unswerving loyalty to his community, his philanthropic spirit, and his business ability.” The Carroll Memorial Library, built in 1936 and still in operation, stands in his honor in downtown Atchison. Several other institutions and landmarks in his hometown also bear his name, including a major hospital, and a bridge crossing the Missouri River.

Nomos Glashütte is a German watchmaker based in Glashutte, Saxony. Founded in 1990, Nomos is best known for its Bauhaus-inspired timepieces that combine the best of modern technology and classic design. The company was founded in 1990 by Roland Schwertner, Uwe Ahrendt and Simon Husslein, who wanted to create watches of superior quality and unique design. The three set out to create their own watch movements, rather than relying on existing Swiss components. After several false starts, they perfected the DUW quality standard and produced their first in-house movement in 2005 – the hand-wound Alpha caliber. This was followed by the fully automatic Beta movement two years later. The Nomos watch collection is divided into six main families, each featuring watches with different designs and functions. The Tangente series is the most recognizable, with its simple three-handed design and minimalistic look, which has become iconic in watchmaking circles. The Club series offers a statement piece with its eye-catching curved lugs, while the Metro series has a rectangular case inspired by the Bauhaus architecture. Nomos also produces a limited number of unique timepieces, including the annual Ahoi Atlantic, which pays tribute to the original oceanliners. Nomos Glashutte has earned international recognition for its exquisite timepieces and its commitment to quality craftsmanship. It is a member of the AHCI – the Académie Horlogère des Créateurs Indépendants, and its watches often feature among the winners of the annual Grand Prix d’Horlogerie de Genève awards. Nomos Glashütte is dedicated to producing ingenious timepieces with a character of their own. Each watch exemplifies the brand's commitment to creating watches that stand the test of time.

Constantin Eftimiu (March 23, 1887 - February 12, 1973) was a Romanian poet, dramatist, and theater director, who was one of the most influential figures in the development of Romanian culture in the early 20th century. Constantin Eftimiu was born in Turnu-Severin, Romania in 1887. He was the son of Nicolae and Ruxandra Eftimiu, both of whom were teachers. He earned his Bachelor's degree at the University of Iasi in 1908 and his Ph.D. in 1911, then studied philosophy and drama at the Sorbonne in Paris. Eftimiu is best known for his lyric poetry, which expresses a passionate patriotism and love of nature. His later plays, such as The Eternal Son (1912) and The Refugees (1922), were unable to match the success of his earlier works. From 1920 to 1940 he was the director of the National Theatre in Bucharest. As a poet, Eftimiu showed a great range of styles. His early works, such as Moş Ion Roată (1908), combine traditional poetic forms with modern themes. His later works, such as Dogma Despre Viaţă (1912) and Amurg de toamnă (1921), rely more on symbol and imagery. Eftimiu's strongest themes were related to patriotism and the history of Romania. He often focused on heroes of Romanian history, such as Mihai Viteazul, and encouraged Romanians to rise to their original glory. In addition to being a poet and playwright, Eftimiu was an influential and prolific theater director. He was a great promoter of both Romanian and foreign plays. At the National Theatre, he staged works by authors such as A. P. Chekhov, George Bernard Shaw and Henrik Ibsen. He also directed his own plays, such as The Refugees and The Eternal Son. During his lifetime, Eftimiu received numerous awards and honors. He was awarded the Medal of Honor of Romania in 1919 and the Medal of Honor of France in 1921. He was also made a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature in London in 1957. After his death in 1973, the Constantin Eftimiu Cultural Foundation was established in his honor. Constantin Eftimiu was an important figure in the development of Romanian culture in the early 20th century. His writings, particularly his lyric poetry and plays, expressed a passionate patriotism and love of nature. His influence extended beyond his works, as he was also an influential theater director, who introduced audiences to the works of various authors. He is remembered today as one of the most important figures in Romanian literary history.

40 Tenth Avenue is a 32-story, 120-unit apartment building located in the Chelsea district of Manhattan, New York City. It was designed by Kohn Pedersen Fox and developed by HFZ Capital Group, led by Ziel Feldman. Set on a hard corner overlooking the High Line, the building contains a generous collection of amenities including a residents' lounge, library, private screening room, music practice room, and 24-hour attended lobby. There is also a private garden courtyard. The building provides a range of studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom and three-bedroom apartments. It is designed to be a “green” building, utilizing high performance materials and systems to make it sustainable. The structure has already been awarded a LEED-Gold certification. The lobby and outdoor terrace was designed by Champalimaud, winner of the Interior Design Magazine 2012 award for best new restaurant in New York City. Amenities also include a fitness center with an outdoor sundeck, spa and juice bar. The building offers breathtaking views of the Hudson River and Midtown Manhattan, as well as a host of restaurants and nightlife in the surrounding Chelsea neighborhood. It's convenient location provides easy access to the NYU and Chelsea Piers, as well as shopping and entertainment destinations. The much-anticipated opening of 40 Tenth Avenue marked the largest single residential ownership in the Chelsea District. The design and amenities of the building bring together the energy of Chelsea and the luxury of the High Line, with spectacular views of the Hudson River, capturing the attention of many potential buyers. 40 Tenth Avenue is an icon of luxury living, providing an unparalleled living experience for its residents. With its unique design, amenities and spectacular location, 40 Tenth Avenue is sure to become one of the most sought-after addresses in Manhattan.

Panetolikos Stadium (Greek: Γήπεδο Παναιτωλικού Transliterated: Gipedo Panetolikou) is the homes of the Greek football club Panetolikos located in Agrinio, Greece. It is one of the most important stadiums in the region and a source of pride for the local people. The stadium was built in 1951, initially as an athletics stadium with a track, three stands and a capacity of 10,000 people. Over the years the stadium was expanded and has now 7 stands and a capacity of 15,000 people. The biggest renovations took place in 2004 when the North Stand was demolished and a new one was constructed. The North Stand and the South Stand are the two biggest in the stadium. The home fans are housed in the North Stand while visiting supporters are held in the South. The stadium features two VIP boxes located on the first level of the North and South Stands, offering the best possible view of the field. The stadium is floodlit and also features a ticket system, food and drink stands, VIP lounges and medical center. In 2003 the stadium hosted its first international game, a friendly between the Greek national team and Scotland's. The most memorable game played at the stadium was the semi-Final of the Greek Cup in 2011 when Panetolikos played against Olympiakos. The Panetolikos Stadium is a source of pride for the club and its fans and has been the venue of many unforgettable moments over the years. The home club creates every year a special atmosphere at the stadium and it is considered as a fortress for Panetolikos. The stadium is not only known for its sporting achievements, but also for its positive social impact, having contributed to many educational, cultural and other activities in the region over the years.

Mark Johnston (born 1959) is an English racehorse trainer, based near Middleham in North Yorkshire, England. He is one of the most successful trainers in horse racing history, establishing a record for a training career in Britain with 4,194 winners during the 2020 season. Johnston was born in Stockport, Cheshire and grew up in Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, graduating in 1982 with a degree in philosophy and economics, and also has a diploma in marketing. A keen amateur jockey as a child and later a raceday steward for the British Horseracing Authority, he began his professional training career in 1987, aged just 28. Johnston was quick to gain success, winning his first major race with Warning in the St Leger Stakes in 1991. Since then he has gone on to be crowned champion trainer six times (in 1993, 1995, 1997, 2000, 2008 and 2020) and win more than 28 major races, including the 2000 and 2011 Oaks with Ramruma and Dancing Rain respectively, the 2000 and 2002 St. Leger Stakes with Millenary and Bollin Eric, and the 2010 and 2011 Dubai World Cup with Monterosso and Prince Bishop respectively. He has also had 12 Royal Ascot winners. Johnston has become renowned for his ability to train horses of all shapes and sizes, from two-year-olds to older stayers, efficiently and to great success. His unique approach has worked with a vast array of horses, and he has been particularly successful with horses bought off the track, as well as those that were born and raised in his stable. Johnston has also been active in multiple other capacities in the sport. He was a founding member of the National Trainers' Federation, served on the board of the British Horseracing Authority for three years, and has been an active voice for the welfare of racehorses. Outside of the racing world, he has served as a Fellow of the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons and a councillor for the British Horse Racing Authority. Today, Mark Johnston is one of the most respected and successful racehorse trainers in the world. He is known for his skill in getting the best out of his horses, his focus on safety and welfare in the sport, and his unrivalled record at British racecourses. He shows no signs of slowing down, and continues to be a major player in the racing world.

The 2017–18 Argentine Primera División season was the 127th season of the Primera División, the top level professional division of the Argentine football league system. A total of 133 teams competed in the league, split between Torneo de Apertura and Torneo de Clausura seasons. The season began on August 5, 2017 and concluded on May 25, 2018. Boca Juniors were the defending champions, but were eliminated by rivals River Plate in the semi-finals of the 2017–18 Copa Libertadores. River Plate were crowned champions of the Apertura after defeating San Lorenzo 4–3 on penalties in the final. Defensa y Justicia won their first ever title in the Clausura. The Primera División consists of two regional tournaments, the Argentine Province League and the Federal A League, each organised in several tiers. The season began in August with teams from the Province League playing for the Apertura, and the Federal A League playing for the Clausura. At the end of each tournament, the winners of the Apertura and Clausura competed in a two-legged championship final, usually held in late-May or early-June. The winners of the final were crowned champions of the season. The Primera División had 134 teams competing in 41 groups at various levels. The champions of each group gained a place in the Primera B Nacional tournament. The bottom team of the Federal A League and the four last-place teams in the Province League had to play the "Promocional" tournament against teams from the Liga Nacional de Fútbol. The Primera División had numerous teams participating, including all of the main clubs from the main cities of Argentina. The clubs from Buenos Aires, like Boca Juniors, River Plate, San Lorenzo and Racing, were the most successful teams. Other major clubs from the province of Buenos Aires include Vélez Sársfield and Independiente. The 2017–18 season saw the return of several teams to the Primera División. These included Aldosivi and Central Córdoba, two of the four relegated teams from the 2016–17 season, as well as San Martín de San Juan, who won their place after winning the 2016–17 Primera B Nacional.

The Lansdowne Club is a private members' club in London, England. Established in 1865, it is considered one of the most prestigious private members' clubs in the world. The Club's mission is "to encourage social intercourse, literature, and the sciences, according to the principles of benign charity". The Club's original home, in a townhouse in Berkeley Square, was bought in 1865 by Arthur Balfour, 1st Earl of Balfour, Lord Arran, and Lord Robert Cecil. The Club later moved to a larger premises in 1883 at 9 Hereford Road, London. The present building, at 9 Fitzmaurice Place in London's Mayfair, was purchased in 1893, and is an impressive five-story mansion with a striking red-brick facade. The building was designed by architect Charles Harrison Townsend, who also designed the nearby Hyde Park Corner tube station, and is considered an excellent example of his work. The Club's facilities are extensive, and include two dining rooms, the Lawrence Room and the Peter Room, as well as a smoking room and library. Many notable figures have been members of the Lansdowne Club, including the Duke of Wellington, Rudyard Kipling, George Bernard Shaw, Bertrand Russell, King Edward VII, and Winston Churchill. The Club is considered among the most exclusive private members' clubs in London. Membership is by invitation only and is limited. Candidates must be recommended to the Club by at least two members and be able to pay an annual subscription fee. Members of the Club benefit from the wide range of social, cultural and sporting events organized by the Club and its committees, from lectures and dinners to charity fundraising events and sporting competitions. The Club also boasts a collection of almost 2,000 works of art. Much of the art collection is displayed throughout the Club's premises and includes works by renowned artists such as Monet, Canaletto and Rembrandt. The Lansdowne Club remains one of the most coveted private members' clubs in London. Its combination of historic charm and modern facilities, combined with its exclusivity, makes it an ideal venue for networking, entertaining and leisure.

The 2nd Massachusetts Cavalry Regiment was an American Civil War cavalry regiment from Massachusetts that served from 1861 to 1865. It was initially a part of the Army of the Potomac and later served as part of the Army of the Shenandoah. The 2nd Massachusetts Cavalry Regiment was formed on August 30 1861 in response to President Abraham Lincoln's call for the formation of troops from the Bay State. It was organized at Camp Meigs in Readville, Massachusetts. The first commander was Captain John M. Moore. The 2nd Massachusetts was initially made up of eight companies and soon expanded to include a total of twelve. The companies were made up mostly of men from the Bay State, but also included some from other states such as Rhode Island and New Hampshire. They were issued standard blue uniforms and horse equipment. The 2nd Massachusetts saw action in many major battles, including Manassas, Chancellorsville, Gettysburg, Bristoe Station, Petersburg and Appomattox. It was also active in several minor actions, raids, and skirmishes. During their time in the war, the 2nd Massachusetts Cavalry Regiment lost 130 men killed in action, 102 died from wounds, 19 died of disease, and 18 were taken prisoner. The regiment was also credited with 429 Rebel prisoners taken, and 355 Rebels killed or wounded. On December 10, 1865 the 2nd Massachusetts Cavalry Regiment was mustered out of service at Winchester, Virginia after nearly four years in the field. The regiment was honored for their service by the citizens of Boston and the Massachusetts General Court, who gave each man a medal for their service. The 2nd Massachusetts was among the many Union regiments whose sacrifices helped preserve the Union.

NDISwrapper is a free open source software project developed to enable the use of certain network cards that do not have a native Linux driver. It is primarily used on Linux-based systems, often embedded devices such as routers, to allow them to use the Windows driver for a given networking device. NDIS (Network Driver Interface Specification) is a Microsoft Windows driver architecture that provides a standard interface between a Windows operating system and a network or modem card. NDIS provides communication interface between user-level applications and lower level physical device drivers, providing a layer of abstraction that allows multiple networking protocols to be used at once. Ndiswrapper allows perfectly compatible Windows network drivers to run on linux. The project was originally started by Thac in 2002 and the development has been hosted by SourceForge since 2005. It has been praised for providing a useful workaround for network card compatibility issues. NDISwrapper consists of three components, the ndiswrapper Linux kernel module, a Windows DLL library, and a user-space utility. The Linux kernel module acts as the interface to the Windows driver, while the Windows DLL library translates the NDIS protocol calls into the form that the Linux kernel can understand. The user-space utility provides a management interface to the NDISwrapper kernel module. NDISwrapper is distributed under the GNU General Public License (GNU GPL). In late 2009, development of NDISwrapper was taken over by the ndiswrapper-authors community. The ndiswrapper-authors team has been tasked with developing, expanding and maintaining the project. Some of the key recent developments include: support for USB devices, support for WPA2 encryption and rewrite of the ndiswrapper source code for improved performance. The ndiswrapper-authors team also maintains an online wiki with comprehensive documentation on using NDISwrapper. This Wiki is a very useful resource for installing and troubleshooting NDISwrapper and contains links to the ndiswrapper-authors discussion forum, as well as other additional resources. Overall, NDISwrapper provides an great way to get support for Windows network drivers on Linux-based systems where native drivers are not available. It is relatively simple to install and use, making it ideal for users who want to get the most out of their systems but lack the technical expertise to build native drivers.

The National Philatelic Society (NPS) is an organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the hobby of stamp collecting. Founded in 1915, it is the oldest philatelic organization in the United States. The Society seeks to promote the worldwide growth of the hobby by inspiring interest and appreciation in collecting, speaking to philatelists, offering support to various philatelic activities, and maintaining an online library of philatelic materials. The NPS also aids stamp collectors, particularly beginners, with educational activities and publications, while offering resources to experienced philatelists. The NPS sponsors exhibition, shows, auctions and sales, and publishes a monthly magazine, which includes news and articles about philately. Additionally, it hosts an annual meeting and symposium each year, bringing together philatelists for presentations and lectures. The NPS also has an extensive library of philatelic books and magazines, as well as an extensive selection of collector items for sale. It offers a variety of benifits to members, including discounts on stamp shows, auctions and sales, as well as access to special member-only auctions. The Society is currently led by an Executive committee, which is comprised of a President, four Vice Presidents, and a Treasurer. All of these officers are elected by the members of the NPS, and serve staggered two-year terms. The National Philatelic Society is a member of the American Philatelic Society and the Philatelic Society of America. It is also affiliated with many smaller specialty societies and organizations dedicated to the hobby. The NPS is open to all those who are interested in stamp collecting and the Society encourages anyone who wishes to join to be an active member. Membership fees are inexpensive, and members of the Society who join before the end of the year will receive a certificate and pin as well as printed versions of the NPS magazines.

Pembroke, Kentucky is a small unincorporated community located in the southern portion of Christian County, Kentucky. It lies along the banks of the Green River, which runs through the county. The population as of the 2010 census was approximately 350 people. The primary purposes of the small community revolve around recreation, farming, and industry. The Green River, which runs through Pembroke, is popular for recreational activities such as fishing and boating. The community is home to numerous parks and boat ramps along the river, allowing for easy access to the water. In addition, Pembroke has many small streams that flow through the area. These waterways are popular for pan fishing and other forms of fishing. Pembroke is home to several small family-owned farms, which produce commodity crops such as corn, wheat, and soybeans. Dairy and poultry farms are also located nearby. There is also a large poultry processing plant in the area, which provides jobs for many of the local residents. Pembroke is located about ten miles east of the city of Hopkinsville and about seven miles north of the Tennessee border. To the east of Pembroke is the town of Eddyville. Both towns are connected by the Clarence Worley Memorial Trail, which is an 18-mile hiking/biking trail. The trail has several picturesque stops along the way, including this small community of Pembroke. The majority of the population of Pembroke is of Christian faith. The main church in the community is the Pembroke Christ Church, a non-denominational church. The church holds weekly services and a variety of activities for the community. Pembroke is also home to the Green River Arts and Crafts Festival, which takes place every summer. This festival features local artists and craftsmen displaying and selling their work, giving attendees the chance to purchase handmade items directly from the maker. There are also live music performances, food stands, and a variety of children's activities. Pembroke is a small rural community in which the residents take pride in their heritage and strive to preserve the small-town atmosphere for which it is known. It provides a peaceful and friendly atmosphere for those living in the area or visiting for the day. Whether enjoying the local attractions or recreation activities offered in the area, Pembroke remains a great destination for all.

Linda Holeman is an internationally-published Canadian writer of fiction and nonfiction works, who has had a long and successful career in both genres. She is a four-time Governor General's Award nominee, and has been twice shortlisted for the CBA Libris Fiction Book Award and twice shortlisted for the McNally-Robinson Book of the Year Award. Growing up in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Holeman attended the University of Manitoba, earning a Bachelor of Education degree. She was initially a teacher, but soon transitioned into full-time writing, beginning her career with her first novel, The Lightkeeper's Daughter. First published in 1984, the book was a critical success and has been reissued five times in Canada and many times around the world. Since then, Holeman has achieved great success with her novels and nonfiction works, many of which have earned her critical acclaim and multiple award nominations. Her fiction works range from historical sagas to contemporary stories, and often draw upon regional folklore. Holeman has also published many non fiction works, including a book of essays entitled Mixing It Up: A British-Canadian Odyssey in the 1980s. Holeman has been honored with the John Hirsch Award for Most Promising Manitoba Writer in 2006, and was short-listed for the Carnegie Medal for Fiction in 2009. She was also the recipient of the Manitoba Book Award for Best Book in 2004. Throughout her career, Holeman’s works have been featured in major newspapers and magazines such as The Globe and Mail, Maclean’s, National Geographic, and Chatelaine. Holeman’s works have been translated into German, Italian, Spanish, Dutch, Vietnamese, Korean, and Greek. She currently lives in Winnipeg, Manitoba, where she continues to write fiction and nonfiction.

Heirs of Empire is a fantasy novel written by Anthony Riches and first published in 2006. The book follows the story of Wensel Rusch and his brother, Joscelin, two young men from vastly different backgrounds. Wensel is a Teutonic Knight, whereas Joscelin is a former slave from the Naglite Empire. Along with their companion and Wensel's love interest, Anghelina Dragot, the two set off on a journey through the wilds of Europe. The story starts in 1217, with Wensel and Joscelin joining forces to fight off an invading army from the west. With the blessing of the Teutonic Knights and the help of a mysterious figure, they are victorious. Soon after, they must flee through a range of hostile lands in search of a refuge from their past. Along the way they uncover secrets long buried within the Naglite Empire, secrets that could affect the course of their destiny and the future of Europe. The trio travels through the depths of the Balkans, past the Black Sea and into the Mediterranean. There they encounter a variety of cultures, from the mysterious Gypsy-like wanderers to the wild steppe nomads and the powerful rulers of distant imperial courts. The journey takes them through storms, forests, and epic battles as they pursue the truth hidden in their pasts and determine their ultimate fate. As the story unfolds, their quest intertwines with a much greater and stranger one, involving ancient secrets and rivaling powers. Heirs of Empire is a thrilling and adventurous tale, full of surprises and danger at every turn. It’s a story of self-discovery, loyalty and courage, set in a mystical and unique world. Overall, Heirs of Empire is a captivating read and a worthwhile adventure, with epic battles, larger-than-life characters, hidden places, incredible cultures and intense battles. It is a tale of brotherhood, courage and adventure, full of intricate and imaginative detail. An intriguing and absorbing novel that will take readers on an exciting and unforgettable journey.

Abbott and Holder is an art dealership and gallery specialised in the promotion of British paintings, watercolours and drawings. Located in the heart of London’s historic arts district, it represents a wide selection of artwork from the 17th Century to the present day. The duo that runs Abbott and Holder are Roderic and Ben, both being experts in Old Master, Modern British, Victorian and early 20th Century British drawings, watercolours and art. They strive to create an atmosphere of exchange and trust to promote their clients' investments. Abbott and Holder have been offering a broad spectrum of fine art services since 1979, focusing on developing a strong portfolio of secure, high-value and profitable artwork. They travel the world, sourcing artwork which they carefully select to promote and bring home to the gallery. Abbott and Holder take pride in the personal service they provide to their established clientele, while also supporting the conservation and preservation of the British art traditions. Abbott and Holder have gained a strong and respected position amongst the art community and have close partnerships with museums and institutions. The gallery regularly participates in art fairs such as BRAFA (Brussels Antiques and Fine Arts Fair), and Masterpiece London, as well as hosting specialised exhibitions, lectures and events. Over the last few years, Abbott and Holder have broadened their portfolio to include Fine Art photography, Scottish Colourists and Post-War British printmaking, further diversifying the range of artwork they proffer.
