By creating a unique atmosphere of trust and knowledge, Abbott and Holder stands at the vanguard of the British art scene, promoting the best of British artwork to buyers and art connoisseurs around the world.

Kokatha is an Indigenous Australian group of the Australian Arrernte people, a group of Aboriginal Australians that live on the traditional lands of the Arrernte people. The Kokatha people are located in the southern part of the Western Arrernte region of South Australia, and their traditional lands lie around Lake Eyre and the Nullarbor Plain in the Northern Territory and South Australia. The Kokatha people are made up of several smaller tribes, including the Wirangu, Yankunytjatjara, Pitjantjatjara and Kadjingaritankalpa. They also share a traditional language, known as Kokatha, as well as a strong cultural and spiritual connection to their lands. Kokatha people are renowned for their traditional knowledge and for their role in the conservation and protection of land and waters. The Kokatha people have an in-depth understanding of, and strong connections with, the environment, wildlife, plants and animals within their traditional territory. The Kokatha people are also involved in many cultural and recreational activities, including music, dance, storytelling, games, hunting and fishing. The music and storytelling of the Kokatha people is well recognised, and includes the creation of unique dot painting designs. The Kokatha people have endured multiple challenges since European arrival and are currently negotiating land claims with the Commonwealth and SA state governments. In 2013, the Kokatha people were officially recognised as Traditional Owners in South Australia, with the help of the Kokatha people, the Kokatha Mula Council. The Kokatha people are also active in the local community, they run and promote programs such as the 'Cultural Connections Program' and the 'Family Nature Connections Program', which aim to bring non-Indigenous people together to discuss and explore the unique culture and nature of the Kokatha people. The Kokatha people are also members of the local Aboriginal Advisory Committee and take part in joint-management of land and water in the traditional country, this includes on-ground projects such as restoring wetlands and re-vegetation initiatives. The Kokatha people and their traditional lands continually face threats from industry, with projects such as fracking, pipeline installation and water extraction highlighting the importance of the traditional custodians of the land and water. The Kokatha people are seeking to protect and preserve their culture, and their traditional lands and waters for future generations. They are working hard to guard their heritage, which includes continuing their connection to the land and water, and honouring the stories of their ancestors.

X-tree is a type of data structure used to store and retrieve data in computer programs. It is similar to a binary tree, but has an additional constraint. It was proposed by the computer scientists C.A.R. Hoare and Jens Myrup Pedersen in 1982. A X-tree is a type of tree-based data structure where each node can have no more than a predetermined number of children. This predetermined number is referred to as the arity of the tree. For example, a binary tree has an arity of two, meaning that each node can only have two children. A X-tree is similar, but allows for a higher arity. The advantage of using a X-tree is the increased flexibility in terms of storing the data. Unlike a binary tree, which requires a specific data arrangement, a X-tree can store a wide variety of shapes and sizes of data. For example, it can be used to store a list of items, such as a phone book or a dictionary, or it can be used to store tree-structured data, such as a database of financial records. A X-tree can also be used to store multi-dimensional data, such as a packet routing table or a geographic information system. This is because they allow the data to be broken down into smaller and easier to manage chunks, thus simplifying the process of searching and retrieving data. The primary disadvantage of using a X-tree is that it can be difficult to manage due to its higher arity. The number of nodes needed to store a given amount of data can increase drastically as the amount of data increases. This can lead to problems such as long search times, and increased complexity when trying to make changes or additions to the data. X-trees can also be slow to access due to the increased number of nodes needed to store the data, which can lead to performance issues. X-trees are a useful data structure for many types of applications, and are often used in medical and financial applications, where large amounts of data need to be stored and quick access is critical. Despite their advantages, however, they can be difficult to manage and require careful optimization to achieve good performance.

The Neuse River waterdog (Necturinus insularis) is a species of aquatic salamander native to the lower Neuse River drainage in eastern North Carolina, United States. As an ectothermic species, the Neuse River waterdog adjusts its activity levels to changing environmental temperatures and can be found in seasonally flooded lowland ponds and backwater sloughs of the larger river systems. The species was first described in 2006 by Chris Blaha, a student at the University of North Carolina - Chapel Hill. Blaha and his colleagues were investigating aquatic amphibian communities of the area, when their genetic analysis revealed that certain specimens of aquatic salamanders from the Neuse River drainage (identified as members of the family Necturidae) were a distinct species that had not been previously described. Due to the new species' small range, the Neuse River waterdog was listed as endangered in 2009, under the U.S. Endangered Species Act. Since then, it has seen a slight increase in population size, which is mainly attributed to successful conservation efforts, including the establishment of wildlife refuges and preserves in the region. The Neuse River waterdog is a large, robust species of aquatic salamander, typically measuring up to 12 centimeters in length. Its dorsal surface is a light brown color with dark, reticulated markings. The ventral side is white, lightly speckled with brown spots. Its snout is short and rounded, and its eyes are small and black. Unlike many other species of salamander, the Neuse River waterdog does not have external gills. The Neuse River waterdog is a highly adaptable animal and can withstand a variety of environmental conditions, including temperatures that range from near freezing to 30°C (86°F). Its diet consists of aquatic invertebrates, including worms, insects, and crustaceans, which it hunts in the shallow, muddy waters of its range. The Neuse River waterdog is an important part of the local ecosystem. As a producer, it provides food for larger animals, including wading birds, fish, and turtles. Additionally, it helps to aerate the water and sediment, filtering out nutrients and pollutants that would otherwise accumulate in the river system. Despite its importance, the species remains vulnerable. There is concern that the Neuse River waterdog could become threatened due to human-caused habitat fragmentation and loss, water pollution, and the introduction of invasive species. In order to ensure the long-term survival of this species and the health of the Neuse River ecosystem, conservation efforts must continue to be made.

Pflügers Archiv: European Journal of Physiology is a scientific journal in the field of physiology. It was established in 1868 by German physiologist and founder of physiological chemistry, Eduard Pflüger and it is published bimonthly by Springer. The journal covers all areas of science and medicine related to physiology, including biomechanics, biophysics, and biochemistry. Pflüger's Archiv is one of the oldest scientific journals of physiology in the world, and has a long and distinguished editorial history. The journal is known for being a major source of information for researchers in the area of physiology. In addition to publishing the latest research and reviews in the field, the journal provides an insightful overview of the historical and contemporary developments in the field, with extensive archival and historical material. Pflüger's Archiv also offers an extensive range of interdisciplinary and applied aspects of physiological research. The journal's editor in chief is Nobel laureate Bertil Hille, who works alongside a team of well-known board members. It publishes original research articles, review articles, editorials, and also Scientific Reviews, symposia, commentaries, and other materials.The journal is indexed and/or abstracted in Biological Abstracts, Chemical Abstracts, Current Contents/Life Sciences, PubMed/MEDLINE, Science Citation Index Expanded, and Scopus. The journal is available in both print and online versions, and is published in English language editions. Authors may submit their work either online or by mail. The articles are peer-reviewed by an international board of experts before being accepted. The editors of the journal work to ensure that all articles meet the highest standards of quality. Pflüger's Archiv: European Journal of Physiology is an important source for researchers in the field of physiology. It provides an invaluable resource for the understanding of physiological processes, and continues to make a valuable contribution to the advancement of knowledge in this field.

Con Jones (born 25 May 1975) is an Australian entrepreneur and philanthropist. He is best known as the founder of Global Corporation, a multinational enterprise with holdings in renewable energy, banking and real estate. Born in the small country town of Boorowa in New South Wales, Con was a visionary entrepreneur from a young age. After completing his Bachelor of Science at the University of Sydney, he began to realise his dreams of founding and leading his own business. In 1998, he founded Global Corporation and established its headquarters in Sydney. Since its establishment, Global Corporation has grown to become one of the largest and most successful companies in Asia-Pacific, with a market capitalisation of over $1 billion. As of 2020, Global Corporation has investments in renewable energy, banking and real estate, particularly in the Pacific region. Apart from his business achievements, Con is highly regarded for his charitable contributions. In 2009, he founded the Global Foundation, a non-profit organisation focused on providing support and access to education for disadvantaged people around the world. The organisation has achieved great success, providing over $150 million in support to date. Con has been widely recognised for his achievements and contributions to the community. In 2019, he was awarded an honorary degree from the University of Sydney in recognition of his philanthropic work. In 2020, he was named one of the ‘100 Most Influential People in the World’ by Time magazine. As a self-made entrepreneur and philanthropist, Con Jones is an inspiring figure who has succeeded in both business and charity, leaving a lasting legacy on the world.

Tony Brown (born Jonathan Anthony Brown, May 7, 1955) is an American record producer, arranger, singer and songwriter. He has been a prominent figure in the music industry for over four decades. Brown is best known for producing and writing a string of hits for a variety of artists, including George Strait, Reba McEntire, Gary Morris, Lionel Richie, Keith Whitley and many others. Brown was born in Nashville, Tennessee. He began his musical career as a touring musician with Conway Twitty before joining the house band of Alan Green at the Exit In, where he worked with fellow Nashville musician Vince Gill. He rose to prominence in the early 1980s when he signed to MCA Records and produced Bonnie Raitt's multi-platinum album "Takin' My Time". This success led to him producing a series of albums for George Strait and Reba McEntire. In addition, Brown was involved in the creation of many other successful albums and singles, most notably "Forever and Ever, Amen" and "When I Call Your Name" for Randy Travis, "Mama He’s Crazy" for the Judds, and "Don't Close Your Eyes" for Keith Whitley. Through the 1990s, Brown continued to produce albums for a variety of artists, both major labels and independents. He received many honors for his work, most notably a Grammy Award for Producer of the Year in 1992. In recent years, Brown has been involved in creating albums and singles for a number of different genres such as pop, country, gospel, and contemporary Christian. He has also gone on to work in television and film, producing soundtracks and music on network series such as Dawson’s Creek and Reba. At present, Brown continues to be a highly sought-after producer and arranger, with his recent credits including Phillip Phillips' 2013 single "Gone, Gone, Gone" and Carrie Underwood's 2018 album Cry Pretty. He has become one of the most respected and sought-after producers in the music industry, and his work has earned him widespread recognition.

Manolis Sfakianakis (born 2 March 1964) is a Greek singer-songwriter and performer. He has been active in the Greek popular music scene since the late 1980s, and is one of the most popular Greek singers. He is a permanent fixture in the annual Greek music festivals, and he has won several awards in the thirty-plus years he has been active in the Greek musical scene. The musical style of Manolis Sfakianakis is largely that of Bouzouki-pop (Μπουζουκική ποπ). He is known for reviving forgotten Greek folk songs and giving them a new, modern interpretation. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest Greek musicians and lyricists of his generation. Manolis Sfakianakis was born in 1964 in Alepohori, Achaia, the homeland of his parents and grandparents. He grew up in Peloponnese, playing bouzouki and bouzouki-style music with his friends. This eventually led him to move to Athens in 1975 to pursue a career in music. After some success in 1980s, his first major break came when his song “Mera Me Ti Mera” was included on the album ‘Me Tis Kardias Tin Kardia’ released in 1988. In 1989, he released his debut album ‘Katapliktika’ which, along with the hit single “Anaparastasi”, quickly shot him to the top of the Greek music scene. Since then he has released over 20 albums and has had numerous number one singles and top 10 albums. Sfakianakis has accumulated many awards and honors for his music. In 2009, he was given the Mad Music Awards Lifetime Achievement award. He was also awarded with a medal from the Greek Minister of Culture in 2012 for his contributions to Greek music. He is also an honorary member of the Greek Union of Authors and Performers. Manolis Sfakianakis is known not only for his music but also for his philanthropy. He has been actively involved in charities supporting refugees, children with disabilities, and poor citizens in Athens. In 2012, Sfakianakis initiated ‘Truth and Life’, a project to build more schools in poor areas of Greece. Manolis Sfakianakis is one of the most beloved and respected musicians in Greece and his influence is recognizable in the works of many popular Greek musicians today. He is a symbol of the true Greek spirit, and his continuing success in the Greek music scene is evidence of his brilliance as a musician and compassionate human being.

Anis Matta is an Indonesian politican who has been a Member of the People's Representative Council (DPR) for the Prosperous Justice Party (PKS) since 2014. He is also a former mayor of Sukabumi, West Java. Anis Matta was born in Sukabumi, West Java on August 26, 1980. He attended high school in Serpong, Tangerang, and later graduated from the Faculty of Business and Economics at the University of Indonesia. Anis Matta began his political career in 2006, when he was elected as Mayor of Sukabumi. During his tenure, he worked hard to improve the city's infrastructure and economic development. He also established a number of development initiatives, such as the "Sukabumi Smart City" project. He was also responsible for increasing the city's regional autonomy index. In 2014, Anis Matta was elected to the People's Representative Council (DPR) for the Prosperous Justice Party (PKS). Since then, he has become an active member of the PKS's faction on the DPR. Anis Matta has been a vocal champion of multiculturalism and pluralism in Indonesia, and a strong advocate of religious tolerance, peace, and justice. He has written several books and has been a regular feature in Indonesian media, both in print and online, where he regularly discusses these issues. Anis Matta has also been involved in philanthropy, founding and supporting a number of charities and organisations in Sukabumi. He also serves as an advisor to several organisations. Anis Matta is married to Li Agni Wulandari, and they have two children.

The National Reality Television Awards, or NRTAs, are an annual event honoring excellence in reality television. The awards were first held in 2008 and are produced by ITV Studios. The award ceremony dignifies excellence in the genre, and is judged by eminent industry members of the Reality Television Academy. Categories range from Best Reality Entertainment Show and Best Reality Competition Show to Best Reality Host and Best Highlight Reel. The NRTAs are honoured by a variety of British and international networks, including ITV, Channel 4, Sky1, E! and MTV. The ceremony is televised annually, with a variety of presenters from the world of reality television, including Simon Cowell, Davina McCall, and many more. The NRTAs have become a great success in recent years, with a wealth of reality stars gracing the red carpet. These celebrities come from all genres of the reality world, such as British television and American reality television, as well as international reality programmes. Previous winners of the awards have included Channel 4’s The Great British Bake Off, ITV2’s Love Island and MTV UK’s Geordie Shore. The NRTAs are a true celebration of the great shows and spectacular talent that can be seen in the world of reality television, where new programmes are constantly being born. Whilst the awards may not be as prestigious or high-profile as the Oscars and BAFTAs, they nevertheless hold an important place in the TV world. Typically held during the summer months, the NRTAs are highly anticipated by those within the reality industry and make for a unique night of television. The awards attract a plethora of stars from the world of TV, as well as ensure a captivating evening for viewers at home. The National Reality Television Awards are now in their eleventh year, and continue to honour the outstanding achievements in the genre.

Women in Ghana have made significant progress over the last few decades when it comes to the rights and freedom to pursue economic and educational opportunities, as well as basic civil liberties. Despite this progress, however, Ghana also has a long way to go to ensure that women have full access to their rights and liberties. The constitution of Ghana asserts the equality of all citizens within the nation, both male and female, and actively seeks to protect the rights of women. Additionally, the state has taken tangible steps to advance the rights of women by establishing the Women’s Development Fund in 1997. The fund provides small loans to rural women to help with capital, as well as grants to local women-owned businesses. Furthermore, Ghana has signed several international agreements that advocate for the safety and rights of women, including the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW). Despite some of these initiatives, men still dominate the professional and political spheres in Ghana. This contributes to a gender gap at all levels of labor, with men still achieving higher wages and positions than women. The traditional patriarchal system continues to reinforce the notion of male dominance in many communities, to the detriment of female progress. In addition, the global pandemic has had a disproportionate impact on women, who are more likely to be unemployed or underemployed. In response to this, the government of Ghana has taken a number of initiatives to help women who have been affected. These initiatives include the launch of an online tool for women to access business resources, access to free ICT services, and a tax waiver for micro and small businesses. These initiatives are a promising start, but more work is needed to ensure that the rights of women are fully protected in Ghana. Women play an important role in the nation’s economy and society, and it is crucial that they are given equal opportunities to reach their full potential. Efforts should be made to reduce the gender gap in the workplace and increase the representation of women in all sectors, including business and politics. Additionally, there should be continued monitoring of the implementation and enforcement of the CEDAW and other laws that protect the rights of women. With these steps, Ghana can move closer to achieving gender equality in the nation.

William Cullen Bryant (November 3, 1794 – June 12, 1878) was an American poet, newspaper editor, and long-time supporter of the abolition of slavery in the United States. Born and raised in Massachusetts, he received an education in the classics, and went on to attend Williams College and study law. He tasted success early on as a poet, becoming well known for “Thanatopsis,” a reflection on death, which was first published in 1817. From 1825–1878, he served as editor of the newspaper the New York Evening Post, where he wrote a weekly political column and organized a team of correspondents. He was also an ardent abolitionist, and advocated on behalf of slaves and black Americans, writing extensively on the costs of slavery both to those enslaved and those in bondage. Bryant was a frequent guest of prominent individuals of the day, including Thomas Jefferson, and Washington Irving, who he met through his work. Wordsworth, Longfellow, and James Fenimore Cooper were among the authors with whom he was well acquainted. In 1876, he became the president of the National Institute of Arts and Letters. He was also made an honorary member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, as well as the American Antiquarian Society. Bryant was known for his moral positions and strong opinions on a variety of issues. He was a proponent of temperance, the establishment of a just society, the protection of the environment, and the value of education. His works have been highly influential, and he is remembered as one of the most important figures in American literature. He is credited for helping to make themes of nature and contemplation popular in poetry. Bryant was a recipient of the Congressional Gold Medal, which was awarded to him in 1870 for both his literary works, and his efforts in the abolition of slavery. He passed away in 1878, at the age of 83.

Reuben Webster Millsaps (1837 - 1921) was an American businessman and philanthropist. Born in Chatham County, North Carolina, he moved with his family to Maryland as a young man. After serving as a wagoner in the Civil War, he moved to Jackson, Mississippi, in 1873. He was an important figure in the development of the city for nearly 50 years, and was one of its largest employers. Millsaps was a self-made man whose ventures included banking, lumber mills, and cotton ginning. He was one of the founders of the Savings and Trust Company of Jackson, served on its board of directors and was president at the time of his death. He also established several lumber mills, including Leaf River Lumber Company, Leaf River Cotton Gins, Rose Ginnery, and Iron Mill of Mississippi. He helped to finance the building of several churches and hospitals in the region, including Hickory Hill Methodist Church, and the MS Baptist Memorial Hospital. He also donated funds to local schools and universities, as well as institutions in Mobile, AL, including Spring Hill College. Furthermore, he and his wife, Marie Magruder (1845–1915), co-founded Millsaps College in 1890. In addition to his financial contribution to Jackson, Millsaps was also a social reformer who sought to improve facilities for African-Americans in the region. He supported the Union soldiers, giving them supplies and protesting for voting rights for newly freed African-Americans. Millsaps was a well respected philanthropist who left a lasting legacy on the Jackson community. In his honor, a park and a nursing facility bear his name, and the local library serves as a fitting tribute to his contributions to the city. He was a leader in business and in civil service, leaving a mark of progress and charity on his adopted city. Millsaps died in 1921 and was buried in Jackson with full military honors.

Hasan Awad (born 1988) is a Syrian-American entrepreneur and investor based in the San Francisco Bay Area who has gained notoriety for founding and leading several successful technology companies, including Palantir Technologies, Zebra Medical Vision, and TelAviv AI Lab. At a young age, Hasan was drawn to technology and entrepreneurship. After observing his father, a successful civil engineer, find success in the technology arena, Hasan decided to pursue software engineering and entrepreneurship. He graduated from the American University of Sharjah in Abu Dhabi with a degree in Computer and Electrical Engineering. After college, he began his career as an early employee at a software startup called Palantir Technologies. Initially, he worked as a software engineer and later became the Director of Product. Within a few years, Palantir became a leading intelligence software provider to government and law enforcement agencies around the world. It also boasts some of the world's largest banks and corporations as clients. Moving on from Palantir, Hasan returned to his passion for technology and founded Zebra Medical Vision in 2014. Zebra Medical Vision is a deep learning Imaging analytics company with the mission of reducing cost and increasing quality of healthcare. The company analyzes medical images and provides automated diagnosis. Its AI-based system helps radiologists and physicians diagnose heart disease, lung issues, hip fractures, and more. Most recently, Hasan established TelAviv AI Lab in 2019. TelAviv AI Lab uses Artificial Intelligence to unlock new ways of diagnosing cancer. The lab focuses on using AI to improve diagnosis accuracy and reduce the amount of time it takes to create a diagnosis. Hasan has been passionate about technology and entrepreneurship since a young age and has built a successful career in both fields. His work and vision have been instrumental in the success of many technology companies and have set a good example for budding entrepreneurs.

Ada Bittenbender (December 16, 1893 – April 24, 1993) was an American teacher, college professor, labor union leader and civil rights advocate. She was born in Indiana and was noted for her activism during the Great Depression and peacetime activism in the United States. Bittenbender was born in rural Indiana to a poor family of German immigrants. After graduating from high school, she attended Butler University where she earned her bachelor's degree in 1914. Bittenbender then began teaching at a rural school in Logansport, Indiana before moving to Chicago to pursue further teaching opportunities throughout the 1920s. During the Great Depression, Bittenbender was involved in labor union organizing activities in the Chicago area. She began working for the Amalgamated Clothing Workers of America in 1933 and eventually became the first woman to serve as the international vice president of the union in 1948. Bittenbender was a prominent leader in labor union organizing efforts in the Chicago area. She was a key organizer of a successful workers' strike against the Havering Corporation, one of the largest clothing companies in the city, which led to improvements in wages and working conditions for the laborers. Bittenbender was also active in civil rights activism, particularly during the period after the Second World War. In 1945 she was part of the organizing efforts for the March on Washington which was led by A. Philip Randolph and Bayard Rustin. She also worked tirelessly to promote racial justice and equal rights in Illinois, and collaborated with other activists to secure voting rights for African Americans in the state. In 1963 she was part of the March on Washington, and in 1966 she joined with Martin Luther King Jr. and others in Selma, Alabama to help organize the historic march that ended in the passage of the Voting Rights Act of 1965. Throughout her life, Bittenbender was a champion for the underprivileged and an advocate for justice and equality in all aspects of life. She was the recipient of numerous awards and honors in recognition of her years of activism, including the 1967 Martin Luther King Jr. Award and a 1989 induction into the Illinois Labor History Society Hall of Fame. Her efforts are remembered today by her granddaughter and namesake, Ada Bittenbender Jenkins, who is a well-known writer and social activist. Ada Bittenbender passed away on April 24, 1993 at the age of 99. She is remembered as a courageous advocate for social justice and labor rights whose life was dedicated to making a difference in her community.

Mynagappally is a village panchayat in the Kollam District of the Indian state of Kerala. It is situated near the Kerala backwaters, in the western part of the district. Mynagappally is one of the major panchayats in the district, and it is a major link between the cities of Quilon, Kollam and Adoor. Mynagappally has a population of over 15,000 people and is situated on the banks of the Mynagappally River. It is an important agricultural centre and supports a thriving coir industry. Mynagappally is home to several ancient temples and churches, and it is known for its rich cultural heritage. The panchayat of Mynagappally is divided into eight wards, and each ward is further divided into nine blocks. The panchayat is administered by an elected body of nine members who are responsible for the local government. The panchayat is responsible for local governance and also provides a number of essential services such as healthcare, education, water supply, roads and sanitation. The panchayat also looks after the welfare of its citizens by providing employment opportunities, subsidies and various other welfare schemes. Mynagappally is also a major commercial hub in the Kollam district. It is a centre for coir production, milk production, and rubber production. The town also has a number of vegetable and fish markets. The economy of Mynagappally is also supported by a number of small-scale and cottage industries that produce carpets, leather goods and household items. Mynagappally is well-connected with the rest of Kerala and Kerala's surrounding states by road. The closest railway station is Kollam Junction, located about 10 km away. Mynagappally is also connected to the airports in Thiruvananthapuram and Cochin, which are located about 150 km and 80 km away respectively. There are a number of buses that connect Mynagappally with other parts of the state. Mynagappally is a major tourist destination in Kerala due to its rich cultural heritage, vast backwaters, and beautiful landscape. There are a number of temples and churches in the area, as well as a couple of beaches that offer tranquil locations for relaxation. Mynagappally also offers a number of opportunities for activities such as kayaking, swimming, canoeing and fishing. It is an ideal destination for those looking for a tranquil holiday in Kerala.

The 1963 Canadian federal election was held on April 8, 1963, to elect members of the House of Commons of Canada to the 24th Parliament of Canada. The Progressive Conservative Party of Canada, under Prime Minister John Diefenbaker, had won an increased majority in the 1962 election. For the Liberals, led by Lester B. Pearson, this was their first election with their new leader. Pearson was a former cabinet minister in the Diefenbaker government. He had tried to displace the Prime Minister by using a secret alliance of Opposition members in the House of Commons in December 1961, but failed. The election results would bring about significant changes to Canada's political landscape. The Progressive Conservatives would suffer their worst defeat since their formation in 1867, and the Liberal Party would score its best result since 1945. The long Conservative majority was replaced by a Liberal minority government, followed in 1965 by a new majority government. The campaign focused largely on economics. Prime Minister Diefenbaker was critical of Pearson for proposing to implement mandatory price controls and said that it was the "most lethal weapon ever seen in economic ammunition." The debate over price and wage controls had polarized the two main parties, leaving the other parties relatively unscathed. The campaign had been thrilling for a time, but it ultimately resulted in a slight shift from Conservative to Liberal. The Progressive Conservatives retained a plurality of seats, but lacked a majority. The Liberals increased their seat total, but still finished 72 seats behind the Progressive Conservatives. In the wake of the election, Pearson's Liberal government was faced with a precarious minority. In order to gain the support of other parties, Pearson implemented tax cuts, an expansion of the Canada Pension Plan, as well as the introduction of Medicare. His government also declared Canada's Official Languages Act, making the two official languages of Canada English and French. In 1965, Pearson's government would go on to win a majority in the next election. The result of the election marked a shift away from the conservative politics of Diefenbaker and signaled a centre-left shift in Canadian politics. It was the first time since 1921 that the Liberals had won an election, and would prove to be an important milestone in Canada's modern history.

Indirect DNA damage is a type of genetic damage that occurs indirectly, without the direct involvement of a mutagen, by altering the transcription, replication, and stability of DNA strands. It is the result of an imbalance of cellular macromolecules and/or molecules, during the metabolic process. As a primary mechanism, it is initiated by oxidative stress and can lead to genetic mutations in organisms, and thus, radiation exposure. The body of an organism is a complex aggregation of cellular components and molecules which have to maintain a balance in order to maintain the organism’s proper functioning. Under normal conditions, the cells, tissues and organs in the body are in equilibrium such that any change in the balance disturbs their normal performance. One of the major causes of imbalance of macromolecules and molecules is oxidative stress, which is generated by the exposure to different sources of stress such as radiation, toxic compounds and other environmental hazards. Oxidative stress leads to the production of free radicals, which are very reactive molecules having unpaired electrons and try to stabilize their inner structure by stealing electrons from other molecules. Consequently, the imbalance of cellular molecules disturbs DNA metabolism, leading to indirect DNA damage. An important metabolism affected by oxidative stress is replication of DNA. During replication, the original DNA double helix separates and copies are formed on each of the single helical strands of DNA. Oxidative stress causes oxidation of certain metabolites involved in the replication, which results in its slowing down or pause due to the loss of components essential to its proceeding. As a result, the DNA strands may become distorted leading to unregulated transcription and replication of genetic material, and frequently, wrong amino acid formation and sequence in proteins. Indirect DNA damage can also lead to DNA instability, which is caused by generation of single stranded DNA containing mismatches and deletions that are formed due to oxidative stress. These single stranded DNA molecules form an loop to increase their stability. Such loops interact between each other to form a pile of heterologous sequences that can lead to chromosomal aberrations. This phenomenon is known as the instability loop and is responsible for the generation of chimeras, translocations and deletions, which can ultimately lead to genetic mutations and cancer. Indirect DNA damage is a serious health hazard and has been linked to a variety of diseases including cancer, autoimmune diseases, diabetes, cardiovascular problems and neurological diseases. Therefore, it is essential to recognize the health hazards posed by indirect DNA damage and to take preventive actions by leading a healthy lifestyle and avoiding exposure to hazardous stimuli such as radiation and toxic compounds.

Val Caniparoli (born February 5, 1947) is a celebrated American dancer, choreographer, and director. Caniparoli began his professional career in 1964, when he joined the Smuin Ballet of San Francisco as a dancer. In 1974, he joined the Joffrey Ballet based in New York City. While with The Joffrey Ballet, he danced numerous principal roles, such as in Gerald Arpino's Sea Shadow, and The Makings of a Gothic. Following his dancer career, Val Caniparoli became a sought after choreographer for numerous companies around the world, including the Pennsylvania Ballet, the Royal Ballet, Ballet San Jose and the San Francisco Ballet. During this time, he created some of his most successful works, such as Lambarena, Swan Lake Act II, and the critically acclaimed Carmen. Caniparoli has been an artistic associate at the San Francisco Ballet since 1987, and in this capacity created over 30 repertoire works for the company. His works have been seen internationally in more than 10 countries, including the United States, Canada, and Israel. His works have also been seen in many regional theaters in the US, such as the Mark Morris Dance Group, Boston Ballet, Ballet West, Atlanta Ballet, and Carolina Ballet. Caniparoli has received awards and recognition for his works, including Dance Magazine's Outstanding Choreography award for his work on A Midsummer Night's Dream, and a Choo-San Goh Choreography award for his piece Sonata Vivente. Caniparoli has also choreographed works for the Royal Winnipeg Ballet, Alberta Ballet, Ballet Nebraska, and the Chicago Festival Ballet. In addition to his choreographic works, Caniparoli has also worked as a director and teacher around the world. In 2010, Caniparoli was voted "Most PopularChoreographer" by Dance Magazine, and continues to be an inspiration in the dance community.

Michał Łasko (born 25 May 1991) is a Polish entrepreneur and venture capitalist. He is the founder of Inovo Ventures, a private equity and venture capital firm. He has been a mentor and investor in Techstars, one of the world's leading startup accelerators since 2013. Born and raised in Kraków, Poland, Łasko was educated at Jagiellonian University, where he received his Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering in 2013. It was during his time at university that he developed a passion for business and venture capital. After graduating, Łasko started a plastics joint venture in Kraków, as well as a venture capital firm in the same city. Following this, he started Inovo Ventures, a venture capital firm focused on the technology and digital sectors, which now has offices in Warsaw and San Francisco. Łasko is known for his dedication and determination to promoting startups and technology investment in Poland and the surrounding area. He has a particularly strong track record investing in healthtech, fintech and software companies. His investments have ranged from early-stage startups to established companies such as TransferGo and Fite. As a mentor and speaker, Łasko has worked with a number of organisations across Europe, such as the Central European Startup Awards and Cracow University of Economics, along with speaking engagements at events such as TEDxKrakow and TEDxWarsaw. He is also a mentor with Techstars, in which he has mentored more than 50 startups. Outside of venture capital and entrepreneurship, Łasko is also an active philanthropist, contributing to organisations such as Food for Life Global, which aims to build food supply chains in developing countries. He has also won several awards for his entrepreneurial achievements, most recently being listed as one of the ‘Top 30 Under 30 Entrepreneurs’ in 2018 by Forbes.

The Ventadour River is a river in the Haute-Vienne department of western France. It is a tributary of the Vienne River, which it joins at Saint-Junien. The Ventadour River originates in the foothills of the Massif Central, near Pierre-Buffière and Saint-Yrieix. It runs for a length of approximately 34 km (21 miles). The Ventadour River tends to keep a steady flow and is not very wide, with a mean width of 1,5 to 2 meters (5 to 6.5 ft.). The main tributary of the Ventadour River is the Claise River. It is joined at Pierrefitte-Nestalot by the Creuse River, a smaller tributary. The area around the Ventadour River is mostly agricultural land, with small villages dotting the landscape. The river's course is subject to occasional flooding. This can be particularly evident near the lower reaches of the Ventadour, where it meets the Vienne River. The river is home to a variety of fish, including pike and European perch, making it a popular spot for anglers and recreational fishing. The banks of the Ventadour are also prime locations for bird-watchers, with wild geese, ducks, and other waterfowl often seen in and around the river. The Ventadour and its banks have been used for centuries as a means of transport and communication, first by navigable vessels and later through roadways. It is now an important economic resource, providing a number of jobs in countless industries, including fishing, logging, and tourism. The environment of the Ventadour River is protected by several laws and regulations enacted by the French government. The river is considered to be an important part of France's natural heritage and is safe from pollution and development. In recent years, the Ventadour River has become a popular tourist destination, with visitors drawn to its riverside communities, as well as its abundant flora and fauna. Along its course, the Ventadour passes through several picturesque towns and regions, making it a popular venue for boating and other outdoor activities. The Ventadour River is a vital part of the French countryside and provides a retreat from the hustle and bustle of the cities. Its scenic beauty, abundance of nature, and importance to the local economy make it an essential part of the French landscape.

Austin Collie (born June 5, 1986) is a former American football wide receiver. He most recently played in the Canadian Football League (CFL) for the Hamilton Tiger-Cats. He played college football at Brigham Young University (BYU) and was drafted by the Indianapolis Colts in the fourth round of the 2009 NFL Draft. Early life and high school career Collie grew up in La Mesa, California and attended Mount Miguel High School, where he was a three-sport athlete in football, basketball and track and field. He was an All-San Diego League performer in both football and basketball. Collie played quarterback his freshman and sophomore years and moved to wide receiver as a junior, catching a team-high 61 passes for 1,034 yards and 14 touchdowns. He was named the San Diego Union-Tribune's San Diego Offensive Player of the Year and selected to the All-CIF first team as a senior. College career Collie attended BYU for his college career. During his freshman season in 2004, he was the only freshman to ever be named captain of the BYU football team and appeared in 11 games, chiefly on special teams. As a sophomore, he started every game and led all Mountain West Conference wide receivers with 84 receptions and earned first-team All-MWC honors. Collie had an outstanding junior season, setting BYU single-season records in receptions (107) and receiving yards (1,538). In 2006, he earned first-team All-Mountain West Conference honors and was an honorable mention All-American. He was also named an Academic All-American. As a senior in 2008, Collie recorded 72 receptions for 1,538 yards and all-time BYU records for career receptions (260) and receiving yards (3,845) and was named a first-team All-MWC and a semifinalist for the Biletnikoff Award, given to the nation's top receiver. Professional career Collie was selected in the fourth round (127th overall) of the 2009 NFL Draft by the Indianapolis Colts. He signed a four-year contract on June 18, 2009. Collie played in seven games for the Colts in 2009 and recorded 30 receptions for 323 yards and two touchdowns. He was placed on injured reserve on November 27, ending his rookie season. In 2010, he played in 13 games and had 60 catches for 649 yards and four touchdowns. Collie later joined the New England Patriots, Philadelphia Eagles, and San Francisco 49ers. He played for the Hamilton Tiger-Cats of the Canadian Football League (CFL) in the 2014 season, but retired prior to the 2015 season. Personal life Collie is married to former BYU track athlete Lacy Larsen and they have four children.

Florida Jayalath (born April 8th 1991) is an American social media star, actress, and entrepreneur. She rose to prominence in 2009 when she began posting comedic videos on her Vine channel, which garnered her over 330,000 followers. She then went on to become the face of numerous brands and the star of several web series, most notably for her role as the host and executive producer of the award-winning docuseries "My Black is Beautiful" for the Oprah Winfrey Network. She is also the founder of "The Connect Network", an online platform designed to facilitate meaningful connections and conversations between people of diverse backgrounds. Jayalath was born in Miami, Florida, where she joined the Academy of Arts at a young age and acted in local plays. She then attended New York University's Tisch School of the Arts, from which she graduated with a Bachelor's Degree in Communication and Media Studies. During this time, she pursued film acting, appearing in various independent projects as well as in a major motion picture, The Switch. After graduating in 2013, Jayalath moved to Los Angeles to begin her professional career. She quickly established herself as a social media star, as well as a host and talent for various platforms. Most notably, she hosted the web series “Daily Love” and acted as the Social Media Correspondent for MTV. She was chosen to host and executive produce the docuseries "My Black is Beautiful" for the Oprah Winfrey Network in 2015. The series won a Gracie Award in 2016. In addition to her television and digital work, Jayalath has been featured in advertisement campaigns and branded content for major brands such as Coca-Cola, AT&T, and many others. She is also the founder and CEO of “The Connect Network”, an online platform connecting diverse people and facilitating meaningful conversations about current events and social issues. In 2019, Jayalath was named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list. She lives in Los Angeles, California. In 2021, she launched her own podcast " The Connect Series" which provides a platform for diverse members of the community to share their personal stories and experiences. Florida Jayalath is a prominent social media star, actress and entrepreneur who has won numerous awards and accolades. She is also an advocate for representation and empowerment of minorities in the media. She currently works in Los Angeles, California.

. Anne Woodrooffe (born in 1949) is an English author, scriptwriter and television producer who has earned an impressive assortment of awards for her work. She is best known for her work on the popular series of childrens books about a rabbit called The Tales of Peter Rabbit, co-written with the late author and illustrator Beatrix Potter. Anne Woodrooffe was born in the county of Essex, England, the daughter of a naval officer and a stay-at-home mother. She attended the University of Cambridge, where she earned a bachelor's degree in English literature. Following her graduation, she began working as a script writer for television shows and movies, eventually becoming a leading producer for the BBC in the late 1970s. In 1981, Anne Woodrooffe penned the first in the series of classic books based on Beatrix Potter's classic novel 'The Tale of Peter Rabbit'. The series has since become a resounding success, and has been translated into a dozen languages, adapted into an Emmy Award-winning television series, and been used in numerous educational programs. In addition to the success of 'The Tales of Peter Rabbit' series, Woodrooffe has written a number of other books for both adults and children. She is well known for her work on two detective series for adults, entitled 'The Cambridge Mystery Series' and 'The Scotland Yard Series' which feature Collins and Kemp respectively as the main characters. In 2000, Woodrooffe was given an honorary doctorate of letters from the University of Essex in recognition of her contribution to English literature over the past thirty years. That same year, she received an Order of the British Empire (OBE) medal from Queen Elizabeth II. In 2004, Woodrooffe was appointed as trustee of the Beatrix Potter Society, where she has since taken up an active role in preserving and promoting Beatrix Potter's cultural legacy. In 2010, she collaborated with the National Trust to write and produce the 'Beatrix Potter Country' series, which aim to provide a comprehensive narrative of life and places in the spots which were particularly inspiring for the writer. Anne Woodrooffe is a celebrated writer, scriptwriter and producer who has contributed significantly to children's literature, television and film. Her work has been appreciated by both adults and children alike, and her books have been enjoyed by generations of readers around the world.

Rhino Foods is an American-based ice cream manufacturer located in Burlington, Vermont, United States. Established in 1988 by brothers Jeff & Barry Taylor, Rhino Foods has grown to be one of the largest manufacturers of ice cream ingredients, producing a wide array of products—from classic cookie dough and classic brownie pieces to candy-filled ice cream bars. The company uses a combination of traditional artisan-style batch processes and technologically advanced production methods in their factory. This commitment to quality (and flavor) encourages the company to use real ingredients including Vermont cream, egg whites and Vermont cane sugar syrup. On site, the company has a Quality Control Lab for intensive sanitation practices and testing. The staff is also trained in food safety, quality assurance and Good Manufacturing Practices, in accordance with the FDA. Rhino Foods also has a remarkable sustainability commitment, working with certified organic farms as well as local suppliers that use sustainable farming practices. They actively work to reduce energy use, water use and other nonrenewable resources. The company has also implemented a zero-waste program and is a leader in creating sustainable products from recycled or naturally regenerating ingredients. The company is a member of the Sustainable Food Trade Association, Vermont Businesses for Social Responsibility, the Vermont Natural Products Alliance and the Vermont Farm to Plate Network. Rhino Foods offers a wide range of products and services, as well as custom manufacturing capabilities. Many of their ingredients and preparations cater to specific needs such as gluten-free friendly, vegan-friendly, and preservative-free products. They offer inclusions (mix-ins) for hard ice cream, frozen custard, gelato and soft serve. Rhino Foods also offers premium toppings and coating chocolates, helping to make ice cream experiences unforgettable. The success of Rhino Foods lies in their commitment to quality, sustainability and reliability. They strive to exceed customers’ expectations in every way—from product innovation to shipping times—leading the industry to new heights. Of course, taste is always top priority. It’s why so many people love Rhino Foods’ products and return for them time and time again.

Kokkinobaphos Master is the first and only Greek master in the gaming industry. He is renowned for his work on mobile games and interactive content and is best known for the popular game RefugeeQuest. Kokkinobaphos was born in Athens, Greece in 1984. He has been an avid gamer since early childhood and began creating content for mobile gaming platforms in 2004. Throughout the years he has been involved in several projects in the interactive field and has specialized in game design, art direction and programming. In 2010, he released his first mobile game, RefugeeQuest, as part of an ongoing effort to spread awareness about the situation of refugees. The game has since had a successful launch and is renowned for its humanitarian approach and delicate subject matter. Kokkinobaphos has worked on multiple mobile games in his career, but RefugeeQuest remains his most popular and acclaimed project. Many have praised the game for being able to balance its educational and entertainment value. His works have also been published in several magazines and have been featured in various exhibitions around the world. Over the years, Kokkinobapos has collaborated with various top companies in the gaming field and has been hard at work developing and releasing a wide range of interactive content. He continues to be heavily involved in the gaming industry and is constantly looking for ways to innovate and push the boundaries of what is possible with interactive content. Kokkinobaphos is the first and only Greek master in the gaming industry and has made a considerable contribution to the landscape. His work has won him multiple awards and recognition and he continues to be one of the most respected and influential figures in the field.

The Optimists of Nine Elms is a British punk rock band formed in 1976 in London, England. The band is composed of vocalist/guitarist Terry Scott, bassist/vocalist Terry Smith, drummer John Hatfield and guitarist/keyboardist Marianne "Maz" Aylward. The band was formed while they were all at school in London, beginning as a pure punk band, playing cover versions of other punk bands' songs. The band soon began writing and recording their own material, and released their first single, "No Time For Love", in March 1977. This was followed by their debut album, Nine Elms, in mid-1977. The album, which was praised for its witty songwriting and aggressive yet melodic sound, established the band's reputation in the punk rock scene, with the single "Lies That Kill" being a UK top twenty hit. The group's second album, Burn It Down, was released in 1980, and was widely lauded by both fans and critics as a darker, grittier record than its predecessor. The band's live shows were also becoming increasingly ambitious, with seven vocalists and multiple instruments creating an intense and powerful energy. The Optimists of Nine Elms toured extensively throughout the UK during this period, playing gigs in pubs and clubs as well as larger venues including the newly opened 9 Elms Station in London. Despite critical and commercial success, the band's third album, Lost in the Fire, flopped upon its release in 1983. Subsequently, the band split up, citing internal creative differences. Today, The Optimists of Nine Elms's music is still appreciated by fans of punk rock, and their influence can still be heard in more modern punk material. Although the band did not achieve the mass global recognition that the Sex Pistols or other punk acts did, it is regarded as one of the best punk bands to come out of Britain.

The Vels were a 1980s R&B group from Detroit, Michigan. It was composed of three members, Kenny "K-Nine" Davis (vocals, drums), Sonny Ellis (keyboards, vocals), and Reggie Moore (guitars, keyboards, vocals). They are best known for writing and recording the #1 Top 40 hit song "Love High" in 1988. The band formed in 1983, when the three members met during high school. Kenny Davis had a background in gospel music and Reggie Moore played in a funk band; they met Sonny Ellis while they were both attending high school. The three members instantly clicked musically, and decided to form a group. The Vels played gigs around Detroit and were eventually discovered by a representative from Island Records. They were signed to the record label in 1987 and released their debut album, On The Line, in 1988. The album gently flowed between soulful and uptempo dance rhythms. The band's biggest hit was "Love High," which reached the top of the US Top 40 chart. The song was featured on MTV and was nominated at the 1989 Grammy Awards. The band was unable to maintain their success and disbanded in 1992. They occasionally reunited and played shows together, but never quite reached the heights of fame they did in their heyday. The Vels' influence is still felt today, with their music helping to shape the modern R&B and soul music scene. Many of their hits are still featured in popular media, and are still cherished as timeless classics from the 1980s. They will undoubtedly continue to be remembered as one of the most important acts of that era.

Postpaid mobile phone refers to a service contract between a mobile phone user and a network carrier that requires the user to pay for the service after the usage. With the postpaid service, the user receives a monthly bill from the network provider based on the services used in the prior billing period. Typically postpaid plans require customers to enter into a one or two year contract, but depending on the network provider, customers may be able to select a month-to-month option. A distinguishing feature of postpaid service is that typically users do not need to pay for the phone up front. For example if a customer signs up for 24 months of service and purchases an iPhone, the customer may not have to pay the full sale price of the phone but over the 24 month the total cost of the phone is incorporated into the monthly service cost. Most carriers will require a credit check when you sign up for postpaid service, as part of the contract requires you to pay for the service at the end of each billing period. Postpaid services also have a wider selection of data plans when compared to prepaid plans. This is due to increased revenue that can be generated from customers who use large data amounts. For example, a postpaid customer is likely to have access to larger data buckets than a prepaid customer. This can make postpaid services attractive to those who do not want to worry about running out of data or having service cut off mid-month. Most carriers will offer both prepaid and postpaid services and some may even offer promotional incentives such as discounts or promotional bonus amounts at the beginning of a contract. When you are comparing between postpaid and prepaid it is important to review each carriers pricing structure to determine how costly each type of plan is in the long run. Additionally, it is important to also review study the features and services that are available with each type of plan. In general, postpaid mobile phone services is a more costly system than prepaid mobile phones but it provides the user the convenience of a monthly billing system. It can be beneficial to those who require a larger data plan than what is available with a prepaid plan, or for customers who need the flexibility of not always having to top-up their prepaid plans.

Thea Burns (born 1994) is a British singer and songwriter from London England. She is a Grammy-nominated pop uplifting artist, and has been signed to RCA Records since 2020. Thea began her musical career at an early age, having played the flute and drums in the church choir, where she learned the basics of classical music theory. By the age of 16, she had written her first song, which led to a series of performances at small venues and on the underground circuit. Thea has released several EPs and singles since signing with RCA records, including her 2020 singles "Love Without Fear", "Not So Alone" and "Fountain". The song "Not So Alone" was a particular success, with the music video gaining over one million views on YouTube and the single being nominated for a Grammy Award. Thea has written and collaborated with some of the biggest names in UK and US pop music, including Clean Bandit, Whitney Houston, Nile Rodgers, Joss Stone and Ne-Yo. She has been an invited guest at multiple high-profile events, such as the Critics' Choice Awards and EMA Awards. Thea's music has been described as thoughtful and uplifting pop with clean, intricate rhythm and catchy melody. Speaking about her own sound, Thea has said, “The style of my music is meant to send a message. A message for love, for peace, for togetherness, for unity. I want to speak to people's hearts. I want people to know that they are not alone. That music can empower them to make a difference in the world. That's my sound”. In addition to her solo work, Thea has been involved in charity work and has been a vocal supporter of cancer charities such as Cancer Research UK and Macmillan. She is also an ambassador for the UK charity, The Prince's Trust. Thea continues to write and release her music, as well as collaborate with other artists and appear at events. As she continues to make her mark in the world of music, Thea hopes to continue to spread messages of positivity and hope through her art.

"I Don't Wanna Go to Bed" is a single by Canadian pop-punk band Simple Plan, released on February 8, 2016. The song was the second single to be released from their fifth studio album, Taking One for the Team (2016). The song was co-written by lead vocalist Pierre Bouvier, bassist David Desrosiers and guitarists Sebastien Lefebvre and Jeff Stinco, alongside producers and songwriters Stephan Moccio and Jamie Scott, the latter two of whom also produced the song. The song features a "strummy, upbeat" sound similar to Simple Plan's other releases and has a "feel good" vibe to it. The single was first mentioned in a Rolling Stone interview with drummer Chuck Comeau in which he said that the song tells the story of never wanting to go to bed, signifying a desire to live life to its fullest. The music video was released on February 8, 2016 and directed by Simple Plan's producer and co-writer, Stephan Moccio. It features footage of Simple Plan at a house party being filmed on iPads by guests. The video features Zendaya and Grant Gustin as two of the partygoers in the video as well as footage from an unfinished Sk8 Park. The song was praised by critics for its upbeat and catchy nature and its "feel good vibes". "I Don't Wanna Go to Bed" was a moderate commercial success in both Canada and the United States. In Canada, the single reached a peak of #18 on the Canadian Hot 100, while in the United States it peaked at #22 on the Billboard Mainstream Top 40. The single also reached the top 40 in Australia, Czech Republic, Italy, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom. The song was performed live at a number of festivals, including the Wango Tango Festival in the United States and Rock Am Ring in Germany. In 2017, the song was featured in the soundtrack of the online video game Rocksmith, the soundtrack of soccer game FIFA 17, and in an advertisement campaign in the United States by Subway. In 2020, the song was featured in a commercial advertising the American fast-food chain Sonic Drive-In.

Kim Jong-suk (Korean: 김정숙; or Kim Jeong-suk; February 16, 1919 – September 22, 1949) was a North Korean anti-Japanese guerrilla fighter, politburo member of the Workers' Party of Korea, and the mother of North Korea's current leader, Kim Jong-un. Born in the Heungnam region of the Hamgyong province in Korea, Kim was considered to be a loyal follower of her husband and leader of the North Korean Worker's Party, Kim Il-sung. A product of the Japanese colonization of Korea, Kim was deeply opposed to the Japanese occupation and organized guerrilla groups to fight against them. She was also an active member of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea, and greatly contributed to the North Korean independence movement. Kim's most prominent contribution to the North Korean cause was becoming an active member in the guerrilla movement against the Japanese rule. During this time, she became the leader of the Changso Faction, a division of the Korean People's Revolutionary Army, and led several successful attacks against Japanese forces. Kim also assisted in underground education and in the transportation of participants in the struggle for independence. In 1946, she was inducted into the Politburo at the first party conference, a feat which was made possible due to her many attempts at revolutionizing the country. After the end of the Japanese occupation, Kim continued to actively participate in the struggle towards a communist state in North Korea. She encouraged the organization of farmers, trained guerrilla units, and was a central figure in the establishment of the Social Democratic Women's Union. She was highly respected due to her diligent efforts, and people referred to her as "The Nation's Mother." In 1949, Kim gave birth to her first son, Kim Jong-il, making her the mother of the future North Korean "dear leader" Kim Jong-il. After the birth of her son, Kim was struck with cerebro-vascular disease, and she died at the age of thirty in September 1949. Since her death, Kim Jong-suk has been honored by the North Korean government as a hero of the North Korean independence movement. Her image can still be seen around North Korea today, including in the documentary film Sea of Blood, which depicts her involvement in the independence struggle. In addition, she was honored posthumously in 1977 when her portrait was hung in the Supreme People's Assembly, and the Kim Jong-suk Medal was established in her name. Kim Jong-suk will always remain a figure of prominence and admiration in North Korean history. She was a brave and hardworking individual who dedicated her life to the struggle for independence and worked tirelessly to ensure the liberation of North Korea. She will be remembered as an icon of liberation and a symbol of selflessness for generations to come.

Nicola Rauti (born 5 May 1995) is an Italian footballer who currently plays as a midfielder for Serie B team Frosinone. Rauti is a product of Roma's youth academy, having signed his first professional contract with the club in August 2011. During his time with Roma, he mainly played for the club's Primavera team, making 18 appearances in Serie A Primavera. He also made his where he played three times in the Coppa Italia. In 2014, Rauti was loaned out to Serie B club Frosinone, where he made 23 appearances and scored one goal. After his successful loan spell, Rauti was signed on a permanent basis by Frosinone in July 2015. Since then he has become an important player for Frosinone, making 123 appearances in the Serie B and providing eight assists. Rauti was also part of Italy's U-20 team at the 2015 FIFA U-20 World Cup in New Zealand. He made four appearances in the tournament and scored one goal in Italy's match against Korea DPR. At the international level, Rauti has represented Italy at the U-14, U-16, U-17, U-18, U-19 and U-20 level. He hasn't yet been capped at the senior level, but he will continue to play for Frosinone in the hopes of earning a senior call-up. Rauti is a talented midfielder who is very comfortable on the ball and is capable of playing in a variety of positions. He is a relentless worker and is always looking to create chances for his side. He is also a hard-working defender who understands the defensive side of the game. He is currently one of the most talented players in Italy's lower divisions and is deserving of a move to the higher levels of Italian football. He will look to continue his impressive performances for Frosinone and break into the senior Italian national team in the near future.

Thomas Radford (born 1943) is an internationally renowned musician and composer from the United Kingdom. He is best known for his spectacular performances of British folk music, and has been a major influence for many performers who have followed in his footsteps. Radford began learning the violin and traditional English folk music in his early twenties after being inspired by a James Madison University professor. He fell in love with the sound and strived to learn as much as he could about the genre. His teachers included Bert Jansch and Ivor Cutler. He began performing locally with other amateur folk players before eventually touring the U.K. and Europe as a solo artist. Radford performed at numerous major British folk festivals, including the Edinburgh Folk Festival, the Cambridge Folk Festival and the Glasgow Folk Festival. He quickly became a major draw with his audience members, commanding large crowds and rave reviews. In 1971, he recorded his first album, The Green Man, a melting pot of traditional and original pieces. This was followed by several other critically acclaimed albums in the 1970s and 1980s. He famously joined forces with fellow folk musicians Bill Leader and Martin Carthy in 1976 to form a folk trio, which was later named 'Radford, Leader & Carthy'. They went on to tour extensively, made an album and gained significant success within the folk music industry. In 2001, he worked with writer Rob Young on a compilation album, Songs and Dances from the British Isles. This album featured some of the best traditional English music from across Britain, such as Scotland, Wales and England. His own compositions were included, as well as some of his own interpretations of his favourite songs. In recognition of his immense contribution to the traditional music industry, Radford won the Gold Badge Award in 2011 and was appointed as a Member of the British Empire in 2017. Radford is still performing various concerts and festivals today. He has highlighted that he is excited for the folk scene to be improving in popularity and for it to enter new generations. His first novel - a collection of folk songs, stories and recipes - is due to be published in 2020.

Sergei Shmatko (born 20 April 1958) is a Russian statesman and former minister of energy from 2009 to 2012. He has held various government positions since 1992 and is a member of United Russia. Early life Shmatko was born on 20 April 1958 in Moscow, where he graduated from a secondary specialized industrial college in 1978. In 1985 he graduated from the Moscow Institute of Electronic Engineering with a specialty in automation and methodical management of technological processes. Career In the early 1990s Shmatko was a major at the Leningrad Military Commandant's Institute. From 1992 to 1995 he was the head of the Moscow Police Department. From 1995 to 2000 he worked as an adviser to the head of the Interior Ministry. In 2000 he became the First Deputy Minister of the Interior. He served in this office until 2002 and then became advisor to the Ministry of Economic Development and Trade. In 2006 Shmatko was appointed Deputy Minister of Energy of the Russian Federation. Three years later he was appointed Minister of Energy in the government of Prime Minister Vladimir Putin. He served in this office until 16 May 2012. In October 2019, Shmatko has been appointed as the Head of the Federal Agency for State Property Management. Political views Shmatko is a member of United Russia, Russia’s dominant political party. His views are primarily pro-Putin and he advocates for greater economic and political unity between European and Russian countries. He has called for energy security in the world and stated that nuclear energy should not be disregarded as an energy source. Awards and honours In 2009 Shmatko was presented with the Order of Friendship, an award bestowed upon individuals who have "made a great contribution to strengthening friendship and cooperation between nations". He also holds a number of honorary titles and awards, including the Order for Services to the Homeland, 1st class, and the Order of Honour. Personal life Shmatko is married and has a son.

The 2019 Asian Women's U23 Volleyball Championship is the sixth edition of the Asian U23 Women's Volleyball Championship, organized by the Asian Volleyball Confederation (AVC). The tournament was held from June 11-20, 2019 at Nouhad Nawfal Sports City, in Zouk Mikael, Lebanon. The 2019 edition featured twenty one teams from across Asia, with teams split into four pools at the start of the tournament. Thailand was the defending champions, having won the 2017 edition in Naypyidaw, Myanmar. In the first round of the tournament, China topped Pool A with an undefeated record of 5-0, while South Korea and Vietnam topped Pools B and D with 4-1 and 4-0 respectively. Pool C was topped by Turkmenistan, who dropped only two sets in the round. In the second round, Malaysia occupied the top spot in Pool A with a 5-0 record, while Vietnam repeated its performance to top Pool B, and China finished unbeaten in Pool C. Thailand came out on top in the fourth pool with just one loss to their name. China eventually emerged as the champions of the tournament, beating Kazakhstan in the finals in three straight sets. The hosts, Lebanon, who started the tournament with a 3-2 loss to China, eventually ended in 9th place after beating Singapore in the playoff match. The final standings saw China, Kazakhstan, Thailand, and South Korea occupy the top four spots respectively. This was the fifth edition to be won by China, who last won in 2016 in Iran. The 2019 edition of the tournament also marked the debut of newly formed unit, the East Timor Volleyball Federation. The international debut of the country ended with a sixteenth place finish, losing all group matches, including the match against Chinese Taipei. The tournament also featured several new regulations designed to help develop volleyball in the underdeveloped parts of Asia, including a newly implemented rule in which countries could field a maximum of two foreign players in the tournament. This regulation was proposed to empower the developing players in the Asian region.

Charles Perceval, 7th Earl of Egmont (1735-1818) was an important figure in British politics during the late 18th and early 19th centuries. He was a close ally of Prime Minister William Pitt, who appointed him as First Lord of the Admiralty in 1783. He served in that post for 17 years, making him the longest-serving First Lord of the Admiralty until the 20th century. The Earl was born the son of Charles Perceval, 6th Earl of Egmont, in 1735. He matriculated from University College, Oxford, in 1752, before serving as an MP for Eye from 1756 to 1776. From 1771 he was an active member of the Cabinet in the House of Lords. His background in naval affairs was crucial to his appointment as First Lord of the Admiralty. As First Lord, the Earl of Egmont presided over a period of great expansion in the Royal Navy, and worked to improve the navy’s response to Napoleonic France. On his orders, in 1783, the Royal Navy was sent to the Caribbean to protect British possessions from attack. During his tenure, the navy underwent a major reorganization, which included the addition of more ships, increased manpower, and greater discipline among officers and enlisted sailors. He retired from the Admiralty in 1800, citing ill health and citing the ongoing Napoleonic Wars. He was succeeded as First Lord of the Admiralty by Lord Barham. In 1801, the Earl of Egmont succeeded to his father's title, and returned to the House of Lords. He continued to serve in Parliament until his death in 1818. He was a noted patron of the arts during his lifetime, and was responsible for introducing a number of important works to the British public. Many of his friendships with writers and musicians are well-documented and still influence the culture to this day. The Earl of Egmont was an influential figure in British politics, and his tireless work in the Admiralty helped shape the modern Royal Navy. He is remembered as a man of quiet dignity, intelligence, and integrity. His legacy as one of the most important members of the House of Lords in the late 18th century is still honoured to this day.

Real Cortijo de San Isidro is a historic estate located in San Isidro, Spain. It is also known as the Cortijo de San Isidro or simply "San Isidro". The estate has been in existence since the 17th century and it is owned by the Agustin family. The estate consists of over 700 hectares of land, including residential buildings, a lake, a chapel, a water mill, and various fields used for agriculture and livestock. A wide variety of crops and livestock can be found on the estate, including corn, almonds, olives, cider apples, and horses. The estate is also home to a number of heritage trees, including up to 250-year-old olive trees. The estate is steeped in history, with a large collection of local artefacts, literature and handcrafted items from all over Spain. The estate also claims to be the home of the first “Limonero” (or lemon tree) ever planted in the area. The estate also houses a museum dedicated to local culture and art. Real Cortijo has become popular with tourists seeking to experience Spain’s past. In 2017, the estate hosted the Avian Migration Festival, a month-long event celebrating the arrival of migratory birds during fall. In 2018, the estate was declared a Biodiversity Hotspot, with visitation restricted in order to maintain the habitat. In addition to its historic value, the estate also serves as a working farm and recreational area. The Agustin family has established a campground and equestrian center, as well as a restaurant which serves local dishes made with ingredients produced on the estate. The estate is also a popular destination for events such as weddings, company parties and sport activities. The estate is maintained by La Fundación Real Cortijo de San Isidro, which was established in 2016 with the aim of preserving the heritage and traditions of the estate. The foundation provides educational activities and organizes events such as concerts, exhibitions and festivals in order to promote local culture. Real Cortijo de San Isidro is a living example of a traditional Spanish estate, a constantly evolving oasis of natural beauty, culture and heritage.

Qianjiang Motorcycle (Chinese: 钱江摩托车; pinyin: qiánjiāng mótuōchē) is a Chinese manufacturer of motorcycles and scooters. Established in the year of 1969, Qianjiang is owned by Danbo Holding Co. Ltd, which is located in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, approximately 240 km south of Shanghai. Qianjiang is one of the leading manufacturers of motorcycles and scooters in China and is known for producing excellent-value motorcycles and scooters. The company focuses on providing competitively-priced and simple-to-use motorbikes, of which many models feature fuel-injected engines and electric-start technology.
