The most popular Qianjiang models are the daily-use CC and the CG150, which is popular for those taking long-distance rides. Qianjiang has also collaborated with other companies to produce more advanced bikes. In recent years, Qianjiang has collaborated with Italian giant, Piaggio, to develop the NKD100 and NKD125 scooters. And in 2021, Qianjiang began co-developing 80cm³ motorcycles with Honda, with the first prototype model being unveiled on April 2021. Qianjiang has also gone beyond motorcycles; the company also produces single-person bike-sharing systems, utilizing electric powered vehicles. The system employs an electronic locking system which allows bikes to be reserved and unlocked with a smartphone. As of 2021 the Qianjiang bike-sharing system has expanded to over 60 cities in China. As of 2021, Qianjiang produces approximately 1 million motorcycles per year and exports to over 20 countries worldwide, including the United States and European countries. The company has received a National Award for Quality Management, amongst other awards and recognitions. Qianjiang is aiming to become a global brand in the manufacturing of ultra-low-emission vehicles. The company is by embracing the growing trend towards green transportation and expanding its product line-up to include more electric-powered models. In 2021, the company’s joint-venture with Honda resulted in the QJ125-4V, an emissions-free, electric-powered scooter that has been well-received around the world. The company is also involved in developing an autonomous electric-powered scooter.

Berith Melin (born May 10, 1945) is a Swedish businessperson who is best known as the founder and former CEO of Inter IKEA Systems B.V., a global company that owns and distributes the IKEA products. Berith Melin was born in Kalmar, Sweden, and graduated from Lund University in 1966. In 1972, he entered the world of business when he was hired as the manager at a small furniture store in his hometown. He was quickly promoted to be the head of the furniture department at a larger chain store in Malmö. Melin's business career really took off in 1983 when he joined the IKEA Group. His first job was as CEO of Inter IKEA Systems B.V., the company behind IKEA's global expansion. Under his leadership, IKEA opened more than 300 stores in over 30 countries. Melin was a driving force behind IKEA's unique business model and implemented innovative methods to keep costs down and maximize profits. He famously used a flat-pack form for many of the store’s products, allowing for more efficient storage and shipment of the products to its customers. This allowed the company to offer its products at lower prices than its competitors. Melin retired from IKEA in 2006 after 23 years of service. He continued to show his dedication to the company by serving as chairman of the IKEA Foundation, the organization responsible for IKEA's philanthropic efforts, until 2011. In 2009, Melin was awarded the Swedish Order of the Polar Star, an honor given by the government of Sweden. His other awards and recognitions include several honorary doctorates and a commendation by the King of Sweden. Berith Melin is respected by many as a business visionary and a driving force behind the international success of IKEA. He is seen as a role model for innovative, customer-driven business models and a strong advocate for corporate social responsibility.

Padilla, Bolivia is a small town in the Bolivian countryside located in the Department of Santa Cruz. It lies 56km from Santa Cruz de la Sierra, the department's capital. Originally founded by the Spanish Empire in 1576, the town has a population of just over 3,000 people. Padilla has a semi-arid climate with high temperatures during the summer months (November-March). Its main form of employment is through agriculture, growing potatoes, manioc, and maize. The area also has a number of beef cattle farms. The economy of Padilla is mainly sustained by tourism. Tourists come to visit the town’s colonial architecture, as well as the surrounding nature reserves. These reserves boast an array of animals and plants, from the endangered giant armadillo to a variety of orchids. Padilla is a culturally diverse town with a mix of Spanish, German, Italian, and indigenous Bolivian traditions. An important event in the town is the Mysicu Festival, which celebrates traditional music and mysticism. The municipality of Padilla is also invested in the preservation of its local areas. One example is the protection and rehabilitation of Rio Caraparí, the local river. In 1964 it was treated by the Padilla public with the support of local authorities and was declared part of the environmental heritage in 2002 by the Santa Cruz government. Padilla is considered to be a traditional contrast to the large and noisy city of Santa Cruz. Its tranquil atmosphere is the ideal place for those looking to escape the hustle and bustle of the Bolivian city life. Overall, Padilla is a rural town full of culture and nature. It is the perfect spot for those looking to experience Bolivian heritage while taking in the area's natural beauty.

Hridayakumari (also known as Hridi) (31 May 1903 – 30 April 1951) was an Indian revolutionary and feminist of Bengal who led an armed struggle to free India from the British rule. She was one of the most prominent women revolutionaries in the Indian independence movement, and was a member the Indian Republican Army and the Azad Hind Fauj. Hridayakumari was born on 31 May 1903 in East Bengal. She was born into a family of high status, but she was determined to contribute to the independence movement. From a young age, she had shown a reluctance to society binding her to traditions, and actively protesting against such traditions to carve out a liberated space for herself. Hridayakumari joined the armed struggle against the British rule along with other women revolutionaries. Bengal had become a hotbed of revolutionary activities, and this was a time of nationalist fervour. Realising the potential of women revolutionaries, Bengal saw some of its most prominent women take a stand against the British rule. Hridayakumari was highly active in this struggle, and was part of the All Bengal Students’ Association – which was an organization to support the independence struggle. During 1921-1922, she was trained in guerilla warfare. In the latter half of 1922, she formed the All Bengal Women’s Organisation with the intention of promoting patriotism and nationalism among women. In 1930, she was part of the group organised by Subhas Chandra Bose which conducted an armed struggle for the independence of India. She was also a member of the Azad Hind Fauj, which was an army of independence fighters. During this period, Hridayakumari was arrested and imprisoned multiple times. She was tortured in prison, but she never gave up her cause, and kept fighting against the British rule. Eventually, she died of tuberculosis in 1951. The Indian Government posthumously awarded her with the Tamra Patra in 2015, in recognition of her brave and unwavering activism. Her name is also inscribed in the Red Fort Museum in Delhi, as acknowledgement of her contribution to the Indian independence movement. Hridayakumari’s astounding courage and determination to fight for India’s independence makes her an inspirational figure today.

Walking the Floor Over You (box set) is a collection of late country music singer Ernest Tubb's most popular records. The set was released by the label Bear Family Records in 2009 and consists of four CDs. Disc one features a selection of Tubb's early recordings from 1936 to 1945, including hits such as "Walking the Floor Over You" and "Soldier's Last Letter". Disc two contains more of Tubb's classic recordings from 1945 to 1952, including the chart-toppers "Slipping Around" and "I'll Never Get Out of This World Alive". Disc three's collection includes recordings from 1953 to 1961, such as the Top 10 hit "Let's Say Goodbye Like We Said Hello". The fourth disc includes live recordings from 1952 to1979. The box set was praised by critics for its accumulation of some of the best music of Tubb's musical career. Dan Forte of Vintage Guitar noted that the recordings capture an "era of country music that has all but disappeared". The album was well-received by Ernest Tubb fans, and won Album of the Year at the 2010 Academy of Country Music Awards. Walking the Floor Over You (box set) is a valuable addition for any fan of Tubb's music. The collection captures the diverse sounds of his career, from early honky-tonk to electric country. It is a testament to the influence and legacy of Ernest Tubb, one of the most successful and significant names in country music.

Jackie Akello (born 12 March 1984) is a Ugandan entrepreneur, public figure and Politician. She is the current Member of Parliament for Amuria District in Uganda. Early life Akello was born on March 12, 1984 in Aciro Sub-county, Amuria District, Eastern Uganda. She attended Primary school at Lango College and later St. Mary's Secondary School before graduating from Nsamizi Training Institute in 2006. Political career Akello was first elected to the 10th Parliament of Uganda in 2016 as a Member of the Parliament of Uganda from the National Resistance Movement party. In Parliament, she serves as the chairperson of the Institute of Parliamentary Studies. In addition, she also serves on the Physical Infrastructure Committee of the 9th Parliament of Uganda and the Gender, Labour, and Social Development Committee of the Parliament of Uganda. Business In addition to her political career, Akello is an entrepreneur, with business interests ranging from finance, real estate, ICT, and hospitality. In 2020, Akello launched the Ugandan Girls Mentorship Drive, an initiative to empower women and girls in the country through mentorship, life-skills training, and access to education and health services. Philanthropy Akello has led several philanthropic initiatives in her district in Amuria. She has provided scholarships to needy students and established a community library, which she opened in 2018, with the mission to improve literacy levels in her community. She also led efforts to build a modern market to support rural entrepreneurs. Personal life Akello is married and mother of two children. She is a devout Christian and an active member of Makerere Pentecostal Church. She was awarded the “Most Inspiring Woman MP of the Year” award in 2019 by the Forum for Democratic Change.

Henderson Park is a community park in Chehalis, Washington, located near the historic downtown core. The park offers a range of recreational activities and amenities, including a playground, picnic shelter, open-field areas, and a walking path. The park is also a popular spot for fishing in the Chehalis River. Built in 1915, the same year the city of Chehalis was founded, Henderson Park is the oldest and largest park in the city. It was named after William Henderson, a prominent local educator and pioneer of the town. The park was further developed in 1935 by the Civilian Conservation Corps, a federal program active during the Great Depression. Today, Henderson Park is widely used for communal events and activities, such as the annual Chehalis Garlic Festival and the Chehalis Farmers Market. It's also popular with walkers, joggers, and cyclists as it provides access to the nearby Chehalis River Trail. The manicured ballpark is also home to the Chehalis Little League and several soccer fields. In 2014, the park underwent a major remodeling project funded by the city, local businesses, and private donations. The upgrades included the installation of a splash park with water features, a shaded playground and shelter, a picnic area, and an upgraded walking path. The upgrades also included the installation of new landscaping and vegetation, as well as a larger parking lot and improved lighting. Henderson Park is open from 6am to 10pm and is free for the public to use. It is located at the corner of N. Main Street and S. Market Street in Chehalis, Washington. It is adjacent to the Chehalis Riverside Park, which includes a swimming pool, community center, and other recreational amenities. Overall, Henderson Park is a great place for Chehalis community members to relax, unwind, and enjoy the outdoors. With its convenient location, ample activities and amenities, and ample green space, it is a popular spot for locals and visitors alike.

Bernard J. Dowd (1928-2020) was a leading Canadian lawyer, jurist and philanthropist. Born near Tillsonburg, Ontario, to John and Margaret Dowd, Bernard was the oldest of their four children. He was an avid reader and an excellent student, graduating top of his class in physics at the University of Toronto in 1948. His studies in law at Osgoode Hall Law School earned him the Outstanding Academic Achievement Award upon graduation in 1951. Dowd began his legal career in 1951 with Shields, Bracken, Morrison & Knill in Toronto, Ontario, where he was a partner until 1960. His practice focused primarily on corporate and securities law. He was the founding partner of Langlois Dowd, a law firm that he established in 1960 and led until 2000, the year he retired. As a leader in the legal profession, Dowd was a sought-after speaker and advisor, advising many large corporations. In 1975, he was appointed Queen’s Counsel for the Province of Ontario. He also held numerous major appointments in the Ontario Court of Appeal, the Ontario Supreme Court, and the Federal Court of Canada, often sitting as an Appellate Judge and giving lectures. Throughout his career, Bernard was dedicated to philanthropy, giving his time and resources to the establishment of charities and the enhancement of educational opportunities in Canada. He created the Langlois Dowd Scholarship Fund in 1989, providing financial assistance to students attending Osgoode Hall Law School. His distinguished commitment to the community earned him recognition by the Law Society of Upper Canada, the Canadian Bar Association, the Empire Club of Canada, and many other organizations. In 1987, Dowd was awarded the Order of Ontario, one of Canada’s highest honours. He was also a long-time Member and Chairman of the Legal Aid Ontario Board, a Member of the Advisory Board of the Ontario Civilian Commission on Police Services, and Grand Patron of the Law Society of Upper Canada Past Presidents’ Foundation. Bernard J. Dowd passed away on February 3, 2020, in Toronto, Ontario at the age of 91. He was remembered fondly by his friends, colleagues and members of the legal community who recognized his tireless dedication to justice and charity.

This Is Augustus Pablo (also known as Original Rockers) is a reggae album released in 2004 on the British label Essential Records. It was the first solo album by the Jamaican musician Augustus Pablo, who is best known for his melodica-driven dub albums in the 1970s. This Is Augustus Pablo is a compilation of new recordings that Pablo made in 1988-89 with the Roots Radics, Eyeball, Blacka Morwell and others, mixed by engineer/producer Clive Hunt. Augustus Pablo (born Horace Swaby, 1954 - 1999) is one of Jamaica's best known and beloved musicians. He is credited with helping to revolutionize the reggae sound, introducing a melodic keyboard sound, and helping to popularize the use of synthesizers. He is also known for utilizing the melodica - a small keyboard that is powered by air - as a unique instrument in the reggae music. Throughout his career, he worked with some of the greatest Jamaican recording artists, including Bob Marley, Lee “Scratch” Perry, and King Tubby. This Is Augustus Pablo consists of up-tempo rocksteady, relaxed reggae, percussive dub and other genres, combining roots reggae and mentor Lloyd "Bullwackie" Barnes' New York-style reggae. The album features a number of Pablo's best-known tunes, including “Organic Rockers” and “Java,” and also boasts two collaborations with Horace Andy, as well as extended dub versions of many of the tracks. The album was released to critical and commercial success and is considered one of the greatest reggae albums of all time. It has been sampled in works by the likes of the Beastie Boys and hip-hop group The Fugees. The album was included in the book “1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die”. In 2006, ‘This Is Augustus Pablo’ was re-issued by the label Esoldun in a 2 CD-set, including several bonus tracks, further emphasizing the greatness of this timeless album. The album is a testament to the genius of Augustus Pablo, and to the lasting impact of his music. Its beauty and inventiveness still resonates today and remains a favorite amongst reggae fans.

Musoshi Mine is a large underground tungsten mine located in Japanese prefecture of Iwate. It is owned and operated by Japanese conglomerate Mitsui & Co. The mine was discovered in 1931 by nearby residents who found tungsten ore in the area and developed an adit, or horizontal underground mining tunnel. It was officially registered as a mining spot in 1938 and began commercial operations in 1941. Since its original discovery, the Musoshi Mine has become one of Japan's largest producers of tungsten ore. It is renowned for its high-grade ore deposits and is the only underground tungsten mine in the country. Europe, China and the United States are major importers of Musoshi Mine ore with the primary customer being Phillips Japan. The tungsten ore mined at Musoshi is often used by the machining and electronics industry due to its hardness and durability. At the mine, a variety of mining techniques are employed including both traditional mining methods and modern mining equipment. The main mining methods employed at Musoshi Mine are sublevel drift mining, room and pillar mining, cut and fill mining and long hole mining. Traditional mining techniques employed at the mine include the use of hand tools and wheeled carts. Ore is transported from the mine via cableways and a gondola lift to the surface. Upon reaching the surface, the ore is processed at a smelter located in the nearby town of Noda. At the smelter, the ore is crushed and heated in a furnace to separate the tungsten from other metals and minerals. Tungsten ore is then sold primarily to manufacturers for use in their product lines or for further processing. Documents from the Japanese Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry describe Musoshi Mine as the country's most productive and advanced underground mine. This is largely due to Mitsui & Co.'s investment in modern mining equipment and safety protocols, which has allowed the mine to maintain higher production rates while mitigating the risk of disasters and accidents. In addition to tungsten ore, Musoshi Mine is known for its tourism and education tours. Tourists can take part in guided tours led by knowledgeable miners who explain the history and operations of the mine to the visitors. As part of the tours, visitors are able to observe the miner's work, visit the mine's guest room and even have the chance to wear miners' apparel. Educational tours exist for children and are designed to introduce them to the basics of tungsten mining and mineral processing. Musoshi Mine has remained an important part of Japanese industry for almost 90 years. Its tungsten ore is used in countless products and its tours offer a unique chance to explore a piece of Japanese history.

Depravity is the debut studio album of American rap-rock band Bully, released on March 16, 2020. The album was recorded over the course of 2019 and is the first full-length project released by the group. Described as a "dark, mature sounding record" the album explores themes such as mental health and relationships with an introspective yet aggressive approach. A major streaming success, Depravity received nominations for the Grammy Award for Best Rock Album and the Juno Award for Rap/Hip-Hop Album of the Year. The lead single, "Do You Know?", was released on February 28, 2020. The song blends elements of rock, hip hop and trap, featuring samples of vocal harmonies. It was positively received by critics, garnering praise for its aggressive nature and the bands potential. The second single, "Outcast", was released on March 6, 2020. Accompanied by an abstract visual, the song is a dark and emotionally charged rap track. It was met with favorable reviews from critics, being praised for its hypnotic production and taunting lyrics. Depravity is a hybrid of rap, rock and trap, combining elements of each genre seamlessly. While on its surface there is a general sound that ties the whole album together, each song manages to stand out from one another: from the bold and melancholic "Inside Out" to the whirlwind of "Deadly Charges". The band is masterful at creating catchy melodies throughout the album and their versatile nature keeps each track feeling fresh. The production on the album is driven by heavy bass and 808 beats, as well as live instrumentation on some tracks. While the production adds a dynamic to the project, it's the bands poignant lyricism and delivery that stands out the most. Tragically honest, each bar and verse speaks to personal struggles and conveys an overarching message of perseverance. Depravity is an ambitious debut that radiates potential and shows an artist at the peak of their creative ability. Bully has created an album that is deeply personal yet ambitious and an experience that is both gritty and cathartic.

Operation Claw (also known as Operation Kapan - Serhat in Turkish) is a joint military operation conducted by the Turkish Armed Forces and Kurdistan Regional Government in Iraq, aimed at eliminating the threat posed by the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) in northern Iraq. The operation began on May 27, 2019. The operation's primary objective is to disrupt PKK activity from its hideouts in the Kurdistan region of Iraq. The PKK has conducted several cross-border attacks against Turkish targets over the years. In response, Turkey has periodically sent troops into Iraq in an effort to neutralize the PKK threat. Operation Claw is the latest in a series of such operations. The operation involves ground forces, air vehicles, and Special Forces units from the Turkish Armed Forces and the Kurdistan Regional Government. The ground forces will enter Iraq and occupy the areas where PKK militants are believed to be present. Turkish air vehicles and drones have been used to provide reconnaissance and surveillance support, as well as to carry out strikes against PKK targets. The Special Forces units will be tasked with carrying out raids against PKK hideouts and targets. The operation has been met with mixed reactions from other countries. While countries such as the United States and the United Kingdom have expressed support for the Turkish government's efforts to ensure its safety and security, Iraq has expressed concern over Turkish military action in the region. In response to these concerns, Turkish authorities have stated that the operation will be conducted in accordance with international law, and that there is no intention to harm civilians or disrupt the economic activities of the region. The operation has sparked a great deal of debate over the political implications of the Turkish government's actions. While most analysts agree that the operation is necessary in order to combat the PKK threat, there is also concern over the potential for increased tensions and instability in the region as a result of the military action. To date, the operation has been successful in its stated objectives, with reports of strikes against PKK targets and the capture of several PKK militants. In the coming months, it is likely that the operation will continue in an effort to eradicate the PKK threat from the region.

Shim Soon-taek (September 29, 1936 – June 17, 2021) was a South Korean film and television producer, editor, and actress. Shim was born in Seoul, South Korea on September 29, 1936. She attended Ewha Womans University, where she graduated with an education degree in 1957. She began her career shortly after with her first job as an assistant producer for MBC. Shim earned recognition for producing some of the most successful and award-winning films in South Korean history. Her most notable works include Illejuxt, which won the Silver Bear at the Berlin International Film Festival and The Gate of Destiny, which won the second place prize at the Moscow International Film Festival. Shim was also the producer of an acclaimed television series The King of the Chosun Dynasty, which was the recipient of numerous awards. Shim's work has also earned her high commendations and recognition. In 1984, she was selected by the Korean Film Council as one of the greatest producers in the history of South Korean cinema. She was also the recipient of the Special Award at the Korean Academic Film Promotion Association in 1986. In 1988, Shim became the first woman in South Korean history to be appointed as an executive producer of MBC. After her successful career as a producer, she then ventured into acting, appearing in various films, television series and plays, primarily as a supportive character. Shim passed away on June 17, 2021 at the age of 84. Throughout her career, Shim has been credited with creating some of the most memorable projects in Korean cinematic history and has won numerous awards. She is remembered for her passion, creativity and hard work, which have immensely contributed to Korean cinema.

The 1988-89 Major Indoor Soccer League season was the fourth in league history. It was also the last season before the MISL experienced its first major contraction, with the teams being scattered to the winds prior to the 1989-90 campaign. No teams folded during the 1988-89 season, and the regular season ran from November 5, 1988 to April 8, 1989. The Tulsa Ambush won the John F. Kennedy Trophy, awarded to the league champion, by defeating the San Diego Sockers in the championship series. The season saw a change in the playoff format. The five teams with the best regular season records advanced to the playoffs, and the playoffs were now a round-robin tournament, with each team playing the other four in head-to-head series. The team with the best record in the round-robin advanced to the finals. The regular season was highlighted by a significant number of offensive performances. The Cleveland Force won the regular season title thanks to a league-high 243 goals scored. The highest scorer was Dallas Sidekicks forward Tatu, who netted 85 goals, breaking the record set a year earlier by San Diego Sockers player Steve Zungul. The playoffs saw the Tulsa Ambush defeat both the Dallas Sidekicks and the Baltimore Blast each in a best-of-three contest. In the finals, the Ambush faced the experienced San Diego Sockers. The Ambush won the first game in the series 10-4, then clinched the championship in the second game, also 10-4. Tulsa’s top performer in the playoffs was Steve Kinsey, who scored 17 goals in 11 playoff games. The 1988-89 MISL season was the last with all original six teams playing in the league. Following the season, the MISL experienced a contraction, reducing the league from six teams to four. The Cleveland Force, Baltimore Blast, and Dallas Sidekicks all either folded or merged with other teams, while the San Diego Sockers and the Tulsa Ambush continued on to the 1989-90 season.

Archie Devine (born August 26,1992) is a Canadian professional basketball player who currently plays for the Toronto Raptors of the National Basketball Association (NBA). Devine attended Canada Prep Academy in St. Catharines, Ontario and then went to play college basketball at the University of Toronto from 2010-2014. In his freshman year, Devine averaged 14.2 points, 5.7 rebounds and 2 assists per game. In his junior and senior years at the University of Toronto, Devine started all 33 games and averaged a career-high 19.3 points, 7.8 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game. Following his collegiate career, Devine was selected in the second round of the 2014 NBA Draft by the Minnesota Timberwolves. He was traded to the Toronto Raptors during his rookie season and went on to become the first Canadian-born player to win an NBA title with the Raptors in 2019. As part of the championship run, Devine averaged 8.1 points, 4 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game in the playoffs. In the 2019-20 season, Devine led the Raptors to their third consecutive appearance in the playoffs, averaging 9.4 points, 4.7 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game, including a career-high 26 points and 9 assists against the Denver Nuggets on December 3, 2019. Devine is known for his all-around game, which showcases his ability to shoot from range and finish at the rim, as well as his athleticism, defensive intensity and leadership. Off the court, he is a passionate advocate of basketball in Canada, showcasing the game in a variety of ways through camps, clinics and other events. He has become a popular figure among Canadian basketball fans, and his potential, presence and contributions to Canadian basketball have earned him the nickname "Canada's Basketball King". As of June 2020, Devine has been featured in the NBA All-Star Weekend Rising Stars Challenge four times and was named the Most Valuable Player in 2019.

GG Tauri is a binary star system located in the Taurus Constellation, approximately 440 light-years away from Earth. The primary component, GG Tauri A, is a pre-main sequence star classified as a T Tauri type star located roughly 20 arc seconds southwest of the secondary component, GG Tauri B. GG Tauri A has a calculated mass of 11-14 times that of our sun and is estimated to be as young as 1 to 4 million years. It is one of the most studied young stars and is of particular interest due to its location near the planetary nebula NGC 1514. GG Tauri's binary companion, GG Tauri B, is significantly less luminous and has a calculated mass of only 1.5-8 times greater than the sun. The two stars are separated by a projected distance of about 441 astronomical units (1AU= Earth-Sun distance). GG Tauri A is estimated to have a temperature of 4500 K, a luminoisty of 60-175 times that of the sun, and an accretion rate onto the protoplanetary disk at about 10-4 solar masses per year. The temperature and luminosity of the primary component have been found to vary over time, suggesting that the disk is not in a steady-state configuration. The two stars in the GG Tauri system are believed to produce a protoplanetary disk around the primary component. This disk is estimated to be between 500-1000AU in diameter and is currently being fed by outflows from both stars. Observations of the disk with the Subaru Telescope in 2016 and 2017 revealed several features of interest. These features included the presence of concentric gap structures, spiral arms, and a flattened structure in the outer region of the disk. The two GG Tauri stars are believed to be in the process of forming their own planetary system and their binary relationship is likely to affect the formation and evolution of these planets. Additional observations of the GG Tauri system can help us to better understand early star formation and the evolution of protoplanetary disks.

Pebble Mine is a proposal for a large-scale mining project in the Bristol Bay watershed of southwestern Alaska. The project generally consists of the construction of an open-pit copper and gold mine coupled with an on-site processing plant, port, and associated infrastructure. The project is estimated to contain 80.6 billion pounds of copper, 107.4 million ounces of gold, and 5.6 billion pounds of molybdenum in its deposit. The proposed Pebble Mine has been the subject of heated debate since the idea was first introduced in the late 1990s. Proponents of the Pebble Mine claim that the project would provide economic and social benefits for Alaska and its residents, including thousands of jobs and hundreds of millions of dollars in revenues. Opponents of Pebble Mine have argued that the risks the project poses to the fragile ecosystem of the Bristol Bay region, and consequent impacts on wildlife and local indigenous populations, outweigh any potential benefits it may provide. The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has launched an effort to restrict the Pebble Mine project under the Clean Water Act. The agency has proposed to institute a policies that would prevent the construction of any large-scale mines like Pebble Mine in the Bristol Bay watershed. If the policies are put in place, the Pebble Mine project would have to find an alternative location, or it would be faced with the choice of finding alternative sources of capital, or abandoning the project altogether. The Pebble Limited Partnership, which is the prime developer of the mine, has criticized the EPA’s decision, arguing that it sets a precedent that invites government intervention and could cost the economy millions of jobs. Meanwhile, a number of local indigenous communities, environmental organizations, and other stakeholders have argued that the EPA’s actions are necessary to protect the Bristol Bay region’s ecosystem and its resources upon which local populations and businesses depend. The outcome of the Pebble Mine debate is yet to be seen. In the meantime, both sides continue to make their case to decision makers and the public in their efforts to influence the final outcome. Despite numerous attempts to move the project forward, experts suggest that the political and regulatory environment in the US and Alaska is currently too uncertain to allow the Pebble Mine project to move forward in its current location.

The 2013 Rayong oil spill was an environmental disaster that occurred off the Rayong coast in Thailand on July 27, 2013. It involved the release of approximately 10,000 barrels (1.6 million liters) of oil from storage tanks belonging to PTT Global Chemicals. The resulting spill acted adversely on local ecosystems and affected the livelihoods of thousands of fishermen. The disaster was believed to have been caused by sabotage and subsequent fire at the tanks located in Map Ta Phut industrial estate. Evidence pointing to sabotage included the presence of an unknown substance in the storage tanks which was later identified as hydrochloric acid, and the presence of a number of empty fuel drums at the site. News of the oil spill spread quickly, creating a sense of heightened panic among local populations. Prompt action by the Thai government and other environmental agencies helped prevent the spread of a greater disaster, as about 9,900 barrels (1.6 million liters) of oil were retrieved from the sea. The aftermath of the oil spill was an extensive and prolonged cleanup process, involving state, private and international organizations. In order to minimize the impact, private contractors were brought in to assist in manual and mechanical recovery operations. The damage caused by the oil spill was immense and devastating. On an ecological level, the 35km stretch of coastline and seabed were largely destroyed due to the presence of the oil and acid in the water. In addition, local fish stocks were destroyed and an estimated 1,000+ fishermen were put out of work due to the impact of the event. In the following years, more and more species of fish began to disappear from the affected areas until the local marine environment had fully recovered. At the time of the spill, PTT Global Chemicals was found to be in breach of existing regulations and an investigation was launched to determine its culpability. Ultimately, the company was found to be guilty of negligence, as it had failed to adequately inspect the tanks and ensure proper undetermined. As a result, PTT Global Chemicals was fined 3 billion baht (approximately USD 88.5 million). The 2013 Rayong oil spill remains one of the worst environmental disasters to ever occur in Thailand, causing irreparable and long-lasting damage to the surrounding ecosystems and the livelihoods of local communities. Although much has been done to prevent such incidents in the future, the effects of the oil spill still linger on today, with locals still feeling its effects 7 years later.

Abraham Rotstein (also known as 'Abe') was a Canadian economist and social theorist who played an important role in the development of the post-Keynesian economics. He was one of the leading intellectuals in academic reforms following World War II, and his work focused on developing a 'modern' economics that was serious about income and wealth inequality, while also arguing that economics needed to be more closely linked to politics. He was born in Toronto in 1925, and he obtained a BA honours in Classics from the University of Toronto in 1947, and he later took his Ph.D. in Economics in 1965 from the same university. Rotstein's academic career spanned several decades, during which time he held a number of important academic positions. He served as Professor of Economics at the University of Toronto from 1965 to 1986, and was also a faculty member of the Centre for Industrial Relations from 1967 to 1972. He was a visiting professor at the Centre for Labour-Management Relations at the University of Amsterdam from 1977 to 1979 and held an appointment as visiting professor in the Department of Industrial Relations and Human Resources at the University of Amsterdam from 1979 to 1981. He was also a faculty member of the Centre for International Studies at the University of Toronto from 1972 to 1975. Throughout his career, Rotstein consistently argued for the need to develop a more open and equitable economy, and he was a fierce critic of the policies of the neoclassical economists. He argued that the 'bias of traditional economic theory' had lead to the widespread belief that only the wealthy are able to benefit from economic progress by emphasising the role of debt and property. He argued that the 'rich do not give to the poor; they exploit them', and he advocated a 'socially responsible' economic policy which would invest in public needs, rather than simply encourage private investment. Rotstein’s work was also highly influential in the development of a ‘social economy’ which emphasised public policy objectives over market-driven concerns. He argued that the role of the state should extend beyond traditional macroeconomic management, to include the regulation and oversight of market mechanisms. He also argued for the creation of a more equitable economic system, and he was particularly critical of income inequality, arguing that the pursuit of 'profit maximisation for the shareholders' had led to the neglect of 'the interests of those upon whom economic decisions have the greatest impact'. In recognition of his significant contribution to economics and public policy, Rotstein was appointed as an Officer of the Order of Canada in 1998. He also received honorary degrees from several universities, including the University of Toronto and Windsor University. After an illustrious career in economics and public policy, Abraham Rotstein died in 1997.

. The 1956 United States Senate election in Illinois took place on November 6, 1956. Incumbent Republican United States Senator Everett McKinley Dirksen won re-election to a third term in office over Democratic challenger Paul Douglas, a former University of Chicago economics professor and United States Senator from 1949 to 1967. Securing 55.90% of the vote, Dirksen defeated Douglas by a substantial margin of 131,188 votes. Dirksen, who was first elected to the United States Senate in 1950, was a popular figure at the time of the election. While not untroubled in his bid for re-election, his large lead in the polls and strong support from incumbent President Dwight D. Eisenhower enabled Dirksen to prevail in the election with comparative ease. Douglas, a Democratic politician, had previously served as a United States Senator from Illinois from 1949 to 1967. He challenged Dirksen’s re-election bid in 1956, and attended a series of political forums and debates during the campaign. His effort failed, however, and he was unable to overtake the incumbent Senator’s commanding lead. In the end, Dirksen’s victory was largely attributable to strong support from President Eisenhower, who campaigned for his re-election bid in Illinois in the months leading up to the election, as well as Dirksen’s well-known popularity among the state’s voters. Dirksen’s victory would represent the fourth of his six consecutive terms in the United States Senate. The election saw moderate voter turnout, with 2,282,863 ballots counted across the state. The result of the election, seeing the re-election of Everett McKinley Dirksen, has been described as a “safe” win. It marked the final United States Senate election in the state of Illinois prior to the ratification of the 17th Amendment to the United States Constitution, which initiated direct popular elections for the chamber. Dirksen’s legacy would endure for generations and, among other things, he is remembered for his leadership in the passage of landmark legislation, such as the Civil Rights Act of 1964. In the following years, he continued to serve his constituents in the United States Senate until his death in 1969.

Adrian Favell (born 1964) is a British sociologist and professor at the University of Leeds. He is a leading scholar in the fields of European studies and cultural sociology, with publications in journals such as the European Journal of Social Theory, Nations and Nationalism and Ethnic and Racial Studies. In his research, Favell focuses on the challenges that contemporary Europe faces in terms of social change, cultural diversity and globalisation. He also explores the ambivalent processes of regional integration and widening divisions between 'old' and 'new' Europe. In particular, he has studied the 'frontier populations' - populations which are living on the boundaries between different political, economic and cultural spaces. Favell has authored or co-authored several books, including The Frontiers of a European Identity (2008); Eurostars and Eurocities: Free Movement and Mobility in an Integrating Europe (2009); and Super-diversity and its Implications (2013). He has also conducted extended research projects for institutions such as the European Commission and the British Council. Favell obtained his BA in Politics, Philosophy and Sociology from the University of Warwick in 1987, and went on to receive his MA (1994) and PhD (2000) from the University of Bristol - one of the leading centres for European Studies in the UK. Following his PhD, he was appointed Senior Lecturer at the University of Leeds in 2001, and Professor of European Studies in 2013. Favell is an active member of several European research networks, including the QUEST 'Quantitative Understanding of Europe, Its Institutions and Its Citizens' research project; he is also the founding editor of the journal National Identities, and has recently acted as a scientific adviser on the migration dimension of the EU's fundamental rights program. In recognition of his achievements in research, he was awarded the 2019 Berlin Prize in Humanities by the American Academy in Berlin - a prize which recognized his contribution to the field of European studies. References # Adrian Favell (https://essl.leeds.ac.uk/sociology/staff/175/Dr_Adrian_Favell). # Super-diversity and its Implications (https://www.routledge.com/Super-Diversity-in-the-UK-and-its-Implications/Favell/p/book/9780415836514). # American Academy in Berlin (https://www.americanacademy.de/people/adrian-favell/).

William Smith (1728-1814) was a loyalist to the British empire during the American Revolution. He was born in 1728 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and was a printer, engraver and publisher. He supported the British empire, both politically and financially throughout the Revolution. He was an outspoken critic of the American Revolution. He believed that the Revolution was a mistake and that the Patriots' views on the matter were wrong. He openly attacked the revolutionaries in a series of newspaper articles, including one entitled The Fathers and Sons of America Exposed, which he published in 1776. His staunch loyalty to the British earned him both praise and condemnation from both sides. William Smith also served as an officer in the First City Troop of Philadelphia. He was one of the founding members of the troop in 1774, and during the Revolutionary War, he commanded a company of the troop in four engagements at Germantown, White Marsh, Burlington, and Neshaminy. In the 1780s, Smith traveled to England to purchase printing equipment that would allow him to work more efficiently. During his stay there, he published a number of articles in defense of loyalism and a few broadsides encouraging fellow loyalists to stay faithful the British cause. He also became the printer for the newly created Pennsylvania Gazette, which was a publication of both Royalist and Loyalist sentiments. He had no problem with standing up for his beliefs and ultimately refused to pay taxes during the war, which resulted in the confiscation of his property. However, after the war ended and amnesty was granted, he was able to retain his printing business and continued to publish loyalist tracts up until his death in 1814. William Smith was one of the few loyalists to remain steadfast in his commitment to the British Empire throughout the course of the American Revolution. His staunch allegiance had earned him both admiration and condemnation, but his actions demonstrated the level of commitment and dedication which many American loyalists had during the fight for independence.

Cabela's Big Game Hunter 2012 is a hunting-themed video game developed and published by Activision in 2011. It is the seventh installment of the Cabela's Big Game Hunter series, and was released for the PC, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 and Wii. It allows players to hunt North American big game species such as whitetail deer, caribou, moose, elk, bighorn sheep, and waterfowl. The game features a 3-D environment and 12 hunting locations from Alaska to Zimbabwe. Players can also choose from over 300 weapons and equipment including bows, firearms, and calls to customize their hunting experience. The simulation element of the game is further complemented by its wildlife artifacts, which allow players to create a virtual trophy room featuring their accomplishments. The game also includes many other features such as log cabins, hunting dogs, and fishing spots, as well as a multiplayer co-op mode. One of the major additions to the franchise is Adventure Mode which allows players to use their unique set of skills to complete seven unique challenges across five continents. The mode includes three special endless challenges with endless waves of enemies that are adjustable in difficulty level. The game also has a Trophy Room feature which allows players to save their progress as they progress in the game. Players can record important events such as their biggest trophy, fastest kills and their most accurate shot, as well as take photos of their trophies. Cabela's Big Game Hunter 2012 received generally positive reviews from critics and players praising the game for its improved graphics and features. It was also successful in the market, selling more than two million copies in the United States alone. It was also nominated for the 2012 DICE awards for best individual sports game.

Dino Dan is a Canadian children's television series about a ten year old prehistoric-obsessed boy named Dan Henderson. Dan finds himself transported to the Prehistoric Age by using a magical stone. In each episode, Dan and his two friends, Trek and Stacy, search his prehistoric world for dinosaurs while preserving their modern world knowledge. Dino Dan is produced by Sinking Ship Entertainment in association with TVOKids, the series premiered on August 16, 2010 and the first season ended on February 18, 2013. It is the first preschool-level live action television series. The series finale of Dino Dan aired on March 22, 2014. The show facts are: Dinosaurs existed in the prehistory and still exist in our modern world today; they have a unique habitat and possess unique traits that set them apart from other species. We learn a lot about them by looking in history books, museums, and by visiting dinosaur-themed parks. Through Dan’s adventures, he gets to explore the world of dinosaurs and learns how to recognize their environment, their traits and the diverse characteristics that make them so special. In each episode, Dan and his two friends go on a 'dino adventure'. Together, they observe and try to learn about the species they encounter. They also confront challenging physical obstacles, such as mud pits and prickly plants, and play dino inspired games. As an educational tool, Dino Dan introduces viewers to the world of dinosaurs, and to the science, technology, engineering and math concepts that are used in the study of dinosaurs. Through Dan’s encounters, we learn interesting facts about different dinosaur species, explore scientific theories and engage in problem solving. In addition to its educational components, Dino Dan is action packed, teaching viewers of all ages the importance of friendships, helping others, and embracing their own creativity. Dino Dan has earned numerous awards and nominations, including a 2011 Gemini Award for "Best Pre-School Program".

Liu Kai (劉開; courtesy name Dijing (帝景)) (1022–1088) was a jinshi (禁史) and general in the Song dynasty of China. Liu was born to a prominent family in Eyang (Yixing), Jiangsu. He had an older brother, Liu Tingen (劉廷根), who was a member of the Forum. At the age of 24, Liu passed the Imperial examinations and was appointed as a provincial official in Wangdu Prefecture (望都縣) in modern Hebei. In 1054, Liu was appointed as governor of Hedong (河東), a strategic port and military base in modern Shandong. During this tenure, he was faced with the complexity of Qiang nomads, who often crossed the borders and raided border regions. In 1064, Liu was appointed as a commander in the imperial army and led a detachment of troops to fight against the Tanguts of the Western Xia. Liu then played a decisive role in the Battle of Chengdu, which was a crucial battle in the war. During the battle, the Song army successfully routed the Tangut forces, routing them from their capital, Zhuozhou (涿州). In 1068, Liu was appointed to lead a naval attack on the Jurchens of the Jin dynasty, a hostile northern neighbour. He led the successful attack on the strategic ports located in the mouth of the Yalu River (烏爾流河). Despite inflicting heavy casualties, Liu's forces were eventually forced to retreat due to the superiority of the Jin forces. In 1086, Liu was appointed to lead troops against the Wuyue kingdom of Shao (韶); he eventually routed the kingdom and the Song forces went on to occupy its capital. Liu was a patriot and a brilliant strategist. He dedicated his entire life to defending his country and was highly appreciated by the Emperor Song Huizong, who granted him a posthumous title as Grand General Wangbei Hou (望北侯). Liu is remembered to this day as an outstanding military leader and an embodiment of patriotism. He is still honored with massive statues and memorial shrines in his native city of Yixing, Jiangsu. In the present day, Liu Kai has become a popular cultural icon; inspiring movies, television shows, novels, games, and songs about his exploits. His story is used to teach lessons of patriotism and courage in Chinese classrooms. From the long history of China, Liu Kai continues to stand out as an influential and prestigious figure, revered and remembered to this day.

Riho Iida (born June 28, 1995) is a Japanese singer, songwriter, stage actress, and former member of the Japanese girl group Angerme. Iida was born in Osaka, Japan. She graduated from Osaka Aoyama High School and Soai University. Her interest in music began when she was in secondary school, and she went on to become a singer and songwriter. In 2009, Iida participated in Hello! Project's 10th generation audition and was selected as a member of S/mileage, the group which later became Angerme in 2014. As a member of the Girl Group, she had two major debut singles titled "Yumemiru 15sai" (夢見る 15才) and "Watashi ga Iu Mae ni Dakishimenakya ne" (私が言う前に抱きしめなきゃね). As a member of Angerme, she has taken part in various performances and participated in musicals and stage plays. She has also played in the NHK short drama series, Itsuka Hi no Ataru Basho de (いつか陽のあたる場所で). In 2019, Iida announced her graduation from Angerme. Following her graduation, she released her first solo single, "Todokanu Omoi" (届かぬ想い). Since then she has released various original music and covers, and with help from her YouTube channel has garnered attention from music fans in Japan for her talent as a singer and songwriter. In 2020, Iida branched out into voice acting and participated in the Japanese drama series, Watashi ni Unmei no Koi Nante Arienaikedo (私に運命の恋なんてありえないけど). She was highly praised for her performance in the drama and has received many positive reviews from the media and fans. Since2020, Iida has also begun to work as a model for the fashion magazine SALiS and other brands such as ZIPCOIN and Chiffon. In addition, she has become an official presenter for music programs such as BACK44TOKYO and Kore kara ONE-ROOM!. Riho Iida is currently a solo artist, active both as a singer and an actress. She is highly respected among the Japanese music industry and fans alike for her talent and capabilities as a performer.

Glory is a hip hop song by American recording artist duo Common and John Legend. The song is part of the soundtrack for the 2014 film Selma. Written by John Stephens and Lonnie Lynn, the track features production from Stephen "Koz" Kozmeniuk, and features instrumentation from drums and piano loops. Glory was released to critical acclaim upon its 2014 release, with the writing and production being praised by music critics. Rolling Stone gave the song four out of five stars and referred to it as an "anthemic title track," while Entertainment Weekly described the song as "epic." The song has gone on to be nominated for several awards, including Academy Awards for Best Original Song and Best Original Score, and was awarded a Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song. The song juxtaposes the Civil Rights Movement of the 1960s with modern-day social issues such as gun violence and police brutality, with Common and Legend's lyrics weaving in references from historical speeches, documents and events of the era, such as the famous Selma to Montgomery march for voting rights. The video for the song was released on December 15, 2014 and features Common, Legend, actors Carmen Ejogo and David Oyelowo and supporting actor Stephan James as they recreate photos and film footage of the Selma march side by side. The video also features news clips and footage of protestors in the wake of the 2014 Ferguson unrest. Glory is one of Common and Legend's most successful collaborations, charting in multiple countries and being certified triple platinum in the US. It has been featured in a live performance by Common and Legend at the 87th Academy Awards ceremony and has been performed by both artists in various live shows and television appearances since its 2014 release. Glory has become an anthem of the civil rights movement and a powerful protest song in the fight for racial justice, with Common and John Legend's collaboration creating a timeless lyrical masterpiece. Glory has been referenced in various publications and interviews, with various artists and figures citing it as an important and meaningful work.

Helen Foster (b. 1874 - d. 1959) was an English stage and early cinema actress. She began her career as a child performer in the 1880s, first appearing in small roles on stage before becoming a successful pantomime performer in her teens. Foster continued acting throughout her life, working in both theatre and film, and eventually establishing herself as a popular character actress during the silent film era. Born in 1874 in London, Foster's early years are largely unknown. She started performing on stage in the late 1880s and rose to prominence in the early 1890s when she took on several popular roles in pantomimes and musical comedies. Her career on the stage flourished and included roles in Charles Francis Coghlan's comedy play Amy Robsart, as well as plays by Shakespeare, Greek tragedy and variety shows. Foster also maintained a strong following throughout the late 1890s and the early years of the 20th century, appearing in a number of West End productions and touring regularly with various productions. Foster's film career began in 1903, when she starred in the film adaptation The Country Girl opposite leading actor and director Cecil Hepworth. Foster went on to work with Hepworth on several subsequent films, including A Tale of Two Cities (1907) and In the Days of Old (1909). She soon established herself as a prominent figure in the burgeoning British film industry and continued to appear in multiple titles through World War I, including the pioneering pseudo-documentary London Up To Date (1912) and Walter West's thriller The Chalice of Sorrow (1920). By the early 1920s, Foster had gotten much success in the film business and became best-known for her portrayals of older women. Her performances in dramas such as The White Peacock (1921) and Easy Virtue (1927) exemplified this. Foster went on to take on a more comedic type of role in the 1930s, appearing in a number of humorous productions including Jack Hulbert's Jack Ahoy (1934) and the early Ealing Studios comedy Potiphar's Wife (1931). Foster's later years were relatively quiet, though she continued to appear in theatre, variety and the occasional film role until 1959. She eventually passed away in London in the same year at the age of 85. During her career she gained a reputation as an excellent character actor, appearing in over 120 productions between the 1880s and 1950s. To this day, she is remembered for her many performances - both as a stage actress and a film actress - which were praised in their time and continue to be viewed and appreciated by modern audiences.

Sheikh Aftab Ahmed (born 1951) is a prominent Pakistani politician who belongs to the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) party. He was a member of the National Assembly of Pakistan from 2008 to 2018, representing the NA-111 constituency in Sialkot. Sheikh Aftab was born in Sialkot in 1951. He has a master’s degree in Political Science from University of the Punjab, and has been very active in politics since the late 1970s. He served as a member of the National Assembly from 1985 to 1988, representing the Sialkot constituency. During the 1990s, he moved to Canada but returned to Pakistan in 2002 and was elected to the National Assembly of Pakistan in 2008 as an independent candidate. He then joined the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz party, and was re-elected to the National Assembly in 2013. He was among the prominent PML-N candidates in the 2018 general elections, but he was defeated by PTI candidate Ghulam Bibi Bharwana, who received 76,376 votes and Sheikh Aftab Ahmed who received 70,461 votes. Throughout his career, Sheikh Aftab has advocated on behalf of the oppressed sections of society, and has highlighted the issues faced by women and children. He has been praised for his efforts to promote education and healthcare in Pakistan, as well as his commitment to egalitarianism. He has also been a strong backer of improving Punjab's infrastructure and has strongly supported the construction of a modern railway line. In recognition of his outstanding services to the people of Pakistan, Sheikh Aftab was awarded the Pride of Performance award in 1997 and the Hilal-e-Imtiaz award in 2011. In 2016, he was appointed as the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly. He currently serves as a senior leader of PML-N and continues to advocate for the rights of the people of Pakistan.

Meri Avidzba (born 12 November 1987) is a Georgian actress and model best known for her roles in the television series, The Bold Type and Code Black. Avidzba was born in Tbilisi, Georgia, to parents of mixed Georgian, Armenian and Russian ancestry. She was raised in the same city until the age of 15 when her family moved to Moscow. After graduating from high school in Moscow, she went to drama school, as she had been interested in acting since childhood. Avidzba made her debut in 2008 when she was 18 in the Georgian musical comedy series, Comedy Stars. Since then, she has had various roles in Georgian television series, such as TV shows and soaps. In 2015, Avidzba was cast in the American television series, The Bold Type. She played the role of "Melissa de la Cruz", a successful professional who is the CEO of a major technology business. The Bold Type has been praised for its portrayal of successful women of color in the media industry and for providing a platform for them to be seen and heard. Avidzba has also had roles in several other American TV series, including Netflix's Sense8 and ABC's Code Black, in which she played a main character's sister. In addition to her acting work, Avidzba models for various companies. She has appeared in numerous campaigns and campaigns for popular domestic and international companies, such as Mercedes-Benz, L'Oreal, and Nike. Avidzba has been a prominent figure in the Georgian media industry, and has also been named one of the "Most Influential Georgians" by Georgian weekly magazine, The Georgian Times. She has also been nominated for various awards such as the Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actress in a Series and other awards for her acting roles. In her personal life, Avidzba speaks multiple languages including English, German, and Russian, and she is a supporter of various charities including the Women’s Aid Fund. Additionally, she has taken part in many environmental protection campaigns. In 2020, Avidzba made her directorial debut with the short film, Red Lines. She is currently working on her first feature film. Avidzba is an inspiration for many young people in Georgia, especially for women aspiring to pursue a career in entertainment and media.

Robert Rolle (died 1660) was the leading English lawyer of his day. He was born in Devon, the son of an lawyer, and was educated at Exeter University. He practiced law in the courts of common pleas, the star chamber and King's Bench, and worked with many of the lawyers of his day, including William Noy and Sir Orlando Bridgeman. His legal career was highly successful as he debated and argued on a variety of cases in the most significant court of his time. He appeared in many of the leading cases, including the Somersett case, which granted freedom to a particular slave affirming his rights to life, liberty, and possession of property. At the time, England was governed by the monarchy of King Charles I, who had the deciding power and influence in the court proceedings. Prosecutors of the time had absolute power to make a case against a defendant and would often arbitrarily refuse to accept a plea or settlement from a defendant. Rolle was seen by many as a good role model for a fair-minded lawyer and challenged the prosecution's arbitrary decisions in court. As his influence spread, King Charles appointed him as counsel to the navy, a position he held until his death in 1660. Although Rolle was criticized for his legal decisions, he stood out in his network of friends and colleagues. He was known to be supportive of civil liberties and never lost sight of the equality he found in natural law. He was very highly respected by the English legal system and stands out as a significant figure in the development of English law. Rolle's work continues to influence the development of English law. Numerous books and articles have been written in his honour, and various foundations and trusts have been set up in his name. In the end, Robert Rolle was a respected lawyer, a proponent of justice, and a leader in the advancement of English law. He will forever be remembered for his contribution to the development of a fair and legal system in England.

Fred Alan Wolf (born December 3, 1934) is an American quantum physicist, author, and lecturer. He is known for his work on the physics of consciousness and has written several books on the subject, most notably Taking the Quantum Leap (1981) and The Eagle's Quest (1991). Wolf was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. He attended Temple University and then the University of Chicago, where he received his B.A. in physics in 1959 and his Ph.D. in theoretical physics in 1962. After leaving the university, Wolf worked as a research scientist at the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center and at the Max Planck Institute for Applied Physics in Stuttgart, Germany. Wolf's major works focus on the relationship between modern quantum physics and consciousness. He is best known for his book Taking the Quantum Leap (1981), which introduced the idea of "quantum consciousness" - the notion that consciousness can influence physical reality. He has since written several other books exploring the implications of quantum physics for our understanding of the world. Wolf also gave public lectures and seminars on his work, including one given at the Esalen Institute in 1978. He has appeared in numerous documentaries and media programs, including the Skeptics Society's podcast and the film What the Bleep Do We Know!? He has been a guest speaker at the Fetzer Institute and the Temenos Academy. In addition to his work in the field of quantum physics, Wolf continues to write and lecture on topics ranging from spirituality and philosophy to pop culture. He lives in San Diego, California and remains active in the scientific and philosophical communities. He also writes regularly for New Realities and writes a bi-weekly column for Fearless Planet magazine. Wolf's latest book, Quantum Fitness: Harnessing the Power of Consciousness and Quantum Physics, was published in 2015. Wolf has remained active in public life and is a frequent guest speaker and panelist at universities, science and spiritual gatherings around the world. He has contributed to numerous radio and television programs, including the History Channel's The Universe, Beyond Human, and the Discovery Channel's When Darwin Met Einstein. He has also contributed to popular magazines such as The Atlantic, Psychology Today, Popular Science, and New Realities. Wolf's life and work have strongly influenced the fields of quantum physics and consciousness. His books, public appearances, and media presence have helped popularize the ideas of quantum physics and consciousness and make them accessible to a wider audience.

The Yunnan Box Turtle, scientifically classified as the Cuora yunnanensis, is a species of freshwater turtle native to the Yunnan Province of China. This species has a high-domed carapace with a yellowish-orange or yellowish-brown background and bright, black-bordered brown markings.It can reach a maximum size of about 8 to 9.5 inches in length and is a member of the family Geoemydidae. The Yunnan box turtle lives in freshwater habitats and streams with clear, slow-moving waters and fallen leaf cover. It is an opportunistic omnivore that feeds on insects, small fish, worms, mollusks, crustaceans, aquatic plants and fruits, and occasionally carrion. Due to extensive overharvesting and destruction of its natural habitat, this species is now endangered and listed as a Vulnerable Species on the IUCN Red List. The Yunnan box turtle is primarily found throughout the basins of the west and middle Yangtze River and the Pearl River in China. With a mere ten percent of its original distribution left, its current habitat is restricted mostly to areas along the banks of the Yuanjiang, Lancang Jiang and Jinjiang Rivers. This species also inhabits parts of Tibet and Northern Vietnam, but these accounts have still not been confirmed. The main threats to the Yunnan box turtle’s survival are due to anthropogenic activities such as destruction of their habitats, overcollection and illegal trade. To protect the species, the Chinese government launched a captive-breeding programme at the Yunnan Wild Animal Conservation and Research Centre, which has released more than 100,000 captive-bred turtles into their natural habitats. Other impactful conservation actions such as banning the collection of wild Yunnan box turtles, enhancing natural habitats and improving the quality of existing protected areas led to the species’ IUCN classification being upgraded from Critically Endangered to Vulnerable in 2008. The Yunnan box turtle is a protected species under Chinese Law. According to the China Endangered Species Law, it is illegal to kill, sell or keep the turtles as pets. Therefore, it is important to raise public awareness of their existence in order to help protect the species from further decline. In addition, there is still a great need for further research on the species to provide more accurate estimates of its population. Generating public interest in the species also has potential to boost its conservation. The Chinese government is currently working with other countries to save the species through a variety of educational programmes and is using online campaigns to raise awareness of the threats faced by the Yunnan box turtle. This species is an important part of Chinese biodiversity and the importance of its conservation should not be overlooked.

Signagi, also known as Sighnaghi, is a small town located in the Kakheti region of Georgia. It is the administrative centre of the Sighnaghi Municipality, which has a population of around 7,000 people. The town is known for its picturesque landscapes and rich culture. Situated 110 kilometres east of Tbilisi, Signagi was founded in the late 18th century by King Erekle II of Georgia. The town was the seat of hereditary rulers of the estate. During the 19th century, Signagi was a large commercial centre with numerous warehouses and trading posts. The town was heavily damaged during the Russo-Persian War (1804-1813), but was quickly rebuilt and today is one of the most visited tourist destinations in Georgia. In the present day, Signagi is an attractive tourist destination with a variety of historical attractions. The attractions include the old walled city, the fortress and churches. The main entrance to the city is the Nine Towers Gate, which was built in the 18th century and is notable for its Baroque style. Other important landmarks within the city include the old armory, a restored old caravanserai, and the old synagogue. Signagi is well known for its wine culture and has recently become an important wine producing region in Georgia. Several local wineries produce high-quality Georgian wines. The nearby Alazani Valley is also home to a number of important Georgian wineries. The local economy is buoyed by tourism and has seen a significant uptick in recent years. The town is full of restaurants, cafés, shops, small inns, and guesthouses in addition to the number of attractions. Signagi is also home to a number of festivals throughout the year, the largest being the festival of Georgian Cuisine, which takes place every summer. The festival celebrates the traditional Georgian cuisine and gathers both local and international guests together to sample authentic Georgian dishes. Overall, Signagi is a charming town full of history and culture which attracts both domestic and international travelers alike. Its Georgian traditions, picturesque landscapes, delicious cuisine, and expansive wineries are sure to help make any trip to the area unforgettable.

Held in La Molina, Catalonia, the FIS Snowboarding World Championships 2011 was the 22nd edition of the FIS Snowboarding World Championships, a major snowboarding event organized by the International Ski Federation (FIS). The championships took place from 12 to 18 December 2011, and featured six disciplines: women's and men's snowboard cross, parallel slalom, halfpipe, slopestyle, and big air. Dagmar Straxmair of Austria successfully defended her world championship victory from the previous year by winning both the women's snowboard cross and parallel slalom events. Straxmair was one of the few female competitors to repeat a victory across two disciplines. The men's snowboard cross was won by Markus Schairer of Austria, while Italy's Omar Visintin claimed the parallel slalom victory. In the halfpipe, Switzerland's Iouri Podladtchikov took gold in the men's competition, and Japan's Maddy Schaffrick claimed victory in the women's event. Slopestyle was won by Norway's Ståle Sandbech (men's) and Finland's Enni Rukajärvi (women's), while the big air title was claimed by snowboarder Sebastien Toutant of Canada (men's) and Nathalie Zoller of Switzerland (women's). The FIS Snowboarding World Championships 2011 was part of the 2011/12 FIS Snowboard World Cup, a prominent series of international snowboarding competitions. The event drew over a hundred of the world's top snowboarders competing in both individual and mixed-team competitions. The La Molina resort provided a suitable and challenging base for the event, and its success established the area as an important international destination for snowboarding. Over the course of the event, athletes from over 20 different countries raced, jumped, and slid their way to medals, as well as to individual and team titles. The 2011 championships was notable for its fierce competition and its large attendance, making it one of the premier snowboarding competitions for the year.

The 1964 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship was the 34th staging of the All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship since its establishment by the Gaelic Athletic Association in 1928. The championship began on 13 June 1964 and ended on 13 September 1964. Kilkenny were the defending champions, however, they were defeated in the Leinster final by Wexford. Wexford went on to win the All-Ireland championship following a 6-13 to 4-3 defeat of Cork in the final. This was their second All-Ireland title in-a-row and their fourth title overall. Kilkenny reached the quarter-final stage of the championship before eventually losing out to Cork. All other provinces were represented in the All-Ireland semi-final, with Wexford, Cork and Galway all making it to the last four. In the All-Ireland semi-finals, Wexford defeated Galway by 4-11 to 4-3 while Cork overcame a Wexford team, coached by future Dublin manager Richie Bennis on a scoreline of 7-7 to 2-3. The All-Ireland final took place at Croke Park on 13 September 1964. Wexford went on to win their fourth All-Ireland title in five years, thanks in no small part to the accuracy of Tony Doran who scored 0-7 from play and 0-2 from frees. His teammate Jackie Quigley scored a total of 4-6 (3-3 from play and 1-3 from frees). Cork failed to equate the successes of their previous year, when they had become the first team to ever win the All-Ireland minor double. Both teams were presented with the GAA's Centenary Trophy before the game and medals afterwards. It was Wexford's fourth All-Ireland title in the minor grade, thereby putting them in joint first place with Cork on the all-time roll of honour. Wexford's Tony Doran was later presented with the GAA All-Star Award following his impressive display in the minor championship.

The Absalon-class frigate is a family of multirole warships built for the Royal Danish Navy by the Odense Steel Shipyard (OSK) of Denmark. The class consists of six ships – Absalon, Esbern Snare, Peter Tordenskjold, Niels Juel, Thetis, and Vædderen – which were built between January 2003 and April 2006. The ships feature most advanced technologies, offering an enhanced capability to the Danish Navy. The Absalon-class has a length of 117m and a beam of 15.8m, and displaces 4,000 tonnes. The hull is reinforced to protect against mines, gunfire, and pressure-activated improvised explosive devices. The vessels are also designed to conduct surveillance operations. The vessels of the Absalon-class are equipped with anti-aircraft and anti-ship weaponry, such as the Otobreda 76mm, the Ba¯ses 36mm, torpedo launchers, and eight surface-to-surface missiles, as well as a hangar capable of carrying two helicopters. The vessels are further supported by 12 to 24 crew members, who can also be over 200 depending on the mission and tasks. The propulsion system of the Absalon-class vessels consists of CODOG Geared Turboshaft engines, two Zorya-Mashproekt gas turbines and two Rolls-Royce Promas Lite controllables pitch probs delivering 9,200 horsepower. The propulsion system gives the vessels a speed of 24 knots or faster. The vessels are also equipped with a variable-depth sonar for surveying the seabed, special forces, and mine countermeasures operations. In addition, they are capable of deploying a self-propelled weapon system (SPWS) as well as unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs). The vessels have a range of 7,000 nautical miles (13,000 km) and are capable of staying at sea for up to 30 days without restocking. They also have a capacity of up to 300 passengers. The Absalon-class vessels are the most advanced ships ever built by the Danish Navy, a fact that the Danish public is particularly proud of. The vessels have been deployed multiple times in anti-piracy and anti-terrorism missions in the Straits of Malacca, the Gulf of Aden, the Mediterranean, and the Middle East, as well as in exercises around the world. In 2013, the Absalon-class was awarded the World Navy Innovation award at the World Naval Frigates and Corvettes Conference for its innovative design and operational excellence.

A Union Representative is an individual or group of individuals who are elected or appointed to represent and safeguard the interests of the members of a labor union within companies, government institutions, or other organizations. They are often delegated to negotiate collective bargaining agreements, mediate labor disputes, work as union advocates for internal grievances, and even protect employment rights. Usually, a union representative is democratically elected by the labor union's members to serve in the particular role. Generally, union representatives are either administrators, organizers, or activists who take part in the activities of the union. They are typically present at executive council meetings and labor union conventions and take part in all decisions relating to union membership rights, benefits, and privileges. Union representatives are also often part of labor unions' professional bodies, such as bargaining committees, which handle negotiations between labor unions and employers. In particular, union representatives who serve on bargaining committees have the responsibility of negotiating union contracts for members and ensuring that any changes in collective bargaining regulations are mutually agreed upon by both sides. In some organizations, the job of the union representative is to investigate, publicize, and defend any claims of discrimination, unfair labor practices, or safety hazards. Union representatives are required to be knowledgeable about the organization's labor laws, rules, and regulations regarding labor disputes, and they may present grievances to management on behalf of union members. Representatives can even represent members in court cases, and in other legal proceedings.
