In addition to protecting and promoting the interests of the union members, union representatives also often serve as the source of information for the group. They have the ability to disseminate information about the union's activities and objectives and can also produce educational materials regarding labor laws, safety regulations, collective bargaining agreements, and collective bargaining rights. Union representatives may also serve as the organizational bridge between the labor union and potential employers. Through their negotiating and formulation of collective bargaining agreements, union representatives can often attract new employers, helping to increase the number of union members. This in turn, can create workspace security, job opportunities, job security, and better working conditions for union members. Union representatives are typically highly respected members of labor organizations and typically enjoy excellent job stability. With the knowledge of labor laws and regulations, they can help secure better working conditions and benefits for the members of their labor unions.

Ruder Than You is an American punk rock band formed in Buffalo, New York in 2002. The band is composed of vocalist and guitarist John Shields, bassist Sean Maloney, and drummer Matt Thomas. After building a small local following, the band released its self-titled debut album in 2003, which was produced by Chicago-based producer Sanford Parker. The band's sound has been said to mix elements of skate punk, post-hardcore, and even hardcore. The primary songwriter, John Shields, often incorporates politically-charged lyrics into their songs, taking a stance against the unjustified use of military force, the current state of American politics, and the biases deep rooted in social injustice. In 2005, the band added a third guitarist, Danny Johnson, and released their sophomore album, Voices, which received much critical acclaim, charting at #5 on the Billboard 200. Ruder Than You’s third album, titled Blitzkrieg was released in 2008 reaching #4 on the Billboard Chart. Produced by iconic punk rock producer Brett Gurewitz, this album signaled a change in the sound of the band, utilizing louder production and the addition of more complex song structures. With the years leading up to 2014, the band remained mostly inactive with few small tours in the years surrounding their 4th studio album, Aging Gracefully, which “carried on the tradition of fiery punk rock while recognizing the improvement of the band’s musicianship” (Scenestar). In 2017, the band began to heavily tour in support of a 5th studio album, and again tapped Brett Gurewitz to produce. After a series of successful tour dates, 2018 saw the release of the punk opus Modern Warfare. The 11 track album saw significant success beyond anything the band had seen prior, and gained them a performance slot on the Late Show with Stephen Colbert in the same year. Ruder Than You is currently continuing to tour and support their discography, while starting to produce new music for a 6th studio album set to be released in 2021. The band’s success continues to be attributed to the sheer intensity of their live performances, as well as the lyrical wit and quality of their albums.

The 2011 Elite League speedway season was the 16th to take place since the first airing of the Speedway Elite League in 1995. 2011 was the last season of the Elite League as the total of ten teams were reduced down to just five for the 2012 season. Opening the season on 8 April, Swindon Robins defeated their rivals Wolverhampton Wolves 50–45 to begin their campaign, while Coventry Bees drew 46–46 at home with Peterborough Panthers. A week later, the Eastbourne Eagles dispatched the Belle Vue Aces 50–42 at Arlington Stadium in the first of the ‘Academy League’ fixtures. After the first round of fixtures, the Wolves led the standings with 7 points, followed by the Robins, Eagles and Panthers on 6 points, with Coventry bringing up the rear of the table. Wolverhampton Wolves maintained their lead throughout the early part of the season, with Swindon and Eastbourne equally matched in second and third place respectively. After 13 rounds of fixtures, the teams faced the first split of the season with early frontrunners Wolverhampton finishing top of the overall standings. Swindon and Eastbourne finished the regular season tied for second place, with a number of young riders making their debut in what was to be the final season of the Elite League. Leicester Lions and Belle Vue finished third and fourth respectively, with Plymouth Devils ending the season in fifth and Coventry Bees finishing bottom of the table. The play-offs saw the four highest placed teams all make the semi-finals, with reigning champions Swindon Robins defeating the Eastbourne Eagles in the first leg, before Wolverhampton Wolves prevailed against Leicester in the second. Swindon and Wolverhampton met in the Grand Final at the prestigious Monmore Green Stadium, with the Robins narrowly defeating the Wolves to be crowned Champions of the Elite League. The 2011 Elite League saw some of the best racing in the history of the league, with a record crowd of over 7,000 racing fans being in attendance for the Grand Final at Monmore Green. With the league set to expand to 12 teams for the 2012 season, the 2011 elite League proved to be an exciting and memorable season for all involved.

James Ferguson (October 29th, 1954 - August 3rd, 2023) was an American professional basketball player for the New York Knicks. He was born in Brooklyn, New York City. He attended Stuyvesant High School, where he was a star on the school’s basketball team. He then attended college at Harvard University, where he was also a star on the basketball team. After his college playing days were over, he was drafted as the sixth overall in the 1976 NBA draft by the Knicks. Ferguson had a successful nine-year career in the NBA. He was known as a strong rebounder and defensive presence, earning five All-Defenesive team selections while playing primarily at the power forward position. He was also known for having an impressive mid-range jumper and a reliable floater that he used to score in the post. In his second season, he was named to the All-Star team and was a major contributor to the Knicks' success, helping them reach the NBA finals in 1977 and 1979. During his career, he averaged 12.4 points, 10.2 rebounds and 1.8 blocks per game. He finished with career averages of 12.4 points, 8.4 rebounds, 1.4 blocks, and .5 steals. When his Knicks playing career ended, he occassionally served as a color commentator for Knicks games. Two decades after his NBA career ended, James Ferguson was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2018, cementing his status as one of the greatest players of his era. He died of complications related to a heart condition in 2023. He was 68 years old. Ferguson is remembered today as one of the greatest New York Knicks and basketball players of all-time and is widely considered to be one of the best rebounders and post players to ever play the game. He was a dedicated hard-working player who put forth tremendous effort on both ends of the court and was an example of excellence and sportsmanship for young players in the game. He is also remembered for his philanthropy, having created the James Ferguson Foundation, which supports children's hospital in his hometown of Brooklyn. To honor his memory, the New York Knicks retired Ferguson's jersey (#22) in a pregame ceremony in 2023. He will forever be remembered and honored for his immense contributions to the sport of basketball.

Robert Small (January 26, 1868 - July 3, 1929) was an Irish born trade unionist from Scotland. He was a leading figure in the trade union movement in the United Kingdom during the early 20th century. Small was born in Dublin, Ireland to a family of limited means. After his father's death in 1888, he moved to Scotland where he worked at a coal mine in Airdrie. In 1896 Small joined the Airdrie Miners' Union and quickly became a prominent leader in the organization, eventually becoming the union's president in 1912. He rose to prominence in the Scottish trade union movement during this time and was a founding member of the coal miners' union in Leeds. He became politically active in 1900 when he was elected as a member of the Harmony and Progress Party, a local socialist party. He was the selected as a delegate to the annual congress of the Trade Union Congress in 1901. He was actively involved in the founding of the Labour Party and was elected onto their National Executive in 1906. From 1908 to 1909, Small held the position of General Secretary of the Miners' Federation of Great Britain. He was an unrelenting advocate for improved working conditions and helped create the 1911 Mines Act, which introduced health and safety regulations in the mining industry. Small was a strong believer in the need for trade unions to become more politically involved in order to improve social and economic equality. His efforts towards this goal culminated with the creation of the Labour Representation Committee in 1906. The committee was created to secure the rights of working people and increase their representation in parliament. Small was instrumental in the formation of this committee and was elected to the executive board of the Labour Party in 1908, 1922 and 1923. Small also played an important role in the formation of the National Union of Railwaymen in 1913, which merged a number of major British railway unions into one. He served as the union's first president and continued in that role until his death. In 1925, he was appointed to the National Executive of the Trades Union Congress and was a key figure in the Parliament of Labour During the 1926 General Strike, Small worked diligently to support the league of strikers and was involved in fundraising efforts to help those affected by the strike. He died in 1929 of tuberculosis in a sanatorium near Edinburgh, Scotland and was buried in Edinburgh's Newington cemetery. Small was a major figure in the British labour movement who devoted his life to improving the working and living conditions of all British workers. He was an advocate for freedom from oppression, fair wages and safe working conditions. His legacy continues to shape the British trade union movement and Labour Party's current policies.

The W National Park massacre occurred on August 7, 2014, in W National Park, located in northeastern Niger. At the time, it was believed to be the deadliest terrorist attack in the country's history. On the morning of August 7th, gunmen launched a series of coordinated attacks against two small villages located in the park.The attacks began at dawn when gunmen on motorbikes attacked the first village, Gossera. The attackers killed at least ninety people, mostly by shooting. The attackers also burned down numerous homes and businesses during the attack. During the assault, the gunmen also destroyed a nearby unoccupied clinic. In addition to the ninety dead, over forty survivors were seriously injured as a result of the attack. Most were women and children. The second village, Gozawa, was attacked shortly after the assault on Gossera. The attackers killed at least twenty-nine people, including several security personnel, and destroyed homes and shops in the village. Immediately following the attacks, Nigerien security forces intensified patrols around the park, and an investigation was opened. On August 17, 2014, Nigerien forces launched a joint operation with forces from neighboring countries to apprehend the attackers. The operation resulted in the capture of several suspected militants who have since been charged with the crimes. The W National Park massacre is a reminder of the continued instability in the country, and the important role of targeted security operations in protecting Niger’s population from further attacks. The incident also stimulated discussions in the international community, with some human rights groups condemning the attack and calling for greater efforts to increase security in the region. Today, several memorials honoring the victims of the massacre have been erected in the region. The attack continues to be a subject of national mourning and an important part of the country’s history.

Kevin Eastman (born June 15, 1968) is an American former professional basketball player. He was drafted as the 12th overall pick in the 1990 NBA Draft by the Seattle SuperSonics. He attended South Arlington High School in Arlington, Texas, and TCU where he averaged 17.6 points and 6.8 rebounds per game in 1989. He was an All-Southwest Conference player in 1988–89 and 1989–90, the SWC Player of the Year in 1989 and an All-American honorable mention in 1990. Eastman was traded to the Los Angeles Clippers in January 1991, and was the starter for the team for the remainder of the season. He was briefly in the 1995-96 season with the Phoenix Suns, and also played in the CBA. During his NBA career, Eastman played in a total of 301 regular season games and averaged 8.2 points and 3.1 rebounds per game. His best statistical season was 1991-92, when he averaged 14.8 points, 5.0 assists and 4.3 rebounds per game. Eastman started his coaching career in 2003 with the Clippers and was an assistant coach until 2011. He then went on to be an assistant coach at UNLV before being appointed as the head coach of the University of Texas of the Permian Basin in 2016. After a brief stint at UTPB, Eastman left the school in 2018 and is currently serving as an assistant coach for the NBA G League's Wisconsin Herd. Eastman was inducted into the Fort Worth Basketball Hall of Fame in 2013. He has also been inducted into the TCU Letterman's Hall of Fame and the Arlington Sports Hall of Fame. Eastman currently resides in Dallas, Texas with his wife and two sons. He enjoys playing golf, fishing and is an avid fan of TCU Football.

The Del Webb Explosion was an industrial disaster that occurred on August 8, 1989 at the Del Webb Corporation's munitions facility in South Jacksonville, FL, part of the much larger Jacksonville Naval Air Station. The explosion, coming from a warehouse full of explosives, injured more than 400 people and leveled 72 buildings in the surrounding area. The explosion was believed to have been caused by a problem with the compactor machine at the plant. The compactor was being used to crush empty crates that had been storing ammunition to facilitate the recycling of the material. However, the compaction process had become stuck, causing the building to fill with smoke and fumes. When workers attempted to clear the blockage, it resulted in a powerful explosion. At the time of the blast, the facility was storing a variety of munitions intended for use in military operations as well as for private purchase. Upon detonation, the resulting explosion was powerful enough to cause extensive damage to the plant and surrounding area, including extensive damage to nearby homes and businesses. In the immediate aftermath of the blast there were four fatalities, two Del Webb workers and two residents from the nearby neighborhood. At least 400 people were injured, many with life-threatening injuries. A survey conducted by state officials after the explosion found that about 72 buildings had been destroyed or damaged beyond repair, including a total of 218 homes that were either damaged or destroyed by the blast. The explosion was classified as a Class “C” disaster, the highest category rating given to industrial accidents in the United States. The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) approved aid to the affected families and individuals, totaling more than $9 million in funding. Cleanup and reconstruction efforts at the plant lasted well over a year. After a thorough review of the accident, improvements were made at the site and it was re-opened in 1990 with considerably fewer ammunition storage facilities. As a result of the disaster, tighter federal regulations were imposed on the handling of explosives in the United States. In the decades following the accident, the Del Webb Corporation has worked to rebuild the community by providing assistance to affected individuals and families, as well as hosting a number of charity events in the area. This included helping to fund the Jacksonville Navy Relief Fund and sponsoring several youth charities.

Lom Peak (Bulgarian: връх Лом) is a peak in the Balkan Mountains, located in southwestern Bulgaria. With an elevation of 2225m, it is the highest peak of the Kartala-Sokolna-Lom massif, as well as the fourth highest mountain in Bulgaria. The peak is located in the Rhodope Mountains, in the municipality of Chepelare. It is situated near the border with Greece, forming part of the Greek–Bulgarian border range. The summit offers spectacular views of the entire region, including the Pirin and Balkan mountains. The peak and its surroundings are part of a nature park established in 1993. The Lom river, which originates from the peak, contributes significantly to the park's flora and fauna. The area is known for its endemic species and abundant biodiversity. The area has been inhabited since antiquity, with evidence of ancient settlements of Thracian people, Romans, and Bulgarians. A small church dedicated to Saint Spas near the peak bears witness to the area's long-lasting religious presence, as does the existence of many caves where the locals used to worship their local gods. The peak can be reached from the village of Lyazimovo, which is the base of the popular site for its ecosystems and pristine forests. The peak can be hiked from the villages of Kartalovo, Lyazimovo, Sokolna and Lopushna. The trip from the Lopushna village to the peak takes around 7 hours, where the tourists are exposed more closely to the mountainous flora and fauna. Lom peak is a popular destination among extreme sports enthusiasts and hikers. It has been featured in the British TV show 'Most Shocking Extreme Adrenaline Adventure' and its breathtaking beauty is depicted on canvas by beautiful paintings done by well-known Bulgarian painters. The peak is among the most photographed spots in the region and is visited by photographers looking to snap panoramic shots. The peak is also part of the European long-distance hiking trail E3, which runs between the Atlantic Coast of France and the Black Sea. The peak is easily reachable by car and is a popular tourist destination in the region. The peak can be reached from the village of Lyazimovo, where accommodation is available for the tourists. The Lom peak offers a spectacular view and can be an unforgettable experience for all types of travellers.

Rajendra Krishan (1922–1987) was an Indian lyricist, screenwriter and playwright active in the Hindi language film industry, or Bollywood, from the 1940s to the early 1980s. He wrote successful and popular songs for many of Bollywood's classic films, including Anarkali (1953), Pyaasa (1957), Chhoti Bahen (1959), Professor (1962), Lawaaris (1981) and others. Krishan was born in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh to a family of middle-class Banrasi Hindus. His family moved to Ambala shortly afterward, where Krishan attended school. He was an avid reader of Hindi poetry, and was deeply influenced by Kabir, Ramprasad, Mirza Ghalib and the Bhakti movement. After graduating from the Government College in Hissar, he joined the Indian Air Force during the Second World War, serving briefly as an instructor. After the war, Krishan moved to Mumbai and joined the film industry as a lyricist. He also worked as a dialogue writer and playwright, occasionally establishing himself as an independent producer. He was one of the most sought-after lyricists of the 1950s and 1960s, and wrote for a variety of genres, including family dramas, romances, and patriotic songs. Krishan is best known for his lyrics on a number of prominent film songs, such as the chartbuster "Haal Kaisa Hai Janab Ka" in Chalti Ka Naam Gaadi (1958), "Eena Meena Deeka" in Aasha (1957) and the classic song of romance "Humne Tumko Dekha" from Gumnaam (1965). He is also remembered for writing the hit title song for Raja Aur Runk (1968), in which he used the fictional language of Hindi movie songs. Krishan was known for writing meaningful, poetic and thought-provoking songs. During his career, he won many awards and accolades, including the Filmfare Award for Best Lyricist in 1958, 1959 and 1962. He also won the Filmfare Award for Best Dialogue in 1959, and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1975. Krishan was an active member of the Progressive Writers Association, and was known to be passionate about left-wing politics. He passed away on 13 June 1987 at the age of 65, leaving behind a vast and influential body of work.

Larry Wade (born November 3, 1981) is an American football coach and former professional player. He is currently the wide receivers coach at the University of Kansas. Wade was born in Miami, Florida, and grew up in nearby Coral Gables. At Christopher Columbus High School, he was an All-State wide receiver and an academic honor roll member. Wade then attended the University of Miami from 2000-2004, where he earned a Bachelor of Science degree in education. While at Miami, Wade played wide receiver for the Hurricanes and was a key contributor to the team's 2001 national championship. He finished his collegiate career with eighty-eight receptions for 1,048 yards and four touchdowns. After college, Wade went on to play in the Arena Football League and NFL Europe. He then returned to the University of Miami to pursue his dream of becoming a coach. From 2006-2008, he served as a graduate assistant with the Miami Hurricanes, helping to coach wide receivers, defensive backs, and punt returners. In 2009, Wade was hired by the University of Central Florida as the wide receivers coach. He would remain at UCF until 2011, when he joined the coaching staff of the NFL's Oakland Raiders as the offensive quality control coach. He was then the wide receivers coach at Purdue University in 2013 and 2014. In 2015, Wade accepted a position to become the wide receivers coach at the University of Kansas, a position he still holds. He was part of the staff that led the Jayhawks to their first bowl game in over a decade during the 2020 season. Off the field, Wade also serves as a mentor to local youths in the community. He is involved with a variety of charities and in 2017, he was awarded the Kansas Jayhawks 'Coach of Character' award. Wade is an avid fisherman and also enjoys spending time with his wife and three daughters. He is always looking for ways to give back to the community and inspire the next generation of football players.

Siphiwe Gloria Ndlovu (born 1989) is a Zimbabwean actress, author and philanthropist. She is best-known for her work in Zimbabwean films and television programs, such as ‘Muvhango’ and ‘Juba’. Ndlovu was born in Harare in 1989. Growing up she had a passion for music, art, writing and acting. She pursued her acting career and graduated from Zimbabwe’s Institute for the Performing Arts in 2011. In 2012, Ndlovu was awarded the Best Actress award at Zimbabwe's Campus Life Awards. She then furthered her career by winning a competition to join the ensemble cast of SABC's TV show Muvhango, playing the role of Vho-Thandaza. Ndlovu has collaborated with other television programs and movies, such as the ‘Big Brother’ spinoff, ‘The Chase’. She has also made appearances in commercials for KFC, African Banking Corporation and Delight Bread. Ndlovu has ventured into producing and writing, creating a short movie, ‘The Other Side’ and co-authoring a best selling novel ‘Let it Go’. Ndlovu is also a corporate brand ambassador for various brands, such as Etihad Airways, Remmogo Skincare and Veiled Beauty Cosmetics. In addition to her entertainment career, Ndlovu is an ambassador to various humanitarian projects in Zimbabwe, such as the Zimbabwean Children's Charity, where she spends her time visiting hospitals, schools and orphanages in Zimbabwe and other countries in the region. She has been appointed to be an ambassador to the United Nation's Water and Sanitation Program. Her talents, work and contributions to society have been recognized by various organizations, including the Zimbabwean Achievers Awards, where she was awarded the Most Inspirational Achiever of the Year for her philanthropic efforts in 2016. Ndlovu currently resides in Johannesburg, South Africa, where she concentrates on pursuing her acting and philanthropic endeavors.

Maryhill Estates is a residential community located in Harrison County, Kentucky, United States. The Estates are situated on the border of the city of Cynthiana and the unincorporated village of North Middletown. Located on the Kentucky River, the community is surrounded by rolling hills and pastures, making its the perfect rural retreat. The origins of Maryhill Estates can be traced back to the mid-1800s, when the area was home to a small community of farmers. By the turn of the century, the area had become a bustling center of trade, with a number of businesses and manufacturing facilities setting up shop. The primary business of the day was the production of coal tar and coke byproducts. As the demand for coal tar and coke grew, more businesses and farms were established in the region, and the population of the area began to swell. The area was first developed into a residential community in the early part of the 20th century, when a group of local real estate developers bought up a portion of land and began the process of subdividing it into residential lots. The development was publicly marketed as a “Satellite Town” for Cynthiana in 1929, and construction began soon after. The new homes quickly attracted a number of affluent professionals, who were looking for a quieter, more rural setting. The combination of the rich agricultural resources, beautiful scenery, and proximity to Cynthiana soon made Maryhill Estates a popular place to call home. As the residential population of the area continued to grow, so did the number of businesses, stores and other services that were established. In the following years, new schools were established, roads were improved and additional amenities were added. Today, Maryhill Estates is home to a blend of rural, modern and historic homes and businesses, making it the perfect place to live and work. With easy access to amenities and services, and a vibrant sense of community, Maryhill Estates is the perfect place to call home.

Spiros Vondas (born 2 December 1967) is a Greek entrepreneur and investor. He is the founder of what is presently known as the Vondas Group, a multinational conglomerate of finance and investment firms headquartered in London. He serves as its current Chairman and CEO. Vondas was born in Athens, Greece, to a family of entrepreneurs. His father, Kostas, had made his fortune in shipping after founding his own shipping line. Vondas grew up in an entrepreneurial atmosphere and was adamant from a young age that he wanted to follow in his father’s footsteps. He began investing in small companies and quickly built a reputation as one of the most successful investors of his generation. Vondas attended the Athens University of Economics and Business and graduated in 1989 with a degree in Economics and Finance. After graduation, he founded the Vondas Group and began to build his portfolio of investments. In the early 2000s, Vondas expanded the scope of his business to include investments in the banking sector. He has since become a major shareholder in banks in countries such as Greece, the United Kingdom, The United States, France, Spain, Hungary, and Cyprus. Vondas is renowned for his success in the banking industry and his investments have garnered a lot of recognition. Credit Suisse named him one of the 'Most Powerful Bankers of the Mediterranean' while Ernst & Young named him 'Entrepreneur of the Year' in the finance sector in 2008. Outside of business, Vondas is a philanthropist. In 2004, he partnered with the Greek government to set up a charity arm of the Vondas Group to focus on providing support to underprivileged communities and educational initiatives. He currently works with the Christian Aid Foundation and is an active patron of several charities across Greece, the UK, and the US. An astute businessman and savvy investor, Vondas has forged a successful career from leading the Vondas Group. He is a firm believer in using his success to benefit others, and has been encouraging people to pursue their dreams through his philanthropic work.

Cyd Zeigler is an American sportswriter and media commentator who specializes in LGBT coverage in sport. He is a co-founder of the media platform Outsports, the first website to cover LGBT athletes and issues in sport, as well as the co-founder of the LGBT sports media event Outsports Pride. Zeigler was born in November 1972 in Jacksonville, Florida. He graduated from the University of Florida in 1995 with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism. He worked at AOL Time Warner in their media department before leaving in 2000 to become the Managing Editor of Outsports.com. Outsports was founded by Zeigler and partner Jim Buzinski in 1999, in order to provide non-judgmental coverage of LGBT athletes in all sports. From the site's launch in 1999 until its closure in 2018, Outsports covered the coming out stories of over 400 athletes, while providing constant investigation into the world of LGBT issues within sport. In 2013, Zeigler and Buzinski founded the annual LGBT sports event Outsports Pride in Los Angeles, to celebrate LGBT inclusivity and announce awards for exceptional media coverage of LGBT issues. In 2013, Zeigler wrote his first book titled "Jockocracy: Gay Athletes and the Cult of Masculinity", which dives into covering the lives of gay professional athletes and provides insight into how a heterosexual male-dominated sport handles LGBT athletes. He regularly contributes to the Huffington Post, Buzzfeed, SB Nation, and ESPN and has appeared numerous times on CNN, MSNBC and the BBC to talk about LGBT athletes and sports coverage. In 2014, he was honored by the Gay and Lesbian Alliance Against Defamation at their inaugural Sports Media Awards, where he accepted the award for Excellence in Commentary. In 2015, he became a National Board Member of the National Gay and Lesbian Sports Hall of Fame. In February 2020 he was honored by the Los Angeles Gay and Lesbian Center with the GLAAD20 Award. Zeigler advocated in June 2020 for the National Hockey League to host an event celebrating queer players, similar to MLB's LGBTQ+ “Pride Night.” In 2021, Zeigler co-authored a book published by Stanford University Press titled, "The Disordered Score: An Inside Look at the Politics, Power, and Intimacy of LGBT Sports Journalism in the 21st Century." Cyd Zeigler continues to provide readers with thoughtful insights and commentary from an LGBT perspective to the sports world and continues to be a pioneer in LGBT sports media.

Rae Morris (born 26 December 1989) is an English singer-songwriter and musician. She began recording as a solo artist in 2011, in her teens, and has since released three studio albums, one EP, and a handful of acclaimed singles. Morris has achieved considerable commercial and critical success, topping the UK Independent Singles Breakers Chart, achieving Gold certified records in several territories, and gaining a nomination for the Brit Awards’ Critics’ Choice Prize in 2015. Morris was born and raised in Blackpool in Lancashire, having started to learn the piano aged four. She began uploading covers of songs to MySpace when she was fifteen, and went on to study music at college, involving producing her own material. In 2011, she was featured on Tom Odell's Stay Tonight, before beginning to form her own material. In 2012, she released her debut single, Its Gonna Be Alright, on home label Urbandawn, which she then followed under her own name, released a handful of EPs, the most popular being From Above and the Cold EP in 2013. She released her debut album, Unguarded, in 2015. It topped the UK Independent Albums chart and charted in the top 40 of the UK Albums Chart. It was named Rough Trade Record's Album of the Year, and was nominated for a BRIT Award for Best British Female Artist. She continued to gain traction, releasing a further two studio albums; Someone Out There in 2018, and also its deluxe edition, Someone Out There Remixed in 2019. Morris’ single Do It was featured in the popular TV show Skins in 2013, and she has since collaborated on songs with Gnash, Rudimental and Fre Jakobson over the years. She has enjoyed a loyal fan base, with two headline tours and numerous cross-European tours including the famous Later… With Jools Holland. Morris’ music is often associated with the synth-pop genre, and has developed from a stripped-back piano-led style to a fully formed pop sound with her latest offering. Her style has been praised for its warm and strident vocals, as well as for its deep and authentic lyrics. Her style of music also draws influences from many other genres of electronica. In 2011, Rae Morris was made an Ambassador for Blackpool Aimhigh, which aimed to bridge the gap between those aged 15-25 and their peers, while promoting singing and the creative arts in Blackpool. She is also an Ambassador for Teenage Cancer Trust. She currently lives in Manchester and is signed to Atlantic Records.

Crêpe paper is a kind of light-weight, crinkled tissue paper that is generally used for a variety of decorative purposes, such as art projects, giftwrapping, flower arrangements, and streamers. It is made from wood pulp fibers and commonly colored, although some styles use plain white or other colors. Crêpe paper is distinct from crepe paper in that the former is a paper with tiny creases along its length, while the latter is a fabric-like paper with a wavy, crinkly texture. The creases of the crêpe paper make it easy to bend and shape into various designs, making it a popular choice for decorations. Early use of crêpe paper was found in the French court during the 17th century, as a way of dressing up courtiers for special occasions. By the 19th century, the delicate paper was being more widely used in Europe and countries around the world for decorating both churches and homes. Crêpe paper is available in a variety of colors and textures, and thickness levels. The paper can be transparent, semi-transparent, or opaque, depending on the type. It is generally sold in rolls from online stores and craft stores. Due to its light weight and delicate texture, crêpe paper is typically used for creating items such as masks, flowers, clothing, banners, decorations, and larger art installations. It is a versatile material, and can be shaped, painted, glued and layered to create custom creations. It can also be used in paper crafting projects, such as making wreaths, garlands, and paper flowers. Because of its versatility, crêpe paper can be a great addition to any Home décor project. It can be used in a variety of ways, including to add color and texture to walls or furniture, to wrap around furniture legs or to make curtains or lampshades. Crêpe paper is also a great way to add a personal touch to special events, such as weddings, birthday parties, bridal showers, baby showers, and more. In recent years, crêpe paper’s popularity has surged in the DIY crafting community, as more people are using the material for their own crafty creations. With its ease of use and wide range of colors and textures, it is an easy material to work with that can yield beautiful and unique results. Overall, crêpe paper is a great addition to any artist or crafter’s repertoire. With its delicate texture and the ability to be easily manipulated in to various shapes, it provides a unique and creative way to add personal touches to any art project or event.

The Count of Lucena is a Spanish aristocratic title bestowed by King Juan Carlos I of Spain to Cayetano Yáñez de la Almedina y Lucena in 1981. The recipient of the title is Don Cayetano Yáñez de la Almedina y Lucena, the first and current Count of Lucena. Don Cayetano Yáñez de la Almedina y Lucena was born in Madrid on April 12, 1948. He is the son of Don Cayetano Yáñez de la Almedina y Vega and Doña Josefina Lucena y Arcocha. He is an attorney at law who specializes in administrative law and is a professor of Human Rights at the University of Cordoba, Spain. Don Cayetano Yáñez de la Almedina y Lucena was the mayor of Argamasilla de Alba (a municipality in the Province of Córdoba, Spain) from 1983 to 1999 and Vice-President of the Province of Córdoba from 1999 to 2004. In 1981, King Juan Carlos I of Spain bestowed the title "Count of Lucena" to Don Cayetano Yáñez de la Almedina y Lucena in recognition of his contributions to civic life and politics in the Province of Córdoba. The title includes the hereditary subordination of the village of Purchena, Spain, and the attachment to it of the towns of Aljucén and Negratín, both in the Province of Granada. As Count of Lucena, Don Cayetano Yáñez de la Almedina y Lucena is a member of the Grand Catalan Council, a body established by King Juan Carlos I of Spain in 1981 as part of the Spanish Monarchy's devolution of powers to the autonomous regions of Spain. In 2009, Don Cayetano Yáñez de la Almedina y Lucena was recognized by the Association of Anthropologist, Economists and Politicians with the "Premio Internacional Amigos de Cervantes," an honorary award given to those persons who have distinguished themselves in the promotion of peace and understanding amongst the peoples of the world. The Count of Lucena, Don Cayetano Yáñez de la Almedina y Lucena is a member of the nobility of Spain and holds an both ancient and modern titles of nobility, such as Count of Lucena, as well as other titles of honour, such as "Grandee of Spain," "Knight of the Order of Isabella the Catholic" and "Grand Master of the Order of the Royal Martyrs of Spain." His official seal shows the arms of the countship, or coat of arms, of Lucena. Don Cayetano Yáñez de la Almedina y Lucena is married to Doña Purificación Palomo Fernández, daughter of Don Luis Palomo Izquierdo and Doña Carolina Fernández Díaz, and has five children. The current Count of Lucena is Don Cayetano Yáñez de la Almedina y Lucena, the first to hold the title.

Midget car racing, also known as midget auto racing or simply midget racing, is a form of auto racing featuring small, specially-built race cars that are approximately one-quarter the size of a full-size car. The term "midget" historically refers to an adult person of short stature, but in the context of motor sports, it refers to a car powered by a diminutive but highly-modified engine. Many midget car drivers have gone on to have successful careers in full-size auto racing, with legends like Mario Andretti and A.J. Foyt having raced both types of cars in their early days. Midget car racing is the most popular form of midget racing in the United States and Canada. It was first developed in the 1930s as a way for auto enthusiasts to race their home-built cars on dirt tracks. It has since grown into a multi-billion dollar sport, with hundreds of events taking place annually across the continent. Most midget car races are contested on smaller dirt tracks, and the cars are often equipped with mid-size engines, front and rear-end suspension, and a variety of other modifications to enhance their capabilities. The National Midget Auto Racing Association (NMRA) is the sanctioning body for most midget car races. The body sets rules and regulations for midget car construction, engines, and all other aspects of race day operations. Midget cars races are also overseen by local sanctioning bodies such as USAC, WoO, WOO and ASCS. In addition to dirt tracks, midget cars also race on paved ovals and road courses. The most popular events for these classes of cars include the Chili Bowl Nationals, the Turkey Night Grand Prix, and the Belleville Midget Nationals. In addition, there are various clubs and racing leagues around the country dedicated to midget car racing. Midget car racing has seen tremendous growth in popularity over the years and is now one of the most popular forms of racing in North America. With the advent of modern safety features and technology, the sport has become much safer while still thrilling to watch and participate in. Drivers and teams continue to push the envelope, developing ever faster and more advanced cars to take home championships, purses and glory.

En résille is a type of decorative ribbon or netting made from materials such as silk, cotton and synthetic fibers. It is most often used for costumes, lingerie and millinery. It is typically made of thread which is woven to form the net, with yarns of different colors and sometimes different textures used to create the desired effect or pattern in the material. The word “résille” is a French term derived from the verb resille, which means “to interlace” or “to lace together”. The netting is often woven in a diamond-shaped pattern and comes in a variety of colors and designs. En résille has been used throughout history in fashion and the decorative arts. As early as the 16th century, résille was used in medieval clothing and accessories and by the 19th century was a popular material used to adorn ladies' fashion items. These garments were often embellished with crystals, beads and other materials. Résille was highly sought after in the early 20th century as well, and lingerie pieces adorned with the material were popular during the period. The material has enjoyed a resurgence in popularity in recent years and has become a staple for the contemporary couture designer. It has made appearances on the catwalk of some of today's top fashion houses, such as Prada and Alexander McQueen, and is often combined with other fabrics and materials in modern garments and accessories. En résille is also used in activities such as dressmaking, beading and embroidery, and is a popular choice for creating a wide range of items from baby bonnets to hats and bags. Beaded résille is also a popular choice for costuming or for fancy dress occasions. The material is extremely versatile and can be manipulated in many different ways with the addition of beads, decorative effects and additional textiles to create a truly unique effect.

4045 Lowengrub is a mid-sized asteroid located in the central area of the asteroid belt. It was classified as both a main-belt asteroid and a Mars-crosser, due to its orbit passing close to that of Mars. Discovered by scientists at the Lowell Observatory on March 16, 1898, it is one of more than 70,000 asteroids discovered to date. It is estimated to measure between 8.6 and 18.6 kilometers in diameter, and completes one revolution around the sun in 5.14 years. In other words, it takes the asteroid approximately 5 years and 2 months to travel around the sun. The asteroid orbits the sun between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, meaning it belongs to the population of asteroids that are located in the asteroid belt. The asteroid is believed to be composed mainly of metals, such as nickel and iron. The Minor Planet Center records 4045 Lowengrub’s orbital elements, meaning it has its own catalogue number (241925). Lowengrub is also notable for being one of the most circular objects in the Solar System, with an eccentricity of 0.013. 4045 Lowengrub was named in honour of Mike Lowengrub for his contributions to planetary astronomy. He was awarded the 2004 Carl Sagan Medal for Excellence in Public Communication of Planetary Science by the Division of Planetary Sciences of the American Astronomical Society. Lowengrub was also the first asteroid to be identified as a near-Earth object, meaning it could potentially collide with Earth. However, the chances of this happening are very small, since the object is currently more than 300 million kilometers away from us. In the near future, Lowengrub is expected to undergo close encounters with both Earth and Mars. In 2086 it passed within 4 million kilometers of Earth, with similar close approaches predicted in 2118 and 2156. In 2087 it will pass within 4 million kilometers of Mars. 4045 Lowengrub is one of the many minor planets that populate our Solar System, and a reminder of the power and complexity of the universe. With its unique characteristics, it will continue to be a source of fascination for astronomers for years to come.

The Mauritanian Regroupment Party (MRP) is a political party in Mauritania founded in 1958 by Moktar Ould Daddah. The party was created by Ould Daddah to help him consolidate his power and promote stability in the country. The MRP sought to unite the different ethnic groups in the country and to end disputes between tribes and regions. The party enjoyed a long period of dominance during the years following independence until the 1990s. The goals of the MRP were twofold: to promote economic development and to serve as a political vehicle for Ould Daddah. In pursuit of these goals, the party used its control of the government to institute various reforms, such as expanding education and increasing the availability of healthcare. It also sought to foster regional integration, moving away from the traditional tribal arrangement of Mauritania’s population. The MRP had a great deal of success in its early years and achieved many of its primary goals. It was influential in the economic development of the country and was widely accepted by the people. In the 1976 elections, Ould Daddah was reelected with 84% of the vote, largely thanks to the support of the MRP. However, in the 1980s, the MRP began to lose its popular appeal as the effects of a long period of drought began to take their toll on the population. Additionally, Ould Daddah’s increasingly authoritarian rule began to alienate people from the party. By the early 1990s, the MRP was in decline and its share of the vote had dwindled to a mere two percent of the electorate. Aside from its policies, the MRP has been credited with helping to bring stability to Mauritania during its early years of independence. Ould Daddah was able to bring together previously divided tribes and regions and to instill a sense of national identity and pride. Though it has lost support over the years, the Mauritanian Regroupment Party remains one of the country’s main political forces.

The List of Minnesota North Stars head coaches is a comprehensive listing of all the Minnesota North Stars head coaches since the team's founding in 1967. The North Stars attained the best success during the 1988–89 season, when the team won the division title and reached the Stanley Cup Finals. The franchise has seen 28 head coaches fill the vacancy since 1967, when the team was initiated into the National Hockey League. The most successful Minnesota North Stars coaches, to date, are Glen Sonmor, who led the team to playoff appearances three years in a row from 1987 to 1989, and Jack Gordon, who remains the team's longest-tenured head coach, coaching for seven seasons from 1978-1985. Roger Neilson was the first head coach of the Minnesota North Stars, coaching the 1967–68 season which saw the team make its debut in the NHL. Parker MacDonald followed suit, then Jack Gordon, who coached the team to its first division championship in the 1979-80 season. Glen Sonmor, who coached the North Stars from 1986 to 1990, was the longest-tenured and most successful head coach for the North Stars. His success brought the franchise to the Stanley Cup Finals in its first season, which the team lost to the Edmonton Oilers. This was followed by reasons of competence and results. After Sonmor left the team, Bob Gainey became the North Star's head coach. He was the first North Stars coach to qualify for the playoffs after the expansion to 14 teams in 1991–92. The post-Gainey era saw Dave Tippett, Ken Hitchcock, Jacques Lemaire, and Marc Crawford at the helm of the Minnesota franchise. Jacques Lemaire was the most successful of these coaches and guided the team to their first post-season appearance after the expansion. Lemaire's tenure was followed by a series of brief coaching tenures. Doug McLean was aided by assistant coach Andy Murray and guided the team to their first division title in 15 seasons. He was then succeeded by former North Stars player, Lorne Henning. Darryl Sutter then took the head coach role for the rest of the 1996–97 season. Jacques Lemaire was then rehired in 2000 and Doug Palazzari succeeded Lemaire in 2003. The Mike Keenan era began in 2005, but Keenan was not retained after the 2007 season. Todd Richards filled the head coach role from 2008 until his dismissal in 2009. Following Richards, the head coaching role was permanently filled by Marc Crawford. Tom Renney and Rich Winter followed the Crawford era and served brief stints as the North Stars' head coach. Dean Evason and Don Granato finished off the Minnesota North Stars' head coach history, and the team became the Dallas Stars in 1993. The Minnesota North Stars' head coach position has seen its share of successes, including a berth in the 1989 Stanley Cup Finals and a division title, as well as a long list of disappointments and unfinished seasons. Despite the team's relocation to Dallas and subsequent change of name, the Minnesota North Stars' legacy remains when it comes to the team's long and storied head coaching history.

The rhinoceros auklet (Cerorhinca monocerata) is a small alcid seabird native to the Pacific coasts of Alaska and British Columbia, as well as offshore islands in the Aleutian Islands, Bering Sea, and Gulf of Alaska. It is considered a close living relative of the extinct great auk, and is sometimes colloquially referred to as a "giant auklet". The rhinoceros auklet is one of the smallest auklets, measuring about 17–19cm in length and weighing 75–110 g. It is primarily grey with a white underside, similar in appearance to other auklets, but is distinguished by its large, pointed bill with a hook at the tip and obvious white lines on the face and around the eyes, giving the species its name. The rhinoceros auklet breeds in colonies on off-shore islands, often in large numbers. They live in burrows or crevices amongst rocks or vegetation, and spend much of the year at sea, where they feed on zooplankton. Nesting activities typically take place during June–July, with the female laying a single egg that is incubated by both the parents. The chick will stay in its burrow until it is fully grown. In recent decades, the rhinoceros auklet population has seen an overall decline. This is largely attributed to the increase in predator predation, mainly due to introduced species such as rats and cats, as well as other human activities such as overfishing. Moreover, climate change has also been linked to shifts in the species’ distribution. Although the rhinoceros auklet is currently listed as a species of least concern by the IUCN, the population is believed to be in decline and should be monitored carefully to prevent further population declines. The conservation of rhinoceros auklets has become a priority in many areas, and numerous programs have been implemented to protect nesting colonies. In British Columbia, the species is listed as a species at risk, and specific measures have been taken to combat nesting predators and to promote safe and successful breeding. In addition, there are several ongoing research projects that are aimed at learning more about the species and gaining a better understanding of its population trends and movements. Overall, the rhinoceros auklet is a fascinating species that plays an important role in the Pacific ocean ecosystem. In order to ensure its future as a species, it is important to continue research activities and conservation efforts in order to protect the species and its habitat.

Uznach Abbey, sometimes referred to as the Abtei St. Gallen, was an Augustinian monastery located in Uznach, a small town located in the canton of St. Gallen, Switzerland. Founded in 1252 by Abbot Arnold, it was one of the most important spiritual and cultural centers in the region until it was disbanded in 1555 following the Protestant Reformation. The abbey was surrounded by a wall which was 2,800 feet long and 4 feet thick. It contained a number of buildings including the monastery itself, a bakery, a cattle house, stables, a brewery, a chapel, a mill, a hospice, a forge and several gardens and orchards. There was also a large cloister that connected the different parts of the complex. The monks of the abbey were known for their horticultural expertise and kept a wide variety of plants, including many medicinal herbs, in their gardens. The abbey also had extensive land holdings in the surrounding area which were used for grazing cattle, and for growing grain and legumes. Uznach was well known for its library which contained over 1,000 manuscripts and books from the Middle Ages. It contained works by important scholars such as Erasmus, Petrarch, and Thomas Aquinas. The abbey also produced fine pieces of art and commissioned a number of wooden carving of Biblical figures during the 16th century. Most notably, in 1523 the abbot ordered the production of a wooden statue of Christ which gained considerable fame in the area. The abbey had a number of important patrons including the counts of Toggenburg and the lords of Kerenbach. Although it remained in operation until 1555, its influence on the region’s culture began to wane in the 15th century due the rise of the Protestant Reformation and the abbey eventually closed its doors. Today, Uznach Abbey is remembered primarily for its library, its art works, and its contribution to the local culture. Parts of the wall are still standing and the site of the monastery is now home to a local museum which contains a collection of artifacts from the abbey. The wooden sculpture of Christ can still be seen in the local St. Ursula Catholic Church.

John Isner (born April 26, 1985 in Greensboro, North Carolina) is an American professional tennis player. He is currently ranked inside the world's top 50 in singles and is considered to be the best American male tennis player since Andy Roddick. Isner first received attention as a standout player for the University of Georgia. He won the NCAA singles championship in 2007 and was a finalist in 2008. After college, Isner turned professional and has since been a successful mainstay on the men's professional tour. He achieved his highest career ranking of World No. 9 on April 2, 2018 and has reached 6 different Grand Slam quarterfinals in his career. Throughout his career Isner has become known for his prowess in playing an aggressive style of tennis and reaching a great heights within the rankings. He has a total of 19 singles titles to his credit, all but one on the ATP World Tour. His greatest success on the tour came in 2018 when he won the Miami Open and reached the semi-finals at the Masters 1000 event in Toronto. He also had a breakthrough in the Grand Slam tournaments that year, reaching the quarterfinals at the US Open and Wimbledon. Isner has also been a strong doubles player, reaching the 2018 French Open doubles presentation ceremony alongside American Jack Sock. The pair made it to the finals of the 2017 French Open and the 2018 US Open, though they ultimately lost in both instances. In 2019, Isner made it to the round of 16 at the French Open and reached quarters at the US Open. He has continued to have success in 2020 despite the interruption of the tennis calendar due to the COVID-19 pandemic, reaching the final of the Miami Open in March. Isner is well-known for his distinctive serve and his preference for playing the game on a very fast hard court surface. His popular nickname is “The Big Man” and he is considered by many to be an important ambassador for the game of professional tennis in the United States.

Francis Gally (1834-1915) was an English clergyman, popular science writer, and advocate for progressive education. He was born in London of English-French parentage and was educated at Marlborough College and Trinity College, Cambridge. Gally was ordained in the Church of England and held several curacies, including vicar of Highgate from 1861 to 1868. He was progressive in his beliefs, advocating the use of new methods of education, and he was often at odds with traditional establishment values. Gally was a Unitarian and supported the rights of individuals against the dictates of the Church and State. He was educated in the sciences, wrote textbooks on anatomy and astronomy, and wrote plays exploring the place of human suffering as part of divine providence. Gally was an advocate of evolution long before its widespread acceptance and he wrote a series of articles called The Mind of Man Under Evolution in 1866. He also wrote books on evolution and popularized the idea of evolution through natural selection. Gally released the best-selling text book, the Compendium of Anatomy, in 1894 and drew on his love of the natural world to illustrate its many excellences. He also wrote a book on astronomy, A Course of Elementary Astronomy, in 1892 in which he explored the topic of the universe in light of evolutionary theory. Although Gally's books on science had wide popularity, his works on progressive education were less so. His works on education ranged from advocating the use of objects as teaching materials in place of the traditional blackboard and book to debating the validity of corporal punishment within the school setting. He also advocated for an examination system that did not reward cramming, but instead developed the individual talents of each student. Gally was known for his great enthusiasm for his students and his support of new methods of teaching. He was a great encourager of those who wanted to push the boundaries of traditional education. Gally's work and ideas received the attention of many prominent social reformers, including William Makepeace Thackeray and Alfred Lord Tennyson. Despite this attention, Gally's death in 1915 received little attention and no obituary was published. Although he may have had a remarkable life, Francis Gally is by and large forgotten today. In 2021, however, his works have been re-examined and he remains an interesting and influential figure in the history of modern education.

Fred Turner (born June 3, 1998) is an Australian-born professional football (soccer) player who currently plays as a defender for English club Middlesbrough. Turner started his career playing in the National Premier Leagues of his home country Australia, where he caught the eye of scouts from Europe due to his athleticism and aggressive tackling. This prompted Middlesbrough to sign Turner in 2017 after several impressive seasons with his former club. Since joining Middlesbrough, Turner has established himself as a key component of their back line and is one of the more reliable players in the squad. Turner has previously made a number of appearances for the Australian U-20 squad, playing a pivotal role in the team's successful campaign in the 2019 AFC U-19 Championship. He also played a prominent part in Australia's qualification for the 2021 FIFA U-20 World Cup, their first World Cup since 2005. At Middlesbrough, Turner has demonstrated a great ability to marshal his defensive line and close down opposing attackers, and has become an important part of their defense. In 2020, Turner was rewarded for his performances by earning a spot in the Football League Team of the Year. Turner's athleticism makes him a great asset for any team, as he has the ability to cover a lot of ground quickly and is very disciplined when defending. His ability to read the game, intercept passes and times his tackles perfectly make him one of the most promising young defenders in England. Off the pitch, Turner is known to have a great attitude towards the game and his teammates. He is always willing to give 110% and is an individual that always works hard to improve himself. In the future, Turner is looking to break into the first team of Middlesbrough and to become a regular starter in the English Premier League. With his undeniable talent and potential, there is no doubt that he can achieve his goals in the near future.

Takashi Aoyagi (born 12 June 1966 in Tokyo, Japan) is a professional animator, animation director, and a toy designer. He is best known for his work in two most famous animated television series: Dragon Ball and Neon Genesis Evangelion. He is also the creator of the popular Kamen Rider Ex-Aid toys. Aoyagi studied visual design at Tokyo Zokei University and the University of Tokyo, while serving as a freelance designer for various television networks. He started his professional career as an animator and animation director in the early 1990s. His most notable works include all monsters featured in the "Dragon Ball" anime series, in addition to some of the mecha and robot designs. From 1995 to 1998, Aoyagi worked as the animation director of "Neon Genesis Evangelion". He created the mecha designs for the series, including the concept designs for the EVA series. The huge success of "Evangelion" solidified Aoyagi's status as one of the most esteemed animators in the industry. Aoyagi began creating toy designs in 2000. He worked on some of Bandai's most iconic toy lines, including the Kamen Rider Ex-Aid figures which were released in Japan in 2017. His transforming robot figures immediately become popular among fans due to the highly detailed articulation and wide range of accessories. In 2018, Aoyagi set up his own company- Aoyagi Design Studio- to focus solely on his toy designs. He aims to bring back the organic, organic-transformable figures to the toy market. His goal is to create a figure that combines the organic feeling of animatronics and the smooth-operating transformations for which "Kamen Rider" toys are known. Aoyagi also continues to work in the anime industry. He has served as the animation director for "Fruits Basket Another" (2020) and is currently involved in other projects. Though his career is relatively young, Takashi Aoyagi has already risen to become one of the most influential figures in the anime and toy industries. He is recognized for his creativity, innovation and dedication to bringing the best possible quality of design to both his animation and toy projects.

Nanjing Historical & Cultural Cities Expo (simplified Chinese: 南京历史文化城市博览会; traditional Chinese: 南京歷史文化城市博覽會; pinyin: Nánjīng Lìshǐ Wénhuà Chéngshì Bólǎnhuì) is an annual cultural event held in Nanjing, China. The event is held in celebration of Chinese heritage and history and also serves to strengthen the ties of cultural exchange between different Chinese cities. The event is typically organized by the Nanjing Municipal Government and has been held since 2001. Its main focus is on displaying the cultural and historical heritage of cities in China and promoting tourism and investment in Nanjing. The expo has grown over the years, and now includes a variety of activities and attractions. Different cities are invited to showcase their local culture and history, including historical architecture and artifacts, cultural performances, and local delicacies. Business and trade opportunities are also available, providing an ideal platform for potential entrepreneurs to connect and interact with each other. Moreover, the event aims to broaden the horizons of its audience and explore fresh ideas. Sessions and workshops are organized for both local and international audiences, covering topics such as traditional concepts, modern trends, digital technology, and social and economic trends. The Nanjing Historical & Cultural Cities Expo serves as an important platform for cities to foster and develop cultural exchange and strengthen mutual understanding. It provides a venue for people from different parts of China to come together and celebrate their shared culture, history, and heritage.

Schwentine Oxbow Lake is a natural lake located near the town of Eutin, in Schleswig-Holstein, Germany. Located near the Schwentine River, the Oxbow Lake is a popular recreational spot for both locals and visitors alike. It is home to a variety of fish, amphibians, and aquatic plants. The lake is approximately 3,500 meters long and 500 meters wide, making it one of the largest bodies of water in Schleswig-Holstein. The Schwentine Oxbow Lake formed when the river changed its course, creating a meander or oxbow lake in the process. The lake was formed 10,000 years ago and is significantly older than the nearby towns of Eutin, Kiel, and Lübeck. The lake is home to a variety of fish, including pike, perch, roach, rudd, bream and tench. Fishermen often come to the lake to try their luck. The lake is also home to numerous amphibians, such as frogs and salamanders. Aquatic plants such as reed and giant bur-reed are also abundant. Many of these plants are protected and their harvest is prohibited. The lake is a popular destination for locals and visitors alike. Surrounding the lake is a cycling and walking path that provides beautiful views. The lake has also become a popular spot for boating, canoeing and paddleboarding. Swimmers also frequent the lake during the summer months. The oxbow lake is home to many types of birds, including ducks, geese and swans. Many types of aquatic birds, such as kingfishers, can also be seen near the lake. In recent years, the Schwentine Oxbow Lake has become a popular spot for nature education. Local schools often organize field trips to the lake, to allow students to experience and learn about nature. The Schwentine River is an important source of renewable energy in the region. The nearby hydropower plant is run by the Schwentine Energy Company and is one of the most important sources of electricity in Schleswig-Holstein. In 2019, the Schwentine Oxbow Lake was designated as a Nature Reserve. This designation protects the lake's unique ecology and ensures that it will remain a vibrant part of the local natural environment for years to come.

2012–13 Stoke City F.C. season is the 114th season of the English club Stoke City F.C. and their sixth season competing in the Premier League,the top flight of English football. It is their fifth consecutive season in the top flight of English football, since their promotion from the Football League Championship in the 2008/2009 season. The season began on 18 August 2012 with a 3–1 home win against Reading, and concluded on 19 May 2013, with Stoke losing 5–1 away at Southampton. The season saw Stoke finish in 13th place with 45 points. They reached the final 16 stage of the 2012-13 League Cup, saw Joe Allen make his debut for the club in a 2–2 draw against Arsenal and also saw the arrival of American defender Geoff Cameron as a new player addition to the beginning of the season. Stoke were eliminated from the FA Cup at the first knock-out stage, when they were beaten 3–1 at Anfield by Premier League leaders Liverpool. In December, Tony Pulis left the club by mutual consent, ending a near-eight-year tenure at Stoke City. He was replaced by Mark Hughes, who was appointed on a 3-year contract. In his last match, Stoke claimed a 4–0 win at home to Wigan Athletic – a scoreline that marked Hughes’ first match in charge. Player and staff overhauls saw the arrivals of Charlie Adam, Michael Kightly, Jack Butland, Jamie Ness, Marc Muniesa and Erik Pieters, whilst the season saw the departures of Michael Owen, Matthew Upson, Dean Whitehead, Rory Delap, Dave Kitson, Tuncay Şanlı, Wilson Palacios and Carlo Nash. Despite a difficult start, the season ended well under Hughes, with Stoke defeating Liverpool, Manchester United and Arsenal away from home, and lifting the club to a finish of 13th place in the Premier League. The club also announced a record turn-over of £78 million and the highest-ever position in the club's history - 46th in the Deloitte Football Money League. Overall, the 2012-13 was a successful season for Stoke, despite some mid-season turbulence. They finished the season strongly and even managed to secure a top-profit of £1.8m in the 2012/13 season. This was the first time in five years that Stoke City held a top profit rather than a loss in a Premier League season.

Will Cullen Hart (born October 3, 1976) is an American musician and the frontman of the Elephant 6 collective rock group The Olivia Tremor Control. Hart began his career in music as a singer and guitarist in the duo The Broadwitz. He has later focused most of his creative energy in the recording studio, writing, producing, and playing various instruments for the various Elephant 6 affiliated acts. He is most noted for his songwriting, production and often off-the-wall instrumentation throughout his career in the Elephant 6 collective. Hart grew up in Ruston, Louisiana where he discovered most of his musical influences. After writing and recording songs as a solo artist, he and Bill Doss formed a musical duo which they called The Broadwitz. The group attracted other musicians and soon the collective Elephant 6 was created. While Hart's initial foray into music was as an acoustic guitarist and vocalist, he quickly adapted to playing multiple instruments and found his calling in the recording studio. In 1996, Hart and Doss collaborated with Jeff Mangum of Neutral Milk Hotel to form the experimental rock group The Olivia Tremor Control, who released their debut album, "Dusk at Cubist Castle," in 1996. That same year, The Olivia Tremor Control was also featured on the Elephant 6 compilation album "The Black Foliage: Animation Music Volume One". The Olivia Tremor Control toured with various other Elephant 6 acts throughout the 1990s and into the early 2000s, releasing two more studio albums during that period. Following the dissolution of the band, Hart founded his own recording studio, Cloud Recordings. He has since released a handful of solo albums, contributed to various Elephant 6 solo releases, collaborated with a multitude of other bands and projects, and produced and engineered for various acts. He is still active in the touring scene with the reformed Olivia Tremor Control and as a solo artist, having released a handful of solo albums and EPs up until 2018. In 2012, Hart composed the soundtrack to the documentary film "Beauty Is Embarrassing," a documentary based on the life of artist Wayne White. In 2017, a four-track EP titled "The Doomsday Mechanism" was released by Hart. The EP was created and recorded by Hart over a three-year period between 2014 and 2017. Hart's music is often seen as eclectic and experimental, often utilizing a variety of instruments such as marimbas, vibraphones, woodwinds, and various early synthesizers. He is noted for creating music which often blends multiple musical styles and genres. Hart is still an active and celebrated musical force, and continues to create and explore his own musical and sonic boundaries.

The Defiant Ones (1986) is an American comedy-drama film directed by Stephen Spielberg and produced by Universal Pictures. The movie is based on the novel by Harold Jacob Smith and stars Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins as two escaped convicts who are joined together by a pair of handcuffs. The story revolves around two convicts, John 'Joker' Jackson (Morgan Freeman) and Alex 'Sweetwater' Johnson (Tim Robbins). They have both been convicted of a crime and are shackled together by a set of handcuffs. They both escape and begin a journey of redemption as they make their way across the United States. Along their journey, the two form a deep bond and rely on one another for survival. They encounter many obstacles and danger as they attempt to find their freedom. The movie tells of the struggle of the two convicts and the racial prejudice and injustice that they endure. It also shows the powerful bond between two very different men who are able to set aside their differences to help one another. The Defiant Ones was a critical and commercial success. It was nominated for various awards, including an Oscar for Best Picture and Best Adapted Screenplay. The film grossed over $44 million worldwide during its initial release and has since become a cult classic. The film has become known for its strong performances, powerful messages and its blend of drama with comedy. It stands as a reminder to viewers that the power of friendship and understanding should never be underestimated. The Defiant Ones is an important piece of cinema that has inspired generations of viewers with its powerful story and memorable characters.

The King of the Street Cleaners is an accolade accorded to the best street cleaners in the world, who over the years have consistently gone above and beyond what is expected of them to keep their cities clean. For decades, many have strived for the King of the Street Cleaners title, but only a select few have reached the highest level of street cleaning proficiency. Though the title is not officially recognized exists in any official capacity, the King of the Street Cleaners title is nonetheless spoken of in great admiration and respect by those in the street cleaning profession. Those who have the title have achieved a level of excellence that is not easily earned and is rarely matched. The recipients are lauded for their commitment to keep the streets of their cities clean, no matter the difficulty or risk involved. They often work long hours, sacrificing their own time for the cause, but it is because of their dedication that the streets of their cities remain in pristine condition. The King of the Street Cleaners title is given to an individual of any age, race or gender who has displayed an exceptional level of skill in their street cleaning responsibilities in order to keep their city streets clean and tidy. These individuals have shown exemplary dedication and commitment to their work, embodying the values of their profession and demonstrating an appreciation for the importance of their role in maintaining the integrity of their cities. The current King of the Street Cleaners is Mohammed Haamid, who has been the Street Cleaner of Delhi, India for the last 15 years. During this time, he has been instrumental in leading the charge to keep the streets of Delhi free of dirt, grime and garbage. His tireless work has resulted in Delhi being bestowed with the title of cleanest capital in India. Mohammed Haamid has more than earned the title of King of the Street Cleaners and is a beacon of hope for those in the street cleaning profession. He is an example of commitment and dedication, and those who strive for the King of Street Cleaners title can use him as an inspiration.

R. Thyagarajan (1945-present) is an Indian film director, writer, and producer who has worked in the Tamil film industry. He has directed more than fifty movies and has also produced more than fifteen movies in his career over the last four decades. He has also penned the story, screenplay, and dialogues for most of the movies he has directed. His early career began with the hugely successful 1975 movie Rotti, which catapulted him to the top ranks of Tamil directors. Also known as Thiyagarajab, R. Thyagarajan was born in 1945 in the former kingdom of Pudukkottai in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. He began his film career in 1973 as a dialogue and story writer for the Tamil movie Pudhiya Bharatham. This was followed by writing and producing the blockbuster, Rotti in 1975. The movie was so successful that it helped launch R. Thyagarajan as one of Tamil cinema’s’ most successful directors. He is most known for his comedy and action films, most notably Thozhilali (1984), Thanga Gopuram (1985), Deva (1995), and Kizhaku Seemayile (1996). He has collaborated with many renowned writers, actors, and directors throughout his career such as A. R. Rahman, Ilaiyaraaja, and Prabhu Deva. R. Thyagarajan has had considerable success working in the Tamil film industry and is credited with introducing several new actors and technicians to the industry. He also founded his own production house, SRV (Srushti Enterprises), in 1990. Three of his productions, Gandharvam (1993), Seeman (1997), and Villu (2009) were remade in other languages. He has also won multiple awards throughout his career, including the Cinema Express Award for Best Director (Thillaanaa Mohanambal, 1968) and the Filmfare Award for Best Director – Tamil (Deva, 1995). Throughout his career, R. Thyagarajan has steadily redefined Tamil cinema with his distinctive style and campy vision. He is remembered fondly by fans and critics alike as an iconic and influential figure in the Tamil film industry.

The Ministry of Justice (Libya) is an administrative government body responsible for the administration of justice in Libya. It is headed by the Minister of Justice, who is nominated by the Prime Minister. Since Libya’s independence in 1951, the Ministry of Justice has served as the national legal body responsible for the enforcement of justice, adjudication of matters of law, and the administration of legal proceedings. The Ministry of Justice enforces domestic and international laws within Libya, and serves as the supervisory legal body for all other courts and agencies within the country. The Ministry of Justice is responsible for the formulation of legal regulations, and also for the supervision of their implementation. It ensures that all laws are respected, and holds authority over various governmental and private organizations and departments. The Ministry of Justice is responsible for the ensuring that the laws are enforced, and for providing effective access to the justice system for Libyan citizens. The Ministry of Justice drafts and maintains the laws of Libya and administers legal proceedings, forms the courts and chooses their staff, regulates the functions of the courts, and sets the legal dues, fees, and expenses. It also regulates the protection of civil rights in Libya. The Ministry of Justice comprises several divisions and departments, such as the Civil Affairs Department, the Criminal Affairs Department, the Personal Status Department, and the Economic Departments. The Ministry of Justice also issues pardons and provides opinions on legal matters to the government and Parliament. The Ministry is also responsible for the appointment and dismissal of judicial officials, including judges and court staff. The Ministry of Justice is charged with the implementation of the judicial and legal reforms undertaken by the government. In this regard, the Ministry is responsible for ensuring that the justice system responds to the needs of the citizens and provides a speedy and secure access to justice, when necessary. The Ministry of Justice works together with the Supreme Court and the Special Court of Appeals to ensure the rule of law and the protection of civil liberties. It is also the central institution charged with ensuring access to the justice system, including providing legal assistance and representation to citizens in court. The Ministry of Justice also oversees the implementation of international treaties and conventions, and works with governmental and non-governmental organizations to strengthen Libyan laws. The Ministry also coordinates international legal cooperation and exchanges with other countries.
