Joe Biden 2020 presidential campaign is the current Presidential campaign of Joe Biden, the former Vice President of the United States, in the 2020 United States presidential election. Biden had been widely speculated to enter the race after serving as Vice President to former President Barack Obama from 2009 to 2017. On April 25, 2019, Biden officially announced his candidacy for the Democratic nomination for President of the United States in 2021. Biden's campaign is focused on the slogan "We Can Do Better," which stresses the idea that the foundation of the country is not broken, but can be strengthened through equality and improved. In his speech announcing his candidacy, Biden said he aims to bring back the soul of the nation, seek justice and equality, expand economic opportunity, and bring back the respect globally that the United States had lost. Biden vows to repair the damage of the Trump administration with a focus on restoring decency, respect, and honor. Biden regards this as the central approach to galvanizing the nation. Biden has advocated for the signing of a national infrastructure bill, a $15 minimum wage, government-funded pre-school and childcare, gun safety legislation, and tax cuts. Biden has proposed a platform of advancing civil rights by empowering women, challenging racism, and promoting LGBTQ rights. He has pledged to deliver on the Obama-Biden promise of reversing 'Don't Ask, Don't Tell' and to support the Equality Act. He has also outlined a plan to protect and strengthen the Social Security and Medicare programs, increase transparency in healthcare, and crack down on prescription drug pricing and monopoly practices in the pharmaceutical industry. He also plans to restore and strengthen labor unions, raise the minimum wage, and implement a fair trade policy that puts workers first. In terms of foreign policy, Biden has campaigned for restoring the United States to its place in world leadership, including through economic and diplomatic approaches. Biden has called for a robust alliance system and for a defensive, yet forward-leaning position with adversaries and ‘neighboring countries. Beyond these principles, he has outlined certain specific policies, such as reviving the Iran Nuclear Deal, re-joining the Paris Climate Agreement, and expanding the United Nations Human Rights Council, among other measures. Throughout his campaign, Biden has emphasized the need for compromise and respect between Democratic and Republican politicians. Biden's campaign has been endorsed by Barack Obama, Hillary Clinton, and other high profile figures. Following Joe Biden's electoral victory in the 2020 United States presidential election, he is expected to be sworn in as the 46th President of the United States on January 20, 2021.

The Hong Kong women's national rugby sevens team is the national rugby sevens team representing Hong Kong in international tournaments. The team is currently governed by the Hong Kong Rugby Union (HKRU), the governing body of rugby union in the country. The team's first official tournament was the 2001 World Cup qualifier which they participated in. Since then, they have developed rapidly and have become a prominent and competitive rugby sevens team in the region. The team is presently in the world's top twelve world competitive nations in the sport and are regulars in both the Sevens World Series and the Asian Rugby Sevens Series. Hong Kong has also won the Asian Sevens Series four times and took the bronze in the Asian women's tournaments in 2005, 2007 and 2009. The team also won the second leg of the 2008 Sevens World Series in Dubai and took third place in the World Cup Qualifier tournament in Hong Kong in 2009. The Hong Kong Sevens team represents more than just a game for the people of Hong Kong. The players have become role models for the younger generation, teaching specific values such as fairness, respect, honesty, modesty, dignity, courage and team spirit. The team's current coach is Fanny Wong, who was appointed in June 2011. In addition, the team is comprised of some of the most talented and experienced players in the sport. Some of the notable players in the team include Dai Gum Feng, Ho Kam Suen, Cheng To and Victoria Wong. The Hong Kong Women's National Rugby Sevens team has played in various tournaments since 2001. The team took part in the 2009 World Cup in Russia and finished in 10th place overall. They have also won several prestigious tournaments such as the 2009 Under 20s National Championship, 2010 Under-21s National Championship and the East Asia Champions Cup in 2010. In the 2018/2019 season, the Hong Kong Women's National Rugby Sevens team won bronze at the 2019 Asian Women's Rugby Sevens Series. This was the team's first podium finish in over a decade and the first ever top three finish in the Asian Women's Rugby Sevens Series. The team's future outlook is looking positive and promising. HKRU has implemented various initiatives and programs to expand the team's reach and recognition. A dedicated Women's Sevens High Performance Program has been setup and a new coaching staff composed of local and international coaches has been appointed to the team. The team's official motto is "One Team, One Nation and One Dream" which signify the values of unity, solidarity and resilience the players show in their performance. As a national team, the Hong Kong Women's National Rugby Sevens team represent not just the sport of rugby sevens but also the courage and strength of the Hong Kong people.

Romolo Valli (1911–1980) was an Italian actor, who was known for his roles in such films as Luchino Visconti's Rocco and His Brothers, The Leopard, and Richard Brooks's The Pride and the Passion. He appeared in more than 90 films, stage productions and television serials over a career that spanned five decades. Born in Kampala, British Uganda, in 1911, Valli made his stage debut in Milan's Teatro Manzoni during the 1930s. His earliest notable film appearances were in Visconti's Ossessione (Obsession - 1943), Senso (1950), and La terra trema (The Earth Trembles - 1948). His most famous role was in Visconti's Rocco and His Brothers (1960), in which he played the middle brother. He also starred in King Vidor's War and Peace (1956), Liliana Cavani's Beyond Good and Evil (1977) and Bernardo Bertolucci's 1900 (1975). On the smaller screen, Valli enjoyed a long career and was best known for the role of Carlo Pinna in the RAI series Una storia d'amore (1971–1975). He was also a frequent guest actor in television serials that were aired on RAI throughout the 1960s, '70s and '80s. In 2002, after his death, he was posthumously awarded Best Actor at the 2002 Taormina Film Festival. Besides his acting career, Valli wrote the script for the 1964 film The Pumpkin Eater, starring Peter Finch and Anne Bancroft and directed by Jack Clayton. Romolo Valli passed away in Rome on 23 October 1980. He is remembered for his strong performances, his ethics and his uncompromising commitment to the Italian cinema. His legacy as an actor, film-maker and theatre producer remain unquestioned to this day.

Allan Sears (born December 29, 1951) is an American entrepreneur and philanthropist. He is the co-founder and former CEO of the data and technology company, LexisNexis, and also serves as co-chair of the Advisory Board of the UN Global Compact. Sears was born in Cleveland, Ohio, to parents Tom and Sara Sears. He earned a B.A. in English from Dartmouth College and an M.B.A. from Harvard Business School. After graduating, he began his career as a consultant with The Boston Consulting Group. In 1979, Sears co-founded LexisNexis, a division of Reed Elsevier. He was CEO and later chairman of the company. He grew LexisNexis into a leader in the market for legal and business research information. In 2008, Sears announced his intention to retire from LexisNexis and focus on his philanthropic work. Throughout his life, Sears has been dedicated to giving back to society. In his philanthropic activities, Sears focuses primarily on education and healthcare. He sits on several university and hospital boards, and his foundation supports numerous causes in the areas of public policy, science and technology. He has personally donated million of dollars of his own to various initiatives. He is a frequent speaker and guest lecturer, often speaking on topics related to technology and entrepreneurship. He is a member of the World Economic Forum and the Council on Foreign Relations. He was selected as one of the 100 Most Influential People in Business Ethics in 2005. In addition to his business and philanthropic work, Sears is a competitive sailor and has won several races in the United States and abroad. Throughout his career, Sears has been a champion of corporate responsibility, ethics, and sustainability. His passion and dedication for responsible business have earned him numerous accolades and awards both nationally and internationally.

Gustavo Carbonieri (born November 17, 1984) is a Brazilian entrepreneur and investor. He is the founder and CEO of Grupo Carbonieri, a leading alternative asset management and investment group in Brazil. Born and raised in São Paulo, Carbonieri attended the Insper Institute of Education and Research, where he earned a bachelor's degree in business administration. After graduating, Carbonieri began his career in the banking industry, primarily focused on credit sercurities and private equity. He then decided to branch out and start a venture capital fund in the real estate industry, Grupo Carbonieri. Grupo Carbonieri is a vertically integrated real estate investment platform that spans from early-stage financing to asset management. The group has made several investments in residential and commercial real estate projects, most notably in land for residential development, and in office and shopping centers. Grupo Carbonieri also has investments in hospitality, infrastructure and development of technological solutions, as well in various private equity related topics. Through its investment vehicles and associated portfolio companies, Grupo Carbonieri covers a wide range of industries and economic activities such as homebuilding, co-working and technology, energy, logistics, and agribusiness, among others. Gustavo Carbonieri is a well-known name in the Brazilian business ecosystem. He has been featured in notable publications such as the Economist and Globo Negócios. Additionally he is a board member at several large companies as well as non-profit organizations. One example is ASPAS, an organization for the preservation of the endangered São Paulo Araras, which Carbonieri frequently contributes to with major donations. Throughout his career, Carbonieri has been an advocate for positive change and social innovation. He has mentored several entrepreneurs and has been a frequent speaker in relevant business events in Brazil and overseas. He is a strong believer of research-driven investments and active asset management. Gustavo Carbonieri's success story is an inspiration for those looking to venture in the business and investment sectors. He is currently based in São Paulo, and still actively working with Grupo Carbonieri while looking for opportunities to transform and improve businesses in Brazil and abroad.

The 2006–07 in Swedish bandy was a season of bandy in Sweden, the men's premier division being Allsvenskan, and the women's premier division being Elitserien. Both Allsvenskan and Elitserien were played between October 2006 and February 2007. The Final Four tournament, where the top four teams of the season competed, was hosted by Skellefteå AIK in Skellefteå on February 24 and 25 of 2007. The season also included the Svenska Cupen cup tournament, with the final being hosted by Vetlanda BK in Vetlanda on March 10 and 11 of 2007. In the men's Allsvenskan, the season was won by Villa Lidköping, with Sala IBK coming in second. The semifinalists were AIK and Skåre BK. The relegation playoffs were played between Gästrike-Hammarby IF (G-HIF) and Hönö IS, with G-HIF ultimately being relegated from Allsvenskan. In the women's Elitserien, the season was won by Skellefteå AIK, with Västerås SK coming in second. The semifinalists were Söderhamn/Ljusne and Köping Bandy. At the Final Four tournament, the men's consolation game was won by Sala IBK against AIK, and the final game was won by Villa Lidköping against Skåre BK. In the Svenska Cupen cup tournament, the semifinal games were won by Vetlanda BK against Västerås SK, and Villa Lidköping against Skåre BK. The final game was won by Vetlanda BK against Villa Lidköping. At the end of the season, the following teams were relegated from the 2006–07 Allsvenskan, and will compete in the 2007–08 Allsvenskan instead: Söderhamn/Ljusne, Köping Bandy, and G-HIF. The 1983–84 United States network television schedule is a list of the official primetime schedules and corresponding time periods for each of the four American television networks, ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox. This was the first season in which Fox broadcast a full slate of programming, as the newly created network launched on October 9, 1983. ABC ABC's schedule was very strong in 1983–84 and featured the return of The Love Boat, the introduction of Remington Steele, the revival of Family Feud, and the spin-off of "The Little House on the Prairie" series, Little House: A New Beginning. ABC's highest rated show of the season was the police procedural "T.J. Hooker". Other notable ABC shows included: Hart to Hart, Hotel, Matt Houston, Dynasty, Too Close for Comfort, Benson, and Three's Company. CBS CBS' 1983–84 lineup was loaded with hits and featured the hits "Magnum P.I.", "Dukes of Hazzard", and "Simon & Simon", as well as Monday Night Football, the detective drama "Jake and the Fatman", the revival of "The Waltons", and the anthology series "The Twilight Zone". New shows included: "Airwolf", "Dallas" spin-off "Knots Landing", "Newhart", "Flamingo Road", and "Call to Glory". NBC NBC launched “The Cosby Show” during this season which quickly became NBC’s highest-rated show, along with its two spin-offs “A Different World” and “Cheers”. "The A-Team" was also a major hit for NBC, along with "Hill Street Blues", "St. Elsewhere", "Knight Rider", "Fame", "Family Ties", and "Miami Vice". Other notable NBC shows included "The Golden Girls", "Highway to Heaven", "It's a Living", and "Facts of Life", and the made-for-TV movie "The Burning Bed". Fox The fledgling network launched with its Wednesday night lineup of "The Late Show with Joan Rivers", "Duet" and "Studs". Other notable Fox shows during the 1983–84 season were "The New Adventures of Beans Baxter" and the made-for-TV movie "The Day After". Overall, the 1983–84 US network television season was a strong one, with strong shows on all four networks. It was a competitive season, with each network aiming to capture the attention of viewers.

Tennessee State Route 64 (SR 64) is a state highway running east-west for 149.7 miles (241 km) through portions of Shelby and Fayette Counties in West Tennessee. The western terminus is at the intersection of US-70, US-64, and SR-14 in Lacon, Tennessee, and the eastern terminus is at the intersection of US-41A and SR-16 in Scotts Hill, Tennessee. SR 64 is part of the historic Natchez Trace Parkway, which was a series of roads that ran from Nashville, Tennessee all the way to Natchez, Mississippi. The route crosses through several small towns and agricultural areas as it winds its way through West Tennessee. Some of the towns along the route include Rockville, Mason, Grand Junction, Somerville, LaGrange, Oakland, and Lansing. The route is mostly two-lane, undivided, rural highway with occasional stretches of four-lane divided highway and passing lanes. SR 64 is also used as a truck route and offers good access to the interchange with US-64/US-70 in Lacon. The eastern terminus is located just a few miles from the I- 40 interchange in Whiteville, and the route is appropriately marked with "Truck Route" signs along its length. SR 64 is signed eastbound from Lacon to Scotts Hill and westbound from Scotts Hill to Lacon. Construction began in the late 1990s to widen parts of SR 64 in Fayette and Shelby Counties. The project was completed in 2003 and included widening of the roadway, construction of passing lanes, and addition of shoulders. SR 64 serves as an important route in West Tennessee and provides access to many small towns and local attractions. Portions of the route are also designated as a scenic highway and offer good views of the countryside. The route is a major connector road between Memphis and the Natchez Trace Parkway and is part of the Great River Road driving tour. Travelers can use SR 64 as an alternative to the congested US-64/US-70 corridor though Interstate 40 also provides an alternate route. The route is patrolled by the Tennessee Highway Patrol and is subject to Tennessee's Self-Defense Act of 2013.

Peter Bakare is a Nigerian multi-award winning filmmaker, writer, actor and journalist. He is best known for his work on critically acclaimed films such as Skinny Girl in Transit, The Delivery Boy and Moka. Bakare’s films tend to be defined by their heavy cultural references and commentary on society in his home country, Nigeria. Early life Bakare was born in Lagos, Nigeria in 1987. At the age of 17, Bakare moved to the United States to pursue further education. He studied Business Administration and Economics at the University of Delaware. Bakare’s first exposure to the entertainment industry came when he interned on the production set of Egypt Henson’s Angels, a short film starring Ray Liotta and Kate Walsh. Career Bakare started his career as a writer and soon moved on to writing and producing short films, documentaries and feature films. His first major film was Skinny Girl in Transit, a comedy-drama that he wrote, produced, and directed. The film, released in 2015, was hailed as a groundbreaking work on women, love and body image in Nigeria. The film received numerous awards and accolades, including the 2016 Best Short Film Award at the Africa International Film Festival. Bakare proceeded to write and direct The Delivery Boy, a coming of age film that follows the story of a young man’s journey to self-discovery. The film made its world premiere in 2017 at the Toronto International Film Festival. Most recently, Bakare wrote, directed, and produced Moka, a documentary that chronicles the story of a girl that goes against her parents’ wishes and becomes an entrepreneur. The film won the Grand Prix at the 2018 Cannes Short Film Festival and won best documentary at the 2018 Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards. Bakare also has ventured into acting. He appeared in a supporting role in the 2018 film, The Wedding Party 2, which was the highest grossing Nigerian film of all time. Bakare briefly dabbled in journalism, working as the Arts Editor for Nigerian lifestyle magazine, The Guardian Life. Personal life Bakare is married with 2 children. Filmography * Skinny Girl in Transit (2015) * The Delivery Boy (2017) * Moka (2018) * The Wedding Party 2 (2018) Awards and Nominations * African International Film Festival - Best Short Film (2016) * African Magic Viewers' Choice Awards - Best Documentary (2018) * Cannes Short Film Festival - Grand Prix (2018)

The German destroyer Z28 was a Type 1936A destroyer of the German Kriegsmarine during the Second World War. Built by Deschimag (Deutsche Schiffs- und Maschinenbau Aktien-Gesellschaft) and launched in 1940, it was armed with five 15 cm SK C/28 guns in single mounts, four 2 cm C/30 anti-aircraft guns, and eight 53.3 cm torpedo tubes in two quad mounts. It had a displacement of 1,620 tons, a length of 117 meters, a beam of 11.7 meters, and two Wagner-Pelton diesel engines with a total output of 56,000 shaft horsepower, giving it a maximum speed of 36 knots. The destroyer saw extensive service during the war, including operations in the Mediterranean and the Baltic Sea. It participated in the Battle of Cape Matapan in March 1941 and the Battle of Crete in May of the same year. Later on, it was involved in the evacuation of wounded soldiers from the port of Trondheim in December 1941 and was damaged by Norwegian coastal batteries later in the same month. In January 1942, Z28 returned to Germany for repairs, and in March it joined the battleship Tirpitz on its operation to raid shipping in the Arctic Ocean. During that mission, it engaged the British destroyer Brilliant in a night action but was forced to flee after being hit by torpedoes and suffering severe damage to its superstructure. After making it back to Germany for repairs, it was transferred to the Mediterranean in April 1942. Z28 took part in the Battle of Sicily in 1943 and later on patrolled the Italian coast. In August 1944, while on patrol in the Strait of Bonifacio, Z28 was ambushed by the British destroyer HMS Redwing and sunk in the ensuing battle. Of the 295 crewmen aboard, only 43 survived the attack. The wreck of Z28 was located in 1987 and was explored by divers the following year. Today, many of the ship's armaments and hull structures are still intact and can be visited by divers. The destroyer is considered to be a war grave, and as such it is protected by Italian law.

Al-Nizamiyya of Baghdad (Arabic: النظامية البغدادية‎) was an Iraqi Islamic university, established in 1065 by the Abbasid Caliph Nizam al-Mulk in Baghdad. The university was one of the largest and most famous medieval universities in the world. It was a center of advanced learning with students gathering from all over the Islamic world. The university offered programs in literature, philosophy, science, theology and law. It was the first Islamic university to teach sharia law and became a peak of Islamic civilization. Instructors at the school included prominent writers such as Al-Ghazali, Al-Jahiz, Al-Mubarrad and Ibn al-Haytham. The curriculum was based on the Shi'a Ibn al-Mualem's al-Madkhal software and was divided into four main branches: theology, law, philosophy and Islamic sciences. Each student was required to take courses in the four main branches and then specialize in one or two subjects of interest. The university offered courses in a wide range of subjects, including literature, philosophy, science, theology and law. Courses in mathematics, astronomy, medicine and geography were also offered. One part of the university was dedicated to astronomy and astrology. Here, there was an observatory, where students could observe stars and planets. Historians believe that the observatory was one of the most advanced at that time. The library of the university is said to have contained the most famous works of Islamic scholarship. This included works of Islamic jurisprudence and philosophy, as well as classics of science, literature and poetry. The university played an important role in the development of Islamic science and culture. It was an important center of scientific and philosophical thought. Al-Nizamiyya is still seen as one of the most influential universities in the history of Islamic scholarship. The university has since been renovated several times, with the current renovation being completed in 2008. Its library is now being modernized and digitalized, with its collections being made accessible online. Al-Nizamiyya is seen by many as an example of the modern Islamic university.

Continuous duty overnight is a phrase typically used to describe working overnight at a job. In such cases, the person who is working will have a continuous shift, typically lasting 8 to 12 hours, and will need to stay on the job through the night, unless they are given permission to take a rest period by their employer. Usually, a shift of this nature will require the worker to remain alert and stay focused throughout the night in order to do their job properly. In recent years, more and more employers have begun offering jobs that require continuous duty overnight shifts. This is done in order to help the employers maximize their profits and reduce the need for additional daytime or weekend shifts. For example, a call center may require its workers to work overnight shifts in order to better serve customers, as calls may come in at any time and need to be answered in order to keep customers satisfied. In addition, an airline may also require its pilots and other flight staff to continuously remain on duty overnight in order to ensure customer safety and satisfaction with their flights. Besides customer service and safety, another motivating factor for employers to offer continuous duty overnight shifts is the potential cost savings that can be achieved. By having job positions continuously staffed, employers can avoid having to pay for overtime for additional shifts or hire additional staff, resulting in considerable cost savings. Continuous overnight shifts can be physically and mentally demanding, as they require a person to remain awake and alert during unpredictable hours while also requiring a certain level of mental focus and efficiency. This can be especially challenging, when combined with the other responsibilities that a person may have in their personal life such as raising their family or managing their own finances. To ensure the safety, efficiency, and well-being of a worker on a continuous overnight shift, employers may provide certain benefits such as extra pay and time-off to alleviate some of the stress. Although the concept of a continuous overnight shift may seem daunting, it does have its advantages. One of the most notable advantages is that a continuous overnight shift will usually result in increased financial rewards due to the extra hours worked, with the possibility of overtime depending on the situation. In addition, because such shifts typically require a high level of focus and attention, the experience gained by working in a continuous overnight shift can be valuable in the long run and may provide useful skills for a person's future endeavors.

Discovery Kids (Latin American TV channel) is a Latin American pay television channel aimed at children between the ages of 4 and 14 years old, owned and operated by Discovery Networks Latin America and based in Buenos Aires, Argentina. It was launched on July 27, 1996 as Animax, and in 1998 was renamed to Discovery Kids. The channel airs a mixture of live-action and animation series, feature films and documentaries. It also operates an on demand service called Discovery Kids Play. The channel is widely available in South and Central America and the Caribbean. The slogan for the channel is "Familia, diversión y conocimiento". Discovery Kids airs content from various sources, including Discovery Communications, Cartoon Network, Nickelodeon and Disney. The channel also produces and airs Original Latin American productions. The most successful series produced by Discovery Kids is "Hijos de la Tierra" (Sons of the Earth), a drama about the adventures of three children and their pet parrot, produced by Dorly Films and aired from 1998 to 2000. The channel has also produced a number of other popular animated series, such as "Mundo Mágico de Oz," "SuperCaminaos," "Conexión Japon" and "Kanuto y Kanula". Other programs have included the reality shows "Olas de Surf" (Surfing Waves) and "Explorando el Universo" (Exploring the Universe), documentaries and sports programs. The channel has also produced original programming, such as the educational program "Laboratorio Magico" (Magic Lab). In 2019, Discovery Kids changed its on air look and added a new brand logo. The updated logo was accompanied by a redesigned on-air graphics package, enhanced programming and news. Discovery Kids is the third-most-viewed channel in Latin America, behind Cartoon Network and Nickelodeon. It reaches millions of viewers across the region and is available on direct-to-home satellite, cable and IPTV platforms.

¿Qué le pasa a mi familia? (English: What is Happening to My Family?) is a Mexican telenovela produced by José Alberto Castro for Televisa. It was based on the 1994 telenovela written by the Venezuelan writer Humberto "Kiko" Olivieri, which was adapted in more than 30 countries. The series premiered on Las Estrellas on October 20, 2014 and aired its last episode on May 24, 2015. The series stars Silvia Navarro, César Évora, Erick Elias, Margarita Magaña, Malillany Marín, Laura Zapata, Federico Ayos and Juan Ferrara. Featuring the special participations of David Zepeda and Eugenio Siller. The story of ¿Qué le pasa a mi familia? revolves around two sisters, the youngest and the eldest, who have chosen two different paths to follow in their lives. Raquel has chosen to live the fast-paced rich life, with its glamour and fine living, while Yessica opts for the simpler life in which to focus on her marriage and religious beliefs. The series begins as Raquel returns to Mexico after a period of exile in Europe following her involvement in a scandal of her past. Her return stirs up the deep secrets of a past that the family had kept in silence. As the story progresses, the audience discovers the secrets that surround each of the characters, and the consequences they have brought to the family. The series received positive reviews. Eugenio Siller received praise for his Romeo and Juliet inspired love story with Silvia Navarro. On June 17, 2015, a new installment called ¿Qué le pasa a mi familia? ¡De Nuevo en Acción! was released as a web series, in which the cast reinterpreted their roles from the first season with comical plots. The first episode premiered on YouTube on June 21, 2015. ¿Qué le pasa a mi familia? proved to be a critical and ratings success, becoming the highest rated telenovela of 2014. As a result, it won an Astrolatino award for Best Telenovela of the Year. It has also been nominated for different awards including Premios TVyNovelas and a Kids' Choice Mexico Award. The series was released on DVD region 1 by Sony Pictures Home Entertainment.

Bulbothrix cinerea is an basidiomycete fungus of the family Parmeliaceae. It was first described by German mycologist C.A. Blom in 1892, who placed it in the genus Dyplolabia. Today, it is classified as a species of Bulbothrix. The fruit body of B. cinerea can be found growing as fruticose lichen on trees, rocks, and other types of substrates. It is pale grayish-brown in color, with a thin, loopy texture. The lower surface of the thallus often has a distinct cat-scratch-like pattern due to the presence of rhizines. The thallus produces flattened, disc-shaped apothecia which contain the asci and spores. The apothecia have a paler center where the asci are located, surrounded by a thin margin which can vary in color from brownish to blackish. Microscopically, the asci contain 5-6 ellipsoidal spores, with dimensions of 10–18 × 5–6 μm. B. cinerea is widespread throughout parts of Europe, North America, and Asia, preferring moist habitats on acidic substrates. It has been studied for its potential as an indicator of air pollution, as it has been shown to be sensitive to levels of nitrogen dioxide and sulfur dioxide in the atmosphere. Other than this, its use in humans is limited. Despite its cosmopolitan distribution, B. cinerea is not common in most areas, and is sometimes considered rare in some regions of Europe. However, in Great Britain, it is perhaps more variable and abundant than in other parts of Europe, and can be found relatively easily with a keen eye and close inspection of potential microhabitats. Overall, B. cinerea is a distinct, albeit rare, species that can be found in many parts of the world. It has a unique appearance, as well as potential use in monitoring of air pollution, making it an interesting and important subject of fungal research.

Ramon Sender (born June 5, 1934 in Madrid, Spain) is a Spanish-American composer, music teacher, author, and documentary filmmaker. He has composed more than 100 pieces of music, including a piano concerto and a trumpet concerto, and his books include the novel Of No Country I Know: A Journey to Red Sands. Sender studied music at San Fernando University in Madrid and at The Juilliard School in New York before serving as a resident composer at the Julliard School's Contemporary Music Center from 1959-1965. During this time he composed largely experimental works using unorthodox instrumentation and incorporating electronic sounds. In 1972 he made his film debut, producing and directing Red Self-Portrait, a documentary about the Spanish Civil War. The film, which he also wrote and in which he appeared as an actor, premiered in New York at The New York Film Festival and has been described as “startling, hypnotic, and enigmatic” by The New York Times. From 1977 to 1978 he gave a series of public lectures on the history of 20th century music, emphasizing the importance of improvisation, experimentation and creative freedom in musical composition. In the mid-80s he lectured at the San Francisco Conservatory of Music, and in the 2000s he ran masterclasses at UC Berkeley and Stanford University. In addition to his work as a composer and teacher, Sender has also received numerous commissions to write a variety of compositions, ranging from chamber music to orchestral works. He has also conducted a number of acclaimed music workshops, classes and lectures around the United States. Sender is considered to be a pioneering figure in the world of avant-garde music and has been praised for his distinctive and uncompromising style. His work has been compared to that of John Cage and Karlheinz Stockhausen, and has been described as having “a passionate intensity, a sense of raw emotion, and a relentless drive” by The San Francisco Chronicle. Sender currently lives in Los Gatos, California, and continues to compose and perform, most recently with the Aurelia Music Ensemble. In 2019, the California Symphony Orchestra premiered an orchestral piece of his composition, "Of No Country I Know", in celebration of his 85th birthday.

Henri van Praag (sometimes simply known as Van Praag) (born January 26, 1960) is a prominent member of the Dutch intellectual elite. He is an anthropologist and politician, credited with being a major figure in the Dutch debate on immigration and integration policies. Van Praag was born in Amsterdam and is the eldest son of Jewish parents who had emigrated to the Netherlands in 1933 as refugees from Nazi Germany. After completing his secondary education he studied at the University of Amsterdam where he received a master's degree in Cultural Anthropology and a PhD in Public Administration. Van Praag has had a long career in public service in the Netherlands. He began his career as a civil servant at Ministries including Health, Culture, and Social Affairs. He served as Head of the Immigration Department from 2001 to 2003, before becoming Special Advisor on Immigration to the Dutch Prime Minister in 2004. In 2006 he co-authored a report on immigration reform which, among other things, suggested integration measures for immigrants that included providing language and employment courses for immigrants, and the creation of an "integration coach" for immigrants who needed help adjusting to Dutch society. Van Praag has also been a strong advocate for multiculturalism and diversity in the Netherlands, and actively promoted the idea of open dialogue between different ethnic and cultural groups. He has frequently argued that immigrants should not be seen as "the Other" in Dutch society, and has pushed for policies aimed at reducing racial stereotypes and discrimination. In 2010, Van Praag was elected to the Dutch House of Representatives with the Labour Party. He served as an MP until he resigned in 2012 in order to pursue concerns related to immigration. Since then, he has continued to work as a campaigner for immigrant rights, speaking at conferences and writing extensively on immigration issues, and regularly appearing in the media as an expert on immigration. He has also been heavily involved in politics related to the Israel-Palestine conflict, and has served as a guest lecturer at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem as well as Israeli universities. In 2019, Van Praag was awarded the Golden Ark Human Rights Award by the Netherlands' Association for Human Rights.

Ettore Ciccotti (born 4 August 1940) is an Italian composer and musician. Ciccotti was born in Rome. He began studying music at the age of 8, learning the piano. During his adolescence he was primarily interested in jazz and studied jazz at the conservatory of Santa Cecilia in Rome. After graduating he moved to New York City, where he worked as a freelance composer and musician in sync with contemporaries like Harry Belafonte, Charles Mingus, and Gil Evans. During this period he wrote hundreds of musical pieces and arrangements in the fields of jazz, funk, and popular music. In the early 1970s, Ciccotti returned to Italy and focussed on soundtracks and other original compositions. His compositions have been used in films and television programs, including films such as L'invenzione della morte, La controfigura and La stella che non c'è, as well as the television series Il commissario De Luca. In recent years, his compositions have featured in numerous commercial campaigns for Italian and international companies, including Corona Extra, Fiat, Raiffeisen, and Rolex. Ciccotti is a frequent collaborator with the composer V. Venuti, and together they have released two albums, Il volume del vento and La luna incantata. Their work has been praised by critics and music fans alike for its rich sound, fusing cinematic and neoclassical influences. In addition to his work as a composer and musician, Ciccotti has also been involved in various teaching and mentoring activities, most notably as a lecturer of music at the Faculty of Arts and Music of Tuoro University, Rome. He also founded the "Eta d'Oro" studio in Rome, which serves as both an educational centre as well as a production studio. Ciccotti has won numerous awards, including in 2011 the prestigious "Silver Ribbon" award for best music, given by the Italian National Syndicate of Film Journalists for his soundtrack for the film Il commissario De Luca. In 2021, Ciccotti released the album Nostalgia, featuring a mix of classical and contemporary music, in collaboration with the Italian pianist Lorenzo dall'Ozzo. The album was praised by critics for its inventive composition and masterful performances. Today, Ciccotti is considered one of the most important names of the Italian music scene, and continues to bring his unique vision to a diverse range of projects. He is also a respected mentor and lecturer, sharing his long experience in the field with the next generation of aspiring composers and musicians.

Gunn Yang (born May 10, 1995) is a Taiwanese-American singer, songwriter, and performer known for her distinctive voice, classical style and use of improvisation. She is currently signed to Sony Music Taiwan and has released three albums and several EPs to date. Yang was born and raised in Taipei, Taiwan. Growing up, she was exposed to a variety of genres, including classical, jazz, and traditional Taiwanese music. She began piano lessons at the age of 5 and singing lessons at the age of 8. She attended the University of the Arts (formerly called the Taiwan Conservatory of Music, where she studied voice and composition. In 2016, Yang released her debut album, My Castle. The album featured mellow, R&B-tinged covers of popular English songs. The album was well-received in Taiwan and established her as a rising star in the local music scene. The following year, Yang released a five-track EP entitled The Return. This time, Yang incorporated more traditional Taiwanese instrumentation and themes into her music. In 2018, her second full-length album, Beginning Light, was released, and became her most successful to date, topping the local charts and being certified multi-platinum. In 2019, Yang was a featured artist on the hit Taiwanese-American television show “The Voice of Taiwan”. Her performance of her song “This Is Not My City” captured the attention of millions of viewers and earned her a spot in the finale. While she did not win the show, she did receive a recording contract from Sony Music Taiwan. Yang’s music continues to explore a variety of genres, ranging from traditional Chinese music to blues and folk. Her live performances often showcase her talents in improvisation and she has collaborated with numerous other artists and regularly plays concerts throughout Taiwan. Today, Yang is one of the most successful female singers in Taiwan. She has been credited with introducing new elements and influences to the traditional Chinese pop music scene and has garnered a devoted fanbase, both in Taiwan and abroad.

Triambak Sharma (born 1972) is an Indian business leader and entrepreneur, who has over twenty years of experience in managing and leading large corporations in Healthcare, IT and technology, retail, agribusiness, and lifestyle industries. He is the founder of Group of Companies, which includes a real-estate development firm, Triambak Estates, a creche chain, Little Brains Academy and an innovative healthcare technology company, WEMED Health Technologies. A Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech) in Electronics and Communication Engineering from National Institute of Technology, Triambak Sharma started his professional career as an engineer and progressed to become an entrepreneur and business leader. During his two-decade-long career, he has worked across various industries – from IT and telecoms to healthcare and lifestyle – taking on increasingly senior roles and responsibilities. In 2008, Triambak Sharma founded Triambak Estates, a real-estate development firm with a focus on creating smart and innovative living spaces for its customers. In 2010, he ventured into the healthcare industry with WEMED Health Technologies, an innovative healthcare technology company which develops medical devices and software applications. In 2012, he founded Little Brains Academy, a creche chain which provides quality early education to children aged 0-3 years. Throughout the years, Triambak Sharma has continuously looked for ways to push the boundaries of innovation in the industries that he is associated with. His focus on enhancing customer experience, combined with his drive for innovation, has seen the Group of Companies grow organically and make deep strides in the field of technology and healthcare. Triambak Sharma is deeply passionate about giving back to the society, and he runs several social welfare programs and campaigns in India, including a free health camp every year for underprivileged children. He also is a know passionate leader, and works on improving the quality of life for individuals across India. Apart from being an entrepreneur and business leader, Triambak Sharma is also an avid reader, and enjoys spending time with his family. He resides in Delhi with his wife and two children.

Bug-O-Nay-Ge-Shig School is a public school that primarily serves Ojibwe people in Cass Lake, Minnesota. The school was established in the 1990s, when a group of Ojibwe tribal leaders and community members recognized the need for educational services for their children and for culturally appropriate education for Ojibwe students. The school is named for Bug-O-Nay-Ge-Shig, a former Ojibwe chief who was instrumental in treaty negotiations with the United States in the 19th century. Bug-O-Nay-Ge-Shig School enrolls students in grades K-12 and covers a wide variety of subjects, including history, math, reading, writing, science, art, music, and physical education. The school also offers extracurricular activities, including basketball, volleyball, baseball, and softball. Additionally, the school offers on-site counseling services, a gymnasium, a library, and an outdoor amphitheater. Bug-O-Nay-Ge-Shig School places a strong emphasis on cultural teachings, weaving Ojibwe language, culture, and history into its curriculum. For example, the school’s art program incorporates traditional Ojibwe beadwork and basketweaving, and the science program employs a project-based approach focused on exploring the natural world through Ojibwe perspectives. All of this is combined with a focus on helping students build the academic and social foundations they need to exceed in their future studies. Bug-O-Nay-Ge-Shig School is a diverse, vibrant, and rewarding learning environment. The school holds a variety of celebrations and events throughout the year, such as the annual spring powwow, Indigenous Peoples’ Day, and a Feast Day in October. These events provide students the opportunity to explore their own history and culture, celebrate their accomplishments, and come together as a community. In addition to its education services, Bug-O-Nay-Ge-Shig School also plays a key role in Cass Lake's community. The school takes part in a number of initiatives to ensure the community remains healthy and prosperous, from the ricing camp that the school hosts each fall to its partnerships with local businesses. It also offers training and mentorship opportunities for interested members of the local community. Overall, Bug-O-Nay-Ge-Shig School is an important and vital educational resource for the Ojibwe people of Cass Lake and its surrounding areas. The school's successful combination of cultural teachings and modern education has helped foster mutual understanding, strengthen the community, and provide an incredible educational opportunity for students.

Tracy Jordan (born 1964) is an American actor, comedian, and musician. He is best known for his role as Tracy Jordan on the television sitcom 30 Rock which aired from 2006-2013. Jordan was born in Wisconsin, though he spent most of his childhood in Chicago. He began his career as an amateur stand-up comedian in 1990, eventually supporting himself as a cab driver while performing at comedy clubs around Chicago. His big break came in 1999, when he was cast in the cult comedy sitcom The Tracy Jordan Show. The show ran for four seasons, though its ratings steadily decreased throughout its run. Jordan earned two Emmy nominations during the show's run for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Comedy Series. In 2006, Jordan was cast as Tracy Jordan on the sitcom 30 Rock. His portrayal of the flamboyant and often outrageous character earned him two Emmy and three Golden Globe Award nominations. Jordan also starred in a recurring role on the NBC series Law & Order: Criminal Intent as Detective Charles Collins from 2008 to 2011. Additionally, he has had guest roles on Saturday Night Live, The Office, and Parks and Recreation. In 2006, Jordan released his debut rap album Busta Rhymes Is My Daddy. The album was met with lukewarm reviews, but it did not deter Jordan from continuing his music career. In 2007, he released his follow-up album Twisted Brain Cells, to better reception. Outside of acting and music, Jordan is a philanthropist. He has worked with causes related to hunger and poverty, animal rights, and disability rights. He also supported President Barack Obama during his 2008 presidential campaign. He was named the Human Rights Campaign's National Coming Out Project Honorary Ambassador in 2012. Jordan lives in Los Angeles with his wife, Angie Jordan, and their three children.

The 1975 Fiesta Bowl was the third edition of the college football bowl game played at Sun Devil Stadium in Tempe, Arizona. It was played on December 31, 1975 and featured the Pacific 8 Conference co-champion UCLA Bruins against the post-season-ineligible Arizona State Sun Devils. The game was sponsored by the Fiesta Bowl organization and was broadcast nationally on NBC. The bowl received its name from the Fiesta Bowl, which had been founded in 1971 and was held annually in the Valley of the Sun until moving to University of Phoenix Stadium in 2007. UCLA entered the game boasting an offense that featured two-time All-American RB Wendell Tyler, while the Sun Devils were led by RB Woody Green and FB Mike Haynes. Arizona State was playing as an independent, ineligible for bowl games due to NCAA probation. UCLA quarterback John Sciarra opened the scoring with a seven-yard touchdown run in the first quarter but Arizona State countered with a 24-yard Tyler run midway through the second quarter. UCLA QB John Sciarra connected with TE Jerrott Willard in the third quarter for a 7-yd touchdown to give UCLA a 14-7 lead. The Sun Devils narrowed the deficit to 14-10 early in the fourth quarter, but Sciarra found Tight End Jerry Robinson for a 20-yard scoring reception to stretch UCLA's lead to 21-10. Arizona State threw a Hail Mary at the end of the game, but it was batted away by UCLA's Safety Brad Leggett sealing the victory for the Bruins. The Bruins would go on to win the 1975 Pacific 8 Conference Championship and received the Rose Bowl berth. Although they lost the Rose Bowl to the Ohio State Buckeyes, they finished the season ranked 6th in the final AP poll. The Sun Devils compiled a 7-4 record in their first season as an independent and were not eligible for postseason play due to NCAA probation. The 1975 Fiesta Bowl was the last bowl game appearance by UCLA until the 1986 season and took place with the backdrop of a renewed excitement for college football in Arizona State and the surrounding area after the formation of the Fiesta Bowl. It remains an important part of both schools' football history.

Physical Sciences-Oncology Centers (PS-OCs) are locations that provide specialized and innovative cancer treatments, tailored to the individual needs of the patient. PS-OCs combine expertise from physical science professionals, such as physicists and engineers, with medical/oncology experts to develop advanced cancer treatments, such as digitally assisted radiotherapy, image-guided radiation therapy, and other emerging technologies. The vision of PS-OCs is to be at the forefront of developing and implementing modern techniques to treat and ultimately cure cancer. By bringing together physical scientists and medical oncologists, PS-OCs are able to bridge the gap between experimental tumor biology and patient treatment outcomes. The unique combination of research and clinical capabilities allows PS-OCs to pursue the development of innovative and personalized treatments on a local level. PS-OCs primarily serve as regional treatment centers, providing cancer care to patients while conducting in-depth research into the progression and treatment of various types of cancer. The physical science experts at PS-OCs use their expertise to address treatments at a molecular level, allowing for the most efficient and effective treatments available. PS-OCs are also involved in numerous clinical trials, continuously pushing the boundaries of innovation and exploration in cancer research. The physical scientists at PS-OCs specialize in different disciplines, including but not limited to: computer science and engineering, applied mathematics, imaging and radiological physics, cancer biology, gene sequencing, pharmacology and clinical trials, medical radiation therapy, nanotechnology, and biostatistics. By leveraging their expertise and skills, PS-OCs are able to develop advanced treatment protocols and refine existing treatments to provide superior diagnostic capabilities, therapy delivery, and overall patient care. In addition to their core missions of innovative treatments, PS-OCs also engage in community outreach to raise awareness and educate the public about the importance of cancer research and early detection. They often offer educational seminars and build partnerships with schools and organizations to further advance their cause. Overall, Physical Sciences-Oncology Centers are dedicated to developing the most advanced and personalized cancer treatments for each individual patient. By leveraging immense research capabilities, creative treatments, and cutting-edge technology, PS-OCs are committed to helping treat and ultimately cure all types of cancer.

Rufus Riddlesbarger (1859–1923) was an American naturalist, conservationist, and photographer. He was born in Richmond, Indiana, and graduated from Purdue University with a degree in agriculture in 1883. He later continued his studies in Vienna, Austria, where he studied forestry and later obtained a PhD in zoology. Riddlesbarger was a well-known figure in early conservationist circles. He campaigned to protect wildlife habitats, lobbied the government to protect endangered species, and encouraged the adoption of wildlife-friendly farming practices. In the early 1900s, he was an active member of the National Audubon Society and helped establish a network of conservation areas in several states across the country. Riddlesbarger was an avid photographer, as well. He was an early adopter of color photography, and was particularly keen on capturing the beauty of animals, birds, and nature. He took many photographs of birds in flight, capturing stunning details and the grace of their movements. Along with photographs, he also wrote novels and scientific papers on birds and the natural world, which were widely published in journals and magazines. In 1906, he released his first book titled "The Life of Birds", which was met with critical acclaim. The book was an insightful look at the habits and behaviors of birds, and the intricate dynamics that occur amongst them. In the final years of his life, Riddlesbarger devoted himself to conservation efforts, helping create a number of nature preserves and conservation areas throughout the US. He also worked to make the government of Indiana more aware of the needs of nature, leading to the passage of the Conservationists Bill of Rights in 1921. Rufus Riddlesbarger passed away in 1923, leaving behind a legacy of dedication and conservation advocacy. His work is still remembered today and he is honored for his contribution to the preservation of the natural environment. He is regarded as one of the major figures in the history of American conservationism and his legacy lives on in the many conservation areas that he helped establish.

The European mink (Mustela lutreola) is an amphibious, weasellike mammal that is ranked as one of the most endangered animals in Europe. It is classified as the sister species to the American mink, existing in fragmented populations that inhabit parts of Belarus, Estonia, Finland, France, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Romania, Russia and Ukraine. The European mink is typically different from the American mink in that it is a darker color, ranging from a reddish-brown to black. It is typically slightly longer with more slender proportions, having a long and thin body and having a length that typically ranges from 40 to 65 cm. The tail of European mink is often less than one-third of the total length. The European mink is a semi-aquatic dwelling mammal that typically inhabits slow-flowing bodies of water, such as wetlands and coastal areas, where it hunts and feeds on aquatic organisms, small rodents, amphibians, fish and crayfish. It prefers wetland habitats with water at least 0.5 meters deep and plenty of vegetation close to water. They use burrows and dens built in the banks of rivers and small lakes, as well as beaver dens for shelter, and may occasionally climb trees in search of prey. Habitat destruction and persecution, as well as competition from the invasive American mink, have caused rapid population decline and extinction, making the European mink globally endangered. The species is legally protected in some countries and listed in the Appendices of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species and the European Habitats Directive. However, in many countries, conservation measures are not enforced and threats continue to threaten the species. Conservation efforts for the European mink focus on reintroduction and captive breeding programs. This has been an ongoing success, particularly in coastal regions. The species is also still found in some isolated areas, where suitable habitats remain intact. Captive breeding programs have also been developed to try and bolster the mink’s numbers. At the same time, efforts have been made to increase the public awareness of the mink, including creation of various educational resources and campaigns to try and engage the public, as well as efforts to create protected areas. As a result, populations of mink have been gradually increasing in some areas, but much work is still needed to ensure its continued survival.

Heaven is a song by American post-punk band Talking Heads, released as a single in 1982. It later appeared on the band's fourth studio album, Speaking in Tongues, which was released later that year. Heaven was written by lead singer David Byrne and produced by Talking Heads with Brian Eno. Heaven is a midtempo funk-fusion song with sparse instrumentation. The song's anthemic chorus features Byrne singing with a multi-tracked vocal choir. The lyrics describe Byrne's view of a possible heavenly afterlife, and express ambivalence about it. The chorus also includes variations on the phrase "Heaven, is a place where nothing ever happens". They were intended to suggest both the beauty and dullness of a peaceful, non-existence in the afterlife. The song's jazzy guitar is by Adrian Belew, and the bass by Tina Weymouth. The single featured the album version on one side and the "Nightclub Version" on the other, which was extended and had additional production by John Potoker. In concert, the song included intro and outro sections with improvisations by Belew featuring a fusion of jazz and funk guitar. Heaven was generally well received by critics. Penny Valentine of Smash Hits called it "a conversationally droll slice of avant-garde pop that drills to the spiritual heart of life", while other reviews likened it to earlier Talking Heads songs like "Once in a Lifetime". It fared well commercially in the United States, topping the Billboard Dance Music/Club Play Singles chart and becoming a moderate hit on the Billboard Hot 100. In the UK, however, it only reached number 99 on the UK Singles Chart. A music video was filmed featuring the band walking around in an abandoned building. Heaven is seen as a classic Talking Heads song, along with songs like "Psycho Killer" and "Burning Down the House". It has also been featured prominently in cult films like Stranger Than Paradise and True Stories, as well as in a 2020 episode of the popular Netflix series Stranger Things.

Chromatrope is an optical device which creates a dynamic illusion of colorful and dazzling light patterns. It is a classic form of animation and entertainment that has been used as far back as the 19th century. The Chromatrope consists of a lantern, two discs and some color filters. The rotation of the discs creates a “chromatic effect” and creates the illusion of a colorful and moving object to onlookers. When the lantern is lit and the discs are set to spin, the colors of the filters mix together to form a variety of dynamic images. Each disc may contain four separate colors filters that mix together as the discs rotate to create a unique kaleidoscopic design. The simple beauty of the chromatrope has been used in a variety of contexts throughout history, including scientific and medical demonstration, as well as entertainment purposes. Victorian England was perhaps where the chromatrope gained the most popularity, being used in variety shows, music hall performances, magic lantern shows, and various explanations of scientific principles. They were even often featured in illustrations before the advent of color photography. Its popularity of the device eventually waned in the early 20th century, when other forms of animation were developed, and it faded into obscurity. In modern times, the chromatrope has re-emerged as a decorative item for home and parties. As a modern day art form, it has been used to create hypnotic and captivating visuals in live events such as concerts and clubs. It even made a return to the scientific demonstration in some universities. Several electronics versions of Chromatrope have even been created, allowing the user to control the flow of the moving mandala pattern, and providing a beautiful backdrop for any event. Overall, the Chromatrope is a simple yet effective device that utilizes real world physics to create an entertaining and mesmerizing visual experience. Its long and varied history makes it a unique and interesting piece of animation and entertainment that is sure to captivate its audience.

Rajmohan Unnithan (born 8 October 1936) is an Indian politician and a former Minister of State in the Central Government. He is a member of the Indian National Congress party, and has been a member of the Kerala Legislative Assembly on five occasions, representing the Kollam constituency in Kerala. Born in Ayoor in the Kollam district of Kerala, Unnithan was educated at the Government Arts College in Thiruvananthapuram and the Maharaja's College in Ernakulam. He entered politics at the age of 26 and won the Kollam assembly seat in 1967. He has consecutively represented the same constituency for over three decades, except for the 2002 elections when he lost to the CPI(M) candidate V.S. Achuthanandan. He is a member of the working committee of the Indian National Congress in Kerala. Unnithan served as the Minister of State for Labour and Employment from 1991 to 1996 in the Narasimha Rao-led Government at the Centre and was a member of the Public Accounts Committee in Parliament from 1991 to 1996. He has also held the post of the Diplomatic Officer of India at the Embassy of India in Nepal from 1996 to 1998. In the state of Kerala, Unnithan worked with the previous Congress-led UDF government as the Minister for Irrigation Foreign Relations, and Cultural Affairs in 2004. He has been actively involved in social work and served as the Chairman of the Kerala Social Welfare Board from 2001 to 2004. The Government of India awarded him the fourth highest Indian civilian honour of Padma Shri in 2004 for his immense contribution in the fields of public service and politics. Unnithan is married to Smt. Meena Unnithan and has two sons, Aanath Unnithan and Dinesh Unnithan, both of whom are actively involved in politics.

The Adventures of Bullwhip Griffin is a 1967 American Western comedy film starring Roddy McDowall, Suzanne Pleshette and Karl Malden. The film was directed by James Neilson and produced by Walt Disney Productions. The film is set in the late 19th century and follows the adventures of a young orphan named Bullwhip Griffin (McDowall). Bullwhip is sent to San Francisco to stay with his aunt and uncle, but he finds himself unwelcome in the city and so he decides to escape by stowing away on a ship. Unfortunately, the ship is attacked by pirates and Bullwhip is forced to fend for himself in the middle of the ocean. With the help of his wits and some lucky coincidences, he finally makes it to shore and, after taking on an alias, he assumes the identity of a bounty hunter. With the help of his newfound notoriety, Bullwhip travels from one end of the West to the other, encountering many colorful characters and dangerous scenarios. He eventually discovers that his uncle is actually a wanted criminal and must do whatever it takes to bring him to justice. The movie is filled with plenty of laughs and adventure as Bullwhip makes his way from one outrageous scenario to the next. The special effects, particularly the stunts and action sequences, are extremely well done and remain impressive to this day. Overall, The Adventures of Bullwhip Griffin is a classic Walt Disney film that offers great family entertainment. With a humorous storyline, fantastic action sequences and a star-studded cast, this film is sure to please any western fan.

Joseph M. Warren (1924–1994) was an American theologian and Methodist minister who worked as the Dean of the Chapel at Duke University and co-created "The Warren Report" for the International Association of Methodist Schools, Colleges and Universities (IAMSCU). Early life Joseph M. Warren was born and raised in Georgia. He received his B.A. in mathematics from Emory University in 1945 and a Master of Divinity degree from Candler School of Theology at Emory in 1948. While at Candler, he was one of the first students to study the emerging fields of Christian ethics and systematic theology. Career In 1948, Warren was appointed to the faculty of Duke University’s Divinity School and Chapel. He was associated with the university for 46 years before retiring in 1994. During his tenure, Warren served in several administrative roles, such as dean of the chapel, director of assessment and program evaluation for the school of divinity, chairperson of the board of directors for the International Association of Methodist Schools, Colleges and Universities (IAMSCU), and president of the Ecumenical Foundation of Higher Education. With the IAMSCU, he co-authored "The Warren Report" which identified trends related to the changes in governance, funding and understanding of their role in the global ecumenical context. He had a particular interest in the history of United Methodism. In 1974, Warren was a founding member of the International Council of Centers for Inter-Religious Studies, devoted to academic and scholarly exchanges across religious boundaries. Through this council he established an international Christian fellowship system that provided opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students to travel abroad and experience the culture and customs of other societies. Personal life In 1950, Warren married Mary Frances Veal. The couple had four children. Throughout his career, Warren received numerous honors, including an honorary Doctor of Divinity degree from Emory University in 1973. Death In 1994, Warren died of pulmonary disease. He is survived by his wife and children.

Legend Tripping is a form of folklore, in which a person, or a group of people visit a location where a legend or myth supposedly exist and take part in a ritual. It is an old phenomenon, and is based on the belief that supernatural entities may exist in certain places. Legend tripping is often associated with activities of a supernatural nature, including ghost hunting, séances, and searching for symbols of the supernatural, such as items associated with lost souls. Legend tripping began in the United States in the late 1800s and early 1900s, and is a popular activity today. Legend tripping might occur in the form of a single individual visiting the location of a haunting, or a group of people gathering at the site of a supposed supernatural event. Participants in legend tripping often look for evidence of a supernatural entity in the form of physical items (e.g. data collected by a psychic), vibrant stories or stories of past or present events, or residual hauntings or ghostly presences. Legend tripping has been identified in many different cultures worldwide. For example, in Japan, legend tripping often involves visiting locations that are either haunted or associated with spirits. According to popular belief, these sites house shadows, or “yurei”, and the spirits of these yurei are believed to be drawn to the site if it is visited by enough people. In Australia, legend tripping often involves visiting Aboriginal sacred sites and taking part in rituals that are believed to bring forth spirits of the dead. Today, legend tripping is a popular form of entertainment which has been spawned by the ubiquity of television shows dedicated to the paranormal and supernatural. Popular television shows often explore haunted locations, supernatural paraphernalia and the stories behind them, creating a demand for individuals and groups to search out such things on their own. This has led to an increase in individuals or groups visiting allegedly haunted sites, although this trend is not exclusive to such locations. Legends tripping is also practiced in non-haunted areas, such as national parks and old cemeteries, which are believed to contain secret or hidden treasures. Legend tripping can be a dangerous and even life-threatening activity, and is not recommended without adult supervision. It is important to remember that there is no scientific evidence that any supernatural being exists, and the risks associated with such activities may outweigh the reward. Always take proper precautions and follow guidance from experienced personnel when engaging in such activities.

The Georgia Tech Center for Music Technology (GTCMT) is an interdisciplinary research and education center in the College of Design at Georgia Institute of Technology. The Center focuses on fostering and supporting research, teaching and innovative activities at the intersection of music, science and technology. Through creative collaboration and research, GTCMT’s mission is to advance the development, use, understanding and appreciation of music technology. The current Director of GTCMT is Gil Weinberg, a scientist and musician, who has made it his mission to develop advanced interactive systems that allow people, whether with or without disabilities, to create and interact with music. Weinberg is also responsible for the development of the Shimon robotic musician, a robotic marimba player that translates musical compositions into physical robot-performed actions. GTCMT provides a wide range of activities that foster creativity and innovation in the field of music technology. The Center has a twofold mission: to promote the use of music technology in the classroom and research lab and to create a community of practice for people interested in music technology. GTCMT offers facilities and curricula for courses and seminars, consortia for research collaboration, and various other projects and events, such as the Music + Maker Series, Georgia Tech/TEDx, and the Georgia Tech Music Business Summit. GTCMT is currently home to more than 20 faculty members from various disciplines. It has partnerships with within the prestigious Georgia Institute of Technology as well as external partners such as the Recording Academy and SoundExchange among others. GTCMT has been involved in many projects, including establishing collaborations and exchanges between students, faculty and visitors in the field of music technology, providing resources and programming for startups, and research projects such as the development of the Shimon robotic musician, exploring the potential of artificial intelligence in music composition, and investigating music quality and its relation to wellbeing. The Center is also home to a number of concert series and events such as the Music + Maker Series, which invites influential figures in music technology to give presentations and workshops. This series has featured luminaries such as Max Mathews, Bill Schottstaedt, and Adil Mehboob Khan among others. The Center also hosts the Music Machine Learning Symposium and a variety of other festivals and concerts. The GTCMT strives to be a hub for music technology at Georgia Tech and beyond. It is dedicated to providing opportunities for students and faculty to explore the relationship between music, science, and technology and to foster innovation in music technology.

Nasi lengko is a classic Javanese dish, traditionally served at ceremonies, such as weddings and circumcisions. It is also a popular breakfast food. The dish references the traditional staple Indonesian food, nasi, meaning "rice," and lengko, which refers to the topping and side dishes. Nasi lengko is usually served accompanied with fried shallots and peanuts, fresh vegetables, and a variety of sambals and condiments. The preparation of nasi lengko is complex and requires the use of highly specialized techniques. Start by boiling white jasmine rice with a pinch of salt. Once the rice is cooked, spread it out to cool and set aside. Meanwhile, prepare the topping and side dishes. For example, a typical nasi lengko dish can include boiled potatoes, hard-boiled eggs, ketoprak (a popular Indonesian dish made with bean sprouts, tofu, and fried shallots), and tahu bacem (a sweet and sour combination of spiced fried tofu, tempeh, and potato). To assemble a plate of nasi lengko, place some of the cooked rice in the center of a plate and arrange the toppings and side dishes around it. Then, spoon some of the condiments and sambals over the rice and toppings. The variety of sambals and condiments can also vary from region to region. Some popular sauces and condiments to include with nasi lengko are sambal kacang, kecap manis, and bumbu balado. Nasi lengko is also a popular street food in many parts of Indonesia. Vendors often offer nasi lengko as a cheap meal option, and the toppings can vary based on the availability of ingredients. The dish is popular due to its convenience and affordability. In addition to its food value, nasi lengko is also culturally significant. The dish is served during traditional ceremonies or gatherings, such as weddings and circumcisions, and has become an important symbol of Indonesian culture and heritage. The social aspect of the dish is also a common feature, as it is often served communally, encouraging guests to interact and enjoy the traditional dishes. Nasi lengko is a traditional Indonesian dish that has been served for centuries. As a tasty, nutritious, and affordable meal, it is a favorite among locals and tourists alike. The dish has also come to symbolize the cultural identity and heritage of the Indonesian people.
