George Dearnaley (b. 1874 – 1964) was a British diver and underwater film maker. He was a pioneer in the world of underwater filmmaking, filming the first underwater film in Britain. George was born in Knotty Ash near Liverpool, England in 1874. He was raised in a family of seven and left school early to help support the family. His early career was a farm labourer and then a mechanic, working on submarines during World War I. In 1921, he patented the “Dearnaley Apparatus” which was a contraption similar to an underwater camera and diving helmet. With the apparatus, George had the ability to take underwater film with ease and accuracy. His first underwater film was called "The Riddle of the Silver King", filmed in the 1910s in Cornwall. The film was a success in the film industry; where George earned his reputation as a pioneer of underwater filmmaking. In 1924 George made the film "Under the Atlantic" which was his most well known and successful film. This followed many successes, his most popular one being “The Underwater Record” from 1931. During his life he described himself as a "diver and underwater cameraman". He was invited to air his underwater films on television in his later years and received much praise from the public. His last film was released in the 1960, which was called “The Last of the Seals”. George Dearnaley passed away on 26 April 1964 at the age of 90. His legacy as an innovator and pioneer in the world of underwater filming still lives on in various documentaries, magazines, and books. George will always be remembered for his courage, determination, and love of the sea.

Tofig Javadov (Azerbaijani: Tofiq Cəvadov; 7 June 1945 – 29 August 2003), was an Azerbaijani politician and government official who served as the Minister of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan from 20 June 1994 to 7 October 1995, and as the deputy prime minister from 7 October 1995 until his untimely death in 2003. Prior to his political career, Javadov worked with a number of prominent Azerbaijani organisations. He was the director of the non-profit Human Rights Society of Azerbaijan from 1996 to 1997. From 1993 to 1995, he was the dean of the faculty of law at the Azerbaijan State University of Economics. He was also the founding director of the Azerbaijan National Research Institute of Economics from 1991 to 1997. In 1994, Javadov was appointed Minister of Internal Affairs by then president Abulfaz Elchibey. During his tenure, Javadov oversaw the dissolution of the CIS personal recog during his time in officenition and the signing of the Azerbaijani-Uzbekistan accords, and was responsible for resolving the 1994-1995 Armenian-Azerbaijani conflict in Nagorno-Karabakh. After the death of Elchibey and the election of Heydar Aliyev to the presidency, Javadov remained a minister in the Aliyev's cabinet until 1995, when he was appointed deputy prime minister. As deputy prime minister, Javadov was responsible for economic policy, foreign affairs and the defence industries. He signed several bilateral agreements with other CIS countries, in particular Azerbaijan's milestone agreement with Russia, and an agreement to join the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development in 1997. In 2001, Javadov was awarded the Order of Azerbaycan. Javadov was scheduled to ascend to the post of prime minister following the 2003 Azerbaijani presidential election, but was killed in a car accident on 29 August 2003. His death deeply shocked Azerbaijani citizens, who believed that Javadov was the most suitable candidate for Prime Minister due to his extensive experience in politics and economics. He was buried in Martyrs' Lane in Baku. Following his death, President Ilham Aliyev and others commemorated Javadov's memory by ordering the construction of a mosque in his name in Baku as well as by renaming the airport road in Baku, which now carries his name. In October 2003, a memorial fund under the management of his wife, Nigar Javadova, was created and funded by the President. A biography of Javadov, Məşhur xəstə Tofiq Cəvadov (5 volumes) by Yagub Mammadov, was published in 2004.

Decatur High School (DHS) is a public high school located in Decatur, Alabama. It is part of the Decatur City Schools district and it is the only high school in the district. It serves grade levels 9-12. Decatur High School was established in 1888 to provide secondary education for local youth. The school was then known as Decatur City High School and was located at the corner of Second Avenue and Seventh Street in Decatur. In 1929, the school moved to a larger campus on Spring Avenue and the name changed to Decatur High School. Decatur High School is considered the oldest public high school in North Alabama. The history of the school is long, rich, and steeped in tradition. Along with the school yearbook and alma mater, the school also has many special traditions such as the DHS 100 Year Celebration and the DHS Alumni Reunion. The school offers a complete academic program and a variety of extracurricular activities, including athletics, music and arts, student government, honor societies, and community service. Decatur High School student body includes a diverse population of students. The school provides a quality education through a challenging curriculum. The school is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools and is a member of the Alabama High School Athletic Association. Its mascot is the Red Raider and its school colors are black and gold. Decatur High School has been home to many distinguished alumni, including ambassadors, politicians, professional athletes, and business leaders. The school is a source of pride and tradition for Decatur, Alabama and its surrounding communities. The school takes pride in its commitment to academic excellence and preparing its students for college, careers, and life. Decatur High School is truly a place where education, character, and spirit come together to shape the future.

Old wave is a term coined in the late 2000s to describe the cultural wave of older music genres, specifically rock and metal. Many up-and-coming acts were attempting to recapture the sound of the old wave in a modern context. It is not to be confused with classic rock, which refers to a particular period in Rock and Roll which started in roughly the mid 60s and ended in roughly the early 80s. The revival of old wave genres started around 2005 when acts such as Steel Panther, Jet, Taking Back Sunday, The Darkness, and Franz Ferdinand began to gain popularity. These acts all had a tendency to take the classic, classic rock sound and lyrics and put them into a modern context by altering their instrumentation and production to fit the times. The new wave brought in a new audience who, after being saturated with processional pop music from the mid 90s onwards, sought to recover the musical "edge" that rock and metal had once possessed. Old wave has come to encompass a number of genres, including classic rock, hard rock, blues-rock, and metalcore. It can be heard in the sound of greats such as AC/DC or Led Zeppelin, but also in the sound of more modern bands like Halestorm or Disturbed. Generally, it is characterized as having an intense, rock-inspired sound, with particular attention being paid to guitar tones, song structures, and vocal delivery. Old wave has had a resurgence in the last decade, and its influence can be seen in the styles of younger bands such as The Pretty Reckless, Halestorm, and Ghost. Due to its blend of classic rock and metal influences, the genre appealed to a wider audience who were looking for something familiar, yet modern. Additionally, many of the acts that were developing in the scene have since gone on to great success, making old wave a viable style in popular music. Though old wave has made a big comeback in recent years, it is still considered to be on the fringe of mainstream music, and for the most part stays confined to specialty radio programs and independent media outlets. Its deep grooves, its blues-based guitar riffs, and its classic metal sound continue to inspire young bands, and will likely be heard for many years to come.

Winter's Tale, published in 1983 and written by Mark Helprin, is a fantasy novel set primarily in 1976 New York City. The novel follows the adventures of Peter Lake, an orphaned thief who, after attempting to break into a Cobble Hill, Brooklyn, mansion owned by a mysterious old man, finds himself intertwined in a centuries-old struggle between good and evil. To complicate matters, Peter is being pursued by a demonic creature named the Ragman, whose duty is to recover a mysterious box stolen by Peter. The novel takes the reader on a journey through Peter's surreal and magical journey beginning on the Upper West Side of Manhattan. There, he meets Beverly, the daughter of the mysterious old man whose mansion he had attempted to burglarize. Beverly, a strong-willed and wise-beyond-her-years young woman, helps Peter on his quest to elude the Ragman. Along the way, Peter is aided by a magical white horse from Central Park and an enormous sky-dwelling dog named Athansor. Throughout the novel, the reader is made aware that the characters are living out a much larger ancient story. As the plot progresses, it is revealed that the characters' lives are inseparable from the myth from which Peter's adventure originates. It is later in the novel that Pearly Soames, the head of The Short Tails — the gang of burglars Peter had been working with — is revealed to be an angel sent by God to oversee Peter's journey. The novel concludes with an epic battle between the forces of good and evil, with Peter ultimately emerging triumphant. He and Beverly are eventually married, and the book concludes with them living happily ever after. Winter's Tale is a magical, suspenseful story of extraordinary characters driven by destiny and myth. Through the journey of its protagonists, the novel provides an imaginative look into the world of good and evil. The themes of destiny, myth, loyalty and courage appear in this epic tale of love, friendship, and faith against overwhelming odds.

''Main School'' is an elementary school located in Hillburn, New York. It serves students in prekindergarten through fifth grade. It is the only public elementary school in Hillburn, and has a student population of approximately 250 children. The school was established in 1937 and has a rich history in Hillburn. It was the first school in the community and has been a staple in the community ever since. Main School has a variety of programs and services for its students. They offer a culturally diverse learning environment and a curriculum that is aligned to the New York State Standards. In addition, the school has a robust Special Education program and English as a Second Language program. The school also offers a variety of extracurricular activities such as student government, art and music classes, community service projects, and science and health-related events. Main School also has an active parent-teacher organization that is dedicated to creating a positive learning environment for students and providing support to teachers and families. The school is led by Principal Kimberly Wladis, who started at Main School in 2019. Under her leadership, Main School has continued to be a leader in educational excellence, while still adhering to Hillburn's values of diversity, honesty, kindness and respect. Main School strives to create an atmosphere that emphasizes collaboration, innovation and student achievement. The school works hard to provide a safe and nurturing learning environment that meets the needs of every student. Overall, Main School is a great educational institution for children in Hillburn, New York and a source of pride for the entire community.

ABC Radio Grandstand is an Australian sports radio station operated by the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC). It is the home of live sports coverage, nationally on the ABC's FM and digital radio networks. ABC Radio Grandstand provides a comprehensive range of sports programs and updates for all Australians. The programs specialize in coverage of AFL and NRL games, as well as other major sports events. They also provide commentary on news headlines and special event interviews. The ABC’s sports radio coverage has been operating in Australia since the 1930s, regularly delivering stories and results of major sporting events to the nation. ABC Radio Grandstand began in the 1960s with its regular coverage of national and international sports news, results and discussion. ABC Radio Grandstand currently covers a range of sports including AFL, cricket, rugby league, soccer, motor sport, golf, netball and politics. The station also covers a range of major international events throughout the year, including the Olympic and Paralympic Games. ABC Radio Grandstand's main programs include: - Grandstand Breakfast: This program is broadcast on weekdays between 7-9am. It covers the news and results of the day with special guests and AFL reviews. - Grandstand Mornings: This program is broadcast on weekdays between 9-12am and covers the current news, results and previews of upcoming AFL and NRL and other sports. - Grandstand Afternoon: This program is broadcast on weekdays between 12-3pm. It covers the latest news and results. - Grandstand Evening: This program is broadcast on weekdays between 3-9pm. It is the home of sports opinions and interviews with special guests throughout the day. - The Saturday Agenda: This program is broadcast on Saturdays between 8-12am. It includes analysis and expert opinions from leading sports journalists. - The Sunday Roundup: This program is broadcast on Sundays between 6-10am. It covers the latest news, reviews and interviews. ABC Radio Grandstand is available across the country through ABC's FM, DAB+ and digital radio networks. It is popular with sports fans and provides live commentary from the nation's major sporting events. ABC Radio Grandstand also has a wide range of podcasts available on their website and social media channels. ABC Radio Grandstand is an essential part of the Australian sports landscape and provides national sports fans with a comprehensive and engaging sports radio experience. It is an established service that has been delivering sports stories and results to Australians for over 80 years.

Andriza Mircovich (born 10 October 1978) is a Montenegrin born film editor, director, producer, and visual effects artist, especially known for his work in the Balkans and Europe. He is best known for such films as Hardcore (2004), 3% (2009), and When the War Comes (2018). Mircovich was born in Montenegro, then part of the former Yugoslavia. He studied at the academy of design in Belgrade before emigrating to the United States where he attended NYU's video and film program. After graduation, he returned to Yugoslavia and continued his career there. Mircovich has been responsible for over one hundred music videos, short films, and videos. He has also worked in television and collaborated with blockbuster films like the Ridley Scott-produced Hannibal Rising, and The East. His music video for the group Dubioza Kolektiv won the Kansai Music Conference Video Award 2019. Mircovich has earned numerous prestigious nominations and awards. He was nominated for a Cannes Lion for best Independent film for his 2009 production of 3%. That same year he was also nominated for a Best Student film at the Belgrade Short Movie Festival. In 2016, Mircovich directed and edited Homeland, a 60 second commercial for a Croatian brewery, which was nominated for a D&AD White Pencil Award. In 2018, he won a Crystal Bear for his feature film When the War Comes at the Berlin International Film Festival. He was also nominated for an award at CinEast in 2019. In recent years, Mircovich has become an influential figure in the filmmaking community in Europe and the Balkans. He has lent his knowledge and experience to master classes and workshops around the world. He was a guest speaker at The Creative Coast Conference in Albania in 2016 and a masterclass speaker at the Trapesum Film Festival in Montenegro in 2019. Mircovich continues to experiment in film with his most recent projects being a design project for the multi-screen video installation Ebb+Flow in 2019 and the video installation Seeking Derivatives the same year. In 2020, he is producing a short documentary of his homeland, Montenegro, which will provide an intimate insight into the complexities of its people and culture.

Tim Couzens is a South African writer, editor, and academic. He is best known for his novels, poetry and histories. He was born in Ladybrand, Free State, on 5 March 1951. Couzens studied at the University of South Africa and the University of the Witwatersrand. He then went on to work as a radio producer for South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC). Couzens has published five novels, two collections of short stories, two collections of essays, and two volumes of poetry. His novels include Room 207 (1987), The Heart of Redness (2000), Suddenly Lala (2007), Plainsong (2012), and Soft Journey (2019). His works have been translated into various languages, such as Afrikaans, French, and Spanish. In addition to his writing, Couzens has also edited several books. He edited Rediscovering the Humanities (2012) and The Oxford Companion to South African Literature (1995) alongside Stephen Gray. He has also edited The Heinemann Book of South African Short Stories alongside Alan Finlay into two volumes. Couzens has also lectured at various institutions, including University of the Free State, Fort Hare University, and Damascus University. He has taught English and Afrikaans literature, and has been recognized for his contributions to the field. In 1992, Couzens was the recipient of the Hertzog Prize for poetry for his works Primary Source (1987) and Social Primer (1992). Additionally, he was the recipients of the Elizabeth M. S. Watson medal in 2002 and the Olive Schreiner Prize in 2000. Couzens is currently a professor at the University of the Witwatersrand and a visiting professor at a number of universities. He is also a board member of various literary organizations and a regular contributor to journals such as New Coin and Die Suide. His works have been acknowledged by scholars in the field of South African literature and studies. Category:South African writers Category:1951 births Category:Living people

IROC XIV was the designation for a one-day, eight-car field race for professional drivers in a closed course race on June 15, 2018, held at Michigan International Speedway in Brooklyn, Michigan, USA. It was the fourteenth year of the International Race of Champions (IROC) series. The race was sponsored by Firestone, who had been part of the series since 1994, and was televised by NBC Sports Network. The IROC series of races featured invitees from various forms of motorsport and was generally regarded as a drivers’ skills competition. The drivers invited to compete in IROC XIV were selected from professional fields of racing by the IROC Selection Committee. Drivers who competed included: Austin Cindric (NASCAR Xfinity Series), Justin Allgaier (NASCAR Xfinity Series), Ryan Blaney (NASCAR Cup Series), Ryan Hunter-Reay (IndyCar Series), Kyle Larson (NASCAR Cup Series), Alexander Rossi (IndyCar Series), Martin Truex Jr. (NASCAR Cup Series), and Tanner Foust (Global RallyCross). The race was held over 75 laps of the two-mile (3.2 km) Michigan International Speedway oval track. Following an abbreviated practice session, the drivers participated in an elimination round, in which the slowest car in each qualifying group was eliminated from further competition; the remaining six cars moved onto the main event. Austin Cindric was declared the overall winner of IROC XIV. Cindric’s strategy of saving fuel, which allowed him to complete the race on two pits stops and not the three which every other competitor required, enabled him to finish ahead of Kyle Larson, who finished in second place, followed by Martin Truex Jr. in third. Justin Allgaier and Alex Rossi placed fourth and fifth respectively, while Tanner Foust and Ryan Blaney rounded out the finishing order. Cindric was presented with the winner's purse of $100,000. Following the race, Cindric said, “I’ve been coming to IROC races since I was 10 or 11 years old, so it’s a dream come true to actually win one.” IROC XIV was the final race of the IROC series, as it was ended in 2018 as a result of series organizers being unable to find a title sponsor for the 2019 season.

John Webber (March 30, 1951 – May 25, 2004) was an American professor of economics and business. He was born in Chicago, Illinois and earned his undergraduate degree from the University of Wisconsin-Madison and received his Masters in business from the University of Washington. Webber was a well-respected professor at the University of Texas at Austin (UT Austin) where he had served since he joined the faculty in 1985. He was an accomplished scholar and published widely in the areas of industrial organization, economic theory, and strategic management. He strongly believed in the power of economic reasoning and the value of diverse perspectives. At the time of his death, he was a senior lecturer for the Department of Business andManagerial Economics at UT Austin. In addition to teaching classes on topics such as micro and macroeconomics, international economics, financial management, and econometrics, he was also the chair of the Faculty Merit Committee and the General Faculty Council. His research was greatly influential as he explored issues related to the theory of the firm, competition, vertical integration, economic modeling and forecasting, government policy, and applied economic research. He wrote and edited books on financial economics and management issues. Webber was also noted for his strong commitment to the Austin community. He was a regular contributor to local newspapers on matters ranging from economic development to taxation reform. In 2003, Webber co-founded a non-profit organization, the Central Texas Economic Alliance, which focused on creating economic opportunities and job creation within Austin. Throughout his career, Webber received numerous awards and recognitions for his extensive contributions to the field of economics and business. Among them, he was recognized by the City of Austin for his contributions to the city's economic development, named a distinguished alumnus for his leadership and service at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and chosen by Business Week as one of their Business Educators of the 21st century. John Webber was an admired and respected leader within the UT-Austin community. He was devoted to his students, regularly attending student-run seminars and lectures to provide constructive critique. He was known to have a good sense of humor and would often crack jokes during class. John Webber tragically died in a car accident on May 25, 2004. He was recognized posthumously as one of Texas Exes' most honored teachers and, in 2010, was inducted into the UT Austin College of Business Hall of Fame. In 2017, the Department of Business and Managerial Economics established the John Webber Memorial Lecture Series in his honor. The John Webber Memorial Lecture Series is held annually by the Department of Business and Managerial Economics and strives to continue his legacy of economic leadership and creative thinking.

Troubadour style is a style of music that originated in the 12th century in western Europe. Its origin is unknown and is often associated with the genre of traditional folk music, but it can also encompass a wide range of styles including courtly love songs, troubadours, church music, and even courtly secular music. Troubadour style songs usually contain lyrics with a focus on courtly love and chivalry. Troubadour style became popular throughout Europe during the 12th and 13th centuries. It was used by French troubadours, a group of travelling minstrels and poets whose songs often were about unrequited love, courtly love, or religious devotion. Troubadours were popular in courts and castles, where they performed their songs for the nobility. The style spread across Europe and other regions in the world, including Spain and northern Africa, influencing the development of many other genres of music. The characteristic that distinguishes troubadour style is its use of polyphony. This technique involves the use of two or more voices singing different melodies simultaneously, creating a unique and complex sound. Troubadours typically used a single voice accompanied by a stringed instrument such as a harp, lute, or cittern. The melodies were typically lyrical, conveying strong emotional content. Often, there was a singing interlude called a refrain, which served to connect the different verses of a song. Aside from its use in music, the term “troubadour style” has also been used in literature, particularly in the works of medieval authors such as Geoffrey Chaucer and Geoffrey of Monmouth. These authors made use of the troubadour style in describing the activities and events of their characters, particularly romantic interactions. Troubadour style remains popular to this day, largely due to its strong emotional content. Many contemporary musicians and singers continue to perform songs in the troubadour style, using modern instruments such as electric and acoustic guitars. Others also incorporate this style into their own music, incorporating traditional elements into modern genres. For example, traditional folk and country singer-songwriters often blend the troubadour style with more contemporary influences.

Luke Rhinehart (born George Cockcroft in New York City, NY on July 25, 1932) is an American author and former psychologist. He is best known for writing the 1971 novel The Dice Man, which has been translated into more than 20 languages. He is also the author of several other novels, including The Search for the Dice Man and Whim, as well as a volume of essays called A Search for Meaning and several nonfiction books. Rhinehart graduated from Cornell University with a degree in psychology and later earned a doctorate in the same field from the University of California, Berkeley. He practiced psychology in various settings including prisons and schools, as well as in private consultation. He eventually became dissatisfied with traditional psychological techniques and theories and left the field in the late 1960s. Throughout his career as a writer and thinker, Rhinehart has rejected traditional approaches to life and decision-making in favor of something he calls "The Lifestyle of Chance", in which decisions are made randomly with the help of a dice. He argues that, by stepping away from pre-ordained choices, people can more fully experience life and find joy and fulfillment. Rhinehart and his theories have been the subject of several novels, films and television series and he has become a figure in popular culture. Rhinehart's work has been controversial, particularly with some religious and moral groups. His philosophy is seen by some as an attempt to provide a framework to deal with the lack of absolutes and the seemingly random nature of life. To others, it is seen as a risk to established morality and fulfillment of personal desires over and above societal values. Rhinehart has also written on a variety of topics unrelated to his dice philosophy, from sexuality and relationships to Zen and Taoism. He is a multi-media artist and continues to write and lecture around the world. His work has been translated into more than 20 languages, and he has been described as "an apostle of possibility and pleasure, a champion of adventure and risk-taking". Today, Rhinehart lives and works in Brooklyn, New York, and remains an influential, though controversial, figure in modern literature and philosophy.

Fai Amata (previously known as Fai Fah Kari) is a prominent Thai pop-punk band from Bangkok, Thailand. Formed in 2000 by four high school friends, Fai Amata has become one of Thailand’s most popular acts, with hits such as “Lai ru”, “Khon Kan”, and “Mai Tah Mai”. As teenagers in 2000, Thailand-born counterparts of the band found themselves drawn to their selective musical interests, finding themselves in the garage at least three times a week, jamming and composing in the confines of their soundproofed walls. Fai Amata eventually took form after the members decided to perform at a school-wide event. After a fairly successful showing, the foursome had decided to take their passion for music to the next level by developing their own music label and studio, Catwalk Collective. The four core members of Fai Amata are vocalist/guitarist Prawit “Pee” Seadprasert, guitarist Namfon “Moe” Skontawan, bassist Manit “Klang” Jussawadee, and drummer Narin “Nada” Thamaphol. Unlike most bands in Thailand, their sound is generally in the lyrically provocative punk genre. They also feature electronic and pop influences, as well as hip-hop styling and melodies. The group has released an abundance of singles, EPs and two studio albums, “Mor Lai Pa Jet” in 2003 and “Tae Hao” in 2005. Other popular singles include “Yah Lao” and “Jab Bap”. Their songs often feature social and political commentary, making it relevant and thought-provoking. The band has been recognized for their outstanding contributions, having won a string of awards, such as “The Best Pop Album” from Siam Music Award and “The Best Punk Song” from the Thai Music Awards. In recent years, Fai Amata embarked on an international tour, traveling to countries such as England, France, Italy, Germany, and the United States. Fai Amata has been widely admired for the success the Thai pop punk scene has achieved, and are credited for the resurgence in the popularity of the genre. They continue to perform and tour, both domestically and internationally, and are poised to remain a presence in the Thai music scene for years to come.

The Larklight trilogy is a series of science-fiction novels by British author Philip Reeve. The series consists of three books, Larklight (2006), Starcross (2007), and Mothstorm (2008). All three books were published to moderate success and are praised for their inventive and imaginative plotlines. The series follows Art and Myrtle Mumby, two children of an eccentric scientist who live in an alternate version of Victorian England. The siblings live with their father in a sprawling, dilapidated mansion called Larklight, located on the moon and in wild space. The trilogy follows their adventures as they, with their own eccentricities and cleverness, explore outer space and fight off the villainous forces of alien species such as the spider-like Spirelanders, the murderous Osirans, and the sinister Crawl. The books are lighthearted in tone and intended for readers aged 10 or above. However, the books have been praised for their complexity and their thoughtful and mature themes, such as loyalty, courage, family, and responsibility. The books are often compared to the works of Jules Verne and Jack London, and have elements of Steampunk, Victorian-era humour, fantastical upgrades of everyday technology, and a unique blend of realism and fantasy. In 2006, Larklight was shortlisted for the Nestlé Children's Book Prize and won the 2006 Emirates Airlines Festival of Literature's Best Children's Series Award while Starcross was nominated for the 2008 Nestle Children's Book Prize and the 2008 Golden Duck Award. In May 2017, it was announced that Elton John's Rocket Pictures had optioned the rights to the trilogy and was developing a live-action movie of the series, with Elton John himself serving as executive producer. A potential release date has yet to be announced. The Larklight trilogy is a beloved book series by traditional science-fiction fans and children alike. Reeve's creative and intricate world building and well-developed characters bridge the gap between children and adult literature, making the series a unique gem of the genre.

The List of Power Stations in Colorado, also known as Generating Facilities and Power Plants, is a comprehensive list of both fuel-fired and renewable energy generated power stations and facilities located in the American state of Colorado. Colorado is the leading state in the production of, and the largest user of, renewable energy produced by wind, solar and hydropower sources. Nuclear There is only one nuclear power station in Colorado, which is located in Pueblo County. The Comanche Peak Nuclear Generating Station consists of two Generating Units operated by Xcel Energy, with a capacity totaling 2,461MW. Fossil Fuel-fired Colorado contains several major coal-fired power plants. The largest power plants are the Craig Power Station at 1,535MW, Comanche Station at 1,259MW, Cherokee Generating Station at 1,314MW, and Pawnee Station at 733MW. Colorado also has many smaller fossil fuel-fired facilities, including three natural gas-fired units (Arapahoe Energy Center, Cameo Generating Station, and Fort St. Vrain Generating Station). Hydroelectric Colorado is relatively abundant in hydropower. It is home to several dams and hydroelectric facilities, including the Dome CANON Reservoir, the Dillon Dam, the Granby Generating Station, and the Reudi Reservoir. Colorado has approximately 8,250 MW of hydropower capacity, with about 6,600 MW provided by Pueblo Dam, the Grand Mesa Project, and the Colorado Big Thompson Project combined. Wind Colorado is home to some of the largest wind farms in the nation. Colorado currently has just over 3.2 GW of wind energy installed. Colorado boasts multiple wind farms such as the Peetz Table Wind Farm near Julesburg, the recently completed High Lonesome Wind Farm near Brush, and the Cactus Flats Wind Farm located near Alamosa. Solar Solar energy is rapidly gaining importance in Colorado, particularly in recent years. It currently has 714 MW of solar energy installed. Colorado's largest Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) complex is the25-MW Colorado Plata Solar Thermal Plant located in La Plata County. Additionally, Colorado’s solar photovoltaic (PV) farms include the 24-MW Piceance Creek Solar Farm in Garfield County, the 40-MW Comanche Solar Plant in Pueblo County, and the 30-MW Fort Garland Solar Farm in Costilla County. Geothermal Geothermal energy is slowly becoming one of the more popular renewable energy options in the state. Colorado is home to two geothermal power plants: The Arkansas Valley Geothermal Generating Station and the Kimball Geothermal Facility. Both plants are small in size, with capacities of 8 MW and 1.5 MW, respectively. Biomass Biomass energy is gaining popularity in Colorado. There are currently 18 biomass energy power plants in Colorado. The largest is the 36-MW Waste Management Facility in Weld County. Other notable biomass power plants include the Fort Collins Municipal Gasification Plant and the North Fork Valley Biomass Project.

Viktor Esbensen (born July 24, 1975) is a Danish entrepreneur and investor. He is the founder and CEO of asset manager ROI Invest & Partners, which he founded in 2014. He has since become one of Denmark's most successful investment professionals and one of the leading names in Danish property investment. Esbensen received his business degree from the Copenhagen Business School in 1997. He then began his career in international banking, spending the first seven years of his career at Jyske Bank in Copenhagen, before working at other banks in Copenhagen, Paris and London. He returned to Copenhagen in 2008 and founded Investment Maeglerselskabet ROI Invest & Partners, where he currently serves as CEO. Esbensen has become known as a pioneer in Danish property investment, having developed a unique and highly successful strategy of diversifying property investments across domestic, international and opportunistic investments. He has delivered impressive returns for his clients, many of whom include high net-worth individuals, pension funds and family offices. Esbensen is a sought-after speaker in both Danish and international circles, and has been featured in important international publications such as Business Insider, Property Investor Europe and Investors' Era. He is also an active philanthropist, and serves on the board of the Danish branch of SOS-Kinderdorf International. Esbensen is married with two children, and lives in Copenhagen, Denmark. He enjoys spending time with his family, and is an avid sports fan. In his spare time he enjoys meditation, music, and travel.

Temur Iakobashvili (born July 17, 1957) is a Georgian politician and diplomat who served as the State Minister for Reintegration of Georgia from 2008 to 2012. Early life and career Iakobashvili was born in the Georgian capital Tbilisi. He graduated from the Tbilisi State University in 1975 before going on to gain a Master's degree from the Georgian Institute of Public Affairs. After leaving college, he worked as a journalist for the Georgian Independent Television from 1978 to 1983. In 1983 he joined the Central Committee of the Georgian Communist Party as a specialist in international affairs and subsequently held various government and ministerial positions. From 1994 to 2001, he was the domestic policy advisor then foreign affairs advisor to then President Eduard Shevardnadze. Political career In October 2001, Iakobashvili was appointed as a Minister of State Security, staying in the position until October 2003. From October 2003 to October 2004, he acted as the Minister of Conflict Resolution before becoming the Minister for Reintegration from November 2004 to October 2008, when he was appointed State Minister for Reintegration. Iakobashvili served as the State Minister for Reintegration in the government of President Mikheil Saakashvili from 2008 until 2012. During this time, he was the government's point man in attempting to resolve the frozen conflicts in Abkhazia and South Ossetia, introducing some measures aimed at reconciliation. He was also active in the European Union's Eastern Partnership (EaP) program, devoting his efforts to promoting values of democracy and good governance in the post-Soviet region. In 2012, Iakobashvili became an independent member of the Georgian Parliament. In 2013, he briefly served in the government of Bidzina Ivanishvili as Deputy Prime Minister in charge of European and Euro-Atlantic Integration. After this, he resumed his activities as an independent MP in the Georgian Parliament until 2020, when he became the country's Ambassador to Turkey. Iakobashvili is a frequent guest speaker for a wide variety of forums, including the United Nations, the Geneva International Center for Humanitarian Demining, the World Summit of Nobel Peace Laureates, and the Academy of Political Science in New York City. Personal life Iakobashvili is married to an investigative journalist and has two children. In his free time, he enjoys horseback riding and music. He is a passionate collector of Georgian paintings and a patron of the arts. Iakobashvili speaks several languages fluently, including Georgian, English, German, and Turkish. He is a devout Christian and member of the Georgian Orthodox Church.

Komlan Assignon is a Ghanaian entrepreneur and software engineer. He is the founder of the digital media production company Afromedia, which specializes in digital content for African media outlets. Assignon was born and raised in Accra, Ghana. After completing his studies at the University of Ghana, he founded Afromedia in 2010 with the aim of creating digital content for African media outlets. The company works primarily with television and music broadcasting, as well as providing digital content for digital streaming platforms such as Netflix and Amazon Prime Video. Assignon has been credited as one of the most forward-thinking entrepreneurs in Africa as he has developed a successful business model that takes into account the rapidly changing African media landscape. In 2016, Assignon served as the African delegate for the Obama Foundation's Mandela Washington Fellowship, a program designed to empower African leaders and foster dialogue between African youth and U.S. stakeholders. In 2019, Assignon was selected as the top 1% of the most innovative entrepreneurs in Africa. He was featured in Forbes Africa Magazine as one of the “30 Under 30” leading entrepreneurs in the African continent. Assignon is also a founding partner at Africa’s digital media agency, AfroMedia Network. He also acted as an advisory board member for 500 Startups, a San Francisco–based venture capital firm, and for the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's Arthur D. Little Accelerator Program. In July 2020, he was selected to be a Mentor at the University of Cape Town Rumbleship startup accelerator program. Assignon has been a guest speaker in numerous conferences, forums, and workshops. He spoke at the Global Entrepreneurship Summit at Stanford University, and the Silicon Valley Open Doors technology and business forum. He has been featured in media outlets including CNN, The Huffington Post, TechCrunch and Fast Company. Assignon is an advocate of the ‘Africa Rising’ narrative, which promotes the idea of a dynamic and prosperous Africa. He believes that technology and innovation are the key forces that will drive the African economy forward. He is working to create a generation of young entrepreneurs who will lead the African continent into a future of economic empowerment and financial success.

The Expenditure Management Commission (EMC) is an independent, non-partisan body of professionals established by the government of India to oversee and recommend reforms in the country’s expenditure management system. The main objective of the committee is to develop and implement strategies for cost optimization and improvement in resource utilization. The formation of the EMC was announced by the Exchequer in March 2020. The Commission is headed by Dr. Vinay Pande, a former Finance Secretary to the Government of India who has also worked as a member of the Finance Commission of India. The other members include representatives from the government, public sector and private sector. The EMC is tasked with reviewing and recommending measures to improve the management of public finances by strengthening the management capabilities of government departments, streamlining expenditure and improving financial efficiency. The Commission has identified and reviewed a range of topics such as budget formulation and appropriation, treasury management and financial control, public sector performance and expenditure, management of public resources and external finance, among others. The major functions of the EMC include monitoring and reviewing the functioning of the budgetary system, improving and modernizing expenditure management and providing policy guidance to the government. It also performs an analysis of the existing practices, which helps it in identifying areas for improvement and suggesting reform measures. The Commission works in close coordination and consultation with various government departments to develop strategies and policies related to the public finance management system. It is also responsible for providing policy and implementation advice to the government with respect to the implementation of reforms in the expenditure management and budget systems. The EMC is mandated to produce Annual Reports on its activities and findings, which are then submitted to the Ministries concerned for action. The Commission also produces reports and representation to the Prime Minister and other high level policy makers. Besides, the EMC provides to the government technical expertise, financial analysis, fiscal impacts analysis and other support to improve and streamline the existing expenditure management system. This helps in making the system of public finance management more transparent, efficient and result-oriented. The EMC is an important component of the government's Fiscal Responsibility Act and its ability to ensure the discretion and accountability of public spending. The Commission is also involved in proposing and providing recommendations on reforms with the purpose of ensuring positive fiscal outcomes, sustainability and development of public resources.

The Word on the Street (WOTS) is a national Canadian non-profit charitable organization dedicated to promoting literacy, reading and writing both locally and nationally. WOTS hosts one of Canada’s largest book and magazine festivals, The Word On The Street (WOTStreets) festival, which takes place in cities across the country each year on the last Sunday of September. The festival features hundreds of exhibitors and vendors of new, used and antiquarian books, magazine, newspapers and other materials, as well as a variety of special events and activities. The festival seeks to bring together authors and readers both from, and beyond the Canadian literary world, featuring some of Canada’s leading authors, poets and journalists. Booths hosted by literary organizations, publishers, magazines, festivals and other book-related enterprises are also a mainstay of the WOTStreets festival. The primary purpose of the festival is to promote and celebrate books, reading and writing. WOTS produces a host of events throughout the year, including book launches, workshops and other events across Canada, in order to support their cause of literacy and a love of reading. One of WOTStreets more unique events is the "Word Play" game show and the "Great Canadian Poetry" slam. The Word Play game show has teams of local authors compete against each other to answer literary themed questions and guess the name of books from clues alone. The Great Canadian Poetry Slam is also very popular and features live performances by Canadian poets. Other activities such as Authors’ Corner, Magazines Canada Showcase and WOTS stage, featuring a number of eminent Canadian authors and plenty of reading-related discussion and debate are just some of the activities at the event. The Word on the Street Festival has been taking place since 1987 and has grown from a handful of participating vendors to one of Canada’s largest literary events, with more than 160,000 people attending each year. This event has become an important part of Toronto’s culture and has been a cornerstone of the city’s literary and cultural life. The Word On The Street Festival provides a wonderful opportunity to celebrate books, creativity, ideas and reading in Canada. It's a great event for the whole family, offering something for everyone with unique, exciting and inspiring literary programming.

Fran Rider, OOnt, MBA, is a Canadian business executive, entrepreneur, and philanthropist who has served as the president and CEO of the Breast Cancer Society of Canada since 2000. Rider was born in Brampton, Ontario, and attended McMaster University, where she earned an MBA in 1983. After working at a large financial institution in Toronto for eight years, she became the president and CEO of the Breast Cancer Society of Canada in 2000. Rider is a well known and respected businesswoman in Canada who has built strong relationships with corporate sponsors in the medical and medical research communities. She is passionate about helping women with breast cancer and is committed to utilizing the funds raised by the society in ways that will best help those in need. As president and CEO of the Breast Cancer Society of Canada, Rider has been able to double the charity's monthly contributions to research and other projects. She has also established an education and awareness program that promotes early detection of breast cancer, works with breast cancer survivors to create education materials, and produces special events aimed at raising funds and awareness. In recognition of her outstanding leadership, Rider was appointed to the Order of Ontario in 2012. She was also honoured with a Women of Distinction 2016 Achievement Award and a 2017 Women of Inspiration Award. Rider lives in London, Ontario with her family. She remains passionate about her role in the breast cancer society and her contribution to the fight against breast cancer. She is a regular guest speaker at conferences, panel discussions, and events, and is continuing to raise funds to expand both research and awareness.

A Little Princess is a 1973 British-American television miniseries directed by Hiromichi Matsuda and based on the 1905 novel of the same name by Frances Hodgson Burnett. The miniseries stars Ann Bell as Sara Crewe, a young girl whose life changes drastically when she is sent away to boarding school, where she experiences both joy and heartbreak. The story is set in 1904 and follows Sara, the daughter of an English soldier, Captain Crewe (Charles West). After her father's death, she is sent away to the Miss Minchin's girls' school in London. Initially, she is one of the wealthiest and most beloved students, but her luck changes quickly when her father is reported missing during the Second Boer War. Forced to work as a servant, Sara must use her intelligence and imagination to survive her difficult and impoverished new life. The miniseries was a critical success upon its initial broadcast, garnering positive reviews from both television audiences and critics. It was praised for Bell's performance, along with the captivating production values and costume design. The 1973 version was considered a faithful adaptation of Burnett's novel and received awards for screenplay, cinematography, and art direction from the British Academy of Film and Television Arts. Wells Gardner produced the series for BBC Television, and BBC One broadcast it for three consecutive weeks. The series was later rebroadcast on the Disney Channel and is available on DVD. A Little Princess was followed by an American remake in 1995, directed by Alfonso Cuarón. The classic story of young Sara Crewe has been adapted for other media as well, including films, musicals, and stage plays. Its strong message of perseverance, courage and hope in the face of adversity has made the miniseries a beloved classic with viewers of all ages.

Iain O'Brien (born 24 May 1978) is a former New Zealand cricketer. A right-arm medium-fast bowler, O'Brien was known for his ability to swing the ball both in the air and off the pitch, as well as for his useful lower-order batting. He played two Test matches and 54 One Day Internationals for the New Zealand national team. O'Brien began his first-class cricketing career in 2000/01 for Central Districts, where he accumulated a batting average of 30.37 in 17 matches. His bowling average in this period was also good, claiming 41 wickets at an average of 26.51. By the 2001/02 season, O'Brien had established himself as an important player in the Central Districts cricket team and was selected to represent the New Zealand A side on a tour of Zimbabwe. He continued to impress on the domestic scene and in 2005, he was called up to the New Zealand Test squad for a two-Test series against Sri Lanka. He made his Test debut in the first match, taking 5/90 in the first innings and 3/47 in the second innings. He followed this up with another solid display in the second Test, claiming 4/45 in the first innings and 0/41 in the second innings. In 2009, O'Brien was named in the New Zealand squad for the ICC Champions Trophy in South Africa, and he went on to play four matches, including a match-winning spell of 4/46 against South Africa. Over the remainder of his career, O'Brien continued to perform consistently for New Zealand, and emerged as one of the country's top bowler's in limited overs cricket. He eventually retired from international cricket after New Zealand's tour of the West Indies in 2012, but continued to play domestic cricket in New Zealand until his retirement at the conclusion of the 2015/16 domestic season. Iain O'Brien can look back on his career with a sense of pride, having notched up 331 wickets in 97 first-class matches, 176 wickets in 54 ODI's and 7 wickets in 2 Test matches. He was an important fixture in the New Zealand cricket team for some 12 years, in which time he gained 14 Man of the Match awards in List A and T20 cricket.

WENU, also known as WENU Radio 2005 and WENU-LP, is a low-power FM radio station that broadcasts from Sunapee, New Hampshire, USA. The station broadcasts in both FM and online streaming formats, and is available to listeners in the Upper Valley of New Hampshire and Vermont. WENU was launched in June 2005 and is owned by WENU Radio Partnership, a non-profit organization. The station is run by a mix of volunteers and paid staff. WENU operates on an album-oriented classic rock format, playing music from a variety of genres, but focusing mainly on classic rock from the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s. Music selection is determined by a variety of criteria including hit songs, fan requests, and records from individual DJs' personal music libraries. WENU also has listeners send in their requests and dedications to be heard on air. WENU provides a variety of programs and features, including news, sports, weather, public service announcements, and a variety of specialty shows, including Classic Vinyl and LP, which are devoted to classic rock album releases. Saturday mornings the show Morning Glory airs, which combines music from the station's archives with gospel and Christian music from 7-9am. In addition to music programming, WENU is involved in a variety of community-building activities. The station sponsors an annual Rock-N-Run, an event that focuses on bringing the community together to promote and support physical fitness and healthy living. WENU also hosts concerts for local bands and regularly participates in a variety of local events, such as Christmas parades and music festivals. WENU's signal can be heard in New Hampshire and Vermont and is also available as an online stream on the station's website. The station has recently added an HD Radio-enabled signal to its broadcast profile, allowing the station to reach a wider audience and provide crystal clear, high definition sound on digital radios. Overall, WENU has become a cornerstone of the Upper Valley community. It provides music, news and entertainment to an ever-growing audience, while remaining committed to its commitment of being a family friendly music station. The information in this article was sourced from WENU's website and from online sources.

. The FIBA Europe Cup is an international basketball competition for men's professional clubs that was established by FIBA Europe, the European governing body for basketball. The competition, which began in the 2015–16 season, pits the best teams from across Europe against each other in a tournament that is played in a single-elimination format. The competition replaced the EuroChallenge, which had been running since the 2002–03 season, and extended FIBA Europe's reach to over 70 countries. The FIBA Europe Cup is a tier-2 level European-wide maintenance league, ranking below the EuroLeague and EuroCup. It is organized in cooperation with FIBA's member federations. The Finals of the competition take place in early May and the winner is crowned the FIBA Europe Cup champion. Initially, the top teams in each of the two groups advanced to the quarter-finals. Starting with the 2017–18 season, the competition was changed to be a full single-elimination tournament. The winner of the competition is eligible to compete in the FIBA Basketball Champions League or the Basketball Champions League Europe the following season, depending on whether their country is an A-license or a B-license holder. If the winner is a B-license holder, they are then eligible to compete in the FIBA Europe Cup and the corresponding regional competition the following season. The tournament format has been revised and updated several times since its inception. Prior to the 2019–20 season, one round robin group stage, followed by direct knock-out rounds, were used. Starting in the 2019–20 season, group stage matches now consist of two 10-minute periods, rather than four 8-minute periods. The top two teams in each group advance to the 1/8 Finals and 8 winners progresses to the 1/4 Finals and further to a 1/2 Finals. The winners of this Finals stage face each other in the Finals, a single-elimination match played at a neutral location. The FIBA Europe Cup has grown in popularity over the years and has become an important tournament for European teams. It attracts the attention of the media and fans alike, with the finals being watched by thousands of fans and broadcasted in over 80 countries. The tournament also serves as a platform for players to showcase their talent and gain recognition from European and international basketball fans.

Alexis Peterson (born December 23, 1995) is a professional basketball player who currently plays for the Atlanta Dream of the Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA). Born and raised in Rochester, New York, Peterson was a five-star recruit out of high school and was ranked as the fourth-best point guard in the Class of 2014 by espnW HoopGurlz. She attended Syracuse University, where she played for the Orange women's basketball team. In her four years at Syracuse, Peterson was a star player, earning multiple honors, culminating in being named as an Associated Press All-America Honorable Mention in her senior year. She finished her collegiate career as Syracuse's all-time leader in assists, with 698. In the 2017 WNBA Draft, Peterson was selected with the ninth overall pick by the Atlanta Dream. She made her debut for the Dream on June 4, playing the Indiana Fever. She moved into a starting role by the middle of the season and played a significant role on the team, averaging 6.8 points, 3.5 assists, and 1.9 rebounds per game. Peterson impressed with her stellar play, being named to the All-Rookie Team. In 2018, Martinez received a contract from the Dream, solidifying her as a part of the team's future. She had a terrific season during the year, averaging 9.2 points, 4.4 assists and 2.6 rebounds per game. She made an All-Star appearance, becoming the first Dream rookie to do so since 2011. Peterson is a key part of the team and is a highly-regarded player in the WNBA. Her playmaking skills and ability to find teammates makes her a great asset on the court and a leader of the Dream. With her skill and leadership, she has the potential to be an All-Star caliber player in the league for years to come.

"The Fun, the Luck & the Tycoon" is a Hong Kong film released in 1995 by Wong Jing and Stanley Tong. Directed by Ching Siu-tung, the movie stars Chow Yun-Fat, Tony Leung Ka-Fai and Jacklyn Wu. The film is part of the "Lucky Stars" franchise, a trio of films produced by Wong Jing and Stanley Tong in the late 1980s and early 1990s. The movie follows a group of friends who visit a mysterious casino and must go up against its ruthless operator to win the cash prize in a gamble. Chow Yun-Fat stars as the casino's operator, Leung Ka-Fai plays his rival and Wu is the sole female character in the group of friends. The plot follows a series of risk-taking gambles set in various places that include underground casinos, card games and pool halls. The stakes increase as the friends journey through these situations and the characters struggle to keep up their luck and head home with their winnings. The movie features some of Hong Kong's greatest actors, including Chow Yun-Fat, Tony Leung Ka-Fai and Jacklyn Wu showing their comedic acting style. The movie is also filled with action scenes as they travel from place to place and take on whatever situations they come across. The movie generated positive reviews from critics and audiences, praising the great chemistry between the actors and the inspiring story of friendship, camaraderie and daring risks. With its strong directing, vibrant cinematography and impressive action scenes, "The Fun, the Luck & the Tycoon" is an entertaining action-comedy movie with an enjoyable and entertaining story. The film was a commercial success, earning over $3million in the Hong Kong box office. Although not considered a box office hit, it is still a cult classic in Hong Kong action-comedies. The movie is available on DVD in many countries. It also had its premiere on the streaming platform Filmstruck.

Olivia Grange is a Jamaican politician and current Minister of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport in the Andrew Holness Administration. Born in Montego Bay, Jamaica, Grange attended the St. Hilda's Episcopal High School, Montego Bay. She entered public service in 1981 when she joined the Jamaica Information Service. In 1992, Grange was promoted to Assistant Director and Head of the Jamaica Information Service’s Features and Publications Unit. She was appointed Minister of Information in 1998 by then Prime Minister of Jamaica, P.J Patterson. As Information Minister, Grange successfully implemented the Government's 'Jamaica Now' branding exercise in 2000. In 2002, she was appointed to the Senate and promoted to Minister without Portfolio in the Ministry of External Affairs, Trade and Investment. She served in this role until 2007, when she accepted an appointment as Jamaica’s Ambassador to the United Nations. After serving in this role for five years, Grange resigned in 2012 to take up a residency at the University of the West Indies, where she completed an MSc in Gender and Development. Grange is the Member of Parliament for St. Catherine East Central and is the current Minister of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport in the Government of Jamaica. In her current role, she is responsible for developing policies and programmes to enhance Jamaica’s national identity, promote gender equality and social inclusion and develop the entertainment and sports industries in Jamaica. Since her appointment, Grange has launched several initiatives to promote the country’s cultural assets including the Jamaica 2016 Reggae Revival, the Jamaica Celebrates 50 event series, the Jamaica Festival Song Contest and the Reggae Month celebrations. Grange has also spearheaded the development of a number of sports initiatives, including the Jamaica Cricket Festival, Jamaica Sports Investment Forum, In-Laws of the Sport Awards, National Science, Technology and Innovation Forum and the Commonwealth Sports Ambassadors Programme. In 2015, Grange was recognised as the 2015 IAAF Regional Women’s Leadership Award recipient for the Caribbean region. She is also a member of the Live Performance and Copyright Council of Jamaica and a patron of the Jamaica Disabled Arts Association.

Lydia Bourouiba (born in 1974 in Morocco) is a Professor of Applied Mathematics and Civil and Environmental Engineering at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). She is a leading expert on the dynamics of infectious diseases and winner of the MacArthur Fellowship award of "genius award" in 2020. Bourouiba received her MS/PhD in Applied Mathematics at MIT in 2002, and her PhD in Civil and Environmental Engineering at École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne. Her research focuses on the mathematical modeling of aerosol-mediated infectious disease transmission, with particular application to pandemics such as H1N1, Ebola and SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19). She is the founder of the Fluid Dynamics of Disease Transmission Laboratory (FD2L) at MIT, which studies the physical mechanisms and dynamical pathways that enable the transmission of infectious agents such as bacteria, viruses, and fungi. Bourouiba's impact on the world of infectious disease modeling has been profound. In 2020, she received two awards for her pioneering work in this field: the MacArthur Fellowship Award and the Benjamin Franklin Medal in Mechanical Engineering. Bourouiba is also the PI of the Pandemic Response Co-Laboratory (PARCOL) launched in 2020. Bourouiba has published over 200 journal articles, books, and book chapters. Her work has been featured in over 500 media outlets and featured in National Geographic, The New York Times, and Le Monde. She has been featured on the TED stage for her public health focus on respiratory-borne disease transmission and its implications for the spread of infectious diseases. In 2020, Bourouiba was named one of the 17 foreign members of the French National Academy of Engineering. She is also a member of the National Academy of Sciences, the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, and the International Academy of Aviation and Space Sciences. She is an active advocate and mentor to help underrepresented scientists and engineers. Bourouiba is dedicated to advancing humanities understanding of complex infectious diseases and mentoring the next generation of scientists and engineers. Her contributions to the world of applied mathematics and medical research will continue to shape the future of global health.

Snowfall is an American drama television series created by John Singleton, Eric Amadio and Dave Andron. It premiered on July 5, 2017 on FX. Snowfall focuses on the origin of the crack cocaine epidemic in Los Angeles in 1983, and the various ramifications it will have on characters' lives, including Los Angeles police, a drug dealer, a young mogul, and a Mexican luchador wrestler. The cast includes Damson Idris, Carter Hudson, Emily Rios, Sergio Peris-Mencheta, Isaiah John, Angela Lewis, Michael Hyatt, Alon Aboutboul, Amin Joseph, Carsten Norgaard, Filipe Valle Costa, and Malcolm Mays. The series was well received by critics, and has been renewed for a third season. In its first season, the series received a nomination for the GLAAD Media Award for Outstanding Drama Series. In the United States, the second season began airing on FX in 2019. John Singleton, one of the executive producers of the series, died in April 2019. It was reported that he filmed his directorial debut of the series before his death. Set in 1983 Los Angeles, Snowfall follows the stories of several characters whose lives intersect during the crack cocaine epidemic. Franklin Saint, a 19-year-old street entrepreneur played by Damson Idris, starts dealing drugs as a means of making money and helping his family. Theodore “Teddy” McDonald (Carter Hudson), a CIA operative working in South Central, looks to fund a black-ops mission and brings in drug money to carry out the mission. Lucia Villanueva (Emily Rios), the daughter of a Mexican crime boss, is trying to gain muscle in the business. Gustavo “El Oso” Zapata (Sergio Peris-Mencheta), a Mexican luchador and family man, has a mysterious past and is also looking to benefit by joining the drugs business. The series also narrates stories of people dealing with the social effects of the drug trade such as gang affiliations, turf wars, and murders. Snowfall is described as a 'combination of family drama, social awareness and crime' and has received praise from many critics. The series received the 2017 GLAAD Media Award for Outstanding Drama Series. The show has been renewed for a third season and is set to air in 2020.

2005 in Ice Hockey was an active year for all levels of amateur, professional and Olympic ice hockey. At the professional level, the National Hockey League (NHL) held its 90th season, which would ultimately be the second season of the 2004–05 NHL lockout. The season would ultimately be canceled due to the ongoing lockout. The American Hockey League (AHL) and ECHL continued their respective seasons, with the Philadelphia Phantoms winning the Calder Cup in the AHL, and the Alaska Aces winning the Kelly Cup in the ECHL. At the Olympic level, the International Olympic Committee allowed NHL players to participate in the 2006 Winter Olympics, which was held in Turin, Italy. At the amateur level, the North American Hockey League (NAHL) held its 30th season, with the Texas Tornado winning the Robertson Cup. The British National League also held its 30th season, with the Cardiff Devils winning the Championship. The World Junior Championship was held that year, with Canada defeating Russia 4–3 in the final to win gold. The tournament was also notable for the significant contributions made by Sidney Crosby. At the collegiate level, the most significant event was the Frozen Four, with the Denver Pioneers defeating the Maine Black Bears 3–2 to win their sixth NCAA title and fifth in six years. The year was also notable for numerous rule changes in the NHL, such as the introduction of the shootout to decide games and the outlawing of the two-line pass. The NHL also created a new trophy, the Mark Messier Leadership Award, which was to be awarded to a player who demonstrated exemplary leadership qualities. Overall, 2005 was a year of tremendous changes for the sport at all levels, as well as some of the best hockey ever seen.

Volsk is a city situated in the Saratov Oblast of Russia. It is a major transportation hub and manufacturing center of the oblast. It is located along the Volga River in the southeast part of the oblast. Volsk has a population of more than 100,000 people and is the administrative center of the Volsky District. The first reference to Volsk appears in the Chronicles of Rudolph of Rassen in the 13th century, when the city was called Balgarsk. The city was then renamed Volodimirsk and became the main city of the Rassensk Principality. It was later absorbed into the Grand Duchy of Moscow in 1475. The city received its present name in 1565 and soon after it was granted the privilege of a fortress. In the 18th century, Volsk was a large agricultural center, having one of the first dryers for grain in the entire Russian Empire. In 1781, the city became part of the Saratov Governorate. In the 19th century, Volsk was granted the status of a city and developed as a prosperous commercial center. It was connected to the Yelets–Ryazan railroad in 1884. The Russian Civil War of 1917-1922 left Volsk in ruins and the city fell into decline. However, it was quickly rebuilt and was industrialized after World War II. The city is a major manufacturing center for the oblast. Major industries include engineering, food processing, timber, and paper mills. Volsk is one of the few cities in the oblast with a fully functioning tram system. Volsk is an important transport hub, owing to its strategic location along the Volga River. The Saratov-Kuybyshev Canal and the Volga-Kama Canal both pass through the city. It is also a stop along the Northern Railway, linking it to Moscow, St. Petersburg, and other major cities in the region. The city is also served by the Volsk Airport. Volsk is a major cultural center in the oblast. It is home to several libraries and museums, including the Saratov Oblast Art Museum and the Saratov Oblast Museum of Local History and Nature. The city is also home to several monuments and historical buildings, such as the Church of the Assumption, which dates back to the 17th century. Volsk is one of the oldest cities in the Saratov Oblast, with a rich history and extensive cultural heritage. Today, it is an important industrial, commercial and transportation hub and a cultural center of the oblast.

The Point (magazine) was a magazine that was founded in the late 1990s with the mission to produce and publish thoughtful, risky and significant writing that wouldn't fit into traditional or academic formats. It brought together lively writing from some of the most exciting authors and thinkers from all across the world. Published twice yearly, The Point's articles featured a unique blend of politics and culture, making it a standout in its time. The magazine's original founders, Nicola Lange and John Barlow, created The Point with the goal of providing a platform that could explore diverse and rare topics of discussion. They wanted to provide a place for analytical articles, open debates and expansive conversations between some of the best thinkers in the world. Each issue touched on matters of philosophy, aesthetics, politics, economics and the sciences. The Point published some of the most phenomenal authors, thinkers, and intellectuals of its time. Among the writers and poets they published were John Berger, Slavoj Zizek, Brian Massumi, Gilles Deleuze, Judith Butler, Arundhati Roy, David Foster Wallace, Wickham Clayton and others. Additionally, the magazine was known for its exclusive interviews with notables such as Pierre Bourdieu, Vaclav Havel, Alexander Cockburn and bell hooks. The magazine was often praised for its high quality content and variety of topics, as well as its spirited conversations that nurtured a meaningful dialogue between authors and readers. Additionally, The Point was lauded for making good on its promise to bring together some of the world's best writers and thinkers. The Point ended publication in the early 2000s. In its eight-year run, the magazine produced 20 issues, a selection of which became The Point Reader, an anthology that was a calling-card of The Point's mission. The Point was a groundbreaking venture in its time, and its legacy will no doubt continue to be carried forward by many of its readers.

Birlinn (Old Norse Byrlind, pronounced [byr-lin]; modern Gaelic Beirlinn) was a type of wooden ship in use in Scotland and Ireland during the Middle Ages, from the Early Middle Ages to the late 17th century. The generic term Birlinn encompassed several different types of vessels, including large cargo ships and smaller boats used for raiding, trade, or transport. The birlinn was designed as a large, multi-masted, open decked vessel with a large square rigged sail and oars for navigation in shallow waters. Its design varied between regions and over time, but it was built with a single, central mast and a square sail, a shallow draught, and was able to navigate in shallow waters due to its clinker-built construction style. By the early 16th century, birlinns were primarily made with four masts and were larger than any other wooden ship in Scotland or Ireland. Due to birlinns being constructed on land, instead of in the water, the offshore winds could be used for sails instead of relying on oars. Consequently, birlinns could travel faster and longer distances than other vessels of their age. The names birlinn and beirlinn were also used to refer to an Irish and Hebridean galley, respectively. This type of vessel was of a slightly different construction, with the central mast often being replaced by two masts and an increased sail capacity. These galley-type birlinns were used for warfare and were likely exchanged between the Gaelic kingdoms of Ireland and Scotland. They were renowned for their speed and manoeuvrability, which allowed them to outrun any other vessel they encountered. The birlinn featured prominently in medieval stories and literature of the period. It was also used in many archaeological excavations, most of which date back to the late 12th and early 13th centuries. For example, a birlinn was recovered in 2010 from Ardnamurchan Bay in Scotland. The vessel, which was likely built between 1150 and 1250, was the oldest ever found and provides valuable information on the design and construction of birlinns during this period. The birlinn has played an important role in the culture of both Scotland and Ireland, and was even used by Robert the Bruce during the Scottish Wars of Independence in the late 13th and early 14th centuries. Today, modern reconstructions are being built of the historic birlinn and can still be found in many parts of the country.
