Inevitably both sisters were flanked in this well-documented struggle with the British in Travancore. Though the two were born into royalty, their lives were filled with tumultuous episodes that entailed their negotiation and survival skills pushed them to battle odds such as the claim of Sree Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma to the throne of Travancore, as well as the imposition of changes to the succession laws which in effect posed to disenfranchise them. Maharani Sethu Lakshmi Bayi’s many contributions to her kingdom and her people are remembered to this day. Sethu Lakshmi Bayi had the distinction of being the first female Dewan of Travancore and had the courage to restore public order. Maharani played a significant role in the social, economic and educational reforms in Travancore state. Its status in terms of literacy rose from 19.4% to 34.4% under her reign. Some of her notable works were the modernization of irrigation systems and the amendment of the temple entry proclamation of 1936 which allowed the admission of the low caste people into temple precincts. Maharani Sethu Parvathi Bayi was a noted scholar, writer and philanthropist. She authored several books, including Kavyabhooshanam (1943), Sthree Sahitya (1943), Sthreemahima (1954, Kannyarkavacham (1963). In the realm of her philanthropic activities, she had established various educational institutions, an Ayurveda hospital and a home for the mentally challenged. The Travancore sisters remain an inspiration for all as they laid the groundwork for the progress of their kingdom and its people. Their struggle for identity is an inspiring story, reminding us that courage and determination can lead to success.

The Haas VF-18 is an sixth-generation Formula One racing car designed and constructed by the Haas F1 Team to race in the 2018 FIA Formula One World Championship. It is the first Haas car to be powered by a Ferrari engine and the first to have titanium components. It was unveiled online on February 5, 2018, and made its track debut during pre-season testing on February 26-March 1. It is driven by drivers Romain Grosjean and Kevin Magnussen, both of whom are returning to the team for a third consecutive year. The team finished eighth in the Constructors' standings, achieving its best ever result in Formula One. The car's chassis is designated the VF-18 and is similar to its predecessor, the VF-17. It was designed by a team of engineers led by technical director Guenther Steiner and chief designer Rob Taylor. Steiner commented in the car's launch statement that the engineers aimed to improve its balance and mechanical grip to increase the driver's confidence. Under the regulations, the VF-18 had to comply with the minimum weight of 728 kg, including the driver, fuel and lubricants, for the season. It was designed to accommodate the introducing of halo head protection device as well as Pirelli's wider tyres for the season. Its suspension setup consists of push-rod activation with rockers. The VF-18 is powered by a Ferrari 062 power unit which is mated to an uprated version of the seven-speed SS357 semi-automatic transmission used by the previous car. It is reported to generate over 900 bhp in qualifying and around 850 bhp in races. The car achieved a podium finish in its first race, with Grosjean finishing third in the 2018 Australian Grand Prix on March 25. They continued to score points throughout the season, with a total of 93 points that earned them eighth in the Constructors' standings. The team also achieved a fastest lap, with Grosjean in the Belgian Grand Prix. The car has since been superseded by the VF-19. References: 1) "Haas F1 Team launches VF-18". Haas F1 Team. February 5, 2018. 2) "The technical secrets of the Haas VF-18". Motorsport.com. February 9, 2018. 3) "Haas VF-18". F1Metrics. February 9, 2018.

Soluble transferrin receptor (sTfR) is a glycoprotein expressed on the surface of erythroid precursors and is related to the human protein transferrin receptor. It acts as an iron-uptake receptor to the cell surface and is used as a marker of erythropoiesis in medical diagnosis. The sTfR gene is located on chromosome 3p25.1-25.2 and has four exons. The full length mRNA contains 1585 nucleotides, which can produce a protein of 353 amino acids with a molecular weight of 39.477 kDa. sTfR shares structural homology with several other cellular receptors including scavenger receptor, major histocompatibility complex class II receptors, cell adhesion molecules and desialylated transferrin receptor. sTfR is primarily expressed in erythroid precursors, though low expression has been detected in hepatocytes, myeloid defined precursors, thymocytes and monocytes. sTfR plays an important role in erythropoiesis by facilitating iron uptake into developing erythrocytes and ensuring the proper development of adequate erythroid precursors. On the cellular surface, sTfR exists in two forms: a membrane-bound form and a soluble form. The soluble form is generated by shedding of membrane-bound sTfR by the action of metalloproteases. The importance of soluble sTfR has been established in recent years since it is more specific and more reliable as a marker of erythropoiesis, due to its independence from changes in erythroid precursors. The level of sTfR in the body can be measured in the serum or plasma of a patient. In healthy individuals, sTfR levels are low, usually between 0.4-1.25 mg/L. However, in cases of anemia, sTfR levels can be significantly higher or lower depending on the underlying cause. In conditions such as iron deficiency anemia, sTfR is generally found to be higher than normal, while in other conditions such as thalassemia, sTfR is usually found to be lower than normal. In addition, soluble transferrin receptor has been used in diagnosis of certain diseases such as sickle cell anemia, hemoglobinopathies, and in monitoring response to therapy in thalassemia patients. The use of sTfR as a biomarker is particularly useful in diagnosing deficiencies and in assessing the severity of anemia. Overall, sTfR is an important biomarker that helps medical specialists in the diagnosis and monitoring of various anemias, as well as the response to treatment. References: 1. Mahmood, S. and Ahmad, Z. (2009). Soluble transferrin receptor: an indicator of erythropoiesis. Trends in Hematology, 8 (3), 59-66. 2. Maniou, E., Wilson, A. and Marsden, H. (2003). Role of the soluble transferrin receptor in iron homeostasis. Blood Cells, Molecules and Diseases, 30 (3), 284-297. 3. Silva, A., Engström, L. and Mori, M. (2017). Soluble Transferrin Receptor: an Emerging Biomarker in Diagnosing Anemia and Other Iron-Related Disorders. International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 18 (7), 1560.

William Guy (August 28, 1975 - present) is an American entrepreneur and small business owner who gained notoriety in the early 2000s for founding PipeDreams, an online marketplace for musical instruments. He was born and raised in Reno, Nevada, and was a child prodigy from a young age. He attended Sierra Sky High School, where he excelled in music and art classes, and was particularly proficient in playing multiple instruments including the drums and piano. After high school, William attended the University of Nevada, Reno and studied computer science, where he was part of an extracurricular program aimed towards developing new computer software. This program allowed William to hone his coding skills and develop a knack for computer engineering. In 2000, William dropped out of college and began working on a revolutionary website for music enthusiasts. He wanted to create a trusted website for music lovers to find and purchase instruments from verified sellers. Thus, in 2002, William launched PipeDreams, an online marketplace for buying and selling high-quality instruments. The website saw wild success and in its first year alone generated close to $6 million in sales. Thanks to this success, William was able to receive investments from large venture capital firms and invest heavily in the business. In 2009, William launched PipeDreams 2.0, an improved version of the website with more features, such as improved customer service and additional payment options. He upgraded the platform, in order to stay current with the competition and remain relevant within the industry. William remains the executive chairman of the company and has supported many charitable organizations, such as Music for a Mission, an initiative aimed at providing music instruments to those in need. William currently resides in Nevada and continues to expand the reach of PipeDreams. He has graduated from college and received an honorary diploma from the university in 2014. He also holds a patent for an automated order fulfillment system.

Zu was an ancient Sumerian thunder god, as well as the god of weather, sky, and storms. He was often depicted holding a double edged axe and a bow, identifying him as a warrior god. He was associated with Erra, Ishum, and Adad. In addition, Zu was also sometimes given the epithet “king of the mountains”, implying that he controlled the power of the mountains. Some of Zu's primary roles were to protect the gods in their palaces and bestow rain upon the city of Nippur so that the land could be fertile and productive. During the Sumerian epic known as The Lament for Ur, Zu was condemned for stealing the Tablet of Destiny from the gods, resulting in them losing control of humankind. In Sumerian mythology, Zu was a powerful figure. He was known as the king of the birds and the protector of the divine kingship. He was sometimes considered to be the messenger of the gods, responsible for delivering the decrees of the gods to mankind. In some stories, Zu was said to have had a magical weapon, called the zicar, which was said to have the power to strike down evil at the behest of the gods. Zu was also said to have had divine attributes and powers, such as being able to raise up armies, grant oracles and be an avenger of the gods. He was described as a furious god, often unleashing great storms upon mankind. Some ancient religions also attributed creation and destruction to his power, suggesting that he was a powerful force for balance and justice. In art, Zu was often depicted alongside goddess Inanna, denoting their shared roles as warriors and leaders. He was occasionally depicted with the wings of a storm bird and the head of a lion. This form was used to illustrate his apocalyptic powers. As a cultural figure, Zu was a source of veneration and celebration in Sumerian culture. He was sometimes considered the enemy of Marduk, the chief god of Babylon. In some stories, he is cursed by Anu, the chief god of the Sumerian pantheon, for stealing the Tablet of Destiny and causing the Sumerian gods an immense amount of grief. Zu is often seen in modern media, particularly in popular fantasy works. He is sometimes depicted as a powerful figure or deity and is seen as an emblem of storm, chaos and destruction. Zu's image has become iconic among some fantasy fans, and his legacy continues to inspire wars and popular literature to this day.

Emma Chambers (born 24 December 1965, Doncaster, West Yorkshire, England) is a British actress, best known for the roles of Alice Tinker in the BBC sitcom The Vicar of Dibley, and Honey Thacker in the romantic comedy film Notting Hill. Chambers began her acting career in the late 1980s with small television roles and performances in theatre. Her breakthrough role came in 1994, when she was cast as Alice Tinker in the popular BBC sitcom The Vicar of Dibley, opposite Dawn French. During her time on the show, Chambers was nominated for the British Comedy Award for Best TV Comedy Actress in 1996 and 1997. In 1999, Chambers starred opposite Hugh Grant and Julia Roberts in the romantic comedy Notting Hill, as Hugh Grant's exasperated older sister and romantic confidante, Honey Thacker. Chambers' performance was critically acclaimed and she was nominated for an ALFS Award for Best Supporting Actress in a British Film. Chambers has appeared in numerous television and film roles, including in the drama series Bremner, Bird and Fortune, the film Stuart Little, and the mystery series Jane Wymark's Midsomer Murders. Her other television credits include roles in Absolutely Fabulous, Florence Nightingale and Jonathan Creek. In addition to her acting roles, Chambers has published two books: Wild West Ham: A Guide to Keeping Chickens and Ducks in Your Garden was released in 2010 and Growing Your Own Vegetables was released in 2011. In 2016, Chambers retired from acting to focus on her writing career and on her hobbies, including chicken keeping and vegetable gardening. Chambers is a self-styled 'soubrette', which is a French term for the secondary comic role, usually a giddy girl or flirtatious young woman. She received the nickname 'Gorgon of Grinning' from BBC Radio 4 presenter John Humphrys due to her distinctive and infectious laughter.

Monty Python's Flying Circus: Just the Words is the title of a box set of the Monty Python's Flying Circus sketch comedy television programme. It was released on 22 October 2012, on DVD, Blu-ray and online streaming services, and contains all four series of the show. Monty Python's Flying Circus was a British comedy troupe consisting of John Cleese, Graham Chapman, Terry Jones, Michael Palin, Eric Idle and Terry Gilliam, who wrote, acted in, and directed the show. From 1969–1974, the comedy show was a groundbreaking and influential series, with episodes airing on the BBC. The Just the Words set contains all 45 episodes of the show, together with more than 50 audio tracks of dialogues, sketches and songs. It was produced by Cleese, Jones and Palin in 2012, along with original series producer Ian MacNaughton, and was released to mark the show's 40th anniversary. The set contains unique material, such as alternate takes, ad-libbed lines, and performances which had been cut from the original broadcasts of the show, as well as a series of interviews with the surviving members, behind-the-scenes features, and montages of sketches. The release of the box set was met with much acclaim, with many critics hailing it as one of the greatest collections from the comedy genre. The Independent newspaper praised the set as "[the] funniest box set of all time". The Monty Python's Flying Circus: Just the Words box set remains a must-have for fans of the Monty Python comedy troupe, and stands as an enduring testament to their comedy genius. It is a collection of comedy skits, musical numbers and nonsequiturs that still manages to be fresh, funny and more relevant than ever, even after all these years.

8 Women is a 2002 French dark comedy musical film written and directed by François Ozon. The film is set in a 1950s country house in France, and is centered around the attempts of the all-female family to determine who killed the patriarch of the family. It features an ensemble cast, including Catherine Deneuve, Fanny Ardant, Isabelle Huppert, Emmanuelle Béart, Virginie Ledoyen, Firmine Richard, Danielle Darrieux, and Ludivine Sagnier. The plot revolves around the matriarch Gaby (Deneuve) and her seven daughters, Suzon (Ledoyen), Augustine (Richard), Pierrette (Darrieux), Catherine (Huppert), Louise (Ardant), and Danielle (Sagnier). After the sudden departure of their father Marcel (played by master of ceremony Jean-Pierre Lorit) and their maid Josephine (Dominique Lamure), they all gather at a family estate in the Bordeaux region of France on Christmas Eve. When Marcel's body is discovered in the middle of the night, the topic of discussion immediately shifts from who will inherit his estate to who might have killed him. Suspicion immediately falls on one of the women, as everyone in the house had a motive to commit the crime. In order to discover the truth, the women engage in all manner of activities, including bouts of physical and mental testing, heated exchanges, and the sharing and unveiling of dark family secrets. Under the watchful eye of Augustine the lawyer, each character performs a musical solo in an attempt to express their innocence or guilt. Through these performances, a hidden history of resentment, love, regret, and betrayal is revealed. As the mystery gradually unravels, so does the truth of exactly what happened that night. Overall, 8 Women is a thought-provoking murder mystery set to the backdrop of a 1950s French country house. Its intricate plot and complex characters make it a stylishly crafted and entertaining film. It has been critically acclaimed for its hilarious comedy, sharp dialogue, and great soundtrack. The film was a rare box office success in France and has since gained a cult following for its dark humor.

Albert Schultens (21 July 1686 - 22 April 1750) was a Dutch Orientalist and theologian, noted for his critical editions of Arabic manuscripts. A native of Groningen, Netherlands, Schultens received his education at the Latin school of the University of Groningen before beginning his study of theology at Leiden University in 1705. Throughout his time at Leiden, Schultens took up the study of Arabic, Persian and Turkish to complement his knowledge of theology. After qualifying as a Doctor of Theology in 1714, Schultens moved to Italy, where he would further deepen his knowledge of languages and ancient manuscripts, including a two-year residence in Rome. Schultens went on to become a professor of ancient languages at Groningen University in 1721, where he was appointed rector in 1737. In 1722, Schultens accepted a position at the recently established University of Harderwijk, where he taught the oriental tongues. In 1743, Schultens returned to Leiden to teach Ancient Languages, a post which he held until his death in 1750. During his lifetime, Schultens wrote numerous books, essays, and commentaries on oriental languages and theological matters. His works include an edition of the Persian poet Hafez, a critical edition of the Koran, a Latin translation of Ali bin Sahl Rabban al-Tabari’s history, a Dutch translation of The Thousand and One Nights, and an Arabic-English dictionary. Schultens’ most notable achievement is his geographic survey of the Islamic world, Nova Descriptione Orbis Arabici. In addition to his contributions to oriental studies, Schultens held a deep interest in theology, making a number of contributions to the field, particularly with regard to Christian-Muslim relations. He is best known for his publications discussing the views of John Calvin on Islam, such as A Defence of John Calvin Against the Defamatory Rabbi at Damascus. Schultens’ works achieved a great deal of recognition in his lifetime, and were highly influential on later Orientalists, particularly Sir William Jones, who in 1784 praised Schultens’ accessible works on the Arabic and Persian language. Schultens’ ongoing legacy is recognized today in institutions such as the Albert Schultens Chair in Arabic and Islamic Studies at Groningen University.

Federico Perez Ponsa (April 11, 1970) is a prominent Argentine lawyer, businessman, and venture capitalist. He currently serves as the CEO of Partners Group, one of Argentina's leading private equity firms. As CEO, Perez Ponsa directs the company's Latin American expansion strategy and actively works to optimize investments for the firm's clients. Born in Mendoza, Argentina, Perez Ponsa began studying law at the University of Buenos Aires. After graduating with a degree in law, he pursued a Master’s degree in business administration from the same university. Upon completion, he entered the business world and quickly established himself as one of Argentina’s leading business minds. In 2004, Perez Ponsa was hired to serve as chairman of the board at a large Argentinian investment bank. As chairman, he helped to facilitate numerous large-scale loans and investments, such as purchasing a major retail chain in the country. Under his leadership, the company achieved a 25% growth rate within three years and nearly doubled its assets. In 2009, Perez Ponsa left the bank to join Partners Group, a private equity firm with global operations. Under Perez Ponsa’s direction, Partners Group has gone from a small firm with just a few partners to a global institution managing billions of dollars in investments. His strategies for optimizing investments have made the company a model for other firms in the industry. In addition to his work at Partners Group, Perez Ponsa is an active participant in the venture capital community. He has given numerous lectures on the subject and his writings have been published in various professional journals. He is currently a senior advisor to several venture capital firms in Argentina and serves as a board member on various corporate and charity boards throughout the country. Perez Ponsa’s accomplishments have been recognized by a number of organizations. He was chosen as one of the top 50 most influential people in the business world by Global Finance Magazine and was recently given the title of Top Businessman of the Year by the same publication. His success has inspired many aspiring entrepreneurs and business students in Argentina.

The Panamerican Esperanto Congress (also known as the Panamerican Esperanto-Congress or PAC) is an international conference held on a rotational basis in several countries within the Americas. It was founded in 1972 by the then-President of the Esperanto League for North America (ELNA) and other Esperanto activists in the Americas region. The first event was held in 1971 in the city of Monterrey in Mexico and the event has been held in several other cities including Washington D.C., San Diego, Toronto and Santiago, Chile. The event typically lasts for about a week and is convened by Esperanto-speaking representatives from participating Member States. Activities include educational events and workshops on topics related to the language and culture of Esperanto. Also, plenary sessions and awards ceremonies are common. Additionally, a culture fair is held where participants can showcase their own national cultural items. In addition to the actual conference, the Panamerican Esperanto Congress also serves as a forum for discussion and the promotion of Esperanto worldwide. Its objective is to establish more solid structures of collaboration and the exchange of ideas among Esperantists of the region, in order to facilitate the development of the language and its culture. With this purpose in mind, various topics and topics of research related to the language and its usage are discussed. The Panamerican Esperanto Congress allows for members to discuss important aspects related to the language and its usage and to collaborate for the promotion of Esperanto. It seeks to bring together Esperantists from all over the region and from different countries, to serve as a platform for the exchange of ideas and experiences. The event also seeks to ensure that Esperantists in the region and around the world can meet and interact on a regular basis and thus contribute to the development of the language and its culture worldwide. On a practical level, the Panamerican Esperanto Congress provides an opportunity for the Esperanto-speaking population of the Americas to interact, strengthen ties, and engage in activities related to the language. Finally, it serves as a platform for learning, building bridges and networking among different regions and countries in the region. The Panamerican Esperanto Congress (PAC) is an important event that has helped to strengthen and promote Esperanto in the Americas. It is an international conference held on a rotational basis in various cities of the region and is organized by the Esperanto League for North America (ELNA). The event seeks to promote Esperanto, establish collaboration and exchange of ideas among participants, and provide opportunities for learning, networking and building bridges across cultures.

MT Sitakund (also known as Masud Tingiwala Sitakund), is a medium-sized fishing trawler owned and operated by Sitakund Fisheries Private Limited, a Bangladeshi seafood processing and trading company. Sitakund Fisheries Private Limited was founded in 1984 and is licensed by the Government of Bangladesh to catch fish from the Bay of Bengal. The first vessel of the Sitakund Fisheries Private Limited was the MV Sitakund, which is a diesel driven trawler with a length of 56 metres, a width of 10 metres and a capacity of 500 metric tons of fish. In 2001, the company acquired the MT Sitakund, a much bigger vessel with a length of 80 metres and a capacity of 1,500 metric tons of fish. The vessel was designed and built by the renowned British shipbuilding firm of John I. Thornycroft & Company in 1964. The MT Sitakund is powered by two diesel engines of 400 horsepower each, supplied by the Albanian company Shkoder Diesel. The trawler can be seen in coastal and offshore waters of the Bay of Bengal catching fish in the depths ranging from 20 metres to 200 metres. It is equipped with advanced fishing equipment, such as underwater cameras and lights, which enables the crew to have a better view and understanding of the fish species in the deep sea. The trawler also has multiple power block winches and trawls, aiding the crew in their fishing expeditions. The vessel has an experienced and dedicated crew of 40 people, who are mainly fishermen from the coastal villages of Bangladesh. The crew consists of fishermen, engine men, technicians, deckhands, and navigation officers, all of who are highly experienced in their respective fields. The MT Sitakund is an important part of the fishing industry of Bangladesh, as it contributes significantly to the country’s fishing and seafood export industry. The trawler supplies fish and other seafoods to markets and customers around the world, furthering the economic all-round benefit of the nation. And with its efficient and reliable performance, the MT Sitakund is indeed an important symbol of the growing economic power of Bangladesh.

Tanikaze Kajinosuke was a professional sumo wrestler from Japan who competed in the professional sumo rankings in the Edo period. He was the 65th Yokozuna, the highest rank in sumo and a hereditary title. Kajinosuke was born in 1798 in Wakayama Prefecture and was known for his great stature and physical strength. He began his professional sumo career at the age of 14, and quickly rose through the ranks of the sport. In 1819, at the age of 21, he won the top division tournament, the grand sumo tournament, or "basho", becoming the youngest ever Yokozuna and the first ever Yokozuna to come from the Wakayama Prefecture. As Yokozuna, his career was very successful, and he won 13 out of the 18 tournaments he competed in. Kajinosuke's winning record was only surpassed by the legendary Yokozuna, Kitanoumi. Kajinosuke was the last of the Yokozuna to hold office and, as a result, was greatly respected by the people of Japan. In 1822, he was made Head of the Sumo Association and continued to lead the sport until his death in 1848. He played a big role in introducing sumo in Osaka and it became one of the most popular sports in the city. Kajinosuke's legacy lives on to this day, and he is still one of the most respected and renowned Yokozuna in the history of sumo. He is posthumously awarded the Order of the Sacred Treasure, the highest honor for sumo in Japan. He is credited for introducing the importance of honor and tradition in the sport, and for helping to elevate it to the level of physical sport and a form of entertainment. Kajinosuke's memory is celebrated at the Tanikaze Kajinosuke Memorial Hall in Wakayama, Japan. His statue is also displayed outside Tokyo's sumo arena.

Third Mind Records is an independent record label originally founded by Paul Oakenfold and Steve Osbourne in 1992 in London, England. The label was initially created to release the latest material by Oakenfold and Osbourne's music projects including Eternal, Electribe 101 and others. Since then, Third Mind has grown to release music from a diverse list of underground, electronic and dance music artists from around the world. The name 'Third Mind' was based on the philosophy of William Burroughs and Brion Gysin, who believed that the best works of art and writing were made when two different writers or musicians would overlap and, when done correctly, create a 'Third Mind.' This idea has been used to inform the label's aesthetic vision for all releases. Oakenfold and Osbourne have since gone on to become major players in the world of electronic music, but Third Mind Records has maintained its independent and underground mentality. With a consistent discography, Third Mind has always served as a platform for up-and-coming and established independent electronic music producers and DJs. The label has released music from dozens of major artists, including The Prodigy, Future Sound of London, Daft Punk and The Chemical Brothers, as well as many lesser-known artists. In 1998, Third Mind released the classic "Sadeness (Part 1)" by Enigma, which became an international hit. The label also released seminal albums from acts like Dave Clarke, Orbital and Slam. Third Mind Records has been instrumental in establishing and popularizing the United Kingdom's electronic music scene. With a wide range of genres, and often taking risks on unknown talent, the label has earned its place as one of the most respected and influential independent labels in the history of the music industry. In recent years the label has shifted its focus to more contemporary sounds such as minimal techno and tech house. Third Mind Records currently has an operation in London, as well as a number of major international DJs and producers on its roster.

The 42nd Parliament of British Columbia, otherwise known as the British Columbia Forty-Second Parliament of British Columbia, is the current legislature of the Province of British Columbia, Canada. It was elected on May 14, 2017, with the BC NDP led by John Horgan, becoming government for the first time since April-May 2001. The legislature will last for 4 year, until the next election in 2021. The BC Liberals will remain a strong opposition, and Andrew Weaver remains the leader of the Green Party. The formation of the legislature is unique due to BC being the only province in Canada with a minority government lead by the NDP. The Greens decided to support the NDP to form a confidence and supply agreement; meaning they will supply and guarantee the confidence of the legislature. This put Andrew Weaver and the Green Party in an anomalous position of holding the balance of power despite only having a single seat in the Legislative Assembly. The 42nd Parliament will place a strong focus on the environment and sustainable economic growth. Notable pieces of legislation include the CleanBC Plan designed to reduce emissions and greenhouse gasses, banning corporate, union and third-party contributions and an agreement between BC and Alberta to establish a local transportation corridor for the proposed Kinder Morgan Trans Mountain Pipeline. Other legislation tabled has been in regards to increasing affordable housing, improving public health and safety, increasing access to post-secondary education and creating more jobs. Most notably, the BC NDP also tabled the Province’s first gender-based budget to focus on ending gender inequality. The 2017-2021 Parliament of British Columbia is notable for being the first minority government in British Columbia’s history. It remains to be seen how successful the Legislature and its governing coalition will be in their term of service.

Oakhurst is an unincorporated community located in Monmouth County, New Jersey, United States. The area was originally named Southards Corner, after a prominent early settler, Abraham Southard. The name was changed to Oakhurst in the early 20th century. The area was settled in the late 17th century, but did not take its current shape until the 19th century. Early settlers located near the area now called Brighton Avenue and this area became known as "The Corners". This area was also known during this time as Southards Corner, until the early 20th century, when it was renamed Oakhurst. The area is known for its tight-knit community, naturally scenic environment and numerous recreational activities. Its proximity to the Jersey Shore provides easy access to the beach and other shore attractions. Oakhurst is also home to a variety of businesses, including stores, restaurants, barber shops and small offices. Oakhurst's public schools are a part of the Ocean Township School District. It has two elementary schools: Wayside Elementary School and Ocean Township Intermediate School. It also has a middle school and a high school. Private schools in the area include St. Mark's Elementary School, Our Lady of Mount Carmel School and Ranney School. Oakhurst has two distinct commercial zones. The first covers a three-block strip along Ocean Avenue and includes several small stores, a pizzeria and a hardware store. The second commercial area is located on Brighton Avenue and includes a variety of stores and restaurants, including a deli, a barber shop and a taco shop. Oakhurst is home to a variety of community organizations, including the Oakhurst Volunteer Fire Company, the Oakhurst Volunteer Ambulance Squad and the Oakhurst Community Association. The association hosts a variety of events throughout the year, including the annual Halloween parade. Oakhurst is known for its picturesque location and its tight-knit community. Its mix of local businesses, community organizations and recreational activities make it a desirable place to live.

Paul Drinkhall (born 24 February 1991) is a professional table tennis player from England. He has represented England at the highest level since 2006. Drinkhall was born in Hartlepool, England, and was introduced to table tennis at a very early age by his father, a former national table tennis champion himself. At the age of 7, he entered his first national tournaments, showing a natural talent for the sport. He went on to become the youngest-ever member of the English National Team in 2006, at the age of 15. Drinkhall has enjoyed a long and successful career, winning numerous medals and titles both domestically and internationally. In 2010, he won his first senior title, at the Spanish Open, becoming the youngest British player to do so. In 2011, he won a gold medal at the Commonwealth Championships, and went on to take bronze at the Commonwealth Games in 2014. In 2016, he achieved his biggest success to date, winning gold at the European Championships. He has also consistently achieved top 10 finishes at multiple ITTF World Tour tournaments over the years. In addition to his success in tournaments, Drinkhall has also been a highly respected coach and ambassador for table tennis in England, working with a variety of organisations and teams. He founded the Paul Drinkhall Academy in 2014 and his work with the UK’s National Talent Program has been pivotal in developing the next generation of table tennis players. Drinkhall is currently the top-ranked table tennis player in England, and ranked 16th in the world, making him one of the highest-ranking English players of all time. He is also the longest serving member of England’s National Team and holds the distinction of being the first English player to reach the European Championships final in over 30 years. In recognition of his immense contribution to table tennis, he was awarded an MBE in the 2021 New Year Honours list. Drinkhall currently resides in Yorkshire and continues to pursue his passion for the sport of table tennis, striving to achieve further success both on and off the table.

Brentford Library is a public library situated in the London Borough of Hounslow, UK. It is one of the largest libraries in the borough and also acts as a reference library, with a comprehensive collection of books, e-books, periodicals and digital media. The library opened in 1924 and underwent a major renovation and re-opening in 2011. The Brentford Library boasts a wide collection of books and periodicals, ranging from fiction to non-fiction. It has many popular children's books and the latest magazines and newspapers. Additionally, the library offers a host of digital resources, such as e-books, audio-books, and databases. The library is accessible to the local community and visitors via the Hounslow bus network, and it also offers disabled access. In addition to its reading room, the Library provides meeting space, computer workstations, Wi-Fi access, and a café. The Library is open from Monday to Friday from 9am to 8pm and on weekends from 1pm to 5.30pm. Brentford Library works closely with the local community, providing a range of activities, services and events to promote reading, writing, and creativity. These include educational demonstrations, book group discussions, art classes, music performances, author talks, workshops, and story-telling sessions. It also has a wide variety of online resources such as language learning and databases, as well as a range of creative activities, all free of charge. The Library holds an annual Summer Reading Challenge, which encourages children to read and take part in an exciting range of recommended books. It also provides free books by post to older adults, who are unable to visit the library during the pandemic. Overall, Brentford Library is a valuable resource for people of all ages and backgrounds. The library works closely with the local community, offering a wide range of resources and activities, including a comprehensive collection of books and digital media. It is an important and vibrant part of the London Borough of Hounslow, and its various services are a testament to its commitment to providing access to lifelong learning.

Château de Lourmarin is a Renaissance castle located in Lourmarin, a small village in southeastern France in the Vaucluse department. The castle was once a fortification and held a strategic position in the Luberon valley and was a residence of the influential regional families of Lourmarin such as the Mauvoisin de Lourmarin, the Marans de Maez, the de Bivaches, the de Villeneuves, and the de La Varennes. Built in the middle of the 16th century, the castle is composed of two courtyards and two defensive towers. The main courtyard is where visitors can find the main hall, with its marble Florentine fireplaces and oak wood carvings. The second courtyard has a balustrade that dates from the 17th century. The castle also has a large park which is the perfect walking background. The castle represents a key part of the regional history and culture. It was acquired in 1971 by the Bordes-Benaroya family, who restored and opened it to the public. Today, it serves as a cultural center providing numerous annual events and activities, most notably concerts by the festival Art en Lourmarin. The estate also works in synergy with many other cultural sites in the area such as the Place Nationale des Arts, the Musée des Arts Contemporains and the Musée Marie Garenne. Various indoor and outdoor exhibitions and activities including drawing and painting courses, theatre, cooking and children’s workshops events the castle throughout the year. The estate’s collections are extensive and include manuscripts, engravings and other objects from the 16th to the 19th centuries and some pieces from the 20th century. One of these, a painted portrait of the Prince and Princess of Monaco, is particularly renowned. Throughout its existence, Château de Lourmarin has had a significant impact on the region’s cultural life and that of neighbouring areas. With its wide range of events and activities it has become a popular destination for tourists, cultural lovers and families alike.

Permanent private hall is a designation given to educational institutions that form part of the University of Oxford and Cambridge University in the United Kingdom. Permanent private halls (PPHs) have a history that goes back over 900 years and have deeply embedded themselves in the culture of the two universities. PPHs provide a distinct opportunity to study at either Oxford or Cambridge due to their more intimate environment and different course offerings. They offer a wide range of humanities and social sciences, as well as the opportunity to pursue specialized studies. As of 2021, Oxford has nine PPHs, and Cambridge has five. Although each PPH is distinct, they all follow the same regulations and deliver the same Oxford/Cambridge qualifications. All students at PPHs must also adhere to many university regulations. Due to their status as educational institutions, each PPH is self-governing, with their individual statutes and regulations determining the legal rights and responsibilities of both students and staff. The university is not responsible for the governance of the PPHs, and the individual PPHs are independent of the university. The university does, however, review the activities of the PPHs and approves or disapproves their academic regulations. An important characteristic of the PPHs is that they are often run by a faith or trust which sets the ethos of the PPH. For example, at St Benet’s Hall, founded by the Benedictine monks, the culture reflects that of the religious order and its Benedictine values. The same is true of other PPHs, such as St. Edmund’s Hall who follows the legacy of its Pontifical foundation. The PPHs also differ from Oxbridge in the way they select their students. Applicants are required to meet certain academic criteria, but the selection process also relies heavily on other factors such as the candidate’s interview, references, and personal statements. This helps to create an intimate and diverse environment in the PPHs. The experience at the PPHs is more intensive than at other Oxford or Cambridge colleges as students must attend lectures, tutorials, and small group supervisions. Generally, these institutions host fewer students than the Oxford and Cambridge colleges. Moreover, the PPHs have a great tradition of both academic excellence and community spirit, ensuring that the students and staff enjoy their university experience. In conclusion, permanent private halls provide a unique opportunity to obtain a world-renowned Oxford or Cambridge qualification and enjoy an intimate and diverse experience that many other universities cannot provide.

Yuka Tsujiyoko (辻横 由佳, Tsujiyoko Yuka), born October 7, 1973, is a Japanese composer and musician known for her work in video game soundtracks. Tsujiyoko grew up with an interest in music, learning to play the piano, violin, and trombone and beginning to compose music of her own. After graduating from the Toho Gakuen College of Music in Tokyo in 1998, Tsujiyoko got a job at Nintendo as an audio staffer, working on sound effects and music of the Nintendo 64 and Gamecube. As her skills and reputation grew, she was chosen to be the main composer for Fire Emblem: The Binding Blade in 2002, and the position made her responsible for all of the background music and sound effects in the game. Naturally, Tsujiyoko went on to compose for subsequent games in the Fire Emblem series, including Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance and Fire Emblem Awakening. Other game soundtracks she composed include outside of the Fire Emblem franchise such as Super Mario Strikers, Animal Crossing: City Folk, Mario Sports Mix, Animal Crossing: New Leaf and Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky. In addition to the game soundtracks, Tsujiyoko has also composed soundtracks for Japanese films and television shows. One of her most well-known non-gaming works is the soundtrack for the 2005 live-action drama adaptation of Plum Blossom. Tsujiyoko has won various awards for her work, including the Achievement Awards 2010 – New Generation at the International Film Music Critics Association Awards. In 2013, she was awarded with the courage award at the Tokyo Anime Awards. Throughout her career, Tsujiyoko has accumulated numerous fans, mainly because of her talent in composing music for popular video game series. Her work is celebrated as some of the best in the industry and she is widely regarded as one of Japan’s top composers.

Araucaria rulei, commonly known as the King Araucaria or Monkeys Puzzle tree, is a species of evergreen coniferous tree in the genus Araucaria. Native to Southern Argentina and parts of Chile, it is a distinctive species noted for its symmetrical branches and perfect cone-shaped crown. The species is on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, as its natural habitat is becoming increasingly fragmented and degraded. Araucaria rulei is an impressive evergreen conifer. It can reach heights of up to 60 feet and has a slim pyramid shape, with horizontal layered branches, each adorned with long, sharp, light green needles. In maturity, the tree forms a perfect cone-shaped crown. Borne on long stems, the cone-shaped fruits are woody, and contain a single, brown, edible seed. A. rulei flourishes in temperate to subtropical climates with moderately warm summers and cool winters. It does not tolerate extreme temperatures and needs protection from strong winds and prolonged periods of intense frost. It prefers a moderately deep, well-drained soil, an acidic pH and sunny exposure. Propagation is by seed, although it can also be grown from cuttings. Araucaria rulei is of cultural and historical significance to the native communities in southern Argentina and Chile. Throughout history, these communities have recognized and honored this tree as a symbol of power and strength. For instance, certain chiefs used this species to crown their war bonnets, a custom that is still practiced today among some native cultures. The King Araucaria is also a popular ornamental species due to its majestic stature and unusual form. Unlike most conifers, this species is handsome year-round and can be grown in a variety of climates. However, populations of Araucaria rulei are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation. Conservation efforts are currently being implemented to protect this species.

The term bothy or bothie (also known as a foambury, sheiling, shieling or peatrobbery) is a type of mountain hut, typically found in Scotland and the northern part of Northern England. Bothies are typically small, simple shelters used as temporary accommodation by walkers, cyclists, or mountaineers. They are mostly built in remote rural areas such as the Highlands and Lake District, and are commonly found on popular walking routes in the UK. Bothies are normally inherited from generations of local farmers, with some huts being over 100 years old. There is no formal ownership of bothies, and they are normally maintained by local countryside trusts or by voluntary bothy associations. Often these organisations require donations to maintain the bothy and provide basic amenities such as firewood, a stove, and basic furniture. Bothies range from small stone cottages to basic wooden huts and are situated in some of the most stunning parts of the countryside. Most are unfurnished, and are used as shelter or overnight accommodation during bad weather or for campers. Some bothies have basic amenities such as fireplaces and stoves, while some of the more luxurious bothies have running water and electric lights. Generally, all items left in bothies should be left for others to use and not taken. Bothies are often located in remote parts of the landscape, so it is important to plan trips carefully and take the necessary safety precautions before travelling to either. This includes checking the weather forecast and taking adequate supplies. In addition, walkers should be familiar with the local area and have the necessary maps and guidebooks to know where they are travelling to and from in order to stay safe and enjoy the experience. Overall, bothies are a great way to enjoy the beauty of the countryside with minimal equipment and budget. Walking to a bothy can be an adventure in itself and the experience will always be enjoyed as the landscape is still wild and untamed but yet full of beauty. It is important to respect bothies and treat them with humility as most are privately owned and without proper maintenance, they could easily be damaged. Therefore, every visitor should always follow rules strictly to maintain the tradition of bothy use as they have done since centuries ago.

Sezgi Sena Akay (born 1978) is a Turkish-American fine artist and film director. She is known for her work exploring identity in duality through the constructed images of her performance-based films. Akay was born in Istanbul, Turkey, and she studied fine arts at the Mimar Sinan University of Fine Arts. The focus of her art-making deals with poetry, performance, photography, sculpture, drawings and filmmaking. In her work, Akay is interested in exploring the relationships between "doubt, flexibility and fragility". Akay moved to the United States in 2009, settling in Houston, Texas. Here, she earned her Masters in Visual Arts from the University of Houston. She then worked at the Women in Film and Television Houston as the Program Director, where she created programs, discussions and workshops for anyone who wanted to become involved in the industry. Akay's films have been shown in international film festivals, as well as exhibitions, including at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston; The New York Times' International Center for Photography, Moscow’s Multimedia Art Museum and The Museum of Contemporary Art in Oslo, Norway. In addition, her first independent feature documentary film, Passage, was featured in the official selections of the Montreal Black Film Festival and the Houston Cinema Arts Festival in 2016. After her film career, Akay returned to focus mostly on artmaking. In 2018, she unveiled a series of 21 photographs entitled "Metamorphosis" at the Texas Gallery in Houston, TX. In her work, Akay examines issues of identity, cultural displacement and racial boundaries. Much of her work also looks at subjects related to the impact of war and violence. In February of 2019, Akay completed a major mural project, commissioned by the Houston Endowment, on the outside of the Houston FotoFest office in Houston, Texas. Entitled The Mural of Migration and Reflections, the large-scale mural spans over 15,000 square feet and was created by over 500 community volunteers. Akay’s work has garnered recognition, including a 2012 Golden Palette Award in the Annual Art Colony Open Gallery competition in Houston, Texas. Her work has also been included in several collections around the world, including The Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, and the Yıldız Technical University, Istanbul. Currently, Akay splits her time between her hometown of Istanbul and Houston, Texas and continues to create visual art and films.
