Leicester Smyth (born 1854, died unknown) was a late 19th-century Irish rower who competed in the Thames and Henley regattas in the Victorian winter of 1888-89. Smyth began to gain recognition in his hometown of Belfast as a member of the Belfast Rowing Club, where he was known for his strong, powerful strokes. He increasingly took part in the "High Class" rowing competitions of the winter season, featuring in regattas including the Caledonian and Belfast Regattas, and soon found himself competing on a larger stage, with the Thames and Henley regattas as his target battlegrounds. In 1888, Smyth entered his first professional rowing competition, the 1888 Thames Regatta. Here, he defeated the New Rowing Club's crew by six lengths to take first place, and word of his success quickly spread throughout the British Isles. Smyth went on to compete in the 1889 Henley Regatta, finishing a creditable second to Eton's crew in the Town Challenge Cup. Despite his successes, very little is known about Leicester Smyth's subsequent life or even his fate. The 1891 British Census does not list Smyth as being in the regular population. It is believed that he likely died in 1890, in between his 1888 and 1889 Thames and Henley successes, at the age of 36. Leicester Smyth's place in Irish rowing history is remembered fondly; he is credited with being the first Irishman to take first place in a professional Thames Regatta, a popular event at that time. He is further remembered today for his inspirational story; a working-class man finding success through hard work and respect at a time where working-class sportsmen were looked down upon.

The Megaupload legal case was an ongoing criminal case in the United States concerning the now-defunct file sharing website Megaupload and its founder, Kim Dotcom. It began on January 19, 2012, when the U.S. Department of Justice initiated criminal proceedings against Megaupload and indicted seven people associated with the website on copyright infringement, racketeering, and money laundering charges. Megaupload was a website that allowed users to upload, store, and download large files. Founded in 2005 by Kim Dotcom, who also owns the sister companies Megavideo, Megalive, and Megaporn, the website was used by millions of people to share pirated copies of copyrighted film, music and software. In January 2012, U.S. authorities, in collaboration with law enforcement in New Zealand, raided Kim Dotcom's home and shut down Megaupload. The U.S. government accused Kim and his associates of engaging in a criminal conspiracy, by using the Megaupload website to commit criminal copyright infringement, as well as making money from piracy. In March that year, the U.S. Department of Justice filed criminal charges against seven people, including Kim Dotcom and his associates, for their involvement in the Megaupload website. The charges included copyright infringement, racketeering, and money laundering, and the seven were indicted on a total of 13 counts. Over the course of the next two years, the Megaupload legal case became increasingly complex and publicized. The U.S. government sought extradition of the accused and unsuccessfully attempted to issue a warrant to seize over $67 million worth of assets held by the defendant. In 2014, the New Zealand High Court found that the defendants had been subject to an illegal search and seizure, and ruled that U.S. authorities had failed to meet the necessary criteria for their arrest and extradition. The DOJ then chose to continue pursuing the criminal case against Kim Dotcom and his associates. The criminal case against Megaupload and the defendants remains ongoing. In 2017, the New Zealand Supreme Court confirmed that the extradition process is still underway, but no further updates have been provided. The case has also resulted in an increasing awareness of copyright infringement and the illegal exchange of intellectual property over the internet. It also provided a wake-up call for Kim Dotcom and the tech industry, who now face stricter regulation when it comes to copyright infringement, piracy, and racketeering.

NGC 3175 is an open cluster of stars located in the constellation of Sextans. It was discovered on April 26, 1793 by German astronomer William Herschel. NGC 3175 has an apparent magnitude of 10.8 and its distance from Earth is estimated to be about 12,400 light years. The stars in NGC 3175 are organized into a sparse grouping and are spread over an area of 10 arc minutes in the sky. The stars of the cluster range in spectral type from F through G to M, with the majority being late-type stars. In addition to its open cluster stars, NGC 3175 also contains several Herbig–Haro objects. These are formed when material such as gas and dust travelling away from a young star in jets gets slowed down and compressed by the interstellar medium, forming knots and nebulae. Most of the Herbig–Haro objects that have been detected in NGC 3175 are located near the southern edge of the cluster. Most of the stars in NGC 3175 are young, with a median age estimated to be about 6.8 million years. This indicates that the cluster is a relatively young star-formation region. The estimated total mass of the cluster is about 3000 times that of the Sun, with the brightest stars being about 10th magnitude. NGC 3175 is visible with a relatively small telescope, or even binoculars, in a dark sky. It is best viewed in March and April, and can be found within 5 degrees of the planet Uranus, and just over 6 degrees west of the bright star Spica. Despite its relatively close distance to Earth, and its relatively young age, only a few stars in NGC 3175 have been studied in any detail. In particular, the star HD 86134 has been found to be a red giant, and several others have been identified as binary stars. In addition, some stars in NGC 3175 display evidence of rapid rotation, which may be the result of close flybys of neighbouring stars. Due to its relative youth, NGC 3175 may be of particular interest to those studying star formation. A better understanding of the cluster, in particular its Herbig–Haro objects, may provide new insight into how stars form and interact with their surroundings.

Corruption in local government is the abuse of public officials' power for private gain through bribery, extortion, patronage, kickbacks, and nepotism. Corruption can take place within all levels of government, whether it be local, state, or federal, however, the highest prevalence of corruption tends to occur at the local level. This type of corruption has a number of causes and effects that are detrimental to the citizens of the local community. Common Causes Corruption in local government is caused by a number of different factors. One of the primary contributors to this issue is the lack of competition in local politics. Many local cities and towns lack the resources to conduct public elections that would select the most qualified official, instead having to rely on the reelection of incumbent officials. These individuals are able to abuse their connections and power to remain in office without much opposition from other challengers. Other factors contributing to local government corruption include the availability of ample government resources for personal gain, lack of oversight and accountability, and ineffective organizational structures and procedures. Effects The prevalence of corruption in local government has a wide variety of detrimental effects on citizens. The greatest detriment occurs when officials use their positions for personal gain, resulting in skewed public policy and a misallocation of public funds. This form of corruption leads to the creation of ineffective laws and policies that prioritize the benefits of the few individuals in power rather than the interests of the public. This harm is compounded when government officials take bribes or engage in kickback schemes, which drain public money while allowing those involved to enjoy financial benefits. When these types of activities are occurring on such a large scale, it also tends to have a serious effect on society's perception of local government. Citizens begin to lose faith and trust in their locally elected officials and their ability to act in their constituents’ interests. This can lead to a culture of apathy and disengagement which can make public engagement and accountability even harder to achieve. Ways to Reduce Corruption There are a number of different strategies that can be used to try and reduce the prevalence of corruption in local government settings. Anti-corruption rules and regulations should be established and widely enforced to ensure that no individual is able to abuse their power for personal gain. Additionally, local governments should also strive to increase transparency and accountability to citizens by giving them better access to information concerning their elected officials and the decisions they are making. Finally, officials must be held to high ethical standards, and any cases of corruption must be punished and dealt with accordingly. Overall, the issue of corruption in local governments is an unfortunate reality that has a serious effect on citizens’ trust and confidence in their elected officials. To combat this issue, citizens must remain diligent in their efforts to ensure that their locally elected officials do not abuse their power and that they are held to a standard of transparency and accountability. Additionally, governments must invest more resources into preventing corruption and stiff penalties must be enforced to those that are found in violation.

Züleyha Gülüm (born 27 April 1958) is a Turkish journalist and author. Known for her work as a political analyst, she is widely regarded as one of the leading commentators on Turkish politics. Gülüm was born in Istanbul and graduated from the University of Istanbul in 1980. She began her career as a journalist in Istanbul, writing for a variety of newspapers and magazines. She covered Europe and the Middle East for 10 years, including the Bosnian War. During her time in Bosnia, she wrote extensively about human rights and the impact of the war on women. In 1997, Gülüm returned to Istanbul to work at the Hürriyet daily newspaper. Here she established her career as a political analyst and wrote on various political topics, including the Kurdish conflict, human rights, and the European Union. Gülüm also worked for the OdaTV network in 2008 and for the Ekonomik Gazete publication in 2010. Gülüm has published two books in Turkish, Female Voices of the Balkans in 2004 and In the Shadow of the Neglected: Bosnian Women in war and peace in 2008. Her writing focuses on the subject of human rights, particularly the rights of minorities and women. Throughout her career, Gülüm has been a strong advocate for Turkish democracy, freedom of speech, and human rights. She has spoken about her work and her views at numerous conferences and workshops in Europe and the United States. In addition, she has been invited numerous times to testify at the European Parliament and the UN Commission on Human Rights. She was awarded the Right Livelihood Award in 2016, in recognition of her commitment to advancing the cause of human rights in Turkey. Gülüm currently resides in Istanbul and continues her work as a journalist and human rights advocate. She has been at the forefront of the struggle to promote human rights and democratic values in Turkey, and her voice has been an important part of the movement for social justice in the country.

The Ministry of Justice (Italian: Ministero della Giustizia) is the Italian government department responsible for overseeing matters related to the judicial system. It is operated within the framework of the executive branch of government and is under the direct supervision of the Prime Minister. The Ministry of Justice works with various other authorities to protect the rule of law and human rights in Italy. It works to prevent injustice, guarantee equal access to justice, and coordinate the work of the country's legal services. The Ministry is tasked with overseeing the judiciary, coordinating the activities of the Higher Council of the Judiciary, and issuing laws regulating the civil and criminal justice systems. It also provides guidance for the operation of non-state actors in relation to matters of public justice. In addition, the Ministry is responsible for training and recruiting personnel for the country's legal system, and coordinating the activities of the Higher Education Authority. It also works to provide assistance to victims of human rights violations, and to combat legal forms of discrimination. The Ministry's main headquarters are located in Rome, and it also has regional offices in all of Italy's major cities. The current Minister of Justice is Alfonso Bonafede, appointed in 2020. The Ministry's work is carried out by several entities. The General Superintendence of Legal Services is responsible for the management and coordination of the various legal services within the Ministry. The State Legal Service is in charge of the management of civil and criminal legal services, while the Military Legal Sector is tasked with the management of military justice. The Office of the Prosecutor General is responsible for supervising the national criminal proceedings and conducts strategic investigations. The Ministry of Justice also works closely with the Ministry of Education, Universities and Research, the Ministry of Health, and the Ministry of Environment. Additionally, it is one of the members of the Integrated System for the Coordination of Citizens and Legal Persons. The Integrated System is used to ensure the correct management of citizen rights, the prevention of criminal activities, and the protection of citizens from unlawful practices.

Auxvasse Creek is a 71.8-mile-long creek in north-central Missouri in the United States. It runsthrough Audrain, Monroe and Montgomery counties. The source of the Auxvasse Creek is located in southeastern Audrain County, located in the north-central portion of Missouri. It then runs north-northwest passing through Montgomery County and then turning northwest following US Highway 54 passing by the community of Auxvasse in western Callaway County. In Lewistown the creek turns more northerly and passes Colesburg and eventually enters the Salt River northwest of Clark in northeast Montgomery County. The Main Fork of Auxvasse Creek passes through Audrain, Monroe and Montgomery counties and is a tributary of the Salt River near Clark. In total, three major branches of the Auxvasse Creek network supply watershed areas in north-central Missouri. The Auxvasse Creek watershed provides a natural platform for supporting many recreational activities which include fishing, hunting, canoeing, kayaking, swimming, camping and nature study. The area is also rich with bird life, playgrounds, and other outdoor recreational opportunities. The Auxvasse Creek area is an excellent location for a variety of forms of outdoor exploration and discovery year-round. Auxvasse Creek is the headwaters of many of the tributary streams, including Buttermilk Creek, Wolf Creek, Sinking Creek, and Commerce Creek. Buttermilk Creek, a tributary of Auxvasse Creek, is a 28-mile-long stream that connects with Wolf and Sinking Creeks in northern Montgomery County. Wolf Creek is a 9.3-mile-long stream that also runs through the Auxvasse Watershed. Other notable tributaries of Auxvasse Creek are McCoy Creek, Brush Creek, and Indian Creek. The Auxvasse Creek is the host of several fishing tournaments conducted annually in the area. Many different species of fish inhabit the creek, including catfish, bass, sunfish, carp and channel catfish, as well as other species. The Auxvasse Creek Watershed is home to many different species of plants and animals, offering a rich ecosystem vital to the health of its inhabitants and the surrounding areas. From a geological point of view, the Auxvasse Creek is a part of the northern Mississippi River Valley. Auxvasse Creek is part of the floodplain which, combined with the various tributaries, supplies the area with a natural resource for recreational activities as well as providing important ground for supporting ecosystems. In August 1984, Auxvasse Creek was declared a State Inland Waterway by the Missouri Department of Natural Resources. This designation places Auxvasse Creek in a special category that allows certain industrial and water development activities to occur in the watershed under rigid guidelines and regulations. This provides an investment opportunity that increases the importance and value of this unique creek. The Auxvasse Creek and its tributaries are essential water resources in central Missouri. These watersheds provide an avenue for recreation, protect the environment, and offer businesses an opportunity to invest in the area. The Auxvasse Creek watershed is a valuable subject of study and consideration and should be protected, preserved and enjoyed.

Dagmar Hase (born 1949) is a German journalist and former politician. She is a leader in the Social Democratic Party (SPD) and was a Member of the European Parliament. Hase was born and raised in East Berlin. She worked as a teacher and journalist before entering politics. In 1986, Hase began her involvement in the SPD, joining the SPD youth organization. While working for this organization, she moved up the ranks to become the party's secretary general in 1989. In 1995, Hase became a member of the European Parliament (MEP) for the German SPD, representing their top list of candidates for the parliament. She held this position for five years until 2000. During this time, she served on the Committee of Legal Affairs and the Committee on the Environment and the Committee on Women's Rights. Hase was also a member of several delegations in the parliament, including the Delegation for Relations with the Pan-African Parliament and the Delegation for Relations with Mercosur (Latin American trade bloc). Hase has also worked for the United Nations in various capacities. From 2001 to 2003, she was the Chief of the Human Resources Management Service in Geneva. From 2003 to 2005, she served as Director of the United Nations Office in Geneva. In 2006, Hase was appointed as the Executive Representative of the Secretary-General for the African Great Lakes Region. She held this position until 2010. Hase has been a vocal supporter of gender equality, particularly in the African Great Lakes Region. She has frequently spoken in favor of female empowerment and encouraging young women to enter into politics. Hase has also called for more equitable distribution of aid to benefit marginalized populations. In addition to her political work, Hase is a keen traveler and enjoys scuba diving and hiking. She currently resides in Berlin.

Ezell's Chicken is a popular family-owned business based in Seattle, Washington. The company is best known for its fried chicken, which it has been serving since 1984. The restaurant is named after the founder, Ezell Stephens, who opened it after years of working in the food service industry. Stephens was born in 1934 in Stillmore, Georgia. He migrated to Seattle in the late 1950s, where he worked as a fry cook at M&M Cafe and other local restaurants. In 1984, he opened his first restaurant in Seattle, which he named Ezell's Fried Chicken. Since then, the restaurant has grown to seven locations in the Seattle area. Ezell's is known for its signature recipe, which is a combination of buttermilk and secret seasonings that give the chicken its distinct flavor. The chicken is seasoned and marinated overnight before being double dipped in the secret seasoning and batter mix. After this, the fried chicken is served hot and crispy. In addition to their signature fried chicken, Ezell's also offers a wide selection of sides and desserts, including macaroni and cheese, collard greens, and peach cobbler. The signature fried chicken is not the only thing that sets the restaurant apart; its service is also known for being fast, friendly and efficient. The restaurant is a favorite of locals, celebrities and visitors alike, who have all praised Ezell's for their excellent customer service. In addition to their restaurants, Ezell's has also expanded into other areas, including catering and food trucks. The company has also spawned a line of products, including fried chicken mix, sauces and spices. In 2013, Ezell's was featured on the Travel Channel's Food Wars show and won the Seattle battle against a local competitor. Ezell's has become a beloved part of the Seattle food scene and is widely regarded as one of the best fried chicken restaurants in the city. The company has become renowned for its generous portions, flavorful recipes and friendly service. Whether you're in Seattle for a visit or a lifetime, there's no denying that Ezell's Fried Chicken is a must-try experience.

The Great Western Highway is a highway running through New South Wales, Australia. The 1,254 km (778 mi) route travels from the outskirts of Sydney at Eastlink in Prestons, southwest of Sydney, to Bourke at the end of the Blue Mountains in New South Wales. The Great Western Highway begins at Eastlink in Prestons, southwest of Sydney. It runs westwards through the Blue Mountains, including towns such as Katoomba, Lithgow and Bathurst. Along the way, it briefly joins with the Silver City Highway, before continuing to the rural towns of Orange, Mudgee, Dunedoo and Gilgandra. The road turns north after Gilgandra, then rejoins the Silver City Highway at Cobar before continuing northwest to Brewarrina, Bourke and the Queensland border. The Great Western Highway is the main link to western New South Wales, and is the major route between Sydney and some of the larger cities in the Orana and Central West regions. It is an important freight route, as well as being used by tourists driving between Sydney and the west. The Great Western Highway was constructed in 1815 at the same time as the expansion of the wool industry in rural Australia. By 1841, it was extended as far west as Bathurst and had become the principal thoroughfare between Sydney and the west. In 1940, improvements in technology and construction techniques allowed the Great Western Highway to be widened and the speed limit of 80 km/h (50 mph) to be applied along its entire length. The Great Western Highway is today a core route in road transport between Sydney and western New South Wales. Improvements to the road in the latter half of the 20th Century have included new sections of divided highway and road widening to widen the highway from a two lane to four lane road between Richmond and Penrith. The safety and speed of the Great Western Highway has considerably increased since the 1960s, when it was subject to many sharp curves and narrow sections. The Great Western Highway passes through significant sites along the way, including Abercrombie Caves, Katoomba Scenic World and the other tourist attractions of the Blue Mountains, and the historic Mudgee Wineries around Mudgee. The entire length of the Great Western Highway is part of the National Highway System and is designated a State Highway. The road has become an important economic corridor in the economic development of western New South Wales. Its importance as a main thoroughfare is expected to increase as population in western New South Wales grows Today, the Great Western Highway is an important road to the people of western New South Wales, providing easy access to major cities, attractions and resources. The highway is the major link to Sydney, the gateway to the Central West region and a vital transportation route for commercial and recreational vehicles. The highway's significance to the people of NSW has earned it the title of 'The Great Western Highway.'

Rondout Creek is a 44.3-mile long tributary of the Hudson River in Ulster and Sullivan Counties, New York. It is one of the Hudson River's largest and most important tributaries, providing over two thirds of the river's fresh water supply. The Rondout is fed by the waters of several other streams, beginning high in the Catskill Mountains and flowing south and east before emptying into the Hudson River near Kingston. The mayor of Rondout Creek was discovered in 1609 by Henry Hudson while searching for the Northwest Passage. The creek was subsequently used as a transportation route by colonial pioneers and eventually connected to the Erie Canal. The creek also provided critical transportation to industries located along its route. An important center of anthracite coal mining and related industries, the creek was the site of the great anthracite rail boycott of 1902, a major landmark in American labor history. Today, Rondout Creek is a major recreation destination for kayaking, canoeing and fishing. The creek was designated an "Outstanding Water Resource" in 2009. The most popular sections for kayaking and canoeing are the sections from the Sam's Point Preserve to its confluence with the Hudson River. The creek is also home to a variety of fish and other aquatic life, including brown trout and largemouth bass. In addition to being an important recreational asset for the region, Rondout Creek also serves many environmental functions. The creek is home to numerous species of aquatic life, including the endangered dwarf wedgemussel. It also provides recreational opportunities to local communities, while also supporting a healthy and productive riparian ecosystem along its banks. Rondout Creek is part of America’s industrial history, and its winding route is also a sign of its enduring importance to the Hudson Valley region. As an important recreational resource and environmental asset, Rondout Creek helps to bring life and vitality to the communities that surround it.

The Italian Social Democratic Party (Italian: Partito Socialdemocratico Italiano; PSDI) is a political party in Italy established in 1945 after World War II. Founded by dissident members of the Italian Liberal Party, it has evolved over the years and now provides representation to both centre-left and centre-right voters. The party's mission statement calls for a commitment to the values of democracy and social progressivism as well as for their expression in the life of the Republic of Italy. It advocates for a strong public sector, the defense of worker's rights, and has strong ties to the European Union. The PSDI is currently led by legislator center-left Riccardo Nencini who was elected leader of the party in December 2016. The PSDI is a member of several different parliamentary groups - most notably the left-wing Party of the European Left, as well as the center-left European Socialists and Italian Socialist Party. They are also members of the Party of Italian Communists and a founder member of the PD. The PSDI has historically been prominent in Italian politics, having been active in all governments between 1996 and 2006, as well as having Prime Minister Luigi Olivetti serve in 1973-1974 and 1980-1981. During the 2018 Italian election, the PSDI was part of the Formation of the Left alliance, which aimed to unite left-leaning parties and provide a alternative to the centre-right coalition led by the Five Star Movement and the Lega Nord. The PSDI was also a part of the Democratic Party-led government from 2018-2019. Despite its historical presence in the government and parliament, the PSDI remains broadly unknown and has had limited electoral success throughout its history. As a result, there is speculation that the PSDI and other smaller parties within center-left will soon face complete absorption into the larger Democratic Party. The Italian Social Democratic Party is a political force with a history going back to the original formation of the Italian state. Despite limited electoral success, the PSDI has achieved a degree of historical success in driving legislation over the years, as well as in contributing to the unity of the Italian left-wing. As changes in the political landscape continue to occur, it remains to be seen whether the PSDI can maintain its hold on Italian politics into the future.

Yang Yongliang (born 1980, Shanghai, China) is an artist whose work is rooted in traditional Chinese landscapes and ink painting, but also interacts with concepts from contemporary practices such as media, technology, and architecture. He has become a leading artist in China and is widely recognized as a respected voice in the global art world. Yang grew up in a traditional Chinese family, and his artistic practice has been shaped by his childhood fascination with traditional landscape painting. He began creating traditional landscape paintings at a very young age and has maintained this technique throughout his career. His works also reference traditional Chinese calligraphy, weaving these traditional themes into more contemporary concepts. Yang uses photography, videography, and large-scale digital prints to create works of art that blend traditional Chinese elements with modern media. His digital prints and installations incorporate elements of traditional Chinese ink painting and calligraphy, merging these forms with modern 3D design and the changes and trends of the city. By combining traditional art forms with the contemporary media, Yang critiques the erasure of Chinese culture and the changes in the urban landscape. He has exhibited widely, including solo exhibitions at the Palazzo Delle Arti in Naples, Italy, Shanghai Modern Art Museum in Shanghai, China, Pace Gallery in Beijing, China, and Chapel Performance Space in Seattle, USA. He has also been exhibited by galleries such as Ben Brown Fine Arts in London, England, and Red Brick Art Museum in Beijing, China. Yang’s work has been recognized by the modern art historical canon, and he has won multiple awards including the 2009 International Art Meeting Prize, the 2009 Shanghai Youth Creation Prize and the 2011 Expo Prize. He is also a professor at the China Academy of Art. Yang’s works have been collected by major institutions, such as the Museum of Modern Art and the Guggenheim Museum in New York, USA; the Louvre in Paris, France; and the Victoria & Albert Museum in London, England. He has also participated in major international events and biennials, including the 2005 Shanghai Biennale and the 2008 Liverpool Biennale. Yang has been described as one of the most influential Chinese artists of his time. Through reinterpreting traditional Chinese art forms and transforming them in modern works of art, his works not only capture the beauty of culture and history, but also reflect on identity and the permanence of global trends.

The Grasshopper is a 1970 American drama directed by Jerry Paris and starring Jacqueline Bisset and Jim Brown. The film follows the story of nomad artist Monica Clayborn (Bisset), who, after graduating college and traveling the world, returns to her home in Dallas to reinvent herself. With the help of her stepfather Joe (Brown), Monica, who is nicknamed The Grasshopper after the adopted father who taught her to paint, seeks a way to find her footing and peace in the oppressive, fast-paced society of the Big City. Monica quickly falls into the club scene and discovers the drug lifestyle, earning money as a waitress and from selling drugs on the side. While her situation is often perilous, she finds the new life of street living both exciting and liberating, and forms a tight-knit circle of lifelong friends who help her through some difficult times. As Monica continues to pursue her dream of being an artist, she also struggles to make a living, an avenue to which her friends are unable to help. Her frustration leads her to commit an unspeakable act, causing her to question her own principles and morality. The Grasshopper was an important film of its time, providing an intertwined glimpse into a turbulent the mid-century lifestyle filled with art, music, drugs, and the pursuit of identity and purpose. Critics praised Bisset's performance as well as her ability to successfully portray a young woman caught between the thrill of lawlessness and the heavier decisions of self-determination. Brown’s portrayal as her stepfather was also commended. The movie also featured an early soundtrack by a then still-unknown Tangerine Dream. The Grasshopper was a pioneering film of the New Hollywood era and spurred a wave of similar coming-of-age dramas set in urban America in the 1970s.

BiTrektual is a new software solution developed to help improve customer service and collaboration. It integrates customer service, sales, operations, and customer data to provide a single comprehensive view of customer relationships. The story of BiTrektual began in 2019 with two computer scientists from the United States. The idea for the software was born out of a need to provide better customer service to organizations of all sizes. When companies use outdated technologies, they struggle to meet customer expectations. The BiTrek team set out to create a solution that offered an easy-to-use store front, large library of useful customer support features, and customer data management capabilities to provide organizations with the tools they needed to deliver excellent customer service. BiTrektual is the result of that effort. It's a cloud-based customer relationship management (CRM) and customer service platform that can be deployed in minutes with a few simple steps. The platform brings all of an organizations customer interactions, sales, and operations into one place to foster collaboration. Organisations can also create tailored experiences and interactions for their customers with the help of custom workflows and automated processes. BiTrektual delivers a customer service experience that can adapt to the unique needs of customers. It also offers data-driven insights that enable organisations to better understand customer behavior, drive upsell opportunities, and identify key areas for improvement. The software platform is easy to set up, integrate, and manage. It has a customizable user interface designed to be used by non-technical personnel. It also has an easy-to-use dashboard, analytical powers and reporting capabilities to assist in decision making and operations. BiTrektual will help organizations stay competitive and deliver the kind of customer service experience that will keep customers coming back. This software will give organizations the ability to quickly identify and address customer needs, tailor customer service for each individual, and measure the efficiency of customer interactions. Overall, BiTrektual is said to provide an improved customer experience, increase customer satisfaction, and foster team collaboration.

D-3 is a video game developed by Taito Corporation and released in 1989. It was released in Japan and then localized in North America, Europe, and Asia by Nintendo. The game was released on the Nintendo Entertainment System and has become a popular cult classic. The game is set in a post-apocalyptic future, where the human race has been wiped out by something known as the D-3 virus. The player takes on the role of Tango, a robotic tank who is traveling through the remains of the former world. As Tango travels, he must battle the virus-infested creatures and discover the source of the virus before it can consume the world. D-3 has been praised for its unique gameplay and its use of difficulty and puzzle-solving elements. The core gameplay consists of a top-down view with the player controlling Tango directly, managing his health and resources to progress through the levels. The game also features the ability to pick up and use various items throughout the levels. The graphics and music of the game have been praised for their time period. The visuals have a gritty and haunting quality to them, and the music has been praised for its unique mix of synthesized and acoustic sounds. The game was commercially successful upon its release, and even to this day, it continues to maintain a strong cult following. It was even re-released on the Wii's virtual console in 2007. Today, it is commonly seen as one of the best NES games and a classic example of the post-apocalyptic genre. Overall, D-3 is a cult classic and an important game in the history of the post-apocalyptic genre. Its unique and challenging gameplay, along with its haunting visuals and soundtrack, make it a title worth playing for all fans of retro gaming.

Chisago Lakes School District is a school district located in Chisago County, Minnesota. It serves students in the cities of Chisago City, Lindstrom, Rush City, Shafer, and Taylors Falls, and in the townships of Chisago Lake, Fish Lake, Hugo, and Stacy. It operates six schools: Chisago Lakes Secondary School, Lakes International Language Academy, Sunrise Elementary and West Forest Lake Elementary in Chisago, Pine City Elementary and Rush City Elementary. The district was officially established in 1983 with the merger of schools in the cities of Chisago and Rush City, along with those from surrounding rural townships. Prior to the merger, the Chisago schools were part of the Chisago Lake School District and the Rush City schools were part of the Rush City School District. The district serves approximately 6,000 students with a staff of approximately 600 full and part-time employees. The curriculum at Chisago Lakes Secondary School and Lakes International Language Academy is based on the state's standards, which are regularly reviewed by the district’s Curriculum Advisory Committee to ensure alignment with district and state goals. In addition to core academic classes, the district offers a range of extracurricular activities such as the arts, athletics, community service and experientially-based learning opportunities. The district also offers programs in special education, Advanced Placement (AP) courses, RtI/MTSS and mental health services. The district sets high expectations for student achievement and maintains a strong focus on workforce preparation for its graduates. In keeping with its commitment to educational excellence, the district is continually looking for ways to support the success of its students. The Chisago Lakes School District is also a member of the Greater Minnesota Partnership, which provides resources and support for schools in out-state Minnesota. Overall, Chisago Lakes School District strives to create a safe, inviting learning environment where all students can thrive and achieve their full potential. The district supports its students to develop the knowledge, skills and values needed to be productive, contributing members of society.

The 2014 Atlanta Braves season was the Braves' 18th season as the Major League Baseball's National League affiliate and their 45th season in Atlanta. It was their first season under new president of baseball operations John Hart and the final season under manager Fredi Gonzalez. The Braves finished the season in second place in the NL East with a 79–83 record, the first non-winning season since 2008. The Braves opened the season with 7 consecutive wins, tying their own franchise record. The team remained in first place in the NL East until late-June, when they started to struggle, merely winning 9 of their next 29 games. The struggles were due to injuries to several key players, starters Kris Medlen and Brandon Beachy left the team with elbow injuries and the team struggled to fill their roles with replacements. Offseason acquisitions, such as starting pitchers Ervin Santana and Aaron Harang, failed to live up to their pre-season hype. Additionally, first baseman Freddie Freeman also suffered a significantly-among of injuries, including an oblique strain and a broken wrist, over the course of the season, causing him to miss over 30 games. The team was able to stay competitive with rookie performances from infielders Tommy La Stella and Chris Johnson, as well as the promotion of catcher Evan Gattis to the major league level. However, it was the pitching staff that kept the Braves within a reasonable distance of first place in the division. The cover stories of their rotation were staff ace Julio Teheran, rookie Alex Wood, and veterans Ervin Santana and Aaron Harang, who provided solid production for a considerable portion of the season. The team was able to maintain a chance for the division and the wild card through mid-September, however a 5-game losing streak extinguished those hopes and realistic focus returned to players such as Gattis and La Stella, who "took outfielder Jason Heyward's spot in the lineup and ran with it" during the season. At the end of the 2014 season, Fredi Gonzalez was dismissed as the manager after 5 years at the helm and John Hart was identified as the Braves new president of baseball operations. Hart's appointment marked the beginning of "the rebuild" in Atlanta and the team moved away from the late-inning game management and bullpen uncertainty which characterized several seasons under Gonzalez.

Cronenberg, Wuppertal is a small rural community in western Germany, outside the city of Wuppertal. It was founded in the Middle Ages and has a population of over 1,300 citizens. It is nestled in the valley of the Sauer and Wupper rivers, which flow together through the picturesque town. The economy of Cronenberg is mainly agricultural, though it has a few small industries, including wood-processing and small-scale manufacturing. A specialty of the region is a spicy local jam, made from the blackberries that grow in the surrounding hills. The community is well-known for its historic architecture, including a medieval timber-framed church dating from around 1365, as well as a 14th-century market cross. There are also a number of 18th-century houses, particularly along the Wuppertal city wall. Cronenberg is also the site of some noteworthy events in the history of Germany. The Battle of Cronenberg was fought here in 1809 between the Prussians and the French. It was a hard-fought encounter which was ultimately won by the Prussians. The battle led to the establishment of Prussia as a nation. The village is also associated with the "Rosenberg Revolt", a peasant uprising in the 1750s. The ultimately unsuccessful revolt was started by a local farm worker in protest against the ruling aristocrats of the region. Cronenberg offers visitors a unique cultural experience. The village has several small shops and cafes, as well as a local art gallery. It is a popular day-trip destination for visitors to Wuppertal, and is just a short drive away. The people of Cronenberg are proud of their local culture and history. They have a strong sense of community and are known for their hospitality, often welcoming visitors to the village with warm smiles and good conversation. Cronenberg, Wuppertal is an idyllic rural community that offers visitors a unique blend of history, culture, and nature. Its picturesque streets and its rich cultural heritage make it a worthwhile destination for anyone looking to explore a corner of Germany that has remained unspoiled.

Geopolitik (alt. geopolitics, from the Greek γεωπολιτική) is the study of the political, military, economic, and cultural influence of a state on its neighboring states in order to achieve or maintain its domination on the world stage. A byproduct of this concept and practice is to analyze the effects of inter-state interaction and the strategic maneuvering and balancing of geopolitical power within a given region. This concept originates from the early 19th century, based on ideas created by German scholars such as Friedrich Ratzel, and is often divided into two strands: the traditional, geopolitical (which has something to do with physical geography and the environment) and the modern, geo-economic geopolitik, which examines the economic and political implications of globalization. The traditional geopolitical school of thought emerged in the late 19th century as a result of the growing nationalism of the era. It proposed that states must seek to expand their borders in order to ensure their survivability, and that the environment within which states interact would be largely determined by their own geopolitical ambitions, be they colonial or continental in origin. Within this framework, territorial gains were seen as desirable by some, while the idea of a “balance of power” taken with anxious alarm by others. The modern, geo-economic school of thought is the result of the combination of the two main ideas behind traditional geopolitics: territorial gains, and power balancing. It sees not just territorial claims, but also economic goals as the true epicenters of power. For this reason, by studying geo-economic forces, many scholars have sought to add a new dimension to the traditional geopolitical worldview. This school emphasizes the importance of an individual state’s economic and trade policies, business decision-making, and even discussions of foreign policy in order to understand its actions in the international arena. Today, geopolitik is a large academic field, and is considered a particularly important tool for foreign policy analysis. Many governments have under their control dedicated departments and institutions charged with monitoring regional political and economic trends and their respective effect on the country's security and development. Moreover, geopolitik has become an important issue for research and discussion, with its implications for both national and international peace and co-operation.

Mike Kasnoff (born 1980) is an American business executive and entrepreneur. He is the co-founder and CEO of Kasnoff Ventures, a venture and commercialization firm headquartered in San Francisco, California. Kasnoff was born in South Plainfield, New Jersey. He graduated from Rutgers University in 2002 with a degree in marketing. He went on to hold various senior positions at several leading technology companies, including Yahoo!, Renzoo and CrowdO. At CrowdO, he was responsible for mobile platform development and strategic partnerships. Kasnoff founded Kasnoff Ventures in 2013. He and his team specialize in start-up, technology and operational consulting services for early-stage ventures and large companies. The company works with both investors and entrepreneurs to help them maximize growth, productivity and user experience. Kasnoff Ventures has been involved in the growth and success of over a dozen early stage ventures in the past 5 years. Kasnoff is actively involved in the startup and venture capital community. He is a mentor at 500 Startups, and serves as an advisor to numerous start-ups in their early stages. He also provides strategic guidance to a number of venture capital firms, helping them identify and secure investments in promising startups. Kasnoff has been featured in several publications and networks, such as Forbes, CNBC, Fox News and Bloomberg. In addition, he is a regular contributor to various business and technology magazines, sharing his insights on the latest trends and topics in the industry. In his free time, Kasnoff volunteers for several charitable causes, including the Make-a-Wish Foundation and Kidsonomics, a program that teaches financial literacy to school age children. He is also a passionate advocate for the environment and sustainability. Kasnoff currently resides in the San Francisco Bay Area.

The Kalamazoo-class monitor was a class of US Navy ironclad ships designed for the Union Navy during the American Civil War. They served in various roles, such as blockade runners and support vessels. The class was originally designed by Capt. John C. Watson at the Naval Academy in Annapolis, Maryland. The class comprised seven wooden-hulled, steam-powered warships of around 1250 tons and 200 feet in length. The class was named after the city of Kalamazoo, Michigan and initially consisted of the USS Kalamazoo, USS Chicopee, USS Montauk, USS Passaconaway, USS Wissahickon, USS Oneota, and USS Tippecanoe. The main armament of the Kalamazoo-class monitors was designed for close-range engagements with Confederate ironclads. They were equipped with eight, 10-inch Dahlgren smoothbore guns, four on each broadside. Additionally, they carried four 3-inch rifles and two 24-pounder howitzers as bow and stern chase guns. The lower deck was armored with four-inch thick iron plates on the sides, and two-inch thick iron plates on the beam and over the gun ports. The Kalamazoo-class monitors performed numerous operations as part of the Union Navy's River Defense Fleet, most notably at the Battle of Mobile Bay during the Civil War. During their short career, the ships saw action in the Gulf of Mexico, the Atlantic Ocean, and off the coast of South America. Following the Civil War, the vessels were placed in various locations throughout the world. The vessels slowly deteriorated over time and most had been scrapped by the early-twentieth century. Today, the USS Montauk is the only remaining monitorship in the world and is preserved as a historic site at the Promised Land State Park in Pennsylvania. The vessel is considered an important relic of America’s Civil War history and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1967. Although the Kalamazoo-class monitors made a relatively short cameo in the history of the US Navy, their memory still lives on.

Walcheren Barracks is a historic military facility located in the city of Leiden, in the province of South Holland, Netherlands. The barracks were built between 1825 and 1834 to house the garrison of troops stationed in the city. During the Second World War, the Walcheren Barracks served as the headquarters for the German forces in the Netherlands. The barracks have since been used as a cultural center, housing several educational and artistic organizations. The Walcheren Barracks was originally constructed at the beginning of the 19th century to serve as a defensive base against the French. The complex, composed of four two-story buildings connected by a central courtyard, was designed by Jan Cornelis Baer in the neoclassical style. Its four large and solid blocks were designed to house up to 1,000 soldiers. During the Second World War, the Barracks served as the base of operations for German forces located in the Leiden area. After the Allied liberation of the Netherlands in 1945, the Barracks were taken over by the Dutch Ministry of Defence. The facility was used to house troops until the 1960s, when it was decommissioned and handed over to the municipality of Leiden for use as a cultural center. The complex was then extensively renovated and refitted. The exterior was restored to its original state, while the interior was adapted for its new purpose. The Walcheren Barracks now houses a number of different educational, cultural, and artistic organizations. These include the Leiden Conservatory of Music, the Leiden Symphony Orchestra, the Leiden Institute of Art History, and the Leiden University Library. Today, the Walcheren Barracks is a popular tourist destination, attracting thousands of visitors each year. It is open to the public for guided tours and hosts a variety of educational events and concerts. The Barracks are a testament to the city’s rich military and cultural history, and a reminder of the courage and resilience of the people of Leiden during the Second World War.

Hippotes (or Hippotus) is an ancient Greek mythical creature, mentioned in various classical texts, usually described as having the head of a horse and the body of a man. He is sometimes also associated with having wings. Hippotes is related to the centaurs, half-man and half-horse creatures who represented untamed nature. In one version of the myth, Hippotes was the son of Ixion and the cloud constructed by Zeus, Nephele. He was one of the Lapiths, a legendary people in Ancient Greece, who fought a battle against the centaurs at the wedding of Pirithous and Hippodamia. The centaurs were uninvited guests of the wedding and they attempted to abduct Hippodamia, the bride. It was Hippotes who fought the centaurs and drove them away. In other versions of the myth, Hippotes was the son of Centaurus and the nymph Chelone. Centaurs were descended from a creature with the upper body of a man and the lower body of a horse. Hippotes was a demigod with the upper body of a man and the lower body of a horse. He is associated with a ruling nature over horses and a divine gift of prophecy, which he would use to warn of coming events. He was a symbol of wisdom and a protector of horses. Hippotes was also associated with the god Ares and is said to have fought in battles with him. He was believed to have fought alongside Heracles during his Tenth Labour, the capture of Cerberus from the underworld. Hippotes fed and managed the horses of the divine hero. The iconography of Hippotes was mainly developed in Sicily, appearing on red-figured vases and terracotta figures, often merged with Ares and the rising of the centaurs. He also appears with Hermes, Castor, Apollo and sometimes, as a tamer of horses, Heracles. He is also depicted as part of the dynasties of heavenly and divine creatures, among the centaurs and satyrs. Hippotes was a popular figure in antiquity and sometimes referred to as a symbol of fertility, wealth, or power. After centuries of use, the iconography of Hippotes became lesser known and more obscure, and his name and identity were largely forgotten. He is still occasionally referenced in classical literature, however, along with his association with Ares, deity of war.

The Young Avengers is a team of teenage superheroes appearing in American comic books published by Marvel Comics. The original members of the team were Kate Bishop, Eli Bradley, Cassie Lang, Tommy Shepherd and Iron Lad. The team was first established by writer Allan Heinberg and artist Jim Cheung in the 2019 comic Young Avengers. The series follows the lives of a group of teenage superheroes as they fight against evil forces in the Marvel Universe. The team's members are associated with established Marvel superheroes, particularly members of the Avengers. The team first appeared in their own self-titled miniseries, and have since been featured in multiple titles and have appeared in numerous crossover storylines. The Young Avengers was formed after a vision of the future showed the team's members being killed by Kang the Conqueror. Heimdall, guardian of the Bifrost, used a time machine to send the team into the past to prevent the future from coming to pass. The team eventually manages to save the future, but in doing so their actions create an alternate future where the team is destroyed by a different threat. The team consists of Kate Bishop, who leads the team and uses the Hawkeye mantle; Eli Bradley, who has the cosmic power of Captain America; Cassie Lang, the daughter of Ant-Man who has the ability to grow and shrink; Tommy Shepherd, the son of Vision and the Scarlet Witch who has reality-warping powers; and Iron Lad, the time-traveler from the future with tech-based powers. Other members have included Wonder Man, an android created by Ultron; Speed, the grandson of Quicksilver; and Wiccan and Hulkling, twin sons of the Scarlet Witch and Vision. The Young Avengers have appeared in various comics and storylines, such as Marvel's musical crossover story "Avengers: Children's Crusade" and the 2020 "Emperor Doom" storyline. They have also appeared in various animated television series, including The Avengers: Earth's Mightiest Heroes and its follow-up series Avengers Assemble. Members of the team have also appeared in various Marvel video games, including Lego Marvel Super Heroes and Marvel: Ultimate Alliance 3: The Black Order. The Young Avengers have also been featured in novels, such as The Avengers: Endgame Prelude, and various other media, such as Funko Pop figurines. The team has been met with critical acclaim, with reviewers praising the diverse backgrounds of the members and their characterization. The series has also been a commercial success, with many collected editions becoming bestsellers.

H. D. Shourie (born Hari Dayal Shourie; 1936- ) is an Indian lawyer who is a champion of free speech and human rights. He is known especially for his involvement in the cases involving Salman Rushdie, the Satanic Verses, and Taslima Nasreen. Shourie was born in Simla, India, in 1936. He studied law at Punjab University in Chandigarh, graduating in 1961. He practiced lawyer and appeared before the Supreme Court in India. He was a part of the legal team in the Salman Rushdie case, filed by the Indian Government in the late 1980s. In the proceedings, Shourie argued that the Indian Government had acted illegally in attempting to ban the publication of the book, The Satanic Verses, and did not have the power to interfere in the affairs of publishers. His arguments are said to have influenced the Court in its decision to grant freedom of speech in the case instead of favoring censorship. Over the years, Shourie has taken part in a wide range of human rights and censorship cases, including defending the rights of the writer Taslima Nasreen in India to be able to express her views without fear. In 2005, he was part of a legal team opposing a law proposed in Delhi that would have stopped people from showing cartoons and other forms of entertainment to children outside of cinemas. The proposed law would have heavily affected street performers and storytellers. Shourie argued against this bill and the High Court in Delhi eventually decided in favor of free speech. Shourie has been an outspoken opponent of censorship and an advocate of free speech throughout his career. He has lectured extensively on the subject matter and written several books defending free speech. In 1998, he wrote a book titled Freedom First: A Critique of Fundamentalism which argued that India should be open to all forms of expression and criticism. In his recent book, Fundamentals Not Freedoms: Are We Degrading Our Political Culture, Shourie critiques a lack of intellectual freedoms in India and draws attention to the importance of having a vibrant and open democracy. Shourie has been a powerful voice in the fields of human rights and freedom of speech in India and continues to be an important figure in these causes. He is an inspiration to many and an example of someone who is willing to stand up for the causes they believe in, no matter the cost.

The 1889–90 season was the nineteenth season of competitive football played by Small Heath F.C., an English football club based in Birmingham. It was the club's first season as members of the Football Alliance and their first as a senior club. Small Heath began their season with a 6–0 home win against Tottenham Hotspur on 6 September 1889. This was the opening game of the inaugural Football Alliance and the first in the club's history as a senior side, having turned professional in the summer. They went on to record league wins against Bootle, Newton Heath, Northwich Victoria and Walsall Town, while their home game against Great Lever ended as a draw. However, these results were not enough to ensure survival in the Football Alliance, and Small Heath were relegated at the end of their first season with a record of six wins, four draws and sixteen defeats. Small Heath's cup season was more successful as they reached the Second Round of the FA Cup. After beating local rivals West Bromwich Albion 4–2 in the First Round, the club faced Nottingham Forest at Stanley Park and lost 1–0. They also entered the Birmingham Senior Cup for the first time and reached the final, which was played at Muntz Street. They faced Aston Villa for a place in the semi-finals of the competition, but were beaten 4–1. The 1889–90 season was the only time Small Heath would compete as a part of the Football Alliance, as the team folded at the end of the season. The club rejoined the Football League the following season, becoming founder members of the Second Division. They remained members of the division until gaining promotion to the First Division in 1894. During the 1889–90 season, Small Heath achieved their highest-ever attendance when, on 27 December 1889, some 20,000 people watched the club's game against West Bromwich Albion at Muntz Street. In the same season, the club also achieved their highest ever victory when they beat Tottenham Hotspur 6–0 on the opening day of the Football Alliance season.

John the Bookmaker controversy was a major scandal that broke out in the United Kingdom in the early 2000s. It was centred around an individual known as John the Bookmaker, Real name John Quinn, who had operated a prolific betting business throughout the UK including the London Stock Exchange and other high-profile financial institutions. John's activities were uncovered through the findings of an extensive investigation by the Financial Services Authority and other relevant regulatory bodies. It was found that he had operated an illegal bookmaking business, taking bets from a variety of people across different sources, and that he was able to do this through deceptive online tools, a complex network of front companies, and false declarations of income. Furthermore, it was discovered that John had bribed key individuals at the London Stock Exchange and other institutions to help him with his activities. The Exchange, who had long been oblivious to his activities and practices, was deeply embarrassed and angered by the revelations. As a result of this scandal, the FSA was forced to take action and John was fined GBP 5 million. He was also banned from ever placing bets again and was put on an indefinite leave with an immediate cessation of his activities. This case highlighted the vulnerabilities of the UK's financial institutions and the need for better regulatory controls and oversight. In addition to the financial sanctions, this scandal also damaged the reputation of the London Stock Exchange and the UK's financial regulators and raised questions about their effectiveness. It also triggered numerous debates on the regulation of the gambling and betting industry. John the Bookmaker controversy has left a permanent stain on the reputation of the United Kingdom financial world, and it continues to be a source of contention and debate to this day. The controversy has caused online gambling websites and services to be more closely regulated and scrutinised and has also led to stricter regulations on bookmakers and other betting businesses.

The Year of the Everlasting Storm, also known as the Year of the Eternal Storm or the Great Storm of 1134, was a period of natural disasters and civil unrest that severely affected much of the Middle East during the 1130s and 1140s CE. The exact cause of the storm remains unknown, though various theories have been proposed, including cyclones, droughts, volcanic activity, and cyclic oceanic changes. It was marked by a series of intense weather events, resulting in loss of life, crop failures, and displacement of populations. The storm is believed to have begun in the late 1130s and lasted for most of the 1140s, lasting an estimated 15 to 17 years. Weather events ranged from floods to an unprecedented heatwave and drought in Syria, Palestine, and Northern Mesopotamia, which caused a series of famines and caused massive demographic and social changes throughout the region. Egypt was hit by a series of powerful sandstorms that destroyed its buildings and agriculture, while further north in Anatolia, severe flooding also wreaked havoc on the region's population. In Palestine, the storms destroyed the majority of the food stores, creating a famine and forcing Jewish families to flee to nearby cities. Around 1145, Geniza documents indicate that the storm had lingered for so long that famished refugees started trading their children for food. In the aftermath, the ruling powers of the region collapsed, with civil war erupting in the Ayyubid Sultanate. The weather changes caused by the storm were also devastating for the region's environment. In some areas, water sources dried up completely, with as much as 90 percent of water sources in some areas completely gone. This led to a rapid decline in crop production, causing food shortages and disruption of the subsistence economy. The lack of resources led to the decline of domesticated animals, with horse and camel populations being the hardest hit. The war and weather events of the Year of the Everlasting Storm had lasting repercussions that continue to affect the region to this day. The area that was once teeming with life now lies mostly desolate, and the suffering caused by the disaster has been estimated to have cost the lives of millions of people. In recent years, it has been used as a cautionary tale by environmentalists, to highlight the dangers of climate change and the need for better adaptation measures.

Leon James (born 6 April 1988) is an English professional footballer who plays as a winger for National League club Aldershot Town. James started his career at a young age in the youth academy of English club Cheltenham Town and signed his first professional contract at the age of 18. While with Cheltenham Town, James made 61 appearances, scoring six goals. During his time with Cheltenham Town, he experienced two brief loan spells in the lower leagues for Kettering Town and Altrincham, resulting in ten appearances for both clubs. In 2012 he moved to Torquay United, signing a two-year deal. While at Torquay United, he made 65 appearances, scoring ten goals. At the end of his two-year contract, he chose to leave the club, having turned down multiple offers to stay. James subsequently joined Dover Athletic on a one-year contract. While with Dover Athletic, he made 33 appearances and scored four goals. At the end of his contract he was released by the club. After a brief spell at Dartford, James signed for Aldershot Town in the National League in 2016. In his time as a professional, James has won the National League South with Dover Athletic and many fans regard him as one of the finest wingers in the English lower leagues.

Martin Ferdinand Morris (born May 3, 1979) is an American entrepreneur and computer scientist. He is the President and Chief Executive Officer of Infinity Cloud Systems, Inc., a well-known Silicon Valley high-tech firm specializing in cloud computing solutions and enterprise applications. Morris was born and raised in Los Angeles, California. He attended the University of California, Berkeley, where he received his Bachelor's and Master's degrees in computer science in 2001 and 2003, respectively. After graduation, Morris went to work at Huawei Technologies, a Chinese multinational telecommunications company, where he was a software engineer. It was at this time that he became interested in the potential of cloud computing, and he soon left Huawei to join Ciber Inc., a major IT solutions provider. At Ciber, Morris managed a team of software engineers and led the development of the company's new cloud computing platform. In 2008, he was named CFO of Ciber, where he was responsible for the company's financial planning, risk management, and business development strategies. In 2011, Morris left Ciber and founded Infinity Cloud Systems, Inc., with the goal of developing software applications and cloud solutions for businesses of all sizes. Since then, he has been instrumental in transforming the company from a startup to an established leader in the cloud computing market. In addition to his work at Infinity Cloud Systems, Morris is an active member of the Palo Alto chapter of the Entrepreneurs' Organization (EO). He is also a regular contributor to TechCrunch, an online technology blog, where he often provides insight and advice for aspiring entrepreneurs. Morris has also been featured in multiple media outlets, such as the Wall Street Journal, Forbes, Bloomberg, and TIME. In 2017, he was named one of the top ten cloud computing influencers in the world. Morris has been married since 2009 to his wife, Barb, and they have three children. In his spare time, he enjoys beach volleyball and playing guitar. Throughout his career, Morris has consistently been awarded for his innovative approaches to technology, proven track record of success in the field, and commitment to developing cutting-edge solutions. He is passionate about helping businesses and individuals embrace cloud technology, and he hopes to continue to do so in the years to come.

10551 Göteborg is a Swedish town located in the province of Västra Götaland. It is situated on the southern shore of Lake Vänern, the largest lake in Sweden, and is part of the municipality of Skövde. The population of 10551 Göteborg is approximately 5,000 people, making it one of the smaller towns in the province. The town is serviced by the line 5 of the Göteborgs Spårväg, making it a convenient location to live for commuters and travellers. The town is home to two historic churches, the Maria Magdalena Church and the Stora Torg, both of which date back to the late 19th century. There are also a few small museums in the town, including the Skøvde Museum and the Norrala Folk Museum. The manorial estate of Norrala, located near the town, is also a popular tourist attraction and is home to a large collection of artefacts related to the ancient Norse and Svear people. In recent years the town has seen an increase in the number of bars, restaurants and other entertainment venues. 10551 Göteborg is also popular amongst the younger demographic due to its proximity to the larger cities of Göteborg and Stockholm, both of which provide excellent nightlife and entertainment offerings.
