In recent years 10551 Göteborg has become one of the most desirable tourist destinations in Sweden, due to its peaceful nature, stunning views of the lake, and laid-back atmosphere. Visitors come to explore the town’s picturesque streets, delicious eateries, and range of activities, making it a popular destination for both locals and tourists alike. The town has something to offer everyone, whether you’re seeking relaxation or excitement. 10551 Göteborg is the perfect holiday spot for any traveller looking to explore the beauty of Sweden.

Marita Engzelius (born 1971) is an award-winning Norwegian wildlife photographer and conservationist. She is best known for her breathtaking photographs of polar bears, seabirds, and the Arctic wilderness, with a focus on highlighting the impact of climate change on the Arctic environment. Engzelius was born in 1971 and grew up in southern Norway. She first developed an interest in the outdoors and nature from her father, a biology teacher, and spent much of her childhood exploring the forests and countryside in and around her hometown. As a young adult, she studied biology at the University of Oslo, but found that she was more interested in the practical aspects of the environment than the scientific aspects. After university, Engzelius spent a summer in Spitsbergen, a group of islands in the high Arctic. That experience, coupled with her lifelong passion for nature, inspired her to become a wildlife photographer. She has since become an acclaimed photographer, with her work having appeared in numerous publications and magazines, including National Geographic, Smithsonian, The Atlantic, and BBC Wildlife. As much as Engzelius loves taking photographs, her passion for the environment extends far beyond the camera. She is a leading voice within the conservation movement and works to protect Arctic wildlife from the rapid impacts of climate change. Her work has been critical in raising awareness of the dangers posed by climate change, and she has worked to create and advance solutions to protect the environment. Engzelius is an advocate for sustainable development in the Arctic and serves as a board member for organizations such as the Norwegian Wild Salmon Centre and the Norwegian Polar Institute. She often serves as a spokeswoman for these organizations, highlighting the need for policy reform to reduce the effects of climate change on the Arctic environment. Engzelius has won numerous awards for her work, including the prestigious Canon Female Photojournalist Award for her work in the high Arctic, the Grand Prix de la Compétition Des Animaux Sauvages, and the IUCN/The IUCN Red List Annual Journalists Award. Her work has been exhibited around the world, including in London, Tokyo, and Paris, and has inspired people to take a stand for protecting and conserving the Arctic environment. Marita Engzelius is a passionate wildlife photographer and conservationist whose work has raised awareness of the urgent need to protect Arctic wildlife from the impacts of climate change. Her photography and outreach have been instrumental in inspiring leaders to create and shape policy to safeguard the environment, and her ongoing work continues to raise awareness and promote positive environmental change.

Shuanglian metro station (simplified Chinese: 双联地铁站; traditional Chinese: 雙联地鐵站; pinyin: Shuānglián Dìtiě Zhàn) is located in the city of Guangzhou, China. It is an underground station on Line 9 of the Guangzhou Metro that opened along with the rest of the line on 28 December 2014. The station has an island platform. It is accessible from Exit B of Shuanglian Overpass and is located beneath the junction of Raoping Road and Huanshi East Road (Chinese: 环市东路). It is surrounded by shopping malls and other commercial establishments. The station's logo is square with a triangle inside, symbolizing the unique shape of the Shuanglian Overpass. It also has a slogan, "Justice and Prosperity", representing the concept of making justice. The station serves areas such as Huanshi East Road, Hongxing Road (Chinese: 红星路), Jiabin Road (Chinese: 嘉宾路) and Xinheng Road (Chinese: 信恒路). It takes about 18 minutes to reach Shuanglian Station from the Guangzhou East Railway Station. Transfer is available with Line 5 at East Railway Station which is located in the East of Luoxi (Chinese: 洛溪). As a major station on Line 9, Shuangian Station is equipped with facilities such as ticket gate, escalators and elevators, as well as other public amenities. The station has free Wi-Fi, ATMs, and a lost and found service. There are also public restrooms and information boards to guide visitors to their desired destinations. Shuanglian Station also provides information about local attractions and tourist destinations. The nearby Chen Clan Academy (Chinese: 陈家祠), for instance, is just a few minutes’ walk from the station. Visitors can also find places of interests nearby such as the Guangdong Provincial Museum (Chinese: 广东省博物馆) and the Guangdong Revolutionary History Memorial Hall (Chinese: 广东革命历史纪念馆). Apart from being a major station on Line 9, Shuanglian Station is also an important thoroughfare for both locals and visitors. The underground section of the station connects to the commercial establishments located outside the station, including the Lions of the East and the Sky Financial Center. The commercial area around Shuanglian Station is well-known for its shops and restaurants, where locals and tourists alike can enjoy a wide variety of food, including regional delicacies and international cuisines. It also has multiple shopping malls and electronic markets, making it a popular spot for shopping among locals and tourists alike.

The Louisville and Nashville Depot of Evergreen, Alabama, is an important landmark in the city that was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1974. The two-story Romanesque Revival style depot was built in 1903 and served as the main passenger depot in the city for the Louisville and Nashville Railroad until 1971. The depot is a two-story red brick building that was designed by noted architect Jarrott McKnight. The interior of the depot was designed to be ornate, with the ceilings and walls covered in tile and mosaic. The building also originally featured three waiting rooms, ticket offices, and a restaurant. The building served as not only a passenger depot, but also a major center of commerce. During the 1930s and 40s many cotton producers used the facility to ship and receive products while several personal offices and freight companies opened at the adjacent freight office. The depot has been an important part of Evergreen's history for over a century and is among the few remaining depots from the Louisville and Nashville Railroad that still exists. The depot is located in the center of the city directly across from the Conecuh County Court House. In October 2019, the Evergreen Preservation Group acquired the building from CSX in an effort to restore the depot and create a gateway to downtown Evergreen for residents and tourists. The preservation group intends to renovate the depot with the assistance of grants from the state and federal governments and to use the facility to host local events. The goal is to create a cultural hub and community center in the heart of the city. The Louisville and Nashville Depot in Evergreen is a critical part of the city's history and has served the community for decades. The recent preservation effort promises to protect this landmark for future generations and to create a vibrant hub for citizens of the city.

Chonda Pierce (born March 4, 1960) is an American stand-up comedian, television host, author, actor, and comedy writer. Pierce has become one of the most successful female comedians in the United States with several of her comedy albums going Platinum. She has been referred to as "the Queen of Clean" for her ability to use her comedy to effectively deliver powerful truths about daily life. Pierce was born and raised in the small town of South Parkersburg, West Virginia. She has described her earliest laughs being in church with her mother and sisters. She moved to Nashville in 1983 and began performing regularly as a standup comic. She was featured on the Grand Ole Opry. In addition to stage performances, Pierce has been featured in several television specials, including the ‘Women of Faith’ series and TBN's ‘Laugh, Smile, Cry’ series. In 2005, Pierce became the first female comedian to narrate a successful animated film, The Wild Stallion. Pierce was most widely known for hosting the game show, Weakest Link-Garbage Edition, with fellow comedian Jeff Foxworthy. This show ran from 2003 to 2006. In 2007, she was featured in her own Showtime Comedy Special, ‘Chonda Pierce-Laughter’s Good Medicine’. She has written several books, launched her own production company—Chonda Pierce Productions, made multiple appearances on the Nashville Network, and appeared on ABC’s 20/20 and Oprah. Pierce has received many awards and honors, including induction into the Gospel Music Hall of Fame, receiving the Gospel Music Association’s Dove Award nine times, and winning the American Comedy award. In addition, Pierce has been recognized with several honorary degrees, including Doctor of Humane Letters from Trevecca University and Adult and Continuing Education. Pierce is a dedicated spokesperson for bringing attention to depression and mental health issues. She has been candid about her own struggles with depression and her journey of recovery. The Lifetime movie ‘Smiling Through the Pain’ (2020) was based on Pierce’s personal story. In 2019, Pierce launched the ‘Renewed with Chonda Pierce’ podcast which focuses on conversations and stories related to mental health and well being. Pierce continues to use her platform to bring attention to the importance of mental health and the need for more compassion in conversations. Pierce is a relentless and beloved comedian and continues to use her voice to bring laughter and hope to the lives of many.

The Philadelphian cricket team in England in 1897 was a team of cricket players from Philadelphia in the United States that toured England in 1897. The team were organised by Alec Hearne and was led by Algy Kingscote. The team had twenty-one players, including seven professionals and fourteen amateurs. The Philadelphia Cricket Club sent fourteen of its current and past members, while the Germantown Cricket Club contributed seven players. The seven professional players were from the United States - Alec Hearne and Harold Weeks from the Philadelphia Cricket Club, and the rest from the Germantown Cricket Club: Hugh Marshall, Harry Wright, I. M. Gregory, W. V. Gregory, and C. Y. Hargrave. The tour began on June 18, 1897, with a draw against Yorkshire in Sheffield. The team then went on to play twenty four-day matches and one three-day match against other county sides, as well as several other first-class and non-first-class teams. They played a total of twenty-six matches, with eight wins, eight losses, and ten draws. In the twenty-four day matches, they won three games and drew the remaining five. These wins were against Worcestershire, Hampshire, and a combined Oxford-Cambridge Universities Junior side. They lost to Surrey, Somerset, Sussex, Kent, and Lancashire. The Philadelphians also competed in the 1897 Gentlemen v Players match and the Gentlemen of England v Australians match. Although they lost both games, they were able to compete soon after arriving in England, something of an accomplishment given the gap in professionalism between the English and American players. At the end of the tour, Alec Hearne was named captain of the Philadelphian team for the tour of North America and Australia in 1898-99. The team played a total of twenty-three first-class and non-first class matches, with eleven wins and four losses. The tour was a success and helped to set the foundation for the future of international cricket and the growth of the game in the United States. The Philadelphian cricket team in England in 1897 is remembered for being the first team of cricketers from the United States to tour England and compete in international cricket, a feat that was not repeated until the tour of Australia and Great Britain by the Philadelphia Wanderers in 1929.

. Pea (disambiguation) Pea is a plant, sometimes referred to as a legume, and its edible seed. It is most commonly found in Pod fruit form, where it is the seed inside a green, inedible casing. The scientific name for the plant is Pisum sativum. Also called garden pea, green pea, and English pea, it is an annual plant in the Fabaceae family. The term "pea" may also refer to: * Sea pea, a species of flowering plant in the lentil genus Lens * Lathyrus sativus, a grass pea species * Pea (color), a greenish-yellow color * Pea protein, a plant-based protein isolate derived from peas * PEA (plant extract), an extract of the pea plant * Pea coat, a type of coat * Persistent erectile dysfunction (also abbreviated PEDA), a form of impotence * Pea, a comic book series by Property of BKV * Pea-Sized, a character from the webcomic, Kemono Michi The name "Pea" is also associated with other items, for example a character from the game Animal Crossing may be called "Peanut" and a species of fish may be called "Peacock". In addition the term "pea" may be used as a slang term, in reference to someone's head. The term "pea" is also occasionally used to refer to people, such as in the expression "you pea". This expression is mostly used in the United Kingdom. The usage of the term "pea" in foodstuffs varies worldwide, depending on the culture and region. Green peas, green pea pods, yellow/orange split peas, and various types of pickled, canned, and frozen peas are all staples in many kitchens. Finally, the term "pea" may also refer to the pinyin spelling of the Chinese characters 豌豆.

Raven Davis (born 12 May 1994) is an American entrepreneur, author, and business coach. She is the founder and CEO of Poised and Powerful, a business training and consulting firm that helps small businesses and entrepreneurs make a bigger impact in their respective industries. She is a well-known advocate of financial literacy and education and has been featured in various publications, including Forbes, The Huffington Post, and Cosmopolitan. Raven grew up in suburban Maryland and received her B.A. in Business Studies and Media & Communications from the University of Maryland Eastern Shore. After a stint in corporate America, she decided to pursue entrepreneurship. With a focus on entrepreneurship, she launched Poised & Powerful in April 2014 and since then has helped countless entrepreneurs grow their businesses. She has provided elite coaching to female entrepreneurs, helping them to become more confident and successful by providing business and financial education, mindset shifts, and practical tools for business growth. Raven is also an advocate for financial literacy and education, especially for women and young people. She has come up with creative ways to help individuals who are struggling with debt and credit issues, from launching a financial literacy program for high school students and working with families to teach them about credit and managing finances. She is a voice and inspiration for women entrepreneurs everywhere and her words have been shared around the globe. In addition to her work in business and financial consulting, Raven is also an author and speaker. She writes to help women become empowered financially, spiritually, and professionally. Her books—The Financial Divorce, The Wealth Conscious Mother: Redefining Wealth Beyond Money, and Principles of Power—have been published in multiple countries and languages. She also appears at various events, such as the Forbes’ Women’s Summit, to empower and motivate her audience. Raven's mission is to equip people with the knowledge, tools and support they need to create a financially successful life. She has done just that, not only through her professional efforts, but through her own personal journey. She has taken her story full circle, from her childhood in Maryland to now living a financially liberated life as an entrepreneur, author and international speaker. Raven continues to work, learn, and motivate all those she encounters and with that, she leaves behind a legacy of power, prosperity, and possibilities.

Facet (geometry) is a term used to describe the numerous flat faces or side surfaces of a three-dimensional object. It is alos referred to as a face, which can refer to either one of the side surfaces or to multiple side surfaces. Each of these facets of a polyhedron, or three-dimensional shape, serve as two-dimensional boundaries or molds of the three-dimensional shape. In Euclidean geometry, a facet of a polyhedron is defined as a piece of the surface that can be bounded by a single line or circle. The edges of the facets are also traditional lines or circles, depending on the shape of the polyhedron. In general, a facet must contain at least three edges, since fewer than three edges can only define a straight line and cannot bound a surface. The number of faces, or facets, a three-dimensional object has is related to the degree of rotation symmetry the object has. A cube, for example, has six faces since it is only able to rotate symmetrically in a full 90-degree increment. While a cube has six faces, it has twelve edges, and eight vertices. It is easy to tell that a shape is a cube or cuboid, as it is defined by its facets: each face is composed of squares, hence there are six facets and the shape itself will have an even number of degrees of symmetry (six). Other three-dimensional shapes such as cylinders, pyramids and cones, have a variety of facets and angles, and no two shapes have exactly the same number of facets. Faceted crystals, such as diamonds, are also known as gemstones, and these types of crystals are commonly prized for their aesthetic beauty. Faceted crystals often have many flat, smoothly polished faces which reflect light, a property which enables the gemstones to sparkle. Each of the faces of a faceted crystal is known as a 'facet', with different angles and sizes lending each crystal its individual and unique beauty. In the manufacturing industry, facets are also used as design elements. Facets in product designs can emphasize the underlying shape of the product, and are used to create streamlined or winding shapes. These shapes, however, are usually accomplished by machining rather than facet grinding as this allows for more precise angles and dimensions. Facet is a versatile word, which is not limited to Euclidean geometry, gemstones, and product design but is also used in computer science, economics and other fields. In computer science, for instance, the word facet can be used to describe characteristics of data, while in economics, facets of narrative or information can be used to describe the outcomes of a system or process.

Sonakanda Fort, located atop a hill in the Five Hills range in Konkan region of India, is a historic monument of India. The fort dates back to between 16th and 17th centuries and was built by the Mughal Empire. The fort is believed to have been built to defend against intrusion by Maratha warriors. The origins of Sonakanda Fort are not clearly known. Historical records indicate that this fort was under Chhatrapati of Kolhapur in 16th century and then was captured by Mughal Emperor Akbar. Later on in 17th century it became a part of Maratha Empire under Chhatrapati Shivaji. The fort is rectangular in shape and has two entrances with four bastions. The two bastions were protected by canons. The strong walls and entrance gateways have stood the test of time and the fort is still intact. The fortress overlooking the Arabian Sea covers an area of about 2 acres. There are four toothed gateways and an oversea path connecting the Sonakanda Fort with the nearby Revdanda Fort. Inside the fort, there are two entrances, three watch towers, a storehouse, remnants of small houses, a well and a rivulet. Besides being a historical monument Sonakanda Fort is also a popular tourist spot. People come to Sonakanda Fort to admire the view while overlooking the Sahyadri hills and nearby coastal belt. The near view from the fort is also a great spot for bird watching as many migratory birds can be seen here. Apart from its historical importance and its picturesque setting, Sonakanda Fort has spiritual significance for Hindus. As per local legend, Lord Hanuman, a character from Hindu mythology, used to reside in the fort. There are several red flags in the premise of the fort that mark the abode of Hanuman. One can spend a day exploring the ruins of this ancient fort. There is a fascinating story around Sonakanda Fort that has its origin in the local folklore. It is believed that once upon a time few fishermen roamed around here and by divine intervention they were granted a wish to be part of a princely life. They were given a fort like Sonakanda and indolent palaces to live in. Today Sonakanda Fort is one of the lesser known forts in Konkan and it lies in a state of decay. Although the fort is an important heritage site, it desperately needs attention and repairs, especially of its crumbling walls. Preservation of this ancient fort is necessary to preserve its historical and spiritual importance.

George Henry Radcliffe Parkinson (1901–1983) was an English physician, who is most noted for his description of Parkinson's disease, named after him. He was, however, also active in the fields of pathology and psychosomatic medicine. Born in Sheffield, Yorkshire, Parkinson graduated from Cambridge University in 1923, and went on to earn his MB BCh from the University of Liverpool in 1926. Becoming a member of the Royal College of Physicians in 1929, he remained a practising doctor in Liverpool until 1944. In 1935, Parkinson published a paper on a condition of the nervous system, which he termed 'paralysis agitans', which would later be changed to Parkinson's Disease after him. He noticed that this condition was associated with a degeneration of neurons in the area of the midbrain of some of his patients, and described rigidity, tremor, and slow movement in the afflicted. Parkinson also wrote on topics such as noise-induced deafness, multiple personality, hypertrophic pulmonary osteo-arthropathy, and thorax and laryngeal cancer. He also wrote on problems of aging and mental illness, and was an outspoken advocate for mental health during this time period. Moving to Australia in 1944, Parkinson worked at the University of Melbourne until his retirement in 1967. During his time in Australia, he was the founding medical director of the Prince Henry Hospital and later of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Victoria. After a long and renowned career, Parkinson died in Melbourne on the 23rd of May, 1983. Following his death, he was posthumously awarded the C. J. Martin Medal of the Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists, in recognition of his pioneering work in the field of Parkinson's Disease, and of his high professional standards in Neurology. In 2006, a bronze bust of Parkinson was unveiled at Royal Melbourne Hospital, in recognition of his contribution to medicine. Legacy Despite the more than 4 decades that have passed since his death, Parkinson remains a highly acclaimed figure in the field of Neurology, with the eponymous neurologic condition that he identified in 1935 having affected numerous patients all over the world. His contribution to the fields of pathology, psychosomatic medicine, mental health, and aging remain unrivaled to this day.

Lightweighting is a process for reducing the overall mass of a product or system. It is a popular approach for engineers and designers needing to improve the strength-to-weight ratio in the products they create. There are several methods for lightweighting, and the optimal approach will depend on the context and the desired outcomes. Lightweighting strategies focus on three primary areas: material choices, component designs, and part assembly methods. The type of material chosen for a project will greatly affect its weight. As lightweight materials become lighter and stronger, the weight of products can be reduced without sacrificing strength and durability. Novel composite materials, such as carbon fiber reinforced plastics, are being used in more application than ever before. Engineers and product designers also employ advanced design techniques to reduce weight and material usage. Finite Element Analysis (FEA) tools are used to identify weak points in the design where additional strength is not needed. This informations helps to ensure products are designed to be as lightweight as possible without compromising on function or safety. Assembly methods also play a significant role in lightweighting. Many manufacturers are opting to combine multiple components into single parts to reduce the overall number of parts in a system. This reduces weight and assembly time by eliminating the need to build and align separate parts. Adhesives and fasteners have also become popular methods for attaching parts, as they are lighter and more secure than conventional hardware. Lightweighting is increasingly important for the automotive industry, where reducing the mass of a vehicle can have a dramatic effect on fuel efficiency. Automakers are rapidly adopting more efficient materials and design techniques to create lighter vehicles that maintain their structural integrity and safety features. Lightweighting offers a number of advantages, including improved energy efficiency, reduced emissions, and increased design freedom. With increasing customer demand for lighter and more efficient products, lightweighting will continue to be an important tool in the design process. Through innovative material choices, advanced design strategies, and modern assembly methods, engineers and product designers are creating products that are stronger, lighter, and more sustainable.

Monte Titano is a 739-metre (2,425 ft) mountain located in the heart of San Marino, the world's fifth smallest sovereign state. It is the highest of the three peaks, Monte Titano being the tallest one, which make up the country of San Marino. An ancient fortress, the Guaita was built on top of Monte Titano in the 11th century and it remains as a symbol of San Marino's independence. This picturesque mountain is a popular tourist destination, and offers an unparalleled view of the surrounding area. The earliest mention of Monte Titano is in an 885 land grant from the Holy Roman Emperor, Charles the Fat, to the tiny Christian community of San Marino. This document is still kept in the archives of the state and is the basis of San Marino's national holiday, November 3. Throughout the centuries, Monte Titano has been the site of many defensive fortifications. The Three Towers of San Marino, known as La Cesta, La Montale, and La Guaita, are situated at the top of Monte Titano and form the nucleus of the city. Each of them is over 1,000 years old and part of the first line of defense for the city of San Marino. La Guaita, the oldest and most impressive of the three towers, was built at the highest point of Monte Titano and it is the most famous of the three. It is a four-story building made of pale gray sandstone, its battleship-like silhouette reminiscent of a battleship. Today, Monte Titano stands as a proud symbol of San Marino's unwavering commitment to its independence and freedom. From the Three Towers of San Marino to the beautiful wooded valleys, Monte Titano offers some of the most breathtaking views of the countryside that can be enjoyed by visitors. Besides offering stunning views of the Apennines, the mountain provides unique recreational opportunities to those looking for adventure or simply for the peace and quiet that the natural surroundings of Monte Titano provide. Aside from its glorious historical buildings, outdoor activities on Monte Titano range from leisurely hikes and biking routes to sportive climbing routes. Monte Titano is a popular destination for travelers who want to explore the culture of San Marino as well as its stunning natural surroundings. It remains an integral part of San Marino history and many locals refer to it as “the mountain of freedom”. With its impressive past, stunning vistas and plethora of outdoor activities, Monte Titano will remain a popular destination for many generations to come.

The Witten–Schwelm railway is an important railway line in the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia. It connects the cities of Witten and Schwelm and is closely linked to the surrounding industrial cities and towns, notably Wetter, Hagen, and Sprockhövel. History Construction of the Witten–Schwelm railway began in 1880. The line was largely completed in 1884 and brought together the towns of Witten and Schwelm. It also connected the industrial towns of Herbede, Geisecke, and Hattingen, greatly improving links between these towns and the surrounding region. Transport Services The Witten–Schwelm railway is currently served by Regional-Express and Regionalbahn trains, which operate between Witten and Schwelm roughly every hour, or more often during peak times. The cities of Hattingen, Witten, Wetter and Schwelm are all located along the line, making it popular with commuters. Additional commuter services sometimes operate during peak times, including a direct service from Herbede to Witten. Long-distance connections are also possible via train connections to towns such as Dortmund, Bochum, Essen, and Düsseldorf. Infrastructure The line is double-track for most of its length, with some stretches of single-track. There are also a few passing loops, most notably near Hattingen, Geisecke, and Herbede. The line features several bridges and tunnels. The most famous is the Herbede Tunnel, which is 245 meters long and was built in the early 1900s. The track is generally in good condition, though signalling and mechanical infrastructure is significantly older than on other lines in the region. This has led to a few issues, including regular closures of the line due to malfunctioning signals and shorter operating hours than on other lines. Future The Witten–Schwelm railway is currently undergoing a program of modernisation and improvement. This includes replacing the outdated signals and mechanical infrastructure, as well as extending the passing loops to allow for increased capacity on the line. Additionally, there are plans to extend the line to Hagen, as part of a greater improvement to transport links in the region. The Witten–Schwelm railway is an important part of the North Rhine-Westphalia region's transport links, and with the current program of modernisation, is likely to become even more essential in the near future.

Sriboonruang Wittayakarn School (SWS) is a private school in Bangkok, Thailand. It is a co-educational, non-denominational institution offering kindergarten through secondary education. Founded in 1974 by Mr. Wirat Wittayakarn, the school is divided into two main divisions: the main Elementary school (Kindergarten to Primary 6) and the Secondary school (Lower & Upper). SWS is known as Bangkok’s premier school academically and it’s also highly respected for its strong emphasis on Thai tradition and culture. The student population currently stands at over 4,000. SWS’s mission is to provide quality education to its students. SWS provides an international curriculum, consisting of an English-language program, a Science and Math program, and an Arts program. The school also offers English language learning programs, as well as an Intensive English Program. As a result, many of its graduates are well-prepared to pursue higher academic study in the West. SWS students consistently rank among the top students in standardized tests and major examinations in Thailand. In addition to its academic program, SWS provides students with extracurricular activities. These include clubs, activities and teams for soccer, basketball, badminton, volleyball, swimming, and track and field. The school also have a theater program, with students performing in both classic plays and original works. To foster its Thai identity, Sriboonruang Wittayakarn School places a great emphasis on cultural activities. As part of its Thai culture education program, the school arranges visits to temples and important historical sites. It also encourages its students to take part in traditional ceremonies and cultural festivals, such as the Song Kran Festival and the New Year festivities. The school has long been recognized as one of the top schools in Bangkok. It has been ranked as one of Bangkok’s five best performings schools in the past five years and has been named a “Kristiyan School” by the government of Thailand, a distinction that only the best Thai schools receive. In recent years, SWS has also become a leader in educational reform, and has adopted several progressive teaching methods and ways of assessing student achievement. Despite its rigorous academic program, the school strives to keep its student-teacher ratios low, so that each student receives the attention they need. Sriboonruang Wittayakarn School is an ideal institution for students who are looking for an international education with a focus on traditional Thai culture and high academic standards. With its strong commitment to excellence and its focus on imparting values of respect and responsibility, the school is one of the premier educational centers in Bangkok.

1520 (MDXX) was an important year in world history. The year saw a number of significant events, ranging from important political changes to technological advancements. In politics and diplomacy, 1520 marked the year that the Treaty of Tordesillas was formally signed by Portugal and Spain, formalizing the de facto division between the two empires and setting the stage for a period of Iberian dominance in the Atlantic. This year also saw the election of Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor - a position of power that Charles V held for more than 40 years. 1520 was also an important year in the history of the Ottoman Empire. Suleiman the Magnificent captured the city of Belgrade, a significant victory in what would become known as the Ottoman-Hungarian wars. At the same time, the conquest of Algiers by the Ottomans also took place, culminating in an eight-year siege of this Mediterranean port. In the field of science and culture, 1520 saw an important development in navigation: the Amazon River was encountered by European explorers, leading to the development of a number of new trade routes and expeditions across the ocean. This year also saw the invention of the printing press and paper money, which revolutionized the way information was spread and commerce was conducted. On a related note, the Diet of Worms saw Martin Luther take a stand against the Catholic Church, leading to the development of Protestantism which would have major implications in Europe and the New World. In 1520, the Aztec Emperor Moctezuma II was defeated and killed by Hernán Cortés in Tenochtitlan, thus ending a major era in Mesoamerican history and setting the stage for the colonization of Latin America by the Spanish and Portuguese empires. In 1520, the world population was estimated to be around 450 million, a figure which would more than double to one billion by the mid-19th century. Overall, 1520 was an important year in the history of the world. It saw the formalization of two major empires, a technological revolution, the beginnings of the Protestant Reformation, and the conquest of a major civilization. As a result, its influence can still be felt today.

Delusional intuition is a concept in which individuals believe they possess non-sensed information about their reality or future. It is theorized that the information is often derived from its juxtaposition with ideas of intuition or a sixth sense. Those who experience delusional intuition often have a strong suggestion of the truth behind the concepts but lack any sort of fact to certify the ideas. Delusional intuition is most commonly associated with psychoanalytic theories, which suggest that it is a form of unconscious information that our mind presents to us without conscious thought. This is a concept coined by Sigmund Freud, who argued that the concept aligned with his psychoanalytic models. Freud suggested, “If we accept that the unconscious exists, then delusional intuition is not necessarily the existence of some extra-sensory power.” Other psychoanalysts such as Carl Jung argued that delusional intuition was a manifestation of the collective unconscious. The concept of delusional intuition has been studied in psychology for several decades. Researchers have suggested that individuals who experience delusional intuition have a capacity to acquire knowledge through non-sensory means. This form of intuition is believed to be a form of creative thinking and provides insight to concepts and experiences beyond the ordinary sensory realm. Proponents of this theory argue that although delusional intuition may not necessarily provide accurate truths, it does have the ability to bring forth new solutions and perspectives to existing problems. However, other researchers have argued that delusional intuition is a misinterpretation of sensory information. They suggest that the scenario and its associated aspects trigger the sensations to be perceived as non-sensory information. For example, individuals might see symbols, patterns or colours that may lack any primary meaning. They instead associate it with another context and interpret the experiences as a form of intuition. Although the concept of delusional intuition is commonly discussed in psychological contexts, much debate still occurs to determine the science behind the phenomenon. Many remain unconvinced that it exists beyond the realm of conjecture and doubt that it is a reliable source of knowledge. Others, however, remain hopeful of the potential of discovering truth behind the concept using scientific research. In conclusion, delusional intuition remains a controversial topic in the psychological field. It suggests that individuals can obtain knowledge through non-sensory means, although its quality and accuracy is yet to be determined. More research is needed to uncover the potential of delusional intuition and to what degree it is able to provide insight to the reality of a situation.

Avantika Shetty is an Indian national who pursued her education in three international institutions, graduated from IIT Bombay with an MS degree, and is a CXO in the Information Technology sector. Avantika was born in Kerala, India and obtained her Bachelor of Technology degree in Computer Science from the University of Hyderabad in 2008. Subsequently, she pursued her Master of Science degree in Telecommunications and Computer Networks from Waseda University, Tokyo, Japan, graduating in 2010. She then moved to the United States, to pursue a Master of Science in Computer Science from Stanford University, graduating in 2012. Prior to the completion of her studies, Avantika joined the Tata Consultancy Services team in 2009, which has been her primary professional association to date. After graduating from Stanford, she started her career in Tata’s Information Technology Services division, where she quickly grew as a technical specialist, where she held various positions, her last was as a “CXO”, in which she oversaw several international projects. Throughout her successful career, Avantika has bagged several awards. She was conferred with the Edison Engineering Award by the Educational Foundation of Edison International in 2013, for her contributions to the engineering industry. In 2018, she was awarded the “Tech Master” award by the Asian Network of Technology and Investment and in 2020, she won the “Excellence in Technology” award at the “10th Asia-Pacific Career and Employer Branding Awards”. Avantika Shetty is also involved in several social activities away from her professional commitments. She has invested in educational initiatives in India, with a focus on providing young people with the resources and opportunities to excel in life. She is also passionate about environment conservation and climate change, and has been associated with many charities and initiatives to promote sustainable development. Avantika Shetty is an accomplished individual, having pursued an extraordinary education, held illustrious positions in one of the most respected organisations in the world, and made a social impact through several initiatives. She is an inspirational figure and an exemplary role model for everyone striving for excellence.

Rosemont College is a private liberal arts college located in Rosemont, Pennsylvania. Founded in 1921 by the Sisters of the Holy Child Jesus, Rosemont is part of a network of 25 independent Catholic colleges and universities across the United States. Rosemont offers more than 40 undergraduate majors and minors, as well as nine graduate and doctoral programs. The college offers seasonal study abroad programs in countries such as Italy, Mexico, and Spain. Rosemont's main campus consists of 51 acres in Lower Merion, Pennsylvania, just outside of Philadelphia. The core campus includes four academic buildings, all organized around an open quadrangle. Along with traditional, on-campus housing, the college also offers a variety of non-traditional housing options, including themed residencies, and supplemental housing for graduate students. The college has a strong commitment to social justice and service. Rosemont sponsors a number of service learning projects each year, as well as seven service trips to different countries every summer. Its robust extra-curricular activities include a wide range of student clubs, honor societies, athletic teams, and student government. Its service organizations include Amnesty International, the Red Cross Club, and the Humane Society Club. Rosemont's Career Development Office helps students with career exploration, job shadowing, internships, and other professional opportunities. The office also has a job board with over 600 job postings. Rosemont partners with a variety of employers to connect its students with career-oriented experiences. Rosemont College has a vibrant alumni network that provides opportunities for social and professional networking. Alumni have gone on to serve in positions of leadership in industry, government, education, health care and other fields. They provide a support network for graduates, offering networking possibilities, internships, and job postings through their LinkedIn group. Rosemont College prides itself as a strong community with a diverse student body, excellent faculty, rich history and traditions, and a commitment to academic excellence.

The Yeti with Betty is a 2019 American horror film directed by April Brown and written by Brown and Sarah-Lisa Bourrette. It stars Justin Badger as a recluse who is hired as the personal caretaker of Betty Lou (Patricia Culligan), an elderly woman in a remote cabin in the woods. Together, they discover the existence of a mysterious yeti creature living in the woods. The Yeti with Betty follows a socially-awkward yeti researcher, Justin (Badger), who becomes a personal caretaker for Betty Lou, an elderly woman in a newly inherited cabin in a remote location. Although Betty is initially completely oblivious to the yeti’s existence, Justin can sense it lurking in the shadows and soon finds himself exploring the unexplored land with Betty. Upon his discoveries in the woods, Justin quickly finds himself being targeted by the unseen force and leads him to risk his life to uncover the truth behind the invisible being. With Betty Lou’s help, the two uncover secrets and clues to the yeti’s existence. Together, they must eventually come together to save themselves and the yeti from a devious, unknown entity. The Yeti with Betty has been generally well-received, praised for its blend of horror and comedy. The film received 7/10 stars from critics, noting its unique atmosphere and intriguing storyline. Cinematography of the exterior locations were also praised, with many citing the remote atmosphere and lush visuals. Additionally, the cast were lauded for their performances, especially Badger’s and Culligan’s development of their characters throughout the film. The Yeti with Betty is available for streaming via Digital Download, DVD, and Blu-ray. The film has also been nominated for several awards, winning Best Horror Feature at the 2019 Nashville Film Festival, Best Narrative Feature at the 2019 San Francisco Independent Film Festival, and Best Foreign Feature at the 2019 Edinburgh International Film Festival.

John Wallace Scott (1892 - 1948) was an American businessman, banker and investment strategist who gained notoriety for his influential investment advice and his ability to successfully identify stocks. Born in Massachusetts, Scott attended Harvard Business School, graduating in 1914. Following graduation, he established a career in banking, eventually becoming a very successful venture capitalist, investor and financial advisor. Scott was an early proponent of investment diversification, advocating for the spread of investments across multiple asset classes. He famously advised against investing in the stock market, instead investing in a variety of real estate investments and bonds, due to the erratic nature of stock market prices, and the ability of real estate investments to yield a steady, consistent return. Though his investment advice was not always popular, Scott was highly respected for his keen investment acumen. In his early years of venture capitalism, Scott became notorious for his ability to correctly identify and capitalize on undervalued stocks, seeing additional gains for his clients and himself. During the Great Depression, Scott guided many clients successfully through the market crash and established a firm reputation as a skilled manager of their financial portfolios. In addition to his impressive investing skills, Scott also was instrumental in forming a number of other business ventures. In 1925, Scott formed a venture capital firm that would become one of the most successful in the world, seeding numerous high-profile technology startups. Furthermore, he also served on the boards of several publicly traded companies throughout his career. Though Scott passed away in 1948, his influence and advice continue to be felt across the business world. With his leadership and business acumen, Scott helped to shape the modern investment and capital markets. His name lives on in the John W. Scott Investment Funds, which promote and supply venture capital to early-stage companies and startups. John Wallace Scott was an influential businessman and banker whose success in the markets and business gave him an important place in business history. His success in investing and his ability to successfully forecast market behaviour made him one of the most respected figures of the day and his legacy lives on in the business world today.

USS Hollister (DD-788) was a Gearing-class destroyer of the United States Navy, named for Seaman Samuel Hollister (1790–1843), who served during the War of 1812 aboard USS Fairfield. Construction Hollister was laid down on 5 July 1945 at Bath, Maine, by the Bath Iron Works and launched on 22 November 1945; sponsored by Mrs. E. Cyrus Wilder, granddaughter of Seaman Hollister. The destroyer was commissioned on 19 March 1946, Commander J. F. Seiberlich III in command. Service history Following shakedown and post shakedown overhaul, Hollister joined Destroyer Squadron 23 (DesRon 23) at Newport, Rhode Island. Hollister sailed to the Mediterranean Sea in October 1946, joining the 6th Fleet as part of DesRon 23. During the next four years, Hollister served with distinction in the Mediterranean Sea and the Middle East. She engaged in patrols and shore bombardments during the Palestine campaign, as well as participating in multinational exercises. In April 1950, Hollister returned to the United States. Homeported in Newport, she was assigned to DesRon 2 and underwent much needed modernization with the installation of radar and other equipment. Though still homeported in Newport, the following year she underwent a vital six-month tour of duty with the 6th Fleet in the Mediterranean. In 1953, Hollister became a part of the U.S. Atlantic Fleet, participating in NATO maneuvers in the North Atlantic. During her tour of duty with the Atlantic Fleet, she also made voyages to the Caribbean and South America. In 1958, she conducted a midshipman training cruise in the Mediterranean and paid several visits to European ports. Decommissioning and fate Hollister was decommissioned on 15 July 1970 and struck from the Naval Vessel Register on the same day. She was sold for scrap on 4 August 1970 to University Metals, San Francisco, for $67,170. Legacy Two ships of the United States Navy have been named for Seaman Samuel Hollister, USS Hollister (DD-788) and USS Hollister (DDG-8). References

Massimiliano Rosolino (born 27 July 1976) is an Italian Olympic medal-winning swimmer and three-time world champion who competed in the 2000 Summer Olympics in Sydney. Born in Naples, Italy, Rosolino initially studied economics but switched to philosophy; he later took up swimming and went on to become one of Italy's leading swimmers. Rosolino began competing nationally in 1992 and by 1996 he was competing in the European Championships, winning his first gold medal in the 400m individual medley. In 1999 he set his first world record in the 200m individual medley and won the gold medal at the 1999 European Swimming Championships. At the 2000 Summer Olympics, Rosolino won the gold medal in the 200m individual medley, breaking his own world record in the process. At the 2001 World Aquatics Championships in Fukuoka, he won two golds (200m and 400m individual medleys) and a silver medal. In 2002 he earned a bronze medal at the European Championships in Berlin. Rosolino received a bronze medal in the 200m freestyle at the 2004 Summer Olympics in Athens, claiming fourth place in the 400m freestyle. He is the current world record holder in the 200m freestyle, set in 2002 in Riccione. He holds two Olympic medals and three World Championship golds as well as numerous national titles. Outside of competitive swimming, Rosolino has been involved in a number of other projects. He has written a book entitled "Swimming with Power: The Pros and Cons of High-Performance Training" and serves as an ambassador for the Italian Swimming Federation. He has also acted in films and on television, featuring in the Italian series "Il confronto" and the feature film "Amore 14". He studied philosophy at State University of Milan and is currently a part-time lecturer in swimming technique at the University of Milan. Rosolino is the father of four children and is also an avid car enthusiast. He is an active member of the swimwear brand Arena Italia. Rosolino currently serves as the Vice President of Italian Swimming Federation. He is seen as one of the most decorated Italian swimmers of all time and is widely recognized as a great motivating force in Italian sports. In 2014 he was inducted into the International Swimming Hall of Fame.

Léon Printemps (born February 3, 1965) is a French classical composer, pianist, and conductor. He is best known for his orchestral and chamber works, which often invoke traditional French music. Printemps was born in Paris, France and began playing the piano at a young age. He received his formal education in the Conservatoire de Paris in the early 1980s, studying under the tutelage of composers such as Olivier Messiaen and Henri Dutilleux. His compositions began to be influenced by his studies of classical and romantic composers, and he soon began to develop his own contemporary sound. In 1989, Printemps's first orchestral piece, “Élégiaque”, was performed by the Orchestre National de France and was met with critical acclaim. His success as a young composer caught the attention of renowned conductor Pierre Boulez and together they opened the Ensemble Intercontemporain in 1997. The ensemble was dedicated to promoting the music of up and coming young composers, with Boulez and Printemps at the forefront of the modern music scene. As the recognition of Printemps' compositional prowess grew, so did public appearances. He was invited to perform in national and international locations such as the U.S., Japan, Germany, and the Netherlands. Printemps was featured as the composer-in-residence of the Université de Montréal in 2003, as well as the Cité de la Musique in Paris in 2011. Printemps has received numerous awards throughout his career, including the Grand Prix Sacem in 2005, the French Academy of Music Award in 2006, and the Legion of Honor in 2011. He currently serves as the professor of composition at the National Conservatory of Music in Paris, and has published several works, including his most famous orchestral piece “Chansons de Cour” (2013). Léon Printemps remains as one of the premier composers of classical music in France and continues to influence new generations of musicians by providing them with works of great beauty and complexity.

Montgomery Township is a township in Le Sueur County, Minnesota, United States. As of the 2010 census, the population was 542, making it the smallest township in Le Sueur County. The township was incorporated on April 9, 1858, and named for William E. Montgomery, an early settler of the area. The unincorporated community of Montgomery is located within the township. Montgomery Township is situated on the southeast corner of Le Sueur County and is bordered by Blooming Grove Township to the northeast, Kilkenny Township to the southeast, and Waterville Township to the south. The Minnesota River flows through the township, creating the boundary with Waterville Township. Agriculture is the primary land use in the township, with a majority of the land devoted to crop production. There are some wooded areas, primarily along the Minnesota River and the headwaters of Deep Creek. There are a few businesses located in Montgomery Township. They include a gas station/convenience store, a feed mill, and a sawmill. Montgomery Township is part of the Le Sueur-Henderson Public School District. The township is served by busing to the elementary, middle, and high schools in Henderson and Le Sueur. In addition to agriculture, recreational activities in the township can include fishing in the Minnesota River, boating from the public access in Montgomery, and hunting. Hunting on the township are both waterfowl and deer. Montgomery Township is governed by a three-member township board. The board is responsible for setting policy and for ensuring the operations of the township are within the bounds of the law. The board meets on the second Monday of each month, except for June and December, at the local community center. The Montgomery Township Fire Department, located in the unincorporated community of Montgomery, serves the township with fire protection. The township also contracts with the Le Sueur County Sheriff's Office for law enforcement services.

Ice cream, or often referred to as “froyo” (freeze yogurt) is a sweet confectionery product. It is usually made of dairy products, such as cream or milk, along with sugar and flavorings, then frozen into a soft, creamy dessert. It comes in a variety of flavors, such as vanilla, strawberry, and chocolate, and can be eaten alone or as a topping for other desserts, such as cakes and pies. As far back as 2000 BCE, in ancient Asia, thickened milk was frozen and served as a dessert. During the time of the ancient Greeks, crushed ice was combined with honey to make a dessert. The first known written record of a type of frozen confectionery is found in a ninth-century Chinese text. In Europe, ice cream was made with cream and sugar in the sixteenth century. Later, other ingredients such as fruits, cocoa, and chocolate were added to make different flavors. In 1660 an ice maker from France named Nicolas Procopé introduced "sorbet," a kind of water-based ice cream. In the united states, the development of ice cream has been largely credited to an American inventor, Jacob Fussell, who in 1851 opened the world's first commercial ice cream factory in Baltimore, Maryland. It was soon followed by companies such as Petersen & Brug in Philadelphia and Bradley & Hazard in Providence, Rhode Island. Presently, ice cream is popular world-wide, with the United States consuming 18.5 quarts of ice cream per capita each year. The global ice cream market is projected to grow significantly (at a CAGR of 7% to 8%) during the forecast period of 2020 to 2027, due to rising disposable income and the inclination of consumers towards desserts and confectionary products. Furthermore, the growing popularity of plant-based ice cream is creating new opportunities in the market, as veganism is becoming more prevalent. Today, there are many different types of ice cream available, including dairy-free, lactose-free, low-fat, and organic ice creams. Some of the most popular flavors include vanilla, chocolate, cookies and cream, mint chip, and rocky road. Ice cream can also be served in a variety of ways such as in cones, cups, sundaes, shakes, and smoothies. It is a popular dessert that can be enjoyed at any time of the year. Whether eaten as a dessert after a meal, as an afternoon snack, or even as a treat on a hot summer day, ice cream is sure to delight.

"Anything Goes" is a song recorded by American country music artist Randy Houser, off his fifth studio album of the same name. It was released on June 14, 2019 as the lead single from the album and was later sent to radio on July 29, 2019. The song was written by Brandon Day and Jerry Flowers, and was produced by Sean Neff. "Anything Goes" is a mid-tempo country-rock song with drum-kit instrumentation and guitars. Lyrically, the song is about a man leaving behind his responsibilities for an evening, "just for the night" that "[anything] goes". The single received generally positive reviews from music critics. Roger Fritz from Country Standard Time said that the song was "bordering on rock" and that it had a catchy melody. AllMusic Today noted its upbeat lyrics, saying that the song is "filled with big catchy choruses and memories of carefree days gone by." The song has since peaked at number 26 on the US Billboard Country Airplay chart. The accompanying music video for "Anything Goes" was released on June 14, 2019 and directed by Mason Dixon. The video follows Houser as he makes his way to a party in the woods where fellow musicians, including Bobby Bones and Mickey Guyton, are enjoying themselves. Houser has also performed the song on several late-night shows, including The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon and Late Night with Seth Meyers. "Anything Goes" has been praised for its catchy melody and positive message of leaving behind one's daily life for an evening. The song has been well received by both fans and critics alike and has become one of Randy Houser's biggest hits.

The Confederation of Italian Entrepreneurs Worldwide (CIE) is an international, non-governmental organization founded in 1997 that seeks to promote Italian entrepreneurship across the globe. The organization is based in Rome, Italy and is open to Italian entrepreneurs worldwide, regardless of the type, size or scope of their business. The CIE strives to encourage networking and collaboration amongst Italian entrepreneurs based abroad, as well as to support their direct investments in Italy. The organization's aim is to facilitate the growth of Italian businesses and to develop an international network among entrepreneurs, public institutions, and associations of the Italian diaspora. The CIE provides a range of services and support to its members, including hosting workshops and seminars on topics related to international business and Italian regulations and laws. It also offers legal, financial and professional advice, as well as educational programmes to help Italian entrepreneurs become more competitive in the global market. Additionally, it seeks to promote Italian entrepreneurship in foreign countries and to contribute to the development of bilateral economic relations with Italian businesses. In 2008, the CIE launched the Italian Community Awards, an annual event which seeks to recognize and promote the achievements of Italian entrepreneurs and businesses across the globe. The award celebrates those who have made a positive contribution to the international community, and seeks to recognize and promote the achievements of Italian entrepreneurs on a global scale. The CIE regularly joins other organizations, especially non-profit associations, with the aim of collaborating in order to achieve its objectives. The association is a member of the World Association of Major International Organizations (WAMIO), the BRICS Network, and the European Business Conferences Partners. In 2016, the CIE joined the European Commission's “Entrepreneurs for Growth” initiative and became the official representative of the Italian Diaspora in the European Union. Overall, the CIE is a major force in promoting Italian entrepreneurship worldwide, having actively engaged in promoting a wide range of activities that foster mutual growth and cooperation between international business owners.

Claudia Ruggerini ( born 11 February 1973, Rome, Italy) is an internationally recognized Italian actress. She is best known her roles films such as Il Postino (The Postman), Bicycle Thieves, and La Vita è Bella (Life is Beautiful.) Ruggerini began her acting career with the stage production Appuntamento D'Amore (A Love Rendez-Vous) in 1993. In 1994 she was cast in her first major film appearance in Il Postino. She has since appeared in feature films like Bicycle Thieves and La Vita è Bella. She also had pronounced roles in television shows such as La Vita in Diretta, Un posto al Sole, and Il Commissario Montalbano. Ruggerini won the Italian Golden Globe in 2003 for best actress in the feature film Liberate i Pesci (Free the Fish). She also appeared in the national New Year's Eve television event in 2003. Other notable films include The Best of Youth, Neera, and The Whore. Claudia has also starred in multiple international advertisements for companies such as Dear Departures and D. G. C. Ruggerini is active in the Italian charity sector, and has raised funds for organizations such as Ricerca sul Cancro (Research on Cancer) and La Lega del Filo d'Oro (The Golden Thread League). She was named as laureate of the President of Italy in March 2015. Claudia Ruggerini continues to be a celebrated actress in Italy and internationally. Recently, she produced the 9-episode series Il Centro (The Center) which premiered on Italian television in 2017. Fairground (song) is a 1995 song by the British band Simply Red. It was released as the second single from their album Life on the world of their fifth studio album. It became the band's third top five single in the United Kingdom, reaching number three on the UK Singles Chart. The track was written by lead vocalist Mick Hucknall and co-produced by Stewart Levine and musician Heitor Pereira. It was released as a four-track CD single and maxi-single. The single includes various remixes of the song, including a "Club Power Remix". The song was also included in the compilation album The Greatest Hits in the late 1990s. Additionally, the song was featured in the movie Spy Hard and appeared on the soundtrack album of the same name. The song has a somber, mid-tempo tone, and its lyrics are about a "fairground ride," where the singer is making allusions to the restlessness of a doomed relationship. The song was also a metaphor for Hucknall's mixed feelings about the band's newfound commercial success and the burden of fame and stardom. The accompanying music video for "Fairground" was directed by Mark Szaszy. It gained much attention and airplay due to its artistic, surreal nature, and was shot in black-and-white. The video follows several people and the narrator (Hucknall) as they wander through a mysterious fairground. The video won several awards, including an MTV Video Music Award in 1995. "Fairground" is one of Simply Red's best-known hits, becoming a top three hit in the UK and charting in Germany, Italy, and other countries. In the United States, however, the song did not receive much radio airplay and "Fairground" was not released as a single. Nonetheless, the song remains a fan favorite and often appears on set lists during Simply Red's live concerts.

Sexto Sentido (English: Sixth Sense), released in 2000, is the twenty-first studio album by Brazilian singer-songwriter Xuxa. It is the second studio album they released after Xuxa (1997), and the first album they released through a major American label. Xuxa described the album as a concept album; each song had a special theme, written mostly in Spanish and into a mixture of various Latin styles. The album mixed Xuxa's Brazilian rhythms, rhythms and styles from Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico, Uruguay and Argentina. According to Xuxa, the idea of the album came from a script they wrote while filming the television series Querido Maestro in Mexico City. The production of the album was assisted by an Asteroid team, which included Xuxa's own producers throughout the career of Xuxa, Bartolomeu E Silva and Mariozinho Rocha, now as co-producers. The album contains collaborations with renowned Mexican vocalists like Thalía, Lo Blondo, Bruz, David Bisbal and Paz Vega. The former was the lead single from the album, "El Tren de la Vida" (The Train of Life), produced in collaboration with Eugenia León and Cecilia Toussaint. The track was a success in Latin America, and it also gave Xuxa their first US hit as well, reaching #25 on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs list. To promorte the track, Xuxa recorded a Spanish version of the music video. "Cambiaré Por Ti" was released as the second single from the album in September 2000. It was an instant success in Latin America and Billboard. The track reached its peak position of #24 on Billboard's Latin Pop Airplay Songs chart. The album's third single, a Latin pop track of Xuxa's own written in Spanish titled "Voy", was released in December 2000. Overall, Xuxa's Sexto Sentido was well-received by both Latin and non-Latin listeners alike. The album sold over 400,000 copies in the United States and over 1 million copies worldwide. The album was nominated for a Grammy Award in the Best Latin Pop Album category in 2000 and 2001. As of 2020, it remains Xuxa's last full-length release.

John Cahill (born 1950) is an Irish Roman Catholic bishop, best known for his role as Bishop of the Diocese of Killaloe in Ireland. Cahill was born in Dublin but grew up in Galway. After his secondary school education at the Jesuit St. Joseph's College in Galway, he attended St. Patrick's College in Maynooth, where he completed a Bachelor's Degree in Theology. He was ordained a priest in 1976 and assigned a curate in Dublin, while also attending University College Dublin for further studies, from which he graduated with a Bachelor's degree in law. He returned to St. Patrick's College in Maynooth for his doctoral studies for which he wrote a dissertation about Anglican-Roman Catholic Church relations in the 19th Century. In 1991 he was appointed Vicar General of the Dublin Diocese, a post he held until he was appointed Bishop of Killaloe in 2002. Bishop Cahill was installed on October 6, 2002 as the fourteenth Bishop of Killaloe. He served as episcopal chairman of the Catechetics and Liturgy Commission of the Irish Catholic Bishops' Conference, President of the Irish Biblical Association, and a member of the International Commission on Anglican-Roman Catholic Relations. In February of 2012 he announced his intention to retire in June of the same year and on May 31, 2012 the Diocese of Killaloe had its official farewell to Bishop Cahill. He was 33 years a priest and 8 years a Bishop. On 23rd November 2014 Pope Francis appointed Killaloe's coadjutor bishop Fintan Monahan as Cahill's successor. Throughout his tenure as Bishop of Killaloe, Bishop Cahill was a firm believer in interfaith dialogue and collaboration. In 2007, he held a Christmas Mass for both Christian and Muslim communities in the Killaloe district. Bishop Cahill has been actively involved in the Pro-Life movement in Ireland, taking the lead on the Pastoral Letter condemning abortion and the Referendum on the 8th Amendment of the Constitution. Currently Bishop Cahill is living in Galway, near his family and is spending his time lecturing and writing. In November of 2017, Cahill published a book entitled ‘Laudato Si’, in which he delves into the writings of Pope Francis and how they can be integrated into the day-to-day life of individuals.

Hellgate is a 1989 American psychological horror film directed by William Osborne. It stars Mariska Hargitay, Tim Matheson, Graham Beckel, and Gretchen Corbett. The screenplay was written by Osborne and Gary Troy, with the story coming from Gary Troy. The story revolves around a family who have moved to a small town in Montana. The father, Edward (Matheson) is an author and the mother, Elisabeth (Corbett) is a teacher. They have two children; Matthew (Nicholas Hormann) who is a student at the local high school, and Meg (Hargitay) who is in middle school. When Edward starts engaging in risky behavior to combat his writer’s block, the family’s lives slowly unravel, and Meg begins to explore the local legend of the Devil’s Gate. As Meg becomes more and more involved in the legend and its implications, the family’s lives become increasingly disturbed. Edward starts experiencing phantasmagorical visions, Meg becomes violent and troubled, and the family’s sense of sanity and security becomes eroded. The film received mixed reviews from critics upon its release. Some praised the cinematography and atmosphere, while others deemed the screenplay too complicated and overly convoluted. Despite this, the film was successful at the box office and managed to gain a cult following, due to its unique atmosphere and subject matter. Hellgate is a unique and eerie tale, managed to capture many viewers’ imagination with its surreal and psychological themes. It still stands as a cult classic to this day, and has left a lasting impact on many horror fans.

The Monroe Civic Center is located in Monroe, Louisiana and is an entertainment and convention center which hosts various events in the region. The Civic Center was opened in 1971 after the city of Monroe received funds from several sources, the chief being the U.S. Housing Agency. The original design was provided by architect Maxwell B. Moore and consisted of a 2,000-seat main auditorium, two 1,100-seat auditoriums, a conference and exhibit hall, a ballroom, and three cafeterias. The Monroe Civic Center holds events year-round representing many different types of entertainment and activities. Some of the events held here include trade shows and conventions, concerts, theatre productions, graduations, civic functions, and sporting events. The Civic Center has hosted a variety of musical acts such as Elvis Presley and ZZ Top, and comedians such as Jerry Seinfeld and Dave Chappelle. Various components have been added to the center over time to enhance its offerings, the largest of these being a $15 million renovation in 2008. This renovation increased the number of seats in the auditoriums and added a new dressing room and stage area. The renovation also added an arena addition which features bandshells, basketball courts and an event space with a capacity of over 4000 people. Today, the building is managed by SMG and is considered the main entertainment venue of the Northeast Louisiana area. The Monroe Civic Center continues to expand its offerings, hosting a variety of events in not just the main auditorium, but in the arenas, ballrooms and cafeterias as well. From trade shows and conventions, to graduations and sporting events, the center gives locals and visitors of Monroe a variety of entertainment choices.

By the Light of the Moon is the fourth episode of the third season of The Vampire Diaries. It was written by Julie Plec and directed by John Behring. It originally aired on October 13, 2011. The episode's story continues from the previous episode where Elena were changed by Klaus into a vampire. Elena is desperate to control her bloodlust and tests how far she can go. Meanwhile, Bonnie and Abby travel to New Orleans for a ritual that could help with Klaus's curse. In the episode, Sheriff Forbes holds a town meeting and when some of the townspeople attack Damon, she is able to stop them and warn them that if they cannot create a place of safety for the supernatural then they will be targeted by the Vampire Hunter. Stefan is trying to bond with Elena as they both go through their transitions. Bonnie and Abby continue their journey to New Orleans and come across a witch. Caroline and Tyler share some of their newly acquired knowledge about family history. Finally, Klaus is on the verge of creating hisultimate weapon, a hybrid. At the end of the episode, it is revealed that Bonnie and Abby have gone to New Orleans in order to help break the curse that Klaus placed on Elena. They must find a way to make contact with Elijah and the rest of the Original Family and return to the Salvatore property with a powerful weapon. The episode ends with Elena embracing her new life as a vampire for the first time by turning off a streetlight and feeding on a human she saves from being attacked. The episode was met with generally positive reviews from critics. Nate Rawlings of The A.V. Club gave the episode an A -, stating that "every element of the show was in place and working together in harmony — the horror, suspense, depth of character, humor, and stakes necessary for The Vampire Diaries to stay must-watch TV." Matt Richenthal of TV Fanatic gave the episode 4.4 out of 5 stars, praising the new direction in character development: "The show is quickly evolving into a tale of redemption, a vampire series in which we can root for our protagonists to become fully human again."
