Königsburg is a small town located in the German state of Bavaria. It is situated in the beautiful Franconian Forest, an area renowned for its nature and outdoor activities. The town is also known for its many annual festivals and events, such as the "Königsburg Wine Festival" and the "Königsburg Christmas Market". The population of the town is about 4,400 inhabitants. The name of the town originates from the Latin word "regnum" (king's borough). This implies that the settlement was originally founded as a royal residence. The first written records of Königsburg date back to the year 1000. In the late Middle Ages, the town was a hub of trade and commerce, thanks to its proximity to the river Main. In the 19th century, Königsburg underwent a period of significant growth and expansion. Its population increased from approximately 2,000 in 1820 to almost 4,400 by the early 20th century. The prosperity of the town was largely based on the wine and spirits trade, as well as on some light industry and tourism. In the 20th century, Königsburg was heavily destroyed in World War II. Much of the town was reconstructed after the war, although some older buildings remain untouched. Today, Königsburg is a popular tourist destination, especially in the summer months. Visitors come to enjoy the delightful scenery, typical Franconian houses, cobblestone streets, and a wide range of outdoor events, such as the "Königsburg Wine Festival". The town is also known for its excellent local and organic food and the numerous wineries in the region. The town of Königsburg is a picturesque example of a typical German small town, where visitors can still feel the authenticity of the region and get a glimpse of traditional Bavarian life. It remains a popular destination for travelers who want to explore all that Bavaria has to offer.

St. Mary Church, Isfahan (Persian: کلیسا مریم اصفهان) is an ancient Armenian Apostolic church located in Isfahan, Iran. It is known by the locals as “Kelisa-ye Miriam” (Church of Mary). It is one of the oldest and largest churches in the historic city of Isfahan, and is a notable example of early Christian architecture. The church was built in the 17th century, by Armenian immigrants from the Ottoman Empire who had settled in the area following the Safavid-Ottoman wars. It was likely the first Armenian church built in Isfahan and is considered to be a significant structure for the local Armenian community. The current building dates from the late 18th century, although parts of the original structure have been preserved. The church features a three-storey building with a central dome, six columns, and a large portico. The pillars are decorated with colourful tiles and the walls are painted white. The courtyard is enclosed by curtains and trees, creating a peaceful atmosphere. The design of the church follows the traditional Armenian style of architecture, which became popular in the region due to its close proximity to Ottoman and Persian territories. Inside the church, there are several chapels dedicated to different Catholic saints, and the main area is used for Divine Liturgy. Other activities such as bible studies and discussion groups are also conducted here. There is also a collection of ancient religious artefacts and curated works of art that are displayed in the church. The St. Mary Church is still an important part of the local Armenian community and is visited by Armenians not just in Iran, but also from various other countries. The church also serves as an important reminder of the history and struggles of the Armenian people, who have traditionally found a home in Isfahan. Today, St. Mary Church serves both the Armenian and Persian Orthodox communities of the area, and continues to act as an important religious and cultural centre. Visitors to Isfahan should not miss the chance to visit this beautiful house of worship.

John Anthony West (1932 - 2018) was an American author and Egyptologist best known for his seminal works on ancient Egypt and its civilization. He is best known for introducing a radical revision in conventional Egyptology, most prominently the suggestion that the Great Sphinx of Giza may in fact be thousands of years older than previously thought. West was born in 1932 in Mineola, New York and earned a B.A. in Fine Arts from Columbia University. He went on to pursue graduate studies at the University of Geneva and Oxford University, but chose not to receive a degree. He then crafted a career as a poet, screenwriter, journalist, and painter. West's interest in Egyptology was first piqued during a childhood visit to the Middle East with his father. Over the years this interest grew, and ultimately formed the basis of his writing and research. In 1979, West presented "The Case for the Great Sphinx", a documentary that argued the sphinx might in fact be thousands of years older than the traditional dates assigned by Egyptologists. This presented a radical departure from the traditional understanding of the sphinx, and attracted the attention of Robert Bauval, whose Orion Correlation Theory West drew on to support his conclusions. In the late 1980s, West organized two exploratory visits to the pyramid complex of Giza. During these visits, West and his team of experts uncovered evidence that further supported his findings. The theory of West and his colleagues also drew the attention of some of the world's leading Egyptologists. While some of the findings of West and his team were further explored by Egyptologists, others were dismissed. Nonetheless, his work is still considered groundbreaking and significantly influenced many later studies on ancient Egypt. West continued to write, eventually authoring several books on the subject of Egyptology. His last book, 'Serpent in the Sky', was published in 1993, and explores an alternative explanation for the origin of civilization. West died in 2018 at the age of 85, leaving behind a legacy of groundbreaking work in Egyptology. His work has inspired others to push the boundaries of conventional Egyptology, introducing new theories and revising the traditional understanding of this ancient civilization.

Lillias Margaret Skene (1901 – 1982) was a British international swimming champion and teacher. She was the first female swimmer to represent Scotland at the Commonwealth Games and the first female to coach a British swimming team. Skene was born in Edinburgh, Scotland in 1901 and was educated at St George's School, Edinburgh. She took up swimming in 1917 and quickly rose through the ranks of competitive swimming, becoming the Scottish champion and a British record holder in 1922. She also represented Scotland at the Women's International Five Nations and the Women's International Six Nations swimming meets. In 1923, Skene was selected as the first female swimmer to represent Scotland at the inaugural British Empire Games, now known as the Commonwealth Games. She won gold in the 100 metre backstroke and a silver medal in the 4x100 relay. She also represented Scotland at the 1924 Summer Olympics in Paris. Skene went on to become the first female coach of a British swimming team. She coached the Britain team at the Women's International Six Nations Meet in 1932 and the first-ever Women's World Swimming Championships in 1954. In 1947, Skene was appointed as a swimming instructor at the Scottish Educational Council. She remained in the role until her retirement in 1969. Her teaching included beginners courses that were designed to help people to learn the basics of swimming and lifesaving skills. Skene was well known within the Scottish swimming community and in 1975 was awarded an MBE in recognition of her coaching and teaching services. In her retirement, Skene wrote several books on swimming lessons as well as a novel and a poetry collection. Skene passed away in 1982. Her legacy lives on through her works and the generations of swimmers she inspired.

Émilie Vina (born August 3, 1997) is a Canadian fashion designer and entrepreneur. She is the founder of the luxury fashion brand Émivida, which primarily focuses on womenswear, as well as footwear, swimwear, and accessories. Vina was born in Montreal, Quebec and grew up in a family of five. She was a creative and energetic child, but it wasn't until she was 14 that she found her true passion: fashion design. At 17, she started to take fashion classes and after graduating high school, she moved to Toronto to pursue a degree in fashion design at Seneca College. In her second year at Seneca, Vina was already producing her own collections. She put on her first fashion show in October 2015, showcasing her Spring/Summer 2016 collection. Word quickly spread about her talent and the young designer was soon invited to participate in fashion weeks in Milan and Paris, as well as New York Fashion Week. Vina’s designs have been well received by critics. Her unique ability to combine fabrics with intricate details make her pieces stand out from the rest. She is best known for her couture evening wear and party dresses, which are often made of luxurious materials such as silk, taffeta, and lace. In 2018, Vina launched her luxury fashion brand Émivida. The brand focuses on creating luxury street wear and contemporary day wear. Since then, her designs have been featured in various magazines and editorials. She has also had the opportunity to design collections for celebrities such as Kehlani, Christina Milian, and Jhené Aiko. In 2019, Vina made history as the youngest Canadian designer to have a fashion brand partnerships with major luxury stores such as Neiman Marcus and Bergdorf Goodman. Vina continues to explore her creativity and push boundaries with her designs. She is continuously collaborating with different celebrities, fashion bloggers, and other influencers. Today, her mission is to create luxurious and timeless designs for the modern woman. Her vision for the future is to continue to “elevate women through quality and unique design.” Category:Canadian fashion designers Category:People from Montreal Category:1997 births Category:Living people

Blackstone & Co is an American real estate and capital services firm based in New York City. Founded in 1985 by Stephen A. Schwarzman and Peter G. Peterson, the firm has grown to be one of the most successful and highly respected real estate investment firms in the world. Blackstone & Co specializes in a range of services related to real estate and capital investments, including acquisitions, mergers, dispositions, development and leasing, investment banking, and capital markets. With 33 offices across the U.S. and Europe, the firm has invested over $8 billion of equity capital across multiple real estate sectors, including office, industrial, multifamily, retail, hospitality, and senior living. In addition, the firm has an extensive international presence in Asia, Mexico, Canada and Latin America. In addition to Blackstone & Co's real estate services, the firm also provides portfolio management, mezzanine finance, and strategic advisory services to institutional and private clients. In recent years, the firm has expanded its operations to include venture capital, private equity, and energy investment activities. Blackstone & Co is widely regarded as one of the most successful and innovative real estate services firms in the world. Its extensive network of clients, partners, and industry contacts gives the firm greater access to capital, investments, and other resources designed to increase returns for its clients. Since its founding, the firm has made several notable investments, including most recently $17.2 billion hotel giant Strategic Hotels & Resorts, the $3 billion sale of Arta Capital Partners to Bain Capital, the leadership of the $2.2 billion dollar purchase of office building giant Equity Office Properties, and a range of other investments. The firm has earned a reputation for innovation, a commitment to building long-term relationships, and a passion for performance. With over 30 years of experience in real estate investing, Blackstone & Co has become a trusted name in the industry.

Sir Hugo was a beloved and respected English nobleman and politician of the 15th century, born in 1434. He was the son of Sir Robert and Lady Margaret of Cornwall, and was of noble lineage. His reputation was as one of the most powerful and influential political figures at the court of King Henry VI. After being educated at Oxford, he entered the world of politics and, in 1459, was appointed Sheriff of Cornwall. He quickly gained the favor of the king and became one of the most influential figures at the royal court. Through his influence, he was able to build powerful alliances of noble families and gain influence over the House of Commons. Sir Hugo was a loyal supporter to King Henry during the Wars of the Roses, and he helped to shape many of the political decisions at the court of the king. He was also involved in the negotiations of the Treaty of London and was instrumental in helping the king to have better mastery over the country. In 1466, he was knighted by the king and was made a baron by Henry VI. He rose to great popularity and was one of the most influential courtiers of the king. During his times, he was known as a good and just man and his influence was felt far and wide. Sir Hugo was a peaceful and prudent ruler. He often sought to resolve disputes between warring factions without further bloodshed. He was an advocate for commerce and foreign relations and strongly opposed the idea of tournaments and similar martial pursuits. One of his greatest accomplishments was the establishment of a peace and trade agreement between the English and French monarchs, an event that became known as the Treaty of London. In 1475, he was awarded the Order of the Garter for his services to the King and the country. Sir Hugo died in 1488 aged 54 after a long and distinguished career. He was remembered as a man of strong political and personal integrity and was widely respected by all members of the royal court. He will forever be remembered as one of the most influential courtiers of his time and a key figure in the history of England.

Valet Girls is a British television miniseries produced by the BBC and broadcast from 1981-1982. It stars Anna Churcher as the lead character, Caroline (Carrie), a young woman working as a valet for a hotel in London. Carrie is an independent and strong-willed woman who is looking to make her way in the world, but she has a lot on her plate as she juggles her career, her personal life, and her love interest, Mark (Alec Mccowen). The series explores the notion of a "Valet Girl" - a term used in the UK to describe young women who worked as hotel and restaurant assistants. The show follows the stories of Carrie and other Valet Girls as they work to find success and survival in a male-dominated workplace while trying to find a way to balance the demands of their job with the complexities of their personal lives. The miniseries, set during the early 1980s in London, contains themes of romance, friendship, and empowerment and challenges gender roles often encountered in traditional working environments. Valet Girls was written and created by BAFTA award-winning writer, Victoria Wood, and also featured acclaimed British actors, Alec McCowen, Mary Healey, and Paul Speller. The series received critical acclaim for its writing and for its successful representation of young women in a contemporary setting. Valet Girls was aired on BBC1 from 1981-1982, and it spawned a spin-off series, "Valet Girls Two", which aired throughout 1983 on the same channel. Together, they ran for 25 episodes, and the show has been released on DVD in the UK and Germany. The show is seen as a groundbreaking representation of female strength, ambition and, ultimately, empowerment during a time when female roles on television were largely limited to traditional stereotypes. It continues to be popular with fans today and is a classic example of British television at its best.

Vulcano, or Vulcano in Italian, is an active volcanic island located in the northern part of the Tyrrhenian Sea that is part of the volcanic arc of the seven Aeolian Islands in Sicily, Italy. The island is approximately 8 km2 in size and lies about 3 km northwest of the nearby island of Lipari. It is connected to the mainland by a ferry service and is home to around 500 people. The main village on the island is called Vulcano Porto. The volcanic activity on the island is mainly concentrated in two major craters, the Fossa cone and the Gran Cratere. The first eruptions of the Fossa cone took place in 183 BC, while the second eruptions occurred in 1550 and again in 1888. The Gran Cratere last erupted in 1888-1890 and the island is still considered an active volcano, although it is currently dormant. Vulcano is known for its medicinal hot springs which have the potential to offer relief for mild to moderate respiratory ailments. The island's main therapeutic attractions are two natural thermal springs, the Sulfurea and the Gran Cratere. The island also has several hot cliff-side waterfalls which are believed to contain mineral-enriched waters. The crater atop the Fossa cone is called Piano, and is the site of Vulcano's active sulfur mines. The mines have been in use since the 16th century and are the major source of sulfur in the region. The sulfur deposits are actively mined and used in the production of sulfuric acid and various sulfur-based products, such as fertilizers, bleach, and explosives. The island is also home to numerous species of wildlife, particularly migratory birds. The most notable resident species on the island is the vulcanello, a species of songbird related to the chaffinch. The vulcanello is found on Vulcano and nearby islands, and is recognized as an endemic species. Aside from the wildlife and sulfur mines, Vulcano is also known for its lovely beaches, volcanic landscapes, and its prominent role in Greek mythology. The island is featured in Homer's Odyssey, as this is believed to be the entrance to Hades, hence the Italian name for the island (Vulcano), meaning “God of Fire”. As of today, Vulcano remains a popular tourist destination and is also home to several quaint fishing villages. Its main attractions are its therapeutic hot springs, beaches, abundant birdlife, and its spectacular scenery.

Mark Fenner (born May 3, 1974) is an American entrepreneur and entrepreneur-in-residence at Dundee Ventures. He is the founder of Fenner Technologies, a company providing technology products and services designed to enable businesses to remain competitive in the digital world. Fenner graduated from the University of Notre Dame in 1997 with a B.A. in Finance/Computer Science and started his career as a software engineer at Microsoft. He then went on to become a Product Manager and then a Program Manager at Microsoft. After leaving Microsoft, Fenner founded Fenner Technologies, a technology product and services provider, in 2002. In 2007, Fenner developed Fenner Technologies’ flagship product, CustomerLY. CustomerLY is an automated customer intelligence and analytics platform which tracks customers’ behavior, purchasing history and marketing campaigns. The platform provides business insights and information that enables companies to better understand their customer base and remain competitive. Fenner’s entrepreneurial efforts are credited with having been instrumental in the success of large companies such as Microsoft, Dell, and Procter & Gamble. Throughout his career, Fenner has appeared in publications such as Inc. Magazine, Businessweek, CIO Magazine and Entrepreneur Magazine. He has spoken at conferences such as the World Economic Forum, the International Conference on Information Technology, and the Estonia Business Summit Conference. He has contributed to multiple publications discussing trends and innovations in the tech industry. Fenner also serves on the Board of Directors of Myndflow, a marketing software and mobile application company, and as an Entrepreneur-in-Residence at Dundee Ventures. He is an advisor to Gaslight Learning, an online education platform, and has been a featured speaker on the European Commission for Social Inclusion. Fenner is currently a mentor to aspiring entrepreneurs and is a frequent guest speaker at entrepreneurship and venture capital events. He is a supporter of building strong business ecosystems and encourages companies to invest in innovations, develop their technology services, and better understand their customers. Given Fenner’s success and experience in the tech industry, he is a renowned leader and authority in technology and digital innovations.

Pugwash, Nova Scotia, is a small village in the Canadian province of Nova Scotia. Located on the Northumberland Shore of the Northumberland Strait, the village is known for its extensive sandy beach, which is frequented by tourists during the summer months. According to the 2016 census, Pugwash has a population of 555. The village was incorporated in 1894, and was founded by the American industrialist, Joseph E. Seeley. The name "Pugwash" comes from the mi'kmaq word, "Pugwesdagun", which translates to "place of eelgrass". This is likely due to the abundant eelgrass beds located along the shores of Pugwash. The village also contains a number of historic buildings, many of which date back to the late 1800s. One of the most notable is the Friends' Meeting House, which is the oldest meeting house of the Religious Society of Friends in Canada and was built in 1817. Pugwash is home to one of the oldest yacht clubs in Canada, the Pugwash Yacht Club, which was established in 1884. The club is located on the Pleasant Point of the Pugwash Harbour, and offers a wide range of activities, such as sailing, rowing and fishing. The Pugwash Harbour is also a popular spot for recreation and sightseeing, offering views of the entire Pugwash area. The village is home to a number of museums, showcasing the local history and culture. Two of the most significant include the Joseph Howe Museum, which celebrates the life of the local patriot and journalist, and the NSLC Heritage Centre, which tells the story of the regions liquor retailers. The village also includes several boutique shops and cafes. Pugwash hosts a yearly pirate-themed festival, the Pugwash Village Pirate Festival, celebrating the village’s connection with the pirates of centuries ago. The festival puts on various performances, workshops, and a large parade throughout the village. This event has become extremely popular among locals and tourists alike and draws large crowds each year. Pugwash is connected to the nearby towns of Amherst and Truro via Highway 6, and is located an hour from the provincial capital of Halifax. It is a popular tourist destination, known for its beautiful beaches, historic sites and relaxed atmosphere.

Vladimir II Monomakh (c. 1053 – 19 May 1125) was a Grand Prince of Kievan Rus' from 1113 to 1125. His reign saw the last flowering of Kievan Rus' as a unified state and the arrival of the Golden Horde from the east. He was the son of Vsevolod I of Kiev and Anastasia. Vladimir II was prince of Novgorod when his father died. He was crowned in 1113 in a grand ceremony in Kyiv and adopted his father's policy of open-handed peace with the tribes of the steppe. Vladimir II secured the Kievan throne by marrying the daughter of the ruling Grand Prince of the Cumans in 1119. After taking the throne, he helped expand Rus territories southward by taking Yuriev, Pereyaslavl, and a number of other towns. In 1120, an alliance with the Pechenegs allowed Vladimir II to expand his rule beyond the Dnieper River, and he was able to return Kiev and Chernigov, which had been taken by the Cumans. The next year he formed a defensive alliance with King Béla of Hungary against the Cumans. In 1123, a war between Vladimir II and a combined Cuman-Polovtsian force forced him to flee Kiev. The Prince then returned to the steppes and helped the Ukrainian prince Mstislav II conquer Galitch to open up new trade routes to the Black Sea. Invaders from the East started to threaten Kievan Rus', and in 1125 the Polovtsi formed a coalition against Vladimir II's army near Pereyaslavl. The Grand Prince led his army to a decisive victory. The Golden Horde (Tatars) arrived soon after, and although Vladimir II was able to drive them back, he realized he could no longer protect Rus' lands from their repeated attacks. Within four years of his death on 19 May 1125, Kievan Rus' was completely conquered and divided among the invaders. Vladimir II's sons, Mstislav and Svyatopolk, were able to briefly revive Kievan power in the late 12th century. His legacy lives on in Russian narrative sources and folklore, and he is remembered as an able prince who firmly maintained the struggles of thestate, tried to preserve and expand its borders, and negotiated success with both friends and foes.

West Balikpapan is an agglomeration of districts located in East Kalimantan, Indonesia. It is one of the principal residential and industrial areas of the city of Balikpapan. It is situated on the eastern coast of the Makassar Straits and is home to a population of around 200,000 people. Origins The name "West Balikpapan" appears to have been applied for the first time in the early 1970s. At the time, urbanization was already underway and Balikpapan was expanding from its original core area, centred in the city's east. Eventually, a second major residential and industrial area emerged in the city's western part, and the name "West Balikpapan" was given to this area by the city's inhabitants. Founding The area of West Balikpapan appears to have gone through two cycles of development, starting in the late 1960s and ending in the mid-1980s. In the first cycle, a number of new settlements cropped up around Tamalanrea, Rimba Indah and Batu Ampar. These settlements consisted mainly of industrial and mining activities, as well as residential and commercial developments. They were quickly followed by more housing and commercial developments, which greatly increased the district's population. However, the rapid growth of West Balikpapan was soon hindered by environmental degradation, rampant crime and conflict with indigenous communities living in the area. Development and Economy In response to these issues, West Balikpapan experienced a period of stagnation in the late 1980s and early 1990s. This led to the formation of a new district government, consisting of representatives of the local residents and business owners. Through their efforts, much of the pollution and conflict in the area was eventually resolved. Furthermore, large-scale development projects were implemented, such as road and housing improvements, in order to make West Balikpapan a more pleasant, livable place to be. Today, West Balikpapan is an important part of Balikpapan. It is regarded as the main centre of business and industry in the city, and it is home to some of the most important economic institutions, including the Balikpapan Stock Exchange. It is also home to numerous government offices and embassies, as well as medical and education facilities. In addition, many shopping malls, movie theatres, restaurants and bars are located in West Balikpapan. All of these factors make West Balikpapan one of the most attractive places to live and work in East Kalimantan.

The Gateway Station is a public transit station located in downtown Pittsburgh, in western Pennsylvania, and is the hub for the Port Authority of Allegheny County’s (PAAC) light rail system. The light rail system transports over 80,000 riders per day to and from the Gateway Station, making it one of the most used light rail stations in the United States. The Gateway Station was opened in 1984, with the completion of the Central Connector Light Rail Service. At that time, the station provided the only direct connection between Downtown Pittsburgh and Station Square on the Southside. It has since been expanded to include several additional lines on the North Shore Connector (only). The Gateway Station has five platforms. Each platform serves one of the three routes of the Port Authority’s light rail system. The red line, (the North Shore Connector), travels from the station, to the North Side and Heinz Field (home of the Pittsburgh Steelers). The blue line, (the Martin Luther King, Jr. East Busway) travels from the station, down to the Eastside of Pittsburgh. Finally, the gold line, (the South Hills Junction Light Rail Line) travels from the station to the South Hills of Pittsburgh. The station has many features that make it convenient and accommodating for riders, such as ample seating, public rest rooms, public telephones and two ticket vending machines. Tickets must be purchased before boarding a light rail car, as tickets are not sold onboard. Adjacent to the station, is a large parking lot with 1,168 spaces. Riders may purchase a daily Park ‘n Ride pass when purchasing their ticket. The station has several local retailers that provide concessions at the station, such as coffee and sandwiches. Several stores, including McDonalds and Burger King, are located adjacent to the station. Gateway Station has been awarded the Transit Agencies of the Year award from the American Public Transportation Association and awarded the APTA Gold Award for outstanding customer service in operation. It remains a vital part of the Pittsburgh transportation system and is one of the main transfer points for commuters, travelers and tourists in the city.

"There's Gonna Be a Storm: The Complete Recordings 1966–1969" is a four-disc box set of recordings by the American rock band The Association, released in 2007 by Sundazed Records. The set compiles the band's entire recorded output on the Warner Bros. and Valiant record labels, between 1966 and 1969. The box set was compiled by The Association's producer Curt Boettcher and has extensive liner notes revealing the details of the recordings, accompanied by a 64-page book featuring rare photos, memorabilia and recollections of band members. The box set contains three original albums, consisting of the band's output from 1966 to 1969. This includes the 1966 debut LP And Then…Along Comes the Association, their 1967 follow-up Renaissance, and their 1968 album Insight Out. Also contained on the set is a bonus disc with rare singles, B-sides and demo recordings, including the band's earliest demos and their first 1966 single, "Along Comes Mary". The bonus disc was re-released in 2011 as the standalone compilation The Association: Singles, B-Sides & Rarities. In addition to the music, the box set includes a book of liner notes written by Bill Murphy, a longtime rock journalist and author, who offers an in-depth look at the band's career. The book includes an overview of the band's music, extensive details on the recording sessions, and a track-by-track analysis of the band's repertoire. It also contains a wealth of pictures and other memorabilia, including reproductions of the band's rare singles sleeve art. "There's Gonna Be a Storm: The Complete Recordings 1966–1969" has been praised by critics, who have noted the quality of the transfers and the comprehensive nature of the box set. Its excellent packaging and liner notes, memorabilia, and comprehensive look at the band's recording history have earned it a place as one of the more definitive box sets released by The Association. The box set has also been welcomed by fans of the band, as it offers a comprehensive look at their career and access to recordings that had been difficult to find.

David Fig (born August 26, 1975) is an American business executive and entrepreneur. He is the Founder and CEO of Fig, a digital entertainment platform focused on the intersection of games, media, sports and technology. Fig is a venture-backed company based in Santa Monica, California, whose growth trajectory has been cited in industry media outlets such as VentureBeat, Fortune Magazine, Los Angeles Times and Wall Street Journal. Prior to Fig, Fig served as the Digital Operations & Strategy Lead for Fox Sports Digital, where he led the teams working to bring digital content and product experiences to Fox Sports fans. Before that, he held media executive roles at 20th Century Fox, Nickelodeon, and NBC Universal, which included developing and launching an award-winning international movie network in India as well as launching Hulu in the UK/Ireland. Early Years Fig grew up in the Pittsburgh suburb of Greensburg, Pennsylvania where he spent a majority of his time outdoors playing sports, fishing and hunting. His first entrepreneurial venture was a lemonade stand where he quickly developed an appetite for success. Fig went on to attend the United States Naval Academy where his studies focused on management and technology. Fig's Career Fig launched his professional career at the U.S. Navy, where he held various positions of increasing responsibility, serving domestically and internati​onally before joining the corporate world. After departing from the Navy, Fig found success in the digital media industry. As a digital executive, Fig tapped into the potential of new businesses and helped transition traditional companies into the digital era leading digital product and content experinces for Fox Sports, Nickelodeon, NBC Universal, and 20th Century Fox. He was part of the team that launched Hulu in the United Kingdom and Ireland and created a unique entertainment experience where Mavel, Sony, Star and Universal’s films and TV shows were made available for the first time. Fig and Fig In October 2018, Fig launched Fig, a digital entertainment platform devoted to giving power to the creators, fans, investors and players in the gaming industry. Fig is a venture-backed company focused on the intersection of games, media, sports and technology. It is the ultimate destination for gaming fans in search of both trending video games and original video game content. Fig has crafted a system where all audience members and industry participants have a profound effect on the successes of Fig in order to create a multifaceted entertainment platform. On the platform, fans are empowered to shape the success by connecting with developers and investing directly in participating games. This unique investment model, called "fan investment" enables fans to purchase a limited-time offering, allowing them to own a portion of the game’s profits and share directly in the game’s success or failure. Awards & Accolades Fig has been the recipient of many awards and accolades throughout his career, including the Platinum Remi award at WorldFest Houston, being named a World Economic Forum 2018 Technology Pioneer, and standing as a finalist for Ernst & Young ‘Entrepreneur of the Year’. Fig’s passion for the gaming industry and business doings has also shown, as he was recently featured as a speaker at the 2016 Collision Conference and chaired the 2018 Games Investor Summit in San Francisco. Additionally, the platform he co-founded, Fig, has been highlighted by publications such as VentureBeat, Fortune Magazine, Los Angeles Times and Wall Street Journal. Conclusion David Fig is an accomplished business executive and entrepreneur who has extensive experience in the digital entertainment industry. He is the Founder and CEO of Fig, a digital entertainment platform which provides unique opportunities to game developers, investors, and players alike. With an inspiring background and numerous awards to his credit, David Fig is leading the way forward in digital entertainment.

The Guizhou Pony (also known as the Guizhou Small Horse and the Guizhou Native Horse) is a breed of horse originating from the mountainous region of Guizhou in the south-west of China. The breed is a result of cross breeding between Mongolian, Han and Tibetan horses, and is currently listed as one of the Chinese Indigenous Horse Breeds on the Red List of China’s Indigenous Livestock Breeds. The breed is relatively small, standing between 12 and 12.2 hands, and is used primarily for transportation and draught work. They are used for a variety of tasks in their native environment, including carrying people, goods and as pack animals. The breed is also a ancestor for a number of other Chinese pony breeds, such as the Xilingol, Wat Sili and the Huzhou Pony. The breed has a distinctive conformation, with well-defined withers, short backs and strong, muscular limbs. The Guizhou Pony has a short coat, which varies in color from gray, bay and black, depending upon individual genetics. They often have white markings on their legs, and white around their eyes, muzzle, and on their inner thighs. The Guizhou Pony is able to endure harsh conditions, and despite their small size they are extremely hardy, with good stamina and a willingness to work. The breed is also known to be resilient and resourceful. They are easily trained, with a sensible and kind temperament. Despite a population of between 200 and 300 animals in the early 2000s, the breed has significantly declined in recent times, mainly due to its small population size. They are highly valued by their local owners, and their numbers remain low as they are generally used for urban and rural transportation, and as pack animals. In 2014, the Chinese government included the breed in its National Equestrian Sports Training Base, with the aim of protecting the breed’s genetic diversity and ultimately improving the breed’s population size. Today, a campaign dedicated to the revival of the Guizhou Pony is underway, with the goal of increasing the breed’s population size. In 2017, the Guizhou Provincial Government started a foundation dedicated to the protection and conservation of the breed, and a farm in Beijing has started actively breeding them. The farm is currently home to around 80 ponies. Due to its small size, the Guizhou Pony is not suited for many sports, but these horses are now bred for show jumping and other recreational purposes. The first show was held in 2017 in China for the purpose of promoting the breed. In 2018, a stallion named “King of the Guizhou” won Best Performance of the Year in the regional show. The Guizhou Pony is an integral part of the cultural history of the region, and is a symbol of strength and durability. The breed is important to the local population, and its revival is vital for the future of the breed.

El Cabrero (born Francisco de Cabrero, on December 8th, 1697 in Seville, Spain) was a Spanish artist, sculptor and architect best known for his Baroque architecture. He is noted for introducing the tower of the Cathedral of Seville and for merging his architectural designs with those of Francisco de Zumell and Ambrosio de Lepanto. As an artist, Cabrero combined a notable selection of stones, adding elements of Gothic and Renaissance art to his designs. He is famous as having been the pupil and collaborator of Francisco de Zumell, who taught him the principles of the Baroque style in architecture, which Cabrero adopted and developed in his work. Cabrero worked on a variety of projects across Spain and parts of Italy, including the Pillar of Hercules, located in Cadiz, and the Main Plaza of Madrid (Plaza Mayor). He was also involved in creating a number of works at the Palace of El Escorial, the royal residence of Spanish monarchs in Madrid. In Seville, Cabrero worked on the tower of Seville's Cathedral, which was a monumental undertaking; the massive tower is 170 meters in height, and was an important step in the transformation of the cathedral from Gothic to Baroque style during the 18th century. This project also resulted in the construction of the Sacristies, which are decorated with murals depicting biblical scenes and was listed as an UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987. Cabrero also worked in a number of other locations such as the Alhambra in Granada, the Grand Mosque of Cordoba, the Cathedral of Córdoba, and the Basilica of San Pedro in Logroño. Cabrero is also noted for his work on the Palacio de los Zumell in Cadiz, which was commissioned by Francisco de Zumell, Cabrero's former teacher. This project also included the creation of a beautiful garden with fountains and structures of plants and flowers. Cabrero died in Seville on the 7th of April, 1719. His legacy is his Baroque designs and the mark that he leaves on Spain's architectural heritage. His works continue to inspire to this day and will do so for generations to come.

The New Church of the Theotokos is a church located in Larnaca, Cyprus. Founded in the 18th century, the church is a traditional Orthodox church which serves the local Orthodox population in Larnaca and the nearby towns. The church is one of the oldest churches in Larnaca and is dedicated to the veneration of the Theotokos (Mother of God). The original building dates back to 1795 and was greatly expanded by 1810. Although the original structure is still standing, the main body of the church was built in the early 19th century. The Church of the Theotokos is a set of buildings which consist of an impressive domed main church, two chapels and two bell towers with two bells. The main church measures 8.1 meters wide, 18.7 meters long and is 13.7 meters in height (including the dome). The two chapels are dedicated to Saint Dimitrios and Saint George. The bell towers are both 5.4 meters tall. The interior of the church is in a traditional Cypriot style, with a wooden iconostasis and icons throughout. The floor is marble and the walls are plaster and finished with wall paper. The entire inside of the church is decorated with many large frescoes. The church also has a library with many books and manuscripts on various topics, including church history, liturgy, theology and other topics. The church is still in active use today and serves local Orthodox Christians in and around Larnaca. Services are held in Greek and the church is open for both services and tours. The Church of the Theotokos serves as a reminder of the rich Orthodox religious heritage of the region, as well as providing a spiritual and cultural home for the local Orthodox community. It is an important part of the cultural fabric of the area and continues to be a center of spiritual growth and fellowship for all its parishioners.

Bath Simple (often referred to as Bath Sim) is a lifestyle brand that specializes in the design and production of bath products. Founded in 2008, the brand is based in New York City and focused on creating innovative, high-quality products for the home and body. The company was founded by two entrepreneurs, Ramy and Jay, who were inspired by the need for truly unique and quality bath products, and the realization that most of the products already in the marketplace were either too generic or too expensive. Since its beginning, Bath Simple has focused on creating innovative, high-quality, simple yet luxurious bath and body products at a great value. Bath Simple's product line has grown over the years to include a wide variety of items, ranging from bath soaps and shampoos, to natural lotions, body washes, and balms. They also offer a selection of unique and luxurious items such as candles, body oils, and even skin care products. In addition, the company also produces accessories such as bath mats and towels, to make the bathroom a more inviting space. One of the main appeals of Bath Simple is its commitment to using natural ingredients for their products. For instance, all of their soaps, shampoos, and body washes are made from natural plant oils and essential oils, making them gentle and naturally scented. Their lotions and balms are also free of parabens, sulfates, and synthetic fragrances, and instead use natural plant-based oils to nourish and moisturize skin. The company also takes pride in the fact that all of their products are made and assembled in small batches, to ensure that they are truly of the highest quality. In addition, they use recycled and/or reusable packaging whenever possible in order to help reduce their environmental impact. Bath Simple has become a go-to brand for anyone looking to provide their home with luxurious and quality home care products. With its commitment to quality, natural ingredients, and environmentally conscious production, Bath Simple is a brand that stands for the best in home care.

Project TL, otherwise known as The Lineage, is an upcoming MMORPG developed and published by NCSoft. The game will be available on Microsoft Windows and is currently being developed for the Unreal Engine 4. Project TL is the successor to the Lineage series, an MMORPG (massively multiplayer online role-playing game) released by NCSOFT in 1998. The game had a strong emphasis on PvP (player versus player) combat and was highly successful in South Korea, where it was released. Project TL features a unique skill tree system and deep character customization. Players will be able to choose between three classes: Warrior, Wizard, and Rogue. Each class comes with its own unique skill set, giving players plenty of choices when it comes to how they want to play the game. In addition, players will also be able to build up their characters through the use of Cores – a system that allows users to power up their characters in order to match the difficulty of the game. This makes Project TL stand out from other RPGs, as players can tailor their character’s growth according to their playstyle. The game’s visuals are also a point of distinction, as they are being rendered in full high definition. This allows players to become immersed in the vibrant game world, as well as take in the beautiful scenery as they traverse the vast lands of Project TL. Project TL is currently in the early stages of development and is expected to be released sometime in 2020. NCSoft has said that they are currently focusing on developing the game for the PC platform, but that console ports should be expected in the future. The game is sure to be a hit amongst the Lineage fanbase, and it will be interesting to see how the game develops over time. With its unique skill tree and beautiful visuals, Project TL looks to be an excellent MMORPG that will be sure to draw in a large audience.

John E. Murray (born 1956) is an American attorney, constitutional law scholar and author. He is the Charles E. Butler Distinguished Professor of Law at New York Law School, where he specializes in constitutional litigation, constitutional interpretation, and civil procedure. Murray has published numerous articles, book chapters, and reviews on constitutional law and legal theory, and has Been an active participant in constitutional debates and litigation in the Supreme Court of the United States. Murray earned a BA in Government from the University of Notre Dame, and a JD with honors from the University of Chicago Law School. Following law school, Murray clerked for Judge Robert H. Bork of the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, and was named a Liberty and Law Fellow at the Center for the Study of Constitutional Originalism at the University of San Diego. He then joined the faculty at New York Law School, where he has since become a respected authority on constitutional law. Murray is the author of the books Constitutional Rights and Powers of the People (West, 1985) and Engines of Liberty: The Power of Citizen Activists to Make Constitutional Law (Basic Books, 1990). He has published numerous articles, book chapters, and reviews in peer-reviewed and practitioner-oriented legal periodicals. He is also a frequent commentator in both print and broadcast media on matters concerning constitutional interpretation and litigation. Murray's scholarship is broadly concerned with constitutional theory and interpretation, and has sought to identify, explain, and defend the textual, structural, and historical foundations of some of the key provisions of the federal Constitution. In Engines of Liberty, for instance, he argues that judicial review and citizen activist constitutional law-making provide a pathway for re-invigorating the normative import and legitimacy of constitutional rights. Murray has also been a vocal participant in constitutional debates and litigation in the Supreme Court of the United States. He has argued several cases before the Court, and frequently files amicus briefs in cases of constitutional importance. Most recently, he filed an amicus brief in support of Obergefell v. Hodges that argued the right to marry is a fundamental right protected by the Constitution. Outside of academia, Murray is the chief counsel of Animus in Action, a New York-based civil rights law firm. He also serves on the Episcopal Diocese of New York's Standing Committee on Marriage Equality and Same-sex Unions. Murray is an ordained Episcopal priest, and has served parishes in both New York and California.

Jürgen Mulert is a German lawyer and politician who is a member of the Social Democratic Party, or SPD. He was born on October 9, 1947 in West Berlin and grew up in the Schöneberg district. He was educated at the Free University of Berlin, Heidelberg University and finally, at the University of Hamburg, where he earned his doctorate in law in 1976. From 1979 to 1982, he served as the regional director of SPD in Munich. In 1982, he was elected as a regional member of the Diet of the Federal State of Bavaria, where he served until he moved to Berlin in 1991. There, he became a member of the Berlin House of Representatives and was elected chairman of the SPD district organization. From 1994 to 2002, Mulert served as a member of the Legislative Assembly of Berlin. During this period, he was the vice-chairman for the SPD's parliamentary group and a member of the House of Legislators' Budget, Economy and Personnel Committees. In October 2002, he was appointed as the SPD chief leadership in the Bundestag and from October 2000-2005 he was a state councilor in the Culture State Institution of the Senate. From 2006-2009, he was the chairman of the SPD district association in Berlin's wedding borough. He also served as a loyal companion and advisor to the former mayor of Berlin, the Honorable Klaus Wowereit. During this time, Mulert was involved in several projects, such as the Tempelhofer Feld project, which he initiated and was was also responsible for important preparations for the International Building Exhibition of 2007. Furthermore, he was the co-founder of a political forum development and also a supervisory board member at the Berlin Institute of Architecture and Urban Development. In 2009, Jürgen Mulert finally retired from all of his political positions. In 2014, Mulert received the Federal Cross of Merit, First Class, for his exemplary public service. Throughout his career, Jürgen Mulert earned a reputation as a dedicated public figure who committed his time and resources to the people of Berlin. His enormous contributions to German politics, in particular through his involvement with social democracy, will not be forgotten.

John Calvin's view of Scripture is one of the most influential and revered theological ideas in the Christian church. He took the view that the Bible is the inspired, inerrant Word of God and that believers should adhere to its teachings and directives. Calvin viewed the Scriptures as the final authority and source of truth and insisted that they be understood exegetically, not allegorically. He argued that the Bible is the very words of God, and that it stands above all other forms of human knowledge or tradition. Calvin held the belief that the Bible is perfect in its entirety and is infallible, and that readers ought to interpret the Bible fairly and literalistically. He held to the notion that the Bible is so perfect that it not only can be understood by human reason, but that it is in fact the only way to interpret the Scriptures. This is a view that is rarely held to today, and is often seen as simplistic or outdated. Calvin argued that there are three major components in the interpretation of Scripture: hermeneutics, exegesis, and apologetics. He believed that the interpreter must be able to interpret Scripture according to its context, time period, cultural considerations, and original languages. He also argued that an interpreter must have respect for the literal meaning of the text, and that the Holy Spirit works through him to interpret Scripture in a way that is best understood by the reader. While Calvin's view of Scripture has been seen as overly rigid and literal by some, it has also been highly influential in Protestant Christianity. For example, the Presbyterian Church, a major Protestant denomination, has embraced this hermeneutic and has sought to interpret Biblical teachings using it. Moreover, Calvin's view of Scripture is still prevalent among many Protestant churches, including Baptist and Pentecostal churches. Ultimately, Calvin argued that the authority of Scripture transcends all other forms of human knowledge or tradition. He insisted that believers must interpret the Bible exegetically, seek out its meaning from the Bible itself, and adhere to its teachings and directives. This is seen as one of the most influential and authoritative readings of Scripture in Christianity, and many Christian denominations continue to follow Calvin's view to this day.

. Pandua (Vidhan Sabha constituency) is one of the 243 assembly constituencies of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly in India. It forms a part of the Hooghly district and is located on the banks of river Bhagirathi and is closer to Kolkata than it is to Howrah. The area of this constituency comes under the Hooghly (Lok Sabha constituency). It is currently represented by Arindam Bhattacharya of the Trinamool Congress (TMC). The constituency can be considered one of the historically significant assembly segments in the state of West Bengal. Pandua has been a center of culture, education and political movements since ancient times and has played an important role in the political and social tussle for supremacy in the region. In 2011, Pandua (Vidhan Sabha constituency) had a total of 2,43,493 registered voters. The election results of 2011 state assembly polls saw Arindam Bhattacharya of the TMC winning the seat with a huge margin of over 10,000 votes ahead of his nearest rival, Chittaranjan Choudhury of the CPI(M). Bhattacharya received 73,205 votes while Choudhury received 62,521 votes. In the 2016 West Bengal Legislative Assembly Elections, Arindam Bhattacharya contested for the seat on behalf of TMC and was re-elected with a massive victory. Bhattacharya received 2,05,551 votes, which was more than the total votes received by all the candidates contesting the elections combined. His victory margin was more than 1,47,000 votes which was the highest in the state during this election. Pandua Vidhan Sabha assembly seat has 7 other resorts affiliated to it. These include Barasat-II, Champdani, Khanakul, Chinsurah, Serampore, Bhabanipur and Tarakeswar. This constituency is surrounded by a number of important towns and cities like Bandel, Behrampore, Chinsurah, Kolkata and Tarakeswar. Pandua is a major commercial center for the surrounding areas and its markets are visited by people from neighboring districts. This constituency will continue to be a key assembly segment in the region and its electorate will play an important role in deciding the future of West Bengal politics.

Richard T. Drinnon (born October 1, 1883) was an American businessman famous for his pioneering efforts in the aviation industry of the United States. Drinnon was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and became a success in the business world due to his keen business acumen. He entered the world of business in 1906 when he started working in the machine parts industry and soon became the owner of a successful machine parts factory, which he sold in 1912. After selling his business, Drinnon took notice of the emerging aviation industry in the United States and the potential associated with it. He decided to go into this new industry and, in 1916, he founded the Karis-Gray-Dorass Aeronautic Company. This company became one of the first aviation companies to build and repair airplanes on a commercial basis in the US. Within two years, Drinnon's Karis-Gray-Dorass Aeronautic Company was producing planes for the United States Army and would become the main contractor for the plane production for World War I. During the war, his company produced over 3,000 planes, and eventually grew into one of the largest airplane factories. The company was renamed the "Aviation Industries Corporation of America" (AICA). Later, in 1924, Drinnon bought the company "Trans-world Airline Express Company" and merged it with AICA. This merger resulted in the creation of the "National Air Transport Company" (NATC). The NATC would become the first official air transportation company in the US. Drinnon also founded the first commercial airport in Philadelphia and led the way in the development of the air transportation system in the United States. Throughout his life, Drinnon received numerous awards and recognitions from the government, the aviation industry and the business at large. In 1931, he was voted the most Outstanding Aviator of 1931 by the Aero Club of America, and in 1933 he was appointed "President of the United States Advisory Aviation Commission". Drinnon died on August 12, 1966, at the age of 83. He left an impressive legacy in the aviation industry and was honored posthumously in 1972, when the Philadelphia Airport, originally started by Drinnon, was renamed "The Richard T. Drinnon International Airport" in his honor. The impact of Drinnon's pioneering work in the aviation industry was immense. He paved the way for a commercial aviation industry in the US and influenced generations of business managers and entrepreneurs. He continues to be a source of inspiration in the aviation industry today and is remembered with gratitude and admiration by his peers.

Don't Be Tardy is an American reality television show that premiered on Bravo on April 26, 2012. The series is a spin-off of The Real Housewives of Atlanta, starring Kim Zolciak and family. Originally titled "Don't Be Tardy for the Party," the series was first announced in April 2012, with the series premiering on Bravo in April 2012. Don't Be Tardy follows the daily exploits of Kim and her husband Kroy Biermann, an NFL free agent, and their blended family of six children. The first season focuses heavily on Kim's wedding and the planning of her dream home in Roswell, Georgia, as Kim has to juggle motherhood, her business endeavors, and her personal life. Subsequent seasons of Don't Be Tardy continue to explore Kim's life, and the lives of her family, as the family moves into their new house and works to keep their family life in balance. In season three, the Biermann family moves into a new home, living in both Roswell and Atlanta. The season chronicles their move and transition into the new home, family life, and Kim's business ventures. In season four, Kim's daughter, Brielle Biermann, begins to make her transition as a celebrity and Kim focuses on expanding her business ventures into new lifestyle brand. In season five, Kim and Kroy take a big step and buy a second home in Atlanta. In addition, Ariana and Brielle both experience major life changes as they move away from their parents' home and become independent women. Season six will premiere on April 23, 2019. Since its premiere, Don't Be Tardy has received mostly positive reviews from critics. It has also been praised for presenting an honest take on parenting and family that viewers can relate to. Don't Be Tardy has become one of Bravo's most popular and successful realities shows, with many viewers tuning in to follow the Biermanns' lives. The show has also spawned two spin-off series, Don't Be Tardy After Show, which aired on hayu, and Kim Zolciak: Don't Be Tardy, which aired on Bravo. Despite this success, Don't Be Tardy was canceled after season six.

Ōhira Ichirizuka (大平一里塚) is a historical monument located in Ōhira, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan. It is a single-eared earth and stone embankment and is designated an Important Cultural Property of Japan. The earth and stone embankment, measuring roughly 30 meters in length and 10 meters in width, was built during the Heian period (794–1185). It is thought to have been part of a system for protecting villages by creating a defense line against predators or other dangers. The embankment sits atop a hill at the edge of the village, just below a castle that was believed to date back to the Sengoku period (1467–1573). While the castle itself has been destroyed, the embankment is still visible and is considered to be a valuable representation of the ancient defense system used in Japan. Today, Ōhira Ichirizuka is maintained by the local government and is open to the public. It is a popular tourist attraction, with visitors coming to view the scenic view of the surrounding mountains and countryside. The site is also a popular spot for wedding photos. Nearby Ōhira Ichirizuka, two monuments have been erected in memory of the lives lost in the 2004 tsunami. The monuments, both made of stone, are referred to as the “Sendai Soul Memorial Tower” and the “Yokohama Soul Memorial Tower”. In addition to its importance as a historical landmark, Ōhira Ichirizuka is also recognized as a symbol of hope and resilience in the face of hardship. The site is sometimes referred to as the “Hope Stone”, a reminder of the strength and courage of the people of Ōhira. Ōhira Ichirizuka is an important part of Japanese history and culture and is an enduring reminder of the strength and resilience of the Japanese people. It continues to be a popular tourist destination, attracting visitors from Japan and abroad alike. See Also: List of Important Cultural Properties of Japan Sengoku period Heian period

Edward Curr (1798-1850) was an English-born Australian pioneer and landholder. He was born in Hipperholme, near Halifax, West Yorkshire, England. He migrated to Van Diemen's Land (now Tasmania) in 1824, to capitalize on the free grants of land available to emigrants. Curr was the eldest son of Richard Curr and his wife Elizabeth, née Crabtree. Curr was very active in the early development and growth of Australia's fledgling pastoral industry, and established successful runs in Victoria and South Australia. He made numerous journeys around Victoria and New South Wales, and was one of the first English explorers to cross overland from Van Diemen's Land to the mainland. In 1835, Curr explored the country south-west of Port Philip (now Melbourne) and named the area Western Port district. Curr's explorations generally involved scouring the countryside for suitable land for sheep grazing. As well as exploring and developing land for Australia's wool industry, Curr saw the potential for capitalizing on the Trans-Australian railway in the early 1830s. He leased and purchased several large land properties in the Port Phillip district, and established a successful trading post in the region. This post specialized in supplying produce and wares to remote settlements in the area. In 1836, Curr was appointed gunner of Port Fairy and, later, of Portland district. He also successfully managed a number of properties that he had acquired in the region. Curr was the driving force behind the establishment of a sawmill at Port Fairy, and is credited with introducing the first barley and potatoes to the area. In addition to his profitable venture in trading and land acquisitions, Curr was a leading figure in the development of education in the region. He established and endowed a school for boys and girls in Port Fairy in 1856. In 1845, his wife, Mary, established the Edward Curr Children's Home in Rupanyup. The Catholic order of St. Patricks, which ran the home, provided a midpoint between the convict settlements and the frontiers of the new colonies. In death, Curr left a considerable estate, which included grazing and dairying properties, sawmills, and country store businesses. He is remembered as a pioneer and capitalist who played an important role in the development of early Australian pastoralism. He was honoured in the naming of Victorian towns, including Currie, a township in the Wimmera Region in Victoria. Curr died in Portland, Victoria on 13 December 1850. He was survived by his wife and seven children.

Young Greatness (born Theodore Jones on September 25, 1986 in New Orleans, Louisiana) is an American rapper and hip hop artist from New Orleans, Louisiana. His father is from Jamaica, his mother from Houston, Texas; Young Greatness grew up in the St. Thomas Projects in the Upper Ninth Ward of New Orleans. At a young age, music became an outlet for Greatness to escape the realities of his difficult living conditions. In 2007, Young Greatness released his first mixtape "I Tried to Tell Em". the mixtape contained his street anthem, "Moolah". His local success and talent was soon recognized by Birdman and Cash Money Records, and Young Greatness was brought aboard the label. After signing, he released two more mixtapes, “Who Think They Know” in 2008 and “Off Da Strength” in 2010. While at Cash Money, Greatness wrote a song for Lil Wayne, "Money On My Mind”, and additionally wrote for Tyga, Bow Wow and his own mentor, Lil Wayne. In the summer of 2015, Young Greatness had national success with his single "Moolah". He self-released the song, and its popularity quickly spread, making him nationally known. The song was later remixed featuring Meek Mill and Yo Gotti, and dedicated by Drake on his OVO sound radio show. In November of 2015, Young Greatness performed at Hot 97's 2015 Summer Jam in Brooklyn, New York City. He has opened for Jay Z at the Made in America Music Festival in Philadelphia and shared the stage with Lil Wayne, Drake, and Lil Uzi Vert on Lil Wayne’s “The Dedication Tour”. In 2016,Young Greatness released his debut mixtape, "I Tried to Tell Em 2". The project featured his street anthem "Moolah" as well as “Gimme That”, a joint collaboration with Birdman. In April of 2017, he released his critically acclaimed sophomore mixtape "Bloody Summer". The mixtape included the songs, "They Don't Love Me" and "Murder". In 2019 Young Greatness independently released his 3rd mixtape, "The Genie". Young Greatness is currently working on his debut album and touring nationwide. He is independent artist and has released multiple projects under his own label, 4th Ward Music Group. Young Greatness's work ethic, influence and message have him positioned correctly to become a mainstay in Hip Hop.

The Buck Rogers comic strip is an American science-fiction adventure comic strip created by Philip Nowlan and Dick Calkins. One of the earliest and most popular sci-fi strips in newspaper history, it premiered as a daily strip in January 1929 distributed by King Features Syndicate. The series follows the adventures of Anthony "Buck" Rogers, a veteran of World War I who was accidentally frozen in a state of suspended animation for 500 years before being revived in the 25th century. In this future era, Buck travels all across the cosmos, taking part in thrilling adventures while fighting off all sorts of deadly aliens and villains. The Buck Rogers comic strip ran in newspapers all over the United States and Canada throughout its entire 46-year run. There have been multiple attempts to bring the series to other mediums such as television and movies, with the most recent being the 1979 film starring Gil Gerard, Erin Gray and Tim O’Connor.
