Capell Bedell (1810-1868) was a British barrister and prodigious translator of Teutonic literature. He was the son of Sir William Bedell, and was born in Caen, Normandy, France. In 1825, he matriculated from Trinity College, Cambridge. After 1831, he was called to the Bar of England, and was an advocate of the Court of Common Pleas. Throughout his life, Bedell published various works related to Teutonic literature, most notably his translations of Icelandic sagas. In 1844, he published a version of Egill Skallagrímsson’s Saga, which was the first English translation of this saga. Bedell also translated several Eddic poems, as well as the Rune Poem, which is the only surviving Rune poem in English. Among his other translations were 'Viglundar Saga' from Thomas Thoroddsen and 'Grettis Saga' from George Stephens in 1862. In 1865, Bedell established the University of London's first Chair in Scandinavian Language and Literature. This prompted a resurgence of interest in Scandinavian language and culture, and consequentially led to increased academic activity in this field. It was likely through Bedell’s efforts that Icelandic Studies, and Scandinavian branch of Germanic studies within the University of London, were formed. All of Bedell's translations were of a very high quality, and were greatly admired. His ability to capture the essence of the material he was working with, while still producing a finished product that was understandable to a contemporary English reader, was commended. In addition to his translations, Bedell was also the author of several works on Scandinavian poetics. Bedell’s work had a lasting impact on the scholarship of Teutonic culture and literature. His translations opened up these works to a wider audience, and provided a greater level of materials to be studied and analysed. Through his dedication and passion for Teutonic literature, Capell Bedell has left a legacy of scholarship and enthusiasm for the field which will continue to be studied for many years.

Ptolemais in Phoenicia (also known as Akko or Accho, from the Hebrew name "Akkō") was an Ancient Hellenistic city-state located in the northern coastal region of the eastern Mediterranean in present-day northern Israel. Ptolemais was founded in the 3rd century BC by Ptolemy I of Egypt. It was originally commissioned as a naval port and trading post between Egypt, Syria, Phoenicia, and the rest of the eastern Mediterranean region. Ptolemy established it as the first city of his Egyptian-Phoenician empire, which he named after himself as "Ptolemais". During its heyday, Ptolemais was a bustling port and commercial center. The city was destroyed by Alexander the Great in 332 BC, but was soon rebuilt by the Ptolemies. It remained an important trading port into the Hellenistic and Roman eras, though it eventually lost much of its significance with the fall of the Ptolemaic dynasty. The city remained largely intact until its destruction by a Crusader army in 1291, after which it lay in ruins until being rediscovered in the 18th century. Over the centuries, it has been occupied in turn by the Mamluks, the Ottoman Empire, the British Empire, the State of Israel and Palestinian militants in the Arab-Israeli War. Today, Ptolemais is a walled city that retains its ancient charm despite the modern changes it has undergone since its founding. It is a popular tourist destination due to its historical sites, including the fortifications, an ancient Maritime museum, and an archaeological excavation site. Most of the original city has been preserved and restored and is open to visitors. It has become a major center of culture, education, and industry in the region, with a major port, an international airport, numerous museums, galleries, and cultural centers, and a thriving economy.

The Jackson State Tigers basketball team is a college basketball program that represents Jackson State University in Jackson, Mississippi, United States. The Tigers compete in the NCAA Division I and are members of the Southwestern Athletic Conference (SWAC). The program has its origins in 1937 when, under the guidance of coach Robert "Gip" Gipson, the university's basketball program became the first African-American college basketball team in the country. The Tigers have appeared in the NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament four times, most recently in 2019. The team made its first major postseason appearance in 1980 when it reached the semifinals of the NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament. The Tigers have won four SWAC regular season championships and three SWAC Tournament championships. Notable Jackson State alums include Hall of Famers Bobby C. Watson and Lenny Wilkens. Watson was a member of the 1972 United States Olympic basketball team, which won the gold medal at the Munich games. Wilkens had a long and distinguished playing and coaching career, including a stint as head coach of the NBA's Atlanta Hawks. He was inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame in 1998. The current head coach of the Jackson State Tigers is Lewis Jackson. Jackson became head coach in 2013 after a nine-year stint at Saint Louis University as an assistant coach. In his four years as head coach of the Tigers, Jackson has led the team to two SWAC regular season titles and two SWAC Tournament championships. He was also named the 2015 SWAC Coach of the Year. Under Jackson's guidance, the Tigers have become one of the premier teams in the SWAC and have made three straight appearances in the NCAA Tournament. The team has also earned recognition nationally with numerous players receiving postseason awards and honors throughout Jackson's tenure. The Jackson State Tigers have established themselves as one of the top men's basketball programs in the Southwestern Athletic Conference and will continue to strive for excellence as they look to increase their on-court success in the coming years.

Mike Ross (born 5 October 1977 in Limerick, Ireland) is a former Irish rugby union player who played as a tighthead prop. He was active as a rugby player from 2001 to 2018. Ross started his rugby career at local Limerick club Shannon RFC and was then recognised by the Munster Rugby Academy. After spending a year at Cork Constitution, he was selected to join the Munster pro-rugby squad in 2001. During the 2002–03 season, Ross won a Munster Senior Cup title. In 2003, Ross was called up to the Irish national team and won the Triple Crown with his teammates in their Grand Slam victory in the 2005 Six Nations Championship. He then went on to represent Ireland at the 2007 Rugby World Cup. This World Cup also marked Ross's breakthrough as one of world's premier props and he was awarded IRB Player of the Year for his performance in the tournament. In 2010, Ross made the move to the English Premiership with London Irish and in 2011, he was part of the Irish squad that won the Six Nations Championship. Ross was then called up to take part in the 2013 British and Irish Lions tour of Australia. In 2018, Ross announced his retirement from rugby union, having amassed 143 caps for Ireland in addition to winning two Six Nations Championships. He was instrumental in the development of the Irish scrum and his contribution to the sport will be remembered for many years to come. After his retirement, Ross returned to Shannon RFC to take up a coaching role in their academy, developing the next generation of young Irish players. He is currently working as an administrator and pundit, appearing regularly as a rugby expert on Irish television.

Vehicle blind spot, also known as a blind spot, refers to the area in a vehicle's rear view mirror that cannot be seen by the driver. The blind spot is caused by the presence of an object or vehicle that is located in the area of the vehicle that cannot be seen from the driver's point of view due to the shape of the mirror, headrests, and other objects. The blind spot is particularly relevant to drivers of cars and trucks, as it limits their vision when changing lanes. This can lead to accidents, as the driver may not be able to see a vehicle that is in their blind spot. Blind spot accidents can also occur due to rapid changes in a vehicle's course or direction while attempting to merge into a lane that may have a vehicle in the blind spot. In order to reduce the risk of a blind spot accident, drivers are encouraged to use the "three-point turn" method when changing lanes. This involves looking over their shoulder at the blind spot before initiating the turn. This allows drivers to check for any vehicles in the blind spot, without having to rely solely on the rear view mirror. Blind spot monitoring systems, also known as Blind Spot Information Systems (BLIS), are becoming increasingly common in modern cars and trucks. This system uses cameras, radar, ultrasonic, or other sensors to detect any vehicles in the blind spot, and then alerts the driver, usually through a light or sound, when a vehicle is detected. This gives drivers an extra layer of safety when changing lanes and merging onto highways. Other technologies, such as lane departure warning systems, are being developed to further reduce the risk of blind spot accidents. Lane departure warning systems track the vehicle’s position within the lane, and alert the driver if the car begins to drift away from the lane. This can be particularly useful in reducing blind spot accidents, as it can warn drivers when they are attempting to merge into an occupied lane. Overall, blind spot accidents are a major cause of vehicle collisions, and these can often be avoided with the proper procedures and technology. Drivers should be aware of the blind spots present in their vehicles, and use common sense and safety measures when changing lanes or merging onto highways. Additionally, blind spot monitoring systems and lane departure warning systems can provide drivers with an extra layer of safety when driving.

James Street (born 28 May 1989) is an English professional cricketer who played county cricket for Yorkshire County Cricket Club (YCCC) and his outstanding performances seen him become an English international in Test and One-Day cricket. He attended King Edward VI Grammar school, Louth and later gained a Bachelor of Science degree in Sports Performance and Coaching from Edge Hill University in Ormskirk. In 2008, Street was drafted by the YCCC and immediately became a star player. His remarkable performances saw him rise to be one of the top bowlers in the first-class county championship and eventually established him as a first-choice player for the one-day and twenty20 formats. His career-best performance came in a test match in December 2013 against India where he took a ten-wicket haul in the match. In 2017 Street was named in the England Test squad for the tour of India and made his debut against India in the third test match where he picked up a four-wicket haul. He continued to perform consistently, cementing his place in the side. His growing success saw him featured in the squad for the 2019 Cricket World Cup in England and Wales. Street retired from professional cricket in June 2020, having not appeared in English match since 2017. He cited dissatisfaction with the amount of first team opportunities available to him and the lack of support from YCCC as contributing factors to his retirement. Since retirement, Street actively participates in professional development initiatives with aspiring cricketers across England and has also taken up volunteer and development programmes with his previous club YCCC. He has also opened up his own cricket coaching agency in effort to pass on his knowledge and experience to cricketers of the future. Street's legacy is firmly established in English cricket. His remarkable performances, evident on the international stage, saw him become a valuable member of successive England teams. He can be looked upon as source of inspiration for current and upcoming cricketers.

The Bush Doctrine is a phrase used to describe the foreign policy approach of the 43rd President of the United States, George W. Bush. This strategy was rooted in the idea of preemptive military action in order to protect the security of the United States, an approach that was first proclaimed in a 2002 speech given by President Bush following the terrorist attacks of September 11th, 2001. The Bush Doctrine was heavily influenced by the ideal of American exceptionalism- the idea that, as the most powerful nation in the world, the U.S. has the right, responsibility, and capacity to intervene in international disputes and protect global peace. Additionally, the Bush Doctrine states that all individuals and nations should exercise their right to self-defense, as long as it upholds the principle of fairness and reciprocity. As such, the Bush Doctrine incites preventive military action, as opposed to simply responding to threats after they have occurred. At its core, the Bush Doctrine is largely composed of two main elements- The first one is the broad geopolitical concept known as "Forward Strategy", where the U.S. engages its geopolitical rivals, such as the Global War on Terror and the War in Iraq, directly with immediate military action. The second element of the doctrine is known as the "Bush Military Doctrine", which is a more aggressive stance that stresses the need for the U.S. to be militarily ready to deal with any potential aggressor at all times. In an attempt to enforce the Bush Doctrine, the U.S. launched its own military operations, nation-rebuilding efforts, and economic sanctions in affected regions. This included increased U.S. military presence in areas such as the Middle East, as well as the introduction of various counter-terrorism, intelligence-gathering, and global surveillance initiatives. Apart from this, the U.S. also introduced a number of measures aimed at promoting democracy abroad, such as free elections and economic development programs. The Bush Doctrine has been met with both criticism and praise. Critics have voiced concerns regarding the legality and morality of preemptive military action, while others have argued that the approach is a necessary response to international threats. Supporters of the Bush Doctrine, however, see the policy as a logical step towards ensuring global security and protecting the interests of the United States. Despite its ongoing controversy, the Bush Doctrine is still seen as an integral part of the U.S. foreign policy. It has become a major benchmark used to measure the international priorities of today's superpower and continues to shape the foreign policy of the United States.

Brian Christie (born June 10, 1950) is a Canadian neuroscientist and professor of psychiatry at the University of Toronto and the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health. Christie has dedicated his research career to discovering and elucidating the mechanisms behind substance use disorder. He is currently working on elucidating dopamine- and glutamate-driven mechanisms underlying the neurobiological pliability contributing to the reinforcing effects of addictive drugs, including the homeostatic control of cell communication networks, the hedonic response associated with drug use, and the role of stress and reward in the treatment of addiction. Christie was born in Montréal, Canada, and received his B.Sc. from Concordia University. He then went on to obtain his PhD from the University of Saskatchewan, after which he moved to the University of Toronto in 1980 to pursue a post-doctoral fellowship focusing on brain circuitry. Shortly after that, he joined the faculty at the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health. Over the past several decades, Christie's research has focused on uncovering the complexity behind substance use problems and exploring ways to disrupt the reinforcing effects of substances. He and his colleagues have developed and recommended a number of pharmacological and behavioural treatments for people with substance use problems. This includes medications such as naltrexone and ketamine, as well as a variety of psychotherapeutic approaches, such as cognitive-behavioural therapy and motivational interviewing. Christie has authored and co-authored several books and over 200 publications in peer-reviewed journals. He has served as an editor for a number of books, as well as a board member for scientific and clinical journals. He has also served as an advisor for Canada's National Institute on Drug Abuse, an expert advisory panel member of Vancouver’s drug strategy, and the Chairman of the National Advisory Council on Alcohol and Drug Abuse in Canada. Christie is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada. In 2020, he was honoured with the James S. McDonnell Foundation Mental Health and Addiction Award for his significant contribution to the field of addiction research. Throughout his career, Christie has been a passionate advocate for people with substance use issues. He has been a champion of public health initiatives and has advocated for investment in drug prevention and treatment programs. Brian Christie’s research substantiates the belief that substance use problems are ultimately preventable and treatable, and his efforts to advance the science in the field of substance use have made a lasting impact on the understanding of the neurological operations behind substance use disorders.

Romano's Macaroni Grill is an American-style Italian casual dining chain that specializes in Italian-American cuisine such as pastas, pizzas, seafood, salads, steaks and other dishes. The restaurant chain is owned and operated by MARG (M&R Acquisition Group, LLC), a Dallas-based private dining and hospitality company. The chain was founded on November 11, 1988 in Leon Springs, Texas by Philip J. Romano. Romano sold the chain to Brinker International on 1995 and Brinker remained the owner until June 2010. At that time, the chain of 211 stores was sold to Mac Chili, LLC, a private equity firm owned by Boca Raton, Florida-based Palmer Fan Holdings, LLC, for an initial cost of $131.5 million. The restaurant chain’s signature dishes include its Chicken Scaloppine, Chicken Carbonara and Pork Chops Marsala. Other popular dishes on the menu include wood-fired pizzas, gourmet pasta dishes and over-stuffed sandwiches. Every dish on the menu uses the freshest ingredients and cooks them to order. The restaurant chain also pays special attention to the preparation of its specialty sauces and homemade dressing, which are made with fresh herbs and spices. At Romano’s Macaroni Grill, customers can also enjoy the pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. The interior of the restaurant is designed with natural wood beams, tiled floors, stucco walls and a high-volume open kitchen that adds to the warm and welcoming atmosphere. In addition, the restaurant also offers a full bar, which serves a variety of wines and cocktails. The restaurant is most famous for its generous portions of Italian-American dishes made from the freshest ingredients. Customers often return to Romano's Macaroni Grill to enjoy its wood-fired pizzas, tasty specials, and perfectly prepared pasta dishes. With its warm atmosphere, generous portions and delicious food, Romano’s Macaroni Grill is a popular destination for everyone.

The 4th Canadian Film Awards were held in April 1953 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, to celebrate and honour excellence in Canadian cinema. Canadian Film Awards are organized each year by the Academy of Canadian Cinema and Television, also known as the Academy. The awards were created to recognize Canadian achievements in the motion picture industry, and to promote a national culture of excellence and recognition for Canadians in the film industry. Categories for the 4th Canadian Film Awards included Best Film, Best Documentary, Best Actor, Best Actress, Best Director, Best Story, Best Score, Best Art Direction, Best Special Effects, Best Costume Design, Best Photograph, Best Soundtrack and Best Short Film. The 1953 awards had a number of firsts, including being the first time an award was given for Best Musical Score and Best Special Effects. The awards also featured a lifetime achievement award for Samuel Bronston, who was a Polish-born director and producer and had previously served as an executive for the 20th Century Fox film studio in Hollywood. Jackie Cooper and Kirk Douglas were two of the guests at the ceremony. Douglas was among the 4th Canadian Film Awards presenters and he presented the Best Actress and Best Director awards to Jean Bernard and Norman Cohn, respectively. The 1953 Canadian Film Awards were generally well-received by Canadians, and the presentations were broadcast on CBC Television as part of CBC's newly-launched television network. Awards were also presented in subsequent years and the Canadian film industry has continued to thrive ever since. The following are the winners of the 4th Canadian Film Awards: Best Film: River of ASudden Best Documentary: The Beaver People Best Actor: Don DeFore for River of ASudden Best Actress: Jean Bernard for River of ASudden Best Director: Norman Cohn for River of ASudden Best Story: Al Kay for River of ASudden Best Score: Carl De Nys for The Beaver People Best Art Direction: David Miller for The Beaver People Best Special Effects: Don Druker for The Beaver People Best Costume Design: Mack Shaine for The Beaver People Best Photograph: Arthur Topgg for The Beaver People Best Soundtrack: Carl De Nys for The Beaver People Best Short Film: The Mitten Shuffle

Bolton High School is a public high school located in Bolton, Connecticut, United States. The school serves students in grades nine through twelve from the towns of Bolton and Andover. Bolton High School opened its doors in 1960. The school is governed by the Regional School District #10 which is comprised of Regional School Superintendent, a school board of seven elected members from each town, and the member towns, Bolton and Andover. The school is a member of the Central Connecticut Conference (CCC), along with other public high schools in the state. Bolton High School consists of seven buildings which are spread out on nearly 170 acres of land. The main building contains more than 58 classrooms and hosts more than 1700 students. The school also has two computer labs and three libraries which offer modern digital resources, such as the Internet. Bolton High School offers a wide variety of courses and extracurricular activities. The academic curriculum includes a core program of English, math, science, social studies, health/physical education, world languages, and career education. The school also provides many specialized elective courses in art, business, family and consumer science, industrial tech, technology, music, online learning, and many more. An honors program for advanced level courses is also integral. The school is known for its various extracurricular activities, including band, cheerleading, chorus, dance, drama, and journalism. The school's athletic teams, commonly referred to as the "Bulldogs," compete in the Central Connecticut Conference to participate in interscholastic competitions in a multitude of sports such as golf, soccer, basketball, softball, football, baseball, and hockey. Bolton High School is well respected as an institution of learning, education, and activities. Every year the school produces many graduates who excel in college and in life. Additionally, Bolton High School strives to provide every student the right to a quality education, as well as instill social values and character building experiences to assist in the successful molding of the members of its student body.

Radnorshire Arms is a public house located in Knighton, Powys, Wales. It was established in 1726 and is the oldest surviving inn in the area. The current building dates back to 1760, and has been home to several royal visitors in its time, including Queen Victoria and King George IV. The building has gone through several transformations over the years. The original pub was destroyed by fire in 1802 and had to be rebuilt. The exterior of the pub is mostly unchanged, but the interior has been modernized over the centuries. Inside, the pub retains many traditional features, including low ceilings, wooden beams, and fireplaces. It is divided into several areas, each with its own unique atmosphere and appeal. There is a snug bar which contains a selection of cask ales, bottled beers and ciders, as well as a great range of spirits and soft drinks. The main bar area itself is decorated with an eclectic mix of traditional artwork, including its signature mural of a local hillside. The pub also serves a variety of traditional pub food and features a selection of daily specials. It also houses a separate restaurant area for diners, featuring a range of British cuisine. The pub also has live music on weekends and hosts quiz nights and karaoke nights throughout the week. The Radnorshire Arms has been awarded many accolades over the years, including being a finalist for the Campaign for Real Ale ‘National Pub of the Year’ several times. It is well known for its friendly atmosphere and exceptional service and is frequented by locals and tourists alike. The pub is also known for hosting a variety of charity events throughout the year in order to raise money for important causes. Overall, the Radnorshire Arms remains a popular and welcoming pub in the Powys region, bringing together locals and visitors alike in a friendly and entertaining atmosphere. For more information visit their website at radnorshire-arms.uk.

TA-SWISS (formerly the Swiss Trust Association) is a Swiss association that promotes the interests of trusts, foundations and other legal entities established in Switzerland. Founded in 1988, TA-SWISS is a non-profit organisation, supporting trustees and advisors in the planning, administration and protection of wealth. TA-SWISS is dedicated to providing the information and support services needed to help trustees and advisors cultivate the personal wealth and success of clients in cooperation with banks, cantons and other stakeholders. Since its founding, TA-SWISS has grown to become an industry leader in the trust and foundation sector. As of 2021, TA-SWISS members include over 250 financial institutions, trust companies, banks, law firms and other legal entities operating in Switzerland. The organisation is supported by prominent individuals, experts and professionals within the trust and foundation industry. The presence of actively engaged stakeholders has enabled a dynamic exchange of ideas and insights that ensure the continued success of TA-SWISS. Objectives of TA-SWISS The primary objective of TA-SWISS is to promote the interests of its members and to protect the economic and legal interests of their clients. It seeks to highlight operational risks and mitigate them through a wide range of best practices, regulations and training seminars. TA-SWISS also seeks to inform authorities and the public at large about the legitimate and responsible use of trustees, foundations and legal entities in Switzerland. TA-SWISS is a progressive organisation that promotes ongoing research and invests in software, infrastructure and innovation to ensure the highest level of support for its members. The services and activities of the Association TA-SWISS provides its members with an array of services in order to ensure the highest quality standards are maintained. These services include research, discussion groups, conferences, seminars and training courses. The implementation of best practices and proactive approach to continuous improvement is a top priority for the association. In addition, TA-SWISS works closely with the cantons and other relevant authorities on a range of issues such as taxation law and inheritance law. The Swiss Trust Association is also actively involved in lobbying activities, aiming to ensure that regulations regarding trustees, public authorities and other stakeholders remain in line with the goals and objectives of the association. As part of its outreach efforts, TA-SWISS participates in thought leadership initiatives, such as providing legal opinions, and producing reports and documents that are used in legal proceedings. Conclusion As a leading voice in the trust and foundation industry, TA-SWISS is recognised for its knowledge, capabilities and experience. Committed to innovation and the highest possible levels of service, TA-SWISS is an essential resource for all those involved in the sector. From its headquarters in Zurich and its branches in Geneva, Bern, Lucerne and Basel, TA-SWISS seeks to ensure that trust and foundation services remain of a high quality and benefit from the resources and expertise that TA-SWISS provides.

Steve Cunningham (born 1966), is an American computer scientist, notable for his contributions to database design, development, and security. He received his B.A. in Computer Science with honors from Johns Hopkins University in 1989, and his M.S. in Computer Science with honors from Austin College in 1991. He is a professor at Texas State University, teaching software engineering since 1998. Steve is a prolific author and conference presenter, and is also a frequent guest lecturer at other universities around the country. His research in database design and development includes topics such as database security, risk analysis, database management systems, software engineering, and data structure. His research has been published in journals such as Computer Science Education, International Journal of Database Management Systems, IEEE Computer Security Issues, and Database Engineering & Applications. In addition to his academic work, Steve is founding the Database Design & Security Institute. This institute provides consulting services on database design and security, offering courses and seminars designed to help database professionals develop secure, reliable, and efficient databases. The institute also conducts training in database management systems and software engineering. Steve is a frequent invited guest lecturer at many universities across the country, and has developed several popular database security courses. He has also co-authored books on Oracle database management and software engineering. He has consulted with numerous organizations, helping them improve their database design and security. In addition to his academic work, Steve is an active member of the International Association of Computer Scientists and is on the Board of the Database Security Association. He is also a member of several other professional organizations, including the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) and the National Education Association (NEA). Steve is an active participant in the local and national IT community, and has authored books, articles, and blog posts on topics related to software engineering and database security. He regularly attends events held by the Software Engineering Institute (SEI) and International Association of Software Architects (IASA). Steve Cunningham is well-known for his thoughtful, in-depth research on database design, development, and security, and has become the leading expert in this field. He is a dedicated mentor to his students, and is instrumental in encouraging university students to pursue educational opportunities in the field of computer science.

Silje is a female name of Scandinavian origin. The meaning of Silje is "calm and peaceful". The name is derived from a combination of the Old Norse elements for "light" and "peace". Silje is a popular name throughout the Nordic countries, including Norway, Sweden, and Denmark. It is especially popular in Norway, where it was the seventeenth most popular name for girls in 2016. The popularity of this name has been increasing in recent years, as it has been given to many prominent Norwegian cultural figures. Silje is a versatile name, as it can be spelled in both its Norse and anglicized forms. The former spelling is the traditional official form, while Silje is the anglicized version that is more commonly used. The name has traditionally been used as an independent given name, but it has also been used as a short form of longer names with the same root such as SiljeMaria or Siljestina. Silje has also been used to create nicknames. Silja and Sili are popular variations. People with the name Silje include: * Silje Nergaard, a Norwegian singer-songwriter * Silje Norendal, a Norwegian snowboarder * Silje Fjellanger, a Norwegian football defender * Silje Wergeland, a Norwegian fashion model * Silje Solberg, a Norwegian ice hockey player The Swedish DJ Alan Walker has a song titled "Silje's Song". Silje has also been used in literature. In Norwegian author Knut Hamsun's novel Growth of the Soil, the two female protagonists are named Silje and Helga. The elements of Silje's meaning make it a perfect name for a baby girl, since it implies a girl of serenity, light and peace. It is the perfect name for a baby who will grow up living a life surrounded by love and happiness.

Albert Dumouchel (March 15, 1952 - June 13, 2018) was a Canadian broadcasting journalist who was known for his wide array and knowledge in numerous areas of news, culture and current affairs. Early life Dumouchel was born in Montreal on March 15, 1952. He attended the University of Montreal, graduating with a Bachelor’s degree in philosophy and literature. He then went on to graduate with a Master’s in communication studies at the same university. Career After completing his studies, Dumouchel started his own independent radio station. He soon began working as a reporter and commentator on major radio networks such as CBC Radio, and held regular postships at Radio-Canada and TQS. Dumouchel was given regular guest spots on television, hosted AM/FM programs on CKAC, RDI, and Radio-Canada. He appeared often on the TV5 network and was part of the original team of reporters for Le Journal de Montréal. He spent close to twenty years hosting L’envolée culturelle for CBC Radio One Montreal and for Radio-Canada. Dumouchel was a regular contributor to La Presse’s rotation of opinion columnists. He also worked in press relations for the arts and culture sector and in 1999-2000, was responsible for the press relations for the Montreal International Jazz Festival. On June 13, 2018, Albert Dumouchel passed away at the age of 66 after a brief illness. Legacy Albert Dumouchel will be remembered for his significant work in the media and his vast contributions to news and culture throughout Canada. In tribute to him, Radio-Canada and CBC, as well as various cultural organizations, held a special broadcast in honour of his life and career. Dumouchel leaves behind a lasting legacy in the art, culture and media industries. He was widely respected for his knowledge and impartiality, always maintaining an ethical approach to journalism and current affairs. Throughout his career he strived to inspire others, working to make his nation proud. On his passing, Radio-Canada said "He has contributed to making Canada the beautiful country it is today."

Plants vs. Zombies is a tower defense and strategy video game developed and originally published by PopCap Games for Windows and Mac OS X systems in 2009. Players assume the role of a homeowner in the game, tasked with using a variety of different plants to repel hordes of zombies from "invading" their home. The idea is to help the homeowner build an arsenal of different plants and then utilize these plants to protect their house from the relentless zombie siege. The game is relatively simple in concept: the player is presented with a grid of squares, representing the homeowner's garden, upon which they can place various plants to thwart the zombie attacks. Each plant has its own special power, and the player must utilize the available plants in an attempt to fend off the zombie attacks. The player must also make strategic decisions in order to outsmart their opponents and survive the waves of zombies. The game also features other elements, which add a certain level of chaos and fun to the proceedings. The zombies themselves come in various shapes and sizes, and have their own special abilities, making them quite difficult to eliminate, as the player may need to use specific plants to take out certain enemies. There are also a few mini-games interspersed throughout the game as well, which can offer the player a breather from the main action in between waves. The graphics of the game are quite cartoonish and cheerful, helping to keep the game lighthearted and enjoyable. The sound effects are also of a high-quality and are particularly good at environmental atmospherics, such as the sound of birds chirping in the background. The music of the game is just as good, and fitting to the action taking place in each wave. There have been several versions of the game released since it first debuted in 2009, including a spin-off game, as well as mobile versions for iOS and Android devices. Plants vs. Zombies has been critically acclaimed since its launch, and is cited as one of the top tower defense games of all time. Thanks to its easy learning curve, engaging gameplay and polished presentation, Plants vs. Zombies is still highly regarded today, and is sure to delight gamers for many more years to come.

Djimrangar Dadnadji (1947 – 2011) was an African traditional chief, farmer, and politician. He was the Chief of Linya, a city in the Ouaddai region of Chad. Chief Dadnadji was born in 1947 in Linya, Chad. He was the son of Vizier Boulaba and Djina Aïchi, who were both farming families. He grew up in a farming village, learning the customs and traditions of his people. As a young man, he worked as a laborer on the farms of the region, and gained a local reputation for being a hard worker. When he was a young man, Chief Dadnadji became involved in local politics. He was eventually elected as the Chief of Linya in the 1960s, and served as the leader of the city for over 40 years. During his time as the chief, Dadnadji was a strong advocate for the rights of the people of Linya, advocating for improved infrastructure and education opportunities. He also sought to improve medical care and health services in the city. In 1998, Dadnadji was elected to the National Assembly of Chad, representing Linya as a representative of the Party for Liberty and Development. He served in the National Assembly until his death in 2011. Throughout his life, Dadnadji was a respected figure and leader in the Ouaddai region. He was known for his dedication to his people and his strong belief in the importance of traditional African values. He was also respected for his leadership ability and his role in the development of the Ouaddai region. Despite his health issues, Dadnadji remained active in politics and traditional life until his death in 2011. He was given a ceremonial funeral in Linya and was buried in his family's ancestral lands. In his memory, the city of Linya has erected a plaque honoring Dadnadji's legacy. Today, Dadnadji's legacy lives on and is remembered by the people of Linya and Ouaddai as a man who devoted his life and efforts to the betterment of his people. He is remembered and respected by many, both in Chad and around the world.

Archelaus was the 4th Century Bishop of Carrhae, a town on the Euphrates River in northern Mesopotamia. He served from 355AD until his death in 373AD. Archelaus is best known for his work on the compilation of the Syrian Canons, or Rules of Church Discipline. His Early Life Little is known about Archelaus' life outside of his involvement in the church. It is believed to have been born in the city of Hierapolis. This is inferred from his writings in which he refers to it as his native town. He received his education from Eustathius of Antioch and became known as "Theophilus of Hierapolis" Writings Archelaus is best known for his work on the compilation of the Syriac Canons. This was a collection of ecclesiastical canons and rules of matrimony, public penance, and absolution. He was using the works of other Fathers and Schismatic authors, which he found in the Patriarchal Library of Antioch. He invoked the help of God and priestly spirit in the compilation. Due to his work on the Canons, Archelaus became recognized throughout the Eastern church as a respected scholar. He was among those consulted during the Synod of Antioch in 363AD regarding the charity famine in Egypt and was also a signatory of three Creeds regarding the Homoousian faith in 367AD. Legacy After Archelaus' death, his works on Syriac Canons would become highly influential in the Eastern liturgies. The 17th Century English clergyman, Richard Jonas, has written a biography on Archelaus, in which he calls him "The Great Bishop of Carrhae". Archelaus' work on the Syriac Canons is still used to teach about the Eastern Christian faith. His writings show the lasting impression he had on the church and how much the Eastern church valued his contributions. A church in modern-day Syria is also named after Archelaus, "Church of Saint Archelaus" which is located in the district of Daraya.

The Real Quiet Storm was a musical phenomenon in the mid to late-1970s, primarily in the United States and later in the UK and other parts of the world. It was characterized by a slow, melodic style of R&B music that blended elements of soul, jazz, and sometimes even funk. The title of the music was derived from an album of the same name released in 1976 by Smokey Robinson. Robinson's album was influenced by what he called "the sound of the storm", which was a melding of his background in Motown soul music with the newer sounds of jazz. These elements created a calming, peaceful sound that Robinson felt was perfect for those mild, seductive summer nights. Shortly after the release of Robinson's album, other artists started to incorporate this sound into their own styles, creating the Quiet Storm-style of music. Perhaps the most successful Quiet Storm artist was Luther Vandross. Vandross established himself as one of the greatest interpreters of Quiet Storm music with his solo works, as well as his collaborations with other artists. His albums "Busy Body" (1983) and "Give Me the Reason" (1986) are acknowledged as masterpieces of the genre. Other prominent Quiet Storm artists include guitarist George Benson, singers such as Luther Ingram, Anita Baker and Freddie Jackson, and groups like the Isley Brothers. Quiet Storm songs generally share certain attributes. They have soulful, mellow, and often romantic lyrics, with subtle melodies and meaningful grooves. Most Quiet Storm songs are between five and seven minutes long, allowing for instrumental solos and extended vocal ad-libs. Today, Quiet Storm music continues to be played on adult contemporary and soft rock radio stations across the world. It remains popular as background music at intimate gatherings, such as dinner parties, as well as at romantic events. Established soul and R&B artists such as Mary J Blige and Jill Scott carry on the legacy of the Quiet Storm, while younger stars such as Maxwell and John Legend keep the music alive for a new generation.

A neuroscience database is a type of online repository used to store and share a variety of neuroscientific data. They are used by neuroscientists, clinical researchers, and other scientists around the world to facilitate the exchange and sharing of data. These databases are often maintained and funded by professional organizations, universities, and research groups. The list of neuroscience databases below includes both public and commercial databases. While some are open to all, others are available to members only. 1. NeuroLex (www.neurolex.org): This is a collaborative, open-access semantic network of neuroscience information. It is developed by Neuroscience Information Framework (NIF), a project of the NIH Blueprint for Neuroscience Research. 2. NeuroMorpho.Org (www.neuromorpho.org): This is a publicly available, semantically enabled 3D archive of neuron types, provided by the OpenWorm project and supported by the National Science Foundation. It includes detailed morphologies of neurons from many different species. 3. InSiGHT (www.insight-genome.org): An open-access, web-based database of genetic variation linked to neurological diseases. 4. PubBrain (www.pubbrain.org): A public search engine for neuroscience publications. It integrates the power of PubMed with advanced search algorithms and visualizations. 5. BrainOnline (www.brainonline.org): A scientific web-portal that provides access to a variety of brain databases and tools. 6. NeuroScholar (www.neuroscholar.org): An online repository of research papers in the field of neuroscience. 7. BrainMap (www.brainmap.org):An online atlas of the brain with high-resolution data from many imaging modalities. 8. Harvard Brain Tissue Resource Center (www.brainbank.harvard.edu): A repository of postmortem brain tissue specimens, primarily from individuals with psychiatric and neurological disorders. 9. HDB (Human Derived Brainbank) (www.hdb.org): A searchable collection of postmortem human brain tissues, sourced from individuals with neurological and psychiatric disorders. 10. Connectome (www.humanconnectomeproject.org): This is an open access digital repository of data from the Human Connectome Project (HCP). It includes information on the structure and function of the human brain, including high-resolution brain images, genetics, behavior and cognition. Neuroscience databases are essential resources for researchers and scientists, providing access to data, tools and knowledge to facilitate their work. However, because these databases are regularly updated and expanded, proper care should be taken when accessing them.

Roman Mints were an important part of the Roman economy for centuries. The mints served as a means of producing coins and other forms of currency in order to facilitate trade and commerce. Mints throughout the Roman Empire were organized in a variety of ways, with some located in major cities and others in influential locations such as Rome, Constantinople, Alexandria, and Antioch. The coins produced were made of bronze, silver, and gold, with some coins having a value spelled out in Greek or Latin. These coins acted as a medium of exchange for goods and services and were essential to the Roman economy. Mints were also used to produce metal pieces called medallions, which were used as rewards for Roman military commanders and allies for their services The diversity and complexity of coins created by the Roman mints speaks to the importance of commerce in Roman society. Coins bore images of rulers, gods, animals, buildings, and other symbols. Other coins, such as the sestertius, featured complex images and elaborate designs. Much of the Roman economy was based on bartering goods and services, but the Roman mints served as a means of moving money from one place to another and facilitated trade at a level not seen in earlier civilizations. The Roman mints were not controlled by the government, but rather operated by private citizens. The cost of producing the coins was high, but this cost was offset by charging a fee for each coin minted. This fee was called a fee per die and was imposed by the workshop producing coins. The mints also charged customers a fee for exchanging coins of different values. In the early days of the Roman Empire, coins were hand-struck. This process was replaced by machine-striking in the 7th century, allowing mints to dramatically increase the production of coins. This increased production enabled the mints to keep up with the demands of trade, ensuring a smoothly functioning economy. The mints in the Roman Empire eventually lost their importance and decline in the 8th century due to the lack of infrastructure and the rise of taxation. By the end of the 9th century, the minting of coins had ceased and mints had all but disappeared. Despite this, the legacy of the Roman mints remains, as their influence can still be seen in the coins used today.

Bristol City (1919) is a professional football club, based in Bristol, England. Founded in 1919, they are currently the oldest football club in the city. The club currently play in the Football League One, the third tier in English football, and are the most successful in the west region of England. Bristol City Sports and Football Club was formed in 1894 as a merger between Bristol South End and St. George's. Despite being a professional team from its founding, Bristol City went through several renamings and mergers, including with Bedminster (1900) and Eastville Rovers (1907). Finally, in July 1919, the four clubs were amalgamated and named Bristol City Football Club. The first Manager of the new Bristol City was Fred Sweet, the first chairmen was J.T. Pickup and a new ground was found and built at White City Stadium, near St George’s. The first-team won their first match in the Combination Competition against Stroud on the 13th of September 1919. The club reached Division One of the English Football League for the first time in 1976, and played in the top division for four seasons between 1979 and 1983; the 1981 season was the most successful, with Dave Sexton's team finishing tenth in the top division. They reached the 1983 FA Cup Final, losing to Manchester United in a replay. Bristol City spent most of the 1990s in Division Two, and were promoted in 2000 to Division One. While there, the club built Ashton Gate Stadium to replace their traditional ground, Twerton Park. This was opened in May 2004, and the team then reached the Football League Championship. Bristol City have a long-standing reputation for the development of young players, many of whom have gone on to become professional footballers. Successful youth team graduates include trophies specialist goalkeeper Dean Sunman, former Manchester United midfielder Stephen Hughes and England's Lee Johnson. Notable greats of the club include modern-era stars such as Lee Tomlin, Bobby Reid, Aden Flint, Luke Freeman, Joe Bryan and Hugo Hebblethwaite. Former players like John Atyeo, Joe Mercer, John Dawkins and Peter Aitken remain legends at Ashton Gate Stadium. In 2019, Bristol City finished in 8th place in the League One, thus qualifying for the play offs, in which they earned promotion to the Championship. References: 1. Henry Kessler (born October 10, 1969) was a Major League Baseball first baseman who played for the Houston Astros during the 1991 season. Kessler was born in Kearney, Nebraska, and attended the University of Nebraska, where he was a member of the Nebraska Cornhuskers baseball team from 1989 to 1991. He played on the 1989 College World Series runner-up team, and was a three-time Big Eight all-conference selection as a first baseman. In 1991, Kessler was drafted by the Houston Astros in the 1st round (20th overall) of the MLB Draft. He debuted for the Astros during the 1991 season and played in 14 games for the team, hitting .250 with two home runs and seven RBIs. Kessler's MLB career would end after the 1991 season, as he was unable to make the Astros' roster in subsequent years. He had brief stints with the minor league teams of the Minnesota Twins, Detroit Tigers and Anaheim Angels through 1994, but did not manage to return to the major leagues. In 1995, Kessler returned to the University of Nebraska as an assistant coach with the Cornhuskers baseball team, and after one season returned to the minor leagues. He finished his career with the Las Vegas Stars in 1998, with whom he had his best statistical season in the minors, hitting .341 with nine home runs and 84 RBIs. Kessler's post-baseball career revolved around his involvement with local charities, such as the Omaha Police Department’s "Shop With A Cop" program and in 2013 he was the recipient of the NCAA Inspiration Award for his work with the children of Kearney. After his retirement from baseball, Kessler stayed relatively out of the public eye, and died on November 21, 2018 in Omaha, Nebraska at the age of 49. Kessler's baseball career may have been short, but he is still fondly remembered by fans from Kearney and Omaha, as well as by former teammates and coaches. He served as an example of how dedication, effort, and hard work can lead to success, regardless of circumstances.

Frogs in culture are revered in many societies around the world for their symbolism. In the two major religions of the world, Christianity and Islam, frogs are said to be clever creatures, but in their own way, also bringers of bad luck. Nonetheless, frogs are very popular in many cultures and symbols of growth, fertility, transformation, fertility, and good luck. These cultural beliefs are often found in religious myths, paintings, literature, and even in everyday products. Frogs are an integral part of Native American culture, with many tribes honoring frogs as a sign of rain, fertility and renewal. They believed that frogs brought about the clouds, and this was seen as a gift from the Great Spirit. Frogs were thought to bring forth abundance, success, and even peace. In many Asian countries, frogs portray luck, fertility, and wealth. The Chinese believed that frog charms and grimy frogs in the grounds, brought riches and prosperity during droughts. In Japan, the frogs are believed to have healing powers. Besides, Japaneses folklore tells that a frog can turn into a human and the older the frog is, the more chance it will have to turn into a human. Frogs have been featured in popular culture. Some examples include, Pixar's popular movie "Finding Nemo", and the frog prince character in "The Princess and the Frog". There is also the Frog Prince who became a classic character throughout European fairy tales. This popular frog character featured the idea of transformation, and by the end of the story become a human prince in many versions of the tale. In popular culture, frogs appear in children's stories and cartoons. In the popular cartoon series "The Muppets", Kermit the Frog is a much-loved character. His message in the show is that it is better to be different and to be true to yourself. He is also a symbol of courage, dependability, talent, curiosity, and loyalty. In conclusion, frogs in culture are seen as symbols of growth, transformation, fertility, and good luck. Throughout history, the frog has been a part of culture in various forms, and continues to remain popular in children's stories, movies, and cartoons today. Regardless of the frog's mixed symbolism, this amphibian has become an important part of culture for many societies.

The Ural Republic (Uralskaya Respublika) was a short-lived semi-autonomous socialist state that was declared in the Russian SFSR (now the Russian Federation) during the Russian Revolution of 1905. It existed for just over eight months, from December 5th, 1905 to August 14th 1906, when it was overshadowed and dissolved by the newly formed Russian Provisional Government. The idea of a socialist republic in the Ural region originated with liberal members of the Union of Liberation, who sought a decentralized government as an alternative to the imperial rule of the Russian Tsar. The Union of Liberation was a liberal political party that advocated for civil liberties and stronger political representation in Russia. In the beginning of December 1905, the Union held its first congress in the Russian SFSR. There were two key points of the congress: the congress declared the formation of a socialist republic and the adoption of a constitution. On December 5th, 1905, the Ural Republic was officially declared and the socialist government embarked on a program of reform. Due to the common liberal orientation of the organization, many policies and initiatives in the Ural Republic were liberal in nature, including the introduction of a new progressive land code, and the implementing of an eight hour work day for workers. Other reforms included having elected provincial assemblies, and granting voting rights to all adults regardless of nationality, ethnicity, or gender. However, the implementation of these reforms was limited due to the lack of resources in the region. Despite the republic's bold goals, it did not survive long. The Ural Republic was a victim of its own internal divisions, caused mostly by conflicting political ideologies between its members. Furthermore, the newly formed Russian Provisional Government had little to no regard for the new republic and refused to recognize it. As a result, the Ural Republic was completely overshadowed and eventually dissolved. Despite the short life of the Ural Republic, its legacy lives on, as the ideals it championed laid the foundations for future Russian social, civil, and political reforms. It also served as an example to other Russian revolutionaries of the potential of a decentralized, socialist-oriented government. The Ural Republic, which was the first of its kind in Russia, can rightfully be considered one of the country's most significant contributions to the Russian Revolution.

Packet switching is a data communication method which breaks information into packets that are then sent over a channel shared by multiple types of communication. This allows multiple messages to be sent at the same time over shared communication lines while limiting the amount of interference each message experiences. Packets, also known as datagrams, are typically identified by their source and/or destination addresses, along with format and control information. Packet switching can support multiple communication protocols, including Ethernet, asynchronous transfer mode, token ring, and X.25. Packet switching was first developed in the 1960s, but was improved throughout the 1970s and 1980s. During this time, the technology moved from mainframe computing to distributed systems and was widely used in digital networks. Packet switching is often combined with other technologies such as frame relay, X.25, and asynchronous transfer mode (ATM). Today, packet switching is still commonly used, particularly in the internet. Packet switching is advantageous over traditional circuit switching in several ways. It makes much more efficient use of bandwidth and resources, as the data being sent is broken into smaller chunks and only the necessary portion of a link will be used to send the data. Packet switching also allows for dynamic traffic routing, as packets can be sent through different channels to their intended destinations. This mode of communication can also support error detection and correction by re-sending packets if errors are detected. There are also potential drawbacks to packet switching. As multiple communication paths can be used for transmission, the amount of time for a message to reach its destination can vary. Additionally, collisions can occur, when the same link is used to transmit two or more packets at the same time. Finally, as packets are routed independently of each other, there is potential for packets to get out of order. Overall, packet switching is an effective method of communication for digital networks, and is widely used in the internet. By breaking data into smaller portions, packet switching allows for efficient communication which can support multiple protocols and dynamic traffic routing. While there are potential drawbacks, packet switching is still an important component of modern digital networks. Andres Valdez is a Filipino-born American soccer player who recently signed to the Major League Soccer club, Orlando City SC. Valdez was born in Davao, Philippines on January 8, 1991 and moved to Tampa, Florida when he was 14 years old in pursuit of his dream of becoming a professional soccer player. He attended Hillsborough High School, where he was twice named All-Conference honorable mention and became the school's all-time leading scorer. In 2009, he was awarded All-Tampa and All-State selections. During his college years, Valdez attended Polk State College and Hillsborough Community College, where he was the conference player of the year in 2015. He was also named to the NJCAA Southeast All-Region First Team and NCCAA National Player of the Year. After a breakout year, Valdez was recruited by top NCAA Div. 1 programs and ultimately signed with UNC Charlotte. In his three seasons with UNC Charlotte, Valdez started every match, scored 19 goals and had 7 assists for a total of 45 points. Valdez signed his first professional contract with USL Championship, Swope Park Rangers in 2018, where he made 19 appearances. He joined San Antonio FC in 2019, where he scored two goals and had two assists in 15 games. This past January, Valdez signed to Major League Soccer Orlando City SC, where his brother, Josue, also plays. He is the first Filipino-American to sign with the MLS club. Since then, he has made two appearances and scored one goal against Inter Miami CF. Away from the pitch, Valdez is involved with his community in Tampa and Charlotte. He has given back by helping out at soccer clinics and partnering with various organizations that are dedicated to helping underprivileged kids. Valdez continues to make history as a Filipino-American soccer player and hopes to inspire a whole new generation of young athletes with similar backgrounds.

55 Cancri is a binary star system located in the constellation of Cancer, and is composed of two stellar components. The primary component is a yellow-orange G-type star around twice as massive and eight times as luminous as the Sun, while the companion is an orange K-type star of approximately 65% the Sun’s mass and around 13% of the luminosity. The two stars are separated by about 8 arc seconds, making 55 Cancri one of the biggest stellar systems in the night sky. The primary star, 55 Cancri A, is the brighter and more prominent star of the pair and has been classified as a S1.5 (subgiant or supergiant) star located 36.6 light years away from the Solar System, with an approximate magnitude of 6.0. It has been studied extensively and the analysis of its photosphere hints that the star may have twice the solar abundance of elements that are heavier than helium, like oxygen and carbon. The companion star, 55 Cancri B, is a type K1 (main sequence star), a bit cooler and dimmer than the primary. It orbits around the primary star at a distance of about 79 astronomical units (AU). Due to its distance from the primary star, the companion has only been observed at near-infrared wavelengths and its exact spectral type remains uncertain. The two stars are separated by a distance of about 142 AU. 55 Cancri is one of the first binary stars to be studied in depth and was used as a model to try to better understand the behavior of stars in binary systems. Observations of the primary indicate that it may have a planet orbiting around it, and this has been confirmed by several follow-up studies. This extrasolar planet, known as 55 Cancri b, was discovered in 2007, destabilizing the star’s orbital plane and perturbing its orbit. The star is visible to the naked eye, located in the eastern horizon near the border between Gemini and Cancer in the night sky. 55 Cancri is part of the YY Geminorum star group, which also includes Zeta Geminorum, Kappa Geminorum, Eta Geminorum, Delta Geminorum, and Gamma Geminorum. 55 Cancri is an important star for astronomers as it not only provides an opportunity for scientists to gain insight into the behavior of binary stars, but also to study the effects of extra-solar planets. It is an ideal target for future studies and offers great potential for further exploration.

The White Angel (2007) is a drama film directed by Marco Risi, starring Luca Argentero, Claudio Santamaria, Emanuela Folliero, Caterina Sylos Labini, and William Di Giulio. Produced by Vito Ciccarelli, Andrea Zaccariello and Maurizio Tedesco, the film won the Gauden Trophy for Best Cultural Data Film at the Shanghai International Film Festival in 2008. Set in a small village in Northern Italy, the film follows 15-year-old Ettore (Argentero) who, following his older brother's death, is sent to live with his uncle Ruggero (Santamaria) with the responsibility of running the family's automobile workshop. Struggling with his new identity as the eldest son, Ettore soon discovers he is not alone in his feelings of having lost his parents and brother. Francesca (Folliero), a mysterious woman who moves into the village and begins working at the family's shop, captures Ettore's attention and is the source of much gossip within the tight-knit town. When Ettore learns from Ruggero that Francesca is his father's illegitimate daughter, Ettore's opinion of her and her lifestyle drastically changes. As Francesca soon reveals she needs money to back her ambition of becoming an athlete, Ettore's attraction towards her is rekindled and he commits to helping her achieve her dream and providing her with the funds necessary. Through their relationship, Ettore and Francesca are able to find hope and happiness in their personal challenges and the shared smiles they exchange. The captivating performances by the cast, especially Argentero and Folliero, successfully bring a frequently-told story to life. The White Angel conveys its themes of loss and redemption with a passion that leaves viewers with a lingering feeling of hope and renewal.

April Fools' Day is a 1954 comedy directed by Don Taylor and released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. It stars Noel Neill, Dick Foran, Katie Johnson, Lyle Talbot, and Emmett Vogan. The film follows four teenagers living in an island village in the Pacific Northwest called Easterly who come up with a prank that results in a series of comical mishaps when a stranger visits their village on April Fools' Day. The film marked the feature film directing debut of Don Taylor and was the last film that Taylor would direct. The film's script was penned by Taylor himself with assistance from George Bradshaw and Kay Lenard, who had previously written episodes for television. The film met with mixed reviews upon its release. Writing in Variety, one critic praised the film as a "light-hearted romp" but also pointed out that it was "pleasant but nothing special". Another writer for the New York Times bemoaned the film's lack of substance and called it "frivolous" and "slightly silly". The movie was a modest commercial success, earning over $2 million domestically against a budget of only $325,000. It also earned director Don Taylor an Academy Award nomination for Best Story. The film is now considered a minor classic of 1950s comedic filmmaking and is particularly noted for showcasing the talents of the young actors who starred in it. It has seen renewed interest in recent years due to its availability on DVD and other platforms. In April 2005, the film was re-released by Turner Classic Movies (TCM) as part of their "TCM Archives" collection. The film was accompanied by an introduction by TCM's host Robert Osborne which provided context for the film's place in film history as well as a discussion of Taylor's directorial debut. April Fools' Day was released in the US on April 1st 1954 and has since gained a cult following among fans of 1950s comedies. It is a beloved example of the unique comedic sensibilities of the era, and still delights viewers today with its gentle humor and lighthearted antics.

Dietrich Georg von Kieser (1785-1864) was a Swedish-Baltic German military officer and statesman who served as Governor-General of the Grand Duchy of Finland from 1831 to 1855. Kieser was born in Riga, in present-day Latvia, in 1785. He was the son of Baron Johann Georg von Kieser and the Baroness Wilhelmine Justina von Kothen. He was educated at the University of Tartu, where he studied physics and mathematics. Kieser joined the Imperial Russian Army in 1803, and served in the Napoleonic campaigns of 1805 and 1812, receiving several decorations and promotions along the way. By 1831 he had been promoted to the rank of Major-General and was appointed as Governor-General of Finland, a position he held until 1855. During his tenure as Governor-General, Kieser oversaw the development of the country’s education system and civil service, and promoted the expansion of the rail network. He also built numerous roads, bridges, and public works, and ensured that the new Grand Ducal Constitution of 1844 granted the people of Finland some autonomy over their internal affairs. Kieser's main legacy, however, was his work in ensuring the autonomy of the Estates of Finland, which he categorically declared as a separate State within the Grand Duchy in 1847. This Declaration of Autonomy enabled the Estates to have their own separate governing institutions, law courts and economic lifelines, independent from the authority of the Grand Duke. Kieser was widely revered in Finland for his services to the country. In 1854, he was awarded the Cross of the Knight of St. Vladimir for his services. He died in Riga in 1864, and was later buried with an honorary guard of the Finnish Vyborg Infantry Regiment in St. Petersburg, in honour of his services to the country. Today, Kieser is remembered in Finland for his role in securing the country's autonomy and in developing the country's infrastructure and civil services. He is commemorated in the Kieser Memorial, a monument located in Kaarlela in Vyborg, erected in his honour. The Dietrich Georg von Kieser Award is also granted annually by the National Union of Finnish Students since 1972 to honour a prominent Finnish statesman or public figure.

Epiphany is the debut studio album by American R&B singer-songwriter Chrisette Michele. It was released on June 26, 2007, by her then-current label, Def Jam Recordings. The album debuted at number one on the US Billboard 200 chart, becoming Michele's first number-one album and selling 83,000 copies in its first week. The album was met with generally positive reviews from music critics. Erika Ramirez from Billboard praised Michele's "strong, soulful voice" and noted that the album "shines with a classic sound reminiscent of classic soul and gospel". AllMusic's Andy Kellman thought that Michele, who wrote and co-wrote most of the songs on the album, effectively bridged contemporary trends with classic sounds. He noted, "With the steady pulse of rap-inflected soul, silky midtempo funk, and dusty-sounding lite-funk and balladry, the sounds are distinctive, not retreaded." The album spawned five singles: "Be OK", "If I Have My Way", "Love Is You", "Best of Me" and the title track, "Epiphany (I'm Leaving)". "Be OK" was the most successful single from the album, charting in the top 40 on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart, and becoming Michele's highest charting single on that chart. The single was also certified Gold by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). The album was certified Gold by the RIAA on March 18, 2008, and has sold 866,000 copies in the United States. In 2009, Michele decided to leave Def Jam and release her next projects independently. Following this decision, Michele released her second studio album, entitled Epiphany: The Gratitude Edition - the album was a re-issue of her debut album with five bonus tracks of her own added on - as a double disc, with the original and bonus pieces on different discs. On October 30, 2009, the album debuted at number three on the Billboard 200 chart, selling an estimate 81,000 copies in its first week. It currently stands as Michele's highest-peaking album on the chart. To date, Epiphany has sold 1,554,000 copies in the United States.

Knowsley Safari Park is a nature conservation park located in Knowsley, Merseyside, England. The park is home to over 700 wild animals from all over the world, including lions, tigers, baboons, giraffes, rhinos, and wolves. The park is open all year round for visitors to view and observe the different species of wildlife. The park was first opened in 1971 and was one of the first of its kind in Europe. Knowsley Safari Park was originally owned by the Stanley family, and was started as an extension of the Earl of Derby’s estate near Liverpool. The park has since been taken over by the Knowsley Safari Park Limited, a privately owned business. The park offers a drive-through safari experience, an off-road safari experience, a sea lion show, and an area with petting animals. Visitors can also rent Safari buses to explore the park more easily. The park also features a variety of educational activities. Naturalists are available throughout the park to answer questions and provide visitors with information about the animals. Knowsley Safari Park also offers a range of shows for visitors to enjoy. These include daily displays of sea lions, birds, and beavers, as well as entertaining displays of exotic animals such as lemurs, meerkats, and monkeys. The park also participates in animal conservation programs and supports local charities. The park is constantly expanding and improving its facilities, and has been named one of the UK’s leading tourism destinations. It was awarded Grade 4 status by the Discover England Quality Assurance Group for 2018, and was featured in the Times Top 100 Best Places to Visit in Britain list. Knowsley Safari Park is one of the UK’s premier wildlife attractions and is able to provide visitors with an unforgettable experience. Whether it’s an adventure with the wild animals or taking a closer look at the educational activities, there is something for everyone at Knowsley Safari Park.

New Indian Model School (NIMS) is a private primary and secondary co-educational school located in Delhi, India. Founded in 1996, NIMS offers a comprehensive education for students from preschool to secondary school. It is an English medium school and is affiliated to the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) in India. NIMS has a strong commitment to creating an environment of holistic learning, where each student is valued and their talents and interests nurtured. The school provides an atmosphere of high academic rigour within a supportive learning environment. It is committed to providing quality education to all its students and enhancing the development of respect and pride in their culture, roots, language and heritage. The school provides various sports, artistic, and intellectual activities to actively engage students in their own learning. NIMS focuses on providing a sound approach to learning and encourages a spirit of adventure, independent inquiry and exploration in its students. It has well-equipped laboratories for Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Math and Computer Science. The school also has a library with a wide selection of books designed to encourage both knowledge and skills development. The school is divided into primary and secondary sections, with classes from Play Group through the Secondary level. The school has three separate sections for students in the pre-primary level, preparatory level, and middle school level. In addition, students also have the opportunity of choosing from a wide range of experiences and extra-curricular activities such as drama, music, arts and dance, sports, and public speaking. NIMS follows a graded system to help the students learn in a comfortable and relaxed setting. A wide range of teachers are available at the primary and secondary level to guide and mentor the students. NIMS puts in a great deal of effort to create a stimulating, motivating and encouraging environment that enables students to realize their aspirations and academic potential. The teachers use innovative teaching methods and regularly work to build a strong partnership with parents to ensure the best education and guidance for their children. NIMS prides itself on developing a good all-round education, preparing students for the challenges they will encounter in higher education and life. It strives to maintain the highest standards of quality education and works very hard to bring out the king in all its students. The school is well-known for its academic excellence, sports, arts and culture. NIMS regularly organizes seminars, workshops and excursions for students, which provides students with the opportunity to explore their overall development.

Dan Vasser is a fictional character from the Fox network television series Journeyman. Dan is a journalist from San Francisco and the protagonist of the series. He is portrayed by Kevin McKidd. Dan discovers he is a "Time Jumper," a human who, every few days, is inexplicably transferred short distances, or further, in time, both backward and forward. Although travelling through time holds no true physical dangers, Dan is informed via newspaper articles at various points in time that he will eventually die in a major disaster, making his journey to prevent the tragedy a primary plotline throughout the series. Dan's primary motivation to explore his time-jumping ability is to re-connect with his former beloved, Livia Beale (Alexa Davalos), whom he inexplicably lost contact with after he proposed to her eight years prior. Dan soon discovers that he is mysteriously travelling through time to save the lives of other people. He soon meets his mentor, Morgan, who informs him that he must help the people in some way in order for him to be able to move on in his life. At times, Dan confronts ethical dilemmas when the person he is rescuing will most likely alter the lives of others, but then again, there are times when not helping the person would lead to greater calamity. Throughout the show, Dan discovers that he can also have an influence in the lives of other people as Dan chooses to be both a father figure and confidante through his time-travelling experiences. Dan's brother Jack (Reed Diamond) and friend Katie (Moon Bloodgood) both come to understand Dan's time-traveling secrets. In the 21st episode, it is discovered that the person guiding Dan is his former love Livia, who also acts as a search engine for the information he needs in order to complete his tasks. Ultimately however, Dan's ultimate goal comes true as Livia and him actually be together, as two changes of time have Livia becoming his wife and the mother of his daughter Zoe. Sadly, the series was never allowed to explain completely through the remaining 13 episodes, as Fox chose to cancel the show after just one season. Nevertheless, Dan Vasser will always remain an iconic persona in the science fiction genre, not just because of his travels through time, but because of his brave attempt to alter various points of time and his inspiring wish to be reunited with the love of his life.

Kalki Jayanti is an annual Hindu religious festival, celebrated to commemorate the birth of Kalki, the tenth and final incarnation of Vishnu, who is believed to have arrived in the form of a horse to bring an end to the current Kali Yuga and initiate a new period of peace, austerity, prosperity and Dharma (righteousness). The festival is celebrated mainly in India and Nepal, particularly by Vaishnavites. The exact date of Kalki Jayanti is celebrated annually according to the Hindu lunar calendar. Generally, the festival is celebrated on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight (Shukla Paksha) in the Hindu month of Jyeshtha (May – June). Kalki Jayanti is generally celebrated with great devotion and dedication throughout India and Nepal. On this day, religious functions and puja rituals are carried out in temples and homes, mostly dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Temples are ornamented with fresh flower garlands and lamps are lit in the evening. Special verses dedicated to Kalki are sung.
