Devotees also observe fast (Upvaas) on this day and take a holy bath in the Ganges River, rivers or lakes. Offerings of flowers and fruits are made to Lord Vishnu before and after chanting mantras and prayers. Prasad (blessed sweets) are served to all who assemble at temples. The celebration of Kalki Jayanti is unique and special with each region having its own way of observing it. In Southern India, especially in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu, large processions are organized to celebrate Kalki Jayanti. Special musical performances are arranged in temples of Lord Vishnu and streets, with devotees dressed in traditional colourful attire. In Northern India, mainly in the states of Rajasthan and Haryana, Kalki Jayanti is celebrated with much pomp and grandeur. Devotees take a holy dip in the holy Yamuna River in Mathura and worship Lord Vishnu for success and prosperity. Kalki Jayanti is a festival that inspires people to live a spiritual and peaceful life according to the ideals of Dharma or righteousness. It marks the victory of Good over Evil and signifies hope and faith in Dharma.

Jean Baptiste Bissot, Sieur de Vincennes (1668–1719) was a French explorer and fur trader who played an important role in opening up the interior of the North American continent to the French and British. Born in Vincennes, France (now part of Paris), Bissot was orphaned at a young age, and taken under the care of his relatives, the Bissot de Vincennes. At the age of seventeen, Bissot enlisted in the French army and took part in the Siege of Lille in 1667. Afterwards, he followed his brothers out to North America to join in the fur trade. He quickly became known throughout the French colonies as an experienced woodsman, able to traverse densely wooded terrain with ease. Bissot’s exploratory work cemented France’s control of the Great Lakes region and much of the upper Mississippi River. In particular, he is credited with improving France’s relationship with Native Americans in the region, and played an important diplomatic role in maintaining peace between the French and Huron tribes. He is also credited with establishing the trading post at Fort Dearborn in present day Chicago. Bissot was a major figure in the Battle of Lake Te-kah-hoken in 1712. In this battle, he led a French-allied Huron force against a British-Iroquois alliance, and is credited with stopping the advance of the British forces and preventing them from gaining a foothold in the region. Bissot was instrumental in the development of the French inland fur trade. He was able to negotiate trade agreements that brought the furs and other goods of the interior American north to the French at much lower prices than they had been paying. Bissot’s most important accomplishment was his role in the founding of Vincennes, Indiana. After the French defeat at the Battle of the Plains of Abraham in 1758, Vincennes' location on the Wabash River was selected by the French as the site for a new strategic post. Along with Father Pierre Gibault, Bissot led the survey of the site and played a large role in constructing the post, which would eventually form the basis of the modern city of Vincennes. Jean Baptiste Bissot, Sieur de Vincennes was a major figure in the opening of North America to the Europeans and to subsequent American development. His exploration and trading talents, along with his diplomatic skills, played an important role in forging relationships between the French and Native American tribes. With his role in the founding of Vincennes, Indiana, Bissot’s legacy lives on today in the form of a vibrant, multi-cultural city.

David Skrela (born 3 March 1979) is a French rugby union player and former coach. He played as fly-half. Early life Skrela was born in Paris, France and began playing rugby in his hometown at the age of 10. He was a member of the French national team that won the Under-21 tournament in the Five Nations Championship in 1999. Rugby career Skrela made his professional rugby debut in 2000, playing for home club Stade Français. He went on to be the most successful fly-half of the Stade Français team, playing 65 times and scoring 395 points. In 2009, he moved to rugby powerhouses Toulouse, where he continued to perform at the highest level. During his third season in Toulouse, he became the top scorer for the Top 14 with 273 points. Skrela joined English Premiership side London Wasps for the 2011/12 season, but due to a knee injury he was forced to cut his season short. International career Skrela made his international debut for France in 2003 against Ireland, and went on to make another 15 appearances for his country over the next six years. He was part of the successful French side that won consecutive Six Nations Grand Slams in 2004 and 2007. Skrela was the starting fly-half in the 2007 Rugby World Cup Final, which France lost to South Africa 15-9. He was one of 11 players in the squad with over 100 international caps. Coaching career In 2015, Skrela retired from playing rugby and moved into coaching. He was appointed as the head coach of French Pro D2 club Massy in September 2015. He stayed in the role until 2017, leading the club to the Pro D2 semifinals. Skrela then shifted back to club rugby, coaching Pro D2 side Vannes in 2019. Under his stewardship, the side finished seventh in the table and just missed out on the promotion play-offs. Since the start of the 2020/21 season, he has been the assistant coach for Toulon in the Top 14. Personal life Skrela has two daughters and is married to his wife Anne. He is an alumnus of the Paris Institute of Political Studies. He enjoys playing golf and travelling in his spare time.

Vitsika is an ancient Greek goddess associated with mirth, festivity, joy, and merriment. She was said to be the daughter of Dionysus, god of wine and revelry, and the nominal equivalent of the Roman goddess Reverentia. She is associated with dancing and singing, activities which often do not require the use of language, suggesting that Vitsika may have originated as a pre-Hellenic deity. Her name derives from the Greek verb Βίαω (Bioó), which means “to snap or crack open." Thus, her name has been linked to the cracking of a whip. This possibly signifies an energizing and invigorating influence, and perhaps the joy of loud music and dancing. In literature, Vitsika is usually depicted in the company of other gods and goddesses, as at the wedding of Peleus and Thetis, where the gods and goddess attended, with Vitsika presiding over the festivities. At the marriage celebration, the laughter of the deities echoed across the sky. She is also often depicted joining the Muses in their revels at the fountain of Aganippe. Her rituals were believed to have centered around music and the sound of a flute (known as a 'Vitsika flute'), as well as sacrificing small animals to her. In some myths, she is said to have had a special harp made at Olympus, inscribed with her own name. Throughout the ages, Vitsika has remained a popular figure in Greek mythology. Ovid describes her in his Metamorphoses as “Joy maddening in her laughter, every bit as seductive and voluptuous as her father Dionysus," Later, Apuleius describes her as “the wild carouser.” For the ancient Greeks, Vitsika was a figure to be invoked in times of distress and sorrow, when joy, festivity, and laughter were needed to help banish gloom and bring brightness to one’s life. Despite her association with longing, tribulation and spiritual joy, Vitsika is more often celebrated in her associations with mirth, merriment, and festivities. To this end, she is depicted in modern art as a female figure bearing a cup filled with delicious beverage and a festive object, often a flute. In modern culture, Vitsika is seen as a reminder of the power of joy and laughter to bring people together and to enliven any occasion. By offering her a toast or a simple song, one can evoke her lighthearted spirit and experience joy on a spiritual level.

Automba Township is an organized township in Carlton County, Minnesota, United States. As of the 2010 census, the township had a population of 290, making it the least populous township in Minnesota. The township was organized in 1891 and named after the Ojibwe chief Automba. The area was primarily a logging community and was the last to be settled in the county. Logging remained the primary economic activity in Automba until the late 20th century. The unincorporated community of Automba is located in the township. The mainly residential community contains stores, a post office, a hills Chapel, and a Baptist church. A single school serves local students. Today, Automba Township is a somewhat rural community. It is mostly composed of farms and woodlands, with a few small commercial establishments. There are two lakes in the township; Automba Lake, which is the largest lake in the county and Lake Bigfork. Both lakes are popular with visitors, offering fishing and recreational opportunities. Automba Township is governed by a three-member board of supervisors. They are responsible for maintaining roads, enforcing zoning regulations and licensing hunting and fishing. The board also approves budgets and other local initiatives. Automba Township generally supports the Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party. The township is represented in the Minnesota House of Representatives by Rob Ecklund (DFL). The township has a fire department, which is staffed by volunteer fire fighters and provides fire protection for the community and its surrounding area. The Automba Township Fire Department is a member of the Northern Minnesota Firefighter's Association. Automba Township is located in a region of Minnesota known as the "Northland." The area is known for its strong sense of community, its abundance of natural resources, and its tight-knit community.

Linearization is a mathematical method used to represent a non-linear system as a linear approximation of its characteristics. It is useful for analyzing and controlling such systems without necessarily having to solve their equations. Linearization can also be used to solve certain types of non-linear equations, such as those with polynomial roots. In mathematics, a system is considered to be linear if its input-output relationship does not change when the value of the inputs are changed. A non-linear system is one in which small changes in the input yield large changes in the output. Linearization involves approximating the behavior of a non-linear system by finding a linear function that describes the behavior of the system. This is done by finding the linear approximation of a non-linear function near a given point. For example, consider the following non-linear equation: y = x^2. In general, this equation is non-linear, since it is not a straight line. However, if we approximate this equation near the point (0,0) (that is, when x is close to zero), we can then linearize the equation. The linear approximation of this equation near (0,0) is y = 2*x, which is a linear equation for small changes in x. Linearization can also be used to investigate the behavior of a non-linear system. For instance, consider the following differential equation: \frac{dx}{dt}=f(x,y,t) Linearizing this equation near a certain point allows us to approximate the behavior of the system in this region. Linearization is also useful for control systems. Linearizing the system allows us to determine the behavior of the system under various inputs. This can be used to calculate the amount of input required to keep the system in a desired state, or to investigate the stability under certain input conditions. In general, linearization is a powerful technique that can be used to investigate and control non-linear systems. By approximating a non-linear system with a linear approximation near a given point, linearization enables us to understand the behavior of the system in this region. Furthermore, this technique can be used to calculate the amount of input required to keep the system in a desired state, or to analyze its stability under certain circumstances.

Cong Xuedi (Chinese: 丛雪蒂; born 16 December 1987) is a Chinese activist, LGBTQ+ advocate, and polymath. She is a co-founder of the prominent LGBT+ civil rights organization the Beijing Gender Health Education Institute. Early Life Cong Xuedi was born in Jiangxi province, China in December 16, 1987. She attended the Experimental High School of China Jiliang University and later studied at Jilin University of Finance and Economics majoring in public finance. It was during this time that Cong Xuedi grew interested in gender and sexuality, in particular the LGBTQ+ community. Activism Following college, Cong Xuedi decided to dedicate her life to improving the lives of LGBTQ+ people in her home country of China. In 2013, she co-founded the Beijing Gender Health Education Institute (BGHEI) to advocate for the rights of LGBTQ+ individuals in China. For the past five years, BGHEI has been at the forefront of China's LGBTQ+ rights movement, advocating for legal and social reforms to the country's social policies. The Institute has also provided programs such as "gender health education" and "safe zones" for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer people. In addition to her BGHEI activism, Cong Xuedi has also supported other important LGBTQ+ initiatives in the country. For example, she was an organizer of the 2018 China Queer Movie Festival and also helped to co-organize the first Chinese Trans Film Festival in 2019. Apart from her advocacy for LGBTQ+ people, Cong Xuedi is also an active promoter of other civil rights movements in China. She helped to organize the 2018 Women's March in Beijing and was also involved in the 2019 protest against the Chinese government's proposed new security law in Hong Kong. She is also a proponent of China's #MeToo movement and has publicly advocated for stronger legal protections against sexual harassment in workplaces and universities. Political Career In 2020 Cong Xuedi ran for a seat in the Shanghai People’s Congress, a quasi-democratic body that is part of the Chinese government. The election was controversial due to the fact that Cong Xuedi was openly LGBTQ+ and had a history of political activism. Despite the fact that she ultimately lost the election, the campaign made waves in Chinese politics. Personal Life Cong Xuedi currently lives in Shanghai, China and has a partner with whom she has two children. In her free time, she enjoys reading, traveling, and spending quality time with her family. She has also written extensively on LGBTQ+ issues and is a renowned speaker at universities and international conferences. Cong Xuedi is renowned for her outspokenness on women's issues, LGBTQ+ rights and social justice. Legacy Cong Xuedi has become a pioneering figure in the fight for LGBTQ+ rights in China, leading the Beijing Gender Health Education Institute in the fight for legal and social reforms for China's queer people. She is an outspoken supporter of the #MeToo movement and has been a vocal advocate for the rights of minorities in China. Cong Xuedi is also a role model for many, representing the values of tolerance, progressivism and human rights in a country where these values are often suppressed.

Arend Glas (born June 29, 1965) is a Dutch entrepreneur and business executive. He is the founder, CEO, and sole shareholder of Glas Vision, a leading intelligent automation solutions company with offices in Amsterdam, London, New York and Toronto. Glas Vision offers automated solutions that help businesses streamline operational processes, increase competitiveness and reduce complexity. Glas was born in a small village in the north of The Netherlands. He grew up on a farm and learned the importance of hard work, diligence and responsibility at a young age. After completing high school, he joined the Dutch Navy and served for four years. During this time, he devoted himself to information technology, developing a strong interest in digital development. After his time in the Navy, Glas founded his own company, Glas Vision. Glas saw an opportunity to apply automation technologies to the operations of companies, which was not yet widely done at the time. His vision was to develop a simple, reliable and powerful automation platform that could benefit businesses in a vast array of industries. The company was an instant success and quickly gained recognition, culminating in Glas being featured in Forbes magazine as one of the “Most Innovative Leaders in Automation”. Glas himself was praised for his bold vision and impeccable execution. Glas Vision continues to be one of the leading technology companies in the industry, and has a strong focus on social responsibility and ecological sustainability. Its solutions are actively used in more than 100 countries worldwide and are employed by companies of all sizes, from start-ups to multinationals. It is credited for having helped its clients improve their efficiency, saving them millions of dollars annually. Arend Glas is a highly respected figure in the technology industry and a passionate advocate for the use of automation to improve business processes. Throughout his career, he has worked to make automation solutions accessible to all businesses, and has played a major role in propelling the industry forward.

Sanders Township is a township in Pennington County, Minnesota, United States. The population was 155 at the 2000 census. The township was named for Ezra Sanders, who was one of the early settlers of the area and an influential political figure in the region. The terrain within the boundaries of Sanders Township is a mix of farmland, forested areas, wetlands and small lakes. A variety of wildlife can be found in the township and the surrounding area, including white-tailed deer, bald eagles, red foxes, coyotes, wild turkeys and a variety of waterfowl. Sanders Township provides recreational opportunities for locals, including hiking and snowmobiling trails and several fishing lakes. In addition, the nearby Mille Lacs Indian Reservation offers hunting, fishing, wild rice harvesting and cultural events. The first settlers in the area arrived in the 1880s, and the township was established in 1895. The area quickly grew, and in 1920 the township had a population of 815 people. As of the 2000 Census, the population had declined to 155, largely due to the decline in local farming in the area. Today, Sanders Township is still predominantly rural and agricultural. The main industries are farming, logging, and tourism. There are several small businesses in the area, including a grocery store, several small stores and a restaurant. Sanders Township is governed by a board of supervisors. The board meets monthly to discuss and make decisions on zoning issues, budgeting and other administrative matters. There are no incorporated villages within the township, although several unincorporated communities exist, including Willowbrook, Autauga, and Myrtle. The township is in the jurisdiction of the Pennington County Sheriff's Department and the Minnesota State Patrol. The Pennington County Ambulance and Rescue Service is also located in the township. The township is part of the Red Lake School District and students attend school in nearby Red Lake Falls. The district includes a K-12 school and several rural schools. The township is served by the Red Lake Falls Post Office and several churches. The Vermillion Presbyterian Church and the Meadow Lutheran Church are the main churches in the township. Sanders Township is a small, rural community that provides a peaceful atmosphere and plenty of recreation opportunities. Despite a population decline in recent years, the township remains committed to maintaining its rural identity and its agricultural roots.

Christian Basso (born June 26, 1992) is an Australian film and television actor, best known for his breakthrough role as Tyler Martin in the 2015 award-winning feature film Holding The Man. He is also known for his roles as Nathan Atkinson in Seven Types of Ambiguity and as Will McGuire in Harrow. Basso grew up in northern Australia and moved to Melbourne to attend university. He studied at the University of Melbourne, majoring in Classical and Performing Arts, graduating in 2014. Upon finishing university, he was selected to join the National Institute of Dramatic Arts Actors Academy and was cast in his first major role in Holding The Man. The film, directed by Neil Armfield, was adapted from the play by Tommy Murphy and based on the memoir of author Timothy Conigrave. Holding The Man tells the story of Conigrave's relationship with John Caleo and the struggles they faced due to the AIDS epidemic. Basso’s performance as Tyler Martin was critically acclaimed, garnering him an AACTA Award nomination for Best Lead Actor in a Television Drama or Young Actor’s Mini-Series. In 2016, Basso starred alongside Hugo Weaving in the psychological thriller Seven Types of Ambiguity. In 2017, he appeared in Harrow, an Australian television series produced by ABC TV in association with Hoodlum Entertainment. The drama follows forensic pathologist Dr. Daniel Harrow, played by Ioan Gruffudd, as he solves difficult cases. Basso plays the role of Will McGuire, a journalism student. Basso’s other acting credits include the 2018 feature film The Tree of Life, starring Emily Browning and Toni Collette, as well as the 2019 comedy The Very Excellent Mr Dundee, with Paul Hogan and Isla Fisher. Throughout his career, Basso has made several television appearances on various networks including ABC, Seven Network, and FOXTEL. In 2019, Basso starred in the mini series Underbelly Files: Chopper, which he filmed in his home country. Basso’s career is only beginning and it is expected to take off. With his recent acting accolades, he is fast becoming one of the most sought after actors in Australia.

The 1520s in music saw a flourishing of polyphony, part songs and motets during the Renaissance period. The decade was a time of experimentation, with composers experimenting with different polyphonic structures, textures and rhythms. During this period, polyphony became increasingly complex, culminating in the works of Thomas Tallis and William Byrd. The range of genres during this period was vast, ranging from sacred music to secular songs. Composers of the 1520s wrote a variety of different sacred pieces, including motets, Mass settings and hymns. These works focus on the spiritual aspects of music and often include intricate melodies and harmonies, as well as harmonies written in the contrapuntal style. The most famous composers of sacred music during this decade include Josquin Desprez, Thomas Tallis and William Byrd. In the field of secular music, the 1520s saw the rise of the Netherlandic-French School and the English Madrigal. This new genre of music was characterized by its lively melodies, contrasting between homophonic and polyphonic structure, and its ability to create vivid scenes and moods. Popular composers of madrigals during this period include Thomas Morley, John Wilbye, and Thomas Weelkes. In addition to these two genres, music during the 1520s was also influenced by popular forms such as the estampie, basse danse and passepied. These popular dance forms, often accompanied by instruments like the lute, commonly appear in music manuscripts from this decade. The influence of the Renaissance period was pervasive throughout Europe, and the 1520s saw a wide variety of regional styles emerge. Composers from Italy such as Palestrina, Gombert and Marenzio incorporated imitative counterpoint into their compositions. In Germany and Austria, the influence of the Reformation lead to the emergence of a distinct chorale style, characterized by its strict contrapuntal settings and German sacred texts. In the New World, the 1520s are particularly noteworthy for the rise of the Mexican chanson. This genre, which has its roots in Spanish folk songs, developed into a distinct style featuring vocal parts and texts written in Spanish and Nahuatl. Popular composers of Mexican chansons include Diego Enciso and Juan López de Flandes. Overall, the 1520s were a pivotal period in musical history. This decade saw the emergence of many different musical styles, forms and genres, and the emergence of composers who would reshape the musical landscape of Europe and the world.

Mina Rzouki (born 25 June 1983) is a British-Italian journalist, author and broadcaster, currently a football presenter and reporter for various broadcast outlets including ESPN, BBC World Service and BBC Sport. She is also a columnist for BBC's Women in Football and Sky Sports News. Rzouki was born and raised in London, to a British father and Italian mother. She graduated with a law degree from University of Westminster in 2005, and in 2006 began a Masters of Arts at the City University of London. Rzouki began her career as a producer for Channel 4 and ITV in 2006. She moved to the BBC in 2008 to become a producer for the Today Programme and then for the World Service, followed by a stint as a presenter for traditional Arab media platforms. In 2011, Rzouki began working for ESPN as a presenter and later became a match analyst and football correspondent. She covered some of the world's biggest sporting events, including the UEFA Champions League, the Premier League, the Women’s World Cup and the 2016 European Championships. During her time at ESPN, she won a prestigious UN recognition for her groundbreaking work. Rzouki joined Sky Sports as a presenter in 2016 and continues to work as a football presenter and reporter for various media outlets including the BBC, as well as being a regular panellist on Sky Sport's Transfer Show. In addition to football, Rzouki has written regularly for print, mainly focused on football, politics, culture and photography. She has written for CNN, Forbes, The New York Times and The Telegraph, among others. In December 2020, she released her first book: Women in Football: Stories of Strength in a Female-Dominated Sport, a collection of interviews with female football players, coaches, managers and academy directors, who paved the way for the modern game of football. Furthermore, Rzouki is an ambassador for the Women Win Football organisation and Women for Football, a founding member of Women in Football network and The International Sport Business Network. She is also an ambassador for My Change and Italian football team Genoa CFC. Rzouki currently lives in Rome, Italy with her husband and their son.

George Hendricks Beverley (1838–1907) was an American carpenter and furniture maker who is remembered as one of the earliest African American entrepreneurs. He was born in Maryland, United States, and settled in Spartanburg, South Carolina. Around the mid-1850s, Beverley began working as a carpenter and eventually opened his own business. At the time, there was no other African American owned and operated furniture store in the area. Beverley's furniture store was larger than most operations of its kind and included a workshop, storage facility, and furniture showroom. Beverley's business flourished because of the high-quality products he produced and sold. In addition, many of his customers were from the plantation society of upcountry South Carolina and northern Georgia, which helped increase his customer base. Beverley took pride in his work and became known for the value and artistry of his furniture. Indeed, a significant portion of his business involved the design, production, and sale of furniture pieces that were requested directly by customers. Beverley was also responsible for carving and selling wooden figurines, most notably, a wooden man on a horse that became a staple at his store. In 1890, Beverley was elected to the South Carolina House of Representatives, making him the first African American to achieve such a political accomplishment in the state. He served a total of four terms and used his political clout to help advocate on behalf of African American rights. Beverley was an inspirational figure in the African American community. He is remembered as an example of what can be achieved with hard work and dedication. Despite the odds, Beverley was able to become an influential entrepreneur and leader in Spartanburg, South Carolina, and his legacy is still remembered today.

Outlaw is a term used to refer to an individual who lives in a state of disregard for the law. It can also refer to a person or group of persons who have been excluded from the protection of the law. The term can apply to both criminal activity and to civil disobedience that challenges laws or customs. Throughout history, legislation and common usage has categorized people as outlaws for various reasons, including being declared enemies of the state, disregarding customs, or breaking unjust laws. In the early periods of history, outlaws were viewed as criminals who lived beyond the law and had no legal protection or recourse from their actions. In ancient Mesopotamia and the Middle Eastern nations, the term "outlaw" was sometimes used to refer to a person under sentence of death for certain crimes. Outlaws were believed to have been barred from seeking redress for grievances, or from attending court or gathering for group activities due to their declaration as enemies of the state. In feudal societies, when kings and other rulers wielded total power and control, the concept of outlawry was used as a tool to control the population. Outlaws were declared enemies of the state and were ceremoniously and forcibly removed from their villages and tribes. They were often branded as criminals, robbers, or thieves and were often subjected to cruel punishments as a way to keep the rest of the population in line. In some cases, particularly during the period of the Wild West, outlaws were seen as folk heroes. These individuals often went against the grain of society and gained notoriety for their exceptional skills, fearlessness, and defiance against tyranny. Today, the term outlaw is still used in certain contexts, such as organized crime or for political dissidents, but has generally come to refer to any individual or group who are considered to be outside of, or rebellious against, the laws of society. In popular culture, the term outlaw has come to also refer to those who flout the law or traditional norms for their own personal gain or sense of justice. Outlaws are typically portrayed as rebels or renegades who challenge the status quo and rebel against the norms of society, or uphold their own individual code of morality or justice.

Hotel Colegial is a boutique hotel located in Gijón, Asturias, Spain. The hotel is situated on the banks of the Eo River and near the principal shopping and business area of the city. It is a four-star hotel specializing in relaxation and luxury accommodation and services. The hotel was opened in 2006, offering superior accommodation in a privileged natural environment. It has 39 comfortable rooms, including standard, superior, family and suite options. All rooms are modernly and tastefully decorated and come fully equipped with air-conditioning, flat-screen satellite television, free Wi-Fi and private bathrooms. Most rooms offer views of the Eo River and the city. Hotel Colegial features a variety of facilities including a restaurant serving a range of Asturian and international dishes, a cafe-bar, a business corner and meeting rooms. There is also a spa area including jacuzzi, sauna, Turkish bath and a fully-equipped gym. The hotel provides free parking, free shuttle bus to and from the railway station, bike rental and other services. It is conveniently located less than 5 km from Gijón-Asturias Airport and the city’s railway station. Hotel Colegial offers an outstanding service, excellent facilities and a tranquil atmosphere, making it the ideal place to stay while visiting Gijón. Its staff is highly professional and friendly and will help you to make the most of your stay.

Cast King is a professional Fortnite esports team. Founded in 2020, it currently fields teams in the European region. The organization is based in the United Kingdom, and operates globally. Cast King was founded in 2020 by a group of professional Fortnite players. The team is an endeavor to assemble a current roster of players from the European region. Cast King is focused on creating an environment for its players that encourages growth, professional competition and a strong community. The Cast King roster currently consists of 8 main players: Ella, Fliss, Refect, Revo, SoaR_Bubu, Zodd, Ownage, and Funkzombies. All eight players have a range of competitive experiences that make Cast King one of the strongest teams in Europe. When it comes to competitive play, Cast King has performed well in tournaments and events. In the 2020 WSOE Invitational Series Final, the team placed 4th overall. As of April 2021, the team has won four Cash Cup Series tournaments, and placed 2nd in four other tournaments. In addition to competitive play, Cast King also promotes and actively participates in many charity events on behalf of their players, raising money for important causes all over the world. This includes, but is not limited to, their “Donate For Change” campaign, through which they have donated over $7,000 to causes such as animal rescue, fighting world hunger and education reform. The players of Cast King are all part of a larger community that consists of both fans and professional esports players alike. As such, the players of Cast King receive support from their growing fan-base, and are always open to conversations with other members of the community. The team is also very committed to creating content and engaging with their fans, creating weekly streams and high-quality video content on their YouTube channel. Through their hard work, dedication and commitment to the craft, Cast King is slowly becoming one of the premier Esports teams in Europe. With their talented roster, passionate fan-base and commitment to charity, Cast King is poised to become a major force in the world of competitive Fortnite.

Aubrey Lewis (1901–1979) was a pioneering African-American psychiatrist and professor at the University of Michigan who led a crucial shift in mental health care in the 1960s. He was the first African-American professor in the Psychiatry Department at the University of Michigan, a member of the American Psychiatric Association, and a professor of psychiatry at Meharry Medical College. Born in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, on November 7, 1901, Dr. Lewis was the son of Isabel and Frank Lewis, who were shop and restaurant owners. Lewis attended the University of Iowa, The Ohio State University, and the University of Michigan, where he earned his medical degree in 1936. After graduation, he interned at the American Hospital of Paris and spent a year in New York, working on cancer research, before settling in Detroit. Following that, Lewis joined the teaching staff of the Wayne State University Medical Center in 1943, making him the first African-American professor in a Department of Psychiatry. His breakthrough came in 1953 when he was appointed professor and head of psychiatry at the University of Michigan. While at the university, he developed an innovative approach to mental health care, including the use of group therapy, which was unusual at the time. Upon his retirement from the university in 1967, he founded the Aubrey Lewis Center in Detroit, which provided a number of mental health services to African-American patients. In addition to his work in clinical psychiatry, Dr. Lewis was a pioneer in the field of community mental health. He served as president of the National Mental Health Association (now Mental Health America) from 1971–1974 and was active in community organizations in Detroit. He was seen as a mentor to many young psychiatrists, including the late Dr. Fred Plum, a highly respected Professor of Psychiatry at Cornell University Medical College, who described him as “a strong advocate for mental health services for African-Americans, [who] was an educator, a mentor and a role model for many in the psychiatric profession.” Throughout his career, Dr. Lewis was a tireless advocate for his patients and the mental health profession. He was a staunch believer in the importance of human relationships and the power of psychology. He wrote several books, serves as a mentor to many, and received numerous awards and honorary memberships. His contributions to the field of mental health care set the groundwork for the recognition of mental illness as a medical condition, and his efforts have paved the way for the integration of mental health services. He was a dedicated mentor and educator who left a lasting legacy of compassion and knowledge.

Heinrich Richter (1811 - 1883) was a German-born painter and engraver who became a prominent figure in British art circles and part of the Pre-Raphaelite movement of the mid 19th century. He was born in Coburg, Saxony, and studied in Leipzig before moving to the Royal Academy of Arts in Dresden in 1834. During his time in Dresden, Richter established close relationships with several of the Pre-Raphaelite artists including William Holman Hunt and John Everett Millais; these relationships were to prove influential throughout his artistic career. Richter moved to England in 1837, settling in Canterbury and then London, where he quickly established a demanding client-base in watercolour portraiture and interior paintings. Although he was best known for his delicate watercolour, he also produced a number of etchings and undertook commissions for stained glass. In 1839 Richter joined the Institution of British Architects, allowing him to gain a greater degree of access to potential patrons, and provide him with greater freedom to experiment with his artwork away from any commercial constraints. It was at this Institution that he met several of the prominent Pre-Raphaelite painters, furthering his career with commissions from the Royal Academy of Arts and the National Gallery. Throughout the 1840s Richter turned his attention to landscape paintings, travelling around the country visiting scenic locations. He was particularly fond of Snowdonia and the Brecon Beacons in Wales, and often returned to these sites to paint their rugged beauty. To complement this Romantic vision of the British landscape, Richter frequently painted pastoral scenes set in the Shropshire countryside. In 1852 Richter joined the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, standing out among its members due to his age, being significantly older than William Holman Hunt, John Everett Millais and Dante Gabriel Rossetti. Despite being painted in the style of the Pre-Raphaelites, Richter's palette quickly moved away from their bright and vivid colours of their heyday, instead concentrating on a more subdued palette of greens and blues. Richter died of pneumonia in 1883; having previously suffered a period of ill-health he was cremated following his death. He is seen as an important figure in the history of British art, painting both in the style of his fellow Pre-Raphaelites but also as a high-profile representative for German art in England.

China–Malawi relations refer to the diplomatic and economic relations between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of Malawi. The countries have enjoyed friendly interactions since Malawi's independence in 1964, and in 1967 Malawi became one of the first African countries to recognize the government of the People's Republic of China. The China-Malawi relationship has been based on mutual trust and has developed steadily over the years. China supports Malawi's economic and social development, and Malawi appreciates China's assistance in these areas. China is a major source of financial, technical and material assistance to Malawi, and since 1969 has provided over $1 billion in assistance, loans and investments to the country. China and Malawi have signed a variety of agreements, including a Framework Agreement on Economic and Technological Cooperation, an Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments and a Memorandum of Understanding on Agriculture Cooperation. In 2017, China became the largest trading partner of Malawi. It is estimated that up to 20% of the country’s total imports come from China. The two countries also cooperate in other areas, such as diplomatic activities, people-to-people exchanges, health, infrastructure, education and disaster preparedness. In 2018, Malawi’s President Peter Mutharika made an official visit to China, and the two countries issued a joint communique that outlined their commitment to further strengthening their bilateral ties. In addition, China and Malawi have held several ministerial-level talks to discuss issues of mutual interest. For example, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his Malawian counterpart visited China in May 2018 to discuss cooperation and trade. The talks focused on China-Africa cooperation, strengthening mutual trust, and improving people-to-people exchanges. China–Malawi relations are expected to continue to develop in the coming years. Both countries are working to enhance cooperation in areas such as agriculture, transportation, trade, finance and investment, and tourism. The two countries have also signed a Free Trade Agreement, which is expected to deepen their economic and trade relations.

Tony Halik (born 3 April 1937, in Vilnius, Lithuania) was a prominent Polish traveler, explorer, globetrotter, author and journalist. He was often referred to in the media as the “Flying Grandfather”, for his ongoing round-the-world trips. Halik graduated from Warsaw University in 1960 with a degree in geology, then began working as a researcher for the Polish Geological Institute. It wasn't long before his adventurous spirit and love for travel was too great to resist and he took off around the world. He is renowned for being the first Pole to travel to every continent in the world, visiting a total of 192 countries. During the course of his travels, he wrote extensively, going so far as to start his own publishing house, “Podróże” (“Travels”). Many of his books are still popular today, particularly “Byłem wszędzie” (“I’ve Been Everywhere”) and “Żyzny kontynent” (“Fertile Continent”). He also wrote extensively for numerous newspapers and magazines, and his travelogues instantly became best selling books. The pinnacle of his career was in 1989 when he became Poland's National Geographic TV show presenter called “Oko Tony’ego” (“Tony’s Eye”). Among the countries Halik traveled to during this project are Iraq, Syria, India, South Africa, the U.S. and others. He received a number of honorary doctorates during his career, was awarded the Knight’s Cross of Polonia Restituta, as well as numerous other awards from both Poland and other countries. Halik viewed his life as an adventure and was an inspiration to many; his motto was “The whole world - for everyone”. He died in 2013 after a lifetime of achievements and globetrotting, leaving a legacy of unforgettable impressions and experiences.

The Breit equation is a model of a nuclear force proposed by American physicist Gregory Breit in 1934. It is used to describe the interaction of two particles in a three-dimensional system. The Breit equation is derived from one of the most popular theories of scattering theory, the scattering amplitude theory. The Breit equation is an extension of the exchange of virtual photons between two particles, and is the basis for the exchange of mesons in particle physics. The Breit equation is written as a function of the energy-momentum product (also known as the Mandelstam invariant or "s-product"). It is expressed as: F(s,e)=G(s,e)+H(s,e) where G and H are functions of s and e. G is the Gamow factor and H is the exchange-forcing term. The Breit equation can be solved analytically for different values of s and e. The Breit equation was originally developed for the purpose of calculating scattering amplitudes for nuclear and particle physics. But it has recently been used in other fields including optically active crystals, plasmon and polaritons, and cavity quantum electrodynamics. The Breit equation is an important tool in particle physics because it can calculate scattering amplitudes for various processes. This allows researchers to investigate the behavior of particles in different circumstances and to better understand the nature of Nature. The Breit equation is also used in quantum field theory to investigate gravitational interactions and quantum electrodynamics. It is also used to study neutrino oscillations and for calculations of the Bragg peak structure for radiation therapy. The Breit equation is a powerful and versatile tool for understanding the nature and behavior of particles. It is an indispensable part of the scientific arsenal used by physicists to study and develop new and improved theories of fundamental interactions.

Posthuman is a term used to describe a hypothetical state of human being that is deemed to be better than what is currently considered to be "human". It is not a concept of which there is one single definition, with interpretations varying from one individual or institution to another. Generally, posthumanism refers to a reimagination of humans and their capabilities, with the potential for radical transformation of humanity involving advances in human evolution, biotechnology and artificial intelligence. Posthumanism holds the promise of increased life expectancy, physical and psychological well-being, and greater cognitive abilities. It is part of a larger discourse of transhumanism, which looks at technology as a way to improve upon the human condition. Transhumanists seek to use technology to expand a human's intellectual and physical capacities beyond their biological limits, as well as to create new forms of life. Posthumanism however, looks beyond just physical change, and at how humans can be created to have radically different mental and social capabilities. Posthumanism is often discussed in relation to science fiction, as it provides a thought experiment through which to explore the potential of humanity's futuristic advancement. Some proponents of posthumanism argue that it presents the potential for a better future where human flourishing and autonomy are realized, while others consider it to be an existential risk to humanity. Posthumanism is associated with a number of different philosophical positions, such as the poststructuralist view of subjectivity as fluid and endlessly reconfigurable in interaction with the material world. Other philosophical perspectives include the cybernetic theories of Norbert Wiener and Henri Bergson's vitalism. Posthumanism has also been linked to certain cultural trends such as the virtual world and cyberpunk. It has been argued that virtual worlds facilitates a new form of self-expression and identity, which can potentially offer more freedom than real life. Cyberpunk on the other hand, concerns itself with the idea that technology has replaced or augmented humans, and that people's lives are becoming immersed in an elaborate technology-driven culture. Whatever form it may take, posthumanism is sure to continue to be an important part of conversations about how technology and humanity can interact. It embodies the promise of science and technology to depart from the physical constraints of our present state, while still striving to preserve human values.

Mount Limbara is an extinct stratovolcano located in the northernmost part of Sardinia, an island off the west coast of Italy. The volcano is made up of three distinct cones and is the largest volcano in Sardinia. It is believed to have last erupted approximately 28,000 years ago. Mount Limbara covers an area of approximately 997 km2 and has a highest elevation of 1,822 metres (5,975 feet). Other prominent peaks in the area include Monte Calvario, Monte Salpetino and Monte Pria. It is part of a vast caldera which covers about half of Sardinia, and as such has shaped the region significantly over its lifetime. The volcano is thought to be the second youngest in Europe, and the youngest in Sardinia. The oldest eruptions associated with Mount Limbara are believed to have been basaltic and hawaiite long before the formation of the caldera. It has produced a diverse range of rocks and minerals, such as andesite, asthenophene, basalt, dacite, felsite and leucitite. This is due to the process of magma going through various stages as it cools, allowing a great variety of elements to come together. The different types of rock also reflect Mount Limbara's long dormant status since its last eruption. The volcano has been important to the local population since antiquity and is thought to be mentioned in the ancient records of the Nuragic people. It was also an important part of Sardinia's socio-economic development, providing vital energy and other resources to the local population. In the early 19th century, coal and limestone were extracted from its slopes in a major industrial endeavour that lasted until the mid-20th century. In modern times, Mount Limbara is a popular tourist destination, with several hillwalking trails winding their way through the mountain range. The national park surrounding Mount Limbara is known for its diverse wildlife, including golden eagle, mouflons, wild boar, red deer and wild turkey. The traditional Sardinian cuisine of Casizzu features many dishes based on the local produce and game. Mount Limbara is an important part of the history, culture and geography of Sardinia, and it is an integral part of the local identity and pride. It is an iconic symbol of the local region and an important component of the island's tourism industry.

Luna E-6 No.5 was the fifth in a series of robotic spacecraft launched by the Soviet Union between 1963 and 1973. It was part of the Luna E-6 remote lunar exploration program and was designed to return a soil sample from the Moon. Launched on April 2, 1968, it was the fifth of six successful missions to return lunar samples to Earth. The goal of the Luna E-6 program was to obtain and return a sample from the Moon for scientific study. The spacecraft resembled a copy of the Yangel’s R-14 ICBM with the same diameter of 2.3 m and a total mass of 3118 kg. Its design was based on the Luna E-6 model that had already been used in several previous unmanned Moon missions. Luna E-6 No.5 was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan by an eight-stage Molniya-M rocket. After reaching lunar orbit, the spacecraft descended to about 20 km above the surface and took four pictures of the area where the sample was to be collected. It then fired its engine for the braking maneuver and began its descent toward the lunar surface. After touching down on the lunar surface, Luna E-6 No.5 used a three-stage extended arm to collect a sample of beneath the surface of the Moon. The sample weighed at least 100 grams and was placed in a protective glass capsule. After collecting the sample, the spacecraft used its engine again to escape from the Moon’s gravity and fired its retro-rockets to reduce its speed, allowing it to enter a geocentric orbit around the Earth. Luna E-6 No.5 successfully returned to Earth on 10 April and impact in the steppe regions of Kazakhstan. Due to its safe return, the Soviet Union was the first country to collect soil samples from the Moon and was a major achievement of the Russian space program. The Luna E-6 No.5 mission was widely publicized and its success opened the way for several other lunar sample return missions. In addition, it served as the template for manned space flights. In 1969, the U.S. Apollo 11 lunar module used a similar type of extended arm to collect a lunar sample.

GameStorm is a fan-organized gaming convention that has taken place in the Pacific Northwest since 1997. It is held annually in late March or early April at the Portland Doubletree Hotel in Portland, Oregon. The convention is sponsored by the Northwest Association of Gamers (NWAG). GameStorm focuses primarily on tabletop (board and card) gaming, role-playing games and miniatures gaming. It is the second largest gaming convention in the Pacific Northwest and draws from all the major cities of the region and beyond, including Seattle, Spokane, Boise, and Vancouver. Every year, the convention includes events with game designers and tournament events, such as X-Wing, Terraforming Mars, and Warhammer 40000, as well as open gaming, where attendees can select from a wide variety of available board games for play. GameStorm also includes a variety of special events and activities. Panels on game design, publishing, art, and teaching are part of the experience. Many publishers and vendors are present with new releases and special deals. Various organized challenges, special tournaments and tournaments of chance occur throughout the weekend. The MIB organization, the international organization dedicated to the hobby of Metagaming, often organizes events at GameStorm, as well. A series of seminars and workshops are held throughout the convention, along with a game library that is available to attendees for game play throughout the weekend. Play-by-Email tournaments are run, and a game auction is held in the evening. Special kids' events, such as costume contests, scavenger hunts, magic workshops, and a talent show, are also featured during the event. GameStorm continues to grow each year in popularity and attendance, and has become an important part of the Pacific Northwest gaming community. It is an opportunity for hobbyists to come together and enjoy their chosen hobby, as well as finding new and interesting new games and participating in tournaments with players from all around the region.

Dieter Lehnhoff (b. April 4, 1940) is a German engineer and inventor best known for his cutting edge technology and innovation in the electrical industry. He studied electrical engineering and industrial technology at Technical University of Munich, graduating in 1964. After graduation, he joined Larsen & Toubro Siemens India, where he was involved in project led by Dr. Adolf Goetzberger to develop large scale solar power generation systems. During his time there, he was awarded a PhD in Electrical Engineering from TUM. In the early 1970s, Dieter returned to Germany and joined HUAWEI Technologies, where he led the company's development of industrial automation. During this time, he developed the concept of programmable logic controllers (PLC) and invented an integrated switchgear system for factories. This resulted in HUAWEI Technologies receiving an award from the German government for their contribution to innovation in the electrical industry. In 1982, Dieter founded his own engineering firm DELattronics, which specialized in electrical engineering and simulation. At DELattronics, he pioneered energy efficient and precision control technology, producing highly innovative products and services. His company’s clients included industrial and engineering companies, energy providers, and education institutions. After several successful years, DELattronics was taken over by Siemens in 1999, and Dieter became Senior Vice President of the company’s automation division. During his time there, he contributed to research and development of new energy efficiency technologies. In 2004, he received the Siemens Innovators Award for his groundbreaking technologies. Following his retirement in 2010, he became an advisor to Siemens on energy efficiency. Apart from his engineering achievements, Dieter has also been involved in teaching and academic research. He taught electrical engineering at Germany's Applied University of Mannheim for 20 years and has written several books and academic papers on electrical engineering. He has won numerous awards and accolades for his engineering achievements, including the German National Champion of Technology in 1974 and the Grand Prize of Merit from the Economic Senate of Germany. Dieter also holds 20 patent registrations for his inventions. In 2010, Dieter founded his own company Lehnhoff Technologies, which produces automation and control solutions for industry, energy and research sectors. To date, his company has successfully produced products that are cost effective, energy efficient and technologically advanced.

Cosmos Engineering is an engineering company founded by Lando and his business partner, David, in May 2021. The company is focused on providing innovative engineering solutions that create meaningful impact in the fields of aerospace, automotive and civil engineering. Cosmos Engineering is a full-service engineering firm that provides engineering design and consultancy services for a wide range of projects. The main areas of expertise include design and simulation engineering, embedded systems, design and engineering testing, and product lifecycle management. The team at Cosmos Engineering has extensive engineering experience and is passionate about inspiring and enabling new ways of thinking and working. The company has the latest technology, a talented engineering team and strategic partnerships that allow them to offer best-in-class solutions. The main areas of focus at Cosmos Engineering are aeronautics, automotive, and civil engineering. In the aerospace industry, Cosmos Engineering performs tasks such as design, simulation, and testing of aircraft components. In the automotive industry, Cosmos Engineering provides engineering solutions for electric, hybrid, and connected vehicles. In the civil engineering industry, Cosmos Engineering focuses on the design, simulation, and testing of structures and infrastructure such as bridges, tunnels, roads, and buildings. Cosmos Engineering believes that engineering should be an open, collaborative, and transparent process. To achieve transparency in their engineering processes, the company has developed several tools and systems that can be used to track and monitor projects throughout their development, such as a project management portal. This portal provides clients with detailed information about the project's status, allowing them to rapidly make decisions and changes throughout the development process. At Cosmos Engineering, the focus is not only on engineering services, but also on challenging the status quo and inspiring others. The company regularly holds hackathons, where the engineering team can come together to develop cutting-edge solutions and spark technology innovation. They also collaborate with a number of stakeholders in their industry, such as universities, government organizations, and corporations. Overall, Cosmos Engineering is a leading engineering company with a mission to bring innovative engineering solutions that create meaningful impact in the fields of aerospace, automotive, and civil engineering.

Pakistan is a nation that has participated in the Asian Games, a biennial multi-sport event held among athletes from all over Asia, since the 1954 Asian Games held in Manila, Philippines. Pakistan has taken part in every edition of the games represented by the Pakistan Olympic Association. Pakistan has achieved a total of 622 medals at the Asian Games, with hockey as its top medal-winning sport. They have won 132 gold medals, 237 silver medals, and 252 bronze medals. Pakistan's best performance was at the 1990 Asian Games in Beijing, where they won a total of 63 medals, including 23 gold medals. Pakistan also performed well at the 1986 Asian Games held in Seoul, where they won a total of 57 medals including 21 gold medals. At the 2010 Asian Games held in Guangzhou, China, Pakistan won a total of 19 medals; 5 gold, 6 silver and 8 bronze. Pakistan's only gold medal in 2010 came from the men's hockey team which won the gold medal after defeating South Korea in the final. At the 2014 Asian Games held in Incheon, South Korea, Pakistan won a total of 15 medals; 6 gold, 4 silver and 5 bronze. Their best performance at this edition of the games came in squash and wrestling, with gold medals in both. At the 2018 Asian Games held in Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia, Pakistan won a total of 18 medals; 4 gold, 12 silver and 2 bronze. The gold medals were won by Muhammad Inam Butt in wrestling, the men's hockey team, the men's squash team, and the women's squash team. Pakistan has participated in all editions of the Asian Games since its inaugural edition in 1954, competing in numerous sports over the years and achieving great success. With its ever-growing tally of medals at the Asian Games, Pakistan has demonstrated its commitment to becoming a greater regional sporting power.

Hemza Mihoubi was an Algerian revolutionary and anti-colonial leader who is best known for his role in leading the Algerian struggle for independence against French colonial rule. Born in 1913 in El Oued, Algeria, Mihoubi was a leader of the Algerian National Liberation Front and a founding member of the Revolutionary Council of Unity and Action (CRUA). Mihoubi was educated in France and was an early advocate of Algerian independence. After the eruption of the Algerian War of Independence (1954–1962), Mihoubi was an active participant and advocate for Algerian freedom. As head of the Revolutionary Council of Unity and Action, Mihoubi organized and popularized the armed struggle against French colonialism. His recruitment of young Algerian men for the Front de Liberation Nationale (FLN) made him a pivotal figure in the battle for Algerian independence. When independence was finally achieved in 1962, Mihoubi was appointed Minister of Information in Ben Bella's first government. He also held other important posts in the Algerian government, including chair of the Organisation de l’armée nationale algérienne (ONA) and Chief of Staff of the Algerian armed forces from 1965 to 1966. Mihoubi's contributions were widely recognized; in January 1962, he was awarded the Band of Honour of the FLN and in 1968, he was given the title of Deputy President of the Republic of Algeria. He also held various leadership posts and helped to draft the 1965 Constitution of Algeria. In the late 1968, Mihoubi was named Prime Minister in a transitional period before Houari Boumediene's rise to power. Mihoubi was, however, removed from his post after he took certain actions that Boumediene viewed as inappropriate. Mihoubi continued to exercise influence, however, serving as ambassador to several countries and remaining active in politics until the end of his life. He died in 1983 in Algiers at the age of 70 and was buried in El Oued. Hemza Mihoubi remains an important figure in Algerian history for his role in leading and advocating for Algerian independence. He was a determined and passionate leader whose legacy continues to inspire present and future generations to fight for freedom and justice.

Armstrong & Getty is an American conservative talk radio show hosted by its namesake hosts Jack Armstrong and Joe Getty. The show broadcasts weekdays from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. Pacific Time, and is simulcast on terrestrial radio stations and internet streaming audio. Armstrong & Getty is one of the most popular talk radio shows in the US, with an audience of over 1.3 million weekly listeners, and has been nationally syndicated since 2001. Armstrong & Getty launched its first radio show in the San Francisco Bay Area in 1994. Armstrong and Getty's witty and irreverent style has resonated with audiences in the Bay Area and beyond, and has gained a national popularity over the past decade. The show has been hosted weekdays from 6-10 am Pacific Time since 1995, and is simulcast on terrestrial and internet streaming audio platforms. Armstrong & Getty covers many topics in its broadcasts, ranging from local, regional and national politics, current affairs, and societal issues. They have been endorsed by popular pundits such as Rush Limbaugh and Glenn Beck, and have had many guests, including working-class Americans, celebrities, and political figures, on the show. The show also features its signature segments, such as “Idiot of the Week”, a weekly segment in which Armstrong & Getty selecting someone they feel has done something especially idiotic. The show also has a comedic segment entitled “Trending News Topics”, in which Armstrong & Getty discuss trending news items in a humorous way. Armstrong & Getty has also acquired national popularity due to their frequent appearances on television shows, such as The O’Reilly Factor, FOX & Friends, and The Daily Show with Jon Stewart. Aside from the radio show, Armstrong & Getty has also had their own syndicated TV show, Armstrong & Getty on 790 KABC in Los Angeles, from 1999 to 2003, and a live Westwood One television special, Armstrong & Getty Live from New York in the summer of 2004. In addition, Armstrong & Getty have written two books: Shut Up and Sing and The Permanent Revolution, both of which cover their political views and perspectives. Armstrong & Getty have been very successful in broadcasting, and continue to be one of the most listened to and respected talk radio shows in the United States.

Paul Shapiro (born October 13, 1978) is an American film and television writer, producer and director. He is best known for directing the independent films Planet of the Apes (2001), The Hotel (2004), Days of Wrath (2008) and March of the Dead (2009). Shapiro was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York. He studied film and television at New York University. His early writing and directing experience included short films, music videos and commercials. In 2001, Shapiro wrote and directed his first feature film, Planet of the Apes. The film was well-received by critics and was eventually released theatrically in the United States. In 2004, Shapiro wrote and directed the independent film The Hotel, starring Stephen Baldwin and Eric Stoltz. The film was a critical and commercial success, and was released theatrically and on home video in the United States. In 2008, Shapiro wrote and directed Days of Wrath, a suspense-thriller starring Jeff Fahey and Tobin Bell. The film was released theatrically in the United States and internationally. In 2009, Shapiro wrote and directed March of the Dead, a zombie movie starring Malcolm McDowell and Michael Biehn. The film was released theatrically in the United States and internationally. Shapiro has been recognized for his work with numerous awards and nominations. He has won two Cinefantastique Visionary Awards, a Hollywood Film Award and a Writers Guild of America Award. He has also received multiple nominations from the Directors Guild of America and been a finalist for the Writers Guild of America's Chesterfield Award. Shapiro is currently in pre-production for his upcoming feature film Zion, scheduled for release in 2020.

Radha Regent Hotel is a four-star luxury hotel in Chennai, India, located close to the Chennai Egmore Railway station. The hotel is owned and operated by Radha Hotels and Resorts, a division of the Radha Group of Companies. The hotel was established in 2008, to cater to the various needs of visitors to Chennai. It has 122 guest rooms, four restaurants, a health center, a business center, and a variety of other facilities. The hotel is designed in a modern contemporary style with every detail carefully planned. The décor is minimalistic, yet elegant with a hint of luxury. The choice of furniture and lighting provide guests with a comfortable and relaxed atmosphere. The hotel offers an array of amenities such as a business center, high-speed internet access, Wi-Fi, 24-hour room service, laundry, and more. The Health Club at the hotel has all the modern facilities such as sauna, steam, Jacuzzi, and a fully equipped gym. In addition, the hotel also offers meeting rooms, a banquet hall, and a conference center for business travelers. For recreational activities, the hotel has a swimming pool at the terrace level with spectacular city views. The hotel also offers a shopping arcade, and a travel desk to make sightseeing tours, booking air tickets and car rentals easier. The hotel provides guests with the perfect blend of comfort, luxury, and convenience. The staff are attentive, courteous and friendly, and will do whatever is needed to ensure a pleasant stay for all guests. The Radha Regent is known for its wonderful hospitality and attention to detail. With its perfect location, and all the amenities on offer, this is one of the best hotels to stay at while in Chennai.

The Canandaigua Street Railroad was a former streetcar system that operated in the city of Canandaigua, New York between 1895 and 1929. It served to provide transportation to the suburbs and to the city center. The first streetcar of the Canandaigua Street Railroad was built in 1895, after plans to build the streetcar system were approved by the City Council in 1894. The system was initially built as a horse-drawn line and was the first such system in Ontario County. However, the line was soon converted to electric streetcars in 1902. The route of the Canandaigua Street Railroad ran from a station located at the corner of Main Street and Brighton Avenue in the city center and then down West Avenue, South Avenue, and East Avenue before terminating at the Canandaigua junction station. This route intermediate stops in the neighborhoods of South Avenue, West Avenue, and East Avenue. In the early days of the streetcar system, fares were very low, costing only five cents for a ride. This contributed to the popularity of the system and it quickly became one of the most important means of transportation in the town.In its later years of operation, the company also operated a fleet of buses which ran on a superseded streetcar route. The service provided by the Canandaigua Street Railroad was quickly becoming more and more obsolete with the development of the automobile and the rise of alternative public transportation. By the end of the 1920s, the system was struggling to stay in operation and it eventually ceased operations in 1929. Today, the former streetcar line is no longer visible; however, some of the original tracks can still be seen in the historic neighborhoods of West Avenue, South Avenue, and East Avenue. The Canandaigua Street Railroad was an important part of the town's history. It provided a reliable and affordable means of transportation to the citizens of Canandaigua, enabling them to move around the town more freely and conveniently. Although it is no longer in operation, its legacy can still be seen around the town.

Shot Hole Disease is a plant disease caused by the pathogen Corythuchinam and is a major problem for many fruit tree ecosystems. The disease is characterized by circular to elliptical spots caused by fungi on the leaves, fruit, and twigs of the host trees. The spots gradually expand until they resemble small “shot holes”. Unfortunately, the disease is often fatal to the host tree and can spread quickly, particularly in environments with high moisture levels. Corythuchinam is an ascomycete fungus and is often referred to as the “shot hole borer”. It is thought to be native to Southeast Asia, but has since spread to other fruit tree ecosystems such as California, Oregon, and Washington. The disease is particularly problematic in California’s Central Valley, where high summer temperatures and humidity levels favor the growth of the pathogen. The disease is spread through spores which can be transported via wind, water, or through pruning tools and infected plant matter. Once in a new environment, the spores latch onto healthy trees and begin to thrive. In an infected tree, the disease begins by gradually causing leaf yellowing and spotting. The spots eventually become circular and eventually give way to “shot holes”. Eventually, twigs and branches will die off, followed by the death of the host tree. As it is often fatal to its host tree, shot hole disease can cause major disruption to local ecosystems. The disease is particularly problematic for commercial growers, as a single orchard can experience near complete losses of their crop due to the disease. To slow the spread of shot hole disease, orchard managers should focus on prevention and early detection. Preventative measures include the use of resistant varieties, prompt pruning of dead and diseased branches, sanitizing pruning tools, and purchasing disease-free planting material. If a tree is already infected, it should be removed immediately to prevent spread. Overall, shot hole disease is a serious problem for many fruit tree ecosystems. If left untreated, it can spread quickly and lead to significant crop losses. To mitigate the disease, it is important to practice preventative measures to reduce chances of infection, and to act swiftly when a tree displays signs of infection.

Amigo is a 2010 Philippine drama film directed by John Sayles and written by Sayles and one of his frequent collaborators, Glenn Datuin. The film stars Joel Torre as Rafael "Amigo" Dacanay, a local mayor caught in the middle of a Philippine-American insurgency at the turn of the twentieth century. The film begins in 1900, with a group of American soldiers led by Major Monroe (Garret Dillahunt) arriving in a small village in the Philippines in an effort to quell the insurgency. Rafael "Amigo" Dacanay (Joel Torre) is the mayor of the village, a former Spanish soldier who has worked hard to keep the peace in the area. His efforts are complicated by the presence of local guerillas fighting for Philippine independence, and he is soon caught in a conflict between what he perceives to be his responsibility to his community and his loyalty to the American forces. Throughout the film Amigo is forced to grapple with the consequences of making seemingly impossible choices. He must decide whether to stand up for his constituents or to help the Americans with their mission. He also faces pressure from within his community surrounding his leadership, as his fellow villagers often express discontent with his decisions. In a symbolic attempt to bridge the gap between himself and his people, Amigo walks a tightrope that stretches above the village, as if to demonstrate his own vulnerability in a situation beyond his control. The film received considerable critical acclaim, with particular praise coming for Sayles' direction and Torre's performance. It was nominated for Best Feature Film at the 2010 Asian Pacific Screen Awards, and was an official selection at the 2010 Toronto International Film Festival. Its complex portrayal of Philippine-American tensions offers an interesting and thought-provoking perspective on a period in history that is often misunderstood or overlooked.

Machrihanish is a small fishing village located on the Kintyre peninsula in Argyll and Bute, Scotland. It has been a popular holiday destination for centuries, and today it is home to small population of permanent residents. The name Machrihanish is derived from the Gaelic phrase "mir a hanish", which translates as "the place at the river's estuary". The village is situated on a sandy beach at the entrance to the Kilbrannan Sound, the narrow sea channel separating the Kintyre peninsula from the island of Gigha. The area is best known for its stunning natural beauty. The village is surrounded by hills and mountains, while the nearby coast offers spectacular views of the open sea. The village also boasts some of the most pristine white sandy beaches in Scotland. Machrihanish is home to a thriving local fishing community. The area's harbours are home to several varieties of local shellfish, most notably oysters, as well as many species of migratory fish, such as cod, coley, silver hake, haddock and monkfish. The local seafood is revered for its excellent taste, and it can be found for sale at many of the local pubs and fishmongers. The village is rich in history and culture. It has a long association with the traditional boatbuilding industry, and in October 2011 it hosted the largest gathering of traditional Rigid Inflatable Boats ever assembled on the Kintyre peninsula. Machrihanish is also home to a thriving sporting scene. The village is home to the world renowned Machrihanish Golf Club, which has held several prestigious competitions, including the Scotland Amateur Championship, the Walker Cup and the British Amateur. The neighbouring Machrihanish Airbase, inaugurated in 1936, is renowned as an exceptional gliding site and welcomes more than 200 glider pilots each year. The local landscape also supports a wide variety of plant and animal life. Local wildlife includes red deer, cetaceans, otters, ospreys and various migratory birds. Botanists are also attracted to the area by the presence of rare species of wildflowers on the hillsides. Today, Machrihanish is a popular holiday destination, with many people drawn to its beautiful scenery and laid-back lifestyle. Whether you’re looking for a relaxing holiday or an outdoor adventure, Machrihanish is an idyllic destination.

The European Rugby Champions Cup is the top-level pan-European professional rugby union club competition which exists to determine the continent's best club rugby team each year. Organized by European Professional Club Rugby (EPCR), the competition was first established in 2014. It replaced the former Heineken Cup, which ran from 1995 to 2014, as the strongest European club rugby competition. The competition is contested by teams from the six main European domestic leagues: the English Premiership, French Top 14, Guinness Pro14 (comprising teams from Ireland, Italy, Scotland, and Wales), and the two main Spanish divisions, the División de Honor and División de Honor Femenina. The current champions are French side La Rochelle, who beat Toulouse in the 2021 final. The Champions Cup involves 20 teams competing in five Pool stages, where each Pool is contested by four teams. Each team plays one another in home and away fixtures, with the three highest-ranked teams in each Pool progressing to the knockout stages of the tournament. At the end of the Pool stages, the top two teams from each and the two third-placed teams with the most tournament points progress to the quarter final stage. The knockout stages are single-elimination, with a single-legged semifinal, followed by the European Rugby Champions Cup Final. The ultimate winners of the tournament are rewarded with the European Rugby Champions Cup Trophy, which is a silver cup modelled on the original design from the Heineken Cup. The Champions Cup also encompasses various awards. These include Player of the Tournament, Top Points Scorer, Top Try Scorer, and several other awards determined by the EPCR. The tournament is widely considered to be one of the best of its kind in the world, and has become internationally celebrated since its inception in 2014. It is followed avidly throughout Europe, Asia, and Oceania, with many fans attending the final each year. In addition to the rugby, the weekend of the Champions Cup Final often hosts other events including concerts, entertainment, and the winners’ presentation ceremony. This adds to the occasion, making it an even more memorable one for players and supporters alike.

Eeva-Kaarina Aronen (born August 1, 1965) is a Finnish diplomat and politician who has served in many roles in the Finnish government, most recently as Ambassador to Armenia and Head of the OSCE Mission to Serbia.
