She has held several posts in the Finnish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, as Director of Education Policy in 2001 and as Director General of the United Nations and Security Policy Department in 2004. Aronen was born inTampere, Finland and studied law at the University of Tampere and international relations at the University of Helsinki. She began her career in the Finnish government in 1988 as an administrative expert in the Ministry for Foreign Affairs, and in 1994 was appointed as the Director of the Political Department at the Finnish Embassy in Moscow. In 1997, Aronen was appointed as the Attaché for Political Affairs in the Embassy of Finland in Washington D.C., followed by her role as Deputy Head of Mission in the Embassy of Finland in Lagos from 1997 to 2000. She then returned to the MFA headquarters in Helsinki to serve as Director of Education Policy from 2001 to 2004. She then moved to the OSCE mission to Serbia as Ambassador in 2004 and held the post till 2009. Aronen has been a highly respected international civil servant due to her leadership and expertise in complex political issues. She has served on many boards and committees, including the International Commissions of the Nordic Council of Ministers, the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), the International Crisis Group, and the NATO Parliamentary Assembly. Additionally, she has been a senior advisor to the Finnish President in International Organizations and chairs the Saferglobe Finland Network. Presently, Aronen serves as Special Adviser to the President of the Republic of Finland on International Organizations and Foreign Policy. She has held this post since 2018, and has managed initiatives on Security and Development, strengthening the European Union, and preserving the international Arctic order. Throughout her career, Aronen has been a strong advocate for the promotion of human rights, sustainable development, and gender equality. She has written on these topics, and her work has been widely recognized and praised.

The List of Honours of Estonia Awarded to Heads of State and Royalty is a compilation of medals and titles given to the heads of state and royalty of foreign nations as recognition and reward for cooperation and services rendered to the Republic of Estonia. These honours are awarded to foreign monarchs, presidents and other significant individuals by the President of Estonia, or on behalf of the President by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or relevant minister. The most notable award is the Order of the Cross of the Eagle, which is the highest-ranking order of Estonia and is awarded to foreign heads of state and members of royal families. It is usually supplemented by the Order of the White Star, another statutory order of the Republic of Estonia. Other honours awarded include the Order of the National Coat of Arms, which is a decoration that recognises outstanding services to Estonia; the Order of the Cross of Terra Mariana, which is an order to recognise civil and military merit; the Order for Merits to Estonia, which is a decoration for services in the interest of Estonia; the Medal of Merit, which rewards those who have merit for the state; and the Medal for Services to Estonian National Culture, which is awarded for a special contribution to Estonian culture. The honours awarded by Estonia to foreign heads of state and royalty are often additional to those from other nations. For example, the King of Sweden was awarded the Order of the Cross of the Eagle on behalf of the President of Estonia in 2005, in addition to the Order of the Seraphim. The President of Bulgaria was awarded the Order of the National Coat of Arms in 2007, in addition to the Order of Civil Merit. The honours awarded by Estonia are generally seen as an essential part of diplomatic relations, and an expression of gratitude and respect that helps to build strong bonds between countries. The medals and awards given by the Republic of Estonia to esteemed foreign heads of state and royalty are a further demonstration of the efforts and commitment to friendly international cooperation.

Debra Houry is an American medical doctor and public health advocate who serves as the Director of the National Center for Injury Prevention and Control at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). She is an emergency medicine physician and injury prevention specialist who has worked since 1997 to reduce deaths from unintentional injuries, such as motor vehicle crashes, falls, burns, drownings, and poisoning. Houry is National Chair of the Injury Free Coalition for Kids, a national alliance of children's hospital-based injury prevention programs. Houry was born in 1968 in Toronto, Ontario and raised in Lod, Israel and Montreal, Quebec. She holds an Ontario Secondary School Diploma and Certificat d’ete duprogramme de francais de McGill Universite. She received her doctor of Medicine M.D. degree from Emory University School of Medicine in Atlanta, Ga and completed her residency in emergency medicine at Denver Health Medical Center in 1997. She was board certified in emergency medicine and a fellow of the American College of Emergency Physicians from 1998 to 2002. Houry is also trained as an injury prevention fellow and holds a Master of Public Health (MPH) degree from the University of Texas School of Public Health in Houston TX and a Master of Science (MS) degree in Clinical Epidemiology from the Graduate Program in Public Health at the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences in Little Rock AR. In October of 2002, Houry served as the medical director for injury prevention at Denver Health and Hospitals and associate professor in the Department of Emergency Medicine at the University of Colorado School of Medicine in Denver. Houry joined CDC in 2007 as Associate Director for Science within CDC's National Center for Injury Prevention and Control. She served as Deputy Director in charge of the Division of Violence Prevention from 2008-2015. In September 2017 Houry became the Director of the CDC's National Center for Injury Prevention and Control. In 2017, Houry was recognized as one of the 20 Influential innovators in Injury Prevention, along with other pioneers, by the CDC Foundation. Her awards include the 2013 CDC Health Champion Award, the National Prevention Award by the American College of Emergency Physicians in 2012, and the AHRQ Research Network Patient safety Award in 2011. She also received the Ohio Chapter of the American College of Emergency Medicine Public Service Award in 2009. Houry's research interests include injury epidemiology and prevention, adolescent health services, school health, and the social determinants of health. She is an active contributor in the United States Department of Homeland Security working group to prevent and prepare for targeted violence and published a formative study about surveillance for intentional injuries in academic emergency departments. Houry appears in the media and gives lectures on injury prevention topics. She also serves as a board member of several organizations, and is the National Chair of the Injury Free Coalition for Kids, a national alliance of children’s hospital- based injury prevention programs. In her free time, Houry enjoys spending time with her family, reading books, and playing the banjo.

Jim Otvos (born May 25, 1967) is an American entrepreneur and venture capitalist best known for founding and managing several venture capital funds, including Mayfield Fund, Onset Ventures, and Draper Fisher Jurvetson. He is also the founder and former CEO of PortablePeople.com, an online job search site. Otvos was born in San Francisco, California to Hungarian parents. After graduating from Menlo School in Atherton, California, he attended the University of California, Berkeley where he studied engineering and economics. After graduating, he went to work for a San Francisco-based venture capital firm. It was during this time that he developed an interest in venture capital and entrepreneurship. In 1995, he founded his first venture capital firm, Mayfield Fund, which specialized in early stage technology investments. The fund grew to be one of the leading VC firms in the Silicon Valley with investments in numerous high tech companies, including Hotmail and Netflix. Otvos then co-founded Onset Ventures in 1999 and Draper Fisher Jurvetson in 2000. In 2003, Otvos founded PortablePeople.com, an online job search site that allowed users to more easily search for jobs. The company rapidly gained a following and was bought by Indeed in 2007. In 2007, Otvos co-founded Luxury Retreats International, Inc. (LRI), a vacation rental company specializing in high-end, luxurious vacation homes. The company has properties in North America, Europe, Central America, and the Caribbean. Throughout his career, Otvos has received numerous awards and accolades for his technology investments and entrepreneurial endeavors. He was named one of the Top 25 Venture Investors by Forbes Magazine in 2012, and has twice been a member of the Forbes Midas List, which recognizes the best venture capital investors in the world. In 2013, he was named a Fellow for the Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation’s Entrepreneurial Leaders for Global Competitiveness program, which honors individuals for making a positive impact on global economic competitiveness. Today, Otvos resides in the San Francisco Bay Area where he continues to work as a venture capitalist and mentor to aspiring entrepreneurs. He is also a board member of the American Hungarian Foundation.

Dominic Schroeder (born June 8th, 1998) is an American musician, songwriter and record producer from Los Angeles, California. A multi-instrumentalist, Schroeder also performs lead vocals in many of his projects. Early life Schroeder was born and raised in Los Angeles, where he studied music from an early age. He attended the University of Southern California, where he studied jazz guitar, piano and composition. He was a member of the USC Thornton Jazz Ensemble and performed at various clubs and events around Los Angeles. His influences include classical, rock and jazz music. Career Schroeder's career began in 2016 when he formed the indie rock band Ghost Roads. The band released their self-titled debut album in 2017, featuring the hit single “The Other Way”, which was produced and co-written by Schroeder. The success of the album led to multiple tours throughout the United States and Europe. In 2018, Schroeder released his debut solo album, Free Love, which was praised for its innovative production and songwriting. He followed up with the EP It's All Good, which was produced with grammy winning producer Teddy Rajah. The album featured collaborations with a wide array of music tastemakers including Eric Clapton and Jamie Foxx. In 2019 Schroeder released the critically acclaimed album We Keep Dreaming, featuring the single “Can't Turn it Around”. The album featured production from the likes of Flying Lotus and Mark Ronson. On June 26th 2020, Schroeder released the album Film on the Horizon. The album features production from progressive French artist Thylacine and features the single “Below”, which is accompanied by a feature length documentary of the same name. Schroeder continues to produce and create innovative music, while also performing across the globe. Discography Albums * Ghost Roads (2017) * Free Love (2018) * We Keep Dreaming (2019) * Film on the Horizon (2020) EPs * It's All Good (2018)

Colonial Forge High School is a comprehensive public high school located in Stafford, Virginia. It is the only secondary educational facility in the Stafford County Public Schools, which serves grades 9 through 12. Opened in 1998, the school serves the areas of Stafford, Falmouth, Brooke, and Aquia Harbour, as well as parts of southern Prince William County. The student body consists of over 2,000 students in the 2019–20 school year. The mission of Colonial Forge High School is to inspire, challenge, and motivate each student to achieve their highest potential through opportunities to participate in diverse educational experiences. Established values of respect, responsibility, and integrity guide students on their pathway to success. The school offers a variety of coursework and advanced academic programs, including AP classes and college-level classes offered by partnerships with local universities. The school also offers a wide variety of extracurricular activities for students to participate in, including athletics, performing and visual arts, student publications, and community service opportunities. Students also have the opportunity to join over 40 student-run clubs, including FBLA and DECA. Colonial Forge High School has earned recognition from U.S. News & World Report, being ranked #7 in Virginia and #234 in the nation. The school has a college-readiness rating of 47.2, and offers a variety of college-preparatory programs and resources for students to help with their transition to college. The athletic program has also achieved success with their teams consistently winning district championships. Colonial Forge High School has worked to build a strong and committed community through its events and initiatives, from themed spirit Weeks to the school's annual "Grateful" Day. On Grateful Day, students and staff join together to recognize and show appreciation for their School and community. The school’s motto is “Student Achievement is Our Plan” which serves as a reminder to every student and staff member to take all the necessary steps to ensure that all students are receiving the best education possible. This motto, combined with a strong community, has forged a successful school that continues to strive for educational excellence.

Karachi is the largest city in Pakistan and one of the most populous cities in the world. With a rich history spanning centuries, Karachi has been the economic capital of Pakistan since independence from the British in 1947. The roots of Karachi go back to the ancient city of Kolachi, located on the coast of the Arabian Sea in Sindh province. Kolachi is said to have been founded in 1729 when various Balochi, Pashtun, and Omani settlers first made the land their home. The city remained in relative obscurity until the British colonization of India in 1839, when it was developed and modernized by the British and became the principal trading port of British India. In 1901, the old city of Kolachi was incorporated into the larger Municipality of Karachi, which was established by the British. This marked the beginning of large-scale urbanization of the city, with the creation of grand public parks, modern architecture, and public institutions. From this point, Karachi began to grow rapidly, becoming the center of politics, industry, and commerce in the newly formed nation of Pakistan after the partition of British India in 1947. During the 1940s and '50s, Karachi witnessed one of its most prosperous periods under the rule of its first mayor, Seth Harchandrai Vishandas. He implemented various long-term economic and social development projects such as reorganizing Banarasi Bazaar, building new parks, and introducing a number of factories in the city. This helped Karachi to enter an era of spectacular economic and population growth. Karachi has experienced a wide range of political upheavals over the years, from sectarian riots in the 1980s to a decades-long military operation by the Pakistani army against Taliban insurgents, which was initiated in 2014. Despite the many challenges, the economic and social progress of the city continues and is being further embellished by the initiatives of the current mayor, Wasim Akhtar. In recent decades, Karachi has emerged as one of the most important cities in South Asia, serving as the commercial and financial hub of Pakistan. As of 2019, Karachi is the second-most populous city in the world, with an estimated 20 million people. It is also a major transport and industrial center with a large international seaport and a modern international airport. The city continues to embark on a journey of development, encompassing many public and private projects with the aim of achieving an even better standard of living for its inhabitants. The future of Karachi undoubtedly looks bright.

Abdoulkader Cissé is a Cape Verdean football player who plays professionally in the Primeira Liga, the top tier of Portuguese football. He currently plays for Varzim S.C. as a defender. Cissé was born on 7 August 1987 in Praia, the capital of Cape Verde. After beginning his career with local side Boavista FC, he moved to Europe and had brief stints with ES Sétif and Portimonense S.C. in Algeria and Portugal respectively. Cissé moved to the Primeira Liga with Varzim S.C in 2010, and became a regular in the team's defence. His performances for the northern side saw him called up to the Cape Verde national side for two friendlies against Algeria and Tunisia in 2011. He also represented his nation at the 2013 and 2015 African Cup of Nations tournaments. During his time with Varzim, Cissé helped the side achieve consecutive promotions from the Liga de Honra in 2011-12 to the Primeira Liga in 2013-14. He was also part of the team that secured the club’s best-ever performance in the Primeira Liga, finishing 12th in 2015-16. Cissé is known for his speed, technique and attacking spirit when playing out of defence. Despite his physicality and aggressive reputation, he has a high disciplinary record, having only been shown the red card on one occasion in his career so far. Off the pitch, Cissé is a highly respected figure among his team mates and the wider Cape Verdean community. He devotes much of his free time to helping vulnerable children in his homeland, and is renowned for his humility and honesty in all facets of his life.

The 1989 German Grand Prix was the penultimate round of the 1989 FIM Grand Prix motorcycle racing season, held over the weekend of August 19th – 20th, 1989 at the Sachsenring, in Germany. It was the twelfth round of the season in the 500cc class. The 500cc Grand Prix commenced with Yamaha rider, Eddie Lawson, winning the pole position by a tenth of a second over the Honda of local rider, Dieter Braun. Panasonic Riders Wayne Gardner and Kevin Schwantz and Dutch rider Wilco Zeelenberg rounded out the front row. Lawson won the race from Gardner, who was running second, but was unable to challenge Lawson due to a back injury he had sustained earlier in the race. Schwantz took third followed by Luca Cadalora, who had come from a lowly 15th on the grid. Keiji Kinoshita put in a good performance, the Japanese rider finishing 18th on a borrowed FZR. Fortuna Yamaha's Christian Sarron recovered from a start line crash to finish outside the points, in 16th, having contested the entire race on just one soft rear tyre. Mónica Rivola also had a crash but managed to finish the race in 13th. The 1989 German Grand Prix podium overall was Lawson, Gardner, and Schwantz, giving the 1989 World Champion Graham Russell his third podium finish in a row. This race marked the last time that Suzuki would win a 500cc Grand Prix race until the 1999 German Grand Prix, when Kenny Roberts Jr. won for the team. This iconic race, held in 1989, marked the start of a pivotal decade in the world of Grand Prix motorcycle racing that included the rise to prominence of the Honda Grand Prix racing team, new riders, and multiple changes to the regulations and the rules of the sport. It also marked the end of an era, with the retirement of Sarron at the end of the year, who had been one of the most successful riders in recent years.

Vernon Prichard (1876-1944) was an American-Canadian industrial worker who is best remembered for his inventiveness in the area of torque measuring devices. Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania in 1876, Prichard moved to Ontario, Canada in 1916. Prichard worked at various factories as a manual laborer during his time in Ontario. It was during this time that he became inspired to invent something related to measuring torque. Between 1916 and 1918, he had developed several prototype devices which he sold to local machine shops. Prichard's most successful invention was the "Prichard Torque Meter," which was capable of measuring torque in both metric and imperial systems. This device was the first of its kind and was used in factories and machine shops across North America. The design of the meter was quite simple. It features a large base which is filled with a measured amount of oil, a spring-loaded piston, and a dial which is calibrated to measure torque in either metric or imperial units. It also had a pressure gauge which allowed the user to measure and control the pressure at which the spring-loaded piston operated. This made it a very accurate and reliable device. Throughout the 1920s and 1930s, Prichard sold the device to various companies, and his success as an inventor made him a well-known figure in Ontario. Eventually, he received several patents for his inventions, including one for the Torque Meter. After his death in 1944, his sons continued to manufacture the device, and it is still in production today. The work of Vernon Prichard is an important example of how a humble manual laborer can use his knowledge and resourcefulness to develop something which has become an important tool for industrial manufacturing. His invention helped revolutionize the way in which torque is measured, and it is still in use today. This is a testament to the legacy that Prichard left behind, and the influence he has had on the manufacturing industry for more than a century.

Asensio Nebot is a Spanish painter, sculptor, and artist. He was born in Barcelona, Spain in 1963. He is known for his abstract expressionism and cubism influence in his work. Nebot attended the Escola de Belles Arts de Barcelona from 1981-1986 and the Universitat de Barcelona from 1988-1991. From 1992-1993 he studied at the Parsons School of Design in New York. Nebot's artwork has been showcased in solo and group exhibitions in Europe, Japan, and the United States. Some of his solo exhibitions include Cèrvoles i Carabasses at Sala Vinçon in Barcelona (2003), A tres bandes, at the Fundació Tarrés in Barcelona, and Traces at Galeria Sergi Arola in Madrid (2012). Nebot utilizes various painting techniques to create his work, often blending together multiple sets of media. He often uses oil paint, collage painting, paper cuttings, and sketches among other materials. Utilizing these elements of painting Nebot often depicts the figure in an abstracted form. Along with these abstract works of art, Nebot also works with sculpture and jewelry making from found objects, which he frequently incorporates into his paintings. Nebot is currently based in Barcelona, however he continues to travel around the world for inspiration for his art. In addition to creating artwork for galleries and museums, Nebot also designs for private clients. His artwork can be found in galleries and collections around the world, including the Agarwal Collection, the Lizana Collection, and the Mir Foundation. Throughout his career, Nebot has received numerous accolades, including the Foundation Tarrés Prize in 2005 and the “Artista pro” Talent Prize from Caja Madrid in 2009. Nebot has also been featured in both art magazines and newspapers like El Mundo and El País. He has held various teaching positions in universities, such as the Universitat de Barcelona, EINA, and the Art Center Saint Martial.

The NIU College of Visual and Performing Arts (CVPA) at Northern Illinois University is a unique educational experience for aspiring theatre, visual arts, and media arts students. Founded in 1960, CVPA has consistently been a leader in the region for providing high-quality arts education and serving students from Northern Illinois and beyond. The college has a deep history of providing students with access to top-notch faculty, state-of-the-art facilities, and a deep commitment to enhancing opportunities for artistic and cultural expression of diverse populations. The college houses five departments - Art, Art History, Music, Theatre and Dance, and Media Arts - offering the largest selection of arts-related degrees and programs in the region. Additionally, CVPA offers an extensive list of courses to students of all majors and an active College which houses student organizations and ensembles dedicated to creating a vibrant and engaging student experience. At CVPA, students have the opportunity to experience some of the best faculty and staff who are experts in their fields. Faculty members are highly accomplished professionals who are also active in the local and regional creative communities. With the expertise of its dedicated professors, CVPA provides a rigorous learning environment and prepares its students for a diverse range of careers in the visual and performing arts. The college is also committed to providing enriching cultural events for the surrounding communities. CVPA has two on-campus performing arts venues, an array of exhibits and gallery spaces, and affiliates with a diverse range of organizations and institutions which bring music, theatre and dance to NIU and the surrounding region. CVPA is not just a place for learning, but also a home for students who want to make an impact. The college provides incentives, internships and research projects to help students hone their skills and become leaders in their chosen field. CVPA is a place for learning, collaboration, and creative exploration. With the right combination of faculty, resources, and opportunities, CVPA ensures that its students have the tools they need to succeed in the visual and performing arts. NIU College of Visual and Performing Arts is home to a diverse group of visual and performing arts students who are transforming the creative landscape of the region and beyond.

Basto (1716–1736) was a British Thoroughbred racehorse who was bred, foaled, and owned by Charles Dutton, 2nd Baron Sherborne. He is notable as the foundation sire and eponym of the Sherborne racehorse stud, and is one of the few sires to have impacted British thoroughbred racing over a century after his death. Basto was sired by the 1690 Byerley Turk stallion, Hobgoblin, out of Hobgoblin's Scottish-bred daughter, the Red Colin mare. His sire was a successful runner in the early 1890s, winning several races, including the Steward's Cup at Epsom. He then went on to sire a number of notable runners, among them Basto. Basto's racing career began when he was four years old, in 1720. He won several races while under the ownership of the 2nd Baron Sherborne, his most notable victory coming in 1721 when he won the King's Plate race, held at Newmarket. This race was one of the premier events for the year's racing season, and Basto stood among a field of 18, showing an impressive ability to finish first despite a large crowd and strong competition. He retired from active competition at the end of 1722. However, Basto's legacy as a sire soon overshadowed his racing career. His progeny, which included Theobald, a successful runner in the 1750s, as well as a number of successful sires, would be instrumental in developing the Sherborne racehorse stud. The stud was inherited by Lord Sherborne's descendant, John Dutton, 5th Baron Sherborne in the early 19th century. Dutton's introduction of many of Basto's direct descendants such as Allin, Pattern, Topper, Jack Andrews, and Black-and-White lead to the founding of the modern thoroughbred breed in England. Basto died in 1736, at the age of twenty. While his own racing career may not have been spectacular, his legacy as a sire, and the foundation sire of the Sherborne Stud, is indelible in the annals of British thoroughbred racing history, and his presence is still felt in the sturdy, bold, and consistent thoroughbreds of today.

. Great Naval Battles: North Atlantic 1939-1943 refers to a series of engagements fought during World War II in the North Atlantic region between the Allied forces and Germany's Kriegsmarine. These battles played a major role in deciding the outcome of the war as the Allies had to secure their supply lines across the Atlantic in order to maintain their offensive against the Axis forces. The battles began with the Battle of the Atlantic, one of the longest campaigns of the war. This was an Allied attempt to prevent Axis forces from cutting off their supply lines. The Royal Navy and its allies had to contend with German U-boats, surface raiders, aircraft, and mines. The Royal Canadian Navy also played an important role in the conflict, particularly in defending convoys from German attacks. The Allies used new tactics, such as the convoy system, in order to try to protect their shipping. This was also aided by the use of new technologies, including improved radar and sonar. Despite these improvements, the Germans were able to damage and sink hundreds of ships in the Atlantic, delaying the Allies’ progress. The Battle of the North Atlantic, which began in January 1943, saw a dramatic shift in the balance of power. The Allies had developed new tactics and newer technology, such as HF/DF or “Huff-Duff” and “hedgehog” antisubmarine weapons. In response, the Germans changed their tactics to remote-controlled torpedoes and sent their forces east to the Azores and West to the Caribbean. The Battle of the Bay of Biscay proved to be one of the major turning points of the war. In June 1943, the British and Canadian Navies, working together as one unit, intercepted and destroyed a large portion of the German U-boat force. This marked the end of German dominance in the North Atlantic and, consequently, the end of their ability to cut off Allied supply lines. The Allied victory in the North Atlantic helped hasten the end of the war. The battles were some of the most important of the conflict and secured the supply lines necessary for Allied success. The North Atlantic culminated in the 1943 Allied victory in the Battle of the Atlantic and was a major factor in the Allies’ ultimate victory in 1945.

Andy Karl (born 1965) is an American stage and film actor, singer, and dancer. Karl is best known for his Broadway roles, in particular his Tony Award-nominated performance in the 2003 revival of Stephen Sondheim's musical, Nine. Karl is also known for his supporting role in the 2011 American romantic comedy-drama film, No Strings Attached, and for playing the role of 'Don Lockwood' in the Broadway production of Singin' in the Rain. Karl was born in Maryland in 1965 and began to develop an interest in performing at an early age, enrolling in the John F. Kennedy Center for Performing Arts as a child. He attended the University of the Arts in Philadelphia to study dance, before leaving to pursue a career in theatre. He made his Broadway debut in the role of 'Sandy dean' in the musical, The Story of My Life in 2002. Later the same year, Karl was nominated for a Tony Award for Best Actor in Musical for his performance in the Stephen Sondheim revival of Nine. He also starred in Legally Blonde: The Musical, where he played the role of 'Emmet Forrest'. His portrayal of 'Emmet Forrest' was widely acclaimed, resulting in Karl winning a Theatre World Award and being nominated for the Laurence Olivier Award in 2013. Karl has since gone on to perform in several other Broadway and off-Broadway productions, including Rock of Ages, On the Twentieth Century, 1776, and Rocky. Karl's film credits include No Strings Attached and Kansas City (2003), in which he starred opposite Olympia Dukakis and Steve Buscemi. Karl made his Broadway debut as 'Don Lockwood/Cosmo Brown' in Singin' in the Rain in 2012 and received critical acclaim for his performance. He then starred in Groundhog Day, where he played 'Phil Connors', a role which earned Karl his second Tony nomination. His stage and screen credits include: Sunday in the Park with George, Evita, Jersey Boys, Pretty Woman the Musical, and Grease Live! Karl is married to the actress Orfeh, with whom he has been working professionally since 2003. The couple have performed together in numerous productions, including The Story of My Life, Saturday Night Fever, and Legally Blonde. They also appear in the 2018 concert, Legends in Concert, alongside Motown stars Martha Reeves, Kiki Dee, and William Bell. Karl is highly renowned for his professionalism and graciousness both on and off the stage, and has won numerous awards including Drama Desk Awards, Drama League Award and an Outer Critics Circle Award. Andy Karl continues to be one of the most celebrated and sought-after actors on both the stage and the screen. His work has been appreciated and enjoyed by millions of audience members across the world.

The Beijing Weather Modification Office (BWMO) is the Chinese capital's official weather-modification agency, established by the National Meteorological Bureau (NMC) and the Ministry of Water Resources of the People's Republic of China. Established in 1958, the aim of the office is to modify the weather in and around Beijing by altering the atmosphere and cloud cover. Its methods include cloud seeding and rain inducement. The main focus of the BWMC is on rainfall, with a focus on enhancing precipitation and helping control flooding, droughts and fires. The office is responsible for monitoring various meteorological elements and data such as temperature, humidity, pressure and rainfall. It works in partnership with the Beijing Meteorological Bureau (BMB) in monitoring and analyzing data from meteorological remote sensing, radar and other equipment to accurately assess weather in the Beijing metropolitan area. The BWMO's "Planned Weather Modification System" uses cloud seeding and rain inducement techniques to try to control and enhance rainfall to benefit agricultural activities and help with flood control. Through 'induced rainfall' techniques, cloud seeding techniques hope to increase the amount of precipitation in an area by introducing a material, usually silver iodide, into the atmosphere of rising clouds. Rainfall induced technology is used in the Beijing area, particularly the rivers and reservoirs, in order to increase the amount of water in the reservoirs at times of drought. The office also helps reduce hail damages, by disrupting the formation of hail and hail clouds. The Beijing Weather Modification Office is relatively new, in comparison with other international weather-modification agencies. The effectiveness of the office's weather-modification techniques have been widely disputed, with some experts and government officials saying it cannot produce unnatural weather, or alter the severity or course of a storm. Others say that, thought it cannot control weather, it can enhance the efficiency of natural influences, and re-distribute precipitation in an area. The office implements a number of policies to ensure that its weather-modification activities comply with Chinese and international laws. Weather Modification is regulated by the Chinese Meteorological Bureau and by the Ministry of Water Resources, with all activities strictly monitored, carefully planned, and regularly evaluated. Despite its controversial techniques, the office continues to operate and is a very important part of the Chinese government's weather management initiatives.

Chin Injeti is a Canadian emcee, producer, and songwriter who has released a number of albums and singles since emerging in 1998. His discography includes five studio albums and a number of singles, collaborations, and instrumental albums. In 1998, Injeti released his first album, Don't Touch the Flatline EP, on Lithium Records. The album, produced entirely by Injeti, featured tracks by Guru, Wordsworth, and El Da Sensei. The following year, Injeti collaborated with turntablist DJ Flipout to release Sofa Surfin' on Beat Factory Records. In 2001, Injeti released his second album, In Control Vol 1. The album featured guest appearances from Planet Asia, One Big E, Da Grassroots, and Self Scientific. It was yet another of Injeti's self-produced projects and was released to critical acclaim. In 2003, Injeti released his third album, Pluggin' Into the Socket, on Battle Axe/Nettwerk Records. The album featured guests MCs such as Sadat X, Planet Asia, and Ras Kass. In 2006, Injeti signed with East West Records and released his fourth album, Elixir Vol. 1. The album featured production work from Illmind, DJ Ace, Tone Mason and others. In 2011, Injetti released his fifth album, Jealousy, on Upstairs Music. The album premiered at the Calgary International Reggae Festival and featured guests like Dutch Robinson, Empathy and B.A.N.G. In 2015, Injeti released an instrumental album titled Polaris. The album was composed of instrumentals Injeti had been working on since 1998 and was released via Upstairs Music. Since then, Injeti has released a number of singles and remixes, including "Let It Flow" featuring Masta Ace and "That's Real" featuring Slakah the Beatchild. Injeti continues to produce music, working with a number of artists in the hip hop and R&B genres. His discography thus far consists of five studio albums, one instrumental album, a handful of collaborations, and a number of singles and remixes. He is one of Canada's most prolific producers, with a long and varied discography showcasing his versatile production talents.

Ali Sardar Jafri (15 December 1913 – 13 July 2000) was an Indian Urdu poet, film lyricist, and scriptwriter. He was one of the most significant figures of the Progressive Writers Movement in 20th-century India. He is considered to be one of the most celebrated poet in Urdu literature, and was honoured with the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1964 for his collection of poems entitled, Gul-e-Naghma. Jafri was born in Musariya, Uttar Pradesh in 1913, and grew up in Allahabad. After studying Islamic history and philosophy, he joined the Nationalist Movement in Allahabad and later became a member of the Muslim League. He soon developed an interest in literature and started writing poetry in Urdu language. He also began writing plays and scripts for films. During the 1940s and 1950s, he wrote several memorable poems, which were widely read and immensely popular. His collection of poems, "Gul-e-Naghma", was published in 1950 and was honored with the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1964. Jafri was involved in the Indian People’s Theatre Association (IPTA) from 1939, and was active in the world of progressive literature and film writing. He was involved in writing the scripts of many remarkable movies such as Daag (1949), Deedar (1951), Mughal-E-Azam (1960), and Ganga Jamuna (1962). He wrote poetry for many films and was also associated with playing lead roles in some of the movies. Jafri was also a cultural activist and an active member of various literary organizations. He was one of the advisory editors of the famous Urdu literary magazine, Ravi. Jafri was deeply influenced by the thought and the ideas of progressive writers and social and political movements. He wrote poems about the aspiration of the common man and the struggles of the economically weaker sections of society. Jafri was also a great humanitarian and remained involved in social and charitable activities and causes throughout his life. Jafri died on 13 July 2000 after a prolonged illness. He will always be remembered for his immense contribution to the world of Urdu literature and his passionate dedication to the empowerment of the less privileged sections of society. He is an inspiration to the future generations of poets and artists who wish to follow in his footsteps.

Henning Alexander von Kleist (30 April 1761 – 13 November 1831) was a Prussian nobleman and soldier who served as an officer in the Prussian Army during the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars. Kleist was born in Pomerania, the son of a cavalry officer who served in the Brandenburg-Prussian Army and his wife, who was of the noble von Caprivi family descended from the Line of Gostyn. He was descended from a long line of warriors and was related to several of Prussia's leading generals and statesmen. Kleist joined the army of Prussia in 1779, rising in rank within a few years and seeinng action in the Netherlands and on the Rhine. In 1795, he was promoted to major and appointed adjutant to the commander of the Prussian Corps in the French Revolutionary Wars, General Yorck von Wartenburg. In 1793, he fought in the Battle of Kaiserslautern and took part in a daring raid on the French camp of Charleroi. Eventually, he was promoted to lieutenant-colonel and then colonel. He participated in the successful Prussian campaign of 1806, and went on to fight in the battles of Eylau and Friedland. In 1808, he was made a general-major and became a Divisional commander of a brigade at Heilsberg and Guttstadt. In 1809, he took part in the battles at Lutzen and Bautzen. It was shortly before the Battle of Leipzig in 1813 that Kleist was awarded the Pour le Mérite, Prussia's highest honor, for his actions at Lützen. Kleist continued to display his bravery during the War of Liberation of 1813–14, distinguishing himself at Waterloo and commanding the entrenchments at Laon. Kleist was appointed chief of staff to Prince August of Prussia in 1830. He was made a Baron of the Royal House of Prussia four years later. Kleist died on 13 November 1831 and was buried at Templin. Kleist's memorial monument in the Town Hall of Neustrelitz depicts him holding a flag in his right hand, with the words: “Here lies the loyal Henning von Kleist, Field Marshal of Infantry, Baron of Prussia and beloved Knight of the Iron Cross, he who served Prussia valiantly and bravely against all invaders, 1831.” The Prussian Army honored General von Kleist by naming several barracks and regiments after him. The 8th Leib Infantry Regiment, founded in 1808, bears General von Kleist's name. As of 2010, the 8th Leib Infantry Regiment was still serving in Prussia.

Tntnet is an open-source web application server and web development framework developed by Christian Schoen in 1998. It is written in C++ and runs on a variety of platforms, including Linux, Windows, and Mac OS X. In addition to supporting all major scripting languages, including PHP and JavaScript, tntnet also allows developers to write applications in C++. Tntnet is designed with component-based architecture, allowing developers to quickly assemble web applications from a variety of components. Tntnet is an extensible architecture, allowing developers to write their own components and libraries in C++. Tntnet has a modular design that allows developers to choose which features they want, and fits seamlessly into existing applications. It strives to be a low-footprint server, consuming minimal resources. Its small size and portability make tntnet ideal for embedded systems and projects with limited resources. Tntnet's API enables developers to quickly and easily build their own web applications. The API includes support for moderntemplates that allow developers to separate HTML and CSS from the application logic. Developers can also access the internal tntnet API and use its components to create applications with additional functionality. The tntnet distribution contains a number of included components, such as GNU TLS for secure connections, FastCGI and SOAP support, and session management. The components are built as libraries, allowing developers to link them directly into their applications. Tntnet is continuously maintained and actively developed, with new features and bug fixes being released on a regular basis. The source code is available under a free software license. Tntnet is well-documented, with a mailing list for support and a number of example applications included in the distribution. Tntnet is an open-source web application server and web development framework for creating dynamic web applications on a variety of platforms. Its component-based architecture, low resource usage, and range of included components make tntnet an ideal framework for building powerful and competitive web applications.

MT9 is a computer numerical control (CNC) machining technology used in the production of parts and components for industrial and commercial applications. Developed by Japanese manufacturer Ishikawa Technology Co. Ltd, this technology is based on a combination of CNC, CAD/CAM software and automated data processing. The MT9 system is a complete machine-tool package which includes a variety of subsystems and tools, including CAD/CAM software, a machining center, an automated material handling system and an automated data processing system. It is used by companies for the production of complicated parts on CNC machines and for automated production of simple to complex parts on either milling or turning machines. This technology also allows for the customization of parts through the creation of customized CAD/CAM programs. The system has the capability of producing very precise parts, as well as parts with complex geometries, with the aid of its automated data-processing software. This software is designed to analyze the dimensions of the part required and then automatically create the CAD/CAM program for production. The system also allows for the pause and resume feature of the machining process, which allows for the production of complex parts with multiple operations. In addition to its production capacity, the MT9 technology also offers comprehensive training programs and technical support. Its comprehensive training programs include a number of modules that cover topics such as CNC machine operation, machining processes and software use. Technical support consists of ongoing technical assistance, repair and maintenance, tool testing and product demonstrations. MT9 CNC machining technology is a growing industry, especially among businesses that need to produce parts with complex geometries or need to complete multiple operations in a short amount of time. It is considered a cost-effective and efficient way to produce parts, with high precision and repeatability. The advantages of using this technology are that it is accurate, reliable, fast and can produce complex parts with ease. Since its first introduction in 1996, the MT9 system has gained popularity due to its unmatched precision, versatility and cost-effectiveness. As it continues to evolve and become integrated into more fields, its applications are likely to expand further. This article is written based on the Wikipedia Version "MT9".

: Inez Y. Kaiser (1893-1969) was an American singer, pianist, composer, and arranger. She is best known for her work on popular recordings from 1930s to 1950s including such hits as "The Music Goes Round and Round" (1935), "What a Man" (1944), and "Don't Take Your Love From Me" (1950). Born in St. Joseph, Missouri to Jewish immigrants, Kaiser moved to Kansas City in 1898. Although largely self-taught, she was a musical prodigy and began performing in public by the age of 11, forming her own orchestra at age 13. She was offered a scholarship to study music in Chicago, but her family could not afford for her to attend. In 1923, Kaiser moved to New York City and began recording soundtracks for silent films. She continued producing soundtracks for several years before turning to composing popular music. Her most successful period was the late 1930s to early 1950s, working with the likes of Benny Goodman, Louis Armstrong, Fats Waller, and Billie Holiday. Her songs were often used as a backdrop for Lindy hop dances and found success on the charts. Kaiser's compositions often featured complex and unique arrangements, indicating her intention use of jazz and swing as musical inspirations. Many of her compositions showcased racial integration, something rarely seen in popular music in that period. Kaiser was a prominent member of the Darktown Strutters Society, a secret organisation of African American and Jewish musicians in the Harlem neighborhood of New York City. Kaiser continued to work as a producer, arranger, and pianist well into the 1950s, releasing her final recording, "The Anniversary Waltz", in 1957 alongside Herb Jeffries. She passed away in 1969 in New York City. In 2018, she was posthumously inducted into the Kansas Music Hall of Fame. Today, Kaiser's contribution to early jazz and swing music of the mid 20th century is celebrated by fans and music historians. Her unique sound, championed by both African American and Jewish musicians alike, showcases her genuine passion for creating music and supporting racial integration.

Eddy Bruma (born May 16, 1988) is a Dutch professional footballer who plays as a winger for Bundesliga club Hertha BSC, where he wears the number 11 shirt. Born in Maastricht, Netherlands, Bruma began his career at local club MVV Maastricht in the 2006–07 season. In his two years with the club, Bruma scored seven goals in 32 league appearances. In 2009, Bruma signed with Serbian side Red Star Belgrade, where he spent three seasons, making 81 league appearances and scoring 15 goals before transferring to Dutch side PSV Eindhoven in 2012. In his three seasons with PSV, Bruma was a key member of the team, helping them to the second position in the Eredivisie in 2012–13 and 2013–14, and to the KNVB Cup title in 2012–13. He was also named as the Dutch Footballer of the Year in 2014. In September 2015, Bruma signed a four-year contract with Turkish club Galatasaray, where he was a regular starter and scored nine goals in 46 league games. In June 2018, Bruma moved to Bundesliga side Hertha BSC, signing a three-year contract with the club. Bruma has so far made 26 league appearances for Hertha, and has scored three goals. Outside of football, Bruma is known for his passion for music. He is a vocalist and lyricist for the Dutch rock band No Man's Land, which he formed with friends in 2013. He is also known for his interest in fashion, and has modeled for a number of brands, including Nike and Adidas. Bruma has been capped four times by the Netherlands national team, making his debut in October 2016 in a friendly against Morocco.

4 (Ensemble) Compositions 1992 is an album of contemporary compositions written by American composer Robert Beaser. Released in 1992, the album contains four pieces, each scored for a unique ensemble of instruments. The ensemble is stocked with virtuosic soloists playing unfamiliar instruments, including oboe, English horn, string quartet, and marimba. Beaser's interest in a variety of folk and classical traditions is reflected in his writing, particularly in his use of polytonality, polyphonic structures, and passages mixing elements of modal and atonal tonalities. Each of the four pieces features some kind of soloist, and their interaction with the larger ensemble provides a unifying element. The first piece, "Lament of the Pines," is a two-movement piece scored for a combination of strings, oboe, and English horn. The opening section is an expression of mourning; the oboe's sorrowful solo is complemented by the strings' somber chords. In the second movement, the second voice, a chorale sung by the strings, emerges with a cheerful and lively tone, lightening the sentiment of the first. The second work, "Garden Music," is written for four marimbas in a large and complex texture. The marimbas move together in a similar way as a chamber orchestra, opening and closing movements in unison. This piece is characterized by its lively rhythm, virtuosic polyphonic writing, and its varied dynamic coloring. The third piece, "Arioso for Oboe and Strings," utilizes the solo oboe and string quartet to build a bright, lyrical piece. The solo line of the oboe is complemented by the string quartet interweaving harmonic and consonant material into the texture. The fourth, and final, piece, "Farewell to Ireland," is a simple and tune-like piece. Composed as a traditional Irish folk melody, the piece is arranged in a more classical texture, utilizing the oboe as a soloist. Featuring some of the finest contemporary composers, 4 (Ensemble) Compositions 1992 displays virtuosic writing with a variety of instrumentations, styles, and colors. By embracing a range of folk, chamber, and classical traditions, Beaser creates a unique and captivating album.

Pyrgotis pyramidias is a species of bee native to the Mediterranean region of the Middle East and North Africa. It is a relatively small and nondescript bee, but is of particular importance due to its role in pollination of the region's native vegetation. Pyrgotis pyramidias has a unique form of mating behavior, in which the female bee sets up a “trap line” of sorts by marking certain plants with secretions, or “traps”, that she sets up to attract potential mates. A prospective mate that lands on the trap emits a pheromone signal that is picked up by the female bee. She then responds to the signal by departing the trap in search of the mate. The bee frequents mostly barren and semi-arid areas with sparse vegetation, places where its main source of food comes from various species of euphorbia. It has also been observed foraging for other flowering plants nearby, such as crepe myrtle and nightshade. As a pollinator, Pyrgotis pyramidias has the important role of spreading the pollen from the native Mediterranean vegetation to the plant species near them. This helps to ensure a continual recruitment of new genetics in the vegetation, as well as increases its viability. The species is listed in the IUCN Red List as a species of least concern, though it is threatened by habitat loss and urbanization. As an important pollinator, conservation efforts should be taken to ensure that this species of bee is not lost. Apart from its important role in pollination, this species of bee has also been studied for its utility in certain industries. For instance, its use in producing cosmetic products (specifically, wax production) due to its particularly abundant wax producing glands, has been explored. In addition, it has been studied in beekeeping to determine its "frugality" which has the potential to increase honey production. Overall, Pyrgotis pyramidias is a small but important species of bee that plays a huge role in maintaining the Mediteranean region’s native vegetation. Continued study of the bee is important not only to ensure its continued survival, but also to help us gain a better understanding of the region’s local ecology.

Washington Yacht Club is a private yacht club located on the Lake Washington Ship Canal in Seattle, Washington. Founded in 1889, it is one of the oldest yacht clubs in the Pacific Northwest and is affiliated with the American Yacht Club Association. The Club is situated on the south shore of Lake Washington, near the Fremont Bridge. It is accessible from the shore and by boat. The grounds includes a large dock, a swimming platform, and pool access. It is a member of the Lake Washington Sailing Association, a nine-club group, and they actively participate in NWISA regattas. The Club facilities include a clubhouse, bar and restaurant, as well as a service marina and boat launch. Guests are always welcome to take advantage of all the amenities offered. They also provide year round sailing and racing programs, with regattas for dinghies, cruisers, one-designs, and multihulls. The Washington Yacht Club is led by a Board of Trustees and executive management team. They offer a variety of memberships, ranging from full-time to occasional, and social memberships. The Club is one of the few yacht clubs in the United States that is open to all genders, races, sexual orientations, and creeds, and encourages diversity among their members. The Club has a long tradition of conforming to standards set forth by the United States Sailing Association. It is recognized for their dedication to sailing within the Northwest, and for their dedication for over 100 years to the sport of sailing. Washington Yacht Club is a staple in the Pacific Northwest sailing community, and is relied upon for hosting sailing related functions, events, and regattas. They offer a unique and engaging atmosphere year-round, and are an integral part of the Seattle sailing scene.

The Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Single-Camera Picture Editing for a Comedy Series is an Emmy Award given annually to the individual or team of picture editors responsible for the editing of a single-camera comedy series. The award has been awarded annually since 2000 and is presented by the Television Academy at the Creative Arts Emmy Awards ceremony. The award is specifically for picture editors. It is one of the many awards that honors those in the field of post-production. Picture editors must be the primary editors of a series and the editing must be done with a single-camera, as opposed to being a multi-camera sitcom edited in a live broadcast format. In 2018, the award went to Debra Light and Jack Neary, the editors of the HBO series Silicon Valley. Light had previously won the award in 2007 for her work on the NBC comedy 30 Rock. The other 2018 nominees included an editor from Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt, an editor from Master of None, and three editors from Veep. The Primetime Emmy Award has been awarded to several prominent comedy series. Shows such as Curb Your Enthusiasm, Modern Family, and Veep have all earned the award multiple times throughout the years. In 2017 and 2018, both Veep and Modern Family were nominated for the award but were beaten out by Atlanta and Silicon Valley respectively. The Emmys for single-camera picture editing for a comedy series has become a respected award in the post-production field. It recognizes the technical skills of the individuals responsible for transforming the scripts and performances of a television series into an enjoyable and engaging experience for viewers. It serves to remind the public of the significant contributions of the editing teams that work behind the scenes on their favorite shows.

The Las Vegas Strip is a stretch of South Las Vegas Boulevard in Clark County, Nevada, known for its concentration of resort hotels and casinos. The Strip is roughly 4.2 miles (6.8 km) long, and is immediately south of the Las Vegas city limits in the unincorporated towns of Paradise and Winchester, but is often referred to simply as Las Vegas. Many of the largest hotel, casino, and resort properties in the world are located on the Strip. The boulevard's cityscape is highlighted by its use of contemporary architecture, lights, and a wide variety of attractions. Its hotels, casinos, restaurants, residential high-rises, entertainment offerings, and skyline have established the Strip as one of the most popular and iconic tourist destinations in the world. Most of the Strip has also been designated an All-American Road, and is considered a scenic route at night. The Las Vegas Strip's first casino opened in 1941, and its first hotel, El Rancho Vegas, opened three years later. The Strip is just north of McCarran International Airport and the Las Vegas Convention Center. Major attractions along the Strip include the Bellagio, Caesars Palace, and The Mirage. It is also home to the Fountains of Bellagio and the High Roller Ferris wheel. Throughout its history, Las Vegas has been a destination for entertainment, gambling, dining, and shopping. As its popularity grew, so did the Strip, with more hotels and casinos being built over time. Today, the Strip boasts some of the world's tallest buildings, with the Stratosphere, the Paris Las Vegas, and the Caesars Palace all over 500 feet tall. The resorts of the Las Vegas Strip are some of the world's most luxurious. Their sheer size rivals that of cities and features of their own. From fantasy-themed resorts to world-class attractions, the Strip offers something for everyone. From Cirque du Soleil to live music and comedy, there's plenty to keep visitors entertained. Additionally, Las Vegas is known for its entertainment, shopping, and dining. The Strip is home to some of the world's largest shopping malls, the Forum Shops at Caesars Palace and the Miracle Mile Shops at Planet Hollywood Resort & Casino. In conclusion, the Las Vegas Strip is one of the most iconic and popular tourist destinations in the world. Home to some of the largest and most luxurious resorts, this iconic boulevard is renowned around the world for its gambling, entertainment, dining, and shopping offerings. From its alluring neon lights to its vibrant nightlife, the Strip has become a symbol of Sin City and its unique spirit.

Plugola is a term used in the marketing industry which refers to an exchange of goods or services for a positive review. It is a form of pay-for-play marketing that benefits both parties, yet is typically controversial and met with scrutiny in the industry. Plugola is not new, with roots stretching back decades; however, new technology has made it far easier to coordinate and take place. Platforms such as Amazon and Yelp have enabled businesses and customers to search for reviews and connected them to those who offer services in exchange for such reviews. This has raised concern by many that ratings and reviews are no longer reflective of genuine experiences, due to a lack of regulation and enforcement related to plugola. Plugola involves both parties – the customer offering the review and the business or services provider – benefitting from the exchange. The customer may be incentivized to leave a positive review in exchange for a service or discount, while the business or service provider can use the reviews to bring in more customers. As a result, plugola can potentially increase the online presence of a business and improve effectiveness of a customer's personal brand. Despite potential short-term success, businesses that engage in plugola face legal recourse since it is viewed as deceptive advertising. The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) requires customer reviews to be “honest and not misleading” and has gone so far as to impose fines on businesses they’ve deemed to be engaging in deceptive advertising. Additionally, there is the potential of creating a poor customer experience if customers are offered discounts in exchange for reviews and decide to save the review for multiple discounts. Along with the customer experience, plugola can have an effect on the quality of reviews being left. Even if the customer is genuine, the root of the review comes from a transaction which may lead to bias or a lack of contextual detail. This is compounded when reviews are posted without disclosing that a customer received a reward or incentive for their review, and then customers become skeptical of reviews posted by that customer on the platform. The debate of plugola is one that will continue as it is a form of marketing that can yield positive results for both the customer and business, yet lacks regulation and may contain deceitful practices. Businesses need to be aware that potential FTC fines as well as customer sentiment should be kept in mind when considering participating in plugola. If done ethically and honestly, this form of pay-for-play marketing could yield positive results in the short and long term.

The Premier League–Football League gulf refers to the vast difference in both wealth and quality between the two highest levels of English professional football. The two levels, referred to by their collective terms, are known as the Premier League (or simply “the top flight”) and the Football League (or “the Championship” and other divisions below it). Added together, these leagues make up the English football pyramid. Financial disparity between the Premier League and the Football League has become a topic of discussion amongst commentators, journalists, and outside observers in recent decades. The gulf in wealth and resources between the two levels first became visible in the early 1990s when the Premier League was formed from the old Football League First Division. In 1992, the Premier League clubs signed a television deal with Sky Sports worth £440 million over five seasons, swelling Premier League clubs with cash. In comparison, the Football League clubs were only able to generate a collective deal of £212 million. The situation was exacerbated by the distribution of the television money. It had been agreed by the Premier League and Sky Sports in the 1992 television deal that all of the teams in the league would receive the same amount of money for appearing on live television, regardless of their on-pitch performance or status. This even distribution of the television money gave teams in the league a huge cushion against financial losses, and discouraged relegation from the top flight. Those teams farther down the pyramid in the Football League divisions have therefore seen the impact of the Premier League–Football League gulf on their finances and fortunes. Clubs at the bottom of the Championship often find it difficult to bridge the gap to Premier League levels of finance, leading to an increasing financial inequality in the English professional game. Consequently, it is very hard for Football League clubs to make the leap to the big-money Premier League, whilst the teams at the bottom of the Premier League enjoy the benefits of its vast financial resources, making relegation unlikely. The English football pyramid is one of the most unequal amongst Europe’s top leagues, with a huge gulf separating the Premier League and the Football League in terms of financial resources, quality of players, and overall quality of competition. The Premier League–Football League gulf has become an oft-discussed topic in recent years, as the English football world has worked to close the gap between the two competitions.

Stealing First Base, also known as stealing home, is a play in baseball in which a runner on-base attempts to advance to the next base without the aid of a batted ball. It is one of the most exciting and daring plays in baseball and is seen frequently in the major leagues. When successful, the play can be the difference between a win and a loss for the team’s win-loss record. Stealing first is regarded as the most difficult base-stealing play, as the runner must reach the bag with only the break of his leadfoot. The pitcher provides the distraction, as he must be focused on the hitter and not on the runner. Speed and audacity are required to pull off a successful steal. The runner must also rely on the vigilance of the pitcher and catcher. When the pitcher or catcher notices the runner attempting to steal a base, they have a few options. The most common, and the one recommended by professionals, is to step off the rubber and, if time allows, make a throw towards the base. Other methods include a throw directly to the base, the catcher making a quick move towards the base, or the pitcher making a quick glance towards the base. It is important for a runner to remember that in order to steal a base, he must not be tagged before he crosses it. The catcher can also attempt to field the pitch, as well as utilize the pickoff move. The pitcher’s pickoff move is when the pitcher looks towards the runner and attempts to tag him before he reaches the bag. When a successful steal happens, the crowd goes wild. First base steals may be risky, but if done correctly, the risk pays off and the team benefits from an extra runner. Watching a runner steal a base is an exciting play that can happen at any moment in the game and it is always a thrilling to watch a runner successfully steal first.

"I Can Dream About You" is a song written and performed by American singer-songwriter Dan Hartman and originally released in 1984. The song was featured in the film Streets of Fire as as the closing theme and was featured on the film's soundtrack album. The song slowed down the tempo and added a saxophone solo, whereas the original was a faster, uptempo dance track. The form of the song is a ballad. The track peaked at number six on the Billboard Hot 100 in the United States, back in 1984. It also charted in the United Kingdom at number forty four. The lyrics of the song tell the story of a man, dreaming of a woman he is attracted to and remembering the happiness they once shared together. It’s been said that the song was written about Karen Lawrence, Dan’s friend and keyboardist for the Edgar Winter Group. The lyrics breathe heartache as the singer dreams about all the things he wishes he could do with his former, departed love: “When I'm feeling down, Blue and lonely Picture your smile, and I can dream about you When I'm in a crowd, I'm so alone Picture your face, and I can dream about you” The song was covered by 3T featuring Michael Jackson in 1995. Meanwhile, a remix of the song was released in 2011 by German DJ and producer David May. The remix peaked at number twenty seven on the German Singles Chart. Furthermore, the song was used in the 2017 Super Bowl ad for Buick. In 2019, the song was featured during a scene in the fifth episode of the second season of the FX series, "Pose". Although "I Can Dream About You" was not a major hit in the United Kingdom, it continues to be a staple on classic, gold and dance radio station and is considered a true classic of the 1980s.

Isotopes of nobelium are the atomic species of nobelium that have different atomic mass numbers. Nobelium is a synthetic, radioactive element with atomic number 102 and the symbol No. It has thirty-seven known isotopes ranging from 239No (the shortest-lived) to 280No. Nobelium-237 has a half-life of just 31seconds and is the most prevalent naturally occurring isotope, accounting for roughly 87% of the nobelium observed in the universe. It is followed in abundance by 252No, with a half-life of 2.97 minutes. Nobelium-252 can only be produced in particle accelerators and has been used to synthesize some of the heavier elements beyond nobelium. Nobelium-254 is calculated to have a half-life of 14 milliseconds, but because it is so short-lived, it is impossible to decay into a stable nucleus and must beta-decay directly to its daughter nucleus. It has been observed gamma-decaying to the daughter nucleus 254Cf (fermium-254), with the minimum half-life believed to be 0.6 milliseconds. Theoretically, there are more than 40 isotopes of nobelium with mass numbers from 239 to 280. In 2009, researchers at the GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research in Germany were able to synthesize a nobelium isotope with mass number 259 and a half-life of 144 ms. This is the longest-lived isotope of nobelium that has been observed to date. Nobelium-263, 266, 267, and 269 have not been observed yet and the exact nature of the decay of nobelium isotopes is still a matter of research. Nobelium-267 was recently hypothesized to be the parent element of a triad of hypothetical superheavy elements, including the still-unobserved elements flerovium and moscovium. Because of the extremely high instability of nobelium and its isotopes, there is limited practical use for nobelium isotopes outside of research settings. In laboratory settings, isotopes of nobelium have been used to investigate nuclear structures, behaviors, and decay rates of nuclei beyond nobelium, as well as to synthesize higher elements. Additionally, nobelium isotopes have been used to study the effects of alpha particle emission on the subsequent decay of material.

Robert Cuffley is a Canadian film director and screenwriter from British Columbia. He is best known for directing the films Chokeslam (2016) and Traveling Light (2009). Cuffley was born in Vancouver, British Columbia and attended the University of British Columbia where he studied film production. While attending university, he wrote, directed and edited several short films, which were showcased at various film festivals. After graduating, he wrote and directed his first feature, Traveling Light (2009). The film was accepted into the prestigious Berlin International Film Festival and has won various awards including a Genie Award. In 2016, Cuffley wrote and directed his second feature, Chokeslam. The film was an official selection at the Toronto International Film Festival and the Vancouver International Film Festival. It was also released theatrically in Canada in February 2016. Cuffley has appeared as a guest on panels and lectures on filmmaking and has taught classes on directing at the University of British Columbia. He is currently developing a television series for CBC and working on a new feature film with support from Telefilm Canada. Cuffley's films are characterized by their black humour, magical realism and thought-provoking characters. He draws inspiration for his films from the diverse mix of culture in British Columbia. Cuffley is an influential figure in the Canadian film industry. He has received several nominations for his work, including a Canadian Screen Award in 2016 and a Leo Award in 2017. He continues to work on television productions and feature films in Canada, with his work earning critical acclaim both domestically and internationally.

The Year of the Spider refers to a period of time in 2019, during which the internet and technology industry experienced a series of significant changes, technological advances, and other notable occurrences. Primarily, the year was associated with the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the emergence of various technological developments and projects, the redefinition of traditional business models, and the rise of cyber-security awareness and threats. In 2019, Google released their first AI assistant called Google Duplex, which enabled users to book their Restaurant and Salon appointments with AI powered robotic voice. Along with that, Google also launched their own self-driving car service. Additionally, Facebook declared the launch of its highly anticipated Libra cryptocurrency, which made waves across the tech industry. On the other hand, tech giants such as Microsoft and Amazon released updates to their own voice assistant AIs such as Cortana and Alexa respectively. Additionally, Microsoft launched updates to its own Quantum computers and Azure cloud platform. The Year of the Spider also saw the emergence of several new trends and technologies, such as the big data analytics and machine learning to bring about a new level of automation to businesses. Additionally, the rise of edge computing opened up new opportunities for data security and analytics. Lastly, the rise of Conversational AI enabled businesses to automate customer service, giving customers an automated yet personalized day-to-day experience. The Year of the Spider also saw several high-profile cyber threats and attacks, such as the series of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks against various businesses that left their tech infrastructure crippled and resulted in loss of data. This further underscored the need for cyber-security awareness and practices. Throughout this period, the internet industry saw a solidification of the social media platforms and the emergence of both new and old ventures, such as TikTok and Instagram, and the influx of new technologies and advancements that enabled both consumers and businesses to take advantage of. As a result, the Year of the Spider saw an upsurge in the development of technological products and services, making it an important year in the history of the internet and technology industry. Overall, the Year of the Spider saw a period of great changes in the internet and technology industry, from the emergence of AI to the rise of cyber-security awareness, and the need for a constantly updated approach to technology. The technological advancements and innovations of this period made the internet a far more efficient and effective tool for the modern day consumer, showcasing the power of technology in the hands of the people.

System Development Corporation (SDC) is a business and technology services provider that provides information systems, technical consulting, software engineering, project engineering, and much more. Founded in 1956, the company provides services to businesses of all sizes in the United States and worldwide. SDC provides a wide range of services to its clients, from consulting to custom software development, with the goal of helping organizations improve their operations and slash their costs. SDC's service offerings include: business process analysis, program management and integration, systems design, and development, operations support, network and database engineering, systems administration, IT security, access management and training. The company also provides a wide range of services in support of enterprise applications, such as Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP). The company is further divided into four divisions: Consulting Services, Business Applications, Web Services, and Technology Solutions. Consulting Services provides financial consulting services for companies’ accounting and tax needs, as well as business process reengineering. The Business Applications division offers software development and integration, enterprise application integration and management, and database maintenance and development. Web Services covers server and network management, web applications, and e-commerce solutions. Technology Solutions focuses on systems design and implementation, performance engineering, and network monitoring. SDC has built a reputation for quality and reliability, winning awards for its work such as “The World’s Best Employee Retention Strategy” from the CIO Magazine, The Microsoft Corporation Partner of the Year Award, The Internet World “GoMarketing” Award, The Transaction Processing Council 2007 Award, and many more. The organization is known for its commitment to ethical standards and community involvement. Due to its reputation, SDC has earned the trust of many prominent organizations. Its past clients include The Department of Justice, NASA, The Centers for Disease Control and prevention, The Pentagon, and The Department of Defense. In an ever-evolving world, SDC continues to remain on the cutting-edge of business and technology and to take a leading role in helping organizations deliver superior customer service through their IT initiatives. Through its vast array of services, and impressive list of clients, it is no surprise SDC has become one of the world’s top providers of business and technology services.

State Highway 24 (SH 24) is a state highway in the Waikato region of New Zealand. It is a major route running south to north between the towns Raglan and Te Awamutu. It is approximately 34 km long and links to other state highways: SH 23, SH 39 and SH 3. The route begins in the south at its junction with SH 23 near the town of Raglan. It makes its way north, going through Hamilton and Cambridge, before terminating at its junction with SH 39 in the north of Te Awamutu. Most of the route is a single carriageway, but there are two-lane sections in Hamilton, Cambridge and Te Awamutu. Near Hamilton, it passes under the Hamilton Expressway, a limited-access motorway. The route passes through varied terrain, including small streams and wetlands, undulating farmlands, low-lying hills and dense forests. SH 24 is the main route connecting the rural towns of Te Awamutu, Cambridge and Raglan, providing vital access to these communities. The route also serves as an alternate route between Hamilton and the Waikato region’s major urban centres. It is heavily used by commuters, visitors and freight services, and is one of the Waikato region’s busiest highways.
